t: The western cattle egret (Ardea ibis) is a species of heron (family Ardeidae) found in the tropics, subtropics and warm temperate zones. Formerly, most taxonomic authorities lumped this species and the eastern cattle egret together (called the cattle egret), but the two cattle egrets are now treated as separate species.
f: It nests in colonies, usually near bodies of water and often with other wading birds.

t: The trumpeter finch (Bucanetes githagineus) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is mainly a desert species which is found in North Africa and Spain through to southern Asia.
f: It has occurred as a vagrant in areas north of its breeding range.

t: The yellow-spotted barbet (Buccanodon duchaillui) is a bird species in the monotypic genus Buccanodon. It belongs to the African barbet family (Lybiidae) which was formerly included in the Capitonidae and sometimes in the Ramphastidae.
f: These song differences led to the description of B. dowsetti as a distinct species.

t: The collared puffbird (Bucco capensis) is a species of bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The chestnut-capped puffbird (Bucco macrodactylus) is a species of bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The spotted puffbird (Bucco tamatia) is a species of puffbird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The bufflehead (Bucephala albeola) is a small sea duck of the genus Bucephala, the goldeneyes. This species was first described by Carl Linnaeus in his landmark 1758 10th edition of Systema Naturae as Anas albeola.
f: It breeds in Alaska and Canada and migrates in winter to southern North America.

t: The common goldeneye or simply goldeneye (Bucephala clangula) is a medium-sized sea duck of the genus Bucephala, the goldeneyes. Its closest relative is the similar Barrow's goldeneye.
f: Its name, Bucephala clangula, means "to resound," referencing its elaborate courtship displays.

t: Barrow's goldeneye (Bucephala islandica) is a medium-sized sea duck of the genus Bucephala, the goldeneyes. The genus name is derived from Ancient Greek boukephalos, "bullheaded", from bous, "bull" and kephale, "head", a reference to the bulbous head shape of the bufflehead.
f: This bird was named after Sir John Barrow.

t: The great hornbill (Buceros bicornis), also known as the concave-casqued hornbill, great Indian hornbill or great pied hornbill, is one of the larger members of the hornbill family. It occurs in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.
f: Due to its large size and colour, and importance in many tribal cultures and rituals, the Government of Kerala declared it as the official Kerala state bird.

t: The rufous hornbill (Buceros hydrocorax), also known as the Philippine hornbill and locally as kalaw (pronounced KAH-lau), is a large species of hornbill endemic to the Philippines (the largest hornbill in the country). It is called the "clock-of-the-mountains" by locals, because of its loud booming call which typically occurs every hour.
f: It is illegal to hunt, capture or possess rufous hornbills under Philippine Law RA 9147.

t: The rhinoceros hornbill (Buceros rhinoceros) is a large species of forest hornbill. In captivity, it can live for up to 35 years.
f: The rhinoceros hornbill is the state bird of the Malaysian state of Sarawak and the country's national bird.

t: The helmeted hornbill (Rhinoplax vigil) is a very large bird in the hornbill family. It is found on the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Borneo, Thailand and Myanmar.
f: The casque (helmetlike structure on the head) accounts for some 11% of its 3 kg weight.

t: The southern ground hornbill (Bucorvus leadbeateri) is one of two species of ground hornbill, both of which are found solely within Africa, and is the largest species in the hornbill order worldwide. Within these regions, they inhabit both woodlands and savannas.
f: It can be found in the southern regions of Africa, ranging from Kenya to South Africa.

t: Bulwer's petrel (Bulweria bulwerii) is a small petrel in the family Procellariidae that is found in tropical and subtropical regions of the Atlantic, Indian and Pacific Oceans.
f: It is named after the English naturalist James Bulwer.

t: The yellow-billed oxpecker (Buphagus africanus) is a passerine bird in the family Buphagidae. It was previously placed in the starling and myna family, Sturnidae.
f: It is native to the savannah of Sub-Saharan Africa from Senegal east to Sudan.

t: The red-billed oxpecker (Buphagus erythrorynchus) is a passerine bird in the oxpecker family, Buphagidae. It is native to the eastern savannah of sub-Saharan Africa, from the Central African Republic east to South Sudan and south to northern and eastern South Africa.
f: It is more widespread than the yellow-billed oxpecker in Southern Africa, where their ranges overlap.

t: The double-striped thick-knee (Hesperoburhinus bistriatus) is a stone-curlew, a group of waders in the family Burhinidae.
f: The vernacular name refers to the prominent joints in the long greenish-grey legs, and bistriatus to the two stripes of the head pattern.

t: The spotted thick-knee (Burhinus capensis), also known as the spotted dikkop or Cape thick-knee, is a wader in the family Burhinidae.
f: It is native to tropical regions of central and southern Africa.

t: The bush stone-curlew or bush thick-knee (Burhinus grallarius, obsolete name Burhinus magnirostris) is a large, ground-dwelling bird endemic to Australia. Its favoured habitat is open plains and woodlands, where it stalks slowly at night in search of invertebrates such as insects.
f: Both sexes care for two eggs laid on the bare ground, usually sited near bush in a shaded position or next to a fallen branch.

t: The Indian stone-curlew or Indian thick-knee (Burhinus indicus) is a species of bird in the family Burhinidae. It was formerly included as a subspecies of the Eurasian stone-curlew.
f: They have large eyes and are brown with streaks and pale marks making it hard to spot against the background of soils and rocks.
The Eurasian stone-curlew, Eurasian thick-knee, or simply stone-curlew (Burhinus oedicnemus), is a northern species of the Burhinidae (stone-curlew) bird family.

t: The Senegal thick-knee (Burhinus senegalensis) is a stone-curlew, a group of waders in the family Burhinidae.
f: Their vernacular scientific name refers to the prominent joints in the long yellow or greenish legs.

t: The Peruvian thick-knee (Hesperoburhinus superciliaris) is a species of bird in the family Burhinidae. It is found in Chile, Ecuador, and Peru.
f: It is a ground-dwelling bird and feeds on insects and small animals.

t: The water thick-knee or water dikkop (Burhinus vermiculatus) is a species of bird in the thick-knee family Burhinidae.
f: The species is found across sub-Saharan Africa, usually close to water.

t: The black-collared hawk (Busarellus nigricollis) is a species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. It is monotypic within the genus Busarellus.
f: The black-collared hawk has the basal phalanges of the inner toe fused, which may be an adaptation to prevent the toe from bending back when catching prey.

t: The grey-faced buzzard (Butastur indicus) is an Asian bird of prey. It is typically 41–46 cm (16–18 in) in length, making it a small-sized raptor.
f: It eats lizards, small mammals and large insects.

t: The white-eyed buzzard (Butastur teesa) is a medium-sized hawk, distinct from the true buzzards in the genus Buteo, found in South Asia. Adults have a rufous tail, a distinctive white iris, and a white throat bearing a dark mesial stripe bordered.
f: They sit upright on perches for prolonged periods and soar on thermals in search of insect and small vertebrate prey.

t: The white-throated hawk (Buteo albigula) is a bird of prey in subfamily Buteoninae, the "soaring" hawks, of family Accipitridae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The zone-tailed hawk (Buteo albonotatus) is a medium-sized hawk of warm, dry parts of the Americas. It is somewhat similar in plumage and flight style to a common scavenger, the turkey vulture, and may benefit from being able to blend into groups of vultures.
f: It feeds on small terrestrial tetrapods of all kinds.

t: The augur buzzard (Buteo augur) is a fairly large African bird of prey. This member of the Buteo genus is distributed in several parts of the central and southern Africa, normally being found from Ethiopia to southern Angola and central Namibia.
f: It is a typical buteonine raptor, being a generalist predator which tends to prefer small mammals supplemented by reptiles and birds among various prey items.

t: It is a species from the widespread genus Buteo in the family Accipitridae.
f: The Madagascar buzzard (Buteo brachypterus) is a bird of prey which is endemic to Madagascar.

t: The short-tailed hawk (Buteo brachyurus) is an American bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes the eagles and Old World vultures. The white-throated hawk (B. albigula) is a close relative and was formerly included in the species B. brachyurus.
f: As a member of the genus Buteo, it is not a true hawk and thus also referred to as a "buteo" or (outside North America) "buzzard".

t: The common buzzard (Buteo buteo) is a medium-sized bird of prey with a large range. It is a member of the genus Buteo in the family Accipitridae.
f: It is the most common diurnal raptor in Europe, with a population of millions.

t: The red-tailed hawk (Buteo jamaicensis) is a bird of prey and one of the most common hawks in North America. In the United States, it is one of three species colloquially known as the "chickenhawk".
f: Pairs stay together for life, taking a new mate only when the original mate dies.

t: The eastern buzzard or Japanese buzzard (Buteo japonicus) is a medium to large bird of prey that is sometimes considered a subspecies of the widespread common buzzard (Buteo buteo). It is native to East Asia and some parts of Russia and South Asia, with some birds wintering in Southeast Asia.
f: It is similar to the steppe buzzard.

t: The rough-legged buzzard (Europe) or rough-legged hawk (North America) (Buteo lagopus) is a medium-large bird of prey. It is found in arctic and subarctic regions of North America, Europe, and Asia during the breeding season, and migrates south for the winter.
f: Along with the kestrels, kites, and osprey, this is one of the few birds of prey to hover regularly.

t: The red-shouldered hawk (Buteo lineatus) is a medium-sized buteo. It is a permanent resident throughout most of its range, though northern birds do migrate, mostly to central Mexico.
f: Its breeding range spans eastern North America, along the coast of California and northern to northeastern-central Mexico.

t: The red-shouldered hawk (Buteo lineatus) is a medium-sized buteo. It is a permanent resident throughout most of its range, though northern birds do migrate, mostly to central Mexico.
f: It breeds along the coast of California and northern Mexico, a surprisingly wide range for a Red-shouldered Hawk.

t: The gray-lined hawk (Buteo nitidus) is a smallish raptor found in open country and forest edges. It is sometimes placed in the genus Asturina as Asturina nitida.
f: The gray-lined hawk is found from El Salvador to Argentina, as well as on the Caribbean island of Trinidad.

The mountain buzzard (Buteo oreophilus) is a bird of prey that lives in montane forests in East Africa, it and the forest buzzard (Buteo trizonatus) of southern Africa were, until recently, considered to be a single species.

t: The gray hawk (Buteo plagiatus) or Mexican goshawk is a smallish raptor found in open country and forest edges. It is sometimes placed in the genus Asturina as Asturina plagiata.
f: The call is a shrill whistled kleee-ooo.

t: The broad-winged hawk (Buteo platypterus) is a medium-sized hawk of the genus Buteo. During the summer, some subspecies are distributed over eastern North America, as far west as British Columbia and Texas; they then migrate south to winter in the Neotropics from Mexico south to southern Brazil.
f: As in most raptors, females are slightly larger than males.

t: The ferruginous hawk (Buteo regalis) is a large bird of prey and belongs to the broad-winged buteo hawks. The generic name buteo is Latin for 'buzzard'.
f: An old colloquial name is ferrugineous rough-leg, due to its similarity to the closely related rough-legged hawk (B. lagopus).

t: Ridgway's hawk (Buteo ridgwayi) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae endemic to the island of Hispaniola (both Haiti and the Dominican Republic) in the Caribbean. It is classified as Critically Endangered because of habitat destruction and human persecution in the Dominican Republic; however, due to conservation efforts, the population is now increasing.
f: It is named in honour of the ornithologist Robert Ridgway.

t: The Hawaiian hawk or ʻio (Buteo solitarius) is a raptor in the genus Buteo endemic to Hawaiʻi, currently restricted to the Big Island. The ʻio is one of two extant birds of prey that are native to Hawaiʻi, the other being the pueo (Hawaiian short-eared owl) and fossil evidence indicates that it inhabited the island of Hawaiʻi, Molokaʻi, Oʻahu, Maui and Kauaʻi at one time.
f: Today, it is known to breed only on the Big Island, in stands of native ʻōhiʻa lehua (Metrosideros polymorpha) trees.

t: Swainson's hawk (Buteo swainsoni) is a large bird species in the Accipitriformes order. It is colloquially known as the grasshopper hawk or locust hawk, as it is very fond of Acrididae (locusts and grasshoppers) and will voraciously eat these insects whenever they are available.
f: This species was named after William Swainson, a British naturalist.
The common black hawk (Buteogallus anthracinus) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes the eagles, hawks, and vultures.

t: The Chaco eagle (Buteogallus coronatus) or crowned solitary eagle, is an endangered bird of prey from eastern and central South America. Due to its rarity, not much is known about its biology or population.
f: Typically it is known simply as the crowned eagle, which leads to potential confusion with the African Stephanoaetus coronatus.

t: The savanna hawk (Buteogallus meridionalis) is a large raptor found in open savanna and swamp edges. It was formerly placed in the genus Heterospizias.
f: It breeds from Panama and Trinidad south to Bolivia, Uruguay and central Argentina.

t: The slate-colored hawk (Buteogallus schistaceus) is a species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae: the hawks, eagles, and allies.
f: It is found in the Amazon rainforest in Brazil, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, Venezuela, and French Guiana.

t: The solitary eagle or montane solitary eagle (Buteogallus solitarius) is a large Neotropical eagle.
f: It is also known as the black solitary eagle.
The great black hawk (Buteogallus urubitinga) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes the eagles, hawks, and Old World vultures.

t: The hooded mountain tanager (Buthraupis montana) is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is the only member of the genus Buthraupis.
f: At 23 centimetres (9.1 in) and 96 grams (3.4 oz), it is one of the largest tanagers.

t: The striated heron (Butorides striata) also known as mangrove heron or little green heron, is a small heron, about 44 cm tall. The breeding habitat is in South America and the Caribbean.
f: It is mostly sedentary and noted for some interesting behavioural traits.

t: The green heron (Butorides virescens) is a small heron of North and Central America. It was long considered conspecific with its sister species the striated heron (Butorides striata); when treated together, they were called "green-backed heron".
f: Butorides is from Middle English butor "bittern" and Ancient Greek -oides, "resembling", and virescens is Latin for "greenish".

t: The white-thighed hornbill (Bycanistes albotibialis) is a species of hornbill. It is sometimes considered to be a subspecies of the brown-cheeked hornbill.
f: It is found in Angola, Benin, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Nigeria, Sudan, and Uganda.

t: The silvery-cheeked hornbill (Bycanistes brevis) is a large species of hornbill found in Africa. In Zimbabwe it is threatened by habitat destruction and its presence in South Africa is marginal, but it remains locally fairly common, especially in the northern and central parts of its range.
f: Silvery-cheeked hornbills are residents of the tall evergreen forests of East Africa from Ethiopia to South Africa.

t: The trumpeter hornbill (Bycanistes bucinator) is a medium-sized hornbill, with length between 58 and 65 cm (23 and 26 in), characterized by a large grey casque on the bill, smaller in females. The eyes are brown or red, with pink surrounding skin.
f: Like other hornbills, the females incubate four to five white eggs while sealed in the nest compartment.

t: The piping hornbill (Bycanistes fistulator) is a bird in the hornbill family. At about 50 cm (20 in) in length, it is the smallest member of the genus Bycanistes.
f: This black-and-white species is found in humid forest and second growth in Central and West Africa, ranging from Senegal east to Uganda and south to Angola.

t: The black-and-white-casqued hornbill (Bycanistes subcylindricus), also known as the grey-cheeked hornbill, is a large black and white hornbill. It has an oversized blackish bill with a large casque on top.
f: It is a monogamous species, and pairs nest in suitable tree cavities.

t: The white cockatoo (Cacatua alba), also known as the umbrella cockatoo, is a medium-sized all-white cockatoo endemic to tropical rainforest on islands of Indonesia. The wings and tail have a pale yellow or lemon color which is exposed when they fly.
f: When surprised, it extends a large and striking head crest, which has a semicircular shape (similar to an umbrella, hence the alternative name).

t: The Solomons corella (Cacatua ducorpsii), also known as Solomons cockatoo, Ducorps's cockatoo or broad-crested corella, is a species of cockatoo endemic to the Solomon Islands archipelago. This small white cockatoo is larger than the Tanimbar corella yet smaller than the umbrella cockatoo.
f: The species is common across most of the Solomons, absent only from Makira in the south.

t: The sulphur-crested cockatoo (Cacatua galerita) is a relatively large white cockatoo found in wooded habitats in Australia, New Guinea, and some of the islands of Indonesia. As highly intelligent birds, they are well known in aviculture, although they can be demanding pets.
f: It is well known in aviculture, although they can be demanding pets.

t: The Tanimbar corella (Cacatua goffiniana), also known as Goffin's cockatoo or Tanimbar cockatoo, is a species of cockatoo endemic to forests of Yamdena, Larat, and Selaru, all islands in the Tanimbar Islands archipelago in Indonesia. It has been introduced to the Kai Islands, Indonesia; Puerto Rico; and Singapore.
f: This species was only formally described in 2004, after it was discovered that the previous formal descriptions pertained to individuals of a different cockatoo species, Ducorps' or Solomons cockatoo (Cacatua ducorpsii).

t: The little corella (Cacatua sanguinea), also known as the short-billed corella, bare-eyed cockatoo, blood-stained cockatoo, and little cockatoo is a white cockatoo native to Australia and southern New Guinea. It was known as Birdirra among the Yindjibarndi people of the central and western Pilbara.
f: The downy feathers are used in traditional ceremonies and dances where they adorn head and armbands.

t: The long-billed corella, also known as long-billed cockatoo or slender-billed corella (Cacatua tenuirostris), is a cockatoo native to Australia, which is similar in appearance to the little corella. It has reddish-pink feathers on the breast and belly.
f: This species is mostly white, with a reddish-pink face and forehead, and has a long, pale beak, which is used to dig for roots and seeds.

t: The yellow-rumped cacique (Cacicus cela) is a passerine bird in the New World family Icteridae. It breeds in much of northern South America from Panama, Venezuela and Trinidad south to Peru, Bolivia and central Brazil.
f: However, they have been sighted as far north as Nayarit state in Mexico.

t: The mountain cacique (Cacicus chrysonotus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The golden-winged cacique (Cacicus chrysopterus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The red-rumped cacique (Cacicus haemorrhous) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile.

t: The band-tailed cacique (Cacicus latirostris) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The casqued cacique (Cacicus oseryi) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and possibly Bolivia.

t: The solitary cacique or solitary black cacique (Cacicus solitarius) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, subtropical or tropical swamps, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela.

t: The scarlet-rumped cacique (Cacicus uropygialis) is a passerine bird species in the New World blackbird family Icteridae.
f: This species has sometimes been split into two species: the scarlet-rumped cacique (Cacicus microrhynchus) and the subtropical cacique (Cacicus uropygialis).

t: The chestnut-breasted cuckoo (Cacomantis castaneiventris) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.
f: It is found in Australia, Indonesia, and Papua New Guinea.

t: The fan-tailed cuckoo (Cacomantis flabelliformis) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae.
f: It is found in Australia, Fiji, New Caledonia, New Guinea, Solomon Islands, and Vanuatu.

t: The white-crowned cuckoo or white-crowned koel (Caliechthrus leucolophus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It was formerly placed in the genus Cacomantis but is now the only species placed in the genus Caliechthrus.
f: It was originally described in 1840 by the German naturalist Salomon Müller as Cuculus leucolophus.

t: The plaintive cuckoo (Cacomantis merulinus) is a species of bird belonging to the genus Cacomantis in the cuckoo family Cuculidae.
f: It is native to Asia, from India, Nepal and China to Indonesia.

t: The pallid cuckoo (Heteroscenes pallidus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It is the only species placed in the genus Heteroscenes.
f: The pallid cuckoo is similar in appearance to the oriental cuckoo (Cuculus optatus), with barred immature pallid cuckoos being often mistaken for oriental cuckoos.
The grey-bellied cuckoo or the Indian plaintive cuckoo (Cacomantis passerinus) is a cuckoo with widespread occurrence throughout Asia.

t: The banded bay cuckoo or bay-banded cuckoo (Cacomantis sonneratii) is a species of small cuckoo found in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. Like others in the genus they have round nostrils.
f: Males sing from exposed branches during the breeding season, which can vary with region.

t: The Sahul brush cuckoo (Cacomantis variolosus), formerly known as the brush cuckoo, is a member of the cuckoo family. It is native to Malesia, New Guinea, the Solomon Islands and northern and eastern Australia.
f: Its call is a familiar sound of the Australian and Indonesian bush.

t: The Muscovy duck (Cairina moschata) is a species of duck native to the Americas, from the Lower Rio Grande Valley of Texas and Mexico south to Argentina and Uruguay.
f: The species has been domesticated, and feral Muscovy ducks can be found locally in New Zealand, Australia, the United States, and in Central and Eastern Europe.

t: The Muscovy duck (Cairina moschata) is a species of duck native to the Americas, from the Lower Rio Grande Valley of Texas and Mexico south to Argentina and Uruguay.
f: The species has been domesticated, and feral Muscovy ducks can be found locally in New Zealand, Australia, the United States, and in Central and Eastern Europe.
The striated fieldwren (Calamanthus fuliginosus) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae, endemic to Australia.

t: The barred wren-warbler or southern barred warbler (Calamonastes fasciolatus) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitat is dry savanna.
f: It is found in Namibia, Botswana, western Angola, northern South Africa and southwestern Zimbabwe.

t: The grey wren-warbler (Calamonastes simplex) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is found in Angola, Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia.
f: It is normally found singly or in pairs and is a dark brownish-grey with inconspicuous barred markings.

t: Stierling's wren-warbler (Calamonastes stierlingi), is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae found in southern Africa.
f: It is sometimes considered a subspecies of the miombo wren-warbler.

t: The lark bunting (Calamospiza melanocorys) is a medium-sized American bunting native to central and western North America.
f: It was designated the state bird of Colorado in 1931.

t: Hume's short-toed lark (Calandrella acutirostris) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.
f: It is found in south-central Asia from Iran and Kazakhstan to China.

t: The greater short-toed lark (Calandrella brachydactyla) is a small passerine bird. The current scientific name is from Ancient Greek.
f: During migration they form large, tight flocks that move in unison; at other times they form loose flocks.

t: The red-capped lark (Calandrella cinerea) is a small passerine bird that breeds in the highlands of eastern Africa southwards from Ethiopia and Somaliland.
f: In the south, its range stretches across the continent to Angola and south to the Cape in South Africa.

t: The Mongolian short-toed lark or Sykes's short-toed lark (Calandrella dukhunensis) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.
f: It breeds in China and Mongolia and winters in southern Asia.

t: The Lapland longspur (Calcarius lapponicus), also known as the Lapland bunting, is a passerine bird in the longspur family Calcariidae.
f: It is a circumpolar arctic breeder and the only member of the genus Calcarius present in Eurasia.

t: The chestnut-collared longspur (Calcarius ornatus) is a species of bird in the family Calcariidae. It breeds in prairie habitats in Canada and the northern United States and winters to the south in the United States and Mexico.
f: Like the other longspurs, it is a small ground-feeding bird that primarily eats seeds.

t: Smith's longspur (Calcarius pictus) is a bird from the family Calcariidae, which also contains the other species of longspurs. A bird of open habitats, it breeds in northern Canada and Alaska, and winters in the southern United States.
f: Primarily a ground-feeding seed-eater, it supplements its diet with insects in the summer.

t: The fawn-coloured lark (Calendulauda africanoides) or fawn-coloured bush-lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.
f: It is found in south-central Africa.

t: The Karoo lark (Calendulauda albescens) or red-backed lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.
f: It is endemic to South Africa where its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.

t: The fawn-coloured lark (Calendulauda africanoides) or fawn-coloured bush-lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.
f: It is found in south-central Africa.
The pink-breasted lark (Calendulauda poecilosterna) or pink-breasted bushlark is a species of passerine bird in the family Alaudidae.

t: The sabota lark (Calendulauda sabota) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. It is found in southern Africa in its natural habitats of dry savannah, moist savannah, and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.
f: It is generally sedentary but local movements occur in drier regions.

t: The red-tailed vanga (Calicalicus madagascariensis) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: In 1760 the French zoologist Mathurin Jacques Brisson included a description of the red-tailed vanga in his Ornithologie based on a specimen collected in Madagascar.

The sharp-tailed sandpiper (Calidris acuminata) is a small-medium migratory wader or shorebird, found mostly in Siberia during the summer breeding period (June to August) and Australia for wintering (September to March).

t: The sanderling (Calidris alba) is a small wading bird. It is a long-distance migrant, wintering south to South America, western and southern Europe, Africa, and Australia.
f: In spring, birds migrating north from South America consume large numbers of horseshoe crab eggs in the Delaware Bay area.

t: The dunlin (Calidris alpina) is a small wader in the genus Calidris. The English name is a dialect form of "dunling", first recorded in 1531–1532.
f: It derives from dun, "dull brown", with the suffix -ling, meaning a person or thing with the given quality.

t: Baird's sandpiper (Calidris bairdii) is a small shorebird. It is among those Calidris species which were formerly sometimes included in the genus Erolia, which was subsumed into the genus Calidris in 1973.
f: It's named after Spencer Fullerton Baird, a 19th-century naturalist and Smithsonian Institution assistant secretary.

t: The red knot or just knot (Calidris canutus) is a medium-sized shorebird which breeds in tundra and the Arctic Cordillera in the far north of Canada, Europe, and Russia. It is the type species of the genus Calidris.
f: North American breeders migrate to coastal areas in Europe and South America, while the Eurasian populations winter in Africa, Papua New Guinea, Australia, and New Zealand.

t: The broad-billed sandpiper (Calidris falcinellus) is a small wader. It was formerly treated in its own monospecific genus Limicola, but this was found to be embedded within the wider genus Calidris, into which it was transferred in 2004.
f: The scientific specific name falcinellus is the diminutive from Latin falx, falcis, "a small sickle".

t: The curlew sandpiper (Calidris ferruginea) is a small wader. It is a long-distance migrant, breeding in the bogs and coastal lowlands of the Siberian Arctic, arriving there in June and staying until August or September.
f: It is a long-distance migrant, breeding in the Siberian Arctic and spending winters across Africa and Eurasia.

t: The white-rumped sandpiper (Calidris fuscicollis) is a small migratory shorebird that breeds in the northern tundra of Canada and Alaska. In flight, it is more easily picked out by its namesake white rump.
f: This bird can be difficult to distinguish from other similar tiny shorebirds; these are known collectively as "peeps" or "stints".

t: The stilt sandpiper (Calidris himantopus) is a small shorebird. The scientific name is from Ancient Greek; the genus name kalidris or skalidris is a term used by Aristotle for a gray-colored waterside bird.
f: The specific himantopus means "strap foot" or "thong foot", and also refers to the stilt.

t: The purple sandpiper (Calidris maritima) is a small shorebird in the sandpiper family Scolopacidae.
f: This is a hardy sandpiper that breeds in the arctic and subarctic regions of Eurasia and North America and winters further south on the Atlantic coast.

t: The western sandpiper (Calidris mauri) is a small migratory shorebird. The genus name is from Ancient Greek kalidris or skalidris, a term used by Aristotle for some grey-coloured waterside birds.
f: It's named after Aristotle, who used the word ‘kalidris' for grey waterside birds.

t: The pectoral sandpiper (Calidris melanotos), often abbreviated pec, is a small, migratory wader that breeds in arctic regions of North America and Asia, wintering in South America and Oceania. The pectoral sandpiper is 19–23 cm (7.5–9.1 in) long, with a wingspan of 38–46 cm (15–18 in).
f: Its nest, a hole scraped in the ground and with a thick lining, is deep enough to protect its four eggs from the cool breezes of its breeding grounds.

t: The little stint (Calidris minuta) is a very small wader. It breeds in arctic Europe and Asia, and is a long-distance migrant, wintering south to Africa and south Asia.
f: It occasionally is a vagrant to North America and to Australia.

t: The genus name is from Ancient Greek kalidris or skalidris, a term used by Aristotle for some grey-coloured waterside birds. The specific minutilla is Medieval Latin for "very small".
f: It's named after Aristotle's term for small, grey waterside birds.

t: The rock sandpiper (Calidris ptilocnemis) is a small shorebird in the sandpiper family Scolopacidae. It is closely related to the purple sandpiper that breeds in arctic regions of northeast Canada and the northwest Palearctic, and in the past was often considered conspecific with it.
f: This is a hardy sandpiper that breeds in the arctic and subarctic regions of Alaska and the Chukotka and Kamchatka Peninsulas.

t: The ruff (Calidris pugnax) is a medium-sized wading bird that breeds in marshes and wet meadows across northern Eurasia. This highly gregarious sandpiper is migratory and sometimes forms huge flocks in its winter grounds, which include southern and western Europe, Africa, southern Asia and Australia.
f: Its name, "ruff," comes from the large, ornamental collar of feathers on the male bird.

t: The semipalmated sandpiper (Calidris pusilla) is a very small shorebird. The genus name is from Ancient Greek kalidris or skalidris, a term used by Aristotle for some grey-coloured waterside birds.
f: The specific pusilla is Latin for "very small".

t: The spoon-billed sandpiper (Calidris pygmaea) is a small wader which breeds on the coasts of the Bering Sea and winters in Southeast Asia. By 2000, the estimated breeding population of the species was 350–500.
f: This species is highly threatened, and it is said that since the 1970s the breeding population has decreased significantly.

The red-necked stint or rufous-necked stint (Calidris ruficollis) is a small migratory wader that breeds in northeast Russia and spends the non-breeding season along the coastlines of Southeast Asia and Australasia.

t: The long-toed stint (Calidris subminuta) is a small wader. The genus name is from Ancient Greek kalidris or skalidris, a term used by Aristotle for some grey-coloured waterside birds.
f: Little is known of the breeding habits of this species, although it nests on the ground, and the male has a display flight.

t: The buff-breasted sandpiper (Calidris subruficollis) is a small shorebird. The species name subruficollis is from Latin subrufus, "reddish" (from sub, "somewhat", and rufus, "rufous") and collis, "-necked/-throated" (from collum, "neck").
f: It is a calidrid sandpiper, notable for its long annual migration, from the arctic region of North America to the pampas region of South America.

t: Temminck's stint (Calidris temminckii) is a small wader native to the Old World. This bird's common name and Latin binomial commemorate the Dutch naturalist Coenraad Jacob Temminck.
f: Temminck's stint is one of the species to which the Agreement on the Conservation of African-Eurasian Migratory Waterbirds (AEWA) applies.

t: The great knot (Calidris tenuirostris) is a medium-sized wader. It is one of the largest species in the genus Calidris.
f: It is a migratory bird which breeds in eastern Siberia, Russia, and flies to southern Asia and Australia in the northern winter.

t: The surfbird (Calidris virgata) is a small stocky wader in the family Scolopacidae. It was once considered to be allied to the turnstones, and placed in the monotypic genus Aphriza, but is now placed in the genus Calidris.
f: On the nesting grounds, these birds mainly eat insects and some seeds.

t: The yellow-faced honeyeater (Caligavis chrysops) is a small to medium-sized bird in the honeyeater family, Meliphagidae. It takes its common and scientific names from the distinctive yellow stripes on the sides of its head.
f: Comparatively short-billed for a honeyeater, it is thought to have adapted to a diet of flies, spiders, and beetles, as well as nectar and pollen from the flowers of plants, such as Banksia and Grevillea, and soft fruits.

t: The black-throated honeyeater (Caligavis subfrenata) is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. The black-throated honeyeater was originally described in 1876 as Lichenostomus subfrenatus, but was moved to Caligavis after a molecular phylogenetic analysis published in 2011 showed that Lichenostomus was polyphyletic.
f: Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

t: The spectacled finch (Callacanthis burtoni) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae. Its natural habitat is temperate forests with a lush landscape.
f: It is native to the Safed Koh and southern slope of the Himalayas.

t: The North Island kōkako (Callaeas wilsoni) is a forest bird endemic to the North Island of New Zealand. Adults have distinctive blue wattles, earning the species the moniker of blue-wattled crow, though they are not corvids.
f: It is grey in colour, with a small black mask.

t: The Siberian rubythroat (Calliope calliope) is a small passerine bird first described by Peter Simon Pallas in 1776. It was formerly classed as a member of the thrush family, Turdidae, but is now more generally considered to be an Old World flycatcher of the family Muscicapidae.
f: The Siberian rubythroat and similar small European species are often called chats.

t: The firethroat (Calliope pectardens) also known as David's rubythroat or Père David's orangethroat is a species of passerine bird in the family Muscicapidae, found in western and central parts of China. It breeds in Sichuan, China, and winters primarily in the Indian subcontinent.
f: Calliope, from classical Greek meaning beautiful-voiced, was one of the muses in Greek mythology.

t: The Himalayan rubythroat (Calliope pectoralis) is a species of passerine bird in the family Muscicapidae. It was also previously considered conspecific with the Chinese rubythroat, together called the white-tailed rubythroat.
f: It is closely related to the Siberian rubythroat which however lacks the distinctive white tail-tips and white tail bases.

t: The Chinese rubythroat (Calliope tschebaiewi) is a small passerine bird in the family Muscicapidae. It was also previously considered conspecific with the Himalayan rubythroat, together called the white-tailed rubythroat.
f: It is closely related to the Siberian rubythroat which however lacks the distinctive white tail-tips and white tail bases.

t: The California quail (Callipepla californica), also known as the California valley quail or Valley quail, is a small ground-dwelling bird in the New World quail family, inhabiting western North America.
f: It is the state bird of California.

t: The elegant quail (Callipepla douglasii) is a species of New World quail endemic to Pacific-slope thorn forest of north-western Mexico, from southern Sonora to Nayarit.
f: These are common, mainly ground-dwelling birds, and the IUCN has rated them as being a "species of least concern".

t: Gambel's quail (Callipepla gambelii) is a small ground-dwelling bird in the New World quail family. It inhabits the desert regions of Arizona, California, Colorado, New Mexico, Nevada, Utah, Texas, and Sonora; also New Mexico-border Chihuahua and the Colorado River region of Baja California.
f: It was named in honor of William Gambel, a 19th-century naturalist who explored the Southwestern United States.

t: The scaled quail (Callipepla squamata), also commonly called blue quail or cottontop, is a species of the New World quail family. It is a bluish gray bird found in the arid regions of the Southwestern United States to Central Mexico.
f: The nest is typically a grass-lined hollow containing 9–16 speckled eggs.

t: The gang-gang cockatoo (Callocephalon fimbriatum) is a parrot found in the cooler and wetter forests and woodlands of Australia, particularly alpine bushland. It is the only species placed in the genus Callocephalon.
f: Mostly mild grey in colour with some lighter scalloping (more pronounced and buffy in females), the male has a red head and crest, while the female has a small fluffy grey crest.
The black-throated magpie-jay (Cyanocorax colliei) is a strikingly long-tailed magpie-jay of northwestern Mexico.

t: The white-throated magpie-jay (Cyanocorax formosus) is a large Central American species of magpie-jay. Magpie-jays are noisy, gregarious birds, often traveling in easy-to-find flocks, mobbing their observers.
f: It is famous for mobbing observers, often traveling in noisy, gregarious flocks.

t: Scopoli's shearwater (Calonectris diomedea) is a seabird in the petrel family Procellariidae. It is brownish grey above with darker wings and mostly white below.
f: It breeds on rocky islands and on steep coasts in the Mediterranean but outside the breeding season it forages in the Atlantic.

t: The brown barbet (Caloramphus fuliginosus) is a species of bird in the family Megalaimidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss, and has lost approximately half of its connected habitat since 1973.

t: The lucifer sheartail or lucifer hummingbird (Calothorax lucifer) is a medium-sized, 10 cm long, green hummingbird with a slightly curved bill and distinctive outward flare of its gorget feathers.
f: Its habitat is in high-altitude areas of northern Mexico and southwestern United States.

t: Anna's hummingbird (Calypte anna) is a North American species of hummingbird named after Anna Masséna, Duchess of Rivoli. It is native to western coastal regions of North America.
f: It's named after a Duchess – Anna's Hummingbird was named after Anna Masséna, Duchess of Rivoli.

t: Costa's hummingbird (Calypte costae) is a species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae. It breeds in the arid, semi-arid and Mediterranean climate zones of the Southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico, mainly in Southern California and the Baja California Peninsula.
f: When not in the US, the species often winters in western Mexico.

t: The green broadbill (Calyptomena viridis) also known as the Asian green broadbill or the lesser green broadbill is a small bird in the family Calyptomenidae.
f: It was formerly classified in the family Eurylaimidae, a group of closely related birds that share the name "broadbill".

t: Whitehead's broadbill (Calyptomena whiteheadi) is a species of bird in the family Calyptomenidae. It is endemic to the mountain ranges of north-central Borneo, where it mainly inhabits montane forests and forest edges at elevations of 900–1,700 m (3,000–5,600 ft).
f: Breeding probably occurs from March to June, with clutches containing one or two eggs.

t: The eastern chat-tanager (Calyptophilus frugivorus) is a Near Threatened species of passerine bird belonging to the family Calyptophilidae.
f: It is endemic to the island of Hispaniola, in the Dominican Republic; it is possibly extirpated from Haiti.

t: The western chat-tanager (Calyptophilus tertius) is a Vulnerable species of passerine bird belonging to the family Calyptophilidae.
f: It is endemic to the island of Hispaniola which is shared by the Dominican Republic and Haiti.

t: The red-tailed black cockatoo (Calyptorhynchus banksii) also known as Banksian- or Banks' black cockatoo, is a large black cockatoo native to Australia. Adult males have a characteristic pair of bright red panels on the tail that gives the species its name.
f: Of the black cockatoos, the red-tailed is the most adaptable to aviculture, although black cockatoos are much rarer and much more expensive in aviculture outside Australia.

t: The yellow-tailed black cockatoo (Zanda funerea) is a large cockatoo native to the south-east of Australia measuring 55–65 cm (22–26 in) in length. It has a short crest on the top of its head.
f: They nest in large hollows high in old growth native trees (~ greater than 200 years old), generally Eucalyptus regnans.

t: The glossy black bird called the glossy black cockatoo (Calyptorhynchus lathami) is a species of bird found in Australia. Adult glossy black cockatoos may reach 50 cm (19.5 in) in length.
f: It is the smallest member of the subfamily Calyptorhynchinae, and found in eastern Australia.

t: Carnaby's black cockatoo (Zanda latirostris), also known as the short-billed black cockatoo, is a large black cockatoo endemic to southwest Australia. It was described in 1948 by naturalist Ivan Carnaby.
f: This cockatoo usually lays a clutch of one to two eggs.

t: The green-backed camaroptera (Camaroptera brachyura), also known as the bleating camaroptera, is a small bird in the family Cisticolidae. This bird is a resident breeder in Africa south of the Sahara Desert.
f: The green-backed camaroptera binds large leaves together low in a bush and builds a grass nest within the leaves.
The olive-green camaroptera (Camaroptera chloronota) is a bird species in the family Cisticolidae, mainly native to the African tropical rainforest.

t: The yellow-browed camaroptera (Camaroptera superciliaris) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is mainly native to the African tropical rainforest.
f: The specific epithet superciliaris is from the Neo-Latin superciliaris, "eyebrowed" from the classical Latin supercilium, "eyebrow".

t: The black cuckooshrike (Campephaga flava) is a species of bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae. It is also known as the African black cuckooshrike.
f: The species is closely related to Petit's cuckooshrike and the red-shouldered cuckooshrike, and forms a superspecies with them.

t: The purple-throated cuckooshrike (Campephaga quiscalina) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
The Guayaquil woodpecker (Campephilus gayaquilensis) is a woodpecker from the subfamily Picinae.

t: The pale-billed woodpecker (Campephilus guatemalensis) is a species of woodpecker of the genus Campephilus.
f: It is found from Mexico to Panama.

t: The crimson-bellied woodpecker (Campephilus haematogaster) is a species of bird in the subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Minnesota, Southern Iowa, and Peru.

t: The cream-backed woodpecker (Campephilus leucopogon) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.

t: The Magellanic woodpecker (Campephilus magellanicus) is a species of large woodpecker found in southern Chile and southwestern Argentina; it is resident within its range.
f: This species is the southernmost example of the genus Campephilus, which includes the famous ivory-billed woodpecker (C. principalis).

t: The crimson-crested woodpecker (Campephilus melanoleucos) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Panama, Trinidad, and in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The powerful woodpecker (Campephilus pollens) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The robust woodpecker (Campephilus robustus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The red-necked woodpecker (Campephilus rubricollis) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The golden-tailed woodpecker (Campethera abingoni) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. It belongs to a species complex that includes the Knysna woodpecker to the south of its range, and the mostly allopatric Mombasa woodpecker to the northeast, with which it perhaps hybridizes.
f: Its specific name commemorates the 5th Earl of Abingdon.

t: The little green woodpecker, or green-backed woodpecker (Campethera maculosa) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) has assessed it as a least-concern species.
f: It is widely distributed in tropical Africa, living in forest edges, clearings, and forest-shrub mosaics.

t: The Mombasa woodpecker (Campethera mombassica) is a species of bird in the family Picidae.
f: It is found in Kenya, Somalia, and Tanzania.

t: The Nubian woodpecker (Campethera nubica) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. It is a fairly common species with a wide range, the population seems stable, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".
f: It is distributed widely in Central and Eastern Africa, from Chad in west to Somalia in east and Tanzania in south.

t: The northern beardless tyrannulet (Camptostoma imberbe) is a small passerine bird in the tyrant flycatcher family. It breeds from southeasternmost Arizona and Texas of the United States through Mexico and Central America to northwestern Costa Rica.
f: The call is a loud whistled Fleeeeeerrr, sometimes broken up as a fleeer-it, or a flee-flee-flee-flee.

t: The southern beardless tyrannulet (Camptostoma obsoletum) is a small passerine bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, in every mainland South American country except Chile, and on Trinidad.

t: The lazuline sabrewing (Campylopterus falcatus) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Venezuela.

t: The violet sabrewing (Campylopterus hemileucurus) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of the subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found from Mexico to Panama.

t: The grey-breasted sabrewing (Campylopterus largipennis) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, the Guianas, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The black-billed scythebill (Campylorhamphus falcularius) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is native to the Atlantic Forest.

t: The curve-billed scythebill (Campylorhamphus procurvoides) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guyana, Guiana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The brown-billed scythebill (Campylorhamphus pusillus) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The red-billed scythebill (Campylorhamphus trochilirostris) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The white-headed wren (Campylorhynchus albobrunneus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Panama.

t: The cactus wren (Campylorhynchus brunneicapillus) is a species of wren that is endemic to the deserts of the southwestern United States and northern and central Mexico. Its plumage is brown, with black and white spots as markings.
f: Its song is a loud raspy chirrup, described as sounding like a car engine that won't start.

t: The giant wren (Campylorhynchus chiapensis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Mexico and Guatemala.

t: The fasciated wren (Campylorhynchus fasciatus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The bicolored wren (Campylorhynchus griseus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Venezuela, Guyana, and Brazil.
The spotted wren (Campylorhynchus gularis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
Boucard's wren (Campylorhynchus jocosus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
The gray-barred wren (Campylorhynchus megalopterus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

t: It lives in dry, riparian woodland, or farmlands, and is found at heights up to 800 m.
f: The stripe-backed wren (Campylorhynchus nuchalis) is a bird found in the savannas of northern Colombia and central Venezuela.
The Veracruz wren (Campylorhynchus rufinucha) is a songbird of the family Troglodytidae.

t: The thrush-like wren (Campylorhynchus turdinus) is a South American species of bird in the family Troglodytidae, the wrens. As suggested by its common and scientific name, its size and coloration are vaguely reminiscent of that of a thrush, although the general impression it gives in life is very different and not at all "thrush-like".
f: Despite its size, it is relatively inconspicuous, and usually revealed only by its loud, complex voice, which is highly characteristic.

t: The Yucatan wren (Campylorhynchus yucatanicus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. One of the critical habitats of this species is the Petenes mangroves ecoregion of the Yucatan coast.
f: Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry shrubland, only found on the narrow coastal strip of the northern Yucatán Peninsula.

t: The band-backed wren (Campylorhynchus zonatus) is a small songbird of the wren family. It occurs in five disjunct areas, the central region being in southern Central America, in Costa Rica and northern Panama.
f: The band-backed wren is a resident breeding species from south-central Gulf Coast Mexico to northwestern Ecuador.

t: The spruce grouse (Canachites canadensis), also known as Canada grouse, spruce hen or fool hen, is a medium-sized grouse closely associated with the coniferous boreal forests or taiga of North America. It is the only member of the genus Canachites.
f: It is one of the most arboreal grouse species, fairly well adapted to perching and moving about in trees.

t: The coyote (/kaɪ(j)oʊt(i)/, KY-(y)oh-t(ee)) (Canis latrans) is a species of canine also known as the American jackal, prairie wolf, and brush wolf. It is native to North America, and it is smaller than its close relative, the gray wolf, and slightly smaller than the closely related eastern wolf and red wolf.
f: The coyote was sighted in eastern Panama (across the Panama Canal from their home range) for the first time in 2013.

t: The wolf (Canis lupus; pl.: wolves), also known as the grey wolf or gray wolf, is a canine native to Eurasia and North America. More than thirty subspecies of Canis lupus have been recognized, including the dog and dingo, though grey wolves, as popularly understood, include only naturally occurring wild subspecies.
f: Single wolves or mated pairs typically have higher success rates in hunting than do large packs.

t: The isthmian wren (Cantorchilus elutus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The fawn-breasted wren (Cantorchilus guarayanus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The stripe-throated wren (Cantorchilus leucopogon) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama.

t: The buff-breasted wren (Cantorchilus leucotis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It occurs in non-Amazonian regions of Venezuela and Colombia and its range extends into eastern Panama.
f: It is found in the Amazon Basin of northern Brazil and Amazonian Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and northern-border Bolivia, and also the Guianan countries of Guyana, Suriname, and French Guiana.
The long-billed wren (Cantorchilus longirostris) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

t: Cabanis's wren (Cantorchilus modestus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: The bay wren (Cantorchilus nigricapillus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is native to southern Central America and northwestern South America.

t: The riverside wren (Cantorchilus semibadius) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The superciliated wren (Cantorchilus superciliaris) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The stripe-breasted wren (Cantorchilus thoracicus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and Panama.

t: The canebrake wren (Cantorchilus zeledoni) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Nicaragua, and Panama.
The gilded barbet (Capito auratus) is a species of bird in the family Capitonidae, the New World barbets, and a close relative of the toucans.

t: The scarlet-crowned barbet (Capito aurovirens) is a species of bird in the family Capitonidae, the New World barbets.
f: It is found in Amazonian Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The black-girdled barbet (Capito dayi) is a species of bird in the family Capitonidae, the New World barbets.
f: It is found in Brazil and Bolivia.

t: The white-mantled barbet (Capito hypoleucus) is a species of bird in the family Capitonidae. Its natural habitats are tropical moist montane forests, pastureland, and plantations.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The black-spotted barbet (Capito niger) is a species of bird in the family Capitonidae, the New World barbets.
f: It is found in Brazil, the Guianas, and Venezuela.

t: The five-colored barbet (Capito quinticolor) is a species of bird in the family Capitonidae, the New World barbets.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The orange-fronted barbet (Capito squamatus) is a species of bird in the family Capitonidae.
f: It is found Ecuador and Colombia.
The scarlet-banded barbet (Capito wallacei) is a species of bird in the New World barbet family, Capitonidae.

t: The savanna nightjar (Caprimulgus affinis), also known as allied nightjar or Franklin's nightjar, is a species of nightjar found in South and Southeast Asia. The IUCN Red List has assessed the species to be of least concern because it has a large range and its population trend is stable.
f: It can be distinguished from similar south Asian nightjar species, like the chirruping nightjar, by its unique vocalisations.

t: The Indian nightjar (Caprimulgus asiaticus) is a small nightjar which is a resident breeder in open lands across South Asia and Southeast Asia. They are sometimes spotted on roads when their eyes gleam red in the spotlight of a vehicle.
f: Like most nightjars it is crepuscular and is best detected from its characteristic calls at dawn and dusk that have been likened to a stone skipping on a frozen lake - a series of clicks that become shorter and more rapid.

t: Jerdon's nightjar (Caprimulgus atripennis) is a medium-sized nightjar species native to southern India and Sri Lanka. Formerly considered as a subspecies of the long-tailed nightjar, it is best recognized by its distinctive call which sounds like a wooden plank being beaten periodically with each note ending in a quaver.
f: The common name commemorates Thomas C.

t: The slender-tailed nightjar (Caprimulgus clarus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.
f: It is found in parts of eastern and central Africa, including the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: The long-tailed nightjar (Caprimulgus climacurus) is one of 98 species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae, the "true nightjars". It is found throughout mainland Africa in open areas, arid semi-deserts, and savannas, with common sightings alongside roadways.
f: It is a nocturnal, insectivorous bird characterized by its distinctive long tail.

t: The European nightjar (Caprimulgus europaeus), common goatsucker, Eurasian nightjar or just nightjar is a crepuscular and nocturnal bird in the nightjar family that breeds across most of Europe and the Palearctic to Mongolia and Northwestern China. The six subspecies differ clinally, the birds becoming smaller and paler towards the east of the range.
f: The Latin generic name refers to the old myth that the nocturnal nightjar suckled from goats, causing them to cease to give milk.

t: The square-tailed nightjar (Caprimulgus fossii) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae which is native to tropical and subtropical woodlands of the Afrotropics. Despite not having a completely "square tail", its naming highlights a distinguishing field mark.
f: It has an extensive range south of the African equator.

t: The jungle nightjar (Caprimulgus indicus) is a species of nightjar found in the Indian subcontinent. The taxonomy of this and related nightjars is complex and a range of treatments have been followed that cover this and several other nightjars in the Asian region.
f: It is found mainly on the edge of forests where it is seen or heard at dusk.

t: The grey nightjar  is a species of nightjar found in East Asia, breeding from southeastern Russia south through China, the Korean Peninsula and Japan to northern Indochina and westward along the Himalayas. It is largely migratory, wintering in Indochina south to Java in Indonesia, but is resident in warmer areas in the south of its breeding range.
f: Like all nightjars, it is crepuscular to nocturnal, feeding on flying insects, including moths, beetles, flying ants, grasshoppers, and others.
The large-tailed nightjar (Caprimulgus macrurus) is a species of nightjar known for its distinctive long, broad tail and cryptic plumage that allows it to blend into its surroundings.

t: The Madagascar nightjar or Madagascan nightjar (Caprimulgus madagascariensis) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is native to Madagascar, Nosy Boraha and Aldabra.

t: The Philippine nightjar (Caprimulgus manillensis) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. Its local names are kandarapa (Tagalog) and tagolilong (Cebuano).
f: It is endemic to the Philippines.
The swamp nightjar or Natal nightjar (Caprimulgus natalensis) is a crepuscular and nocturnal bird in the nightjar family found in Africa.

t: The fiery-necked nightjar (Caprimulgus pectoralis) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae, which is found mostly in Africa south of the equator, though it has been spotted in a few countries north of the equator. It is most often found in woodland savannas or other deciduous woodlands.
f: The fiery-necked nightjar breeds after the dry season and typically produce two clutches with two eggs per clutch.

t: The montane nightjar (Caprimulgus poliocephalus), mountain nightjar or Abyssinian nightjar, is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.
f: It is native to upland regions of Central and Eastern Africa where it is a locally common species.

t: It breeds in Iberia and North Africa, and winters in tropical West Africa.
f: The red-necked nightjar (Caprimulgus ruficollis) is the largest of the nightjars occurring in Europe.

t: The rufous-cheeked nightjar (Caprimulgus rufigena) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is an intra-African migrant that breeds in the south of its range.
f: They can hunt at night thanks to their large eyes that are adept at seeing in the dark.

t: The freckled nightjar or freckled rock nightjar (Caprimulgus tristigma) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.
f: It has a wide yet patchy distribution throughout the Afrotropics.

t: The yellow tyrannulet (Capsiempis flaveola) is a small passerine bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Panama, and in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The crested caracara (Caracara plancus) is a bird of prey (raptor) in the falcon family, Falconidae. It was formerly placed in the genus Polyborus before being given in its own genus, Caracara.
f: Documented, albeit rare, sightings have occurred as far north as Minnesota and the Canadian provinces of Alberta, Ontario, and Prince Edward Island.

t: The crested caracara (Caracara plancus) is a bird of prey (raptor) in the falcon family, Falconidae. It was formerly placed in the genus Polyborus before being given in its own genus, Caracara.
f: Documented, albeit rare, sightings have occurred as far north as Minnesota and the Canadian provinces of Alberta, Ontario, and Prince Edward Island.

t: The Canada warbler (Cardellina canadensis) is a small boreal songbird of the New World warbler family (Parulidae).
f: It summers in Canada and northeastern United States and winters in northern South America.

t: Wilson's warbler (Cardellina pusilla) is a small New World warbler. The male has a black crown patch; depending on the subspecies, that mark is reduced or absent in the female.
f: It is greenish above and yellow below, with rounded wings and a long, slim tail.

t: The red warbler (Cardellina rubra) is a small passerine bird of the New World warbler family Parulidae endemic to the highlands of Mexico, north of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec. It is closely related to, and forms a superspecies with, the pink-headed warbler of southern Mexico and Guatemala.
f: It is closely related to the pink-headed warbler, forming a superspecies with it.

t: The red-faced warbler (Cardellina rubrifrons) is a species of bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers.
f: It is found from the southwestern United States south to El Salvador and Honduras.

t: The pink-headed warbler (Cardellina versicolor) is a small passerine bird found in the southwestern highlands of Guatemala and the central and southeastern highlands of the Mexican state of Chiapas. It is a fairly common to common resident of humid to semi-humid pine-oak, pine-evergreen and evergreen forest and edge, at altitudes ranging from 1,800–3,500 m (5,900–11,500 ft) above sea level.
f: The adult is primarily red, with a silvery-pink head and chest.

t: The northern cardinal (Cardinalis cardinalis), also commonly known as the common cardinal, red cardinal, or simply cardinal, is a bird in the genus Cardinalis. It can be found in southeastern Canada, through the eastern United States from Maine to Minnesota to Texas, New Mexico, southern Arizona, southern California and south through Mexico, Belize, and Guatemala.
f: It is the state bird of Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, North Carolina, Ohio, Virginia, and West Virginia.

t: The vermilion cardinal (Cardinalis phoeniceus) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: This distinctive species with a short, stout bill, red crest, and red wings closely resembles the northern cardinal and the vermilion cardinal, which are in the same genus.
f: The pyrrhuloxia or desert cardinal (Cardinalis sinuatus) is a medium-sized North American songbird found in the American southwest and northern Mexico.

t: The common linnet or Eurasian linnet (Linaria cannabina) is a small passerine bird of the finch family, Fringillidae.
f: It derives its common name and the scientific name, Linaria, from its fondness for hemp seeds and flax seeds—flax being the English name of the plant from which linen is made.

t: The European goldfinch, or simply goldfinch (Carduelis carduelis), is a small passerine bird in the finch family that is native to the Palearctic zone in Europe, northern Africa, and western Asia. The breeding male has a red face with black markings around the eyes, and a black-and-white head.
f: It was famously depicted in Italian Renaissance paintings of the Madonna and Child.

t: The citril finch (Carduelis citrinella), also known as the Alpine citril finch, is a small songbird, a member of the true finch family, Fringillidae. Its northernmost breeding area is found in the Black Forest of southwestern Germany.
f: This bird is a resident breeder in the mountains of southwestern Europe from Spain to the Alps.

t: The Corsican finch (Carduelis corsicana), also known as the Corsican citril finch or Mediterranean citril finch, is a species of passerine bird belonging to the family Fringillidae, the "true" finches.
f: This species is endemic to Corsica and Sardinia and nearby islands in France and Italy.

t: The red-legged seriema is widely distributed in South America, occurring in central and eastern Brazil through eastern Bolivia and Paraguay to Uruguay and central Argentina (south to La Pampa).
f: Like the black-legged seriema, farmers often use them as guard animals to protect poultry from predators and sometimes human intruders.

t: The Bornean ground cuckoo (Carpococcyx radiceus) is a large, terrestrial species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. As suggested by its common name, it is endemic to the island of Borneo, being found in the sections belonging to Brunei, Malaysia, and Indonesia.
f: It is restricted to humid forest.

The coral-billed ground cuckoo (Carpococcyx renauldi), also known as Renauld's ground cuckoo, is a large, terrestrial species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae, found in Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The Chinese white-browed rosefinch (Carpodacus dubius) is a true finch species (family Fringillidae). Its natural habitats are temperate forests and temperate shrubland.
f: It is found in central China and eastern Tibet.
The common rosefinch (Carpodacus erythrinus) or scarlet rosefinch is the most widespread and common rosefinch of Asia and Europe.

t: The red-fronted rosefinch (Carpodacus Puniceus) is a species of rosefinch in the finch family Fringillidae. It is sometimes placed in the monotypic genus Pyrrhospiza. found in Afghanistan, Bhutan, China, India, Kazakhstan, Nepal, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan.
f: Its natural habitat is montane tundra.

t: The pink-browed rosefinch (Carpodacus rodochroa) is a finch in the family Fringillidae. Nicholas Aylward Vigors first described the species in 1831.
f: It is migratory and ranges across the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent, mainly in the Himalayas.

t: The great rosefinch (Carpodacus rubicilla) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae. Its natural habitats are tundra and temperate grassland.
f: It is found in Afghanistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, India, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan and east to China.

t: The streaked rosefinch (Carpodacus rubicilloides) is a true finch species (family Fringillidae). Its natural habitat is boreal shrubland.
f: It is found on the Himalayan Plateau.

t: The Siberian long-tailed rosefinch (Carpodacus sibiricus) is a species of finch of the family Fringillidae. It is found in Japan, Kazakhstan, North Korea, South Korea, and Russia.
f: It is a very rare vagrant to Europe, but like several related Asiatic rosefinches, is reasonably frequent in the cage bird trade, so many records have been considered to relate to escapes.

t: The Sinai rosefinch (Carpodacus synoicus) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae. The male has a pink face and breast with a whitish forehead and crown and the female is pale gray-brown overall with a whitish belly.
f: It is the national bird of Jordan.

t: The Himalayan white-browed rosefinch (Carpodacus thura) is a true finch species (family Fringillidae). Its natural habitats are temperate forests and temperate shrubland.
f: Rages across the Himalayas, being found from Afghanistan in the west, eastwards across India to Tibet, Bhutan and Nepal.
The hooded berryeater (Carpornis cucullata) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.
The black-headed berryeater (Carpornis melanocephala) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.

t: The pale rockfinch or pale rock sparrow (Carpospiza brachydactyla) is a small sparrow found in the Middle East and Central Asia. It is the only member of the genus Carpospiza.
f: The range of pale rockfinch extends from eastern Turkey to Afghanistan, and south into the Arabian Peninsula and northern Africa as far as Ethiopia.

t: The golden monarch (Carterornis chrysomela) is a species of passerine bird in the family Monarchidae found in New Guinea. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: The golden monarch displays marked sexual dimorphism, the male a striking golden colour with black mask, wings and tail, the female a golden or golden-olive colour.

t: The white-eared monarch (Carterornis leucotis), or white-eared flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is endemic to north-eastern Australia.

t: The white-naped monarch (Carterornis pileatus) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is endemic to Indonesia, where it occurs in the Maluku Islands.

t: The yellow-green grosbeak (Caryothraustes canadensis) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals, grosbeaks, and “tanager” allies.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Suriname, and Venezuela.
The black-faced grosbeak (Caryothraustes poliogaster) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals, grosbeaks, and “tanager” allies. it is found from Mexico to Panama.

t: The rufous casiornis (Casiornis rufus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, and as a vagrant to Chile.

t: The Mexican cacique or yellow-winged cacique (Cassiculus melanicterus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in El Salvador,Guatemala and Mexico.

t: The southern cassowary (Casuarius casuarius), also known as double-wattled cassowary, Australian cassowary, or two-wattled cassowary, is a large, flightless, mostly black bird, found in Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, and northeastern Australia. It is one of the three living species of cassowary, alongside the dwarf cassowary and the northern cassowary.
f: Southern cassowaries are among the largest birds in the world, only weighing less than ostriches.

t: The plushcap (Catamblyrhynchus diadema) is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae and it is the only member of the genus Catamblyrhynchus. The plushcap was in its own family until recently when it was grouped with the tanagers.
f: The plushcap is one of the most distinctive of all Neotropical passerines in both its appearance and behavior.

t: The band-tailed seedeater (Catamenia analis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
The paramo seedeater (Catamenia homochroa) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.

t: The plain-colored seedeater (Catamenia inornata) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, and subtropical or tropical high-altitude grassland.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The turkey vulture (Cathartes aura) is the most widespread of the New World vultures. One of three species in the genus Cathartes of the family Cathartidae, the turkey vulture ranges from southern Canada to the southernmost tip of South America.
f: Lacking a syrinx—the vocal organ of birds—its only vocalizations are grunts or low hisses.

t: The lesser yellow-headed vulture (Cathartes burrovianus), also known as the savannah vulture, is a species of bird in the New World vulture family Cathartidae. It was considered to be the same species as the greater yellow-headed vulture until they were split in 1964.
f: It lays its eggs on flat surfaces, such as the floors of caves, or in the hollows of stumps.

t: The orange-billed nightingale-thrush (Catharus aurantiirostris) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies. It is found from northern Mexico through Central America (except Belize) into northern South America.
f: In addition it has been documented in Brazil and as a vagrant to the United States.

t: Bicknell's thrush (Catharus bicknelli) is a medium-sized thrush, at 17.5 cm (6.9 in) and 28 g (0.99 oz). One of North America's rarest and most localized songbirds, it breeds on coniferous mountain tops and disturbed habitats of northeastern North America.
f: It was named after Eugene Bicknell, an American amateur ornithologist, who made the first scientific discovery of the species on Slide Mountain in the Catskills in the late 19th century.

t: The yellow-throated nightingale-thrush or Gould's nightingale-thrush (Catharus dryas) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies.
f: It is found from Mexico to Nicaragua.

t: The ruddy-capped nightingale-thrush (Catharus frantzii) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies.
f: It is found from Mexico to Panama.

t: The slaty-backed nightingale-thrush (Catharus fuscater) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: Alternate names for this species include Wilson's thrush (named so after Alexander Wilson) and tawny thrush. Up to six subspecies exist, which are grouped into the eastern veery (C. fuscescens fuscescens), the western veery or willow thrush (C. fuscescens salicicolus), and the Newfoundland veery (C. fuscescens fuliginosus).
f: The English name may imitate the call.

t: The black-billed nightingale-thrush (Catharus gracilirostris) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.
The hermit thrush (Catharus guttatus) is a medium-sized North American thrush.
