t: The speckled nightingale-thrush or Sclater's nightingale-thrush (Catharus maculatus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies.
f: It is found from Colombia and Venezuela to Bolivia.

t: The black-headed nightingale-thrush (Catharus mexicanus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies. It is found in Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, and Panama.
f: It has also been recorded as a vagrant in Texas.

t: The gray-cheeked thrush (Catharus minimus) is a medium-sized thrush. This species is 15–17 cm (5.9–6.7 in) in length, and has the white-dark-white underwing pattern characteristic of Catharus thrushes.
f: The gray-cheeked thrush is all but indistinguishable from Bicknell's thrush except by its slightly larger size and different song.
The russet nightingale-thrush (Catharus occidentalis) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies.

t: Swainson's thrush (Catharus ustulatus), also called olive-backed thrush, russet-backed thrush, and salmonberry bird is a medium-sized thrush. It is a member of genus Catharus and is typical of it in terms of its subdued coloration and beautiful, ascending flute-like voice.
f: Swainson's thrush was named after William Swainson, an English ornithologist.

t: The canyon wren (Catherpes mexicanus) is a small North American songbird of the wren family Troglodytidae. A non-migratory species, these birds are found throughout western North America in dry, rocky environments such as cliffs, outcrops, and canyons.
f: It is a small bird that is hard to see on its rocky habitat, and is often located by its loud distinctive song.

t: The cheer pheasant (Catreus wallichii), also known as Wallich's pheasant and chir pheasant, is a vulnerable species of the pheasant family, Phasianidae. It is the only member in the genus Catreus.
f: The scientific name commemorates Danish botanist Nathaniel Wallich.

t: The lesser striped swallow (Cecropis abyssinica) is a large swallow. It breeds in Sub-Saharan Africa from Sierra Leone and southern Sudan south into eastern South Africa.
f: It is partially migratory with South African birds wintering further north.
The greater striped swallow (Cecropis cucullata) is a large swallow that is native to Africa south of the equator.

t: The red-breasted swallow (Cecropis semirufa), also known as the rufous-chested swallow, is a member of the family Hirundinidae, found in Sub-Saharan Africa.
f: It is confined to the tropical rainforest during the wet season.

t: The eastern red-rumped swallow (Cecropis daurica) is a small passerine bird in the swallow family Hirundinidae. The European red-rumped swallow and the African red-rumped swallow were formerly considered as subspecies of the eastern red-rumped swallow.
f: It is found in open, often hilly, areas with clearings and cultivation across eastern and southeastern Asia to north-eastern India and Taiwan.

t: The chestnut-colored woodpecker (Celeus castaneus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Belize, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The chestnut woodpecker (Celeus elegans) a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found on Trinidad and in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The blond-crested woodpecker (Celeus flavescens) is a species of bird in the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The cream-colored woodpecker (Celeus flavus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in most mainland South American countries except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The helmeted woodpecker (Celeus galeatus) is a Vulnerable species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The scaly-breasted woodpecker (Celeus undatus grammicus), also known as the scale-breasted woodpecker, is a subspecies complex of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The cinnamon woodpecker (Celeus loricatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The pale-crested woodpecker (Celeus lugubris) a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.
Kaempfer's woodpecker (Celeus obrieni), also known as the Piauí woodpecker and previously as the caatinga woodpecker, is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
The ochre-backed woodpecker (Celeus ochraceus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.

t: The rufous-headed woodpecker (Celeus spectabilis) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The ringed woodpecker (Celeus torquatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The waved woodpecker (Celeus undatus) or variable woodpecker is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The greater sage-grouse (Centrocercus urophasianus), also known as the sagehen, is the largest grouse in North America. Its range is sagebrush country in the western United States and southern Alberta and Saskatchewan, Canada.
f: Greater sage-grouse do not have a muscular crop and are not able to digest hard seeds like other grouse.

t: Baird's sparrow (Centronyx bairdii) is a species of North American birds in the family Passerellidae of order Passeriformes.
f: It is a migratory bird native to the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

t: Henslow's sparrow (Centronyx henslowii) is a North American passerine bird in the family Passerellidae. It was originally classified in the genus Emberiza and called Henslow's bunting.
f: It was named by John James Audubon in honor of John Stevens Henslow.

t: The Andaman coucal or brown coucal (Centropus andamanensis) is a species of non-parasitic cuckoo found in the Andamans, Coco and Table Islands. It is sometimes treated as a subspecies of the greater coucal.
f: It is found mainly in forested habitats and thickly covered gardens.

t: The lesser coucal (Centropus bengalensis) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It has a wide distribution range that overlaps with several other similar species.
f: It is distinguished by its smaller size, less prominent bill, pale shaft streaks on the feathers of the head and back.

t: The bay coucal (Centropus celebensis) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

t: The green-billed coucal (Centropus chlororhynchos) is a member of the cuckoos. It is endemic to Sri Lanka's wet zone and listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List, as the small population declined due to forest destruction and fragmentation.
f: Its typical clutch is 2–3 eggs.

t: The black-throated coucal (Centropus leucogaster) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. The subspecies found in northern and central Zaire is sometimes split as Neumann's coucal (Centropus neumanni).
f: It is found in West Africa in dense second growth along forest edge and grassy swamps.

t: The black-faced coucal (Centropus melanops) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It is a striking coucal with its cream head contrasted with a black mask and tail and chestnut wings.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines found in the islands of Mindanao, Basilan Dinagat Islands Bohol, Leyte, Biliran and Samar.

t: The ivory-billed coucal or greater black coucal (Centropus menbeki) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is found in the Aru Islands and New Guinea.

t: The buff-headed coucal (Centropus milo) is a species of coucal. These are often placed in the cuckoo family (Cuculidae) but seem to warrant recognition as a distinct family.
f: C. milo is a common endemic of the central islands of the Solomon Islands.

t: The blue-headed coucal (Centropus monachus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It is a common bird with a wide range, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".
f: It is native to tropical central Africa where its typical habitat is swamps, river banks, forest edges and generally wet locations.

t: The pheasant coucal (Centropus phasianinus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It is found in Australia, Timor and New Guinea.
f: The pheasant coucal is unusual among Australian cuckoos in that it incubates and raises its own young instead of laying its eggs in the nest of another species.

t: The short-toed coucal (Centropus rectunguis) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: It is a medium-sized member of its genus and is found in lightly-wooded country and savannah in central and southern Africa.
f: The Senegal coucal (Centropus senegalensis) is a member of the cuckoo order of birds, the Cuculiformes, which also includes the roadrunners and the anis.

t: The greater coucal or crow pheasant (Centropus sinensis), is a large non-parasitic member of the cuckoo order of birds, the Cuculiformes. A widespread resident in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, it is divided into several subspecies, some being treated as full species.
f: They are weak fliers, and are often seen clambering about in vegetation or walking on the ground as they forage for insects, eggs and nestlings of other birds.

t: The white-browed coucal or lark-heeled cuckoo (Centropus superciliosus), is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It inhabits areas with thick cover afforded by rank undergrowth and scrub, including in suitable coastal regions.
f: It is found in sub-Saharan Africa.

t: The Malagasy coucal or Madagascar coucal (Centropus toulou) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It is found in Madagascar and in the Seychelles, where it occurs on Aldabra and was formerly present on Assumption Island and Cosmoledo.
f: Its natural habitats are dense vegetation in subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, mangrove forests, rough grassland, marshes and reedbeds.

t: The Philippine coucal (Centropus viridis) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines.

t: The long-wattled umbrellabird (Cephalopterus penduliger) is an umbrellabird in the Cotingidae family. The long-wattled umbrellabird is considered rare and it resides in humid to wet premontane and cloud forest.
f: Its Spanish names include pájaro bolsón, pájaro toro, dungali, and vaca del monte.

t: The pigeon guillemot (Cepphus columba) () is a species of bird in the auk family, Alcidae. One of three species in the genus Cepphus, it is most closely related to the spectacled guillemot.
f: Both parents incubate the eggs and feed the chicks.

t: The black guillemot or tystie (Cepphus grylle) is a medium-sized seabird of the Alcidae family, native throughout northern Atlantic coasts and eastern North American coasts. It is resident in much of its range, but large populations from the high arctic migrate southwards in winter.
f: The bird can be seen in and around its breeding habitat of rocky shores, cliffs and islands in single or smalls groups of pairs.

t: The black-casqued hornbill (Ceratogymna atrata), or black-casqued wattled hornbill, is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is found fairly commonly across sub-Saharan Africa, being known from Sierra Leone and Liberia in Western Africa , south to Angola and east to the Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Uganda.
f: They are currently considered of near threatened, and their population is declining.

t: The round-tailed manakin (Ceratopipra chloromeros) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The scarlet-horned manakin (Ceratopipra cornuta) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Guyana, and Venezuela.

t: The golden-headed manakin (Ceratopipra erythrocephala) is a small passerine bird which breeds in tropical Central and South America in both wet and dry forests, secondary growth and plantations. It is a small manakin, about 9.4 centimetres (3.7 in) long.
f: At breeding time, males are involved in a cooperative lekking behaviour during which they jump, slide and dart from perch to perch.

t: The red-capped manakin (Ceratopipra mentalis) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is found in Belize, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Peru and Panama.

t: The red-headed manakin (Ceratopipra rubrocapilla) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.
The sharp-tailed ibis (Cercibis oxycerca) is a species of ibis native to open wet savannas in parts of northern South America.

t: The dusky long-tailed cuckoo (Cercococcyx mechowi) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. The IUCN has assessed it as a least-concern species.
f: It is found in forests in Central Africa.

t: The barred long-tailed cuckoo (Cercococcyx montanus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae.
f: It is found in the Albertine Rift montane forests and disjunctly throughout East Africa.

t: The olive long-tailed cuckoo (Cercococcyx olivinus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It is found throughout the African tropical rainforest.
f: It lays its nests on the ground, and forages from the canopy of trees.
The Rio de Janeiro antbird (Cercomacra brasiliana) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The Rio Branco antbird (Cercomacra carbonaria) is a Vulnerable bird species in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil and Guyana.

t: The grey antbird (Cercomacra cinerascens) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The Bananal antbird (Cercomacra ferdinandi) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is endemic to central Brazil.

t: The Manu antbird (Cercomacra manu) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, Bolivia, and Peru.

t: The Mato Grosso antbird (Cercomacra melanaria) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The jet antbird (Cercomacra nigricans) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, and Venezuela.

t: The riparian antbird (Cercomacroides fuscicauda) is a species of passerine bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: Willis's antbird (Cercomacroides laeta), also known as the laeta antbird, is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil and Guyana.

t: The blackish antbird (Cercomacroides nigrescens) is a species of passerine bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, and Suriname.
Parker's antbird (Cercomacroides parkeri) is a species of passerine bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The black antbird (Cercomacroides serva) is a species of passerine bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The dusky antbird or tyrannine antbird (Cercomacroides tyrannina) is a passerine bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found from Mexico south through Central America and in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The miombo scrub robin (Tychaedon barbata) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. This species was formerly placed in the genus Cercotrichas.
f: It is found in Angola, Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Malawi, Mozambique, Tanzania, and Zambia.

t: The Karoo scrub robin (Tychaedon coryphoeus) or Karoo robin is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitats are dry shrubland and Mediterranean-type shrubby vegetation.
f: It is found in Lesotho, Namibia, and South Africa.

t: The rufous-tailed scrub robin (Cercotrichas galactotes) is a medium-sized member of the family Muscicapidae. Other common names include the rufous scrub robin, rufous bush chat, rufous bush robin and the rufous warbler.
f: Their clear thrush-like song has a sad tone.

t: The brown-backed scrub robin (Cercotrichas hartlaubi) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitat is moist savanna.
f: It is found in Angola, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: The white-browed scrub robin (Cercotrichas leucophrys), also known as the red-backed scrub-robin, is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is native to sub-Saharan Africa, especially East and southern Africa.
f: Within range, its Turdus-like song is one of the often-heard sounds of the bush.

t: The Kalahari scrub robin (Cercotrichas paena) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae.
f: It is sometimes known as the sandy scrub robin.

t: The black scrub robin (Cercotrichas podobe) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitat is dry savanna.
f: It is native to the Sahel and montane Arabian Peninsula.

t: The bearded scrub robin (Tychaedon quadrivirgata), also known as the eastern bearded scrub robin, is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. This species was formerly placed in the genus Cercotrichas.
f: It is found in eastern and southern Africa.

t: The brown scrub robin (Tychaedon signata) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical dry or moist forests.
f: It is found in Eswatini, Mozambique and, South Africa.

t: The rhinoceros auklet (Cerorhinca monocerata) is a seabird and a close relative of the puffins. It is the only extant species of the genus Cerorhinca.
f: It possesses fluorescent properties, likely involved in reproductive signalling within the rhino auklet.
The brown creeper (Certhia americana), also known as the American treecreeper, is a small songbird, the only North American member of the treecreeper family Certhiidae.

t: The short-toed treecreeper (Certhia brachydactyla) is a small passerine bird found in woodlands through much of the warmer regions of Europe and into north Africa. It has a generally more southerly distribution than the other European treecreeper species, the common treecreeper, with which it is easily confused where they both occur.
f: This common, unwary, but inconspicuous species feeds mainly on insects which are picked from the tree trunk as the treecreeper ascends with short hops.

t: The Sikkim treecreeper (Certhia discolor) is a species of bird in the treecreeper family. It is found in Bhutan, Nepal and Northeast India.
f: The form C. d. manipurensis of southern Manipur and southwestern Burma has a rich cinnamon throat and breast, and molecular evidence and is usually now treated as a separate species, the Hume's treecreeper, C. manipurensis Hume, 1850.

t: The Eurasian treecreeper or common treecreeper (Certhia familiaris) is a small passerine bird also known in the British Isles, where it is the only living member of its genus, simply as treecreeper. It is similar to other treecreepers, and has a curved bill, patterned brown upperparts, whitish underparts, and long stiff tail feathers which help it creep up tree trunks.
f: It can be most easily distinguished from the similar short-toed treecreeper, which shares much of its European range, by its different song.

t: The bar-tailed treecreeper (Certhia himalayana), or the Himalayan treecreeper, is a species of bird in the family Certhiidae. It is found in Afghanistan, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Myanmar, Nepal, Tibet, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan.
f: It is found primarily in the northern parts of the Indian subcontinent, particularly in the Himalayas, as well as in adjoining regions.

t: Hodgson's treecreeper (Certhia hodgsoni) is a small passerine bird from the southern rim of the Himalayas.
f: Its specific distinctness from the common treecreeper (C. familiaris) was recently validated.

t: Hume's treecreeper (Certhia manipurensis) was earlier included within the brown-throated treecreeper complex and identified as a separate species on the basis of their distinctive calls. This species in the treecreeper family is found in Assam, Myanmar, Shan Mountains, Northern Thailand, Laos and the Dalat Plateau.
f: The name commemorates the British naturalist Allan Octavian Hume who worked in India.

t: The spot-throated woodcreeper (Certhiasomus stictolaemus) is a species of bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Venezuela, and possibly Suriname.

t: It is a member of the South American ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: The yellow-chinned spinetail (Certhiaxis cinnamomeus) is a passerine bird found in the tropical New World from Trinidad and Colombia south to Argentina and Uruguay.

t: The red-and-white spinetail (Certhiaxis mustelinus) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, and Peru.

t: The short-clawed lark (Certhilauda chuana) or short-clawed bush-lark, is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. Its natural habitat is dry savannah.
f: It is found in Botswana and South Africa.

t: The eastern long-billed lark (Certhilauda semitorquata), also known as the Kaffrarian long-billed lark or Eastern longbill, is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry lowland grassland.
f: It is found in south-eastern Africa.

t: The Karoo long-billed lark (Certhilauda subcoronata) or Karoo longbill is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae.
f: It is found in southern Africa in its natural habitat of subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.

t: The pied honeyeater (Certhionyx variegatus) is a species of bird in the family of honeyeaters Meliphagidae and the sole species in the genus Certhionyx (Christidis & Boles 2008). This species is also known as the black and white honeyeater or western pied honeyeater.
f: It is endemic to Australia and is listed as a vulnerable species under Schedule 2 of the Threatened Species Conservation Act 1995 (NSW).

t: The pied kingfisher (Ceryle rudis) is a species of water kingfisher widely distributed across Africa and Asia. Originally described by Carl Linnaeus in 1758, it has five recognised subspecies, and is the only member of the genus Ceryle.
f: Males have a double band across the breast, while females have a single broken breast band.

t: The grey-sided bush warbler (Cettia brunnifrons) is a species of bush warbler (family Cettiidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
f: It is found from northern Pakistan to central China.
The chestnut-headed tesia (Cettia castaneocoronata) is a small insectivorous songbird formerly of the "Old World warbler" family but nowadays placed in the bush warbler family (Cettiidae).

t: Cetti's warbler (Cettia cetti) is a small, brown warbler in the family Cettiidae, which breeds in southern and western Europe, northwest Africa and the east Palearctic as far as Afghanistan and northwest Pakistan. This species is often difficult to see because of its skulking habits.
f: The bird is named after the 18th-century Italian zoologist, Francesco Cetti.

t: The chestnut-crowned bush warbler (Cettia major) is a species of warbler found in South Asia. Although its population trend is observed to be decreasing, its decline is not happening in rapid fashion.
f: Although overall population size has not been quantified, this is one of the species that is declining due to habitat destruction.

t: The blue malkoha or chattering yellowbill (Ceuthmochares aereus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It was formerly conspecific with the green malkoha until split in 2016.
f: It is widely distributed across the African tropical rainforest.

t: The green malkoha or whistling yellowbill (Ceuthmochares australis) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. This species and the blue malkoha were previously considered conspecific and together known as the yellowbill.
f: Unlike some other cuckoos the green malkoha is not a brood parasite, instead it cares for its own young.
The azure kingfisher (Ceyx azureus) is a small kingfisher in the river kingfisher subfamily, Alcedininae.

t: The black-backed dwarf kingfisher (Ceyx erithaca), also known as the three-toed kingfisher, is a pocket-sized bird in the family Alcedinidae. It was formerly considered as conspecific with the rufous-backed dwarf kingfisher and together the species complex was known by the English name "oriental dwarf kingfisher".
f: It resides in lowland forests, typically near streams or ponds, where it feeds upon insects, spiders, worms, crabs, fish, frogs, and lizards.

t: The white-bellied woodstar (Chaetocercus mulsant) is a species of hummingbird in tribe Mellisugini of subfamily Trochilinae, the "bee hummingbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
The Cape rockjumper or rufous rockjumper (Chaetops frenatus) is a medium-sized insectivorous passerine bird endemic to the mountain Fynbos of southernmost South Africa.
The short-tailed swift (Chaetura brachyura) is a bird in the Apodidae, or swift family.

t: Chapman's swift (Chaetura chapmani) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Peru, Suriname, Trinidad, Venezuela, and possibly Ecuador.

t: The grey-rumped swift or gray-rumped swift (Chaetura cinereiventris) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae.
f: It is found in Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and Panama; in every mainland South American country except Chile, French Guiana, Suriname, and Uruguay; in Trinidad and Tobago; and on Grenada.

t: Sick's swift (Chaetura meridionalis) is a species of swift in the family Apodidae. The English name commemorates the German-born ornithologist Helmut Sick who studied South American birds.
f: It was previously considered conspecific with the smaller ashy-tailed swift, but a study published in 1997 found that Sick's swift was closer to the chimney swift.

t: The chimney swift (Chaetura pelagica) is a bird belonging to the swift family Apodidae. A member of the genus Chaetura, it is closely related to both Vaux's swift and Chapman's swift; in the past, the three were sometimes considered to be conspecific.
f: Like all swifts, it is incapable of perching on flat surfaces, and can only perch on vertical surfaces.

t: The band-rumped swift (Chaetura spinicaudus) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae.
f: It is found from Panama south through Colombia into Ecuador, east from Venezuela into the Guianas and Brazil, and on Trinidad.

t: Vaux's swift (Chaetura vauxi) is a small swift native to North America, Central America, and northern South America.
f: It was named for the American scientist William Sansom Vaux.

t: The amethyst sunbird, also called the black sunbird (Chalcomitra amethystina), is a species of passerine bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is native to the Afrotropics, mostly south of the equator.
f: They are commonly found in well-watered habitats, and undertake seasonal movements to visit flowering woodlands.

t: The scarlet-chested sunbird (Chalcomitra senegalensis) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae.
f: It is found in many areas of Sub-Saharan Africa, and from South Sudan to South Africa.
The ruby-cheeked sunbird (Chalcoparia singalensis) is a species of sunbird in the family Nectariniidae.

t: The emerald dove or common emerald dove (Chalcophaps indica), also called Asian emerald dove and grey-capped emerald dove, is a widespread resident breeding pigeon native to the tropical and subtropical parts of the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. The dove is also known by the names of green dove and green-winged pigeon.
f: The common emerald dove is the state bird of the Indian state of Tamil Nadu.

t: It was formerly conspecific with the common emerald dove.
f: The Pacific emerald dove or brown-capped emerald dove (Chalcophaps longirostris) is a pigeon which is a widespread resident breeding bird in the tropical and sub-tropical parts of Indonesia, northern and eastern Australia, Timor-Leste, and Papua New Guinea.

t: Stephan's emerald dove, also known as Stephan's dove (Chalcophaps stephani), is a species of bird in the pigeon family Columbidae. Formally described by the French zoologist Jacques Pucheran in 1853, the dove is named after Étienne Jacquinot, the father of the French naturalist Honoré Jacquinot.
f: Stephan's emerald doves migrate locally in response to local climactic conditions and food availability.

t: The white-vented plumeleteer (Chalybura buffonii) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The bronze-tailed plumeleteer (Chalybura urochrysia) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The wrentit (Chamaea fasciata) is a small bird that lives in chaparral, oak woodlands, and bushland on the western coast of North America, from Oregon south through California to northern Baja California. It is the only species in the genus Chamaea.
f: Its common name reflects the uncertainty, and its external resemblance to both tits and wrens.

t: The sickle-winged guan (Chamaepetes goudotii) is a species of bird in the chachalaca, guan, and curassow family Cracidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The black guan (Chamaepetes unicolor) is a species of bird in the chachalaca, guan, and curassow family Cracidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The white-chested alethe (Chamaetylas fuelleborni) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in Malawi, Mozambique, Tanzania, and Zambia.

t: The brown-chested alethe (Chamaetylas poliocephala) is a species of bird in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It has a discontinuous range of presence across the African tropical rainforest.

t: The short-tailed antthrush (Chamaeza campanisona) is a species of bird in the family Formicariidae.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile, French Guiana, and Uruguay.

t: The cryptic antthrush (Chamaeza meruloides), also known as Such's antthrush, is a species of bird in the family Formicariidae.
f: It is endemic to the Atlantic Forest in southeastern Brazil.

t: The barred antthrush (Chamaeza mollissima) is a species of bird in the family Formicariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru.

t: The striated antthrush (Chamaeza nobilis), sometimes called the noble antthrush, is a species of bird in the family Formicariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The rufous-tailed antthrush or Brazilian antthrush (Chamaeza ruficauda) is a species of bird in the family Formicariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Brazil.

t: Schwartz's antthrush (Chamaeza turdina), also known as the scalloped antthrush, is a species of bird in the family Formicariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The Kentish plover (Anarhynchus alexandrinus) is a small wader (40–44 g (1.4–1.6 oz)) of the family Charadriidae that breeds on the shores of saline lakes, lagoons, and coasts, populating sand dunes, marshes, semi-arid desert, and tundra. Some populations are migratory and often winter in Africa, whereas other populations, such as various island populations, do not migrate.
f: Its common English name comes from the county of Kent, where it was once found, but it has not bred in Britain since 1979.

t: The double-banded plover (Anarhynchus bicinctus), known as the banded dotterel or pohowera in New Zealand, is a species of bird in the plover family.
f: Two subspecies are recognised: the nominate Anarhynchus bicinctus bicinctus, which breeds throughout New Zealand, including the Chatham Islands, and A. b. exilis, which breeds in New Zealand's subantarctic Auckland Islands.

t: The collared plover (Anarhynchus collaris) is a small shorebird in the plover family, Charadriidae. It lives along coasts and riverbanks of the tropical to temperate Americas, from central Mexico south to Chile and Argentina.
f: Like many ground-nesting species, adults perform a broken-wing display to lure presumed threats away from their nest and young.

t: The little ringed plover (Thinornis dubius) is a small plover native to the Old World. It has mostly brown upperparts, a black neckband and a black mask around the eye with a noticeable yellow eyering.
f: Its diet consists mainly of insects and worms, which it forages for in muddy areas.

t: The two-banded plover (Anarhynchus falklandicus) is a species of bird in subfamily Charadriinae of family Charadriidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, the Falkland Islands, and Uruguay.

t: The common ringed plover, great ringed plover or ringed plover (Charadrius hiaticula) is a species of bird in the family Charadriidae.
f: It breeds across much of northern Eurasia, as well as Greenland.

t: The Javan plover (Anarhynchus javanicus) is a Charadriidae species with an unclear taxonomic status. Endemic to Indonesia and Timor-Leste, it inhabits sandy shores and intertidal mudflats, where it is thought to breed year-round.
f: Its diet mainly consists of crustaceans, worms, and mollusks.

t: The greater sand plover (Anarhynchus leschenaultii) is a small wader in the plover family of birds. The specific leschenaultii commemorates the French botanist Jean Baptiste Leschenault de la Tour.
f: The spelling is often given as "greater sandplover" or "greater sand-plover", but the official IOC and British Ornithologists' Union spelling is "Greater Sand Plover".

t: The piping plover (Charadrius melodus) is a small, sand-colored shorebird that nests and feeds along coastal sand and gravel beaches in North America. The adult has yellow-orange-red legs, a black band across the forehead from eye to eye, and a black stripe running along the breast line.
f: Its name, derived from its plaintive bell-like whistles, is often heard before the bird is visible.

t: The rufous-chested dotterel (Zonibyx modestus) or rufous-chested plover, is a species of bird in subfamily Charadriinae of family Charadriidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Uruguay, and the Falkland Islands.

t: The Siberian sand plover (Anarhynchus mongolus) is a small wader in the plover family of birds. The International Ornithologists' Union split the Tibetan sand plover from the lesser sand plover and changed its vernacular name to Siberian sand plover.
f: The specific mongolus is Latin and refers to Mongolia, which at the time of naming referred to a larger area than the present country.

t: The mountain plover (Anarhynchus montanus) is a medium-sized ground bird in the plover family (Charadriidae). Unlike most plovers, it is usually not found near bodies of water or even on wet soil; it prefers dry habitat with short grass (usually due to grazing) and bare ground.
f: It is misnamed, as it lives on level land.

t: The Eurasian dotterel (Eudromias morinellus), also known in Europe as just dotterel, is a small wader in the plover family of birds. It is the only species placed in the genus Eudromias.
f: The Eurasian dotterel is a migratory species, breeding in Northern Europe and Eurosiberia and migrating south to North Africa and the Middle East in the winter.

t: The snowy plover (Anarhynchus nivosus, formerly Charadrius nivosus) is a small shorebird found in the Americas. It is a member of the bird family Charadriidae, which includes the plovers, dotterels, and lapwings.
f: Snowy plovers can also be distinguished from other plovers in having an all-black and slender bill, and gray to black legs.

t: The Malaysian plover or Malay plover (Anarhynchus peronii, syn.
f: Charadrius peronii) is a small (c. 35–42 g) wader that nests on beaches and salt flats in Southeast Asia.

t: The long-billed plover (Thinornis placidus) is a species of wading bird in the family Charadriidae. The long-billed plover is a migratory bird, so it breeds and spends the winter in different parts of its range.
f: It can be found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brunei, Cambodia, China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Japan, Laos, Malaysia, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, North Korea, Russia, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The semipalmated plover (Charadrius semipalmatus) is a small plover. Charadrius is a Late Latin word for a yellowish bird mentioned in the fourth-century Vulgate.
f: It's named semipalmatus because its partially webbed feet resemble a half-palm.

t: The three-banded plover, or three-banded sandplover (Charadrius tricollaris, syn.: Thinornis tricollaris), is a small wader. This plover is resident and generally sedentary in much of East Africa, southern Africa and Madagascar.
f: This species is often seen as single individuals, but it will form small flocks.

t: The oriental plover (Anarhynchus veredus), also known as the oriental dotterel, is a medium-sized plover closely related to the Caspian plover.
f: It breeds in parts of Mongolia and China, migrating southwards each year to spend its non-breeding season in Indonesia, New Guinea and northern Australia.

t: The killdeer (Charadrius vociferus) is a large plover found in the Americas. Its shrill, two-syllable call is often heard, sounding like "kill deer".
f: Its multiple responses to predation range from calling to the "ungulate display", which can be fatal for the performing individual.

t: Wilson's plover (Anarhynchus wilsonia) is a small bird of the family Charadriidae. Wilson's plover is a coastal wader which breeds on both coasts of the Americas from the equator northwards.
f: It was named after the Scottish-American ornithologist Alexander Wilson by his friend George Ord in 1814.

t: The coal-crested finch (Charitospiza eucosma) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Though previously classified in the bunting and American sparrow family Emberizidae, molecular phylogenetic studies have shown that it is a member of the large tanager family Thraupidae.
f: It feeds on seed of plants specifically found in these habitats.

t: The West Papuan lorikeet (Charmosyna papou) is a species of parrot in the family Psittaculidae.
f: Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The Oʻahu ʻelepaio (Chasiempis ibidis) is a monarch flycatcher endemic to the Hawaiian Island of Oʻahu. It is one of the three distinct, closely related species of ʻelepaio native to the Hawaiian archipelago, including the Hawaiʻi ʻelepaio and the Kauʻi ʻelepaio.
f: They are found in high elevations on the slopes of Oʻahu and primarily consume insects.

t: The Hawaiʻi ʻelepaio (Chasiempis sandwichensis), also Hawaiian ʻelepaio, is a monarch flycatcher found on the Big Island of Hawaii.
f: Until 2010, all three ʻelepaio species, the Kauaʻi ʻelepaio (Chasiempis sclateri), the Oʻahu ʻelepaio (Chasiempis ibidis) and this species were considered conspecific.

t: The Kauaʻi ʻelepaio (Chasiempis sclateri) is a monarch flycatcher found on the Hawaiian Island of Kauaʻi. Whether this fluctuation is natural and thus the birds' numbers will rebound or whether it signifies a novel threat remains to be seen.
f: It numbered 40,000 around 1970, but declined by half in the 1990s.

t: The northern screamer (Chauna chavaria) is a species of bird in family Anhimidae of the waterfowl order Anseriformes.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The southern screamer (Chauna torquata) is a species of bird in family Anhimidae of the waterfowl order Anseriformes.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: The swallow-winged puffbird (Chelidoptera tenebrosa) is a species of bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.
f: It is also called the swallow-wing.

The yellow-bellied fantail (Chelidorhynx hypoxanthus), also known as the yellow-bellied fairy-fantail, is found in the Indian subcontinent, the Himalayas, and portions of Southeast Asia including Thailand, Vietnam, and Myanmar.

t: The snow goose (Anser caerulescens) is a species of goose native to North America. Both white and dark morphs exist, the latter often known as blue goose.
f: It's known as the "blue goose" due to a dark morph of the species.

t: Ross's goose (Anser rossii) is a white goose with black wingtips and a relatively short neck. It is similar in appearance to a white-phase snow goose, but about 40% smaller.
f: It's named in honor of Bernard R. Ross, a figure associated with the Hudson's Bay Company.

t: The Australian wood duck, maned duck, or maned goose (Chenonetta jubata) is a dabbling duck found throughout much of Australia.
f: It is the only living species in the genus Chenonetta.

t: The spike-heeled lark (Chersomanes albofasciata) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry shrubland and subtropical or tropical seasonally wet or flooded lowland grassland.
f: It is found in southern Africa.

t: Dupont's lark (Chersophilus duponti) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae of the monotypic genus Chersophilus.
f: It is found in northern Africa and Spain.

t: The glittering-throated emerald (Chionomesa fimbriata) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, the Guianas, Peru, Trinidad and Venezuela.

t: The sapphire-spangled emerald (Chionomesa lactea) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is regularly found in Bolivia, Brazil, Peru, and Venezuela; as a vagrant in Argentina; and has possibly occurred in Ecuador.

t: The Yungas manakin (Chiroxiphia boliviana) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, and Peru.

t: The blue manakin or swallow-tailed manakin (Chiroxiphia caudata) is a small species of bird in the family Pipridae. It is found mainly in the Atlantic Forest of south-eastern Brazil, eastern Paraguay and far north-eastern Argentina.
f: At breeding time, males are involved in lekking behaviour when they sing and dance to impress females.

t: The lance-tailed manakin (Chiroxiphia lanceolata) is a small passerine bird which breeds in tropical Central and South America from Costa Rica to northern Venezuela. This manakin is a fairly common bird of dry and moist deciduous forests, but not rainforest.
f: At breeding time, males are involved in a cooperative behaviour during which they jump up and down alternately.

t: The long-tailed manakin (Chiroxiphia linearis) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae native to Central America where it inhabits both wet and dry tropical and subtropical forests. It is a small, plump bird about 10 centimetres (4 in) long.
f: At breeding time, males are involved in a cooperative lekking behaviour with a complex coordinated courtship dance.

t: The blue-backed manakin (Chiroxiphia pareola) is a small passerine bird which breeds in tropical South America, its range extending from Colombia and Tobago to southeastern Brazil. It is found in deciduous forests but not evergreen rainforests.
f: At breeding time, males are involved in a cooperative lekking behaviour during which they jump and twirl.

t: The spotted bowerbird (Chlamydera maculata) is a sedentary, mid-sized passerine found across broad parts of the drier habitats of eastern Australia. Spotted bowerbirds are locally common, however, overall the population is thought to be in decline.
f: The species is known for its remarkable behaviours, like many other bowerbirds (Ptilonorynchidae), which include bower building and decorating, courtship displays and vocal mimicry.

t: The great bowerbird (Chlamydera nuchalis) is a common and conspicuous resident of northern Australia, from the area around Broome across the Top End to Cape York Peninsula and as far south as Mount Isa and Townsville. Favoured habitat is a broad range of forest and woodland, and the margins of vine forests, monsoon forest, and mangrove swamps.
f: Only a male with a successful bower can attract mates.

t: The black-fronted tern (Chlidonias albostriatus), sea martin, ploughboy, or tarapiroe (Māori), is a medium-small tern endemic to New Zealand. Their breeding range is restricted to the South Island, where they will form breeding colonies on braided river islands.
f: Black-fronted terns can be found in coastal habitats from the southern tip of the North Island to the eastern South Island as well as Stewart Island.

t: The whiskered tern (Chlidonias hybrida) is a tern in the family Laridae. The genus name is from Ancient Greek khelidonios, "swallow-like", from khelidon, "swallow".
f: The specific hybridus is Latin for hybrid; Peter Simon Pallas thought it might be a hybrid of white-winged black tern and common tern, writing "Sterna fissipes [Chlidonias leucopterus] et Hirundine [Sterna hirundo] natam".

t: The white-winged tern or white-winged black tern (Chlidonias leucopterus) is a species of tern in the family Laridae. The genus name is from Ancient Greek khelidonios, "swallow-like", from khelidon, "swallow".
f: It is a small species generally found in or near bodies of fresh water across much of the world, including Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia.

t: The black tern (Chlidonias niger) is a small tern generally found in or near inland water that breeds in Europe, Western Asia and North America.
f: In winter the birds migrate to coastal areas of Africa and South America.

t: The upland goose or Magellan goose (Chloephaga picta) is a sheldgoose of the shelduck-sheldgoose subfamily of the Anatidae, the biological family that includes the ducks and most duck-like waterfowl such as the geese and swans. Population estimates suggest the insular subpopulations are stable, but continental populations show a recent decline in abundance.
f: Sheldgeese resemble true geese and display similar habits, yet they are more closely related to shelducks and ducks.

t: The white-bellied emerald (Chlorestes candida) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: The White-chinned sapphire (Chlorestes cyanus) is a small species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae. It is found in northern and eastern South America.
f: This species is known for its distinctive steel-blue tail and sexual dimorphism, with males displaying a violet-blue head and throat and a coral-red bill, while females have subdued green plumage.

t: The blue-throated goldentail (Chlorestes eliciae), also known as the blue-throated sapphire, is a species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae. It is found in Belize, Colombia, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, and Panama.
f: This species can be distinguished by its straight, bright red bill with a black tip.
The violet-bellied hummingbird (Chlorestes julie) is a species of hummingbird characterized by the male's shimmering violet belly.

t: The blue-chinned sapphire or blue-chinned emerald (Chlorestes notata) is a hummingbird that ranges from Colombia south and east to the Guianas, Trinidad and Tobago, Peru, and Brazil. There have been occasional records from Tobago.
f: The song is a high metallic ssooo-ssooo-ssooo.

t: The European greenfinch, or simply the greenfinch (Chloris chloris), is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is mainly resident, but some of the populations from the far north migrate further south.
f: It has been introduced into Australia, New Zealand, Uruguay, and Argentina.

t: The Vietnamese greenfinch (Chloris monguilloti) is a small passerine bird in the family Fringillidae. Its natural habitat is open montane pine forest and scrubland.
f: It is found only in Đà Lạt Plateau of southern Vietnam.

The Oriental greenfinch (Chloris sinica), also known as the grey-capped greenfinch, is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae that breeds in broadleaf and conifer woodlands of the East Palearctic.
The yellow-breasted greenfinch (Chloris spinoides) is a small passerine bird in the family Fringillidae that is native to the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent.

t: The American pygmy kingfisher (Chloroceryle aenea) is a species of "water kingfisher" in subfamily Cerylinae of family Alcedinidae.
f: It is found in the American tropics from southern Mexico south through Central America into every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The Amazon kingfisher (Chloroceryle amazona) is a species of "water kingfisher" in subfamily Cerylinae of family Alcedinidae.
f: It is found in the lowlands of the American tropics from southern Mexico south through Central America to northern Argentina.

t: The green kingfisher (Chloroceryle americana) is a species of "water kingfisher" in the subfamily Cerylinae of the family Alcedinidae.
f: It is found from southern Texas in the United States south through Central America, and in every mainland South American country except Chile.

t: The green-and-rufous kingfisher (Chloroceryle inda) is a species of "water kingfisher" in subfamily Cerylinae of family Alcedinidae.
f: It is found in the American tropics from Nicaragua to Panama and in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, and Uruguay.

t: The glistening-green tanager (Chlorochrysa phoenicotis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.
f: Males are almost entirely bright glistening emerald green, with small gray patches behind and below the eye with another on the shoulders.

t: The yellow-bellied greenbul (Chlorocichla flaviventris) is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, and dry savanna.
f: It is found in eastern, southern and west-central Africa.

t: The joyful greenbul (Chlorocichla laetissima) or joyful bulbul, is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. Its natural habitats are boreal forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in east-central Africa.

t: The simple greenbul (Chlorocichla simplex) or simple leaflove, is a species of songbird in the bulbul family of passerine birds. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, and subtropical or tropical moist shrubland.
f: It is widespread throughout the African tropical rainforest.

t: The Oʻahu ʻamakihi (Chlorodrepanis flava) is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper in the family Fringillidae. The male is rich yellow below, sharply contrasted with greenish upper parts.
f: It is endemic to the island of Oʻahu in Hawaiʻi, and is likely the only surviving honeycreeper endemic to the island.

t: The Kauaʻi ʻamakihi (Chlorodrepanis stejnegeri) is a species of Hawaiian honeycreepers endemic to Kauaʻi in the family Fringillidae. The species Hawaiian name is associated with is Kihikihi, or kihi, which stems from the word amakihi.
f: Kihikihi, meaning curved, makes a reference to the bill of the Kauaʻi ʻamakihi.
The Hawaiʻi ʻamakihi (Chlorodrepanis virens), also known as the common ʻamakihi, is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper.

t: The green honeycreeper (Chlorophanes spiza) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in the tropical New World from southern Mexico south to Brazil, and on Trinidad.

t: The golden-browed chlorophonia (Chlorophonia callophrys) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The blue-naped chlorophonia (Chlorophonia cyanea) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile, French Guiana, Suriname, and Uruguay.

t: The golden-rumped euphonia (Chlorophonia cyanocephala) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile and formerly was also found on Trinidad.

t: The elegant euphonia or blue-hooded euphonia (Chlorophonia elegantissima) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Mexico and every Central American country.

t: The yellow-collared chlorophonia (Chlorophonia flavirostris) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama.

t: The Hispaniolan euphonia (Chlorophonia musica) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is endemic to the Caribbean island of Hispaniola that is shared by the Dominican Republic and Haiti.

t: The blue-crowned chlorophonia (Chlorophonia occipitalis) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: The chestnut-breasted chlorophonia (Chlorophonia pyrrhophrys) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The cardinal woodpecker (Dendropicos fuscescens) is a widespread and common resident breeder in much of sub-Saharan Africa. It occurs in a wide range of habitats, ranging from dense forest to thorn bush.
f: They feed primarily on tree-boring insects; using their adhering tongues they extract the insects from holes in wood or bark.

t: The African grey woodpecker (Dendropicos goertae) is a species of bird in the woodpecker family Picidae. Is a widespread and frequently common resident breeder in much of Sub-Saharan and equatorial Africa.
f: It is a species associated with forest and bush which nests in a tree hole, often in an oil palm, laying two to four eggs.

t: The olive woodpecker (Dendropicos griseocephalus) is a species of bird in the woodpecker family Picidae. It is in the Dendropicos genus, which comprises small woodpeckers native to Sub-Saharan Africa.
f: It can last anywhere from 1 to 8 months.

t: The bearded woodpecker (Chloropicus namaquus) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. It is native to tropical central Africa.
f: It has a distinctive black and white head and brownish barred body.

t: The eastern grey woodpecker (Dendropicos spodocephalus), also known as grey-headed woodpecker and mountain gray woodpecker, is a species of bird in the woodpecker family Picidae. It is a resident breeder in eastern Africa.
f: It has a large range and is a fairly common species.

t: The golden-fronted leafbird (Chloropsis aurifrons) is a species of leafbird. It is found from the Indian subcontinent and south-western China, to south-east Asia and Sumatra.
f: It builds its nest in a tree, laying 2-3 eggs.

t: It was formerly considered as conspecific with the widespread blue-winged leafbird.
f: The Javan leafbird (Chloropsis cochinchinensis) is a species of leafbird found in old-growth and second growth forests in Java.

t: The lesser green leafbird (Chloropsis cyanopogon) is a species of bird in the family Chloropseidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The orange-bellied leafbird (Chloropsis hardwickii) is a bird native to the central and eastern Himalayas, Yunnan and northern parts of Southeast Asia. The greyish-crowned leafbird, which is found in Hainan, is again considered conspecific.
f: The scientific name commemorates the English naturalist Thomas Hardwicke.

t: Jerdon's leafbird (Chloropsis jerdoni) is a species of leafbird found in forest and woodland in India and Sri Lanka. It has traditionally been considered a subspecies of the blue-winged leafbird (C. cochinchinensis), but differ in measurements and morphology, it lacking the blue flight feathers for which the blue-winged leafbird was named.
f: They are very shy of water, will only come down to drink for very short periods and are quick to flee.

t: The greater green leafbird (Chloropsis sonnerati) is a species of bird in the family Chloropseidae. It is distinguished from the lesser green leafbird (Chloropsis cyanopogon) by its powerful beak, yellow throat and eye ring of the female; and lack of a yellow border along the black throat patch found in the male C. cyanopogan.
f: The greater green leafbird has a loud voice, consisting of an ascending whistle chee-zi-chee.

t: The grass-green tanager (Chlorornis riefferii) is a small South America bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is the only member of the genus Chlorornis.
f: Its nest is made of mosses and ferns, and its eggs are gray with light purple-grey dots.

t: The ashy-throated chlorospingus (Chlorospingus canigularis) or ashy-throated bush tanager, is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The yellow-throated chlorospingus or yellow-throated bush tanager (Chlorospingus flavigularis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, and Peru.

t: The common chlorospingus (Chlorospingus flavopectus), also referred to as common bush tanager, is a small passerine bird. It is a resident breeder in the highlands from central Mexico south to Bolivia and northwest Argentina.
f: Some populations in fact appear to be more distinct than several other members of Chlorospingus.

t: The sooty-capped chlorospingus (Chlorospingus pileatus) or sooty-capped bush tanager, is a small passerine bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The dusky chlorospingus or dusky bush tanager (Chlorospingus semifuscus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The red-billed emerald (Chlorostilbon gibsoni) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The glittering-bellied emerald (Chlorostilbon lucidus) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The blue-tailed emerald (Chlorostilbon mellisugus) is a hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in tropical and subtropical South America east of the Andes from Colombia east to the Guianas and Trinidad, and south to northern Bolivia and central Brazil.

t: Carmiol's tanager (Chlorothraupis carmioli) is a species of bird in the cardinal family Cardinalidae that is found in Central America from Nicaragua southwards to northwest Colombia. It was formerly considered as conspecific with the yellow-lored tanager.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest.

t: The lemon-spectacled tanager (Chlorothraupis olivacea) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical moist montane forest, and heavily degraded former forest.

t: The ochre-breasted tanager (Chlorothraupis stolzmanni) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae. As a fairly common species with a stable population, the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated this bird as being of "least concern".
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The brown parrotbill (Paradoxornis unicolor) is a bird found in the central and eastern Himalayas. It is also known as the brown suthora.
f: The bird moves in small groups and will sometimes join mixed species foraging flocks.

t: The lark sparrow (Chondestes grammacus) is a fairly large New World sparrow.
f: It is the only member of the genus Chondestes.

t: The hook-billed kite (Chondrohierax uncinatus), is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as kites, eagles, and harriers.
f: It occurs in the Americas, including the Rio Grande Valley of Texas in the United States, Mexico, the Caribbean, Central America, and tropical South America.

t: The lesser nighthawk (Chordeiles acutipennis) is a nightjar found throughout a large part of the Americas. This bird looks similar to the common nighthawk but is slightly smaller, has a slightly less deeply forked tail, and is more buffy in coloration.
f: Their distinctive mouths are very well adapted for capturing insects mid-flight.

t: The Antillean nighthawk (Chordeiles gundlachii) is a nightjar native to the Caribbean, The Bahamas, and Florida Keys.
f: Its specific epithet, gundlachii, is in honor of Cuban naturalist Juan Gundlach.

t: The common nighthawk or bullbat (Chordeiles minor) is a medium-sized crepuscular or nocturnal bird of the Americas within the nightjar (Caprimulgidae) family, whose presence and identity are best revealed by its vocalization. This bird is most conspicuous when in its buoyant and erratic flight.
f: Typically dark (gray, black and brown), displaying cryptic colouration and intricate patterns, this bird is difficult to spot with the naked eye during the day.

t: The nacunda nighthawk (Chordeiles nacunda) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. Its natural habitats are dry savanna, subtropical or tropical seasonally wet or flooded lowland grassland, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, Uruguay, and Venezuela.

t: The least nighthawk (Chordeiles pusillus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The brown-headed gull (Chroicocephalus brunnicephalus) is a small gull which breeds in the high plateaus of central Asia from Tajikistan to Ordos in Inner Mongolia. As is the case with many gulls, was traditionally placed in the genus Larus.
f: It is migratory, wintering on the coasts and large inland lakes of the Indian subcontinent.

t: The grey-headed gull (Chroicocephalus cirrocephalus), also known as the grey-hooded gull, is a small species of gull which breeds patchily in South America and Africa south of the Sahara. This species has occurred as a rare vagrant to the United States, Italy, and Spain.
f: It is not truly migratory, but is dispersive, becoming more widespread in winter.

t: The slender-billed gull (Chroicocephalus genei) is a mid-sized gull which breeds very locally around the Mediterranean and the north of the western Indian Ocean (e.g. Pakistan) on islands and coastal lagoons.
f: Most of the population is somewhat migratory, wintering further south to as far as North Africa and India.

t: The brown-hooded gull (Chroicocephalus maculipennis) is a species of gull, found in South America in Argentina, southeastern Brazil, Chile, Uruguay, and in the South Atlantic Ocean on the Falkland Islands. Like the other species of the genus Chroicocephalus, it was formerly included in a broad view of the genus Larus.
f: Its specific epithet, maculipennis, means 'spotted wings' (macula + penna).

t: The silver gull (Chroicocephalus novaehollandiae) is a gull in Oceania. It has been found throughout the continent, but particularly at or near coastal areas.
f: It is the most common gull of Australia.

t: Bonaparte's gull (Chroicocephalus philadelphia) is a gull found mainly in northern North America. Its plumage is mainly white with grey upperparts.
f: At 28 to 38 cm (11 to 15 in) in length, it is one of the smallest species of gull.

t: The black-headed gull (Chroicocephalus ridibundus) is a small gull that breeds in much of the Palearctic in Europe and Asia, and also locally in smaller numbers in coastal eastern Canada. Most of the population is migratory and winters further south, but many also remain in the milder areas of northwestern Europe.
f: It was formerly known as "common black-headed gull" to distinguish it from Pallas's gull.

t: It was formerly considered a separate species but is now usually treated as a subspecies of the silver gull (Chroicocephalus novaehollandiae). The Māori name of this species is tarāpunga or akiaki.
f: A national survey of breeding red-billed gulls carried out in 2014–2016 recorded 27,831 pairs nesting in New Zealand.

t: The Andean gull (Chroicocephalus serranus) is a species in subfamily Larinae of the family Laridae, the gulls, terns, and skimmers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: Horsfield's bronze cuckoo (Chalcites basalis) is a small cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. Its size averages 22 g (0.78 oz) and is distinguished by its green and bronze iridescent colouring on its back and incomplete brown barring from neck to tail.
f: Horsfield's bronze cuckoo can be distinguished from other bronze cuckoos by its white eyebrow and brown eye stripe.
The diederik cuckoo (Chrysococcyx caprius), formerly dideric cuckoo or didric cuckoo, is a member of the cuckoo family of birds, Cuculidae, which also includes the roadrunners and the anis.
The African emerald cuckoo (Chrysococcyx cupreus) is a species of cuckoo that is native to Africa.

t: Klaas's cuckoo (Chrysococcyx klaas) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae which is native to the wooded regions of sub-Saharan Africa.
f: The specific name honours Klaas, the Khoikhoi man who collected the type specimen.

t: The shining bronze cuckoo or pīpīwharauroa (Chalcites lucidus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae, found in Australia, Indonesia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, and Vanuatu. It was formerly placed in the genus Chrysococcyx.
f: It may also parasitise other Acanthizidae species, and is also the most southerly ranging brood parasitic bird species in the world, extending to at least 46°S in New Zealand.

t: The Asian emerald cuckoo (Chrysococcyx maculatus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The little bronze cuckoo (Chalcites minutillus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It was formerly placed in the genus Chrysococcyx.
f: It is the world's smallest cuckoo.

t: The black-eared cuckoo (Chalcites osculans) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. They are usually observed by themselves or in a pair as they don't raise their own young, rather they leave eggs in another species nest to be raised by host.
f: Found across Australia, it migrates to eastern Indonesia and southern New Guinea.
The violet cuckoo (Chrysococcyx xanthorhynchus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae.

t: The white-naped woodpecker (Chrysocolaptes festivus) is woodpecker which is a widespread but a scarce breeder in the Indian subcontinent. It is associated with open forest and scrub with some trees.
f: It nests in a tree hole, laying one or two white eggs.

t: The greater flameback (Chrysocolaptes guttacristatus), also known as the greater goldenback or large golden-backed woodpecker, is a woodpecker species.
f: It occurs widely in the northern Indian subcontinent, eastwards to southern China, the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, western and central Java and northeast Borneo.

t: The ruby-topaz hummingbird (Chrysolampis mosquitus), commonly referred to simply as the ruby topaz, is a species of hummingbird in the subfamily Polytminae, the mangoes.
f: It is found in Aruba, Bolivia, Bonaire, Brazil, Colombia, Curaçao, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, and Venezuela.

t: Lady Amherst's pheasant (Chrysolophus amherstiae) is a bird of the order Galliformes and the family Phasianidae. The genus name is from the Ancient Greek: χρυσόλόφος chrusolophos, "with golden crest".
f: The English name and amherstiae commemorates Sarah Amherst, who was responsible for sending the first specimen of the bird to London in 1828.

t: The golden pheasant (Chrysolophus pictus), also known as the Chinese pheasant, and rainbow pheasant, is a gamebird of the order Galliformes (gallinaceous birds) and the family Phasianidae (pheasants).
f: The genus name is from Ancient Greek khrusolophos, "with golden crest", and pictus is Latin for "painted" from pingere, "to paint".

t: Jerdon's babbler (Chrysomma altirostre) is a passerine bird native to wetlands and grasslands of the Indian sub-continent. It is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List since 1994.
f: The common name commemorates the surgeon-naturalist Thomas C.

t: The yellow-eyed babbler (Chrysomma sinense) is a passerine bird native to South and Southeast Asia. It inhabits shrubland, grassland and wetland habitats.
f: Its common name refers to the traditional placement in the Old World babbler family Timaliidae although the genus Chrysomma forms a clade along with the parrotbills within the family Paradoxornithidae.

t: The yellow-hooded blackbird (Chrysomus icterocephalus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds. It is found in Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, Trinidad, and Venezuela.
f: It has been recorded as a vagrant on Aruba, Bonaire, and Curaçao.

t: The chestnut-capped blackbird (Chrysomus ruficapillus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The greater yellownape (Chrysophlegma flavinucha) is a species of bird in the woodpecker family Picidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in East Asia from northern and eastern India to south-eastern China, Indochina, Hainan, and Sumatra.
The checker-throated woodpecker, checker-throated yellownape, or Javan yellownape (Chrysophlegma mentale) is a species of bird in the family Picidae native to Southeast Asia.

t: The banded woodpecker (Chrysophlegma miniaceum) or the banded red woodpecker is a species of bird in the family Picidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The black-and-yellow tanager (Chrysothlypis chrysomelas) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, and Panama.

t: The scarlet-and-white tanager (Chrysothlypis salmoni) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in Colombia and northern Ecuador.
f: It feeds mainly on fruit and arthropods.

t: The golden-tailed sapphire (Chrysuronia oenone) is a species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
The versicoloured emerald (Chrysuronia versicolor) is a species of hummingbird from central and eastern South America.

t: The black-legged seriema (Chunga burmeisteri) is one of two living species of seriemas in the family Cariamidae. It is found from southeastern Bolivia and northern Paraguay south into north-central Argentina.
f: It seldom flies, instead pursuing prey and eluding danger on foot.

t: The rufous-banded owl (Strix albitarsis) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The black-banded owl (Strix huhula) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae. Its natural habitats are varied subtropical or tropical forests ranging from lowlands to areas of medium altitude, and it has been found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.
f: Entirely nocturnal, this midsized black and white neotropical bird is a resident species, and therefore never migrates out of its native South America.
The black-and-white owl (Strix nigrolineata) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.

t: The mottled owl (Strix virgata) is a medium-sized owl found in Central and South America from Mexico to Brazil and Argentina. The head and back are mottled brown and the underparts whitish, with vertical bars on the chest and throat.
f: The eyes are dark and the head is round and they do not have ear tufts.

t: The collared palm thrush (Cichladusa arquata) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is found in Botswana, Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.
f: The Collared palm thrush is an odd and distinctive bird, easily recognized by its unique features.

t: The spotted palm thrush (Cichladusa guttata), also known as the spotted morning-thrush, is a species of bird in the Muscicapidae family. They are small birds mostly consisting of the colors brown, black, and cream.
f: These birds create a variety of different vocal duets as a form of communication.
The pale-browed treehunter (Cichlocolaptes leucophrus) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The rufous-brown solitaire (Cichlopsis leucogenys) is a species of bird in the thrush family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The magnificent bird-of-paradise (Diphyllodes magnificus) is a species of bird-of-paradise. The magnificent bird-of-paradise is evaluated as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species.
f: They are listed in Appendix II of CITES.

t: The king bird-of-paradise (Cicinnurus regius) is a passerine bird of the Paradisaeidae (bird-of-paradise) family. It is considered by the IOC checklist to be the only member of the genus Cicinnurus, although the genus Diphyllodes is closely related and is subsumed under Cicinnurus by many other authorities.
f: Some populations range quite high into the hills and lower mountains, and these are poorly known as yet.

t: Wilson's bird-of-paradise (Diphyllodes respublica) is a species of passerine bird of the family Paradisaeidae. He did so by dropping leaves on the forest floor, which irritated the bird into clearing them away.
f: The first footage of the Wilson's bird-of-paradise ever to be filmed was recorded in 1996 by David Attenborough for the BBC documentary Attenborough in Paradise.

t: The white stork (Ciconia ciconia) is a large bird in the stork family, Ciconiidae. Its plumage is mainly white, with black on the bird's wings.
f: It avoids crossing the Mediterranean Sea, detouring via the Levant or Gibraltar to find soaring air thermals.

t: The black stork (Ciconia nigra) is a large bird in the stork family Ciconiidae. It was first described by Carl Linnaeus in the 10th edition of his Systema Naturae.
f: Breeding pairs usually build nests in large forest trees—most commonly deciduous but also coniferous—which can be seen from long distances, as well as on large boulders, or under overhanging ledges in mountainous areas.

t: The blue-fronted robin (Cinclidium frontale) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is the only species in the monotypic genus Cinclidium.
f: Blue-fronted robins are a bird species with limited published research.

t: The grey trembler (Cinclocerthia gutturalis) is a songbird species in the family Mimidae, the mockingbirds and thrashers.
f: It is found only on Martinique and Saint Lucia in the Lesser Antilles of the Caribbean Sea.

t: The chestnut-winged cinclodes (Cinclodes albidiventris) is a species of bird in the family Furnariidae. It was formerly considered a subspecies of the bar-winged cinclodes.
f: It is found in Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The cream-winged cinclodes (Cinclodes albiventris) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.

t: The stout-billed cinclodes (Cinclodes excelsior) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The buff-winged cinclodes (Cinclodes fuscus) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay, Uruguay and as a vagrant on the Falkland Islands.
The Chilean seaside cinclodes or simply seaside cinclodes (Cinclodes nigrofumosus) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The grey-flanked cinclodes (Cinclodes oustaleti), formerly known as Oustalet's cinclodes, is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Chile.
The long-tailed cinclodes (Cinclodes pabsti) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
