t: The dark-bellied cinclodes (Cinclodes patagonicus) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Chile.

t: The brown songlark (Cincloramphus cruralis), also Australian songlark, is a small passerine bird found throughout much of Australia. A member of the family Locustellidae, this species is notable for sexual size dimorphism, among the most pronounced in any bird.
f: It is a moderate-sized bird of nondescript plumage; the female brownish above and paler below, the larger male a darker brown.

t: The Papuan grassbird (Cincloramphus macrurus) is a species of typical grassbird in the family Locustellidae. The species was once treated as several subspecies of the tawny grassbird, but the two do not interbreed where their ranges are sympatric.
f: The species is endemic to New Guinea and its satellite islands.
The rufous songlark (Cincloramphus mathewsi) is a species in the family Locustellidae endemic to Australia.

t: The tawny grassbird (Cincloramphus timoriensis) is a large songbird that is a member of the family Locustellidae commonly found in grassland and reedbed habitats. Its underside is paler and it has a long graduated tail.
f: It is streaked above and has a distinctive rich brown cap.

t: The painted quail-thrush (Cinclosoma ajax) is a species of bird in the family Cinclosomatidae.
f: Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
The chestnut-breasted quail-thrush (Cinclosoma castaneothorax) is a small endemic Australian bird which is predominantly found within the semi-arid deserts of New South Wales and Queensland.

t: The spotted quail-thrush (Cinclosoma punctatum) is a species of bird in the family Cinclosomatidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical, tropical and temperate dry forest.
f: It is generally cryptic and terrestrial.

t: The white-throated dipper (Cinclus cinclus), also known as the European dipper or just dipper, is an aquatic, passerine bird found in Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.
f: The species is divided into several subspecies, based primarily on colour differences, particularly of the pectoral band.
The American dipper (Cinclus mexicanus), also known as a water ouzel, is a semiaquatic bird species native from North America.

t: The brown dipper (Cinclus pallasii), also known as Pallas's dipper, Asian dipper or the Asiatic dipper, is an aquatic songbird found in the mountains of the east Palearctic. Its plumage is chocolate-brown with a slightly lighter coloured back and breast.
f: It is a thrush-like bird with a cocked tail.

t: The fulvous wren (Cinnycerthia fulva) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru.

t: The sepia-brown wren or Sharpe's wren (Cinnycerthia olivascens) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
The Peruvian wren (Cinnycerthia peruana) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

t: The rufous wren (Cinnycerthia unirufa) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The violet-backed starling (Cinnyricinclus leucogaster), also known as the plum-coloured starling or amethyst starling, or Ndambamukula in the Venda language, is a relatively small species (17 cm) of starling in the family Sturnidae. It is the only member of the genus Cinnyricinclus.
f: This strongly sexually dimorphic species is found widely in the woodlands and savannah forest edges of mainland sub-Saharan Africa.

t: The greater double-collared sunbird (Cinnyris afer) is a small bird in the sunbird family.
f: It was formerly placed in genus Nectarinia.

t: The purple sunbird (Cinnyris asiaticus) is a small bird in the sunbird family. It occurs in parts of the Arabian peninsula and South and Southeast Asia.
f: It has a fast and direct flight and can take nectar by hovering like a hummingbird but often perches at the base of flowers.

t: The purple-banded sunbird (Cinnyris bifasciatus) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. The Tsavo sunbird, sometimes lumped with the purple-banded, is here considered a separate species.
f: It is found in Angola, Botswana, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Eswatini, Gabon, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Rwanda, Somalia, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

t: The southern double-collared sunbird or lesser double-collared sunbird (Cinnyris chalybeus) is a small passerine bird which breeds in southern Africa.
f: It is mainly resident, but partially migratory in the north-east of its range.

t: The olive-bellied sunbird (Cinnyris chloropygius) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae.
f: It is widely spread across the African tropical rainforest primarily throughout West and Central Africa, but is also found in Southern and East Africa.

t: The splendid sunbird (Cinnyris coccinigastrus) is a sunbird. The sunbirds are a group of very small Old World passerine birds which feed largely on nectar, although they will also feed on insects, especially when feeding young.
f: Most species can take nectar by hovering like a hummingbird, but usually perch to feed most of the time.

t: The copper sunbird (Cinnyris cupreus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Nectariniidae.
f: It is native to tropical Africa, its range extending from Senegal and Guinea in the west to South Sudan and Kenya in the east, and southwards to Angola, Zambia, Zimbabwe and Mozambique.

t: The red-chested sunbird (Cinnyris erythrocercus) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae.
f: It is found in Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: The dusky sunbird (Cinnyris fuscus) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. This relatively dull sunbird is found in arid savanna, thickets and shrubland (e.g.
f: Karoo) in Angola, Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa.
The western miombo sunbird (Cinnyris gertrudis) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae.

t: The Abyssinian sunbird (Cinnyris habessinicus), formerly the shining sunbird, is a species of passerine bird in the sunbird family Nectariniidae.
f: The Arabian sunbird was formerly treated as a subspecies.

t: The garden sunbird (Cinnyris jugularis), previously known as the olive-backed sunbird, is a species of passerine bird in the family Nectariniidae that is found in the Philippines except on the Palawan island group. It was formerly considered to be conspecific with seven other species: the ornate sunbird, Palawan sunbird, Sahul sunbird, Tukangbesi sunbird, Flores Sea sunbird, South Moluccan sunbird and the Mamberamo sunbird.
f: It is primarily nectarivorous, but will take insects and spiders, particularly when feeding chicks.

t: Loten's sunbird (Cinnyris lotenius), also known as the long-billed sunbird or maroon-breasted sunbird, is a sunbird endemic to peninsular India and Sri Lanka.
f: Like other sunbirds, it is also insectivorous and builds characteristic hanging nests.

t: The Marico sunbird (Cinnyris mariquensis) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae, which is native to woodlands of the eastern and southern Afrotropics.The bird is typically found in the southeast of the continent of Africa. It is of least concern on the IUCN Red List and has an unknown population size that has yet to be quantified.
f: The Marico sunbird has conservation regions located all over its range, so it is unlikely to go extinct.

t: The eastern double-collared sunbird (Cinnyris mediocris) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae.
f: It is found in upland areas of Kenya and northern Tanzania.

t: The black-bellied sunbird (Cinnyris nectarinioides) is a small sunbird located primarily in Africa. Two subspecies are recognized: the Cinnyris nectarinioides erlangeri, which is smaller and found in Ethiopia, Somalia, and Kenya; and the Cinnyris nectarinioides nectarinioides, which is larger and found in Kenya and Tanzania.
f: The black-bellied sunbird feeds on nectar, insects and spiders, the latter having gained it the nickname "spiderhunter".

t: The Palestine sunbird (Cinnyris osea) is a small passerine bird of the sunbird family, Nectariniidae. Found in parts of the Middle East and sub-Saharan Africa, it is also known as the northern orange-tufted sunbird.
f: In 2015 the Palestinian Authority adopted the species as a national bird, after it lost in Israel's national bird public vote in 2008 in favor of the hoopoe.

t: The beautiful sunbird (Cinnyris pulchellus), formerly placed in the genus Nectarinia, is a small passerine bird in the sunbird family Nectariniidae. It was formerly considered to be conspecific with the gorgeous sunbird (Cinnyris melanogastrus).
f: It is native to tropical Africa, its range extending from Senegal and Guinea in the west to Sudan, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Tanzania and Kenya in the east.

t: The regal sunbird (Cinnyris regius) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae.
f: It is native to the Albertine Rift montane forests.

t: The northern double-collared sunbird (Cinnyris reichenowi), is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae.
f: It is found in Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Sudan, and Uganda.

t: The flame-breasted sunbird (Cinnyris solaris) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found on Timor and other islands, primarily in the Indonesian province of Nusa Tenggara Timur.

t: The souimanga sunbird (Cinnyris sovimanga) is a small passerine bird of the sunbird family, Nectariniidae.
f: It is native to the islands of the western Indian Ocean where it occurs on Madagascar, the Aldabra Group and the Glorioso Islands.

t: The white-bellied sunbird (Cinnyris talatala), also known as the white-breasted sunbird, is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae.
f: It is found in Angola, Botswana, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Eswatini, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

t: The variable sunbird or yellow-bellied sunbird (Cinnyris venustus), formerly Nectarinia venusta, is a sunbird. The sunbirds are a group of small Old World passerine birds which feed largely on nectar, although they will also take insects, especially when feeding young.
f: Most species can take nectar by hovering like a hummingbird, but usually perch to feed most of the time.

t: The short-toed snake eagle (Circaetus gallicus), also known as the short-toed eagle, is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as kites, buzzards and harriers. The genus name Circaetus is from the Ancient Greek kirkos, a type of hawk, and aetos, "eagle".
f: The specific gallicus means "of Gallia".

t: It is also known as the Eurasian marsh harrier. Formerly, a number of relatives were included in C. aeruginosus, which was then known as "marsh harrier".
f: The western marsh harrier (Circus aeruginosus) is a large harrier, a bird of prey from temperate and subtropical western Eurasia and adjacent Africa.

t: The swamp harrier (Circus approximans), also known as the Australasian marsh harrier or Australasian harrier, is a large, slim bird of prey widely distributed across Australasia. It arrived in New Zealand within the last 700 years, replacing the larger species, the extinct New Zealand endemic Eyles's harrier.
f: In New Zealand, it is also known by the Māori name kāhu.

t: The long-winged harrier (Circus buffoni) is a common bird of prey species endemic to South America. They are members of the family Accipitridae, under the genus Circus which encompasses other harrier species.
f: The long-winged harrier is a carnivorous bird, and will feed on many different animals found in its habitat.

t: The hen harrier (Circus cyaneus) is a bird of prey. It breeds in open areas such as marshes and grasslands in Eurasia and is migratory, moving further south outside of the breeding season.
f: Birds in milder regions, such as France and Great Britain, may be resident year-round, but the higher altitudes are largely deserted in winter.

t: The northern harrier (Circus hudsonius), also known as the marsh hawk or ring-tailed hawk, is a bird of prey. It breeds throughout the northern parts of the Northern Hemisphere in Canada and the northernmost United States.
f: The northern harrier migrates south in winter, with breeding birds in Canada and northern Great Plains of the U.S. moving to the American south, Mexico, and Central America.

t: The pallid harrier (Circus macrourus) is a species of harrier, a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. It breeds in southern parts of eastern Europe and central Asia and Iran and winters mainly in India and southeast Asia.
f: In 2019, a pair bred in Spain for the first time.

t: The pied harrier (Circus melanoleucos) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, named for the male's distinctive white and black colouration. They are primarily solitary although will sometimes form loose groups.
f: It is a migratory bird endemic to Asia, ranging roughly from southern Siberia to the Philippines.

t: Montagu's harrier (Circus pygargus) is a species of harrier, a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. It breeds in large open areas in the Palearctic and is migratory, wintering in Africa, the Indian subcontinent and parts of the Arabian Peninsula.
f: Its common name commemorates the British naturalist George Montagu.

t: It was previously considered to be conspecific with the western marsh harrier (Circus aeruginosus) but is now usually classified as a separate species. It has two subspecies: C. s. spilonotus in eastern Asia and C. s. spilothorax (Papuan harrier, perhaps a separate species) in New Guinea.
f: The eastern marsh harrier (Circus spilonotus) is a bird of prey belonging to the marsh harrier group of harriers.

t: The common green magpie (Cissa chinensis) is a member of the crow family, roughly the size of the Eurasian jay or slightly smaller. In the wild, specimens are usually a bright and lush green in colour , slightly lighter on the underside and have a thick black stripe from the bill through the eyes to the nape.
f: This bird seeks food both on the ground and in the canopy of the trees, and takes a very high percentage of animal prey from countless invertebrates, small reptiles, mammals and young birds and eggs.
The Indochinese green magpie (Cissa hypoleuca), also known as the yellow-breasted magpie, is a small colourful bird native to the forests of China and Vietnam.

t: The Bornean green magpie (Cissa jefferyi) is a passerine bird in the crow family, Corvidae. It is endemic to montane forests on the southeast Asian island of Borneo.
f: It dwells in thick vegetation in the mid and upper storeys of forests, and makes only short flights.

t: The magpie tanager (Cissopis leverianus) is a South American species of tanager. It is the only member of the monotypic genus Cissopis.
f: The cup-shaped nest is lined with grass, leaves, or other plant materials and is located low in trees near the ground or in shrubs in dense vegetation.

t: The rock-loving cisticola (Cisticola aberrans), also known as the lazy cisticola, is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It was formerly considered to be conspecific with the Huambo cisticola (Cisticola bailunduensis).
f: It is widespread throughout sub-Saharan Africa and is usually associated with rocky wooded terrain with interspersed patchy grass tussocks.

t: The chattering cisticola (Cisticola anonymus) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitats are dry savanna and swamps.
f: It is native to the African tropical rainforest.

t: The desert cisticola (Cisticola aridulus) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It forages primarily in grassy vegetation.
f: It is present throughout much of sub-Saharan Africa, although relatively absent from central and coastal western areas of the continent.

t: The wing-snapping cisticola (Cisticola ayresii), also known as Ayres' cisticola, is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae.
f: Its scientific name honours South African ornithologist Thomas Ayres.

t: The short-winged cisticola (Cisticola brachypterus), also known as the siffling cisticola, is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae.
f: The short-winged cisticola resembles the neddicky, a similar member of the genus Cisticola, but lacks the rufous crown with a shorter tail and clear buff underparts.

t: The singing cisticola (Cisticola cantans) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.
f: It is native to northern and eastern sub-Saharan Africa.

t: The Madagascar cisticola (Cisticola cherina) is a species of bird in the cisticola family (Cisticolidae). It inhabits areas to the west of the ˞Indian Ocean.
f: It forms a superspecies with the closely related zitting cisticola and the Socotra cisticola.

t: The rattling cisticola (Cisticola chiniana) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae which is native to Africa south of the equator, and parts of East Africa. Especially during summer, it is highly conspicuous due to its strident and repetitive call-notes from prominent perches.
f: It is a common to abundant species in open savanna and scrubland habitats, whether in arid, moist or upland regions.

t: Chubb's cisticola (Cisticola chubbi) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is native to the Western High Plateau, the Albertine Rift montane forests and the East African montane forests.
f: It spends most of its time in dense vegetation.

t: The ashy cisticola (Cisticola cinereolus) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitats are dry savanna, subtropical or tropical dry shrubland, and subtropical or tropical dry lowland grassland.
f: It is found in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, and Tanzania.

t: The red-faced cisticola (Cisticola erythrops) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical seasonally wet or flooded lowland grassland and swamps.
f: It is widely present across sub-Saharan Africa (rare in southern Africa).

t: The golden-headed cisticola (Cisticola exilis), also known as the bright-capped cisticola, is a species of warbler in the family Cisticolidae, found in Australia and thirteen Asian countries. Growing to 9–11.5 cm (3.5–4.5 in) long, it is usually brown and cream in colour, but has a different appearance during the mating season, with a gold-coloured body and a much shorter tail.
f: Known as the "finest tailor of all birds", it constructs nests out of plants and spider threads.

t: The neddicky, or piping cisticola (Cisticola fulvicapilla), is a small passerine bird in the family Cisticolidae, which is native to Africa, southwards of the equator. The common name, neddicky, is the Afrikaans name for the species.
f: Its strongholds are the light woodlands and shrublands of the subtropics and temperate regions of southern Africa.

t: The coastal cisticola (Cisticola haematocephalus), also known as the umbabird, is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is found on the coastal plain of East Africa.
f: Alternate common names are Mombasa black-backed cisticola.

t: Hunter's cisticola (Cisticola hunteri) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitats are tropical moist montane and high-elevation shrubland.
f: It is found in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: A small bird found mainly in grasslands, it is best identified by its rufous rump; in addition it lacks any gold on the collar and the brownish tail is tipped with white. They build their pouch nest suspended within a clump of grass.
f: During the breeding season males have a zigzagging flight display accompanied by regular "zit" calls that give it its English name.

t: The wailing cisticola (Cisticola lais) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is found in Angola, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.
f: The appearance of their eggs varies widely; they can be white, pale blue, spotted, or streaked.

t: The whistling cisticola (Cisticola lateralis) is a species of bird in the Cisticolidae family. Its natural habitats include subtropical or tropical dry forests, dry savanna, and moist savanna.
f: It is native to the African tropical rainforest and adjacent areas.

t: The winding cisticola (Cisticola marginatus) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae.
f: It has a scattered distribution across Africa south of the Sahara, and north of 11°S.

t: The croaking cisticola (Cisticola natalensis) is an Old World warbler in the family Cisticolidae. It is a resident breeder in Africa south of the Sahara.
f: It is best distinguished from its many African relatives by its size and froglike croaking breep-breep song.

t: The black-lored cisticola (Cisticola nigriloris) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.
f: It is found in Malawi, Tanzania, and Zambia.

t: The churring cisticola (Cisticola njombe) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical high-elevation grassland.
f: It is found in Malawi, Tanzania, and Zambia.

t: The chirping cisticola (Cisticola pipiens) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical seasonally wet or flooded lowland grassland and swamps.
f: It is found in Angola, Botswana, Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Namibia, Tanzania, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

t: The stout cisticola (Cisticola robustus) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitats are boreal forest, moist savanna, and subtropical or tropical high-altitude grassland.
f: It is found in Angola, Burundi, Cameroon, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia.

t: The grey-backed cisticola or red-headed cisticola (Cisticola subruficapilla) is a small passerine bird. This cisticola is a resident breeder in southernmost Angola, Namibia and western South Africa.
f: The grey-backed cisticola is a very common bird of coastal fynbos, karoo shrub and grassy areas on estuarine flats.

t: The cloud cisticola or tink-tink cisticola (Cisticola textrix) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae.
f: It is found in Angola, Eswatini, Lesotho, Mozambique, South Africa, and Zambia, and its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry lowland grassland.
Levaillant's cisticola (Cisticola tinniens), also known as the tinkling cisticola, is a small passerine bird which is native to marshlands in the uplands of Africa, southwards of the equator.

t: The trilling cisticola (Cisticola woosnami) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitats are dry savanna and subtropical or tropical dry lowland grassland.
f: It is found in Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia.
Apolinar's wren (Cistothorus apolinari) is a passerine bird in the family Troglodytidae.

t: The marsh wren (Cistothorus palustris) is a small North American songbird of the wren family.
f: It was formerly called the long-billed marsh wren to distinguish it from the sedge wren.

t: The grass wren (Cistothorus platensis) is a species of passerine bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is widely distributed in central and southern America.

t: The sedge wren (Cistothorus stellaris) is a small and secretive passerine bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is widely distributed in North America.
f: It is often found in wet grasslands and meadows where it nests in the tall grasses and sedges and feeds on insects.

t: The chestnut-winged cuckoo or red-winged crested cuckoo (Clamator coromandus) is a cuckoo found in Southeast Asia and parts of South Asia. It has dark glossy upperparts, a black head with long crest chestnut wings, a long graduated glossy black tail, rufous throat dusky underside and a narrow white nuchal half collar.
f: They breed along the Himalayas and migrate south in winter to Sri Lanka, southern India and tropical Southeast Asia including parts of Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines.

t: The great spotted cuckoo (Clamator glandarius) is a member of the cuckoo order of birds, the Cuculiformes, which also includes the roadrunners, the anis and the coucals. It is widely spread throughout Africa and the Mediterranean Basin.
f: It is a brood parasite that lays its eggs in the nests of corvids, in particular the Eurasian magpie.

t: The Jacobin cuckoo (Clamator jacobinus), also pied cuckoo or pied crested cuckoo, is a member of the cuckoo order of birds that is found in Africa and Asia. It has been associated with a bird in Indian mythology and poetry, known as the chātaka (Sanskrit: चातक) represented as a bird with a beak on its head that waits for rains to quench its thirst.
f: It is partially migratory and in India, it has been considered a harbinger of the monsoon rains due to the timing of its arrival.

t: Levaillant's cuckoo (Clamator levaillantii) is a cuckoo which is a resident breeding species in Africa south of the Sahara. It was named in honour of the French explorer, collector and ornithologist, François Le Vaillant.
f: It is a brood parasite, using the nests of bulbuls and babblers.

t: The greater spotted eagle (Clanga clanga), also called the spotted eagle, is a large migratory bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. It is a member of the subfamily Aquilinae, commonly known as "booted eagles".
f: As is common among a few species of raptors, the oldest chick is much larger than its younger siblings, and will often attack and kill the younger siblings.

t: The lesser spotted eagle (Clanga pomarina) is a large Eastern European bird of prey. Like all typical eagles, it belongs to the family Accipitridae.
f: The typical eagles are often united with the buteos, sea eagles, and other more heavy-set Accipitridae, but more recently it appears as if they are less distinct from the more slender accipitrine hawks than believed.

t: The long-tailed duck (Clangula hyemalis) is a medium-sized sea duck that breeds in the tundra and taiga regions of the arctic and winters along the northern coastlines of the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
f: It is the only member of the genus Clangula.

t: The blue ground dove (Claravis pretiosa) is a small New World tropical dove.
f: It is a resident breeder from southeastern Mexico to northwestern Peru and northern Argentina, and on Trinidad in the Caribbean.

t: The canebrake groundcreeper (Clibanornis dendrocolaptoides) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The henna-hooded foliage-gleaner (Clibanornis erythrocephalus) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The henna-capped foliage-gleaner or chestnut-capped foliage-gleaner (Clibanornis rectirostris) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil and Paraguay.

t: The ruddy foliage-gleaner (Clibanornis rubiginosus) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: Its range is highly disjunct, with populations in Mexico, several Central American countries, and in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The Santa Marta foliage-gleaner (Clibanornis rufipectus) is a vulnerable species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is endemic to Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in Colombia.

t: The brown treecreeper (Climacteris picumnus) is the largest Australasian treecreeper. The bird, endemic to eastern Australia, has a broad distribution, occupying areas from Cape York, Queensland, throughout New South Wales and Victoria to Port Augusta and the Flinders Ranges, South Australia.
f: Found in a diverse range of habitats varying from coastal forests to mallee shrub-lands, the brown treecreeper often occupies eucalypt-dominated woodland habitats up to 1,000 metres (3,300 ft), avoiding areas with a dense shrubby understorey.

t: The recurve-billed bushbird (Clytoctantes alixii) is an Endangered species of Thamnophilid antbird that inhabits dense stands of secondary vegetation at the northern end of the Andes in Colombia and Venezuela. It is named for its extraordinary bill, which curves upwards.
f: Until 2007, the bird was almost unknown in life and apart from earlier specimens it had only been seen in life once at an army ant swarm in Colombia in 1965.
The Brazilian ruby (Heliodoxa rubricauda) is a species of hummingbird in the "brilliants", tribe Heliantheini, in the subfamily Lesbiinae.

t: The Fiji shrikebill (Clytorhynchus vitiensis) is a songbird species in the family Monarchidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in American Samoa, Fiji, and Tonga.

t: The grey-hooded bush tanager (Cnemoscopus rubrirostris) is a species of South American bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
f: It is the only member of the genus Cnemoscopus.

t: The fuscous flycatcher (Cnemotriccus fuscatus) is a small passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Trinidad and Tobago and in every mainland South American country except Chile.

t: The brownish twistwing (Cnipodectes subbrunneus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, and Peru.
The swee waxbill (Coccopygia melanotis), is a common species of estrildid finch native to Southern Africa.

t: The yellow-bellied waxbill (Coccopygia quartinia) is a species of estrildid finch native to East Africa. It breeds in east central and south-eastern Africa.
f: The bird is now named yellow-bellied swee.

t: The hooded grosbeak or Albiellé's grosbeak (Hesperiphona abeillei) is a passerine bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Guatemala, El Salvador, and Mexico.

t: The hawfinch (Coccothraustes coccothraustes) is a passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is the only extant species placed in the genus Coccothraustes.
f: The song of this unobtrusive bird is quiet and mumbled.

t: The evening grosbeak (Hesperiphona vespertina) is a passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae found in North America. The evening grosbeak is bulky, with a large bill and short tail.
f: Its migration pattern is variable, sometimes reaching as far south as the southern U.S. in winters.

t: The ash-colored cuckoo (Coccycua cinerea) is an American bird species of the cuckoo family (Cuculidae). It was formerly placed in the genus Coccyzus or Micrococcyx.
f: Its range extends from northern and central Argentina to Uruguay and São Paulo (state); its wintering range extend northwards towards Amazonas.

t: The little cuckoo (Coccycua minuta) is a species of bird in the cuckoo family (Cuculidae) from South America and Panama.
f: It was formerly placed in the genus Piaya, but was moved to the reinstated genus Coccycua following the discovery that its closest living relatives are a couple species traditionally placed in Coccyzus or Micrococcyx, rather than the other members of Piaya.

t: The yellow-billed cuckoo (Coccyzus americanus) is a member of the cuckoo family. These likely refer to the bird's habit of calling on hot days, often presaging rain showers or thunderstorms.
f: Common folk names for this bird in the southern United States are rain crow and storm crow.

t: The black-billed cuckoo (Coccyzus erythropthalmus) is a New World species in the Cuculidae (cuckoo) family. The scientific name is from Ancient Greek.
f: Although many cuckoos are obligate brood parasites, C. erythropthalmus often incubate their own chicks.

t: The pearly-breasted cuckoo (Coccyzus euleri) is a species of bird in the tribe Phaenicophaeini, subfamily Cuculinae of the cuckoo family Cuculidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Paraguay, Suriname, Venezuela, and possibly Colombia and Panama.

t: The Hispaniolan lizard cuckoo (Coccyzus longirostris) is a species of bird in the tribe Phaenicophaeini, subfamily Cuculinae of the cuckoo family Cuculidae.
f: It is endemic to the island of Hispaniola that is shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

t: The dark-billed cuckoo (Coccyzus melacoryphus) is a species of bird in the tribe Phaenicophaeini, subfamily Cuculinae of the cuckoo family Cuculidae. It has also occurred as a vagrant in Chile and several other countries and islands.
f: It is regularly found in every mainland South American country except Chile plus the Galápagos Islands.

t: The great lizard cuckoo (Coccyzus merlini) is a species of bird in the tribe Phaenicophaeini, subfamily Cuculinae of the cuckoo family Cuculidae.
f: It is found in the Bahamas and Cuba.
The mangrove cuckoo (Coccyzus minor) is a species of cuckoo that is native to the Neotropics.
The Puerto Rican lizard cuckoo (Coccyzus vieilloti) is a species of bird in the tribe Phaenicophaeini, subfamily Cuculinae of the cuckoo family Cuculidae.

t: The boat-billed heron (Cochlearius cochlearius), colloquially known as the boatbill, is an atypical member of the heron family. It is the only member of the genus Cochlearius and was formerly placed in a monotypic family, the Cochleariidae.
f: It is a nocturnal bird, and breeds semi-colonially in mangrove trees, laying two to four bluish-white eggs in a twig nest.

t: The green cochoa (Cochoa viridis) is a bird species that was variously placed with the thrushes of family Turdidae or the related Muscicapidae (Old World flycatchers).
f: It is considered closer to the former.

t: The bronzy inca (Coeligena coeligena) is a species of hummingbird in the "brilliants", tribe Heliantheini in subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The rainbow starfrontlet (Coeligena iris) is a species of hummingbird in the "brilliants", tribe Heliantheini in subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The buff-winged starfrontlet (Coeligena lutetiae) is a species of hummingbird in the "brilliants", tribe Heliantheini in subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The brown inca (Coeligena wilsoni) is a species of hummingbird in the "brilliants", tribe Heliantheini in subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The bananaquit (Coereba flaveola) is a species of passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. This small, active nectarivore is found in warmer parts of the Americas and is generally common.
f: Its name, Bananaquit, comes from its yellow color and the word "quit" for small tropical birds.
The black-necked woodpecker or black-necked flicker (Colaptes atricollis) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.

t: The northern flicker or common flicker (Colaptes auratus) is a medium-sized bird of the woodpecker family. It is native to most of North America, parts of Central America, Cuba, and the Cayman Islands, and is one of the few woodpecker species that migrate.
f: Many of these names derive from attempts to imitate some of its calls.

t: The northern flicker or common flicker (Colaptes auratus) is a medium-sized bird of the woodpecker family. It is native to most of North America, parts of Central America, Cuba, and the Cayman Islands, and is one of the few woodpecker species that migrate.
f: Many of these names derive from attempts to imitate some of its calls.

t: The grey-crowned woodpecker (Colaptes auricularis) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is endemic to western Mexico.

t: The campo flicker (Colaptes campestris) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Suriname, and Uruguay.
Yellow underwings distinguish the gilded flicker from the northern flicker (Colaptes auratus) found within the same region, which has red underwings.

t: Fernandina's flicker (Colaptes fernandinae), also known as the Cuban flicker, is a species of bird in the woodpecker family, Picidae.
f: Endemic to Cuba, it is severely threatened by habitat loss and is one of the most endangered species of woodpecker in the world.

t: The green-barred woodpecker or green-barred flicker (Colaptes melanochloros) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.

t: The Chilean flicker (Colaptes pitius) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Chile.

t: The spot-breasted woodpecker or spot-breasted flicker (Colaptes punctigula) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Panama and every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The crimson-mantled woodpecker (Colaptes rivolii) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The golden-olive woodpecker (Colaptes rubiginosus) is a species of bird in the subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found from Mexico south and east through Panama, in every mainland South American country except Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The Andean flicker (Colaptes rupicola) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The sparkling violetear (Colibri coruscans) is a species of hummingbird widespread in highlands of northern and western South America, including a large part of the Andes (from Argentina and northwards), the Venezuelan Coastal Range, and the Tepuis. It is highly vocal and territorial.
f: It occurs in a wide range of semi-open habitats, even in gardens and parks within major cities such as Quito, and is often the most common species of hummingbird in its range.

t: The lesser violetear (Colibri cyanotus), also known as the mountain violet-ear, is a medium-sized, metallic green hummingbird species commonly found in forested areas from Costa Rica south to the Andes and Argentina and east to Venezuela.
f: This species and the Mexican violetear were formerly considered as conspecific and named the 'green violetear'.

t: The breeding habitat is forest at altitudes between 400 and 1600 m, but the brown Violet-ear will spread widely into the lowlands when not nesting. It is replaced at higher altitudes by its relative, the lesser violetear (C. cyanotus), but their ranges overlap widely.
f: The song is a vigorous repetition of the chit call, and is delivered by up to several dozen breeding males in loose leks.

t: The white-vented violetear (Colibri serrirostris) is a species of hummingbird in the subfamily Polytminae, the mangoes. It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.
f: In April, 2024, one was also photographed at Batsu Gardens in Costa Rica.

t: The Mexican violetear (Colibri thalassinus) is a medium-sized, metallic green hummingbird species commonly found in forested areas from Mexico to Nicaragua.
f: This species, together with the lesser violetear were previously considered conspecific, and together called the green violetear.

t: The crested bobwhite (Colinus cristatus) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae. It is found in northern South America, extending through Panama to just reach Costa Rica.
f: It also occurs on Aruba and the Netherlands Antilles.

t: The Yucatan bobwhite or black-throated bobwhite (Colinus nigrogularis) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae. It is found in Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.
f: A specific example of occurrence is the Petenes mangroves of the Yucatan.

t: It is a member of the group of species known as New World quail (Odontophoridae). They were initially placed with the Old World quail in the pheasant family (Phasianidae), but are not particularly closely related.
f: The name "bobwhite" is an onomatopoeic derivation from its characteristic whistling call.

t: The white-backed mousebird (Colius colius) is a large species of mousebird. It is distributed in western and central regions of southern Africa from Namibia and southern Botswana eastwards to Central Transvaal and the eastern Cape.
f: This mousebird prefers scrubby dry habitats, such as thornveld, fynbos scrub and semi-desert.

t: It is found throughout most of Central, Eastern and Southern Africa.
f: The speckled mousebird (Colius striatus) is the largest species of mousebird, as well as one of the most common.

t: The plume-toed swiftlet (Collocalia affinis) is a small bird in the swift family Apodidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found on some eastern Indian Ocean islands, the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, and lowland Borneo.

t: Bower's shrikethrush (Colluricincla boweri), also known as the stripe-breasted shrike-thrush, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found on the southeast coast of Cape York Peninsula.

t: The grey shrikethrush or grey shrike-thrush (Colluricincla harmonica), formerly commonly known as grey thrush, is a songbird of Australasia. It is also found in New Guinea.
f: It is moderately common to common in most parts of Australia, but absent from the driest of the inland deserts.

The little shrikethrush or little shrike-thrush (Colluricincla megarhyncha) is a species of passerine bird in the family Pachycephalidae that is found in New Guinea as well as in north and east Australia.

t: The long-tailed tyrant (Colonia colonus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Central America from Honduras to Panama and in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The Patagonian tyrant (Colorhamphus parvirostris) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina and Chile.

t: The African olive pigeon or Rameron pigeon (Columba arquatrix) is a pigeon which is a resident breeding bird in much of eastern and southern Africa from Ethiopia to the Cape. It is locally common, although sizeable gaps in its distribution occur due to its habitat requirements.
f: Populations also are found in western Angola, southwestern Saudi Arabia and northern Yemen.

t: The eastern bronze-naped pigeon (Columba delegorguei), also known as Delegorgue's pigeon, is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. It is found in Angola, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, South Africa, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.
f: The species is named after the collector, Adulphe Delegorgue.

t: The speckled pigeon (Columba guinea), also known as the African rock pigeon or Guinea pigeon, is a pigeon that is a resident breeding bird in much of Africa south of the Sahara.
f: It is a common and widespread species in open habitats over much of its range, although there are sizable gaps in its distribution.

t: The western bronze-naped pigeon (Columba iriditorques) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae, part of the subgenus Turturoena. It is found in most countries of Africa.
f: A medium sized bird, it has a pale, broad terminal tail band which is noticeable on landing.

t: The black wood pigeon or Japanese wood pigeon (Columba janthina) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. It is found in East Asia, occurring mainly on offshore islands of the Pacific's Korea Strait, Philippine Sea and East China Sea around Japan, Korea, China, and Taiwan.
f: The species is in decline owing to habitat loss, habitat degradation, deforestation and hunting.

t: The lemon dove or cinnamon dove (Aplopelia larvata) is a species of bird in the pigeon family Columbidae found in montane forests of sub-Saharan Africa. Adults have a greenish-glossed neck and white markings on the head, and juveniles are rather more brown with pale feather fringe barring and have greyer facial markings.
f: The lemon dove has a generally brownish-grey plumage with a cinnamon brown breast.

t: The rock dove (Columba livia), also known as the common pigeon or rock pigeon (but see also Petrophassa), is a member of the bird family Columbidae (doves and pigeons). In common usage, it is often simply referred to as the "pigeon", although the rock dove is the wild form of the bird; the pigeons familiar to most people are the domesticated forms of the wild rock dove.
f: Habitats include various open and semi-open environments where they are able to forage on the ground.

t: The domestic pigeon (Columba livia "domestica" or Columba livia forma domestica) is a domesticated bird derived from the rock dove (Columba livia), of which it is also a subspecies. Although often termed a "subspecies", the domesticated pigeon does not constitute an accepted zoological subspecies of the rock dove, but a collection of over 350 breeds.
f: The rock dove is among the world's first birds to be domesticated; Mesopotamian cuneiform tablets mention the domestication of pigeons more than 5,000 years ago, as do Egyptian hieroglyphs.

t: The stock dove (Columba oenas) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae, the doves and pigeons. It is widely distributed in the western Palearctic, north to central Scandinavia and south to northwest Africa.
f: Western and southern populations are resident, while northeastern populations are migratory to avoid the colder winters there.

t: The common wood pigeon (Columba palumbus), also known simply as the wood pigeon, is a large pigeon native to the western Palearctic. It belongs to the genus Columba, which includes closely related species such as the rock dove (Columba livia).
f: It has a flexible diet, feeding mainly on plant material, including cereals, and is therefore considered an agricultural pest.

The afep pigeon (Columba unicincta), also known as the African woodpigeon or grey woodpigeon, is a member of the family Columbidae, native to the African tropical rainforest from Sierra Leone east to Uganda.
The metallic pigeon (Columba vitiensis) also known as white-throated pigeon, is a medium-sized bird up to 37 cm long, in the family Columbidae.

t: The Ecuadorian ground dove (Columbina buckleyi) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The croaking ground dove (Columbina cruziana) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The blue-eyed ground dove (Columbina cyanopis) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is endemic to the Cerrado region of Brazil.

t: The Inca dove or Mexican dove (Columbina inca) is a small New World dove. The species was first described by French surgeon and naturalist René Lesson in 1847.
f: It is a slender species, with a gray-brown body covered in feathers that resemble a scaled pattern.

t: The plain-breasted ground dove (Columbina minuta) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It lacks the scaled appearance to the feathers of the similar and typically more abundant common ground dove.

t: The common ground dove (Columbina passerina) is a small bird that inhabits the southern United States, parts of Central America, the Caribbean and northern South America. It is considered to be the smallest dove that inhabits the United States.
f: It is considered the smallest dove that inhabits the United States.

t: The Picui ground dove or Picui dove (Columbina picui) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: The scaled dove (Columbina squammata), also known as scaly dove, Ridgway's dove, mottled dove, and South American zebra dove, is found in Brazil, Bolivia, Argentina, Colombia, French Guiana, Paraguay, Trinidad and Tobago,Venezuela and Uruguay.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry shrubland, subtropical or tropical moist shrubland, subtropical or tropical seasonally wet or flooded lowland grassland, and heavily degraded former forest.

t: The ruddy ground dove (Columbina talpacoti) is a small New World tropical dove. It is a resident breeder from Mexico south to Brazil, Peru and Paraguay, and northern Argentina, and on Trinidad and Tobago.
f: Individual birds can sometimes be seen in the southwestern USA, from southern Texas to southernmost California, primarily during winter.
The scarlet-throated tanager (Compsothraupis loricata) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.

t: The black-faced cotinga (Conioptilon mcilhennyi) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The capped conebill (Conirostrum albifrons) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: This member of the tanager family is a resident breeder in South America from Colombia, Venezuela and Trinidad south and east to the Guianas, northeast Peru and Brazil.
f: The bicolored conebill (Conirostrum bicolor) is a small passerine bird.

t: The giant conebill (Conirostrum binghami) is a small passerine bird, one of the tanager family. It is closely related to the regular conebills Conirostrum though it differs in its larger size and nuthatch-like foraging habits.
f: Both parents incubate the eggs, feed the chicks and remove the fecal sacs.

t: The cinereous conebill (Conirostrum cinereum) is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist shrubland, subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: Its range extends from south-western Colombia et northern Chile and Bolivia.

t: The white-eared conebill (Conirostrum leucogenys) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Colombia, Panama, and Venezuela.
The pearly-breasted conebill (Conirostrum margaritae) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.

t: The rufous-browed conebill (Conirostrum rufum) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.
f: It is found in Colombia and far western Venezuela.

t: The blue-backed conebill (Conirostrum sitticolor) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae (South American tanagers). Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The chestnut-vented conebill (Conirostrum speciosum) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The tamarugo conebill (Conirostrum tamarugense) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It breeds in northern Chile and is a vagrant to southern Peru, and receives its name from the tamarugo, a type of shrub to which it is closely associated.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: Conocephalus brevipennis, the short-winged meadow katydid, is a species of meadow katydid in the family Tettigoniidae.
f: It is found in North America and the Caribbean.
Conocephalus fasciatus, the slender meadow katydid, is a species of katydid of the family Tettigoniidae that is native to the United States and Canada.

t: The white-ringed flycatcher (Conopias albovittatus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The lemon-browed flycatcher (Conopias cinchoneti) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Venezuela, and possibly Bolivia.

t: The yellow-throated flycatcher (Conopias parvus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, Venezuela, and possibly Bolivia.

t: The three-striped flycatcher (Conopias trivirgatus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The slaty gnateater (Conopophaga ardesiaca) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru.

t: The chestnut-belted gnateater (Conopophaga aurita) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae, the gnateaters. Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is found in the Amazon Basin of northern Brazil, southern Colombia and eastern Peru and Ecuador; also the Guianan countries of Guyana, Suriname and eastern French Guiana.

t: The chestnut-crowned gnateater (Conopophaga castaneiceps) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The Ceará Gnateater or Caatinga Gnateater (Conopophaga cearae) is a passerine bird of the gnateater family, Conopophagidae. It is found in forest understory and bushes in northeastern Brazil.
f: The Ceara Gnateater is locally called "chupa-dente", or "tooth-sucker" in Portuguese due to the sound it produces when it vocalizes.

t: The rufous gnateater (Conopophaga lineata) is a passerine bird of the gnateater family, Conopophagidae. It is found in forest understory and bushes in eastern Brazil from Rio Grande do Sul north to central Brazil.
f: It is often elusive and hard to see, but is commoner and less shy than other gnateaters.
The black-bellied gnateater (Conopophaga melanogaster) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae.

t: The black-cheeked gnateater (Conopophaga melanops) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae endemic to Brazil.
f: The male is distinguished by its orange crown, black face and white throat, while the female has brown plumage.

t: The ash-throated gnateater (Conopophaga peruviana) is a species of bird in the family Conopophagidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The rufous-banded honeyeater (Conopophila albogularis) is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. It is found in the Aru Islands, New Guinea and northern Australia.
f: The rufous-banded honeyeater is considered one of the most common small birds in the suburban ecosystem of Darwin, Australia, notable because its lack of introduced bird species.

t: The great parrotbill (Paradoxornis aemodius) is a bird species the Paradoxornithidae family. It was previously placed in a monotypic genus, the Conostoma.
f: It is found in Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, and Nepal.

t: The black-and-white tanager (Conothraupis speculigera) is a bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found primarily in Ecuador and Peru but in migration and as a vagrant has appeared in several other countries.

t: The Cuban pewee or crescent-eyed pewee (Contopus caribaeus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Cuba and the Bahamas.

t: The southern tropical pewee (Contopus cinereus) is a small passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The olive-sided flycatcher (Contopus cooperi) is a small to medium sized passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatcher family. It is an agile flyer and mainly consumes flying insects caught in flight.
f: It is a migratory species that travels from South America to North America to breed during the summer.

t: The smoke-colored pewee (Contopus fumigatus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae. Smoke-colored pewees are found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, and Venezuela.
f: The species is characterized by a uniform dusky-grey plumage.

t: The dark pewee (Contopus lugubris) is a small passerine bird in the tyrant flycatcher family. It is endemic to the Talamancan montane forests of Costa Rica and western Panama.
f: The eggs are undescribed, but the female builds the nest, lays only two eggs and incubates the eggs for 15–16 days before they hatch.

t: The blackish pewee (Contopus nigrescens) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Brazil, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, and possibly Colombia.

t: The greater pewee (Contopus pertinax), formerly known as Coues's flycatcher, is a passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found from Arizona and New Mexico to Nicaragua.
The western wood pewee (Contopus sordidulus) is a small tyrant flycatcher.

t: The eastern wood pewee (Contopus virens) is a small tyrant flycatcher from North, Central and South America. This bird and the western wood pewee (C. sordidulus) were formerly considered a single species.
f: The two species are virtually identical in appearance, and can be distinguished most easily by their calls.

t: The Andaman shama (Copsychus albiventris) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is endemic to the Andaman Islands.
f: It is considered a restricted-range species because it occurs only within this island group.
The Madagascar magpie-robin (Copsychus albospecularis) is a species of chat in the Old World flycatcher family, Muscicapidae.

t: The Black shama (Copsychus cebuensis) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forest, tropical moist shrubland, and plantations.
f: It is endemic to the island of Cebu, Philippines where it is known locally as "Siloy".

t: The Indian robin (Copsychus fulicatus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Muscicapidae. The males of the northern subspecies have brown backs whose extent gradually reduces southwards, with the males of the southern subspecies having all-black backs.
f: It is widespread in the Indian subcontinent and ranges across Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

t: The white-browed shama (Copsychus luzoniensis) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. The Visayan shama (C. superciliaris), formerly considered a subspecies, was split as a distinct species in 2021.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines found only on the islands of Luzon, Marinduque and the Polillo Islands.

t: The white-rumped shama (Copsychus malabaricus) is a passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. The Larwo shama, the Kangean shama and the Sri Lanka shama were formerly considered to be conspecific with the white-rumped shama.
f: It was once considered the same species as the Larwo, Kangean, and Sri Lanka shamas.

t: The Philippine magpie-robin (Copsychus mindanensis) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It was formerly a subspecies of Oriental magpie-robin but was designated as its own species.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines.

t: The white-vented shama (Copsychus niger) is a species of bird in the chat and flycatcher family Muscicapidae. Along with the Black shama, White-browed shama and Visayan shama are the four endemic shamas of the country.
f: It is endemic to the Palawan, Balabac and Calamian islands in the Philippines.

t: The rufous-tailed shama (Copsychus pyrropygus) is a species of passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. It is found in extreme southern Thailand, Malaysia, Sumatra, and Borneo, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical swamps.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The Oriental magpie-robin (Copsychus saularis) is a small passerine bird that was formerly classed as a member of the thrush family Turdidae, but now considered an Old World flycatcher. The males are distinctive black and white birds with a long tail that is held upright as they forage on the ground or perch conspicuously.
f: It is particularly well known for its songs and is popular as cagebirds.

t: The Abyssinian roller (Coracias abyssinicus), or Senegal roller, is a member of the roller family of birds which breeds across tropical Africa in a belt south of the Sahara, known as the Sahel.
f: It is resident in the southern part of its range, but northern breeding populations are short-distance migrants, moving further south after the wet season.

t: The Indian roller (Coracias benghalensis) is a bird of the family Coraciidae. It is 30–34 cm (12–13 in) long with a wingspan of 65–74 cm (26–29 in) and weighs 166–176 g (5.9–6.2 oz).
f: The species is best known for the aerobatic displays of males during the breeding season.

t: The lilac-breasted roller (Coracias caudatus) is an African bird of the roller family, Coraciidae. It is widely distributed in Southern and Eastern Africa, and is a vagrant to the southern Arabian Peninsula.
f: This species is unofficially considered the national bird of Kenya.

t: The European roller (Coracias garrulus) is the only member of the roller family Coraciidae breeding in Europe. Its range extends into the Maghreb, West Asia and Central Asia.
f: It usually nests in tree holes.

t: The grey cuckooshrike (Ceblepyris caesius) is a species of bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae. There are two subspecies that occur in forest patches of southern and central Africa respectively.
f: It is a medium-sized forest bird, with grey to blue-grey plumage and large black eyes.

t: The Madagascar cuckooshrike (Ceblepyris cinereus), also known as the ashy cuckooshrike, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae. It is found in Madagascar, and Mayotte.
f: The Comoros cuckooshrike (Ceblepyris cucullatus) is sometimes considered a distinct species.

t: The barred cuckooshrike (Coracina lineata), also called the yellow-eyed cuckooshrike, is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.
f: It is found in eastern Australia, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, and Solomon Islands.

t: The hooded cuckooshrike (Coracina longicauda) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in the New Guinea Highlands.

t: The Indian cuckooshrike (Coracina macei) is a species of bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae that is found on the Indian subcontinent.
f: Formerly under the English name "large cuckooshrike" this species included many subspecies and had a large range that included Southeast Asia.

t: The black-faced cuckooshrike (Coracina novaehollandiae) is a common omnivorous passerine bird native to Australia and southern New Guinea. It has a protected status in New South Wales, under the National Parks and Wildlife Act, 1974.
f: But they can also occur in urban areas, and are a fairly common sight on power lines in Australian cities such as Sydney and Perth.

t: The white-bellied cuckooshrike (Coracina papuensis) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.
f: It is found in Australia, the Moluccas, New Guinea and the Solomon Islands.

t: The white-breasted cuckooshrike (Ceblepyris pectoralis) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and dry savanna.
f: The species forages at mid-canopy level and is typically found alone or in pairs.

t: The bar-bellied cuckooshrike (Coracina striata) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae. The plumage varies among the subspecies, with different amounts of barring on the underparts.
f: It is found in Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Philippines, and its natural habitats include mangrove forest, dry forest, swamp forest, and secondary forest.

t: The lesser vasa parrot or black parrot (Coracopsis nigra) is a black coloured parrot endemic to most of Madagascar. It is one of four species of vasa parrots, the others being the greater vasa parrot (C. vasa), the Seychelles black parrot (C. barklyi), and the Comoros black parrot (C. sibilans).
f: They build their nests in tree hollows and go through courtship in February.

t: The greater vasa parrot (Coracopsis vasa) is one of two species of vasa parrot, the other being the lesser vasa parrot (C. nigra).
f: The greater vasa parrot can be found throughout Madagascar and the Comoros.

t: Although a common and widespread species, it has a somewhat more restricted distribution than its compatriot, the turkey vulture, which breeds well into Canada and all the way south to Tierra del Fuego. It is the only extant member of the genus Coragyps, which is in the family Cathartidae.
f: Lacking a syrinx—the vocal organ of birds—its only vocalizations are grunts or low hisses.

t: The white-ruffed manakin (Corapipo altera) is a sub-oscine (Tyranni), passerine bird in the manakin family. It is a resident breeder in the tropical New World from eastern Honduras to northwestern Colombia.
f: At breeding time, males are involved in lekking behaviour on the forest floor during which they puff out their neck feathers.

t: The white-throated manakin (Corapipo gutturalis) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The white-winged chough (Corcorax melanorhamphos) is one of only two surviving species of the Australian mud-nest builders family, Corcoracidae, and is the only member of the genus Corcorax.
f: It is native to southern and eastern Australia and is an example of convergent evolution as it is only distantly related to the European choughs that it closely resembles in shape, and for which it was named.

t: The white-throated treecreeper (Cormobates leucophaea) is an Australian treecreeper found in the forests of eastern Australia. The Dilmun is the totem of Worimi women.
f: It is also called Dilmun in the Gathang language of the Worimi people, who reside in eastern Port Stephens and Great Lakes regions of coastal New South Wales, Australia.

t: The Papuan treecreeper (Cormobates placens) is a species of bird in the family Climacteridae. It was previously considered a subspecies of the white-throated treecreeper (C. leucophaea).
f: It is found in the highlands of New Guinea.

t: The ruby-crowned kinglet (Corthylio calendula) is a very small passerine bird found throughout North America. It is a member of the kinglet family.
f: It is one of the smallest songbirds in North America.

t: The white-necked raven (Corvus albicollis), also known as the collared raven, is a species of raven native to eastern and southern Africa.
f: It is somewhat smaller (50–54 cm in length) than the common raven or its nearest relative, the thick-billed raven C. crassirostris.

t: The pied crow (Corvus albus) is a widely distributed African bird species in the crow genus of the family Corvidae. Its behaviour, though, is more typical of the Eurasian carrion crows, and it may be a modern link (along with the Somali crow) between the Eurasian crows and the common raven.
f: Structurally, the pied crow is better thought of as a small crow-sized raven, especially as it can hybridise with the Somali crow (dwarf raven) where their ranges meet in the Horn of Africa.

t: The Cape crow or black crow (Corvus capensis) is slightly larger (48–50 cm in length) than the carrion crow and is completely black with a slight gloss of purple in its feathers. It also has proportionately longer legs, wings, and tail, and has a much longer, slimmer bill that seems to be adapted for probing into the ground for invertebrates.
f: The head feathers have a coppery-purple gloss and the throat feathers are quite long and fluffed out in some calls and displays.

t: The American crow (Corvus brachyrhynchos) is a large passerine bird species of the family Corvidae. It is a common bird found throughout much of North America, only absent from the tundra biome.
f: It is highly intelligent, similar to other Corvidae, and is adaptable to human environments.

t: The common raven or northern raven (Corvus corax) is a large all-black passerine bird. It is the most widely distributed of all corvids, found across the Northern Hemisphere.
f: Although their typical lifespan is considerably shorter, common ravens can live more than 23 years in the wild.

t: The hooded crow (Corvus cornix), also colloquially called just hoodie, is a Eurasian bird subspecies of the carrion crow (Corvus corone) in the genus Corvus. Widely distributed, it is found across Northern, Eastern, and Southeastern Europe, as well as parts of the Middle East.
f: It is an ashy-grey bird with black head, throat, wings, tail, and thigh feathers, as well as a black bill, eyes, and feet.

t: The carrion crow (Corvus corone) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic. Along with the hooded crow (Corvus cornix), the carrion crow occupies a similar ecological niche in Eurasia to the American crow (Corvus brachyrhynchos) in North America.
f: The two species look very similar to one another, but can be differentiated by size, as the carrion crow is larger and of a stockier build compared to the American crow.

t: The Australian raven (Corvus coronoides) is a passerine corvid bird native to Australia. Measuring 46–53 centimetres (18–21 in) in length, it has an all-black plumage, beak and mouth, as well as strong, greyish-black legs and feet.
f: The nest is a bowl-shaped structure of sticks sited high in a tree, or occasionally in a man-made structure such as a windmill or other building.
The Chihuahuan raven (Corvus cryptoleucus) is a species in the family Corvidae that is native to the United States and Mexico.

t: The Daurian jackdaw (Coloeus dauuricus) is a bird in the crow family, Corvidae, native to eastern Asia. It is closely related to the western jackdaw.
f: The name derives from the Dauria region of eastern Russia.

t: The Sunda crow (Corvus enca) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae that is found in South-East Asia, from Malaysia to Borneo. The Sunda crow is part of the Corvus enca species complex, which was formerly treated as a single species and known as the slender-billed crow.
f: The violet crow was also once included, but has been shown to be distinct genetically and separated as Corvus violaceus.

t: The Flores crow (Corvus florensis) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The rook (Corvus frugilegus) is a member of the family Corvidae in the passerine order of birds. It is found in the Palearctic, its range extending from Scandinavia and western Europe to eastern Siberia.
f: Rooks nest collectively in the tops of tall trees, often close to farms or villages; the groups of nests are known as rookeries.

t: The Hawaiian crow or ʻalalā (Corvus hawaiiensis) is a species of bird in the crow family, Corvidae, that is currently extinct in the wild, though reintroduction programs are underway. It is about the size of the carrion crow at 48–50 cm (19–20 in) in length, but with more rounded wings and a much thicker bill.
f: The species is known for its strong flying ability and resourcefulness, and the reasons for its various extirpations are not fully understood.
The Tamaulipas crow (Corvus imparatus) is a crow found in northeastern Mexico and southern Texas.

t: The Jamaican crow (Corvus jamaicensis) is a comparatively small corvid (35–38 cm in length).
f: It shares several key morphological features with two other West Indian species, the Cuban crow (Corvus nasicus) and the white-necked crow (Corvus leucognaphalus) of Hispaniola, which are very closely related to it.
The white-necked crow (Corvus leucognaphalus) is the largest of the four Caribbean corvids.

t: The large-billed crow (Corvus macrorhynchos), formerly referred to widely as the jungle crow, is a widespread Asian species of crow. It has a large bill, which is the source of its scientific name macrorhynchos (Ancient Greek for "long-billed") and it is sometimes known by the common name thick-billed crow.
f: It is very adaptable and is able to survive on a wide range of food sources, making it capable of colonizing new areas, due to which it is often considered a nuisance, especially on islands.

t: The little raven (Corvus mellori) is a species of the family Corvidae that is native to southeastern Australia. An adult individual is about 48–50 cm (19–19.5 in) in length, with completely black plumage, beak, and legs; as with all Australian species of Corvus, the black feathers have a grey base, and the iris of the adult bird is white .
f: Although the little raven was first named by Gregory Mathews in 1912, it was only in 1967 that there was consensus to separate it from the Australian raven (C. coronoides) as a distinct species.

t: The western jackdaw (Coloeus monedula), also known as the Eurasian jackdaw, the European jackdaw, or simply the jackdaw, is a passerine bird in the crow family. It is found across Europe, western Asia and western North Africa; it is mostly resident, although northern and eastern populations migrate south in the winter.
f: The common name derives from the word jack, denoting "small", and daw, a less common synonym for "jackdaw", and the native English name for the bird.
The Cuban crow (Corvus nasicus) is a crow species native to the northern Caribbean.

t: The Torresian crow (Corvus orru), also called the Australian crow or Papuan crow, is a passerine bird in the crow family native to the north and west of Australia and nearby islands in Indonesia and Papua New Guinea. The species has a black plumage, beak and mouth with white irises.
f: The base of the feathers on the head and neck are white.
The fish crow (Corvus ossifragus) is a species of crow associated with wetland habitats in the eastern and southeastern United States.
The Hispaniolan palm crow (Corvus palmarum) is a relatively small corvid endemic to the Caribbean island of Hispaniola, which is shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic.
The fan-tailed raven (Corvus rhipidurus) is a passerine bird of the crow family native to Eastern Africa and the Arabian Peninsula.

t: The brown-necked raven (Corvus ruficollis) is a larger bird (52–56 cm in length) than the carrion crow though not as large as the common raven. It has similar proportions to the common raven but the bill is not so large or deep and the wings tend to be a little more pointed in profile.
f: The feathers of this species often fade quite quickly to a brownish black (even the truly black feathers) and the bird can look distinctly brown by the time it moults.
The Sinaloa crow (Corvus sinaloae) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays.

t: The house crow (Corvus splendens), also known as the Indian, greynecked, Ceylon or Colombo crow, is a common bird of the crow family that is of Asian origin but now found in many parts of the world, where they arrived assisted by shipping. It is between the jackdaw and the carrion crow in size (40 cm (16 in) in length) but is slimmer than either.
f: The wings, tail and legs are black.

t: The forest raven (Corvus tasmanicus), also commonly known as the Tasmanian raven, is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae native to Tasmania and parts of southern Victoria, such as Wilsons Promontory and Portland. Populations are also found in parts of New South Wales, including Dorrigo and Armidale.
f: An omnivorous and opportunistic feeder, the forest raven eats a wide variety of plant and animal material, as well as food waste from urban areas and roadkill.

t: The tail feathers are relatively long and graduated and the legs are relatively short. The overall colouring of the adult bird is black with randomly bleached wing and tail feathers.
f: The bill is unusual too in being very variable, bluish on upper mandible and pinkish-white on the lower in some specimens, while on others the whole bill is pinkish white with a darker tip.

t: The piping crow (Corvus typicus) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is endemic to Sulawesi in Indonesia.

t: The long-billed crow (Corvus validus) is a crow that is endemic to the Northern Maluku Islands. It is classified by the International Union for Conservation of Nature as a "near-threatened species".
f: This crow is large with glossy plumage, a large bill and white irises.

t: The dusky broadbill (Corydon sumatranus) is a species of bird in the family Eurylaimidae, the broadbills. It is native to Southeast Asia.
f: It may be slowly declining due to habitat loss, especially from logging, but it has a large enough range that it is still considered to be a least-concern species.

t: The black-masked finch (Coryphaspiza melanotis) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Peru.

t: The lark-like brushrunner (Coryphistera alaudina) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The red pileated finch (Coryphospingus cucullatus), also known as the red-crested finch, is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, and possibly Guyana and Suriname.

t: The grey pileated finch (Coryphospingus pileatus), also known as the pileated finch, is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Venezuela, and possibly Bolivia and French Guiana.

t: The great blue turaco (Corythaeola cristata) is a bird species of the family Musophagidae. It has predominantly grey-blue plumage with an upright blue-black crest around 10 cm (3.9 in) high.
f: At 70–76 cm (28–30 in) in length, it is the largest species of turaco.

t: The grey go-away-bird (Crinifer concolor), also known as grey lourie, grey loerie, or kwêvoël, is a bold and common turaco of the southern Afrotropics. They are present in arid to moist, open woodlands and thorn savanna, especially near surface water.
f: Within their range, their unique appearance and habits preclude confusion with other bird species.
The white-bellied go-away-bird (Crinifer leucogaster) is a bird of eastern Africa in the family Musophagidae, commonly known as turacos.

t: The southern antpipit (Corythopis delalandi) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The ringed antpipit (Corythopis torquatus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
