f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The malachite kingfisher (Corythornis cristatus) is a river kingfisher which is widely distributed in Africa south of the Sahara.
f: It is largely resident except for seasonal climate-related movements.

t: The coscoroba swan (Coscoroba coscoroba) is a species of waterfowl in the subfamily Anserinae of the family Anatidae. It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay, Uruguay, and the Falkland Islands.
f: It is one of South America's largest species of waterfowl.

t: The white-crowned robin-chat (Cossypha albicapillus) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its range extends mainly across the western region of the Sudanian savanna.
f: It has typically been assumed to be monogamous.

t: The olive-flanked ground robin (Dessonornis anomalus), also known as the olive-flanked robin-chat, is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitat is tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Malawi, and Mozambique.

t: Archer's ground robin or Archer's robin-chat, (Dessonornis archeri) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is found in the Albertine Rift montane forests.
f: The bird's common name commemorates the British explorer and colonial official Sir Geoffrey Francis Archer.

t: The Cape robin-chat (Dessonornis caffer) is a small passerine bird of the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. It has a disjunct range from South Sudan to South Africa.
f: It is an accomplished songster like other robin-chats, but is rather less colourful than most, and frequents either drier settings or higher altitudes.

t: The blue-shouldered robin-chat (Cossypha cyanocampter) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is widespread across the African tropical rainforest.

t: The chorister robin-chat (Cossypha dichroa) (previously known as the chorister robin) is a species of bird in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. Its distribution stretches from the southern Western Cape through the Eastern Cape, KwaZulu-Natal, and Mpumalanga to northern Limpopo.
f: It is found in South Africa and Eswatini.

t: The white-browed robin-chat (Cossypha heuglini), also known as Heuglin's robin, is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. The IUCN classifies it as a least-concern species.
f: Found in east, central and southern Africa, its natural habitats include riverine forest and thickets, and it is also found near humans.

t: The white-throated robin-chat or white-throated robin (Dessonornis humeralis) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitats are dry savannah and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.
f: It is endemic to Botswana, Eswatini, Mozambique, South Africa, and Zimbabwe.

t: The red-capped robin-chat or Natal robin (Cossypha natalensis) is a species of passerine bird belonging to the family Muscicapidae.
f: This species is found in central and eastern Sub-Saharan Africa.

t: The snowy-crowned robin-chat (Cossypha niveicapilla) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is also known as the snowy-headed robin-chat.
f: Its disjunct range extends across the northern half of Sub-Saharan Africa (rare in the Horn of Africa).

t: The grey-winged robin-chat or grey-winged akalat (Sheppardia polioptera) is a bird in the family Muscicapidae. The species was first described by Anton Reichenow in 1892.
f: It is found in Angola, Burundi, Cameroon, the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ivory Coast, Guinea, Kenya, Liberia, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia.

t: Rüppell's robin-chat (Cossypha semirufa) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae, that is native to the Afrotropics.
f: It is named for the German naturalist Eduard Rüppell.
The yellow rail (Coturnicops noveboracensis) is a small secretive marsh bird of the family Rallidae that is found in North America.

The rain quail or black-breasted quail (Coturnix coromandelica) is a species of quail found in the Indian Sub-continent and South-east Asia; its range including Pakistan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam.

t: The common quail (Coturnix coturnix) or European quail is a small ground-nesting game bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae. With its characteristic call of three repeated chirps (repeated three times in quick succession), this species of quail is more often heard than seen.
f: It is mainly migratory, breeding in the Palearctic and wintering in Africa and southern India.

t: The harlequin quail (Coturnix delegorguei) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae. It occurs in sub-Saharan Africa and in the Arabian Peninsula.
f: The species is named after the collector, Adulphe Delegorgue.

t: The Japanese quail (Coturnix japonica), also known as the coturnix quail, is a species of Old World quail found in East Asia. First considered a subspecies of the common quail, it is now considered as a separate species.
f: The Japanese quail has played an active role in the lives of humanity since the 12th century, and continues to play major roles in industry and scientific research.

t: The stubble quail (Coturnix pectoralis), whose other common names include grey quail and pectoral quail, is a species of Old World quail native to Australia. The species is widespread in mainland Australia and is listed as least concern by the IUCN, and can be found throughout all states and territories of Australia except Tasmania.
f: It is the only native upland game bird that can be legally hunted in Australia, though with strict game law restrictions.

t: The blue coua (Coua caerulea) is a species of bird in the cuckoo family, Cuculidae.
f: It is endemic to the island of Madagascar.

t: Coquerel's coua (Coua coquereli) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. Its habitat is subtropical or tropical dry forests.
f: It was named in 1867 by the French naturalist Alfred Grandidier in honor of the French navy surgeon and naturalist Charles Coquerel.

t: The crested coua (Coua cristata) is a common medium-sized bird member of the cuckoo family, Cuculidae. The crested coua is a weak flyer, so it will often be observed hopping from branch to branch in high canopies.
f: It is endemic to Madagascar, mainly found in the coastal regions of the island.

t: The giant coua (Coua gigas) is a bird species from the Coua genus in the cuckoo family that is endemic to the dry forests of western and southern Madagascar. The genus Coua contains 10 species, more than any other genus in Madagascar.
f: Couas probably originated from a particular Asian ground-cuckoo.

t: The red-fronted coua (Coua reynaudii) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae.
f: Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

t: The red-capped coua (Coua ruficeps) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is endemic to northwest Madagascar.
The red-breasted coua (Coua serriana) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae.

t: The hooded butcherbird (Cracticus cassicus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Artamidae.
f: Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

t: The pied butcherbird (Cracticus nigrogularis) is a songbird native to Australia. Initially described by John Gould in 1837, it is a black-and-white bird 28 to 32 cm (11 to 12.5 in) long with a long, hooked bill.
f: It nests in trees, constructing a cup-shaped structure out of sticks and laying two to five eggs.

t: The black butcherbird (Melloria quoyi) is a species of butcherbird in the family Artamidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest.
f: It is found in Australia, Indonesia, and Papua New Guinea.

t: The grey butcherbird (Cracticus torquatus) is a widely distributed species endemic to Australia. It occurs in a range of different habitats including arid, semi-arid and temperate zones.
f: It appears to be adapting well to city living, and can be encountered in the suburbs of many Australian cities including Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney and Hobart.
The creamy-crested spinetail (Cranioleuca albicapilla) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The light-crowned spinetail (Cranioleuca albiceps) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru.

t: The line-cheeked spinetail (Cranioleuca antisiensis) is an arboreal species of bird in the ovenbird family Furnariidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, woodland and scrub.
f: It is a common species in the Andes in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The ash-browed spinetail (Cranioleuca curtata) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The tepui spinetail (Cranioleuca demissa) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Guyana, and Venezuela.

t: The red-faced spinetail (Cranioleuca erythrops) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, and Panama.

t: The speckled spinetail (Thripophaga gutturata) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The streak-capped spinetail (Cranioleuca hellmayri) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.
The Marcapata spinetail (Cranioleuca marcapatae) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The olive spinetail (Cranioleuca obsoleta) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.
The pallid spinetail (Cranioleuca pallida) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The stripe-crowned spinetail (Cranioleuca pyrrhophia) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
The grey-headed spinetail (Cranioleuca semicinerea) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The crested spinetail (Cranioleuca subcristata) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: Parker's spinetail (Cranioleuca vulpecula) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The rusty-backed spinetail (Cranioleuca vulpina) is a Neotropical species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Paraguay, Peru, Venezuela, and possibly Guyana.

t: The rusty mouse-warbler (Origma murina), is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Indonesia and Papua New Guinea, in a 1,270,000 km² distribution.

t: The mountain mouse-warbler (Origma robusta) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. This species was formerly placed in the genus Crateroscelis, but following the publication of a molecular phylogenetic study of the scrubwrens and mouse-warblers in 2018, it was moved to the genus Origma.
f: It is found in Indonesia and Papua New Guinea, where its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
The blue-billed curassow (Crax alberti) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.

t: The black curassow (Crax alector), also known as the smooth-billed curassow and the crested curassow, is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found in humid forests in northern South America in Colombia, Venezuela, the Guianas including Suriname, and far northern Brazil, and is introduced to Bahamas, Cuba, Jamaica, Haiti, Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico and Lesser Antilles.

t: The bare-faced curassow (Crax fasciolata) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, curassows, etc. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is found in Brazil, Paraguay, and eastern Bolivia, and extreme northeast Argentina, in the cerrado, pantanal, and the southeastern region of the Amazon basin.

t: The great curassow (Crax rubra) is a large, pheasant-like bird from the Neotropical rainforests, its range extending from eastern Mexico, through Central America to western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador. Male birds are black with curly crests and yellow beaks; females come in three colour morphs, barred, rufous and black.
f: These birds form small groups, foraging mainly on the ground for fruits and arthropods, and the occasional small vertebrate, but they roost and nest in trees.

t: The swallow-tailed gull (Creagrus furcatus) is an equatorial seabird in the gull family, Laridae. It is the only species in the genus Creagrus, which derives from the Latin Creagra and the Greek kreourgos which means butcher, also from kreas, meat; according to Jobling it would mean "hook for meat" referring to the hooked bill of this species.
f: It is the only fully nocturnal gull and seabird in the world, preying on squid and small fish which rise to the surface at night to feed on plankton.

t: The wattled starling (Creatophora cinerea) is a nomadic resident bird in eastern and southern Africa. It is a species of grassland, open woodland, and cultivation.
f: Its bare face patches and ability to open-bill feed in grassland are unique amongst African starlings.

t: The corn crake, corncrake or landrail (Crex crex) is a bird in the rail family. It breeds in Europe and Asia as far east as western China, and migrates to Africa for the Northern Hemisphere's winter.
f: The corn crake is omnivorous but mainly feeds on invertebrates, the occasional small frog or mammal, and plant material including grass seed and cereal grain.

t: The western plantain-eater (Crinifer piscator), also known as the grey plantain-eater or western grey plantain-eater, is a large member of the turaco family, a group of large arboreal passerine-like birds restricted to Africa. This species is a resident breeder in open woodland habitats in tropical west Africa.
f: It lays two or three eggs in a tree platform nest.

t: The western bearded greenbul (Criniger barbatus) is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
The red-tailed greenbul (Criniger calurus), also known as the red-tailed bulbul, is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae, native to the African tropical rainforest.

t: The eastern bearded greenbul (Criniger chloronotus) is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found from south-eastern Nigeria to Central African Republic, north-eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Congo and extreme north-western Angola.
The white-throated canary (Crithagra albogularis) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae.
The black-throated canary (Crithagra atrogularis), also known as the black-throated seedeater, is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae.

t: The southern grosbeak-canary, also known as Kenya grosbeak-canary (Crithagra buchanani) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.
f: It is found in Kenya and Tanzania.

t: The white-bellied canary (Crithagra dorsostriata) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae. Its natural habitat is dry savanna.
f: It is found in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: The yellow canary (Crithagra flaviventris) is a small passerine bird in the true finch family.
f: It is a resident breeder in much of the western and central regions of southern Africa and has been introduced to Ascension and St Helena islands.

t: The streaky-headed seedeater or streaky-headed canary (Crithagra gularis) is a small passerine bird in the finch family. Its presence in an area is revealed foremost by its callnotes.
f: It is an unobtrusive but widespread species in suitable habitats of southern Africa.

t: The southern citril (Crithagra hyposticta or Serinus hyposticus) is a species of finch in the Fringillidae family. The southern citril was formerly placed in the genus Serinus but phylogenetic analysis using mitochondrial and nuclear DNA sequences found that the genus was polyphyletic.
f: It is endemic to the eastern Afromontane.

t: The Yemen serin (Crithagra menachensis) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae. The Yemen serin was formerly placed in the genus Serinus but phylogenetic analysis using mitochondrial and nuclear DNA sequences found that the genus was polyphyletic.
f: It is found in Oman, Saudi Arabia, and Yemen.

t: The yellow-fronted canary (Crithagra mozambica) is a small passerine bird in the finch family. This bird is a resident breeder in Africa south of the Sahara Desert.
f: It is sometimes known in aviculture as the green singing finch or the green singer.

t: Reichenow's seedeater (Crithagra reichenowi) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae. The Reichenow's seedeater was formerly placed in the genus Serinus but phylogenetic analysis using mitochondrial and nuclear DNA sequences found that the genus was polyphyletic.
f: It is sometimes considered conspecific with the black-throated canary.

t: The forest canary (Crithagra scotops) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in South Africa and Eswatini.

t: The streaky seedeater (Crithagra striolata) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae.
f: It is native to the eastern Afromontane.

t: The brimstone canary or bully canary (Crithagra sulphurata) is a small passerine bird in the finch family. It is a resident breeder in central and southern Africa.
f: It is not truly migratory, but undertakes some seasonal movements.

t: The Madagascan yellowbrow (Crossleyia xanthophrys), also known as the yellow-browed oxylabes, is a species of Malagasy warbler, formerly placed in the family Sylviidae. Found only in Madagascar, it was previously the sole member of the genus Crossleyia until the rare and endangered dusky tetraka (formerly in the genus Xanthomixis) was moved to Crossleyia based on a molecular genetic study published online in 2019.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The smooth-billed ani (Crotophaga ani) is a bird in the cuckoo family. It was introduced to Galápagos around the 1960s and is potentially impacting native and endemic species across the archipelago.
f: It is a resident breeding species from southern Florida, the Caribbean, parts of Central America, south to western Ecuador, Brazil, northern Argentina and southern Chile.

t: The greater ani (Crotophaga major) is a bird in the cuckoo family. It is found through tropical South America south to northern Argentina.
f: It is sometimes referred to as the black cuckoo.

t: The groove-billed ani (Crotophaga sulcirostris) is a tropical bird in the cuckoo family with a long tail and a large, curved beak. It is a resident species throughout most of its range, from southern Texas, central Mexico and The Bahamas, through Central America, to northern Colombia and Venezuela, and coastal Ecuador and Peru.
f: It only retreats from the northern limits of its range in Texas and northern Mexico during winter.

t: The racket-tailed treepie (Crypsirina temia) is an Asian treepie, a member of the crow family, Corvidae. It has a velvety-black forehead of short, plush black feathers with the rest of the bird being an oily green colour, though appearing black in dim light.
f: It moves through the trees with great agility and uses its remarkable tail as a balancing organ.

t: Victorin's warbler (Cryptillas victorini) or Victorin's scrub warbler, is a species of African warbler, formerly placed in the family Sylviidae. It was recently split from the genus Bradypterus and now belongs to a monotypic genus Cryptillas.
f: It is endemic to the fynbos of South Africa's coastal Afromontane area.

t: The plumbeous hawk (Cryptoleucopteryx plumbea) is a species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae belonging to the monotypic genus Cryptoleucopteryx.
f: It ranges 33 to 37 cm in length and 71 to 79 cm in wingspan.

t: The speckle-breasted antpitta (Cryptopezus nattereri) is a species of bird in the family Grallariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The green manakin (Cryptopipo holochlora) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The red-faced crimsonwing (Cryptospiza reichenovii) is a common species of estrildid finch found in Africa. It is native to the Afromontane.
f: It has an estimated global extent of occurrence of 390,000 km2.

t: The cryptic warbler (Cryptosylvicola randrianasoloi) is a species of Malagasy warbler in the family Bernieridae. It was formerly placed in the Old World warbler family Sylviidae.
f: It was first discovered in 1992 near the Analamazaotra Special Reserve in Madagascar, and is endemic to the forests on the eastern part of island between Anjanaharibe-Sud Special Reserve and Andohahela National Park.
The black-capped tinamou (Crypturellus atrocapillus) is a type of tinamou commonly found in the moist forest lowlands in subtropical and tropical regions.
Bartlett's tinamou (Crypturellus bartletti) is a type of tinamou found in lowland forest in South America.
The slaty-breasted tinamou or Boucard's tinamou (Crypturellus boucardi) is a type of tinamou commonly found in lowland moist forests of Mexico and Central America.

t: The cinereous tinamou (Crypturellus cinereus), also known as brushland tinamou, is a type of ground bird found in swamp and lowland forests in northern South America. They have some localized names that have been used by the indigenous people such as in Amazonas where they are called inambu-pixuna, and in Pará, Brazil where they are called nambu-sujo.
f: They are part of the oldest families of the world today and have fossils discovered dating back tens of millions of years.
The thicket tinamou or rufescent tinamou (Crypturellus cinnamomeus) is a type of tinamou commonly found in moist forests in subtropical and tropical central Mexico.

t: The grey-legged tinamou (Crypturellus duidae), alternatively, the gray-legged tinamou, is a small ground-dwelling bird endemic to the neotropics.
f: It is a rarely seen bird due to its small size and discreet appearance.
The red-legged tinamou or red-footed tinamou, (Crypturellus erythropus) is a ground-dwelling bird found in the tropics and lower subtropics of northern South America.

t: The yellow-legged tinamou (Crypturellus noctivagus) is a species of tinamou found in wooded and shrubby habitats in tropical and subtropical eastern Brazil. This superficially quail-like bird has a grey-brown plumage and two easily separated subspecies.
f: It has declined due to human activities, and is therefore listed as Near Threatened by the IUCN.
The brown tinamou (Crypturellus obsoletus) is a brownish ground bird found in humid lowland and montane forest in tropical and subtropical South America.
The small-billed tinamou (Crypturellus parvirostris) is a type of tinamou commonly found in dry savanna in Amazonian South America.

t: The little tinamou (Crypturellus soui) is a species of tinamou.
f: It is found in Central and South America, as well as on the Caribbean island of Trinidad.
The Brazilian tinamou (Crypturellus strigulosus) is a type of tinamou found in tropical moist lowland forest in regions of Amazonian South America.
The Tataupa tinamou (Crypturellus tataupa) is a type of tinamou commonly found in dry forest in subtropical and tropical regions in southeastern South America.
The pale-browed tinamou (Crypturellus transfasciatus) is a type of tinamou found in tropical dry forests in Peru and Ecuador.
The undulated tinamou (Crypturellus undulatus) is a species of ground bird found in a wide range of wooded habitats in eastern and northern South America.
The variegated tinamou (Crypturellus variegatus) is a type of tinamou commonly found in moist forest lowlands in subtropical and tropical regions of northern South America.

t: The cuckoo, common cuckoo, European cuckoo or Eurasian cuckoo (Cuculus canorus) is a member of the cuckoo order of birds, Cuculiformes, which includes the roadrunners, the anis and the coucals. This species is a widespread summer migrant to Europe and Asia, and winters in Africa.
f: The adult too is a mimic, in its case of the sparrowhawk; since that species is a predator, the mimicry gives the female time to lay her eggs without being attacked.

t: The black cuckoo (Cuculus clamosus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. This cuckoo has a very wide range and is quite common so it is classified as a least-concern species by the International Union for Conservation of Nature.
f: The species is distributed widely across sub-Saharan Africa.

t: The African cuckoo or African grey cuckoo (Cuculus gularis) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. A fairly common bird, the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".
f: It is found in Sub-Saharan Africa where it migrates within the continent, generally arriving and breeding in any one locality during the rainy season.

t: The Sunda cuckoo or Sunda lesser cuckoo (Cuculus lepidus) is a South-east Asian bird belonging to the genus Cuculus in the cuckoo family, Cuculidae.
f: It was formerly classified with the Himalayan cuckoo (C. saturatus) and Oriental cuckoo (C. optatus) in a single species, C. saturatus, but is now often regarded as a separate species based on differences in voice, size and plumage.

t: The Indian cuckoo or short-winged cuckoo (Cuculus micropterus) is a member of the cuckoo order of birds, the Cuculiformes, that is found in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. It is a solitary and shy bird, found in forests and open woodland at up to 3,600 m (11,800 ft).
f: It ranges from India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal and Sri Lanka east to Indonesia and north to China and Russia.

t: The Oriental cuckoo or Horsfield's cuckoo (Cuculus optatus) is a bird belonging to the genus Cuculus in the cuckoo family Cuculidae. It was formerly classified as a subspecies of the Himalayan cuckoo (C. saturatus), with the name 'Oriental cuckoo' used for the combined species.
f: Differences in voice and size suggest that it should be treated as a separate species.

t: The lesser cuckoo (Cuculus poliocephalus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae.
f: It is native to East Asia and the Himalayas; it winters to East Africa and Sri Lanka.

t: The Madagascar cuckoo or Madagascan cuckoo (Cuculus rochii), also known as the Madagascar lesser cuckoo, is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae.
f: Though it breeds only in Madagascar, it winters to eastern Africa (from the African Great Lakes region to Zanzibar).

t: The Himalayan cuckoo or Oriental cuckoo (Cuculus saturatus) is a brooding parasitic bird that is part of the Cuculidae family. The species breeds from the Himalayas eastward to southern China and Taiwan.
f: It migrates to southeast Asia and the Greater Sunda Islands for the winter.

t: The red-chested cuckoo (Cuculus solitarius) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. In Afrikaans, it is known as "Piet-my-vrou", after its call.
f: It is a medium-sized bird found in Africa, south of the Sahara.

t: The grey-headed canary-flycatcher (Culicicapa ceylonensis), sometimes known as the grey-headed flycatcher, is a species of small flycatcher-like bird found in tropical Asia. It has a square crest, a grey hood and yellow underparts.
f: They are found mainly in forested habitats where they often join other birds in mixed-species foraging flocks.

t: The citrine canary-flycatcher (Culicicapa helianthea) is a species of bird in the family Stenostiridae. It is found in Sulawesi and the Philippines.
f: The term citrine refers to its yellowish colouration.

t: The sharp-tailed grass tyrant or sharp-tailed tyrant (Culicivora caudacuta) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The austral blackbird (Curaeus curaeus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae. Its natural habitats are temperate forests, subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Argentina and Chile, and it migrates to regions close by.

t: The banded parisoma (Curruca boehmi), banded tit warbler or banded warbler, is a species of Old World warbler in the family Sylviidae. It is found in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and Tanzania.
f: The bird has variable spotting on the throat, white patches on his wing and outer tail, and buff coloring on the belly and undertail.

t: The greater whitethroat or common whitethroat (Curruca communis) is a common and widespread Old World warbler which breeds throughout Europe and across much of temperate western Asia.
f: This small passerine bird is strongly migratory, and winters in tropical Africa, Arabia, and Pakistan.

t: The spectacled warbler (Curruca conspicillata) is a species of passerine bird in the warbler genus Curruca in the family Sylviidae. The specific conspicillata is from Latin conspicillum, a place to look from, equivalent to "spectacled".
f: The song is a fast high warble.

t: The eastern Orphean warbler (Curruca crassirostris) is an Old World warbler of the genus Curruca. This species occurs in summer around the Mediterranean, through the Balkans via Turkey, the Caucasus and surrounding regions to Central Asia.
f: The song is a series of warbling liroo-liroo and scolding notes.

t: The lesser whitethroat (Curruca curruca) is a common and widespread Old World warbler which breeds in temperate Europe, except the southwest, and in the western and central Palearctic. This small passerine bird is strongly migratory, wintering in Africa just south of the Sahara, Arabia and India.
f: The lesser whitethroat's song is a fast and rattling sequence of tet or che calls, quite different from the common whitethroat's scolding song.

t: The western Orphean warbler (Curruca hortensis) is an Old World warbler of the genus Curruca. This species occurs in summer around the Mediterranean, through western Europe and extending into northwest Africa.
f: It is migratory, wintering in Sub-Saharan Africa.

t: The western subalpine warbler (Curruca iberiae) is a small Sylviidae warbler which breeds in the southernmost areas of Europe and north-western Africa. Like most Curruca species, it has distinct male and female plumages.
f: The subalpine warbler's song is fast and rattling, and is similar to the lesser whitethroat.

t: The Sardinian warbler (Curruca melanocephala) is a common and widespread Sylviidae warbler from the Mediterranean region. Like most Curruca species, it has distinct male and female plumages.
f: The Sardinian warbler's song is fast and rattling, and is very characteristic of the Mediterranean areas where this bird breeds.

t: The barred warbler (Curruca nisoria) is a species of bird in the warbler family Sylviidae which breeds across temperate regions of central and eastern Europe and western and central Asia. This passerine bird is strongly migratory, and winters in tropical eastern Africa.
f: The female is similar but slightly paler and has only light barring.

t: The chestnut-vented warbler, chestnut-vented tit-babbler or rufous-vented warbler (Curruca subcoerulea) is an Old World warbler of the family Sylviidae. The chestnut-vented warbler breeds in southern Africa in Angola, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Namibia, South Africa, Lesotho, Mozambique and Eswatini.
f: This is a common species found in a range of habitats including fynbos, scrub, thickets and dry riverbeds.

t: The Dartford warbler (Curruca undata) is a Sylviid warbler from the warmer parts of western Europe and northwestern Africa. It is a small warbler with a long thin tail and a thin pointed bill.
f: The Dartford warbler is usually resident all year in its breeding range, but there is some limited migration.

t: The Vietnamese cutia (Cutia legalleni) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in Laos and Vietnam.
f: In recent times, it is more often elevated to full species status.

t: The Himalayan cutia (Cutia nipalensis) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae. This species inhabits the Himalayan region, from India to northern Thailand.
f: Its scientific name ultimately means "the khutya from Nepal", as Cutia is derived from the Nepali name for these birds, and nipalensis is Latin for "from Nepal".

t: The purple honeycreeper (Cyanerpes caeruleus) is a small Neotropical bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Panama, on Trinidad, and in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The red-legged honeycreeper (Cyanerpes cyaneus) is a small songbird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies. It has also occurred as a vagrant in the United States, Argentina, and some southern Caribbean islands.
f: It is regularly found in Mexico, every Central American country, Trinidad and Tobago, and every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The blue-backed tanager (Cyanicterus cyanicterus)is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The Eurasian blue tit (Cyanistes caeruleus) is a small passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae. It is easily recognised by its blue and yellow plumage and small size.
f: These birds are known for their acrobatic abilities; they can grip the outermost branches of trees and shrubs and hang upside down while searching for food.

t: The azure tit (Cyanistes cyanus) is a species of Eurasian birds in the order of passeriformes in the family Paridae.
f: This small species is the only member of the family Paridae to have a white cap, and was described in 1770 by Peter Simon Pallas.

t: The African blue tit (Cyanistes teneriffae) is a species of bird in the family Paridae. It is found in northern Africa, Pantelleria (Italy) and the Canary Islands (Spain).
f: The species has been used in many research studies due to its island populations and relevance to evolutionary hypotheses.

t: The blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America. It lives in most of the eastern and central United States; some eastern populations may be migratory.
f: Blue jays can be very aggressive to other birds; they sometimes raid nests and have even been found to have decapitated other birds.

t: Steller's jay (Cyanocitta stelleri) is a bird native to western North America and the mountains of Central America, closely related to the blue jay (C. cristata) found in eastern North America. It is also sometimes colloquially called a "blue jay" in the Pacific Northwest, but is distinct from the blue jay of eastern North America.
f: It is the only crested jay west of the Rocky Mountains.

t: The blue bunting (Cyanocompsa parellina) is a species of passerine in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks.
f: It is found in Belize, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.
The black-chested jay (Cyanocorax affinis) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae.

t: The purplish-backed jay (Cyanocorax beecheii) is a bird of the crow family Corvidae, with purple feathers on its back, wings, and tail and black feathers elsewhere. The International Union for Conservation of Nature has assessed it as being a "species of least concern".
f: It is endemic to northwestern Mexico, where its habitat is mainly dry deciduous forest.

t: The azure jay (Cyanocorax coeruleus) (Brazilian Portuguese: gralha-azul) is a Near Threatened species of passeriform bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and possibly Paraguay and Uruguay.

t: The Cayenne jay (Cyanocorax cayanus) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae. It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.
f: In 1760 the French zoologist Mathurin Jacques Brisson included a description of the Cayenne jay in his Ornithologie based on a specimen collected in Cayenne, French Guiana.

t: The plush-crested jay (Cyanocorax chrysops) is a jay of the family Corvidae (which includes the crows and their many allies).
f: It is found in central-southern South America: in southwestern Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina, including southern regions of the Amazon Basin river systems bordering the Pantanal.

t: The curl-crested jay (Cyanocorax cristatellus) is a species of jay native to South America. This New World jay is a beautiful and large (35 cm/14 in overall) bird with predominantly dark blue back, an almost black head and neck, and snow-white chest and underparts.
f: The range on the river systems is only the upstream half of the drainages.

t: The purplish jay (Cyanocorax cyanomelas) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, and as a vagrant to Uruguay.

t: The white-naped jay (Cyanocorax cyanopogon) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae. It is endemic to Brazil - where it is known as the Gralha Cancã or the Cancão.
f: They are capable of interbreeding with plush-crested jays, and hybrids between the species have been observed.

t: The tufted jay (Cyanocorax dickeyi), also known as the painted jay and Dickey's jay, is a species of bird in the crow family Corvidae. It is endemic to a small area of the Sierra Madre Occidental in the Mexican states of Sinaloa, Durango, and Nayarit.
f: It forms social flocks centred around a single breeding pair, with some flocks remaining together over several generations.

t: The bushy-crested jay (Cyanocorax melanocyaneus) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae. There are two subspecies, C. m. melanocyaneus which is found in Guatemala and southern El Salvador, and C. m. chavezi from Honduras and northeastern Nicaragua.
f: It is found in Central America, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and heavily degraded former forest.

t: The white-tailed jay (Cyanocorax mystacalis), also known as the moustached jay, is a species of bird in the crow family Corvidae. It is found in Ecuador and Peru.
f: It has several calls, the most common being described as "cha-cha-cha-cha".

t: The San Blas jay (Cyanocorax sanblasianus) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae.
f: It is endemic to Mexico where its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry forests; it is a common species and has been rated as "least concern" by the IUCN.

t: The violaceous jay (Cyanocorax violaceus) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Venezuela, and possibly Guyana.

t: The Inca jay (Cyanocorax yncas) is a bird species of the New World jays, which is native to the Andes of South America.
f: It is widely known as querrequerre in Spanish, an onomatopoeic name derived from the bird's call.

t: The Yucatan jay (Cyanocorax yucatanicus) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and their allies. It is native to the Yucatán Peninsula where its habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest, plantations and cleared areas at altitudes up to 250 m (820 ft).
f: Immature birds have yellow bills.

t: The rufous-fronted babbler (Cyanoderma rufifrons) is a babbler species in the Old World babbler family. It occurs in the Eastern Himalayan foothills, Myanmar, Thailand, northern Indochina and south to the Malay Peninsula and the islands of Sumatra and Borneo.
f: The buff-chested babbler is now subsumed into this species.

t: The golden babbler (Cyanoderma chrysaeum) is a babbler species in the family Timaliidae. It occurs from the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas to Southeast Asia and inhabits subtropical lowland and montane forests.
f: Since 2016, it is recognised as a Cyanoderma species.
The chestnut-winged babbler (Cyanoderma erythropterum) is a babbler species in the family Timaliidae.

t: The crescent-chested babbler (Cyanoderma melanothorax) is a babbler species in the family Timaliidae and is native to the Indonesian islands of Java and Bali. It inhabits subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, montane forest and shrubland.
f: Myiothera melanothorax was the scientific name proposed by Coenraad Jacob Temminck in 1823 who described a babbler from Java.

t: The black-chinned babbler (Cyanoderma pyrrhops) is a babbler species in the family Timaliidae. It occurs in the foothills of the Himalayas from the Murree Hills in Pakistan to eastern Nepal.
f: Stachyris pyrrhops was the scientific name proposed by Edward Blyth in 1844 who described a greenish olivaceous babbler with a black chin and black lores from Nepal.

t: The rufous-capped babbler (Cyanoderma ruficeps) is a babbler species in the family Timaliidae. It inhabits temperate forest with dense bushes or bamboo and is listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List.
f: It occurs from the Eastern Himalayas to northern Thailand, Laos, eastern China to Vietnam and Taiwan.

t: The Madagascar blue vanga (Cyanolanius madagascarinus) is a bird species in the family Vangidae.
f: It is found in Madagascar, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

t: The burrowing parrot (Cyanoliseus patagonus), also known as the burrowing parakeet or the Patagonian conure, is a species of parrot native to Argentina and Chile. It belongs to the monotypic genus Cyanoliseus, with four subspecies that are currently recognized.
f: Named for their nesting habits, burrowing parrots excavate elaborate burrows in cliff faces and ravines in order to rear their chicks.

t: The ultramarine grosbeak (Cyanoloxia brissonii) is a species of grosbeak in the family Cardinalidae.
f: It is found in a wide range of semi-open habitats in eastern and central South America, with a disjunct population in northern South America.

t: The blue-black grosbeak (Cyanoloxia cyanoides) is a species of songbird in the family Cardinalidae. In addition, in 2018 the committee split the eastern lowland population into a new species, the Amazonian grosbeak (Cyanoloxia rothschildii).
f: The South American Classification Committee of the American Ornithological Society places this species in genus Cyanoloxia.

t: The glaucous-blue grosbeak (Cyanoloxia glaucocaerulea), also known as the indigo grosbeak, is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks.
f: It is found in Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The Amazonian grosbeak or Rothschild's grosbeak (Cyanoloxia rothschildii) is a species of grosbeak in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks.
f: It is found in much of the Amazon Basin, in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The black-collared jay (Cyanolyca armillata) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Venezuela.

t: The azure-hooded jay (Cyanolyca cucullata) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: Females lay three to four eggs, and the young fledge after twenty days.
The white-throated jay (Cyanolyca mirabilis), also known as the Omiltemi jay, is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays.

t: It is endemic to Mexico, and is classified as Near Threatened by the IUCN Red List.
f: The dwarf jay (Cyanolyca nanus) is the smallest bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays.

t: The beautiful jay (Cyanolyca pulchra) is a species of bird in the crow and jay family Corvidae. It is closely related to the azure-hooded jay, and the two species are considered sister species.
f: Only one nest has been described so far, it is a cup constructed with sticks and decorated on the outside with moss and lined with thin plant fibres.

t: The black-throated jay or Strickland's jay (Cyanolyca pumilo) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays.
f: It is found in Mexico, Guatemala and Honduras.

t: The turquoise jay (Cyanolyca turcosa) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae. The turquoise jay is a vibrant blue jay with a black face mask and collar.
f: This bird is omnivorous and is known to eat insects, berries, eggs, and young birds of other species.

t: The white-collared jay (Cyanolyca viridicyanus) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru.

t: The blue-throated brown sunbird (Cyanomitra cyanolaema) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae.
f: It is widespread across the African tropical rainforest.

t: The olive sunbird (Cyanomitra olivacea) is a large African species of sunbird belonging to the family Nectariniidae which encompasses species of sunbirds, spiderhunters, and flowerpeckers, and sugarbirds. It has a large distribution that spans across central Africa from western countries including Senegal, Guinea, and Angola towards eastern countries including Ethiopia, Kenya, and Mozambique.
f: This range also extends to southern African countries including South Africa and Zimbabwe.

t: The grey sunbird or mouse-coloured sunbird (Cyanomitra veroxii) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae.
f: It is native to shoreline areas of Africa, from Somalia to South Africa.
The green-headed sunbird (Cyanomitra verticalis) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae.

t: The Iberian magpie (Cyanopica cooki) is a bird in the crow family.
f: It is 31–35 cm (12–14 in) long and similar in overall shape to the Eurasian magpie (Pica pica) but is slenderer with proportionately smaller legs and bill.

t: The azure-winged magpie (Cyanopica cyanus) is a bird in the crow family. It is 31–35 cm long and similar in overall shape to the Eurasian magpie (Pica pica) but is more slender with proportionately smaller legs and bill.
f: It has a glossy black top to the head and a white throat.

t: Zappey's flycatcher (Cyanoptila cumatilis) is a songbird in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. It closely similar to, and was formerly considered to be conspecific with, the blue-and-white flycatcher, which breeds further east from northeastern China east to Japan.
f: It is migratory, breeding in central China from central Sichuan northeast to the mountains west of Beijing, and wintering south to the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, and Java.

t: The blue-and-white flycatcher (Cyanoptila cyanomelana) is a migratory songbird in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. The species is also known as the Japanese flycatcher.
f: It winters in South East Asia, especially in Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Sumatra and Borneo.

t: The red-crowned parakeet (Cyanoramphus novaezelandiae), also known as red-fronted parakeet and by its Māori name of kākāriki, is a small parrot from New Zealand. It is characterised by its bright green plumage and the red pattern on its head.
f: This versatile bird can feed on a variety food items and can be found in many habitat types.

t: The rufous-browed peppershrike (Cyclarhis gujanensis) is a passerine bird in the vireo family.
f: It is widespread and often common in woodland, forest edge, and cultivation with some tall trees from Mexico and Trinidad south to Argentina and Uruguay.

t: The black-billed peppershrike (Cyclarhis nigrirostris) is a species of bird in the family Vireonidae. It inhabits subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in the Andes of Colombia and northern Ecuador.

t: The black swan (Cygnus atratus) is a large waterbird, a species of swan which breeds mainly in the southeast and southwest regions of Australia. Within Australia, the black swan is nomadic, with erratic migration patterns dependent on climatic conditions.
f: Black swans can be found singly, or in loose companies numbering into the hundreds or even thousands.

t: The trumpeter swan (Cygnus buccinator), or simply the trumpeter, is a species of swan found in North America. The heaviest living bird native to North America, it is also the largest extant species of waterfowl, with a wingspan of 185 to 304.8 cm (6 ft 2 in to 10 ft 2 in).
f: It is the American counterpart and a close relative of the whooper swan (Cygnus cygnus) of Eurasia and has even been considered the same species by some authorities.

t: The tundra swan (Cygnus columbianus) is a species of swan which breeds in the arctic, and overwinters in North America, Europe, and Asia. It is the smallest of the Holarctic swans, at 115–150 cm (45–59 in) in length, 168–211 cm (66–83 in) in wingspan and 3.4–9.6 kg (7.5–21.2 lb) in weight.
f: They have few natural predators, although sometimes Arctic foxes, parasitic jaegers, and glaucous gulls will prey upon their eggs and chicks.

t: The whooper swan (/ˈhuːpə(ɹ) swɒn/ "hooper swan"; Cygnus cygnus), is a large northern hemisphere swan.
f: It is the Eurasian counterpart of the North American trumpeter swan.

t: The black-necked swan (Cygnus melancoryphus) is a species of South American waterfowl in the tribe Cygnini of the subfamily Anserinae. It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Uruguay, and the Falkland Islands.
f: The black-necked swan is the smallest true swan on average, weighing between 3.5–8.7 kg (7.7–19.2 lb) as adults, but it is still the largest species of waterfowl native to South America.

t: The mute swan (Cygnus olor) is a species of swan and a member of the family Anatidae within the waterfowl order. It is native to much of Europe and parts of Asia and (as a rare winter visitor) the far north of Africa.
f: It is an introduced species in North America, home to the largest populations outside of its native range, with additional smaller introductions in Australasia and Southern Africa.

t: The fasciated antshrike (Cymbilaimus lineatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Central America from Honduras south and in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The bamboo antshrike (Cymbilaimus sanctaemariae) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The black-and-red broadbill (Cymbirhynchus macrorhynchos) is a species of bird in the typical broadbill family, Eurylaimidae. It is the only species in the genus Cymbirhynchus.
f: Nests are built by both sexes, out of creepers, fungal hyphae, moss, and other plant matter.

t: The broad-billed hummingbird (Cynanthus latirostris) is a small hummingbird that resides in Mexico and the southwestern United States. Males and females have different features (see sexual dimorphism).
f: The bird is also known for its other common names – the Colibrí Pico Ancho in Spanish and Colibri circé in French.

t: The Sunda blue flycatcher (Cyornis caerulatus), also known as the large-billed blue-flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is found in Sumatra and Borneo.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The white-tailed flycatcher (Leucoptilon concretum) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is found in submountain forests from the eastern Himalayas and northern Myanmar to southern China, western and southern Thailand, the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra and Borneo.
f: It is the only member of the monotypic genus Leucoptilon.

t: The Chinese blue flycatcher (Cyornis glaucicomans) is a small passerine bird in the flycatcher family, Muscicapidae. It previously was considered a subspecies of the blue-throated blue flycatcher.
f: The Chinese blue flycatcher is native to mid-southern China; it winters to the Tenasserim Hills and the Malay Peninsula.

t: The Hainan blue flycatcher (Cyornis hainanus) is a bird in the family Muscicapidae. The species was first described by William Robert Ogilvie-Grant in 1900.
f: It is native to southern China, Hainan and Indochina.

t: The blue-fronted blue flycatcher (Eumyias hoevelli), also known as the blue-fronted flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae.
f: Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The fulvous-chested jungle flycatcher (Cyornis olivaceus) is a species of bird in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, and Thailand.

t: The Sulawesi blue flycatcher (Cyornis omissus) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The white-bellied blue flycatcher (Cyornis pallidipes) is a small passerine bird in the flycatcher family Muscicapidae. Males are dark blue with a lighter shade of blue on the brow and have a greyish white belly.
f: It is endemic to the Western Ghats (including the Nilgiris) of southwest India.

t: The pale-chinned flycatcher (Cyornis poliogenys) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It has also been known in the past as pale-chinned blue flycatcher (on the IOC World Bird List up to 2023), and Brook's flycatcher.
f: Its nesting season is April–June.

t: The blue-throated blue flycatcher (Cyornis rubeculoides) is a small passerine bird in the flycatcher family, Muscicapidae. The habitat of this species is a thicker forest than other species of flycatchers.
f: It resembles Cyornis tickelliae but easily separated by the blue throat.

t: The mangrove blue flycatcher (Cyornis rufigastra) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.
f: It is native to Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The Indochinese blue flycatcher (Cyornis sumatrensis) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is found from southern Myanmar and the Malay Peninsula to Indochina and northeastern Sumatra.
f: It was previously considered conspecific with Tickell's blue flycatcher.

t: The Bornean blue flycatcher (Cyornis superbus) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, and Malaysia, where it is endemic to the island of Borneo.

t: Tickell's blue flycatcher (Cyornis tickelliae) is a small passerine bird in the flycatcher family. This is an insectivorous species which breeds in tropical Asia, from the Indian subcontinent eastwards to Bangladesh and western Myanmar.
f: They are found in dense scrub to forest habitats.

t: The Malaysian blue flycatcher (Cyornis turcosus) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It has a brilliant blue upperparts, a pale orange throat and chest, and a white belly.
f: A slightly paler female has a whitish throat, while a male's is blue; the sexes are otherwise quite similar.

t: The grey-chested jungle flycatcher (Cyornis umbratilis) is a species of bird in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The pale blue flycatcher (Cyornis unicolor) is a bird in the family Muscicapidae. The species was first described by Edward Blyth in 1843.
f: Both birds can often be found in the same locale.

t: The hill blue flycatcher (Cyornis whitei) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It was treated as a subspecies of Cyornis banyumas before molecular phylogenetic studies found them to be distinct.
f: It is found in southern China, northeastern India and Southeast Asia.

t: It is native to the Amazon rainforest in South America, from the lowlands into the foothills of the Andes.
f: The musician wren or organ wren (Cyphorhinus arada) is a species of wren named for its elaborate song.

t: The song wren (Cyphorhinus phaeocephalus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The southern chestnut-breasted wren (Cyphorhinus thoracicus) is a species of passerine bird in the wren family Troglodytidae that is found in southern Peru and the extreme northwest of Bolivia.
f: It was formerly considered to be conspecific with the northern chestnut-breasted wren (Cyphorhinus dichrous) with the English name "chestnut-breasted wren".

t: The American black swift, or more simply black swift (Cypseloides niger), is a species of bird that is found from northern British Columbia in Canada through the United States and Mexico to Costa Rica and Brazil.
f: They are also found in the Caribbean.

t: The Asian palm swift (Cypsiurus balasiensis) is a small swift. It is very similar to the African palm swift, Cypsiurus parvus, and was formerly considered to be the same species.
f: Asian palm swift has very short legs which it uses only for clinging to vertical surfaces, since swifts never settle voluntarily on the ground.

t: It is very similar to the Asian palm swift, Cypsiurus balasiensis, and was formerly considered to be the same species. The Malagasy palm swift was also recently split from this species.
f: The African palm swift (Cypsiurus parvus) is a small swift.

t: The white-rumped tanager (Cypsnagra hirundinacea) is a South American bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is the only member of the genus Cypsnagra.
f: The cup shaped nests are placed only 1–2 metres (3–7 ft) off the ground and are made of woven grasses.

t: It is also known as Mearns's quail, the harlequin quail (for the male's striking pattern), and the fool quail (for its behavior).
f: The Montezuma quail (Cyrtonyx montezumae) is a stubby, secretive New World quail of Mexico and some nearby parts of the United States.

t: The ocellated quail (Cyrtonyx ocellatus) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail.
f: It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: Cyrtoxipha columbiana, the Columbian trig, is a species of cricket in the family Trigonidiidae (the winged bush crickets, or “trigs”).
f: It is endemic to most of the southeastern United States, up to New Jersey, although sightings are also reported from further north, including New York and Massachusetts.

t: The rufous-bellied kookaburra (Dacelo gaudichaud), originally known as Gaudichaud's kookaburra after French botanist Charles Gaudichaud-Beaupré, is a species of kookaburra that is widely distributed through the forests of lowland New Guinea. It has a black cap, blue-tinged wings, and a pale, rufous belly and tail feathers, but its white bill distinguishes it very clearly from other kookaburras with their black bills.
f: Rufous-bellied kookaburras can be found in the middle story of the tropical rainforest, where they fly out directly and swiftly from their perch to seize large insects from trees.

t: The blue-winged kookaburra (Dacelo leachii) is a large species of kingfisher native to northern Australia and southern New Guinea. Measuring around 40 cm (16 in), it is slightly smaller than the more familiar laughing kookaburra.
f: It has blue wings and brown shoulders and blue rump.

t: The laughing kookaburra (Dacelo novaeguineae) is a bird in the kingfisher subfamily Halcyoninae. It is a large kingfisher with a whitish head and a brown eye-stripe.
f: A predator of a wide variety of small animals, the laughing kookaburra typically waits perched on a branch until it sees an animal on the ground and then flies down and pounces on its prey.

t: The blue dacnis or turquoise honeycreeper (Dacnis cayana) is a small passerine bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Central America from Honduras to Panama, on Trinidad, and in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The yellow-bellied dacnis (Dacnis flaviventer) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The black-faced dacnis (Dacnis lineata) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The scarlet-thighed dacnis (Dacnis venusta) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama.

t: The singing quail (Dactylortyx thoracicus) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail.
f: It is found in Belize, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.

t: About 10–11 cm long, it is also known as the Australian nuthatch, orange-winged sittella and the barkpecker.
f: The varied sittella (Daphoenositta chrysoptera) is a small songbird native to Australia.

t: The pintado petrel (Daption capense), also called the Cape petrel, or Cape fulmar, is a common seabird of the Southern Ocean from the family Procellariidae. It is the only member of the genus Daption, and is allied to the fulmarine petrels and the giant petrels.
f: It is an abundant seabird, with an estimated population of around 2 million.

t: The black caracara (Daptrius ater) is a bird of prey in the family Falconidae that is found in Amazonian and French Guianan lowlands, mainly occurring along rivers. It was formerly the only species placed in the genus Daptrius but based on genetic studies the genus now includes species that were formerly placed in the genera Milvago and Phalcoboenus.
f: Since migration has not been observed, they are considered resident, or sedentary, remaining in the tropics year round.

t: The scale-feathered malkoha (Dasylophus cumingi) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It is a spectacular looking bird with its white hood, red eyes and yellowish bill with a line of scaled feathers down from the bill and up over the crown, contrasted with rufous neck and back and a black lower body and tail.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines found only in the islands of Luzon, Catanduanes and Marinduque.

t: The eastern bristlebird (Dasyornis brachypterus) is a species of bird in the bristlebird family, Dasyornithidae. Its natural habitats are temperate forests, temperate shrubland, and temperate grassland.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The rufous bristlebird (Dasyornis broadbenti) is one of three extant species of bristlebirds. It is endemic to Australia and three subspecies have been described, from coastal south-western Western Australia, south-eastern South Australia and south-western Victoria.
f: It is threatened by habitat destruction.

t: The western bristlebird (Dasyornis longirostris) is a species of bird in the family Dasyornithidae.
f: It is endemic to the coastal heaths of western Australia (east and west of Albany).

t: The whistling long-tailed woodcreeper (Deconychura longicauda), also known as the northern long-tailed woodcreeper, is a species of bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, and Suriname.

t: The Asian house martin (Delichon dasypus) is a migratory passerine bird of the swallow family Hirundinidae. It has mainly blue-black upperparts, other than its white rump, and has pale grey underparts.
f: Both sexes build the nest, incubate the three or four white eggs and feed the chicks.

t: It feeds on insects which are caught in flight, and it migrates to climates where flying insects are plentiful. It has a blue head and upperparts, white rump and pure white underparts, and is found in both open country and near human habitation.
f: It builds a closed cup nest from mud pellets under eaves or similar locations on buildings usually in colonies.

t: The sooty grouse (Dendragapus fuliginosus) is a species of forest-dwelling grouse native to North America's Pacific Coast Ranges.
f: It is closely related to the dusky grouse (Dendragapus obscurus), and the two were previously considered a single species, the blue grouse.

t: The dusky grouse (Dendragapus obscurus) is a species of forest-dwelling grouse native to the Rocky Mountains in North America.
f: It is closely related to the sooty grouse (Dendragapus fuliginosus), and the two were previously considered a single species, the blue grouse.

t: The cinnamon-throated woodcreeper (Dendrexetastes rufigula) is a sub-oscine passerine bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The tawny-winged woodcreeper (Dendrocincla anabatina) is a passerine bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Belize, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The plain-brown woodcreeper (Dendrocincla fuliginosa), is a sub-oscine passerine bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in the tropical New World from Honduras through South America to central Brazil and in Trinidad and Tobago.

t: The ruddy woodcreeper (Dendrocincla homochroa) is a passerine bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found from southern Mexico to northern Colombia and extreme northern Venezuela.

t: The white-chinned woodcreeper (Dendrocincla merula) is a species of bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The plain-winged woodcreeper or thrush-like woodcreeper (Dendrocincla turdina) is a sub-oscine passerine bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The tyrannine woodcreeper (Dendrocincla tyrannina) is a species of bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The Bornean treepie (Dendrocitta cinerascens) is a passerine bird belonging to the treepies genus, Dendrocitta, of in the crow family, Corvidae. It is sometimes treated as a subspecies of the Sumatran treepie (D. occipitalis).
f: It is endemic to the island of Borneo.

t: The grey treepie (Dendrocitta formosae), also known as the Himalayan treepie, is an Asian treepie, a medium-sized and long-tailed member of the crow family. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1863.
f: They sometimes take part in mixed species flocks with laughingthrushes, especially the white-throated laughingthrush.

t: The white-bellied treepie (Dendrocitta leucogastra) is a bird of the crow family endemic to the forests of southern India.
f: They overlap in distribution in some areas with the rufous treepie but are easy to tell apart both from appearance and call.

t: The rufous treepie (Dendrocitta vagabunda) is a treepie, native to the Indian subcontinent and adjoining parts of Southeast Asia. It is a member of the crow family, Corvidae.
f: Like other corvids it is very adaptable, omnivorous and opportunistic in feeding.

t: The Amazonian barred woodcreeper (Dendrocolaptes certhia) is a sub-oscine passerine bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The black-banded woodcreeper (Dendrocolaptes picumnus) is a sub-oscine passerine bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found discontinuously from Chiapas, Mexico, to Panama and in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The planalto woodcreeper (Dendrocolaptes platyrostris) is a sub-oscine passerine bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The northern barred woodcreeper (Dendrocolaptes sanctithomae) is a sub-oscine passerine bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found from southern Mexico through Central America to Colombia, Venezuela and Ecuador.

t: The freckle-breasted woodpecker (Dendrocopos analis) is a species of bird in the family Picidae.
f: It is found in Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam.

t: The Darjeeling woodpecker (Dendrocopos darjellensis) is a species of bird in the family Picidae.
f: It is found in the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the Himalayas, and in some adjoining areas.

t: The Himalayan woodpecker (Dendrocopos himalayensis) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. Its natural habitats are boreal forests and temperate forests.
f: It is found in the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent, primarily the Himalayas and some adjoining areas, and ranges across Afghanistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan and Pakistan.

t: The rufous-bellied woodpecker or rufous-bellied sapsucker (Dendrocopos hyperythrus) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. It is found along the Himalayas in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, ranging across Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, Hong Kong, India, Korea, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, Manchuria, Ussuriland and Vietnam.
f: This woodpecker has a habit of making a series of small pits on the bark of trees leading to its being considered an Asiatic member of the sapsuckers in the past.

t: The white-winged woodpecker (Dendrocopos leucopterus) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. The white-winged woodpecker's natural habitats are temperate forests and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in Afghanistan, China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan.
The white-backed woodpecker (Dendrocopos leucotos) is a Eurasian woodpecker belonging to the genus Dendrocopos.

t: The fulvous-breasted woodpecker (Dendrocopos macei) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. The freckle-breasted woodpecker was formerly considered conspecific with this species.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, India and Myanmar.

t: The great spotted woodpecker (Dendrocopos major) is a medium-sized woodpecker with pied black and white plumage and a red patch on the lower belly. Males and young birds also have red markings on the neck or head.
f: Great spotted woodpeckers chisel into trees to find food or excavate nest holes, and also drum for contact and territorial advertisement; like other woodpeckers, they have anatomical adaptations to manage the physical stresses from the hammering action.
The Syrian woodpecker (Dendrocopos syriacus) is a member of the woodpecker family, the Picidae.

t: The brown-fronted woodpecker (Dendrocoptes auriceps) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. It is found in Afghanistan, India, Nepal, Pakistan and Bhutan.
f: It ranges across the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent, primarily the lower-to-middle altitudes of the Himalayas.
The middle spotted woodpecker (Dendrocoptes medius) is a mainly European woodpecker belonging to the genus Dendrocoptes.

t: They inhabit tropical and subtropical Australia, the Philippines, Borneo, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste, and the Pacific Islands.
f: The wandering whistling duck (Dendrocygna arcuata) is a species of whistling duck.

t: The black-bellied whistling duck (Dendrocygna autumnalis) or black-bellied tree duck, is a whistling duck that before 2000 bred mainly from the southernmost United States to south-central South America. It can be found year-round in much of the United States.
f: Since it is one of only two whistling duck species native to North America, it is occasionally just known as the "whistling duck" or "Mexican squealer" in the southern USA.

t: It has plumage that is mainly reddish brown, long legs and a long grey bill, and shows a distinctive white band across its black tail in flight. Like other members of its ancient lineage, it has a whistling call which is given in flight or on the ground.
f: The fulvous whistling duck feeds in wetlands by day or night on seeds and other parts of plants.

t: The plumed whistling duck (Dendrocygna eytoni), also called the grass whistling duck, is a species of bird in the whistling duck subfamily of the family Anatidae. It is resident and breeds in Australia, in a broad arc covering the northern half and most of the eastern third of the continent.
f: There are also non-breeding and seasonally uncertain populations in New Zealand, the Solomon Islands, Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.

t: The lesser whistling duck (Dendrocygna javanica), also known as Indian whistling duck or lesser whistling teal, is a species of whistling duck that breeds in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. They are nocturnal feeders that during the day may be found in flocks around lakes and wet paddy fields.
f: They can perch on trees and sometimes build their nest in the hollow of a tree.

t: The white-faced whistling duck (Dendrocygna viduata) is a whistling duck that breeds in sub-Saharan Africa and much of South America. This species is gregarious, and the flocks of a thousand or more arrive at dawn at favored sites.
f: As the name implies, these are noisy birds with a clear three-note whistling call.

t: The chestnut-winged foliage-gleaner (Dendroma erythroptera) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The buff-fronted foliage-gleaner (Dendroma rufa) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is native to the Neotropical realm.

t: The forest wagtail (Dendronanthus indicus) is a medium-sized passerine bird in the wagtail family Motacillidae. It has a distinctive plumage that sets it apart from other wagtails and has the habit of wagging its tail sideways unlike the usual up and down movements of the other wagtail species.
f: It is the only wagtail species that nests in trees.

t: The straight-billed woodcreeper (Dendroplex picus) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Panama, Trinidad, and in every mainland South American country except Chile, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay.

t: The bearded wood partridge (Dendrortyx barbatus) is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail.
f: It inhabits the Sierra Madre Oriental of Mexico.

t: The buffy-crowned wood partridge (Dendrortyx leucophrys) is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail.
f: It is found in Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Costa Rica and Nicaragua.
The long-tailed wood partridge (Dendrortyx macroura) is a bird species in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail.

t: The red-fan parrot (Deroptyus accipitrinus), also known as the hawk-headed parrot, is a New World parrot hailing from the Amazon rainforest. It is found in Brazil, Suriname, Bolivia, Ecuador, Colombia, areas of northeast Peru, Venezuela, French Guiana and Guyana.
f: It is the only member of the genus Deroptyus.

t: The midget flowerpecker (Dicaeum aeneum) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae. It is found in the Solomon Islands archipelago.
f: This species does not migrate and has inhabited the Solomon Islands since 1900.

t: The thick-billed flowerpecker (Pachyglossa agilis) is a tiny bird in the flowerpecker group. It is a resident bird with a wide distribution across tropical southern Asia from India east to Indonesia and Timor with several populations recognized as subspecies some of which are sometimes treated as full species.
f: They feed predominantly on fruits and are active birds that are mainly seen in the tops of trees in forests.

t: The red-keeled flowerpecker or red-striped flowerpecker (Dicaeum australe) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae. It is endemic to the Philippines.
f: It is one of the more common birds in the Philippines as it is able to thrive in a wide array of habitats.

t: The yellow-vented flowerpecker (Pachyglossa chrysorrhea) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brunei, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The Nilgiri flowerpecker (Dicaeum concolor) is a tiny bird in the flowerpecker family. Formerly a subspecies of what used to be termed as the plain flowerpecker although that name is now reserved for Dicaeum minullum.
f: Like others of the group, it feeds predominantly on nectar and fruits.

t: The scarlet-backed flowerpecker (Dicaeum cruentatum) is a species of passerine bird in the flowerpecker family Dicaeidae. It is found in subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and occasionally gardens in a number of countries throughout South and East Asia.
f: Sexually dimorphic, the male has navy blue upperparts with a bright red streak down its back from its crown to its tail coverts, while the female and juvenile are predominantly olive green.

t: The pale-billed flowerpecker or Tickell's flowerpecker (Dicaeum erythrorhynchos) is a tiny bird that feeds on nectar and berries, found in India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and western Myanmar. They have a rapid chipping call and the pinkish curved beak separates it from other species in the region.
f: The bird is common especially in urban gardens with berry bearing trees.
The mistletoebird eats mainly the berries of the parasitic mistletoe and is a vector for the spread of the mistletoe's seeds through its digestive system.

t: The fire-breasted flowerpecker (Dicaeum ignipectus) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae found in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. Unlike many other species in the genus, this species has marked sexual dimorphism with the male having contrasting upper and lower parts with a distinctive bright orange breast patch.
f: Like other flowerpeckers, this tiny bird feeds on fruits and plays an important role in the dispersal of fruiting plants.
