t: The plain flowerpecker (Dicaeum minullum) is a bird in the family Dicaeidae. The species was described and given its binomial name by Robert Swinhoe in 1870.
f: It is found in the central Himalayas, through western Indonesia to Taiwan.

t: The pygmy flowerpecker (Dicaeum pygmaeum) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae. Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forest and tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines.

t: The orange-bellied flowerpecker (Dicaeum trigonostigma) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The mottled flowerpecker or white-mottled flowerpecker (Dicaeum tristrami) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae. It inhabits primary forest and secondary growth, most commonly in the mountains.
f: It is endemic to Makira in the Solomon Islands.

t: The banded antbird (Dichrozona cincta) – sometimes called banded antwren despite not being close to the true antwrens – is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The fork-tailed drongo (Dicrurus adsimilis), also called the common drongo or African drongo, is a small bird found from the Sahel to South Africa that lives in wooded habitats, particularly woodlands and savannas. It is part of the family Dicruridae and has four recognized subspecies, D. a adsimilis, D. a. apivorus, D. a. fugax and D. a. jubaensis.
f: The fork-tailed drongo is known for its ability to deceptively mimic other bird alarm calls in order for a certain animal to flee the scene so it can steal their food (kleptoparasitism).

t: The bronzed drongo (Dicrurus aeneus) is a small Indomalayan bird belonging to the drongo group. They are resident in the forests of the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.
f: They capture insects flying in the shade of the forest canopy by making aerial sallies from their perches.

t: The Andaman Drongo (Dicrurus andamanensis) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae. There are two subspecies, the nominate race being found across the main islands of the archipelago, and the race dicruriformis occurring on Great Coco Island and Table Island in the north of the chain.
f: The species is endemic to the Andaman Islands of the Indian Ocean.

t: The crow-billed drongo (Dicrurus annectens) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae. It is native to moist tropical forests of southeastern Asia where its range extends from India to the Philippines and Indonesia.
f: It breeds between April and June, the cup-shaped nest being built in the fork of a branch by both birds, the female afterwards incubating the eggs.

t: The shining drongo (Dicrurus atripennis) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae.
f: It is native to the African tropical rainforest.

t: The balicassiao (Dicrurus balicassius) is a species of passerine bird in the family Dicruridae. Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines.

t: The spangled drongo (Dicrurus bracteatus) is a bird of the family Dicruridae. It feeds on insects and small vertebrates.
f: It is the only drongo to be found in Australia, where it can be recognised by its black, iridescent plumage and its characteristic forked tail.

t: The white-bellied drongo (Dicrurus caerulescens) is a species of drongo found across the Indian Subcontinent. Like other members of the family Dicruridae, they are insectivorous and mainly black in colour, but with a white belly and vent.
f: Young birds are, however, all black and may be confused with the black drongo, which is smaller and more compact in appearance.

t: The fork-tailed drongo (Dicrurus adsimilis), also called the common drongo or African drongo, is a small bird found from the Sahel to South Africa that lives in wooded habitats, particularly woodlands and savannas. It is part of the family Dicruridae and has four recognized subspecies, D. a adsimilis, D. a. apivorus, D. a. fugax and D. a. jubaensis.
f: The fork-tailed drongo is known for its ability to deceptively mimic other bird alarm calls in order for a certain animal to flee the scene so it can steal their food (kleptoparasitism).

t: The crested drongo (Dicrurus forficatus) is a passerine bird in the family Dicruridae. There are two subspecies; D. f. forficatus is endemic to Madagascar and D. f. potior, which is larger, is found on the Comoro Islands.
f: It is black with a bluish-green sheen, a distinctive crest on the forehead and a forked tail.

t: The hair-crested drongo (Dicrurus hottentottus) is an Asian bird of the family Dicruridae. This species was formerly considered conspecific with Dicrurus bracteatus, for which the name "spangled drongo" – formerly used for both – is now usually reserved.
f: It is native from Pakistan, Bangladesh, India, and Bhutan through Indochina to China, Indonesia, and Brunei.

t: The ashy drongo (Dicrurus leucophaeus) is a species of bird in the drongo family Dicruridae.
f: It is found widely distributed across eastern and Southeast Asia, with several populations that vary in the shade of grey, migration patterns and in the size or presence of white patches around the eye.

t: The square-tailed drongo (Dicrurus ludwigii), formerly the common square-tailed drongo, is a passerine bird in the family Dicruridae. It is a common resident breeder in parts of southern Africa.
f: Two to three eggs are laid in a cup nest in a fork high in a tree.

t: The black drongo (Dicrurus macrocercus) is a small Asian passerine bird of the drongo family Dicruridae. It is a common resident breeder in much of tropical southern Asia from southwest Iran through Pakistan, India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka east to southern China and Indonesia and accidental visitor of Japan.
f: The species is known for its aggressive behaviour towards much larger birds, such as crows, never hesitating to dive-bomb any bird of prey that invades its territory.

t: The Sulawesi drongo (Dicrurus montanus) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is endemic to Sulawesi in Indonesia.

t: The greater racket-tailed drongo (Dicrurus paradiseus) is a medium-sized Asian bird which is distinctive in having elongated outer tail feathers with webbing restricted to the tips. They are placed along with other drongos in the family Dicruridae.
f: These drongos will sometimes steal insect prey caught or disturbed by other foragers in the flock and another idea is that vocal mimicry helps them in diverting the attention of smaller birds to aid their piracy.

t: The lesser racket-tailed drongo (Dicrurus remifer) is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae. It is found in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, ranging across Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, and Vietnam.
f: It is found in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.

t: The white-sided flowerpiercer (Diglossa albilatera) is a fairly common and widespread species of flowerpiercer. The white-sided flowerpiercer is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
f: Flowerpiercers are a genus of birds within the tanager family Thraupidae, with specially adapted bills that enable them to pierce the sides of flower blossoms to access the nectar.

t: The cinnamon-bellied flowerpiercer (Diglossa baritula) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.
f: It is a species known to be a nectar robber, apparently taking nectar while not pollinating the plant.

t: The black-throated flowerpiercer (Diglossa brunneiventris) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in the northern Andes .

t: The bluish flowerpiercer (Diglossa caerulescens) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.
f: It is found in humid montane forest in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela.

t: The masked flowerpiercer (Diglossa cyanea) is a species of bird in the tanager family, Thraupidae. It is found in humid montane forest and scrub in Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia.
f: Flowerpiercers got their name from the fact that they have a sharp hook on the tip of their upper mandible which they use to slice open the base of flowers to get at the nectar.

t: The golden-eyed flowerpiercer (Diglossa glauca), also known as the deep-blue flowerpiercer, is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is found in humid Andean forests in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia.
f: It is the only species of flowerpiercer with bright yellow eyes.

t: The chestnut-bellied flowerpiercer (Diglossa gloriosissima) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The black flowerpiercer (Diglossa humeralis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae of the order Passeriformes. The black flowerpiercer is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
f: The family Thraupidae is known for tanagers and other very similar species of birds, but it is still facing classification issues.

t: The indigo flowerpiercer (Diglossa indigotica) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.
f: It is found in humid forest on the lower west Andean slopes in northern Ecuador and Colombia.

t: The glossy flowerpiercer (Diglossa lafresnayii) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, subtropical or tropical high-altitude grassland, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The moustached flowerpiercer (Diglossa mystacalis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It was first described by French ornithologist Frédéric de Lafresnaye in 1846.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru.

t: The slaty flowerpiercer (Diglossa plumbea) is a passerine bird endemic to the Talamancan montane forests. This is a common bird in mountain forest canopy and edges, and especially in sunlit clearings and areas with flowering shrubs, which can include gardens.
f: The male's song consists of a mixture of whistles, warbles and trilled notes, see-chew see-chew see-chew seer seer surrzeep, tsee tsew tsink tsink tsink.

t: The rusty flowerpiercer (Diglossa sittoides) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The white-headed buffalo weaver or white-faced buffalo-weaver (Dinemellia dinemelli) is a species of passerine bird in the family Ploceidae native to East Africa.
f: The buffalo part of its name derives from its habit of following the African buffalo, feeding on disturbed insects.

t: The black-rumped flameback (Dinopium benghalense), also known as the lesser golden-backed woodpecker or lesser goldenback, is a woodpecker found widely distributed in the Indian subcontinent. It has a characteristic rattling-whinnying call and an undulating flight.
f: It is one of the few woodpeckers that are seen in urban areas.
The common flameback (Dinopium javanense), also referred to as the common goldenback, is a small (28–30 cm), three-toed woodpecker in the family Picidae, found throughout South and Southeast Asia.
The olive-backed woodpecker (Gecinulus rafflesii) is a species of bird in the woodpecker family Picidae that is found in Southeast Asia.

t: The snowy albatross (Diomedea exulans), also known as the wandering albatross, white-winged albatross, or goonie, is a large seabird from the family Diomedeidae; they have a circumpolar range in the Southern Ocean. Together with the Amsterdam albatross, it forms the wandering albatross species complex, which some began referring to more recently as "snowy".
f: It is the largest species of albatross and was long considered to be the same species as the Tristan albatross and the Antipodean albatross.

t: The red-shouldered macaw (Diopsittaca nobilis) is a small green South American parrot, a member of a large group of Neotropical parrots called macaws. It is the smallest macaw, being 30 cm (12 in) in length – similar in size to the Aratinga parakeets.
f: The species is named for the red coverts on its wings.

t: The diuca finch (Diuca diuca) is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, and Uruguay.
f: It is the only member of the genus Diuca.

t: The melodious blackbird (Dives dives) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found from Mexico to Costa Rica.

t: The scrub blackbird (Dives warczewiczi) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The bobolink (Dolichonyx oryzivorus) is a small New World blackbird and the only member of the genus Dolichonyx. The bobolink breeds in the summer in the United States and Canada, with most of the summer range in the northern U.S.
f: An old name for this species is the "rice bird", from its tendency to feed on cultivated grains during winter and migration.

t: The black-capped donacobius (Donacobius atricapilla) is a conspicuous, vocal South American bird and the only bird in the genus Donacobius and family Donacobiidae.
f: It is distributed across the northern half of South America.

t: The long-tailed reed finch (Donacospiza albifrons) is a species of South American bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
f: It is the only member of its genus Donacospiza.

t: The green-fronted lancebill (Doryfera ludovicae) is a species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae.
f: Primarily known for its incredibly long bill and "glittering" green patch of feathers on its forehead, D. ludovicae is found in subtropical and tropical moist montane forest and prefers regions that include fast moving rivers and streams.

t: The ʻiʻiwi (pronounced , ee-EE-wee or , ee-EE-vee) or scarlet honeycreeper (Drepanis coccinea) is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper.
f: The ʻiʻiwi is a highly recognizable symbol of Hawaii.

t: The black-billed sicklebill (Drepanornis albertisi), also referred to as the buff-tailed sicklebill , is a species of bird-of-paradise.
f: It, along with its congener, are the only members of the genus Drepanornis.

t: The crab-plover or crab plover (Dromas ardeola) is a coastal wader (shorebird). It is the only member of the genus Dromas and the family Dromadidae.
f: It is unique among waders in making use of ground warmth to aid the incubation of its eggs.

t: The pavonine cuckoo (Dromococcyx pavoninus) is a Neotropical cuckoo with a long graduated tail and a short crest.
f: It is one of three species of Neotropical cuckoo which are known to be brood parasites.

t: The pheasant cuckoo (Dromococcyx phasianellus) is a species of neotropical cuckoo in the subfamily Neomorphinae of the family Cuculidae.
f: It is native to Central and South America where it occurs in lowland tropical forest.

t: The southern scrub robin (Drymodes brunneopygia) is a species of bird in the family Petroicidae. Its range includes several disjoint regions from central New South Wales through western Victoria and southern South Australia, through to the southwestern area of Western Australia.
f: It is endemic to Australia, where it occurs in mallee and heathland in the semi-arid southern parts of the continent.
The East Andean antbird (Drymophila caudata) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The striated antbird (Drymophila devillei) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
The ferruginous antbird (Drymophila ferruginea) is an insectivorous bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
The rufous-tailed antbird (Drymophila genei) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The Santa Marta antbird (Drymophila hellmayri) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is endemic to the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in Colombia.

t: Klages's antbird (Drymophila klagesi) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The dusky-tailed antbird (Drymophila malura) is an insectivorous bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.
The ochre-rumped antbird (Drymophila ochropyga) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: Bertoni's antbird (Drymophila rubricollis) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.
The scaled antbird (Drymophila squamata) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The streak-headed antbird (Drymophila striaticeps) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The scimitar-billed woodcreeper (Drymornis bridgesii) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The red-cockaded woodpecker (Leuconotopicus borealis) is a woodpecker endemic to the southeastern United States.
f: It is a threatened species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973.

t: The scarlet-backed woodpecker (Veniliornis callonotus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador and Peru.

t: The crimson-naped woodpecker, crimson-breasted woodpecker or scarlet-breasted woodpecker (Dryobates cathpharius) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. It is found in Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar and Nepal.
f: It was previously considered conspecific with necklaced woodpecker.

t: The smoky-brown woodpecker (Leuconotopicus fumigatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Belize, Bolivia, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The red-rumped woodpecker (Veniliornis kirkii) is a species of bird in the subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found from Costa Rica south to Peru and east to Brazil, Guyana, and Trinidad and Tobago.

t: The lesser spotted woodpecker (Dryobates minor) is a member of the woodpecker family Picidae. Some taxonomic authorities continue to list the species there.
f: It was formerly assigned to the genus Dendrocopos (sometimes incorrectly spelt as Dendrocopus).

t: Nuttall's woodpecker (Dryobates nuttallii) is a species of woodpecker named after naturalist Thomas Nuttall in 1843.
f: They are found in oak woodlands of California and are similar to the ladder-backed woodpecker in both genetics and appearance.

t: The little woodpecker (Veniliornis passerinus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile, Suriname, and Uruguay.

t: The downy woodpecker (Dryobates pubescens) is a species of woodpecker, the smallest in North America. Length ranges from 14 to 18 cm (5.5 to 7.1 in).
f: The bird nests in tree cavities and feeds primarily on insects, although it supplements its diet with seeds and berries.
The ladder-backed woodpecker (Dryobates scalaris) is a North American woodpecker.

t: The Arizona woodpecker (L. arizonae) was formerly considered the northern subspecies of this bird until the 42nd supplement of the American Ornithologists Union checklist, which officially split them into two separate species.
f: Strickland's woodpecker (Leuconotopicus stricklandi) is a medium-sized species of woodpecker endemic to Mexico.

t: The hairy woodpecker (Leuconotopicus villosus) is a medium-sized woodpecker that is found over a large area of North America. With an estimated population in 2020 of almost nine million individuals, the hairy woodpecker is listed by the IUCN as a species of least concern.
f: It is approximately 250 mm (9.8 in) in length with a 380 mm (15 in) wingspan.

t: The white-bellied woodpecker or great black woodpecker (Dryocopus javensis) is a woodpecker species inhabiting evergreen forests in tropical Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. It has 14 subspecies, and many of its island forms are endangered, some are extinct.
f: It is among the largest of the Asiatic woodpeckers and nests in large dead trees, often beside rivers.
The lineated woodpecker (Dryocopus lineatus) is a very large woodpecker which is a resident breeding bird from southern Mexico to northern Argentina and Trinidad in the Caribbean.

t: The black woodpecker (Dryocopus martius) is a large woodpecker that lives in mature forests across the northern Palearctic. It is the sole representative of its genus in that region, and its range is expanding.
f: The black woodpecker is easily the largest woodpecker species in Europe as well as in the portion of Asia where it lives and is one of the largest species worldwide.

t: The pileated woodpecker ( PY-lee-ay-tid, PIL-ee-; Dryocopus pileatus) is a large, crow-sized woodpecker with a prominent red crest, white neck stripe, and a mostly black body. This woodpecker is native to North America, where it is the largest confirmed extant woodpecker species and the third-largest extant species of woodpecker in the world, after the great slaty woodpecker and the black woodpecker.
f: This woodpecker is primarily an insectivore, eating insects that live in trees; it is famous for making large, nearly rectangular carvings into trees, which are used to extract prey inside the tree or to make a nest.

t: The black-bodied woodpecker (Dryocopus schulzii) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, and Paraguay.

t: The white-throated rail (Dryolimnas cuvieri) or Cuvier's rail is a species of bird in the family Rallidae.
f: It is a fairly large rail, and has a flightless subspecies.

t: The Pine Barrens tree frog (Dryophytes andersonii) is a species of New World tree frog. Habitat loss is a concern because this species depends on specialized wetlands and shallow, acidic ponds to survive and reproduce.
f: It is becoming rare due to habitat loss.

t: The bird-voiced tree frog (Dryophytes avivoca) is a species of frog in the family Hylidae, endemic to the United States.
f: Its natural habitats are temperate forests, shrub-dominated wetlands, and swamps.

t: Cope's gray treefrog (Dryophytes chrysoscelis) is a species of treefrog found in the United States and Canada. It is almost indistinguishable from the gray treefrog (Dryophytes versicolor), and shares much of its geographic range.
f: The only readily noticeable difference between the two species is the mating call — Cope's has a faster-paced and slightly higher-pitched call than D. versicolor.

t: The American green tree frog (Dryophytes cinereus or Hyla cinerea) is a common arboreal species of New World tree frog belonging to the family Hylidae. Sometimes, light yellowish spots are present on the dorsum.
f: This nocturnal insectivore is moderately sized and has a bright green to reddish-brown coloration.
The pine woods tree frog (Dryophytes femoralis) is a species of frog in the family Hylidae, endemic to the southeastern United States.

t: Formerly known as Hyla gratiosa.
f: Dryophytes gratiosus, commonly known as the barking tree frog, is a species of tree frog endemic to the south-eastern United States.

t: The squirrel tree frog (Dryophytes squirellus) is a small species of tree frog found in the southeastern United States, from Texas to Virginia. It is an introduced species to the Bahamas.
f: They can also be varying shades of yellow or brown, sometimes with white or brown blotching.

t: The gray treefrog (Dryophytes versicolor) is a species of small arboreal frog in the family Hylidae. The species is native to much of the eastern United States and southeastern Canada.
f: It is sometimes referred to as the eastern gray treefrog, northern gray treefrog, common gray treefrog, or tetraploid gray treefrog to distinguish it from its more southern, genetically distinct relative, Cope's gray treefrog.

t: The black-backed puffback (Dryoscopus cubla) is a species of passerine bird in the family Malaconotidae. They are common to fairly common sedentary bushshrikes in various wooded habitats in Africa south of the equator.
f: They draw attention to themselves by their varied repertoire of whistling, clicking and rasping sounds.

t: The northern puffback (Dryoscopus gambensis) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in northern sub-Saharan Africa.
f: It forms a superspecies with the black-backed puffback, which replaces it in eastern equatorial and southern Africa.

t: The Congo serpent eagle (Circaetus spectabilis) is a species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. This species is distributed across the African tropical rainforest, including upper and lower Guinean forests.
f: It is a very vocal raptor, and often is one of the most heard species in its habitat.

t: The chestnut-bellied mountain tanager (Dubusia castaneoventris) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru.

t: The buff-banded mountain tanager (Dubusia taeniata), formerly known as the buff-breasted mountain tanager, is a species of Neotropical bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The green imperial pigeon (Ducula aenea) is a large forest pigeon.
f: The large range extends from Nepal, southern India and Sri Lanka eastwards to southern China, Indonesia and the Philippines.

The mountain imperial pigeon (Ducula badia), also known as the maroon-backed imperial pigeon or Hodgson's imperial pigeon, is a species of bird in the pigeon and dove family with a wide range in southeastern Asia.

t: The cinnamon-bellied imperial pigeon or cinnamon imperial pigeon (Ducula basilica) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. It is endemic to the northern Moluccas.
f: The cinnamon-bellied imperial pigeon was formally described in 1854 by the French naturalist Charles Lucien Bonaparte from a specimen collected in Gilolo now Halmahera, the largest island in the Maluku Islands.

t: The pied imperial pigeon (Ducula bicolor) is a relatively large, pied species of pigeon. It remains locally common, and is therefore considered to be of least concern by BirdLife International and IUCN.
f: It is mainly found on small islands and in coastal regions.

t: The elegant imperial pigeon (Ducula concinna), also known as blue-tailed imperial-pigeon, is a large pigeon, with upperparts mainly dark blue-green in colour with an iridescent sheen.
f: Head, neck and underparts are mostly pale grey, with red-brown undertail coverts.

t: The dark-backed imperial pigeon (Ducula lacernulata) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is endemic to the Lesser Sunda Islands.

t: The barking imperial pigeon (Ducula latrans), also known as Peale's imperial pigeon, is a species of bird in the pigeon family Columbidae. Its natural habitats are mature tropical moist lowland forests and tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is endemic to Fiji, where it occurs on most of the medium and large islands.

t: The Pacific imperial pigeon, Pacific pigeon, Pacific fruit pigeon or lupe (Ducula pacifica) is a widespread pigeon species in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in American Samoa, the Cook Islands, the smaller islands of eastern Fiji, Kiribati, Niue, the smaller satellite islands of Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tokelau, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu, and Wallis and Futuna Islands.

t: The spectacled imperial pigeon (Ducula perspicillata) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest, especially recently disturbed forests.
f: It is endemic to the Maluku Islands.

t: Pinon's imperial pigeon or Pinon imperial pigeon (Ducula pinon) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. Several subspecies have been designated: Ducula pinon pinon (Quoy and Gaimard) - Western Papuan Islands; Aru Islands; southern New Guinea from the Mimika River to Hall Sound.
f: The species is named after Rose de Freycinet née Pinon.

t: The island imperial pigeon or floury imperial pigeon (Ducula pistrinaria) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) has assessed it as a least-concern species.
f: It is found in the Bismarck Archipelago and the Solomon Islands archipelago, living in primary and secondary forests and mangroves.

t: The pink-bellied imperial pigeon (Ducula poliocephala), also known as the zone-tailed pigeon, is found in the Philippines. It is a large and striking dove reaching sizes of up to 42cm long.
f: It is illegal to hunt, capture or possess these birds under Philippine Law RA 9147.

t: The red-knobbed imperial pigeon (Ducula rubricera) is a bird species in the family Columbidae. It is found in Bismarck Archipelago and the Solomon Islands archipelago.
f: Red-knobbed imperial pigeons frequently forage in groups of five to ten individuals.

t: The Torresian imperial pigeon (Ducula spilorrhoa), also known as the nutmeg pigeon, white nutmeg pigeon, Australian pied imperial pigeon or Torres Strait pigeon (Meriam Mir: deumer), is a relatively large, pied species of pigeon. It is found in forest, woodland, savanna, mangrove and scrub in Australia , New Guinea, Aru Islands, islands in the Geelvink Bay, D'Entrecasteaux Islands and Louisiade Archipelago.
f: As far as known, most populations are resident or only take part in minor local movements.

t: Zoe's imperial pigeon or Zoe imperial pigeon (Ducula zoeae), also known as the banded imperial pigeon, is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical mangrove forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is named after Zoë Lesson (fl. 1810), the wife of French ornithologist René-Primevère Lesson, who described it.

t: The palmchat (Dulus dominicus) is a medium-sized passerine bird endemic to the Caribbean island of Hispaniola (split between the Dominican Republic and Haiti). It is the only species in the genus Dulus and the family Dulidae, and is related to the waxwing family Bombycillidae and the silky-flycatchers in Ptiliogonatidae.
f: Its name reflects its strong association with palms for feeding, roosting, and nesting.

t: The gray catbird (Dumetella carolinensis), also spelled grey catbird, is a medium-sized North American and Central American perching bird of the mimid family. It is the only member of the "catbird" genus Dumetella.
f: Like the black catbird (Melanoptila glabrirostris), it is among the basal lineages of the Mimidae, probably a closer relative of the Caribbean thrasher and trembler assemblage than of the mockingbirds and Toxostoma thrashers.

t: The dark-fronted babbler (Dumetia atriceps) is an Old World babbler found in the Western Ghats of India and the forests of Sri Lanka. They forage in flocks in the undergrowth of forests constantly making calls and uttering alarm calls when disturbed.
f: They are small chestnut brown birds with a dark black cap, a whitish underside and pale yellow iris.

t: The tawny-bellied babbler (Dumetia hyperythra) also known in older Indian works as the rufous-bellied babbler is a small babbler that forages in small groups in low scrub forests. Like other members of the large Old World babbler family they are passerine birds characterised by soft fluffy plumage.
f: The nominate hyperythra found in northern and eastern India is uniformly brown underneath while albogularis of the western Indian peninsula is white throated.

t: The white-streaked antvireo or white-spotted antvireo (Dysithamnus leucostictus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The plain antvireo (Dysithamnus mentalis) is a passerine bird species in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country except El Salvador, on both Trinidad and Tobago, and in every mainland South American country except Chile, French Guiana, Suriname, and Uruguay.

t: The bicolored antvireo (Dysithamnus occidentalis) is a Near Threatened insectivorous bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
The plumbeous antvireo (Dysithamnus plumbeus) is a Vulnerable species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The spot-crowned antvireo (Dysithamnus puncticeps) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, and Panama.
The spot-breasted antvireo (Dysithamnus stictothorax) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The streak-crowned antvireo (Dysithamnus striaticeps) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Honduras, and Nicaragua.
The rufous-backed antvireo (Dysithamnus xanthopterus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The Moluccan eclectus (Eclectus roratus) is a parrot native to the Maluku Islands (Moluccas). Joseph Forshaw, in his book Parrots of the World, noted that the first European ornithologists to see eclectus parrots thought they were of two distinct species.
f: It is unusual in the parrot order for its extreme sexual dimorphism of the colours of the plumage; the male having a mostly bright emerald green plumage and the female a mostly bright red and purple/blue plumage.

t: The black-bellied cuckooshrike or black-bellied cicadabird (Edolisoma montanum) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

t: The Sahul cicadabird (Edolisoma tenuirostre), previously known as the common cicadabird or slender-billed cicadabird, is a species of passerine bird in the family Campephagidae. It is found in Australia, New Guinea and the Bismarck Archipelago.
f: The common cicadabird was described as a "great speciator" by Mayr & Diamond (2001); and Pedersen et al. (2018) described how this species rapidly colonized and diversified across the Indo-Pacific island region and Australia in the Pleistocene.

t: The little blue heron (Egretta caerulea) is a small heron of the genus Egretta. It is a small, darkly colored heron with a two-toned bill.
f: As with clutch sizes, diet can vary regionally.
The Chinese egret or Swinhoe's egret (Egretta eulophotes) is a threatened species of egret from east Asia, first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1860.

t: The little egret (Egretta garzetta) is a species of small heron in the family Ardeidae. It is a white bird with a slender black beak, long black legs and, in the western race, yellow feet.
f: At one time common in Western Europe, it was hunted extensively in the 19th century to provide plumes for the decoration of hats and became locally extinct in northwestern Europe and scarce in the south.

t: The western reef heron (Egretta gularis), also called the western reef egret, is a medium-sized heron found in Africa and parts of Asia, with vagrancy occurring in Europe and the Americas. There have been suggestions that the species hybridizes with the little egret, and based on this, some authors treat schistacea and gularis as subspecies of Egretta garzetta.
f: There are also differences in size, structure and foraging behaviour.

t: It is a medium-sized heron, pale, slightly bluish-grey, with yellow legs and white facial markings.
f: It can be found almost anywhere near shallow water, fresh or salt, and although it is prompt to depart the scene on long, slow-beating wings if disturbed, it will boldly raid suburban fish ponds.

t: The reddish egret (Egretta rufescens) is a medium-sized heron that is a resident breeder in Central America, the Bahamas, the Caribbean, the Gulf Coast of the United States (primarily Texas), and Mexico. In the past, this bird was a victim of the plume trade and is North America's "rarest and least studied ardeid."
f: The egret is known for its unusual foraging behavior compared to other herons as well as its association with mud flats, its habitat of choice.

t: The Pacific reef heron (Egretta sacra), also known as the eastern reef heron or eastern reef egret, is a species of heron found throughout southern Asia and Oceania. It occurs in two colour morphs with either slaty grey or pure white plumage.
f: The sexes are similar in appearance.

t: The snowy egret (Egretta thula) is a small white heron. The genus name comes from Provençal French for the little egret, aigrette, which is a diminutive of aigron, 'heron'.
f: At one time, the plumes of the snowy egret were in great demand as decorations for women's hats.

t: The tricolored heron (Egretta tricolor), formerly known as the Louisiana heron, is a small species of heron native to coastal parts of the Americas.
f: The species is more solitary than other species of heron in the Americas and eats a diet consisting mostly of small fish.

t: In the past it was included in the babbler genus Spelaeornis as S. formosus, but molecular phylogenetic studies in 2014 provided evidence that it was distinct from the babblers, having no other close living relatives within the passerine bird clade Passerida. This led to the creation of a new family, Elachuridae, to accommodate just one species (a monotypic taxon).
f: The spotted elachura or spotted wren-babbler (Elachura formosa) is a species of passerine bird found in the forests of the eastern Himalayas and Southeast Asia.

t: The white-crested elaenia (Elaenia albiceps) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: Coopmans's elaenia (Elaenia brachyptera) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The lesser elaenia (Elaenia chiriquensis) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, on Trinidad, in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay, and as a vagrant on Bonaire and Curaçao.

t: The plain-crested elaenia (Elaenia cristata) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.
The Blue Mountain elaenia (Elaenia fallax) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.

t: The yellow-bellied elaenia (Elaenia flavogaster) is a small bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Mexico, in every Central American country, in every mainland South American country except Chile, on Trinidad and Tobago, and on several islands in the Lesser Antilles.

t: The mountain elaenia (Elaenia frantzii) is a small passerine bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, and Venezuela.

t: The mottle-backed elaenia (Elaenia gigas) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The Caribbean elaenia (Elaenia martinica) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in the West Indies, in parts of Central America, and on islands just off the northern South American coast.

t: The olivaceous elaenia (Elaenia mesoleuca) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The highland elaenia (Elaenia obscura) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The tepui elaenia (Elaenia olivina) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Brazil, Guyana, and Venezuela.

t: The sierran elaenia (Elaenia pallatangae) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The small-billed elaenia (Elaenia parvirostris) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile, plus Aruba and Trinidad.

t: The rufous-crowned elaenia (Elaenia ruficeps) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The small-headed elaenia (Elaenia sordida), also known as the Brazilian elaenia, is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The large elaenia (Elaenia spectabilis) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: The slaty elaenia (Elaenia strepera) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Peru, and Venezuela, and as a vagrant in Ecuador and on Trinidad.

t: The swallow-tailed kite (Elanoides forficatus) is a pernine raptor which breeds from the southeastern United States to eastern Peru and northern Argentina. It is the only species in the genus Elanoides.
f: Most North and Central American breeders winter in South America where the species is resident year round.

t: The black-winged kite (Elanus caeruleus), also known as the black-shouldered kite , is a small diurnal bird of prey in the family Accipitridae best known for its habit of hovering over open grasslands in the manner of the much smaller kestrels. This Palearctic and Afrotropical species was sometimes combined with the Australian black-shouldered kite (Elanus axillaris) and the white-tailed kite (Elanus leucurus) of North and South America which together form a superspecies.
f: They are well adapted to utilize periodic upsurges in rodent populations and can raise multiple broods in a single year unlike most birds of prey.

t: The white-tailed kite (Elanus leucurus) is a small raptor found in South America and parts of western North America.
f: It replaces the related Old World black-winged kite in its native range.

t: The keel-billed motmot (Electron carinatum) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the motmot family Momotidae.
f: It is found in Belize, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: The broad-billed motmot (Electron platyrhynchum) is a fairly common Central and South American bird of the Momotidae family. There exist six subspecies of the broad-billed motmot.
f: They are nonmigratory, sedentary birds that are most frequently seen in singles or pairs.

t: The white-breasted tapaculo (Eleoscytalopus indigoticus) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is endemic to the Atlantic forest of southeastern Brazil.

t: The sickle-winged nightjar (Eleothreptus anomalus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and possibly Uruguay.

The greenhouse frog (Eleutherodactylus planirostris) is a species of frog in the family Eleutherodactylidae, native to Cuba, the Bahamas, and the Cayman Islands, and it has been introduced to other areas, such as Florida, Hawaii, Guam, Hong Kong and Shenzhen.

t: The white-bellied hummingbird (Elliotomyia chionogaster) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The white-tailed crested flycatcher (Elminia albonotata) is a species of bird in the flycatcher family Stenostiridae. It has a discontinuous distribution in eastern Africa.
f: They are monogamous, at the start of the season the male displays to the female using its tail and feeds the female.
The African blue flycatcher or blue-crested flycatcher (Elminia longicauda) is a species of bird in the family Stenostiridae from western and central Sub-Saharan Africa.
The black-fronted dotterel (Thinornis melanops) is a small plover in the family Charadriidae that is found throughout much of Australia and New Zealand.

t: The sickle-winged chat or sicklewing chat (Emarginata sinuata) is a small passerine bird of the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae endemic to southern Africa. It is a common resident breeder in South Africa and Lesotho, and is also found in southernmost areas of Botswana and Namibia.
f: In western coastal areas, it also occurs on agricultural land.

t: The yellow-breasted bunting (Emberiza aureola) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae that is found across the Boreal and East Palearctic. The genus name Emberiza is from Old German Embritz, a bunting.
f: The bird's call is a distinctive zick, and the song is a clear tru-tru, tri-tri.

t: The red-headed bunting (Emberiza bruniceps) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae. It breeds in central Asia, including Afghanistan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia; Russia (European Russia, Central Asian Russia), Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and China.
f: The song, given from a high perch, is a jerky sweet-sweet-churri-churri-churri.

t: The grey-necked bunting (Emberiza buchanani), sometimes referred to as grey-hooded bunting (a name also in use for chestnut-eared bunting) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae. Like other buntings it is found in small flocks.
f: It breeds along a wide distribution range from the Caspian Sea to the Altai Mountains in Central Asia and winters in parts of Southern Asia.

t: Cabanis's bunting (Emberiza cabanisi) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae. The common name and Latin binomial commemorate the German ornithologist Jean Louis Cabanis.
f: It is found across most of sub-Saharan Africa in its natural habitats of subtropical or tropical dry forests and dry savannah.
Cretzschmar's bunting (Emberiza caesia) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group now separated by most modern authors from the finches, Fringillidae.

t: The corn bunting (Emberiza calandra) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group now separated by most modern authors from the finches, Fringillidae. This is a large bunting with heavily streaked buff-brown plumage.
f: The sexes are similar but the male is slightly larger than the female.
The Cape bunting (Emberiza capensis) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae.

t: The yellow-browed bunting (Emberiza chrysophrys) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group now separated by most modern taxonomists from the finches (Fringillidae). The genus name Emberiza is from Old German Embritz, a bunting.
f: In the wild, the adults' diet consists of seeds, but they feed insects to nestlings.

t: The rock bunting (Emberiza cia) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group now separated by most modern authors from the finches, Fringillidae. The genus name Emberiza is from Old German Embritz, a bunting.
f: The specific cia is from a local Italian name for this bird, from zirlare, "to chirp".

t: The cinereous bunting (Emberiza cineracea) is a bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a passerine family now separated by most modern authors from the finches, Fringillidae.
f: This species was first described by Christian Ludwig Brehm.
The meadow bunting or Siberian meadow bunting (Emberiza cioides) is a passerine bird of eastern Asia which belongs to the genus Emberiza in the bunting family Emberizidae.

t: The cirl bunting ( SURL) (Emberiza cirlus) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group now separated by most modern authors from the finches, Fringillidae. It breeds across southern Europe, on the Mediterranean islands and in north Africa.
f: It is a resident of these warmer areas, and does not migrate in winter.

t: The yellowhammer (Emberiza citrinella) is a passerine bird in the bunting family that is native to Eurasia and has been introduced to New Zealand and Australia. Most European birds remain in the breeding range year-round, but the eastern subspecies is partially migratory, with much of the population wintering further south.
f: Its song has a rhythm like "A little bit of bread and no cheese".

t: The yellow-throated bunting (Emberiza elegans), also known as the elegant bunting, is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae. It is found in China, Japan, Korea, Myanmar, Russia, and Taiwan.
f: Emberiza elegans follows Type II chain migration.

t: The golden-breasted bunting (Emberiza flaviventris) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae.
f: It occurs in dry open woodlands and moist savanna in Africa south of the Sahara, but is absent from the equatorial forest belt.

t: The chestnut-eared bunting (Emberiza fucata), also called grey-headed bunting or grey-hooded bunting, with the latter name also used for grey-necked bunting, is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae. The genus name Emberiza is from Old German Embritz, a bunting.
f: The specific fucata is Latin for "painted" from fucare, "to paint red".

t: Godlewski's bunting (Emberiza godlewskii) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae.
f: It is named after the Polish collector Victor Godlewski who obtained a specimen of which on the basis of which it was described by Taczanowski.

t: The ortolan (Emberiza hortulana), also called ortolan bunting, is a Eurasian bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a passerine family now separated by most modern scholars from the finches, Fringillidae. The genus name Emberiza is from Alemannic German Embritz, a bunting.
f: The specific name hortulana is from the Italian name for this bird, ortolana.

t: The lark-like bunting (Emberiza impetuani) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae, which is native to south-western Africa. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.
f: It is found in Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia, South Africa, and Zimbabwe.

t: The crested bunting (Emberiza lathami) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae. It is sparrow sized with males having rufous wings and tail on a black body and females being less contrastingly coloured in dull brown.
f: Both males and females have the distinctive crest.

t: The pine bunting (Emberiza leucocephalos) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group most modern authors now separate from the finches, Fringillidae.
f: It lives in Eurosiberia east of the Urals.

t: The black-headed bunting (Emberiza melanocephala) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae. It breeds in south-east Europe east to Iran and migrates in winter mainly to India, with some individuals moving further into south-east Asia.
f: In other plumages, they can be hard to separate from the closely related red-headed bunting and natural hybridization occurs between the two species in the zone of overlap of their breeding ranges in northern Iran.
Pallas's reed bunting (Emberiza pallasi), also known as Pallas's bunting, is a passerine bird in the Old World bunting family, Emberizidae.
The little bunting (Emberiza pusilla) is a passerine bird belonging to the bunting family (Emberizidae).

t: The rustic bunting (Emberiza rustica) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group now separated by most modern authors from the finches, Fringillidae. The genus name Emberiza is from Old German Embritz, a bunting.
f: The call is a zit, similar to that of a song thrush (Turdus philomelos), and the song is a melancholic delee-deloo-delee.

t: The house bunting (Emberiza sahari) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae. It is a resident breeder of dry country from northwestern Africa from Morocco south to Mali and east to Chad.
f: The house bunting bred in Europe for the first time in 2023, in Algeciras in southern Spain.

t: The common reed bunting (Emberiza schoeniclus), or simply reed bunting, is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae. This species breeds throughout Europe and much of the Palearctic region.
f: While most individuals migrate south in winter, those in the milder south and west of the range are resident.

t: The black-faced bunting (Emberiza spodocephala) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group now separated by most modern authors from the finches, Fringillidae. The genus name Emberiza is from Old German Embritz, a bunting.
f: It sound very "metallic" and it is a very short and not exactly a song at all.

t: The white-capped bunting or chestnut-breasted bunting (Emberiza stewarti) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae. Its natural habitats are boreal forests, boreal shrubland, and temperate grassland.
f: It is found in Afghanistan, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Nepal, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan.
The striolated bunting (Emberiza striolata) is a passerine bird in the bunting family Emberizidae, a group now separated by most modern authors from the finches, Fringillidae.

t: The yellow bunting or Japanese yellow bunting (Emberiza sulphurata) is a passerine bird of eastern Asia in the bunting family Emberizidae. It is threatened by habitat loss, the use of pesticides and trapping for the cagebird industry.
f: The name "yellow bunting" can also refer to the yellowhammer (Emberiza citrinella).

t: The cinnamon-breasted bunting (Emberiza tahapisi) or cinnamon-breasted rock-bunting is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae.
f: It is widespread in Africa south of the Sahara.

t: Tristram's bunting (Emberiza tristrami) is a bird in the family Emberizidae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1870.
f: It is accidental in Japan, Korea, Laos, Myanmar, Russia, Mongolia, Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam and north-eastern India.

t: The grey bunting (Emberiza variabilis) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae. Its natural habitats are boreal forests and temperate forests.
f: It breeds in southern Kamchatka, Sakhalin, Kuril Islands and northern Japan, it migrates to southern Japan and the Nansei archipelago.

t: The ochre-rumped bunting (Emberiza yessoensis), also known as the Japanese reed bunting, is a bird in the family Emberizidae. It is found in Manchuria, Korea and Japan.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The wedge-tailed grass finch (Emberizoides herbicola) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Colombia, Panama, and every mainland South American country except Chile.

t: The lesser grass finch (Emberizoides ypiranganus), also known as the gray-cheeked grass-finch, is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
The serra finch or pale-throated Pampa-finch (Embernagra longicauda) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.

t: The Pampa finch (Embernagra platensis), also known as the great Pampa-finch, is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The grey-capped warbler (Eminia lepida) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It is monotypic (only species) in the genus Eminia.
f: Grey-capped warblers maintain a diet of insects and other invertebrates, including caterpillars, moths, grasshoppers, and mantids.

t: The pine flycatcher (Empidonax affinis) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers. It is found in Guatemala and Mexico.
f: It has also been recorded as a vagrant to Arizona in the U.S.A.

t: The white-throated flycatcher (Empidonax albigularis) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Mexico and every country in Central America.

t: The alder flycatcher (Empidonax alnorum) is a small insect-eating bird in the tyrant flycatcher family. The genus name Empidonax is from Ancient Greek empis, "gnat", and anax, "master".
f: The specific alnorum is Latin and means "of the alders".

t: The black-capped flycatcher (Empidonax atriceps) is a very small passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The western flycatcher (Empidonax difficilis) is a small insectivorous bird in the family Tyrannidae.
f: It is native to western North America, where it breeds in the Rocky Mountains and Pacific Coast forests and mountain ranges from California to Alaska and south to central Mexico; northern populations migrate south to Mexico for the winter.

t: The yellowish flycatcher (Empidonax flavescens) is a small passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found from Mexico to Panama.
The yellow-bellied flycatcher (Empidonax flaviventris) is a small insect-eating bird of the tyrant flycatcher family.

t: The buff-breasted flycatcher (Empidonax fulvifrons) is a small passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found from the southwestern U.S.A. to Honduras.

t: Hammond's flycatcher (Empidonax hammondii) is a flycatcher in the family Tyrannidae. This small insectivorous bird inhabits the coniferous and mixed forests of western North America.
f: The name of this bird commemorates William Alexander Hammond who was the surgeon general of the US Army.

t: The least flycatcher (Empidonax minimus) (also called chebec, or chebecker, after the sound it makes) is a small insect-eating bird.
f: It is the smallest Empidonax flycatcher in eastern North America.

t: The American dusky flycatcher (Empidonax oberholseri), or simply dusky flycatcher, is a small insectivorous passerine of the tyrant flycatcher family. The dusky flycatcher is one of many species in the genus Empidonax.
f: These species are very similar in appearance and behavior, and they are notoriously difficult to differentiate.

t: The western flycatcher (Empidonax difficilis) is a small insectivorous bird in the family Tyrannidae.
f: It is native to western North America, where it breeds in the Rocky Mountains and Pacific Coast forests and mountain ranges from California to Alaska and south to central Mexico; northern populations migrate south to Mexico for the winter.
The willow flycatcher (Empidonax traillii) is a small insect-eating, migrant bird of the tyrant flycatcher family native to North America.
The Acadian flycatcher (Empidonax virescens) is a small insect-eating bird of the tyrant flycatcher family.

t: The American gray flycatcher, American grey flycatcher, or just gray flycatcher (Empidonax wrightii) as it is known in North America, is a small, insectivorous passerine in the tyrant flycatcher family. It is common in the arid regions of western North America, especially the Great Basin.
f: The American gray flycatcher, however, can be identified by a unique behavior, its downward tail wag.

t: The crowned slaty flycatcher (Empidonomus aurantioatrocristatus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers. It is found in every mainland South American country except Suriname though only as a vagrant to Chile, French Guiana, and Venezuela.
f: There are also single records of it in Panama and the U.S. state of Louisiana.

t: The variegated flycatcher (Empidonomus varius) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers. It is found on Trinidad and in every mainland South American country except Chile.
f: In addition it has been documented as a vagrant in several U.S. states and the Canadian province of Ontario.

t: The austral parakeet, austral conure, cachaña, rawilma or emerald parakeet (Enicognathus ferrugineus) is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Argentina, Chile, and possibly the Falkland Islands.

t: The slender-billed parakeet (Enicognathus leptorhynchus) or choroy, is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is endemic to Chile, where it is known by the local common name choroy.

t: The white-crowned forktail (Enicurus leschenaulti) is a species of forktail in the family Muscicapidae. Formally described in 1818, it has five subspecies, each occupying a different geographic range.
f: The largest of the forktails, Enicurus leschenaulti, is between 25 and 28 centimetres (9.8 and 11.0 in) long.

t: The spotted forktail (Enicurus maculatus) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is found in the Himalayas and the hills of Northeast India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and southern China including Yunnan.
f: The tail is deeply forked, graduated black and white.

t: The slaty-backed forktail (Enicurus schistaceus) is a species of forktail in the family Muscicapidae. A slim, medium-sized forktail, it is distinguished from similar species by its slate grey forehead, crown, and mantle.
f: It breeds between February and July, laying 3–4 pinkish, bluish, or white eggs; both sexes incubate the eggs.

t: The black solitaire (Entomodestes coracinus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes.

t: The white-eared solitaire (Entomodestes leucotis) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes.

t: The blue-faced honeyeater (Entomyzon cyanotis), also colloquially known as the bananabird, is a passerine bird of the honeyeater family, Meliphagidae. It is the only member of its genus, and it is most closely related to honeyeaters of the genus Melithreptus.
f: They often take over and renovate old babbler nests, in which the female lays and incubates two or rarely three eggs.

t: The galah (; Eolophus roseicapilla), less commonly known as the pink and grey cockatoo, galah cockatoo, or rose-breasted cockatoo, is an Australian species of cockatoo and the only member of the genus Eolophus. The species is endemic to mainland Australia.
f: The galah is adapted to a wide variety of modified and unmodified habitats and is one of Australia's most abundant and widespread bird species.
The Chinese grosbeak, yellow-billed grosbeak, or black-tailed hawfinch (Eophona migratoria) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae.

t: The Japanese grosbeak (Eophona personata) or Ikaru is a finch native to the East Palearctic.
f: It is also sometimes referred to as the Japanese or masked hawfinch due to superficial similarities to the well-known Eurasian species.

t: The eastern yellow robin (Eopsaltria australis) is an Australasian robin of coastal and sub-coastal eastern Australia. Tropical Northern Queensland birds are mainly restricted to the warm heights of the Great Dividing Range.
f: The extent of the eastern yellow robin's residence is from the extreme southeast corner of South Australia through most of Victoria and the eastern half of New South Wales and north as far as Cooktown.

t: The saddle-billed stork or saddlebill (Ephippiorhynchus senegalensis) is a large wading bird in the stork family, Ciconiidae. It is a widespread species which is a resident breeder in sub-Saharan Africa from Sudan, Ethiopia, and Kenya south to South Africa and in the Gambia, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, and Chad in west Africa.
f: It is considered endangered in South Africa.

t: The black sicklebill (Epimachus fastosus) is a large member of the birds of paradise family, Paradisaeidae.
f: This species is found throughout most of central New Guinea and the Vogelkop region to the northwest in montane forests at altitudes from 1,800 to 2,150 m (5,900 to 7,100 ft).

t: The brown sicklebill (Epimachus meyeri) is a species of bird-of-paradise that is found in the mountain forests of New Guinea. Its appearance resembles the closely related and larger black sicklebill.
f: Its diet consists mainly of fruits, arthropods and small animals.

t: The Rio Madeira stipplethroat (Epinecrophylla amazonica) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds". It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.
f: In the past it has also been called eastern stipple-throated antwren, Madeira stipple-throated antwren, Rio Madeira antwren, and Madeira antwren.

t: The rufous-tailed stipplethroat (Epinecrophylla erythrura), formerly called the rufous-tailed antwren, is a species of insectivorous bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The checker-throated stipplethroat (Epinecrophylla fulviventris), previously called fulvous-bellied antwren or checker-throated antwren, is a small passerine bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The brown-bellied stipplethroat, previously called brown-bellied antwren (Epinecrophylla gutturalis) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The rufous-backed stipplethroat (Epinecrophylla haematonota) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds". In its complex taxonomic history, Epinecrophylla haematonota has also been called the rufous-backed antwren, stipple-throated antwren, Napo stipple-throated antwren, and western stipple-throated antwren.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The white-eyed stipplethroat, previously called white-eyed antwren (Epinecrophylla leucophthalma), is a species of bird in the family Thamnophilidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The ornate stipplethroat (Epinecrophylla ornata), formerly called the ornate antwren, is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The foothill stipplethroat (Epinecrophylla spodionota), previously called the foothill antwren, is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The crimson chat (Epthianura tricolor) is a species of small bird found in Australia.
f: It is also known as the tricoloured chat, saltbush canary, and crimson-breasted nun.

t: The Karoo eremomela (Eremomela gregalis), also known as the yellow-rumped eremomela, is a species of bird formerly placed in the "Old World warbler" assemblage, but now placed in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.
f: It is found in Namibia and South Africa.

t: The yellow-bellied eremomela (Eremomela icteropygialis) is an Old World warbler. However, the taxonomy of the "African warblers", an assemblage of usually species-poor and apparently rather ancient "odd warblers" from Africa is currently in a state of flux.
f: The yellow-bellied eremomela is a common breeding species in Africa south of the Sahara in its habitat of open woodland, savannah, and dry scrub.

t: The Senegal eremomela (Eremomela pusilla) is a member of the African warbler family, the Cisticolidae.
f: It occurs in the savannas of western Sub-Saharan Africa.
The green-capped eremomela or greencap eremomela (Eremomela scotops) is a species of bird formerly placed in the "Old World warbler" assemblage, but now placed in the family Cisticolidae.

t: The horned lark or shore lark (Eremophila alpestris) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found across the northern hemisphere.

t: The ashy-crowned sparrow-lark (Eremopterix griseus) is a small sparrow-sized member of the lark family. It is found in the plains in open land with bare ground, grass and scrub across South Asia.

t: The black-crowned sparrow-lark (Eremopterix nigriceps) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae. Its natural habitat is dry savanna.
f: It is found across northern Africa from Mauritania through the Middle East to north-western India.

t: The European robin (Erithacus rubecula), known simply as the robin or robin redbreast in the British Isles, is a small insectivorous passerine bird belonging to the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. It is found across Europe, as far east as Western Siberia, and as far south as North Africa.
f: First-winter immatures resemble the adults, except they have more obvious yellow-brown tips to the wing covert feathers, which are inconspicuous or absent in adults.

t: The white-bellied erpornis (Erpornis zantholeuca) or simply erpornis is a species of bird. It is the only member of the genus Erpornis.
f: This bird is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brunei, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The little yellow flycatcher (Erythrocercus holochlorus) is a species of bird in the family Erythrocercidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist shrubland.

t: The black-necklaced scimitar babbler (Erythrogenys erythrocnemis) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

t: The rusty-cheeked scimitar babbler (Erythrogenys erythrogenys) is a passerine bird in the babbler family Timaliidae that is found in the Himalayas from northeast Pakistan to Bhutan.
f: It was formerly considered as conspecific with the red-eyed scimitar babbler that is found in eastern Myanmar and northwestern Thailand.

t: The black-streaked scimitar babbler (Erythrogenys gravivox) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae.
f: It is found in China, Laos, Myanmar and Vietnam, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

t: The large scimitar babbler (Erythrogenys hypoleucos) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

t: The spot-breasted scimitar babbler (Erythrogenys mcclellandi) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae. It is found in Eastern Himalaya and western Myanmar.

t: The grey-sided scimitar babbler (Erythrogenys swinhoei) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae.

t: The blue-banded pitta (Erythropitta arquata) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae.

t: The Philippine pitta (Erythropitta erythrogaster) or blue-breasted pitta, is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. It is found in Indonesia and the Philippines.

t: The garnet pitta (Erythropitta granatina) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The Papuan pitta (Erythropitta macklotii) is a species of pitta. It was formerly considered a subspecies of the red-bellied pitta.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The North Moluccan pitta (Erythropitta rufiventris) is a species of pitta. It was long considered a subspecies of the red-bellied pitta, but was split on the basis of genetic and morphological studies.
f: It is endemic to Indonesia where it occurs on the northern Moluccas.

t: The black-crowned pitta (Erythropitta ussheri), also known as the black-headed pitta, black-and-crimson pitta, black-and-scarlet pitta or black-crowned garnet pitta, is a brightly coloured, ground-dwelling, bird species in the pitta family Pittidae.
f: It is endemic to the Southeast Asian island of Borneo.

t: It has an estimated global extent of occurrence of 10,000,000 km2. It is found in subtropical and tropical zones in both montane and lowland moist forest areas, where it is most often associated with forest edges and disturbed habitat.
f: It feeds largely on seeds of grasses, including in Australia several exotic genera especially Brachiaria.

t: The beach stone-curlew (Esacus magnirostris) or beach thick-knee is a large, ground-dwelling bird that occurs in Australasia, the islands of South-east Asia. At 55 cm (22 in) and 1 kg (2.2 lb), it is one of the world's largest shorebirds.
f: It is less strictly nocturnal than most stone-curlews, and can sometimes be seen foraging by daylight, moving slowly and deliberately, with occasional short runs.

t: The common waxbill (Estrilda astrild), also known as the St Helena waxbill, is a small passerine bird belonging to the estrildid finch family. f: It is popular and easy to keep in captivity.

t: The black-crowned waxbill (Estrilda nonnula) is a common species of estrildid finch found in western-central Africa.

t: The fawn-breasted waxbill (Estrilda paludicola) is a common species of estrildid finch found in central Africa. Estrilda paludicola, E. ochrogaster and E. poliopareia have been lumped into E. paludicola (Dowsett and Forbes-Watson 1993).
f: It has an estimated global extent of occurrence of 1,800,000 km2.

t: The black-rumped waxbill (Estrilda troglodytes) is a common species of estrildid finch found in Southern Africa. The status of the species is evaluated as Least Concern.

t: The red-headed barbet (Eubucco bourcierii) is a species of bird in the family Capitonidae, the New World barbets.
