t: The lemon-throated barbet (Eubucco richardsoni) is a species of bird in the New World barbet family Capitonidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The rufous-rumped antwren (Euchrepomis callinota) is a species of bird in subfamily Euchrepomidinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The chestnut-shouldered antwren (Euchrepomis humeralis) is a species of bird in subfamily Euchrepomidinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The ash-winged antwren (Euchrepomis spodioptila) is a species of bird in subfamily Euchrepomidinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, Venezuela, and possibly Peru.

t: The grey-headed tanager (Eucometis penicillata) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country except El Salvador, and every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, French Guiana, and Uruguay.

t: The American white ibis (Eudocimus albus) is a species of bird in the ibis family, Threskiornithidae. It is found from the southern half of the US East Coast (from southern New Jersey to Georgia), along the Gulf Coast states (Florida, Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana and Texas) and south through most of the Caribbean coastal regions of Central America.
f: Crayfish are its preferred food in most regions, but it can adjust its diet according to the habitat and prey abundance.

t: The elegant crested tinamou or martineta tinamou (Eudromia elegans) is a medium-sized tinamou that can be found in southern Chile and Argentina in Shrubland. This species is terrestrial due to their poor flying ability.
f: The bird has an omnivorous diet.

t: The black-billed koel (Eudynamys melanorhynchus) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It has often been considered conspecific with E. scolopaceus, but they are increasingly treated as separate species.
f: It is endemic to forest and woodland on the Indonesian islands of Sulawesi, Sula, Banggai, Togian and other smaller nearby islands.

t: The Pacific koel (Eudynamys orientalis), also known as the eastern koel or formerly common koel, is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae.
f: In northern Australia, it is colloquially known as the rainbird or stormbird.

t: The Asian koel (Eudynamys scolopaceus) is a member of the cuckoo family of birds, the Cuculidae. It is found in the Indian subcontinent, China, and Southeast Asia.
f: They are unusual among the cuckoos in being largely frugivorous as adults.

t: The western rockhopper penguin (Eudyptes chrysocome) is a species of rockhopper penguin. It occurs in subantarctic waters around the southern coast of South America and nearby islands.
f: These two taxa together had previously also been considered conspecific with the northern rockhopper penguin (E. moseleyi).

t: The little penguin (Eudyptula minor) is the smallest species of penguin in the world, and originates from New Zealand and Australia. It is commonly known as the fairy penguin, little blue penguin, or blue penguin, owing to its slate-blue plumage, and is also known by its Māori name kororā.
f: Eudyptula minor feathers are dense in melanosomes, which increase water resistance and give them their unique blue colour.

t: Rivoli's hummingbird (Eugenes fulgens), also known as the magnificent hummingbird, is a species of hummingbird in the "mountain gems", tribe Lampornithini in subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, and the United States.

t: The Talamanca hummingbird (Eugenes spectabilis) or admirable hummingbird, is a species of hummingbird in the "mountain gems", tribe Lampornithini in subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The ochre-flanked tapaculo (Eugralla paradoxa) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in south-central Chile and adjacent western Argentina.

t: The turquoise-browed motmot (Eumomota superciliosa) is a colourful, medium-sized bird of the motmot family, Momotidae. It is the only species in its genus Eumomota.
f: It has a preference for higher tree diversity and richness, alongside a low open canopy and dense understory.

t: The Nilgiri flycatcher (Eumyias albicaudatus) is an Old World flycatcher with a very restricted range in the hills of southern India. It was formerly referred to as the Nilgiri verditer flycatcher because of its similarity to the verditer flycatcher, a winter migrant to the Nilgiris, which, however, has distinct dark lores and a lighter shade of blue.
f: There are two small white patches at the base of the tail.

t: The indigo flycatcher (Eumyias indigo) is a species of bird in the Old World flycatcher family, Muscicapidae. Its natural habitat is tropical moist submontane montane forests between 900m to 3000m, where it is a common to fairly common species.
f: It is found in Indonesia and Malaysia, where it is found in Sumatra, Java and northern montane areas of Borneo.

t: The turquoise flycatcher (Eumyias panayensis), also known as the island flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Indonesia (Sulawesi, Maluku, Ambon) and the Philippines.

t: The verditer flycatcher (Eumyias thalassinus) is an Old World flycatcher. It is found from the Himalayas through Southeast Asia to Sumatra.
f: This species is named after its distinctive shade of copper-sulphate blue and has a dark patch between the eyes and above the bill base.
Eunemobius carolinus, the Carolina ground cricket, is a species of ground cricket in the family Trigonidiidae.

t: The African silverbill (Euodice cantans) is a small passerine bird formerly considered conspecific with the Asian species Indian silverbill, (Euodice malabarica). This species has also been introduced to other countries such as Portugal, Qatar and United States.
f: This estrildid finch is a common resident breeding bird in dry savanna habitat, south of the Sahara Desert.

t: The Indian silverbill or white-throated munia (Euodice malabarica) is a small passerine bird found in the Indian subcontinent and adjoining regions that was formerly considered to include the closely related African silverbill (Euodice cantans). It has also been introduced into many other parts of the world and has become established in some areas.
f: This estrildid finch is a common resident breeding bird in the drier regions of the Middle East and the Indian subcontinent.

t: The rail-babbler or Malaysian rail-babbler (Eupetes macrocerus) is a brown and pied rail-like ground-living bird. It is the only species in the genus Eupetes and family Eupetidae.
f: It is distantly related to African rockfowl.
The sombre hummingbird (Eupetomena cirrochloris) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.

t: The swallow-tailed hummingbird (Eupetomena macroura) is a species in the hummingbird family (Trochilidae), found mainly in east-central South America. Most authorities place it in the genus Eupetomena, although some place it in Campylopterus based on song and the thick shafts of the males' first primaries.
f: Its common name and specific epithet (which means "large-tailed") both refer to the long, deeply forked, somewhat swallow-like tail.

t: The rusty blackbird (Euphagus carolinus) is a medium-sized New World blackbird, closely related to grackles ("rusty grackle" is an older name for the species). Formerly abundant, the rusty blackbird has undergone one of the most rapid declines of any abundant bird species in North America in recent years, for reasons that are not well understood.
f: It is a bird that prefers wet forested areas, breeding in the boreal forest and muskeg across northern Canada, and migrating southeast to the United States during winter.

t: Brewer's blackbird (Euphagus cyanocephalus) is a medium-sized New World blackbird.
f: It is named after the ornithologist Thomas Mayo Brewer.

t: The stripe-tailed hummingbird (Eupherusa eximia) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found from southeastern Mexico to Panama.

t: The scrub euphonia (Euphonia affinis) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found from Mexico to Costa Rica.

t: The tawny-capped euphonia (Euphonia anneae) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, and Panama.

t: The golden-sided euphonia (Euphonia cayennensis) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in northern Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname and eastern Venezuela.

t: The green-chinned euphonia or green-throated euphonia (Euphonia chalybea) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The purple-throated euphonia (Euphonia chlorotica) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile, though in French Guiana only as a vagrant.

t: The white-lored euphonia or golden-bellied euphonia (Euphonia chrysopasta) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
The velvet-fronted euphonia (Euphonia concinna) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.

t: The elegant euphonia or blue-hooded euphonia (Chlorophonia elegantissima) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Mexico and every Central American country.

t: Finsch's euphonia (Euphonia finschi) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname and Venezuela.

t: The fulvous-vented euphonia (Euphonia fulvicrissa) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama.

t: The olive-backed euphonia (Euphonia gouldi) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found from Mexico to Panama.

t: The yellow-throated euphonia (Euphonia hirundinacea) is a species of songbird in the family Fringillidae. It is found in southeastern Mexico and throughout Central America with its range stretching from Belize south to western Panama.
f: It has a shrill song that alternates between high-pitched and moderately pitched and appears to be able to mimic some calls of other birds.

t: The spot-crowned euphonia (Euphonia imitans) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The thick-billed euphonia (Euphonia laniirostris) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The yellow-crowned euphonia (Euphonia luteicapilla) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The bronze-green euphonia (Euphonia mesochrysa) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The white-vented euphonia (Euphonia minuta) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found from Mexico through much of Central America and in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The chestnut-bellied euphonia (Euphonia pectoralis) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The plumbeous euphonia (Euphonia plumbea) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, Venezuela, and as a vagrant to French Guiana.

t: The rufous-bellied euphonia (Euphonia rufiventris) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The Trinidad euphonia (Euphonia trinitatis) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae. It is common in northern Colombia and northern Venezuela and uncommon to rare on the Caribbean island of Trinidad.
f: Its calls are high-pitched, plaintive whistles: the two most common are a single-pitched, double-noted "pee pee" or "tee dee", or a rising, double-noted "puwee", "cooleee" or "duu dee".

t: The violaceous euphonia (Euphonia violacea) is a small passerine bird in the true finch family Fringillidae.
f: It is widely distributed in eastern South America.

t: The orange-bellied euphonia (Euphonia xanthogaster) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The yellow-crowned bishop (Euplectes afer) is a species of passerine bird in the family Ploceidae native to Africa south of the Sahara. Four subspecies are recognised.
f: It is highly sexually dimorphic in its breeding season, during which the male adopts a distinctive yellow and black plumage, contrasting with the female's predominantly brown coloration.

t: The red-collared widowbird (Euplectes ardens) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae. Red-collared widowbirds are found in grasslands and bush clearings in western and southern Africa.
f: They are known for their long tails and brilliant red badges, both of which act as sexual ornaments.

t: The yellow bishop (Euplectes capensis), also known as Cape bishop, Cape widow or yellow-rumped widow, is a resident breeding Afromontane bird species.
f: This common weaver occurs in less arid vegetated areas, such as fynbos, moist grassland and bracken-covered valleys at altitudes from sea level to the Ethiopian Highlands.

t: The northern red bishop or orange bishop (Euplectes franciscanus) is a small passerine bird in the family Ploceidae. It is part of the largest genus in the family with over 60 different species.
f: It is most common throughout the northern African continent but has also been introduced to areas in the western hemisphere.

The black-winged red bishop (Euplectes hordeaceus), formerly known in southern Africa as the fire-crowned bishop, is a resident breeding bird species in tropical Africa from Senegal to Sudan and south to Angola, Tanzania, Zimbabwe and Mozambique.

t: The southern red bishop or red bishop (Euplectes orix) is a small passerine bird belonging to the bishop and widowbird genus Euplectes in the weaver family, the Ploceidae. North of the Equator, it is replaced by the northern red bishop or orange bishop (E. franciscanus) which was formerly regarded as a subspecies of this species.
f: It is common in wetlands and grassland in Africa south of the Equator.

t: The long-tailed widowbird (Euplectes progne) is a species of bird in the weaver family Ploceidae. The species is found in Angola, Botswana, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Lesotho, South Africa, Eswatini, and Zambia.
f: The tail during flight display is expanded vertically into a deep, long keel below the male as he flies with slow wingbeats 0.5 to 2 metres (20 to 78 inches) above his territory.

t: The southern black korhaan (Afrotis afra), also known as the black bustard, is a species of bird in the bustard family, Otididae. This small bustard is found in southwestern South Africa, from Namaqualand, south to Cape Town and east to Makhanda.
f: It prefers semi-arid habitats such as grasslands, shrublands and savannas where it can easily prey on ground-dwelling arthropods and eat seeds.

t: The northern black korhaan (Afrotis afraoides), also known as the white-quilled bustard, is a species of bird in the bustard family, Otididae. Its habitat is primarily open grassland and scrub.
f: It is widely distributed across Southern Africa.

t: The blue korhaan or blue bustard (Eupodotis caerulescens) is a species of bird in the family Otididae which is native to South Africa. Its natural habitat is plateau grassland, dry shrubland, arable land and pastureland.
f: Its call is a series of frog-like croaks, usually uttered in flight.

t: The red-crested korhaan or red-crested bustard (Lophotis ruficrista) is a species of bird in the family Otididae.
f: It is found in Angola, Botswana, Eswatini, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

t: The white-bellied bustard or white-bellied korhaan (Eupodotis senegalensis) is an African species of bustard. Despite its wide distribution and easily identifiable characteristics, very few studies have been conducted on this species and little is known about its life history and behavior.
f: It is widespread in sub-Saharan Africa in grassland and open woodland habitats.

t: The karoo korhaan (Heterotetrax vigorsii), also known as karoo bustard, is a species of bird in the bustard family, Otididae, from Southern Africa. There are two subspecies, the nominate race, from south-eastern South Africa, and H. v. namaqua (Roberts, 1932), from north-western South Africa and southern Namibia.
f: Karoo korhaans are omnivorous, but plant material is dominant in their diet.

t: The peach-fronted parakeet (Eupsittula aurea), known as the peach-fronted conure in aviculture, is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, and Suriname.

t: The Caatinga parakeet (Eupsittula cactorum), also called the cactus parakeet and in aviculture the cactus conure, is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is endemic to eastern Brazil.

t: Eupsittula canicularis, also known as the orange-fronted parakeet, orange-fronted conure, half-moon conure or Petz's conure is a vulnerable species of birds in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found from western Mexico to Costa Rica.

t: The olive-throated parakeet (Eupsittula nana), also known as the olive-throated conure in aviculture, is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found from Mexico to Costa Rica and in Jamaica; it has been introduced to the Dominican Republic on Hispaniola.

t: The brown-throated parakeet (Eupsittula pertinax), also known as the St. Thomas conure or brown-throated conure in aviculture, is a species of bird in the subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, the northern mainland of South America, and islands off the South American coast.

t: The eared quetzal (Euptilotis neoxenus), also known as the eared trogon, is a species of bird in the trogon family, Trogonidae. It is native to streamside pine-oak forests and canyons in the Sierra Madre Occidental of Mexico from northern Sonora and Chihuahua south to western Michoacán.
f: The species has occurred on rare occasions in southeastern Arizona, where it has been recorded nesting.

t: Ansorge's greenbul (Eurillas ansorgei) or Ansorge's bulbul, is a species of the bulbul family of passerine birds. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in western and central Africa.

t: The plain greenbul (Eurillas curvirostris) is a species of the bulbul family of passerine birds. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is mainly native to the Guineo-Congolian region.

t: The yellow-whiskered greenbul or yellow-whiskered bulbul (Eurillas latirostris) is a species of the bulbul family of passerine birds. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical moist montane forest, and subtropical or tropical moist shrubland.
f: It is found in western and central Africa.

t: The little greenbul (Eurillas virens) is a species of the bulbul family of passerine birds.
f: It is found in many parts of sub-Saharan Africa.

t: Its binomial name commemorates the German naturalist and explorer Eduard Rüppell.
f: The northern white-crowned shrike or white-rumped shrike (Eurocephalus ruppelli), is a shrike found in dry thornbush, semi-desert, and open acacia woodland in east Africa from south eastern South Sudan and southern Ethiopia to Tanzania.

t: The spotted nightjar or spotted eared-nightjar (Eurostopodus argus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It inhabits much of mainland Australia and has also been found in several Indonesian islands.
f: Spotted nightjars are larger and more colorful than other species of nightjar, and are known for their intricately flecked plumage patterns which allow them to camouflage well against the ground.

t: The white-throated nightjar or white-throated eared nightjar (Eurostopodus mystacalis) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry forests.
f: It is endemic to eastern Australia; it is a non-breeding winter visitor in Papua New Guinea.

t: The banded broadbill (Eurylaimus javanicus) is a species of bird in the typical broadbill family Eurylaimidae found in Mainland Southeast Asia and the Greater Sunda Islands. It is sometimes split into two species, one including only the nominate subspecies, E. j. javanicus, and one including all the remaining subspecies.
f: Despite its conspicuous appearance, the bird is usually hard to see due to its sluggishness and is usually only noticed when it vocalises.

t: The black-and-yellow broadbill (Eurylaimus ochromalus) is a species of bird in the typical broadbill family Eurylaimidae. A small, distinctive species, it has a black head, breastband, and upperparts, a white neckband, yellow streaking on the back and wings, and vinous-pink underparts that turn yellow towards the belly.
f: Eggs are laid in clutches of two or three, sometimes containing a fourth runt egg, and are incubated by both sexes.

t: The sunbittern (Eurypyga helias) is a bittern-like bird of tropical regions of the Americas, and the sole member of the family Eurypygidae (sometimes spelled Eurypigidae) and genus Eurypyga. It is found in Central and South America, and has three subspecies.
f: The sunbittern shows both morphological and molecular similarities with the kagu (Rhynochetos jubatus) of New Caledonia, indicating a Gondwanan origin, both species being placed in the clade Eurypygiformes.

t: The broad-billed roller (Eurystomus glaucurus) is a member of the roller family of birds which breeds across tropical Africa and Madagascar in all but the driest regions.
f: It is a wet season breeder, which migrates from the northern and southern areas of its range towards the moister equatorial belt in the dry season.

t: The Oriental dollarbird (Eurystomus orientalis) is a bird of the roller family, so named because of the distinctive pale blue or white, coin-shaped spots on its wings.
f: It can be found from Australia to Korea, Japan and India.

t: The fulvous-faced scrub tyrant, or tawny-fronted pygmy-tyrant (Euscarthmus fulviceps) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Ecuador, Peru, and possibly Colombia.

t: The fulvous-crowned scrub tyrant, or tawny-crowned pygmy-tyrant, (Euscarthmus meloryphus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela.

t: The rufous-sided scrub tyrant, or rufous-sided pygmy-tyrant, (Euscarthmus rufomarginatus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Suriname.

t: The white-tipped sicklebill (Eutoxeres aquila) is a species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The spruce grouse (Canachites canadensis), also known as Canada grouse, spruce hen or fool hen, is a medium-sized grouse closely associated with the coniferous boreal forests or taiga of North America. It is the only member of the genus Canachites.
f: It is one of the most arboreal grouse species, fairly well adapted to perching and moving about in trees.

t: The Amur falcon (Falco amurensis) is a small raptor of the falcon family.
f: It breeds in south-eastern Siberia and Northern China before migrating in large flocks across India and over the Arabian Sea to winter in Southern and East African coasts.

t: The brown falcon (Falco berigora) is a relatively large falcon native to Australia and New Guinea. A number of plumage morphs occur, with the primary distinction being between the pale morph and the dark morph.
f: Both morphs usually have dark brown upper parts and wing coverts.

t: The merlin (Falco columbarius) is a small species of falcon from the Northern Hemisphere, with numerous subspecies throughout North America and Eurasia. A bird of prey, the merlin breeds in the northern Holarctic; some migrate to subtropical and northern tropical regions in winter.
f: In recent decades, merlin populations in North America have been significantly increasing, with some merlins becoming so well adapted to city life that they forgo migration; in Europe, populations increased up to about 2000, but have been steady subsequently.

t: The orange-breasted falcon (Falco deiroleucus) is a bird of prey in the family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras. Despite its wide range, it is scarce, and considered by IUCN to be Near Threatened.
f: It is found in southern Mexico, Belize, Guatemala, Panama, and in all South American countries except Chile and Uruguay, though in Argentina only in the far northwest.

t: The aplomado falcon (Falco femoralis) is a medium-sized falcon of the Americas. The species' largest continuous range is in South America, but not in the deep interior Amazon Basin.
f: Aplomado is an unusual Spanish word for "lead-colored", referring to the blue-grey areas of the plumage; an approximate English translation would be "plumbeous falcon".

t: The prairie falcon (Falco mexicanus) is a medium-sized falcon found in Western North America. A separate species from the peregrine falcon, with which it shares some visual similarities, the prairie falcon is, essentially, an arid-climate divergence of earlier peregrine falcon lineage.
f: The prairie falcon is the only larger falcon species native strictly to North America .

t: The lesser kestrel (Falco naumanni) is a small falcon. It is a summer migrant, wintering in Africa and Pakistan and sometimes even to India and Iraq.
f: This species breeds from the Mediterranean across Afghanistan and Central Asia, to China and Mongolia.

t: The New Zealand falcon  is New Zealand's only falcon, and one of only four living native and two endemic birds of prey. It is frequently mistaken for the larger and more common swamp harrier.
f: It is the country's most threatened bird of prey, with only around 5000–15000 individuals remaining.

t: The peregrine falcon (Falco peregrinus), sometimes referred to simply as the peregrine, is a bird of prey (raptor) in the family Falconidae known for its speed. A large, crow-sized falcon, it has a blue-grey back, barred white underparts and a black head.
f: The only major ice-free landmasses from which it is entirely absent are the islands of New Zealand, making it the world's most widespread raptor and one of the most widely found wild bird species.

t: The bat falcon (Falco rufigularis) is a bird of prey in the family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.
f: It is found in Mexico, Central America, Trinidad, and every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The gyrfalcon ( or ) (Falco rusticolus), also abbreviated as gyr, is a bird of prey and the largest species in the falcon family, Falconidae. A high-latitude species, the gyrfalcon breeds on the Arctic coasts and tundra, the islands of northern North America and Siberia, where it is mainly a resident species.
f: Some gyrfalcons disperse more widely after the breeding season or in winter, and individual vagrancy can take birds for long distances.

t: The American kestrel (Falco sparverius) is the smallest and most common falcon in the Americas. It has a roughly two-to-one range in size over subspecies and sex, varying in size from about the weight of a blue jay to a mourning dove.
f: It sometimes hovers in the air with rapid wing beats while homing in on prey.

t: The Eurasian hobby (Falco subbuteo), or just hobby, is a small, slim falcon.
f: It belongs to a group of similar falcons often considered a subgenus of Falco.

t: The common kestrel (Falco tinnunculus), also known as the European kestrel, Eurasian kestrel, Old World kestrel, is a species of predatory bird belonging to the kestrel group of the falcon family Falconidae. In the United Kingdom, where no other kestrel species commonly occurs, it is generally just called the "kestrel".
f: It has colonized a few oceanic islands, but vagrant individuals are generally rare; in the whole of Micronesia for example, the species was only recorded twice each on Guam and Saipan in the Marianas.

t: The red-footed falcon (Falco vespertinus), formerly the western red-footed falcon, is a bird of prey. It belongs to the family Falconidae, the falcons.
f: It is a regular wanderer to western Europe, and in August 2004 a red-footed falcon was found in North America for the first time on the island of Martha's Vineyard, Massachusetts.

t: The sickle-billed vanga (Falculea palliata) is a species of bird in the vanga family Vangidae. It is monotypic within the genus Falculea.
f: Its natural habitats are tropical dry forests and tropical dry shrubland.

t: The eastern shriketit (Falcunculus frontatus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Falcunculidae. It is also known as bark tit, crested tit or yellow-bellied tit.
f: It is found in south-eastern Australia from the southeast of South Australia, throughout Victoria, eastern New South Wales to southeastern Queensland, with some scattered occurrences further north and west in Queensland.

t: The Zapata wren (Ferminia cerverai) is a medium-sized grayish-brown bird that lives in dense shrubs of the Zapata Swamp, Cuba. It is the only member of the monotypical genus Ferminia, which is endemic to Cuba and endangered.
f: This species was first described in 1926 by Thomas Barbour and named after its co-discoverer, Fermín Zanón Cervera.

t: The taiga flycatcher or red-throated flycatcher (Ficedula albicilla) is a migratory bird in the family Muscicapidae. The species was first described by Peter Simon Pallas in 1811.
f: The specific name albicilla is from Latin albus, white, and Neo-Latin cilla tail; this meaning of cilla arose from a misunderstanding of motacilla, the name for the wagtail.

t: The collared flycatcher (Ficedula albicollis) is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family, one of the four species of Western Palearctic black-and-white flycatchers. It breeds in southeast Europe  and Eastern France to the Balkan Peninsula and Ukraine and is migratory, wintering in Sub-Saharan Africa.
f: Pied flycatchers can mimic the song of the collared flycatcher in sympatric populations.

t: The little slaty flycatcher (Ficedula basilanica) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is found on the islands of Mindanao, Leyte and Samar in the Philippines.

t: The rufous-chested flycatcher (Ficedula dumetoria) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand.

t: The green-backed flycatcher (Ficedula elisae) is a bird in the family Muscicapidae, which contains the Old World flycatchers.

t: The slaty-backed flycatcher (Ficedula erithacus) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The snowy-browed flycatcher (Ficedula hyperythra) is a species of bird in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

t: The European pied flycatcher (Ficedula hypoleuca) is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family. One of the four species of Western Palearctic black-and-white flycatchers, it hybridises to a limited extent with the collared flycatcher.
f: This species commonly feeds on caterpillars, flies, spiders, ants, bees and similar prey.

t: The mugimaki flycatcher (Ficedula mugimaki) is a small passerine bird of eastern Asia belonging to the genus Ficedula in the Old World flycatcher family, Muscicapidae. The bird is also known as the robin flycatcher.

t: The narcissus flycatcher (Ficedula narcissina) is a passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family. t: The black-and-orange flycatcher (Ficedula nigrorufa) or black-and-rufous flycatcher is a species of flycatcher endemic to the central and southern Western Ghats, the Nilgiris and Palni hill ranges in southern India.
f: It is unique among the Ficedula flycatchers in having rufous coloration on its back and prior to molecular studies was suggested to be related to the chats and thrushes.

t: The red-breasted flycatcher (Ficedula parva) is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family. It breeds in eastern Europe and across Central Asia and is migratory, wintering in south Asia.
f: It forms a superspecies with the closely related taiga flycatcher and Kashmir flycatcher and can be distinguished from the former by its different song, warmer-toned plumage and the more extensive orange throat patch.

t: The rusty-tailed flycatcher (Ficedula ruficauda) is a small passerine bird in the flycatcher family Muscicapidae. It is found mainly in the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent and some parts of southwest India, as well as pockets of Central Asia including Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.

t: The semicollared flycatcher (Ficedula semitorquata) is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family, one of the four species of Western Palearctic black-and-white flycatchers. It breeds in montane forests of the southeastern corner of Europe (Balkan Peninsula) to Northwest Iran.
f: Tracking studies using geolocators have revealed that weather conditions during spring migration can have a large impact on the timing of semicollared flycatcher migration and survival of adult birds.

t: The rufous-gorgeted flycatcher (Ficedula strophiata) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is native to the Himalayas and Patkai ranges, central/southern China, northern Indochina and eastern Vietnam.

t: The Kashmir flycatcher (Ficedula subrubra) is a small passerine bird in the flycatcher family Muscicapidae. It breeds in the Northwest Himalayas and winters in southern India and Sri Lanka.

t: The ultramarine flycatcher or the white-browed blue flycatcher (Ficedula superciliaris) is a small arboreal Old World flycatcher in the Ficedula genus.

t: Sykes's lark (Galerida deva) is a species of lark found in the dry open country of India. Its distribution is mainly restricted to central India, although stray records have been found elsewhere on the sub-continent.
f: It can imitate the calls of 34 other birds within its habitat.

t: The large-billed lark or southern thick-billed lark (Galerida magnirostris) is a small passerine bird found in southern Africa. The name "thick-billed lark" more commonly refers to the species of the same name (i.e.
f: The name "large-billed lark" may also refer to Bradfield's lark.
The Malabar lark, or Malabar crested lark (Galerida malabarica) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in western India.

t: Thekla's lark (Galerida theklae), also known as the Thekla lark, is a species of lark that breeds on the Iberian Peninsula and in North and East Africa south to Kenya. This is a common bird of dry open country, often at some altitude.
f: It is a sedentary (non-migratory) species.

t: The watercock (Gallicrex cinerea) is a waterbird in the rail and crake family, Rallidae that is widely distributed across Southeast Asia.
f: It is the only member of the genus Gallicrex.

t: The puna snipe (Gallinago andina) is a bird in tribe Scolopancinai and subfamily Scolopacinae of family Scolopacidae, the sandpipers and relatives.
f: It is native to the puna grassland.

t: Wilson's snipe (Gallinago delicata) is a small, stocky shorebird. The specific name delicata is Latin for "dainty".
f: The generic name Gallinago is Neo-Latin for a woodcock or snipe from Latin gallina, "hen" and the suffix -ago, "resembling".

t: The common snipe  is a small, stocky wader native to the Old World, where it breeds in marshes, bogs, tundra and wet meadows. It is usually shy and well-camouflaged, foraging in soft mud mainly for insects and earthworms but also some plant material.
f: During courtship, males perform a "winnowing" display; flying high in circles and then taking shallow dives to produce a "drumming" sound by vibrating the tail feathers.

t: Latham's snipe (Gallinago hardwickii), also Japanese snipe is a medium-sized, long-billed, migratory snipe of the East Asian–Australasian Flyway. The origin of the bird's common name is not clear.
f: However, he had no apparent connection with the snipe named after him.

t: The imperial snipe (Gallinago imperialis) is a small stocky wader which breeds in the Andes. It is not known if it is migratory.
f: For a century it was known only from two specimens collected near Bogotá, Colombia, and was presumed extinct, but it was rediscovered in Peru in 1967 and Ecuador in 1988.

t: Jameson's snipe (Gallinago jamesoni or Chubbia jamesoni) or the Andean snipe, is a small, stocky wader. It breeds in the Andes in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela.
f: It appears to be entirely sedentary, with no evidence of migration.

t: The Magellanic snipe (Gallinago magellanica) is a bird in tribe Scolopancinai and subfamily Scolopacinae of family Scolopacidae, the sandpipers and relatives.
f: It is found in Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, and the Falkland Islands.

t: The great snipe (Gallinago media) is a small stocky wader in the genus Gallinago. This bird's breeding habitat is marshes and wet meadows with short vegetation in northeastern Europe and northern Asia, from Scandinavia and Poland east across northern Russia to western Siberia, and south to northern Kazakhstan.
f: Great snipe are migratory, wintering in tropical Africa.

t: Swinhoe's snipe (Gallinago megala), also known as forest snipe or Chinese snipe, is a medium-sized (length 27–29 cm, wingspan 38–44 cm, weight 120 gm), long-billed, migratory wader.
f: The common name commemorates the British naturalist Robert Swinhoe who first described the species in 1861.

t: The noble snipe (Gallinago nobilis) is a small stocky wader.
f: It breeds in the Andes of Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela above or just below the treeline.

t: The Pantanal snipe (Gallinago paraguaiae) is a bird in tribe Scolopancinai and subfamily Scolopacinae of family Scolopacidae, the sandpipers and relatives.
f: It is found on Trinidad and Tobago and in every mainland South American country (though only as a vagrant in Ecuador.)
The pin-tailed snipe or pintail snipe (Gallinago stenura) is a species of bird in the family Scolopacidae, the sandpipers.

t: The giant snipe (Gallinago undulata) is a stocky wader. The nominate subspecies G. u. undulata occurs in two distinct areas, one in Colombia, and the other from Venezuela through Guyana, Suriname and French Guiana to extreme north-eastern Brazil.
f: It ranges from the lowlands up to 2,200 m altitude.

t: The common moorhen (Gallinula chloropus), also known as the waterhen, is a bird species in the rail family (Rallidae). It is distributed across many parts of the Old World, across Africa, Europe, and Asia.
f: The species is not found in the polar regions or many tropical rainforests; generally it is one of the most common Old World rail species, together with the Eurasian coot in some regions.

t: The common gallinule (Gallinula galeata) is a bird in the family Rallidae. It was split from the common moorhen by the American Ornithologists' Union in July 2011.
f: The common gallinule is one of the most conspicuous rail species in North America, along with the American coot.

t: The dusky moorhen (Gallinula tenebrosa) is a bird species in the rail family and is one of the eight extant species in the moorhen genus. It occurs in Australia, New Guinea, Borneo and Indonesia.
f: It is often confused with the purple swamphen and the Eurasian coot due to similar appearance and overlapping distributions.

t: The weka, also known as the Māori hen or woodhen (Gallirallus australis) is a flightless bird species of the rail family. Some authorities consider it as the only extant member of the genus Gallirallus.
f: Weka usually lay eggs between August and January; both sexes help to incubate.

t: The buff-banded rail (Gallirallus philippensis) is a distinctively coloured, highly dispersive, medium-sized rail of the rail family, Rallidae.
f: The species was formerly placed in the genus Hypotaenidia.

t: The barred rail (Gallirallus torquatus) is a species of rail found across the Philippines, Sulawesi (Indonesia) and Salawati (western New Guinea). The species was formerly sometimes placed in the genus Hypotaenidia.
f: The species is common, but shy and difficult to see.

t: The Sri Lanka spurfowl (Galloperdix bicalcarata) is a member of the pheasant family which is endemic to the dense rainforests of Sri Lanka. In Sri Lanka, this bird is known as haban kukula - හබන් කුකුලා in Sinhala.
f: Often the only indication of its presence is its distinctive ringing call, consisting of series of three-syllabled whistles.

t: The red spurfowl (Galloperdix spadicea) is a member of the pheasant family and is endemic to India. It has a distinctive call and is often hard to see except for a few seconds when it flushes from the undergrowth.
f: It is a bird of forests, and is quite secretive despite its size.

t: The red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), also known as the Indian red junglefowl (and formerly the bankiva or bankiva-fowl), is a species of tropical, galliform bird in the phasianid family, found across much of Southeast Asia and parts of South Asia. The red junglefowl was the primary species to give rise to today's many breeds of chicken (G. g. domesticus).
f: Whole genome sequencing has revealed that the chicken was first domesticated from red junglefowl ca. 8,000 years ago, with this domestication event involving multiple maternal origins.

t: The chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) is the domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia. It was first domesticated around 8,000 years ago and is one of the most common and widespread domesticated animals in the world.
f: A hen bred for laying can produce over 300 eggs per year.

t: The Sri Lankan junglefowl (Gallus lafayettii), also known as the Ceylon junglefowl or Lafayette's junglefowl, is a member of the Galliformes bird order. It is closely related to the red junglefowl (G. gallus), the wild junglefowl from which the chicken was domesticated.
f: It is a common endemic bird in Sri Lanka, where it is the national bird.

t: The grey junglefowl (Gallus sonneratii), also known as Sonnerat's junglefowl, is one of the wild ancestors of the domestic chicken together with the red junglefowl and other junglefowls. Local names include Komri in Rajasthan, Geera kur or Parda komri in Gondi, Jangli Murghi in Hindi, Raan kombdi in Marathi, Kattu Kozhi in Tamil and Malayalam, Kaadu koli in Kannada and Tella adavi kodi in Telugu.
f: The species epithet commemorates the French explorer Pierre Sonnerat.

t: The green junglefowl (Gallus varius), also known as Javan junglefowl, forktail or green Javanese junglefowl, is the most distantly related and the first to diverge at least 4 million years ago among the four species of the junglefowl. Green junglefowl is a medium-sized (up to 75 cm long) bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae.
f: Hybridization with domestic chicken has also been reported.

t: The pearl kite (Gampsonyx swainsonii) is a very small raptor found in open savanna habitat adjacent to deciduous woodland in Central and South America. It is the only member of the genus Gampsonyx.
f: The scientific name commemorates the English naturalist William Swainson.

t: The white-hooded babbler (Gampsorhynchus rufulus) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found from the eastern Himalayas to central Myanmar and southwestern China.

t: The collared babbler (Gampsorhynchus torquatus) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The Chinese hwamei or melodious laughingthrush (Garrulax canorus) is a passerine bird of eastern Asia in the laughingthrush family Leiothrichidae. The name "hwamei" comes from its Chinese name huà méi, which means "painted eyebrow", referring to the distinctive marking around the bird's eyes.
f: The species is a popular cagebird because of its attractive song.

t: The white-crested laughingthrush (Garrulax leucolophus) is a member of the family Leiothrichidae.
f: It is a highly social and vocal bird found in forest and scrub from the Himalayan foothills to Southeast Asia.

t: The black-hooded laughingthrush (Garrulax milleti) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in Laos and Vietnam.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.
The lesser necklaced laughingthrush (Garrulax monileger) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

t: The Sunda laughingthrush (Garrulax palliatus) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found on the islands of Sumatra and Borneo in Brunei, Indonesia, and Malaysia.
f: It is threatened by human activity such as hunting, logging, and trapping.

t: The white-necked laughingthrush (Garrulax strepitans) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Yunnan, Laos, Myanmar and Thailand.

t: The Taiwan hwamei (Garrulax taewanus) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1859.
f: The whistling song is long, melodious and varied.

t: The Eurasian jay (Garrulus glandarius) is a species of passerine bird in the family Corvidae. It has pinkish brown plumage with a black stripe on each side of a whitish throat, a bright blue panel on the upper wing and a black tail.
f: The Eurasian jay is a woodland bird that occurs over a vast region from western Europe and north-west Africa to the Indian subcontinent and farther to the eastern seaboard of Asia and down into south-east Asia.

t: The black-headed jay or lanceolated jay (Garrulus lanceolatus) is a species of passerine bird in the crow family Corvidae. It is found in open wooded country across the Himalayas and into eastern Afghanistan.
f: A relatively large songbird, it has a largely grey body with a black head, an untidy crest, white streaks on the throat, and a pale bill.

t: Lidth's jay (Garrulus lidthi), also known as the Amami jay, is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae native to the Ryukyu Islands, Japan. Measuring up to 38 cm (15 in) in total length, it is slightly larger than its close relative the Eurasian jay, with a proportionately stouter bill and also a longer tail.
f: The species was threatened in the past by hunting for its feathers, which were used for decorating ladies' hats.

t: Gastrophryne carolinensis, the eastern narrow-mouthed toad, is a species of microhylid frog. It is a relatively small, toad-like amphibian found in damp, shady habitats.
f: The species is highly fossorial, and feeds primarily on ants.

t: Gastrophryne olivacea, the Great Plains narrow-mouthed toad or western narrow-mouthed toad, is a species of microhylid frog found throughout much of the south-central United States from Nebraska south through Texas, and into northern Mexico.
f: Though not a true toad, evidenced by the smooth, moist skin, its common name is due to its terrestrial habit.

t: The yellow-billed loon (Gavia adamsii), also known as the white-billed diver, is the largest member of the loon or diver family. Breeding adults have a black head, white underparts and a chequered black-and-white mantle.
f: This species, like all divers, is a specialist fish-eater, catching its prey underwater.

t: The black-throated loon (Gavia arctica), also known as the Arctic loon and the black-throated diver, is a migratory aquatic bird found in the Northern Hemisphere, primarily breeding in freshwater lakes in northern Europe and Asia. It winters along sheltered, ice-free coasts of the north-east Atlantic Ocean and the eastern and western Pacific Ocean.
f: The flanks are also white, a feature that can be used to separate this bird from the Pacific loon.

t: The common loon or great northern diver (Gavia immer) is a large member of the loon, or diver, family of birds. Breeding adults have a plumage that includes a broad black head and neck with a greenish, purplish, or bluish sheen, blackish or blackish-grey upperparts, and pure white underparts except some black on the undertail coverts and vent.
f: The chicks are capable of diving underwater when just a few days old, and they fly to their wintering areas before ice forms in the fall.
The Pacific loon or Pacific diver (Gavia pacifica) is a medium-sized member of the loon, or diver, family.

t: The red-throated loon (North America) or red-throated diver (Britain and Ireland) (Gavia stellata) is a migratory aquatic bird found in the Northern Hemisphere. The most widely distributed member of the loon or diver family, it breeds primarily in Arctic regions, and it winters in northern coastal waters.
f: Fish form the bulk of its diet, though amphibians, invertebrates, and plant material are sometimes eaten as well.

t: The mangrove honeyeater (Gavicalis fasciogularis) is a species of bird in the honeyeater family Meliphagidae. These two species form a genus with the singing honeyeater.
f: The species was once considered to be conspecific with the varied honeyeater, but it is now treated as a separate species.

t: The singing honeyeater (Gavicalis virescens) is a small bird found in Australia, and is part of the honeyeater family Meliphagidae. The bird lives in a wide range of shrubland, woodland, and coastal habitat.
f: It is relatively common and is widespread right across Australia west of the Great Dividing Range, through to the west coast and on Western Australian coastal islands.

t: The pale-headed woodpecker (Gecinulus grantia) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, and Vietnam.
f: It is a bamboo specialist, and a montane bird.

t: The bamboo woodpecker, or Gecinulus viridis, is a species of bird in the family Picidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in Myanmar, Laos, Thailand and Malaysia.

t: The gull-billed tern (Gelochelidon nilotica) is a tern in the family Laridae. The Australian gull-billed tern was previously considered a subspecies.
f: It is widely distributed and breeds in scattered localities in Europe, Asia, northwest Africa, and the Americas.
The striated earthcreeper (Geocerthia serrana) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The greater roadrunner (Geococcyx californianus) is a long-legged bird in the cuckoo family, Cuculidae, from the Aridoamerica region in the Southwestern United States and Mexico. Along with the lesser roadrunner, it is one of two species in the genus Geococcyx.
f: The scientific name means "Californian earth-cuckoo".

t: The lesser roadrunner (Geococcyx velox) is a large, long-legged bird that is a member of the cuckoo family, Cuculidae. Along with the greater roadrunner, it is one of two species in the genus Geococcyx.
f: Its Latin name means "swift earth-cuckoo".

t: The red-cheeked parrot (Geoffroyus geoffroyi) is a species of parrot in the family Psittaculidae found in Indonesia, Papua New Guinea and the tip of northern Queensland, Australia. There are 17 subspecies currently recognized.
f: It exhibits sexual dimorphism; the adult male has red cheeks and a mauve nape and top of head, while the female is duller with a brown head.
The song parrot or singing parrot (Geoffroyus heteroclitus) is a species of parrot in the family Psittaculidae.

t: The orange-headed thrush (Geokichla citrina) is a bird in the thrush family. It is common in well-wooded areas of the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.
f: The species shows a preference for shady damp areas, and like many Geokichla and Zoothera thrushes, can be quite secretive.
The orange ground thrush (Geokichla gurneyi) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.

t: The spotted ground thrush (Geokichla guttata) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Malawi, South Africa, Sudan, Tanzania, and possibly Mozambique.

t: The orange-sided thrush or orange-banded thrush (Geokichla peronii) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It is found on Timor island and the southern Maluku Islands.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The Abyssinian ground thrush (Geokichla piaggiae) is a thrush from the family Turdidae which is native to north-east Africa where it lives at high altitude in montane forests.
f: Its binomial nomenclature honors the 19th century Italian explorer of East Africa Carlo Piaggia.

t: The Siberian thrush (Geokichla sibirica) is a member of the thrush family, Turdidae. The genus name Geokichla comes from Ancient Greek geo-, "ground-" and kikhle, " thrush".
f: The Siberian thrush is similar in size to the song thrush.

t: The spot-winged thrush (Geokichla spiloptera) is an Asian thrush, a group within the large thrush family Turdidae.
f: It is an endemic resident breeder in Sri Lanka.

t: The bar-shouldered dove (Geopelia humeralis) is a species of long tailed dove native to Australia and Southern New Guinea. It is protected under the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974.
f: Its voice is a distinctive and melodious "cook-a-wook" or "coolicoo".

t: The peaceful dove (Geopelia placida) is a pigeon native to Australia and New Guinea. The peaceful dove is closely related to the zebra dove of south-east Asia and the barred dove of eastern Indonesia.
f: Until recently, the three were classed as a single species, Geopelia striata, known as peaceful dove or zebra dove.

t: The zebra dove (Geopelia striata), also known as the barred ground dove, or barred dove, is a species of bird of the dove family, Columbidae, native to Southeast Asia. They are small birds with a long tail, predominantly brownish-grey in colour with black-and-white barring.
f: The species is known for its pleasant, soft, staccato cooing calls.

t: The short-billed miner (Geositta antarctica) is a species of bird in the subfamily Sclerurinae, the leaftossers and miners, of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Chile.

t: The common miner (Geositta cunicularia) is a passerine bird in the subfamily Sclerurinae, the leaftossers and miners, of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: The puna miner (Geositta punensis) is a passerine bird in the subfamily Sclerurinae, the leaftossers and miners, of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.

t: The rufous-banded miner (Geositta rufipennis) is a species of bird in the subfamily Sclerurinae, the leaftossers and miners, of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile.

t: The slender-billed miner (Geositta tenuirostris) is a species of bird in the subfamily Sclerurinae, the leaftossers and miners, of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The ash-breasted sierra finch (Geospizopsis plebejus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry shrubland, subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, and subtropical or tropical high-altitude grassland.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The plumbeous sierra finch (Geospizopsis unicolor) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical high-altitude grassland and pastureland.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The masked yellowthroat (Geothlypis aequinoctialis) is a species of bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, Trinidad, and Venezuela.
Belding's yellowthroat (Geothlypis beldingi) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers.

t: The Kentucky warbler (Geothlypis formosa) is a small species of New World warbler.
f: It is a sluggish and heavy warbler with a short tail, preferring to spend most of its time on or near the ground, except when singing.
The hooded yellowthroat (Geothlypis nelsoni) is a species of bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers.

t: The mourning warbler (Geothlypis philadelphia) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family. Mourning warblers are neotropical migrants native to eastern and central North America and wintering in Central and South America.
f: The "mourning" in this bird's name refers to the male's hood, thought to resemble a mourning veil.

t: The grey-crowned yellowthroat (Geothlypis poliocephala) is a species of bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers.
f: It is found from Mexico to Panama.
The Bahama yellowthroat (Geothlypis rostrata) is a species of bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers.

t: The olive-crowned yellowthroat (Geothlypis semiflava) is a species of bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama.
The black-polled yellowthroat (Geothlypis speciosa) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers.

t: MacGillivray's warbler (Geothlypis tolmiei) is a species of bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers.
f: It is found from southeastern Alaska and western Canada to Panama.

t: The common yellowthroat (Geothlypis trichas) is a New World warbler. In the northern parts of its range the birds are migratory, wintering in the southern parts of the breeding range, Central America and the West Indies.
f: It is an abundant breeder in North America, ranging from southern Canada to central Mexico.

t: The Key West quail-dove (Geotrygon chrysia) is a species of bird from the doves and pigeon family Columbidae.
f: It is probably most closely related to the bridled quail-dove.

t: The ruddy quail-dove (Geotrygon montana) is a species of bird in the dove and pigeon family Columbidae. It breeds throughout the West Indies, Central America, and tropical South America.
f: Some nests are built on the ground.

t: The violaceous quail-dove (Geotrygon violacea) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Guyana, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.
The white-tailed hawk (Geranoaetus albicaudatus) is a large bird of prey species found in tropical and subtropical environments of the Americas.

t: The black-chested buzzard-eagle (Geranoaetus melanoleucus) is a bird of prey of the hawk and eagle family (Accipitridae). This species is also known as the black buzzard-eagle, the gray buzzard-eagle, or analogously with "eagle" or "eagle-buzzard" replacing "buzzard-eagle", or as the Chilean blue eagle.
f: It lives in open regions of South America.

t: The variable hawk (Geranoaetus polyosoma) is a polymorphic species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. Its taxonomy is disputed, with some splitting it into the widespread red-backed hawk (G. polyosoma) and the Puna hawk or Gurney's hawk (G. poecilochrous) of the central and north Andean highlands, but the differences between the two are unclear.
f: It is widespread and often common in open habitats in western and southern South America, including the Falkland Islands.

t: The crane hawk (Geranospiza caerulescens) is a species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Geranospiza.

t: The northern bald ibis, hermit ibis, or Waldrapp (Geronticus eremita) is a migratory Old World ibis found in open areas such as grasslands, rocky mountains, and semi-deserts, often close to running water. This 70–80 cm (28–31 in) glossy black ibis, which, unlike many members of the ibis family, is non-wading, has an unfeathered red face and head, and a long, curved red bill.
f: The northern bald ibis was once widespread across the Middle East, northern Africa, southern and central Europe, with a fossil record dating back at least 1.8 million years.

t: The green-backed gerygone (Gerygone chloronota) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae found in northern Australia and New Guinea.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.

t: The fan-tailed gerygone (Gerygone flavolateralis) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. The Rennell gerygone (G. citrina) of the Solomon Islands was formerly considered conspecific, but was split as a distinct species by the IOC in 2021.
f: It is found in New Caledonia and Vanuatu.

t: The western gerygone (Gerygone fusca) is a small, brownish-grey species of passerine bird, which is found in inland and south-west Australia. It is not currently threatened with extinction (IUCN: Least Concern).
f: It is an arboreal, insectivore of open forest, woodland and dry shrubland.

t: The grey warbler (Gerygone igata), also known by its Māori name riroriro, is an insectivorous bird in the family Acanthizidae endemic to New Zealand. Internationally, ornithologists usually refer to it as the grey gerygone or New Zealand gerygone to avoid confusion with unrelated birds also known as warblers.
f: These insectivorous birds feed on insects living in shrubs, and often feed on the wing.

t: The mangrove gerygone (Gerygone levigaster) is a species of bird in the Australian warbler family Acanthizidae. The species is also known as the mangrove warbler.
f: The song, which is similar to that of the western gerygone, has been described as "sweet, rich, tuneful".
The large-billed gerygone (Gerygone magnirostris) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae found in northern Australia and New Guinea.

t: The brown gerygone (Gerygone mouki), previously known as the brown warbler, is a small passerine bird native to eastern coastal Australia. The upper parts are olive-brown , while its face and underparts are a much paler grey, cream, or washed-out brown.
f: It may be sighted in coastal rainforest, singly or in small groups of two to four.

t: The white-throated gerygone (Gerygone olivacea) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is found in Australia and Papua New Guinea.
f: Its common names include white-throated warbler, white-throated flyeater, bush canary, and native canary.
The fairy gerygone (Gerygone palpebrosa), previously known as the fairy warbler, is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae native to New Guinea and Queensland, Australia.

t: The golden-bellied gerygone (Gerygone sulphurea) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Cambodia, Vietnam and Thailand.

t: The collared pratincole (Glareola pratincola), also known as the common pratincole or red-winged pratincole, is a wader in the pratincole family, Glareolidae.
f: As with other pratincoles, it is native to the Old World.

t: The lavender waxbill (Glaucestrilda caerulescens) is a common species of estrildid finch native to Central Africa and successfully introduced on Hawaiʻi.
f: It has an estimated global extent of occurrence of 620,000 km2 (240,000 sq mi).

t: The Yungas pygmy owl (Glaucidium bolivianum), is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, and Peru.

t: The ferruginous pygmy owl (Glaucidium brasilianum) is a species of small owl found in the southwestern United States, extending south through Mexico, Central America, and into South America, including countries like Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay and Argentina.
f: It is the most widely distributed species of pygmy owl in Central and South America and is believed to be one of the most common owls in these regions, where it lives in a variety of semi-open wooded habitats.

t: The African barred owlet (Glaucidium capense) is a species of small owl in the family Strigidae found in much of southern, central and eastern Africa.
f: The taxon may be four species rather than a single species.

t: The Javan owlet (Glaucidium castanopterum) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is native to the islands of Java and Bali.

t: The chestnut-backed owlet (Glaucidium castanotum) (often misspelled Glaucidium castanonotum), is an owl which is endemic to Sri Lanka. This species was formerly considered to be a subspecies of the jungle owlet.
f: This species is a part of the larger grouping of owls known as typical owls, Strigidae, which contains most of the smaller owl species.

t: The Costa Rican pygmy owl (Glaucidium costaricanum) is a small "typical owl" in subfamily Surniinae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The Asian barred owlet (Glaucidium cuculoides), also known as the cuckoo owlet, is a species of pygmy owl native to the forests and shrublands of mainland Southeast Asia to the foothills of the Himalayas of northern Pakistan. It is a smaller owl, measuring 22–25 cm (8.7–9.8 in), making it one of the larger pygmy owls.
f: They are primarily insectivorous but will eat lizards, small rodents and birds as well.

t: The northern pygmy owl (Glaucidium gnoma) is a small owl native to western North America.
f: Seven subspecies are accepted, of which three have sometimes been treated as separate species.

t: The Central American pygmy owl (Glaucidium griseiceps) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Belize, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The Amazonian pygmy owl (Glaucidium hardyi), also known as Hardy's pygmy owl, is an owl found in northern South America and the Amazon Basin.
f: A member of the Strigidae family, it is a true owl.

t: The Andean pygmy owl (Glaucidium jardinii) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
The East Brazilian pygmy owl (Glaucidium minutissimum), also known as least pygmy-owl or Sick's pygmy-owl, is a small owl in the typical owl family.

t: The austral pygmy owl (Glaucidium nana) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found mainly in central and southern Chile, but also in some parts of southern Argentina.

t: The cloud-forest pygmy owl or cloudforest pygmy owl (Glaucidium nubicola) is a short, muscular, small-sized species of owl found throughout the Andes of western Colombia and north-western Ecuador, being confined to cloud forests between 900–2000 m a.s.l. Its epithet nubicola is Latin for "cloud-inhabiting", because this species is restricted to very humid cloud forests.
f: Below this altitudinal range the Central American pygmy owl (Glaucidium griseiceps) occurs; above it, the Andean pygmy owl (Glaucidium jardinii) occurs.

t: The Colima pygmy owl (Glaucidium palmarum) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is endemic to the western part of Mexico.

t: The subtropical pygmy owl (Glaucidium parkeri) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: It is dark reddish to greyish-brown, with spotted sides and half of a white ring around the back of the neck. This species is found in the boreal forests of Northern and Central Europe to Siberia.
f: The Eurasian pygmy owl (Glaucidium passerinum) is the smallest owl in Europe.

t: The pearl-spotted owlet (Glaucidium perlatum) is a small bird of prey found in sub-Saharan Africa. They belong to the Strigidae family, otherwise known as the typical owls or the true owls, which contains most species of owl.
f: Pearl-spotted owlets are brownish and heavily spotted white, with two distinct black false 'eyes' at the back of their head.

t: The Pacific pygmy owl (Glaucidium peruanum), or Peruvian pygmy owl, is a small "typical owl" in subfamily Surniinae.
f: It is found in Chile, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The jungle owlet (Glaucidium radiatum) or barred jungle owlet is native to the Indian Subcontinent. There are two subspecies, with that found in the Western Ghats sometimes considered a full species.
f: The species is often found singly, in pairs or small groups, and they are usually detected by their calls at dawn and dusk.

t: The Tamaulipas pygmy owl (Glaucidium sanchezi) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae. However, at 53 g (1.9 oz), it is slightly heavier than the long-whiskered owlet and the elf owl.
f: This is one of the smallest owls in the world, with a mean length of 13.5 cm (5.3 in).
The Cuban pygmy owl (Glaucidium siju) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae that is endemic to Cuba.

t: The red-chested owlet (Glaucidium tephronotum) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae, native to the African tropical rainforest.
f: Its habits and behaviour are poorly known.

t: The hook-billed hermit (Glaucis dohrnii) is a threatened species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae.
f: It is endemic to a small area of Brazil.

t: The rufous-breasted hermit or hairy hermit (Glaucis hirsutus) is a hummingbird that breeds from Panama south to Bolivia, and on Trinidad, Tobago and Grenada.
f: It is a widespread and generally common species, though local populations may change in numbers and disappear altogether in marginal habitat.
The tawny-crowned honeyeater (Gliciphila melanops) is a passerine bird native to southern Australia.

t: The musk lorikeet (Trichoglossus concinnus) is a species of bird in the parrot family Psittaculidae.
f: It inhabits south-central/eastern Australia.

t: The wedge-billed woodcreeper (Glyphorynchus spirurus) is a sub-oscine passerine bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Mexico, Central America, Brazil, Bolivia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The chopi blackbird (Gnorimopsar chopi) is a species of passerine bird belonging to the family Icteridae, which contains the New World blackbirds, grackles, New World orioles and related species. This species is found in South America south of the Amazon rainforest.
f: It is the only species in the monospecific genus Gnorimopsar.

t: The Malayan night heron (Gorsachius melanolophus), also known as Malaysian night heron and tiger bittern, is a medium-sized heron.
f: It is distributed in southern and eastern Asia.

t: The southern hill myna (Gracula indica) is a member of the starling family. This species moves around in flocks in the forest, and members of a flock keep in contact with a wide range of vocalizations.
f: It is a resident of the forested regions of south India and Sri Lanka.

t: The Sri Lanka hill myna or Ceylon myna (Gracula ptilogenys) is a myna, a member of the starling family. This bird is endemic to Sri Lanka.
f: The Sri Lanka myna builds a nest in a hole.

t: The common hill myna (Gracula religiosa), sometimes spelled "mynah" and formerly simply known as the hill myna or myna bird, is a species of starling found in the hills of South and Southeast Asia. The Sri Lanka hill myna, a former subspecies of G. religiosa, is now generally accepted as a separate species G. ptilogenys.
f: Its specific name religiosa may allude to the practice of teaching mynas to repeat sacred prayers.

t: The Indian pied myna (Gracupica contra) is a species of starling found in the Indian subcontinent. It is often seen within cities and villages although it is not as bold as the common myna.
f: It is usually found in small groups mainly on the plains and low foothills.

t: The black-collared starling (Gracupica nigricollis) is a species of starling with black and white plumage and a black collar. Its habitats include grassland, dry forest and human settlements.
f: It is found in southern China and most of mainland Southeast Asia, and has been introduced to Taiwan, Malaysia and Singapore.

t: The white-throated antpitta (Grallaria albigula) is a species of bird in the family Grallariidae.

t: The giant antpitta (Grallaria gigantea) is a perching bird species in the antpitta family (Grallariidae). It is presumably a close relative of the similar undulated antpitta, G. squamigera, which occurs to the south of G. gigantea.

t: The scaled antpitta (Grallaria guatimalensis) is a species of bird in the family Grallariidae. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Guyana, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela It has occurred as a vagrant on Trinidad.

t: The chestnut-naped antpitta (Grallaria nuchalis) is a species of bird in the family Grallariidae.

t: The Urubamba antpitta (Grallaria occabambae) is a bird in the family Grallariidae. It is a member of the rufous antpitta species complex and was elevated from subspecies to species in 2020 on the basis of differences in plumage and vocalization.

The rusty-tinged antpitta (Grallaria przewalskii) is a species of bird in the family Grallariidae.

t: The crescent-faced antpitta (Grallaricula lineifrons) is a species of bird in the family Grallariidae.

The ochre-fronted antpitta (Grallaricula ochraceifrons) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Grallariidae.
