t: The magpie-lark (Grallina cyanoleuca), also known as wee magpie, peewee, peewit, mudlark or Murray magpie, is a passerine bird native to Australia, Timor, and southern New Guinea. The male and female both have black and white plumage, though with different patterns.
f: John Latham described the species in 1801.

t: The striated laughingthrush (Grammatoptila striata) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in the northern temperate regions of the Indian subcontinent and ranges across Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Tibet and Nepal.
f: It was at one time placed in the genus Garrulax but following the publication of a comprehensive molecular phylogenetic study in 2018, it was moved to be the only species in the resurrected genus Grammatoptila.

t: The rose-breasted chat (Granatellus pelzelni) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname and Venezuela.

t: The grey-throated chat (Granatellus sallaei) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks.
f: It is found in Belize, Guatemala, and Mexico.
The red-breasted chat (Granatellus venustus) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks.
The purple grenadier (Granatina ianthinogaster) is a common species of estrildid finch found in eastern Africa.
The painted honeyeater (Grantiella picta) is a species of honeyeater in a monotypic genus.

t: The short-tailed parrot (Graydidascalus brachyurus) is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, and Peru.

t: The whooping crane (Grus americana) is an endangered crane species, native to North America, named for its "whooping" calls. Along with the sandhill crane (Antigone canadensis), it is one of only two crane species native to North America, and it is also the tallest North American bird species, with an estimated 22–30+ year life expectancy in the wild.
f: The total number of cranes in the surviving migratory population, plus three reintroduced flocks and in-captivity, is just over 830 birds as of 2025.

t: The common crane (Grus grus), also known as the Eurasian crane, is a bird of the family Gruidae, the cranes. Along with the sandhill crane (Antigone canadensis), demoiselle crane and the brolga (Antigone rubicunda), it is one of only four crane species not currently classified as threatened with extinction or conservation dependent on the species level.
f: A medium-sized species, it is the only crane commonly found in Europe besides the demoiselle crane (Grus virgo) and the Siberian crane (Leucogeranus leucogeranus) that only are regular in the far eastern part of the continent.

t: The red-crowned crane (Grus japonensis), also called the Japanese crane and the Manchurian crane, is a large Northeast Asian crane among the rarest cranes in the world.
f: In some parts of its range, it is known as a symbol of luck, longevity, and fidelity.
The hooded crane (Grus monacha) is a crane native to East Asia and a frequent migratory bird in South Korea and Japan.

t: The black-necked crane (Grus nigricollis) is a medium-sized crane in Asia that breeds on the Tibetan Plateau and remote parts of India and Bhutan. It is 139 cm (55 in) long with a 235 cm (7.71 ft) wingspan, and it weighs 5.5 kg (12 lb).
f: A festival in Bhutan celebrates the bird while the Indian union territory of Ladakh has designated it as the state bird.

Gryllus assimilis, commonly known as the Jamaican field cricket and sometimes referred to as the silent cricket (a misnomer) among other names, is one of many cricket species known as a field cricket.
Gryllus fultoni, the southern wood cricket, is a species of cricket in the subfamily Gryllinae.

t: Gryllus pennsylvanicus is known as the fall field cricket. It tends to be absent in most of the southwestern United States including southern California.
f: G. pennsylvanicus is widespread across much of North America from southern Ontario into parts of northern Mexico.

t: Gryllus rubens, commonly known as the southeastern field cricket, is one of many cricket species known as a field cricket. Its northern range spans from southern Delaware to the extreme southeastern corner of Kansas, with a southern range stretching from Florida to eastern Texas.
f: It occurs throughout most of the Southeastern United States.

t: The golden parakeet, golden conure, or Queen of Bavaria conure (Guaruba guarouba) is a medium-sized golden-yellow Neotropical parrot native to the Amazon Basin of interior northern Brazil. It is the only species placed in the genus Guaruba.
f: It is listed on CITES appendix I.

t: The yellow cardinal (Gubernatrix cristata) is a species of South American bird in the tanager family Thraupidae.
f: It is the only member of its genus, Gubernatrix.

t: The streamer-tailed tyrant (Gubernetes yetapa) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay, and as a vagrant to Uruguay.

t: The guira cuckoo, known in Spanish as the pirincho (Guira guira), is a gregarious species of cuckoo found widely in open and semi-open habitats throughout eastern and southeastern South America. Its range has expanded significantly as a result of deforestation, and it is commonly seen in suburban parks and gardens.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Guira.

t: The eastern crested guinea fowl (Guttera pucherani) is a species of guinea fowl native to East Africa. It is one of three species that were formerly considered to be one and the same species, the crested guinea fowl.
f: It is found in Somalia to Tanzania, Zanzibar and Tumbatu Island, where it inhabits open forest, woodland and forest-savanna mosaics.

t: The Atlantic white tern (Gygis alba), also known as the common white tern, is a small seabird found in the Atlantic Ocean. Other names for the species include angel tern and white noddy.
f: It is sometimes known as the fairy tern, although this name is potentially confusing as it is also the common name of Sternula nereis.

t: The Puerto Rican owl (Gymnasio nudipes) or múcaro común (Spanish via Taino), formerly known as the Puerto Rican screech owl, is a mid-sized "typical owl" in subfamily Striginae.
f: It is endemic to the archipelago of Puerto Rico though it formerly also inhabited the Virgin Islands.

t: The grey-throated barbet (Gymnobucco bonapartei) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family (African barbets).
f: It is found in Angola, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: The naked-faced barbet (Gymnobucco calvus) is a bird species in the family Lybiidae (the African barbets). It used to be placed in the family Bucconidae (puffbirds), which has been split up; alternatively, it may be included in a vastly expanded Ramphastidae (toucans).
f: It is found in Angola, Benin, Cameroon, Republic of the Congo, DRC, Ivory Coast, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, and Togo.

t: The bare-crowned antbird (Gymnocichla nudiceps) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Belize, Colombia, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The California condor (Gymnogyps californianus) is a New World vulture and the largest North American land bird. It is the only surviving member of the genus Gymnogyps, although four extinct members of the genus are also known.
f: It is one of the world's longest-living birds, with a lifespan of up to 60 years.

t: The oriole blackbird (Gymnomystax mexicanus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae.
f: Its genus, Gymnomystax, is monotypic.

t: The duetting giant honeyeater (Gymnomyza brunneirostris), formerly known as the giant honeyeater, is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: The International Ornithologists' Union accepted these proposals and introduced the name "yellow-billed giant honeyeater" for G. viridis and "duetting giant honeyeater" for G. brunneirostris.

t: The mao or maʻomaʻo (Gymnomyza samoensis) is a passerine bird belonging to the genus Gymnomyza in the honeyeater family Meliphagidae. It is an endangered species and is endemic to the Samoan Islands.
f: A single whitish brown speckled egg is laid in a simple sticky cup nest.

t: The bicolored antbird (Gymnopithys bicolor) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The white-cheeked antbird (Gymnopithys leucaspis) is an insectivorous bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The rufous-throated antbird (Gymnopithys rufigula) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The Australian magpie (Gymnorhina tibicen) is a black and white passerine bird native to Australia and southern New Guinea, and introduced to New Zealand, and the Fijian island of Taveuni. Although once considered to be three separate species, it is now considered to be one, with nine recognised subspecies.
f: Described as one of Australia's most accomplished songbirds, the Australian magpie has an array of complex vocalisations.

t: The pinyon jay (Gymnorhinus cyanocephalus) is a species of jay, and is the only member of the genus Gymnorhinus. Native to Western North America, the species ranges from central Oregon to northern Baja California, and eastward as far as western Oklahoma, though wanderers are often sighted beyond this range.
f: It is typically found within foothills, especially where pinyon pines (Pinus edulis and Pinus monophylla) occur.

t: The Sahel bush sparrow (Gymnoris dentata) or bush petronia, is a species of bird in the family Passeridae.
f: It is found in Africa from Mauritania to Guinea and east to Eritrea and the south-western Arabian Peninsula in its natural habitats of dry savanna and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.

t: The yellow-spotted bush sparrow or yellow-spotted petronia (Gymnoris pyrgita) is a species of bird in the sparrow family, Passeridae. Its natural habitats are dry savannah and subtropical or tropical dry lowland grassland.
f: It is common throughout the Sahel and the Horn of Africa.

t: The yellow-throated bush sparrow (Gymnoris superciliaris), also known as the yellow-throated petronia, is a species of bird in the sparrow family Passeridae.
f: It is found in south-central and southern Africa in its natural habitats of subtropical or tropical dry forests, dry savanna, and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.

t: The yellow-throated sparrow or chestnut-shouldered petronia (Gymnoris xanthocollis) is a species of sparrow found in southern Asia. They forage on the ground for grain and for berries in bushes.
f: It is a species mostly of the dry savannah.

t: The white-backed vulture (Gyps africanus) is an Old World vulture in the family Accipitridae, which also includes eagles, kites, buzzards and hawks.
f: It is the most common vulture species in the continent of Africa.

t: It is also known as the Eurasian griffon or griffon vulture, although the latter term is sometimes used for the genus Gyps as a whole.
f: The Eurasian griffon vulture (Gyps fulvus) is a large Old World vulture in the bird of prey family Accipitridae.

t: The Himalayan vulture (Gyps himalayensis) or Himalayan griffon vulture is an Old World vulture native to the Himalayas and foothills in North and Northeastern India, as well as the adjacent Tibetan Plateau. It is listed as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List.
f: After the cinereous vulture (Aegypius monachus), it is the second-largest Old World vulture species, and among the world's largest true raptors.

t: The streaked wren-babbler (Gypsophila brevicaudata) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam.

t: The rusty-breasted wren-babbler (Gypsophila rufipectus) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is endemic to western Sumatra in Indonesia.

t: The black-cheeked ant tanager (Driophlox atrimaxillaris) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae.
f: It was formerly placed with the red-crowned ant tanager in the genus Habia.

t: The crested ant tanager (Driophlox cristata) is a bird in the family Cardinalidae that is endemic to Colombia.
f: It was formerly placed with the red-crowned ant tanager in the genus Habia.

t: The red-throated ant tanager (Driophlox fuscicauda) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals, grosbeaks, and “tanager” allies.
f: It is found from Mexico to Colombia.
The sooty ant tanager (Driophlox gutturalis) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals, grosbeaks, and “tanager” allies.

t: The red-crowned ant tanager (Habia rubica) is a medium-sized passerine bird from tropical America. It is the only species now placed in the genus Habia.
f: This species was long placed with the tanagers (Thraupidae), but it is actually closer to the cardinals (Cardinalidae).

t: The blackish oystercatcher (Haematopus ater) is a species of wading bird in the oystercatcher family Haematopodidae. It is found in Argentina, Chile, the Falkland Islands and Peru, and is a vagrant to Uruguay.
f: The population is estimated at 15,000–80,000.

t: The black oystercatcher (Haematopus bachmani) is a conspicuous black bird found on the shoreline of western North America, ranging from the Aleutian Islands of Alaska to the coast of the Baja California peninsula. It is the only representative of the oystercatcher family (Haematopodidae) over most of its range, overlapping slightly with the American oystercatcher (H. palliatus) on the coast of Baja California.
f: Its scientific name was derived by John James Audubon from that of his friend John Bachman.

t: The South Island oystercatcher or South Island pied oystercatcher (Haematopus finschi) is one of two common oystercatcher species found in New Zealand. The indigenous Māori name is tōrea.
f: Its name is often contracted to the acronym "SIPO" (rhyming with "typo").

t: The sooty oystercatcher (Haematopus fuliginosus) is a species of oystercatcher. It prefers rocky coastlines, but will occasionally live in estuaries.
f: It is a wading bird endemic to Australia and commonly found on its coastline.

t: The Magellanic oystercatcher (Haematopus leucopodus) is a species of wader in the family Haematopodidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Chile and the Falkland Islands in freshwater lake and sandy shore habitats.

t: The pied oystercatcher (Haematopus longirostris) is a species of oystercatcher. The similar South Island pied oystercatcher (H. finschi) occurs in New Zealand.
f: It is a wading bird native to Australia and commonly found on its coastline.

t: The Eurasian oystercatcher or European oystercatcher (Haematopus ostralegus), also known as the common pied oystercatcher, or (in Europe) just oystercatcher, is a wader in the oystercatcher bird family Haematopodidae. It has striking black and white plumage, a long straight orange-red bill, red eyes and relatively short dull pink legs.
f: The sexes are similar in appearance but the bill of the female is longer than that of the male.

t: The American oystercatcher (Haematopus palliatus), occasionally called the American pied oystercatcher, is a member of family Haematopodidae. The current population of American oystercatchers is estimated to be 50,000 – 99,999 mature individuals.
f: Originally called the "sea pie", it was renamed in 1731 when naturalist Mark Catesby claimed that he had observed the bird eating oysters.

t: The variable oystercatcher (Haematopus unicolor) is a species of wader in the family Haematopodidae.
f: They are also known as 'red bills'.

t: The crimson-headed partridge (Haematortyx sanguiniceps) is a species of bird in the pheasant, partridge, and francolin family Phasianidae. Described by the British ornithologist Richard Bowdler Sharpe in 1879, it is the only species in the genus Haematortyx.
f: It is mainly found at elevations of 1,000–1,700 m (3,300–5,600 ft), but can be seen as low as 185 m (607 ft) and as high as 3,050 m (10,010 ft).

t: Cassin's finch (Haemorhous cassinii) is a bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.
f: This species and the other "American rosefinches" are placed in the genus Haemorhous.

t: The house finch (Haemorhous mexicanus) is a North American bird in the finch family. The house finch and the other two American rosefinches (Cassin's and purple finch) are placed in the genus Haemorhous.
f: There are estimated to be 40 million house finches across North America, making it the second-most populous finch, just behind the American goldfinch.

t: The purple finch (Haemorhous purpureus) is a bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.
f: It breeds in the northern United States, southern Canada, and the west coast of North America.

t: The sooty antbird (Hafferia fortis) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The blue-lored antbird (Hafferia immaculata) is a species of antbird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: Zeledon's antbird (Hafferia zeledoni) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The brown-hooded kingfisher (Halcyon albiventris) is a species of bird in the subfamily Halcyoninae, the tree kingfishers. It is found in Sub-Saharan Africa, living in woodland, scrubland, forest edges, and also suburban areas.
f: It has a brown head and blackish and turquoise wings.
The chocolate-backed kingfisher (Halcyon badia) is a species of kingfisher in the subfamily Halcyoninae, native to the African tropical rainforest.

t: The striped kingfisher (Halcyon chelicuti) is a species of bird in the tree kingfisher subfamily. It was first described by Edward, Lord Stanley, in Salt's Voyage to Abyssinia in 1814 as "Chelicut kingfisher" Alaudo Chelicuti.
f: The species' name chelicuti derives from Chelicut in Ethiopia, the location at which Stanley's type specimen was obtained.
The ruddy kingfisher (Halcyon coromanda) is a medium-sized tree kingfisher, widely distributed in east and southeast Asia.

t: The brown-breasted kingfisher (Halcyon gularis) is a tree kingfisher endemic to the Philippines, where it is widely distributed.
f: This kingfisher is a resident over much of its range.

t: The grey-headed kingfisher (Halcyon leucocephala) is a species of bird in the kingfisher family, Alcedinidae. It is found across large parts of Africa and southern Arabia, from Mauritania through Senegal and the Gambia, east to Ethiopia, Somalia, Yemen, Oman and Saudi Arabia, and south all the way through to South Africa.
f: It is also found in islands off the African coast such as the Cape Verde islands and Zanzibar.

t: The blue-breasted kingfisher (Halcyon malimbica) is a tree kingfisher widely distributed across Equatorial Africa. This kingfisher is essentially resident, but retreats from drier savanna areas to wetter habitats in the dry season.
f: A single clutch of two round white eggs is typical.

t: The black-capped kingfisher (Halcyon pileata) is a tree kingfisher which is widely distributed in tropical Asia from India east to China, Korea and Southeast Asia. This most northerly of the tree kingfishers is resident over much of its range, but northern populations are migratory, wintering south of their range in Sri Lanka, Thailand, Borneo and Java.
f: The species is mainly found in coastal and mangrove habitats but can sometimes be found far inland.
The woodland kingfisher (Halcyon senegalensis) is a tree kingfisher that is widely distributed in Africa south of the Sahara.

t: The white-throated kingfisher (Halcyon smyrnensis) also known as the white-breasted kingfisher is a tree kingfisher, widely distributed in Asia from the Sinai east through the Indian subcontinent to China and Indonesia. This kingfisher is a resident over much of its range, although some populations may make short distance movements.
f: It can often be found well away from water where it feeds on a wide range of prey that includes small reptiles, amphibians, crabs, small rodents and even birds.

t: The white-tailed eagle (Haliaeetus albicilla), sometimes known as the "sea eagle", is a large bird of prey, widely distributed across temperate Eurasia. Like other eagles, it is a member of the family Accipitridae (or accipitrids) which also includes other diurnal raptors such as hawks, kites, and harriers.
f: It requires old-growth trees or ample sea cliffs for nesting, and an abundant food supply of fish and birds (largely water birds) over nearly any other prey.

t: The lesser fish eagle (Icthyophaga humilis) is a species of Icthyophaga found in the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the foothills of the Himalayas, and south-east Asia. There are records from Gujarat, Central India and in more recent times from the Kaveri river valley in southern India, although the south Indian records are now thought to come from an isolated population, disjunct from the species' normal range.
f: Lesser fish eagles are fish-eating birds that have feet adapted to aid in gripping slippery fish.

t: The grey-headed fish eagle (Icthyophaga ichthyaetus) is a fish-eating bird of prey from Southeast Asia. It is a large stocky raptor with adults having dark brown upper body, grey head and lighter underbelly and white legs.
f: Juveniles are paler with darker streaking.

t: The bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a bird of prey found in North America. A sea eagle, it has two known subspecies and forms a species pair with the white-tailed eagle (Haliaeetus albicilla), which occupies the same niche as the bald eagle in the Palearctic.
f: It builds the largest nest of any North American bird and the largest tree nests ever recorded for any animal species, up to 4 m (13 ft) deep, 2.5 m (8.2 ft) wide, and 1 metric ton (1.1 short tons) in weight.

t: The white-bellied sea eagle (Icthyophaga leucogaster), also known as the white-breasted sea eagle, is a large diurnal bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. Originally described by Johann Friedrich Gmelin in 1788, it is closely related to Sanford's sea eagle of the Solomon Islands, and the two are considered a superspecies.
f: Resident from India and Sri Lanka through Southeast Asia to Australia on coasts and major waterways, the white-bellied sea eagle breeds and hunts near water, and fish form around half of its diet.

t: Steller's sea eagle (Haliaeetus pelagicus), also known as the Pacific sea eagle or white-shouldered eagle, is a very large diurnal bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. It was described first by Peter Simon Pallas in 1811.
f: Typically, it is the heaviest eagle in the world, at about 5 to 10 kg (11 to 22 lb), but in some other standard measurements, may be smaller than the harpy eagle (Harpia harpyja) and the Philippine eagle (Pithecophaga jefferyi).

t: The African fish eagle (Icthyophaga vocifer) or the African sea eagle is a large species of eagle found throughout sub-Saharan Africa wherever large bodies of open water with an abundant food supply occur. As a result of its large range, it is known in many languages.
f: It is the national bird of Malawi, Namibia, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

t: The brahminy kite is found mainly on the coast and in inland wetlands, where it feeds on dead fish and other prey.
f: Adults have a reddish-brown body plumage contrasting with their white head and breast which make them easy to distinguish from other birds of prey.

t: The whistling kite (Haliastur sphenurus) is a medium-sized diurnal raptor found throughout Australia (including coastal islands), New Caledonia and much of New Guinea (excluding the central mountains and the northwest). Some authorities put this species in the genus Milvus, despite marked differences in behaviour, voice and plumage between this species and other members of that genus.
f: Also called the whistling eagle or whistling hawk, it is named for its loud whistling call, which it often gives in flight.

t: The yellow-breasted crake (Laterallus flaviventer) is a species of bird in the subfamily Rallinae of family Rallidae, the rails, gallinules, and coots.
f: It is found on several Caribbean islands and in most of Central America and South America.

t: The rusty-faced parrot (Hapalopsittaca amazonina) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela and possibly Ecuador.
Fuertes's parrot (Hapalopsittaca fuertesi), also known as the indigo-winged parrot, is an Endangered species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.

t: The white-faced nunbird (Hapaloptila castanea) is a species of bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The greenish puffleg (Haplophaedia aureliae) is a species of hummingbird in the "brilliants", tribe Heliantheini in subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, and Peru.

t: The uniform finch (Haplospiza unicolor) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in the southern Atlantic Forest of Brazil, Paraguay and far northeastern Argentina.

t: The Philippine trogon (Harpactes ardens) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae. It is endemic to the Philippines found on regions of Luzon, Eastern Visayas, and Mindanao.
f: It is the only species of trogon in the country.

t: Diard's trogon (Harpactes diardii) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.
f: Diard's trogon eats caterpillars, beetles, stick-insects, locustids and other Orthoptera, and fruits.

t: The scarlet-rumped trogon (Harpactes duvaucelii) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae. It is distinguishable from other trogons by its small size and reddish rump.
f: It has also been called the red-rumped trogon and Duvaucel's trogon.
The red-headed trogon (Harpactes erythrocephalus) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae.

t: The Malabar trogon (Harpactes fasciatus) is a species of bird in the trogon family. It is found in the forests of India and Sri Lanka.
f: The birds utter low, guttural calls that can be heard only at close quarters, and perch still on a branch under the forest canopy, often facing away from the viewer, making them easy to miss despite their colourful plumage.

t: The red-naped trogon (Harpactes kasumba) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The orange-breasted trogon (Harpactes oreskios) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae. It is a colorful, sedentary species that inhabits the lower canopy of the lowlands and forest of southern China, southeast Asia, Borneo, Sumatra and Java.
f: Adults breed between January and May, excavating their nest into dead tree stumps.
The cinnamon-rumped trogon (Harpactes orrhophaeus) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae, known for their colorful plumage.

t: Ward's trogon (Harpactes wardi) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae. Its range includes the northeastern parts of the Indian subcontinent stretching eastwards to Southeast Asia.
f: It also has a disjunct population in northern Vietnam, but there are no recent records from there.

t: The double-toothed kite (Harpagus bidentatus) is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Accipitrinae, the "true" hawks, of family Accipitridae.
f: It is found from central Mexico through Central America into much of northern and eastern South America.

t: The rufous-thighed kite (Harpagus diodon) is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Accipitrinae, the "true" hawks, of family Accipitridae.
f: It is found regularly in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Guyana, Paraguay, and Suriname and as a vagrant in Colombia, French Guiana, and Venezuela.

t: The harpy eagle (Harpia harpyja) is a large neotropical species of eagle. It is also called the American harpy eagle to distinguish it from the Papuan eagle, which is sometimes known as the New Guinea harpy eagle or Papuan harpy eagle.
f: It is the largest bird of prey throughout its range, and among the largest extant species of eagles in the world.

t: The Papuan eagle (Harpyopsis novaeguineae) is a large bird of prey. It is also known by several other names, including Papuan harpy eagle, New Guinea eagle, New Guinea harpy eagle, or kapul eagle, the latter name from the local name for a usually arboreal marsupial that the eagle is known to regularly hunt.
f: Unique amongst eagles, the Papuan eagle is a surprisingly fast and agile terrestrial avian predator and is capable of chasing down prey on the forest floor.

t: The collared sunbird (Hedydipna collaris) is a bird species of the family Nectariniidae. The sunbirds are a group of very small Old World passerine birds which feed largely on nectar, although they will also take insects, especially when feeding young.
f: Most species can take nectar by hovering like a hummingbird, but usually perch to feed most of the time.

t: The Nile Valley sunbird (Hedydipna metallica) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is found in Djibouti, Egypt, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Rwanda, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Sudan, Libya, and Yemen.
f: The display includes a hovering, accompanied by body rocking and wing-whirring.
The pygmy sunbird (Hedydipna platura) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae.

t: The amethyst-throated sunangel (Heliangelus amethysticollis) is a species of hummingbird in the "coquettes", tribe Lesbiini of subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The tourmaline sunangel (Heliangelus exortis) is a species of hummingbird in the "coquettes", tribe Lesbiini of subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The purple-throated sunangel (Heliangelus viola) is a species of hummingbird in the "coquettes", tribe Lesbiini of subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The slender-billed kite (Helicolestes hamatus) is a South American bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. The species was recategorized into and has once again been removed from the genus Rostrhamus.
f: It is found along a scattered range in forested parts of tropical northern and central South America, and far eastern Panama.

t: The sharp-billed treehunter (Heliobletus contaminatus), sometimes called the sharp-billed xenops, is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The green-crowned brilliant (Heliodoxa jacula) is species of hummingbird in the "brilliants", tribe Heliantheini in subfamily Lesbiinae. It is also known as the green-fronted brilliant.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, and Panama.

t: The violet-fronted brilliant (Heliodoxa leadbeateri) is a species of hummingbird in the "brilliants", tribe Heliantheini in subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The fawn-breasted brilliant (Heliodoxa rubinoides) is a medium-sized species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae. It is native to South America, where it occurs in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
f: Other common names include lilac-throated brilliant in English and brillante pechigamuza, colibrí de vientre ocre, and diamante pechigamuza in Spanish.

t: The plain-capped starthroat (Heliomaster constantii) is a species of hummingbird in the "mountain gems", tribe Lampornithini in subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found from Mexico to Costa Rica.

t: The long-billed starthroat (Heliomaster longirostris) is a species of hummingbird in the "mountain gems", tribe Lampornithini in subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Mexico, Central America, Trinidad, and all but the four southernmost countries of South America.

t: The sungrebe or American finfoot (Heliornis fulica) is a small aquatic gruiform found in the tropical and subtropical Americas from northeastern Mexico to central Ecuador and southern Brazil. The sungrebe is now the only species placed in the genus Heliornis that was erected by the French naturalist Pierre Bonnaterre in 1791 with the sungrebe as the type species.
f: Sungrebes are unique among birds in that males have "pouches", folds of skin under their wings in which they carry their young from hatching until the chicks are able to swim for themselves.

t: The black-eared fairy (Heliothryx auritus) is a species of hummingbird in the subfamily Polytminae, the mangoes.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The white-browed spinetail (Hellmayrea gularis) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The worm-eating warbler (Helmitheros vermivorum) is a small New World warbler that breeds in the Eastern United States and migrates to southern Mexico, the Caribbean, and Central America for the winter.
f: It is the only species in the genus Helmitheros.

t: Pallas's grasshopper warbler (Helopsaltes certhiola), also known as the rusty-rumped warbler, is an Old World warbler in the genus Helopsaltes. It breeds in the eastern Palearctic: from the Altai Mountains, Mongolia and Transbaikalia to northeastern China, the Korean Peninsula, and islands in the Sea of Okhotsk (Sakhalin and Kuril Islands).
f: It is migratory, wintering from India eastward to Indonesia.

t: Middendorff's grasshopper warbler (Helopsaltes ochotensis) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Locustellidae. It breeds in eastern Siberia to northern Japan, Kamchatka Peninsula and northern Kuril Islands.
f: It winters in the Philippines, Borneo and Sulawesi and in small numbers in China, Hong Kong, South Korea, Malaysia, Taiwan and the U.S.A.

t: The marsh grassbird (Helopsaltes pryeri), also known as the Japanese swamp warbler, is a species of Old World warbler in the family Locustellidae. It is found in China, Japan, South Korea, Mongolia, and Russia.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The heart-spotted woodpecker (Hemicircus canente) is a species of bird in the woodpecker family. They have a wide distribution across Asia with populations in the forests of southwestern and central India which are slightly separated from their ranges in the Himalayas and Southeast Asia.
f: They move about in pairs or small groups and are often found in mixed-species foraging flocks.

t: The grey-and-buff woodpecker (Hemicircus concretus) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. Its natural habitats are lowland and montane tropical or subtropical moist broadleaf forests.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia (Sumatra and Borneo), Malaysia, southern Myanmar, and southern Thailand, but has become regionally extinct in Singapore.

t: The ʻakiapōlāʻau (ah-kee-ah-POH-lah-ow), also known as the Hawaiian woodpecker, is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper that is endemic to the island of Hawaii. Its natural habitats are dry and montane moist forests, and it is the only bird species on the island to occupy the woodpecker niche.
f: It is the only member of the subgenus Heterorhynchus, which has a woodpecker-like feeding habitat and exclusively preys on insects, in contrast to the nukupuʻu, which were both insect-eaters and also hummingbird-like nectarivores.

t: The kererū (Hemiphaga novaeseelandiae), also known as kūkupa (northern Māori dialects), New Zealand pigeon or wood pigeon, is a species of pigeon native to New Zealand. Johann Friedrich Gmelin described the bird in 1789 as a large, conspicuous pigeon up to 50 cm (20 in) in length and 550–850 g (19–30 oz) in weight, with a white breast and iridescent green–blue plumage.
f: They construct nests with twigs in trees, with a single egg clutch.

t: The whiskered treeswift (Hemiprocne comata) is a species of bird in the family Hemiprocnidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical mangrove forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is the smallest of 4 species in genus Hemiprocne and is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The crested treeswift (Hemiprocne coronata) is a species of tree swift. It is distinct in flight, with long, bowed wings and a deeply forked tail that usually appears narrow and pointed.
f: It was for some time considered the same species as its eastern relative, the gray-rumped treeswift (Hemiprocne longipennis), but they do not interbreed where their ranges overlap.

t: The grey-rumped treeswift (Hemiprocne longipennis) is a species of bird in the Hemiprocnidae family. Currently, four extant species are placed in the family.
f: Like the other members of the Hemiprocnidae, this species is closely related to true swifts, but unlike true swifts, the treeswifts are arboreal, often seen perched on trees, high-tension power transmission lines, and pylons.

t: The moustached treeswift (Hemiprocne mystacea) is a species of bird in the family Hemiprocnidae. It is found in the northern Moluccas, New Guinea, Bismarck and the Solomon Islands archipelagos.
f: Recent scientific studies, such as Rohwer and Wang's quantitative analysis in 2010, have highlighted the unique feather replacement patterns that contribute to its agile flight and successful prey capture.

t: The black-winged flycatcher-shrike (Hemipus hirundinaceus) is a species of bird in the flycatcher-shrike genus, Hemipus. It is usually placed in the Vangidae.
f: It is found in the Malay Peninsula and the Greater Sunda Islands.

t: The bar-winged flycatcher-shrike (Hemipus picatus) is a small passerine bird usually placed in the Vangidae. It is found in the forests of tropical southern Asia from the Himalayas and hills of southern India to Indonesia.
f: They perch upright and have a distinctive pattern of black and white, males being more shiny black than the females.

t: The yellow-backed tanager (Hemithraupis flavicollis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Panama and every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The guira tanager (Hemithraupis guira) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.
The rufous-headed tanager (Hemithraupis ruficapilla) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.

t: The cinnamon-breasted tody-tyrant (Hemitriccus cinnamomeipectus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The Acre tody-tyrant (Hemitriccus cohnhafti) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The drab-breasted bamboo tyrant or drab-breasted pygmy-tyrant (Hemitriccus diops) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The flammulated bamboo tyrant (Hemitriccus flammulatus), also called flammulated pygmy-tyrant, is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.

t: The Amazonian inezia, or Amazonian tyrannulet, (Inezia subflava) is a species of passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, and Venezuela.

t: The slender-billed inezia, or slender-billed tyrannulet, (Inezia tenuirostris) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The white-browed purpletuft (Iodopleura isabellae) is a small species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
The buff-throated purpletuft (Iodopleura pipra) is a small Endangered species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.

t: The buff-vented bulbul (Iole crypta) is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. It is found in south-eastern Myanmar, south-western Thailand, on the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra and nearby islands.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The yellow-browed bulbul (Acritillas indica), or golden-browed bulbul, is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. It is found in the forests of southern India and Sri Lanka.
f: The yellow-browed bulbul is mainly yellow on the underside and olive above with a distinct yellow brow.

t: The grey-eyed bulbul (Iole propinqua) is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae.
f: It is found in Southeast Asia in its natural habitat of subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

t: The olive bulbul (Iole viridescens) is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found from southern Myanmar to south-western Thailand and the Malay Peninsula.

t: The white-throated robin or irania (Irania gutturalis) is a small, migratory passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae, and the only member of the genus Irania. Males have lead-grey upperparts and bright orange underparts with a namesake white throat patch.
f: It breeds on high-altitude mountain slopes with dense scrub in western Asia and winters in East Africa.

t: The Philippine fairy-bluebird (Irena cyanogastra) is a species of bird in the family Irenidae. Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forest and tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines being found in the islands of Luzon, Mindanao, Samar Leyte, and Bohol.

t: The Asian fairy-bluebird (Irena puella) is a medium-sized, arboreal passerine bird. This fairy-bluebird is found in forests across tropical southern Asia, Indochina and the Greater Sundas.
f: Both species are considered as sacred to the Tagalog people as they are perceived as tigmamanukan omens.

t: The yellow-throated tanager (Iridosornis analis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The purplish-mantled tanager (Iridosornis porphyrocephalus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The golden-crowned tanager (Iridosornis rufivertex) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The rufous-bellied antwren (Isleria guttata) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The plain-throated antwren (Isleria hauxwelli) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The blood pheasant (Ithaginis cruentus) or blood partridge is a galliforme bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae and the only species in the genus Ithaginis. It is a relatively small, short-tailed pheasant that is widespread in the lower Himalayas ranging across North and East India, Nepal, Bhutan, South China and northern Myanmar.
f: The blood pheasant is the state bird of Sikkim, India.

t: The cinnamon bittern (Botaurus cinnamomeus) or chestnut bittern is a small Old World bittern, breeding in tropical and subtropical Asia from India east to China and Indonesia. This species was formerly placed in the genus Ixobrychus.
f: It is mainly resident, but some northern birds migrate short distances.

t: The black-backed bittern (Botaurus dubius), also known as the black-backed least bittern or Australian little bittern, is a little-known species of heron in the family Ardeidae found in Australia and vagrant to southern New Guinea. This species was formerly placed in the genus Ixobrychus.
f: Formerly lumped with the little bittern, it is one of the smallest herons in the world.

t: Von Schrenck's bittern or Schrenck's bittern (Botaurus eurhythmus) is a small bittern named after Leopold von Schrenck, the 19th-century Russian zoologist. It breeds in southeast Siberia, east China, the Korean Peninsula and Japan.
f: It winters from the Malay Peninsula to the Greater Sunda Islands, Sulawesi and the Philippines.

t: The least bittern (Botaurus exilis) is a small heron, the smallest member of the family Ardeidae found in the Americas.
f: This species was formerly placed in the genus Ixobrychus.

t: The black bittern (Botaurus flavicollis) is a bittern of Old World origin, breeding in tropical Asia from Pakistan, India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka east to China, Indonesia, and Australia. This species was formerly placed in the genus Ixobrychus.
f: It is mainly resident, but some northern birds migrate short distances.

t: The stripe-backed bittern (Botaurus involucris) is a South American bird species belonging to the family Ardeidae. It was formerly placed in the genus Ixobrychus.
f: Commonly found near freshwater swamps, marshes, lake shores and streams, stripe-backed bitterns are distributed in two disjunct populations in the north and south of the continent, spanning both sides of the Andes.

t: The little bittern (Botaurus minutus) is a wading bird in the heron family, Ardeidae.
f: This species was formerly placed in the genus Ixobrychus.

t: The yellow bittern (Botaurus sinensis) is a small bittern of Old World origins that breeds in the northern Indian subcontinent, east to the Russian Far East, Japan, and Indonesia. It has been recorded as a vagrant in Alaska.
f: It is mainly a resident bird, but some northern birds migrate short distances.

t: The spotted greenbul (Ixonotus guttatus) or spotted bulbul, is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. It is classified in the monotypic genus Ixonotus.
f: It is widely spread throughout the African tropical rainforest, from Sierra Leone and Guinea to Ghana; southern Nigeria to Uganda, northern Tanzania, eastern and central Democratic Republic of the Congo and extreme north-western Angola.

t: The varied thrush (Ixoreus naevius) is a member of the thrush family, Turdidae.
f: It is the only species in the monotypic genus Ixoreus.

t: The streaked bulbul (Ixos malaccensis), or green-backed bulbul, is a songbird species in the bulbul family (Pycnonotidae). It is found on the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, and Borneo.
f: It is becoming rare due to habitat loss.

t: The mountain bulbul (Ixos mcclellandii) is a songbird species in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. It is often placed in Hypsipetes, but seems to be closer to the type species of the genus Ixos, the Sunda bulbul.
f: It is named after British East India Company Surgeon John McClelland.

t: The speckled tanager (Ixothraupis guttata) is a medium-sized passerine bird. It is a resident breeder in Costa Rica, Panama, Trinidad, Venezuela, Colombia, Guyana, Suriname and the north of Brazil.
f: The small cup nest is built in a tree and the normal clutch is two brown-blotched white eggs.

t: The spotted tanager (Ixothraupis punctata) is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The rufous-throated tanager (Ixothraupis rufigula) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The dotted tanager (Ixothraupis varia) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The jabiru ( or ; Jabiru mycteria) is a large stork found in the Americas from Mexico to Argentina, except west of the Andes. The only member of the genus of the same name, it is most common in the Pantanal region of Brazil and the eastern Paraguayan Chaco.
f: The name comes from the Tupi–Guaraní languages and means 'swollen neck'.

t: The three-toed jacamar (Jacamaralcyon tridactyla) is a species of bird in the family Galbulidae. It is monotypic within the genus Jacamaralcyon.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The great jacamar (Jacamerops aureus) is a species of bird in the family Galbulidae. It is placed in the monotypic genus Jacamerops.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela, where its natural habitat is subtropical and tropical moist lowland forests.

t: The wattled jacana (Jacana jacana) is a wader in the family Jacanidae found throughout much of South America east of the Andes, as well as western Panama and Trinidad. It is the only species in the Jacanidae family with such a large distribution.
f: Wattled jacanas have long toes and claws which help them walk through aquatic vegetation.

t: The northern jacana or northern jaçana (Jacana spinosa) is a wader which is known as a resident breeder from coastal Mexico to western Panama, and on Cuba, Jamaica and Hispaniola in the Caribbean. The jacanas are a group of wetland birds, which are identifiable by their huge feet and claws, which enable them to walk on floating vegetation in the shallow lakes that are their preferred habitat.
f: It is sometimes known to breed in Texas, United States, and has also been recorded on several occasions as a vagrant in Arizona.

t: The dark-eyed junco (Junco hyemalis) is a species of junco, a group of small, grayish New World sparrows. It is a variable species, much like the related fox sparrow (Passerella iliaca), and its systematics are still not completely resolved.
f: The species is common across much of temperate North America and in summer it ranges far into the Arctic.

t: The yellow-eyed junco (Junco phaeonotus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.
f: It is found from the southwestern United States to Guatemala.

t: The red-throated wryneck (Jynx ruficollis), also known as the rufous-necked wryneck or red-breasted wryneck, is a species of wryneck in the woodpecker family closely related to the Eurasian wryneck. Its three subspecies are resident in much of sub-Saharan Africa in open habitats with some trees.
f: The red-throated wryneck nests in pre-existing holes, usually in trees, preferring old barbet or woodpecker nests.

t: The Eurasian wryneck or northern wryneck (Jynx torquilla) is a species of wryneck in the woodpecker family. It mainly breeds in temperate regions of Europe and Asia.
f: When disturbed at the nest, they use this snake-like head twisting and hissing as a threat display.

t: The grey-chested babbler (Kakamega poliothorax), also known as the grey-chested kakamega or grey-chested illadopsis, is a species of bird in the family Modulatricidae. It is found in the Cameroon line, western Kenya and the Albertine rift montane forests.
f: It is the only species in its genus.

t: The lizard buzzard (Kaupifalco monogrammicus), or lizard hawk, is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. It is the only species placed in the genus Kaupifalco.
f: Despite its name, it may be more closely related to the Accipiter hawks than the Buteo buzzards.

t: The striped wren-babbler (Kenopia striata) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is monotypic within the genus Kenopia.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: It is native to China, Japan, and the Russian Far East. This species is a part of the family known as typical owls (Strigidae), which contains most species of owl.
f: Blakiston's fish owl (Ketupa blakistoni), the largest living species of owl, is a fish owl, a sub-group of eagle-owls that specialize in hunting in riparian areas.

t: The buffy fish owl (Ketupa ketupu), also known as the Malay fish owl, is a fish owl in the family Strigidae. Due to its wide distribution and assumed stable population, it is listed as least concern on the IUCN Red List since 2004.
f: It is native to Southeast Asia and lives foremost in tropical forests and wetlands.

t: The brown fish owl (Ketupa zeylonensis) is a fish owl species in the family known as typical owls, Strigidae. It is native from Turkey to South and Southeast Asia.
f: Of the four living species of fish owl, it is the most widely distributed, most common and best-studied.

t: The violet-headed hummingbird (Klais guimeti) is a species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical moist montane forest, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is the only species in the genus Klais.

t: The black-capped hemispingus (Kleinothraupis atropileus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in the Andes mountains of Colombia, Ecuador, Venezuela and Peru.

t: Parodi's hemispingus (Kleinothraupis parodii) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, endemic to Peru.
f: Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The white-winged black tyrant (Knipolegus aterrimus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay, Peru, and as a vagrant to Brazil and Chile.

t: Hudson's black tyrant (Knipolegus hudsoni) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay, and as a vagrant to Brazil and Peru.

t: The riverside tyrant (Knipolegus orenocensis) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The rufous-tailed tyrant (Knipolegus poecilurus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The purple-naped spiderhunter or purple-naped sunbird (Kurochkinegramma hypogrammicum) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is the only species in the genus Kurochkinegramma.
f: A subsequent 2017 study, conducted by some of the same authors and using additional sequence data, found that the purple-naped spiderhunter occupied a basal position to Arachnothera.

t: The banded kingfisher (Lacedo pulchella) is a tree kingfisher found in lowland tropical forests of southeast Asia. Male and female adults are very different in plumage.
f: It is the only member of the genus Lacedo.

t: The mountain velvetbreast (Lafresnaya lafresnayi) is a species of hummingbird in the "brilliants", tribe Heliantheini in subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: Jameson's firefinch (Lagonosticta rhodopareia) is a common species of estrildid finch, sparsely spread across sub-Saharan Africa.
f: It has an estimated global extent of occurrence of 2,600,000 km2.

t: The African firefinch (Lagonosticta rubricata), also called the blue-billed firefinch, is a common species of estrildid finch found in many parts of Africa.
f: It has an estimated global extent of occurrence of 5,400,000 km2 (2,100,000 mi2).

t: The red-billed firefinch or Senegal firefinch (Lagonosticta senegala) is a small seed-eating bird in the family Estrildidae. It was introduced to Egypt, but the population there has become extinct.
f: This is a resident breeding bird in most of Sub-Saharan Africa with an estimated global extent of occurrence of 10,000,000 km2.

t: The willow ptarmigan ( TAR-mi-gən; Lagopus lagopus) is a bird in the grouse tribe Tetraonini of the pheasant family Phasianidae. It is also known as the willow grouse.
f: It is the state bird of Alaska.

t: The white-tailed ptarmigan (Lagopus leucura), also known as the snow quail, is the smallest bird in the grouse tribe. It is a permanent resident of high altitudes on or above the tree line and is native to Alaska and the mountainous parts of Canada and the western United States.
f: The nest is a simple depression in the ground in which up to eight eggs are laid.

t: The rock ptarmigan (Lagopus muta) is a medium-sized game bird in the grouse tribe. It is the official bird for the Canadian territory of Nunavut, where it is known as the aqiggiq (ᐊᕿᒡᒋᖅ), and the official game bird for the province of Newfoundland and Labrador.
f: It is known simply as the ptarmigan in Europe.

t: The rufous-bellied triller (Lalage aurea) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.
f: It is endemic to North Maluku in Indonesia.

t: The lesser cuckooshrike (Lalage fimbriata) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, and Thailand.
f: It generally keeps to treetops, where it can be seen singly or in pairs and often in mixed flocks.

t: The varied triller (Lalage leucomela) like its better-known relative the white-winged triller, is a smaller member of the cuckoo-shrike family, Campephagidae. Common to very common in the north, they are uncommon to rare in the colder south.
f: Varied trillers work their way slowly and methodically through foliage at any level (sometimes on the ground), searching in pairs or small groups for insects and fruit, and making repeated rolling contact calls almost continuously.

t: The long-tailed triller (Lalage leucopyga) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae. The Norfolk Island subspecies of the long-tailed triller, the Norfolk triller, has become extinct.
f: It is found in New Caledonia, Solomon Islands, and Vanuatu.

t: The Polynesian triller (Lalage maculosa) is a passerine bird belonging to the triller genus Lalage in the cuckoo-shrike family Campephagidae. It has numerous subspecies distributed across the islands of the south-west Pacific.
f: The song is short and high-pitched.
The black-headed cuckooshrike (Lalage melanoptera) is a species of cuckooshrike found in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.

t: The black-winged cuckooshrike (Lalage melaschistos), also known as lesser grey cuckooshrike or dark grey cuckooshrike, is a species of cuckooshrike found in South to Southeast Asia. They have broad based bills with grey upper parts, black wings, white vent, graduated white-tipped tails, black bills and legs.
f: Despite the name, they (cuckooshrikes) are unrelated to either shrikes or cuckoos.

t: The pied triller (Lalage nigra) is a species of bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae.
f: It is found in Brunei, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The white-winged triller (Lalage tricolor) is one of the smaller members of the cuckooshrike family, Campephagidae. It is found throughout mainland Australia and possibly on the islands to the north, including New Guinea and eastern Indonesia.
f: In the non-breeding season, male birds appear similar to the female, retaining blackish feathers only on the wings and tail.

t: The amethyst-throated mountaingem (Lampornis amethystinus), also called amethyst-throated mountain-gem or amethyst-throated hummingbird, is a species of hummingbird in tribe Lampornithini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.

t: The blue-throated mountaingem, also known as the blue-throated mountain-gem or blue-throated hummingbird (Lampornis clemenciae) is a species of hummingbird in tribe Lampornithini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in the United States and Mexico.

t: The green-breasted mountaingem or green-breasted mountain-gem (Lampornis sybillae) is a species of hummingbird in tribe Lampornithini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Honduras and Nicaragua.

t: The green-throated mountaingem or green-throated mountain-gem (Lampornis viridipallens) is a species of hummingbird in tribe Lampornithini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.

t: The velvet-fronted grackle (Lampropsar tanagrinus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, monotypic within the genus Lampropsar.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, and Venezuela where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical swamps and heavily degraded former forest.

t: The red-billed pied tanager (Lamprospiza melanoleuca) is a species of bird in the family Mitrospingidae. Placed in family Thraupidae, the "true" tanagers, for over two centuries, the International Ornithological Committee reclassified this species to Mitrospingidae in 2018.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru and Suriname.

t: Burchell's starling (Lamprotornis australis) or Burchell's glossy-starling is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae. The monogamous and presumably sedentary species is native to dry and mesic woodlands and savannah of southern Africa.
f: The name of this bird commemorates the English naturalist William John Burchell.

t: It is common in most of its range, but largely absent from the arid northwest and the eastern lowlands of South Africa. It is found in open habitats such as grassland, karoo scrub, thornbush and agricultural land, and often associates with farm animals.
f: The pied starling or African pied starling (Lamprotornis bicolor) is a bird endemic to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini.

t: The long-tailed glossy starling (Lamprotornis caudatus) is a member of the starling family of birds. It is a resident breeder in tropical Africa from Senegal east to Sudan.
f: The long-tailed glossy starling builds a nest in a hole.

t: The greater blue-eared starling or greater blue-eared glossy-starling (Lamprotornis chalybaeus) is a bird that breeds from Senegal east to Ethiopia and south through eastern Africa to northeastern South Africa and Angola.
f: It is a very common species of open woodland bird, and undertakes some seasonal migration.
The lesser blue-eared starling or lesser blue-eared glossy-starling (Lamprotornis chloropterus) is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae.

t: Hildebrandt's starling (Lamprotornis hildebrandti) is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae. It forms a superspecies with and has previously been included in the same species as Shelley's starling, a migratory species ranging from Ethiopia and Somalia to Kenya.
f: The species is named after Johann Maria Hildebrandt, a German collector who was the first European to obtain specimens.

t: Meves's starling (Lamprotornis mevesii), also Meves's glossy starling and Long-tailed starling, is a species of starling in the genus Lamprotornis. It is found in Angola, Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.
f: It can be distinguished from the similar Burchell's starling by its longer tail with strongly graduated feathers , and from other long-tailed species of Lamprotornis by its dark eyes.

t: The Cape starling (Lamprotornis nitens), also known as red-shouldered glossy-starling or Cape glossy starling, is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae.
f: It is found in Southern Africa, where it lives in woodlands, bushveld and in suburbs.

t: Rüppell's starling (Lamprotornis purpuroptera), also known as Rueppell's glossy-starling or Rueppell's long-tailed starling, is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae.
f: It is found in the African countries of Burundi, Chad, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.
The splendid starling (Lamprotornis splendidus), also known as the splendid glossy-starling, is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae.
The superb starling (Lamprotornis superbus) is a member of the starling family of birds.

t: The ashy starling (Lamprotornis unicolor) is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae. It is alternatively placed in the genus Cosmopsarus or Spreo.
f: It is found in Kenya and Tanzania.

t: The Ethiopian boubou (Laniarius aethiopicus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in Eritrea, Ethiopia, northwest Somalia, and northern Kenya.
f: It has a narrow wing stripe, extending across the median and larger wing coverts, and often a bit onto the secondary remiges.

t: It has black upper parts with a white flash on the wing, and bright scarlet underparts. The International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated it as a "least-concern species".
f: The crimson-breasted shrike (Laniarius atrococcineus) or the crimson-breasted gonolek, ('gonolek' - supposedly imitative of its call), or the crimson-breasted boubou, is a southern African bird.
The yellow-breasted boubou (Laniarius atroflavus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae.

t: The yellow-crowned gonolek (Laniarius barbarus), also known as the common gonolek, is a medium-sized passerine bird in the bushshrike family. It is a common resident breeding bird in equatorial Africa from Senegal and Democratic Republic of Congo east to Ethiopia.
f: The nest is a cup structure in a bush or tree in which two eggs are laid.

t: The swamp boubou (Laniarius bicolor), also known as the Gabon boubou, is a species of bird in the Malaconotidae or bushshrike family. It is native to western and southern Central Africa.
f: The pair bond appears to be maintained by duetting, which in the south is generally synchronous or overlapping.

t: The black-headed gonolek (Laniarius erythrogaster) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in the African countries of Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.
f: However, close to human habitation and in gardens, it often becomes much bolder.

t: The southern boubou (Laniarius ferrugineus) ('ferrugineus' - rust-coloured) is a species of bushshrike. Though these passerine birds and their relations were once included with true shrikes in the Laniidae, they are not closely related to that family.
f: It frequents dense thickets in forests, mangroves, scrub and gardens.

t: Fülleborn's boubou (Laniarius fuelleborni) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in Malawi, Tanzania, and Zambia, where its typical habitat is humid montane forest, dense undergrowth, secondary growth, forest edges and bamboo groves.
f: The name of this bird commemorates the German physician Friedrich Fülleborn.

t: The slate-colored boubou or slate-coloured boubou (Laniarius funebris) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.
f: Songs are frequently sung in a duet between the male and female of a mated pair.

t: Lühder's bushshrike (Laniarius luehderi) is a species of bird (a shrike) in the family Malaconotidae. The common name and Latin binomial commemorate the German naturalist ornithologist W.
f: It is found in Angola, Burundi, Cameroon, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: The tropical boubou or bell shrike (Laniarius aethiopicus) is a medium-sized passerine bird of sub-Saharan Africa.
f: This very diverse "species" with its numerous subspecies and morphs has since long posed a taxonomic problem, and recent research suggests it is a cryptic species complex that has now been split into several species.

t: The papyrus gonolek (Laniarius mufumbiri) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, and Uganda.
f: It has specialised habitat requirements, being restricted to papyrus swamps.
The mountain sooty boubou (Laniarius poensis), western boubou or mountain boubou, is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae.

t: The East Coast boubou or Zanzibar boubou (Laniarius sublacteus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found from southeast Somalia to northeast Tanzania, and Zanzibar island.
f: It has vestigial or no white wing stripe.
The Brazilian laniisoma (Laniisoma elegans) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.

t: The black-throated shrike-tanager (Lanio aurantius) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.

t: The fulvous shrike-tanager (Lanio fulvus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The white-throated shrike-tanager (Lanio leucothorax) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The white-winged shrike-tanager (Lanio versicolor) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The cinereous mourner (Laniocera hypopyrra) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The speckled mourner (Laniocera rufescens) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae.
f: It is found in Mexico, in every Central American country except El Salvador, and in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The northern shrike (Lanius borealis) is a large songbird species in the shrike family (Laniidae) native to North America and Siberia.
f: Long considered a subspecies of the great grey shrike, it was classified as a distinct species in 2017.

t: The bull-headed shrike (Lanius bucephalus) is a passerine bird of eastern Asia belonging to the shrike family Laniidae. It is 19–20 cm (approx. 7.48-7.9 inches) long.
f: The isolated race sicarius is found only in the mountains of Gansu Province in west-central China.

t: The long-tailed fiscal (Lanius cabanisi) is a species of bird in the shrike family Laniidae. The species is closely related to the more widespread grey-backed fiscal and is sometimes placed in a separate subgenus, Neolanius, with that species.
f: This conspicuous fiscal can often be seen in small groups perching in the open especially noticeable on telegraph poles and wires.

t: The southern fiscal or fiscal shrike (Lanius collaris) is a member of the shrike family found through most of southern Africa. It was previously lumped together with the northern fiscal (Lanius humeralis).
f: It is also sometimes named jackie hangman or butcher bird due to its habit of impaling its prey on acacia thorns to store the food for later consumption.

t: The red-backed shrike (Lanius collurio) is a carnivorous passerine bird and member of the shrike family, Laniidae. Its breeding range stretches from Western Europe east to central Russia.
f: It is migratory and winters in the eastern areas of tropical Africa and southern Africa.

t: The Burmese shrike (Lanius collurioides) is a species of bird in the family Laniidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Laos, Myanmar (Burma), Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The yellow-billed shrike (Corvinella corvina) is a large passerine bird in the shrike family. It is the only species placed in the genus Corvinella.
f: It is sometimes known as the long-tailed shrike, but this invites confusion with the long-tailed shrike, Lanius schach, of tropical southern Asia.

t: The brown shrike (Lanius cristatus) is a bird in the shrike family that is found mainly in Asia. It is closely related to the red-backed shrike (L. collurio) and isabelline shrike (L. isabellinus).
f: Like most other shrikes, it has a distinctive black "bandit-mask" through the eye and is found mainly in open scrub habitats, where it perches on the tops of thorny bushes in search of prey.

t: The great grey shrike (Lanius excubitor) is a large and predatory songbird species in the shrike family (Laniidae). It forms a superspecies with its parapatric southern relatives, the Iberian grey shrike (L. meridionalis), the Chinese grey shrike (L. sphenocerus) and the American loggerhead shrike (L. ludovicianus).
f: Most populations migrate south in winter to temperate regions.

t: The northern fiscal (Lanius humeralis) is a member of the shrike family found through most of Sub-Saharan Africa. Together they were called the common fiscal.
f: It used to be grouped with the southern fiscal (Lanius collaris).

t: The isabelline shrike or Daurian shrike (Lanius isabellinus) is a member of the shrike family (Laniidae). It is found in an extensive area between the Caspian Sea and north and central China southeast to the Qaidam Basin.
f: It was previously considered conspecific with the red-backed shrike and red-tailed shrike.

t: The loggerhead shrike (Lanius ludovicianus) is a passerine bird in the family Laniidae. It is the only member of the shrike family endemic to North America; the related northern shrike (L. borealis) occurs north of its range; however, it is also found in Siberia.
f: It is nicknamed the butcherbird after its carnivorous tendencies, as it consumes prey such as insects, amphibians, lizards, small mammals and small birds, and some prey end up displayed and stored at a site, for example in a tree.

t: The Iberian grey shrike (Lanius meridionalis) is a species of shrike endemic to southwestern Europe. It is closely related to the great grey shrike, Lanius excubitor, and its plumage is generally similar to it apart from the differences noted below.
f: The Iberian was previously considered conspecific with the great grey; where they co-occur, they do not interbreed and are separated by choice of habitat.

t: The lesser grey shrike (Lanius minor) is a passerine bird in the shrike family Laniidae. It breeds in South and Central Europe and western Asia and migrates to winter quarters in southern Africa in the early autumn, returning in spring.
f: Lesser grey shrikes frequently hover when hunting on their breeding grounds, but do not do so while moulting on non-breeding grounds.

t: The masked shrike (Lanius nubicus) is a species of bird in the shrike family, Laniidae. It breeds in southeastern Europe and at the eastern end of the Mediterranean, with a separate population in eastern Iraq and western Iran.
f: The species' calls are short and grating, but the song has melodic warbler-like components.

t: The red-tailed shrike or Turkestan shrike (Lanius phoenicuroides) is a member of the shrike family (Laniidae).
f: It was formerly considered conspecific with the isabelline shrike and the red-backed shrike.

t: The long-tailed shrike or rufous-backed shrike (Lanius schach) is a member of the bird family Laniidae, the shrikes. They are found widely distributed across Asia and there are variations in plumage across the range.
f: The species ranges across much of Asia, both on the mainland and the eastern archipelagos.

t: The woodchat shrike (Lanius senator) is a member of the shrike family Laniidae. It is mainly insectivorous and favours open wooded areas with scattered trees such as orchards, particularly when there is bare or sandy ground.
f: It can be identified by its red-brown crown and nape.

t: The Chinese grey shrike (Lanius sphenocercus) is a species of bird in the family Laniidae. Its natural habitat is temperate forests.
f: It is found in China, Japan, North Korea, South Korea, Mongolia, and the Russian Far East.
The grey-backed shrike (Lanius tephronotus) is a bird in the family Laniidae inhabiting South-east Asia.

t: The tiger shrike or thick-billed shrike (Lanius tigrinus) is a small passerine bird which belongs to the genus Lanius in the shrike family, Laniidae. It is found in wooded habitats across eastern Asia.
f: Its nest is built in a tree and three to six eggs are laid.
The bay-backed shrike (Lanius vittatus) is a member of the bird family Laniidae, the shrikes, resident in South Asia.

t: The Inca tern (Larosterna inca) is a near-threatened species of tern in the subfamily Sterninae of the family Laridae (the gulls, terns, and skimmers).
f: It is found along the Pacific coasts of Chile, Ecuador and Perú, and has appeared as a vagrant in Central America and Hawaii.

t: The European herring gull or simply herring gull (Larus argentatus) is a large gull, up to 66 cm (26 in) long. It breeds throughout the northern and western coasts of Europe.
f: They have a varied diet, including fish, crustaceans, as well as some plants, and are also scavengers, consuming carrion and food left by or stolen from humans.

t: Adults are white with gray back and wings, black wingtips with white spots, and pink legs. Immature birds are gray-brown and are darker and more uniform than European herring gulls, with a darker tail.
f: It usually nests near water, laying around three eggs in a scrape on the ground.

t: Belcher's gull (Larus belcheri), also known as the band-tailed gull, is a bird in the family Laridae found along the Pacific coast of South America. It formerly included the very similar Olrog's gull as a subspecies, but that bird occurs on the Atlantic coast of South America and is now accepted as a separate species Larus atlanticus.
f: Non-breeding adults have a brownish-black head and a white eye-ring.

t: The short-billed gull (Larus brachyrhynchus) is a species of gull that breeds in northwestern North America. Most authorities, including the American Ornithological Society in 2021, have split the two populations as distinct species.
f: In North America, it was previously known as the mew gull, when it was considered conspecific with the palearctic common gull (Larus canus).

t: The Caspian gull (Larus cachinnans) is a large gull and a member of the herring and lesser black-backed gull complex. The scientific name is from Latin.
