f: Larus appears to have referred to a gull or other large seabird, and cachinnans means 'laughing', from cachinnare 'to laugh'.

t: The California gull (Larus californicus) is a medium-sized gull, smaller on average than the herring gull, but larger on average than the ring-billed gull (though it may overlap in size with both).
f: Although named after California, it can be found annually across most of western North America, from the Canadian prairie provinces in the northeast and south through western Mexico.

t: The common gull (Larus canus) is a medium-sized gull that breeds in cool temperate regions of the Palearctic from Iceland and Scotland east to Kamchatka in the Russian Far East. The closely related short-billed gull was formerly often included in this species, which was then sometimes known collectively as "mew gull".
f: Most common gulls migrate further south in winter, reaching the Mediterranean Sea, the southern Caspian Sea, and the seas around China and Japan; northwest European populations are at least partly resident.
The black-tailed gull (Larus crassirostris) is a gull native to shorelines of East Asia.

t: The ring-billed gull (Larus delawarensis) is a medium-sized gull native to North America, breeding in Canada and the northern Contiguous United States, and wintering mainly in the United States and northern Mexico. The genus name is from Latin Larus which appears to have referred to a gull or other large seabird.
f: The specific delawarensis refers to the Delaware River.

t: The kelp gull (Larus dominicanus), also known as the Dominican gull, is a gull that breeds on coasts and islands through much of the Southern Hemisphere. The nominate L. d. dominicanus is the subspecies found around South America, parts of Australia (where it overlaps with the Pacific gull), and New Zealand .
f: The specific name comes from the Dominican Order of friars, who wear black and white habits.

t: The kelp gull (Larus dominicanus), also known as the Dominican gull, is a gull that breeds on coasts and islands through much of the Southern Hemisphere. The nominate L. d. dominicanus is the subspecies found around South America, parts of Australia (where it overlaps with the Pacific gull), and New Zealand .
f: The specific name comes from the Dominican Order of friars, who wear black and white habits.

t: The lesser black-backed gull (Larus fuscus) is a large gull that breeds on the Atlantic and Arctic coasts of Europe. However, it has increased dramatically in North America, especially along the east coast.
f: It is migratory, wintering from the British Isles south to West Africa.

t: The glaucous-winged gull (Larus glaucescens) is a large, white-headed gull. The genus name is from Latin Larus which appears to have referred to a gull or other large seabird.
f: The specific glaucescens is Neo-Latin for "glaucous" from the Ancient Greek, glaukos, denoting the grey color of its wings.

t: The Iceland gull (Larus glaucoides) is a medium-sized gull that breeds in the Arctic regions of Canada and Greenland, but not in Iceland (as its name suggests), where it is only seen during winter. The genus name is from Latin larus, which appears to have referred to a gull or other large seabird.
f: The specific name glaucoides denotes its resemblance to Larus glaucus, a synonym of Larus hyperboreus, the glaucous gull; -oides is Ancient Greek and means "resembling".

t: Heermann's gull (Larus heermanni) is a gull resident in the United States, Mexico and extreme southwestern British Columbia, nearly all nesting on Isla Rasa in the Gulf of California. They are usually found near shores or well out to sea, very rarely inland.
f: The species is named after Adolphus Lewis Heermann, nineteenth-century explorer and naturalist.

t: The glaucous gull (Larus hyperboreus) is a large gull, the second-largest gull in the world. The genus name is from Latin larus, which appears to have referred to a gull or other large seabird.
f: The specific name hyperboreus is Latin for "northern" from the Ancient Greek Huperboreoi people from the far north "Glaucous" is from Latin glaucus and denotes the grey colour of the gull.

t: The yellow-footed gull (Larus livens) is a large gull, closely related to the western gull and thought to be a subspecies until the 1960s.
f: It is endemic to the Gulf of California.

t: The great black-backed gull (Larus marinus) is the largest member of the gull and tern family Laridae. It is a very aggressive hunter, pirate and scavenger which breeds on the North Atlantic coasts and islands of northern Europe and northeastern North America.
f: Southern populations are generally sedentary, while those breeding in the far north (northern Norway, northwest Russia) migrate farther south in winter.

t: It was formerly treated as a subspecies of either the Caspian gull L. cachinnans, or more broadly as a subspecies of the herring gull L. argentatus. The genus name is from Latin Larus which appears to have referred to a gull or other large seabird, and the species name honours the German zoologist Karl Michahelles.
f: The yellow-legged gull or western yellow-legged gull (Larus michahellis) is a large gull found in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, which has only recently achieved wide recognition as a distinct species.

t: The western gull (Larus occidentalis) is a large white-headed gull that lives on the west coast of North America and the Pacific Ocean. It was previously considered conspecific with the yellow-footed gull (Larus livens) of the Gulf of California.
f: The western gull ranges from British Columbia, Canada, to Baja California, Mexico.

t: The slaty-backed gull (Larus schistisagus) is a large, white-headed gull that breeds on the north-eastern coast of the Palearctic, but travels widely during nonbreeding seasons. Another alternate name is Pacific gull, though it also applies to a Southern Hemisphere species, L. pacificus.
f: It is similar in appearance to the western gull and the glaucous-winged gull.

t: Thayer's gull (Larus glaucoides thayeri) is a subspecies of the Iceland gull.
f: It is a large gull native to North America.

t: The Japanese robin (Larvivora akahige) is a small passerine bird in the family Muscicapidae. This species was formerly named Erithacus akahige, or Komadori.
f: The name "Japanese robin" is also sometimes used for the red-billed leiothrix (Leiothrix lutea).

t: The Indian blue robin (Larvivora brunnea) is a small bird found in the Indian subcontinent. Formerly considered a thrush, it is now considered one of the Old World flycatchers in the family Muscicapidae.
f: It is migratory, breeding in the forests along the Himalayas of Nepal, India, Myanmar and Bangladesh.

t: The Siberian blue robin (Larvivora cyane) is a small passerine bird that was formerly classified as a member of the thrush family, Turdidae, but is now more generally considered to belong to the Old World flycatcher family, Muscicapidae. It and similar small European species are often called chats.
f: This bird is a migratory insectivorous species breeding in the eastern Palearctic from Siberia and northern Mongolia, northeastern China, Korea and across to Japan.

t: The Ryukyu robin (Larvivora komadori) is a bird endemic to the Ryūkyū Islands, of Japan. The Okinawa robin (Larvivora namiyei) previously was considered a subspecies.
f: The specific name komadori is, somewhat confusingly, the common name of its relative the Japanese robin in Japanese.

t: The rufous-tailed robin (Larvivora sibilans) is a small passerine bird. Its breeding range extends from southern Siberia and the Sea of Okhotsk to southern China and southeastern Asia.
f: It has a number of alternative English names: pseudorobin, red-tailed robin, Swinhoe's red-tailed robin, Swinhoe's robin, Swinhoe's pseudorobin, Swinhoe's nightingale or whistling nightingale.

t: The white-throated crake (Laterallus albigularis) is a species of bird in subfamily Rallinae of family Rallidae, the rails, gallinules, and coots.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, and Venezuela.

t: The grey-breasted crake (Laterallus exilis) is a species of bird in subfamily Rallinae of family Rallidae, the rails, gallinules, and coots.
f: It is found in Belize, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, Trinidad and Tobago, and every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The black rail (Laterallus jamaicensis) is a mouse-sized member of the rail family Rallidae that occurs in both North and South America.
f: It is the smallest rail present in North America and is known for its secretive nature.

t: The red-and-white crake (Rufirallus leucopyrrhus) is a species of bird in subfamily Rallinae of family Rallidae, the rails, gallinules, and coots. This species was formerly placed in the genus Laterallus.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
The rusty-flanked crake (Laterallus levraudi) is a Vulnerable species of bird in subfamily Rallinae of family Rallidae, the rails, gallinules, and coots.

t: The rufous-sided crake (Laterallus melanophaius) is a species of bird in subfamily Rallinae of family Rallidae, the rails, gallinules, and coots.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile.

t: The ruddy crake (Laterallus ruber) is a bird in the rail family, Rallidae.
f: Other names the ruddy crake is known by are "red rail", "ruddy rail" and "red crake".

t: The rufous-faced crake (Rufirallus xenopterus) is a species of bird in subfamily Rallinae of family Rallidae, the rails, gallinules, and coots. This species was formerly placed in the genus Laterallus.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The swift parrot (Lathamus discolor), also known by the palawa kani name swift waylitja, is a species of broad-tailed parrot, found only in southeastern Australia. The species breeds in Tasmania during the summer and migrates north to southeastern mainland Australia from Griffith-Warialda in New South Wales and west to Adelaide in the winter.
f: It is a nomadic migrant, and it settles in an area only when there is food available.

t: Euler's flycatcher (Lathrotriccus euleri) is a small passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers. It formerly was found on Grenada.
f: It is found on Trinidad and in every mainland South American country except Chile.

t: The grey-breasted flycatcher (Lathrotriccus griseipectus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: Some authorities consider it a subspecies of the rufous-vented grass babbler.
f: The swamp grass babbler or swamp prinia (Laticilla cinerascens) is a small bird of the Indian subcontinent.

t: The piratic flycatcher (Legatus leucophaius) is a passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers. It has also occurred several times as a vagrant in the southern United States.
f: It is found in Mexico, in every Central American country except El Salvador, in Trinidad and Tobago, and in every mainland South American country except Chile, though in Uruguay only as a vagrant.

t: The yellow-crowned woodpecker (Leiopicus mahrattensis) or Mahratta woodpecker is a species of small pied woodpecker found in the Indian subcontinent.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Leiopicus.

t: The rufous-backed sibia (Leioptila annectens) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found from the Himalayas to south-central Vietnam.
f: It was formerly placed in the genus Heterophasia but is now the only species in the genus Leioptila.
The orange-crowned warbler (Leiothlypis celata) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.

t: The Colima warbler (Leiothlypis crissalis) is a New World warbler. It is mainly found in the Sierra Madre Occidental and Oriental mountains of central Mexico, though its range just barely extends into adjacent southwestern Texas in the Chisos Mountains of Big Bend National Park.
f: They are mainly dark gray and brownish in coloration, with a pale underside.

t: Lucy's warbler (Leiothlypis luciae) is a small New World warbler found in North America. This species ranges includes southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico.
f: It is one of only two warblers to nest in cavities.

t: The Tennessee warbler (Leiothlypis peregrina) is a New World warbler that breeds in eastern North America and winters in southern Central America, the Caribbean, and northern South America.
f: The specific name peregrina is from Latin peregrinus "wanderer".

t: The Nashville warbler (Leiothlypis ruficapilla) is a small songbird in the New World warbler family, found in North and Central America. It has a gray head and a green back, and its underparts are yellow and white.
f: It breeds in parts of the northern and western United States and southern Canada, and migrates to winter in southern California and Texas, Mexico, and the north of Central America.

t: Virginia's warbler (Leiothlypis virginiae) is a species of New World warbler. The bird's common eastern range is central and southern mountains of Colorado, central Wyoming, and central and western New Mexico.
f: Despite what its name may suggest, Virginia's warbler is not actually named after the American State of Virginia, which makes sense as the birds' typical range only reaches as far east as the state of Texas.
The silver-eared mesia (Leiothrix argentauris) is a species of bird from South East Asia.

t: The red-billed leiothrix (Leiothrix lutea) is a member of the family Leiothrichidae, native to southern China and the Himalayas. Their backs are dull olive green, and they have a bright yellow-orange throat with a yellow chin; females are somewhat duller than males, and juveniles have black bills.
f: Adults have bright red bills and a yellowish-white ring around their eyes.

t: The Peruvian meadowlark (Leistes bellicosus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The long-tailed meadowlark (Leistes loyca) is a passerine bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in Argentina, Chile, and the Falkland Islands.

t: The red-breasted meadowlark (Leistes militaris) is a passerine bird in the New World family Icteridae.
f: It was formerly named red-breasted blackbird but is not closely related to the red-winged blackbird group.

t: The white-browed meadowlark (Leistes superciliaris) is a passerine bird in the New World family Icteridae. It was formerly named white-browed blackbird but is not closely related to the red-winged blackbird group.
f: In display the male flies up to 10 m in the air, then parachutes down on folded wings whilst singing an initially buzzing song, followed by a series of notes TZZZZZZ-teee-chu-chu-chak-chak.
The spot-crowned woodcreeper (Lepidocolaptes affinis), is a passerine bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae. it is found in Middle America from Mexico to Panama.

t: The Guianan woodcreeper (Lepidocolaptes albolineatus) or lineated woodcreeper is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The narrow-billed woodcreeper (Lepidocolaptes angustirostris) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Suriname, and Uruguay.

t: The Duida woodcreeper (Lepidocolaptes duidae) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Ecuador, Peru, Venezuela, and possibly Colombia.
The scalloped woodcreeper (Lepidocolaptes falcinellus) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The Inambari woodcreeper (Lepidocolaptes fatimalimae) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The dusky-capped woodcreeper (Lepidocolaptes fuscicapillus) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Brazil.

t: The montane woodcreeper (Lepidocolaptes lacrymiger) is a perching bird species in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
The white-striped woodcreeper (Lepidocolaptes leucogaster) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The streak-headed woodcreeper (Lepidocolaptes souleyetii) is a passerine bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Mexico, Central America, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Venezuela, and on Trinidad.
The scaled woodcreeper (Lepidocolaptes squamatus) is a species of bird in the subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The blue-capped manakin (Lepidothrix coronata) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae. The males have a brilliant blue cap; some have black, others have green body plumage, but the relationship between the subspecies is not well understood.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
The opal-crowned manakin (Lepidothrix iris) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Pipridae.

t: The blue-rumped manakin (Lepidothrix isidorei) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The snow-capped manakin (Lepidothrix nattereri) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Brazil.

t: The white-fronted manakin (Lepidothrix serena) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae, the manakins. It is native to French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname and northeastern Brazil where it inhabits subtropical and tropical moist lowland forest.
f: The male is mainly black, with a blue rump, yellow belly patches and a conspicuous patch of white feathers extending forwards from its forehead.

t: The orange-bellied manakin (Lepidothrix suavissima), also known as the tepui manakin, is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Guyana, and Venezuela.

t: The plain-mantled tit-spinetail (Leptasthenura aegithaloides) is a small passerine bird of South America in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.

t: The Andean tit-spinetail (Leptasthenura andicola) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The brown-capped tit-spinetail (Leptasthenura fuliginiceps) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Bolivia.
The rusty-crowned tit-spinetail (Leptasthenura pileata) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The tufted tit-spinetail (Leptasthenura platensis) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, and possibly Paraguay.

t: The Araucaria tit-spinetail (Leptasthenura setaria) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Brazil.
The streak-backed tit-spinetail, or streaked tit-spinetail, (Leptasthenura striata) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
The striolated tit-spinetail (Leptasthenura striolata) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
The white-browed tit-spinetail (Leptasthenura xenothorax) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The black sunbird (Leptocoma aspasia) is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest.
f: It is found in eastern Indonesia and New Guinea.

t: Van Hasselt's sunbird (Leptocoma brasiliana), is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.
f: It is found in Northeast India, Bangladesh and Southeast Asia.

t: The copper-throated sunbird (Leptocoma calcostetha) is a small passerine within the Nectariniidae family. As a member of the Nectariniidae family, they possess downward curved beaks and have pectoral tufts of yellow feathers.
f: They sustain themselves by consuming nectar as well as small invertebrates.

t: The crimson-backed sunbird or small sunbird (Leptocoma minima) is a sunbird endemic to the Western Ghats of India. They are tiny birds that are resident and are found in forests but are particularly attracted to gardens at the edge of the forest where people grow suitable flower-bearing plants.
f: Like other sunbirds, they feed mainly on nectar although they take insects, especially to feed their young.

t: The purple-throated sunbird (Leptocoma sperata), is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. Its natural habitats are lowland tropical forests and tropical mangrove forests of Maratua and the Philippines.
f: The Van Hasselt's sunbird was previously considered conspecific.

t: The purple-rumped sunbird (Leptocoma zeylonica) is a sunbird endemic to the Indian Subcontinent. Like other sunbirds, they are small in size, feeding mainly on nectar but sometimes take insects, particularly when feeding young.
f: They can hover for short durations but usually perch to lap nectar from flowers.

t: The gray-headed kite (Leptodon cayanensis) is a raptor found in open woodland and swamp forests. It shares the genus Leptodon with the extremely rare white-collared kite.
f: It breeds from eastern Mexico and Trinidad south to Peru, Bolivia, Brazil and northern Argentina.

t: The white-browed tit-warbler (Leptopoecile sophiae) is a species of bird in the family Aegithalidae. The species was first described by Nikolai Severtzov in 1873.
f: It is resident in the Tian Shan and central China as well as in the Himalayas where it is mainly found in winter.

t: The sepia-capped flycatcher (Leptopogon amaurocephalus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country except El Salvador, and every mainland South American country except Chile; it is known in Uruguay as a vagrant.

t: The rufous-breasted flycatcher (Leptopogon rufipectus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela.

t: The slaty-capped flycatcher (Leptopogon superciliaris) is a small passerine bird in the tyrant flycatcher family.
f: It is found from Costa Rica south to Bolivia and east to Venezuela and Trinidad.
The Inca flycatcher (Leptopogon taczanowskii) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.

t: The marabou stork (Leptoptilos crumenifer) is a large wading bird in the stork family Ciconiidae native to sub-Saharan Africa. It breeds in both wet and arid habitats, often near human habitation, especially landfill sites.
f: It has often been credited with the largest wingspan of any land bird, with an average of 2.6 metres (8.5 ft) and some recorded examples of up to 3.2 metres (10 ft).

t: The golden-plumed parakeet (Leptosittaca branickii) is a Neotropical parrot species within the family Psittacidae, belonging to the monotypic genus Leptosittaca. This somewhat Aratinga-like species is found in humid temperate highland forests, especially with Podocarpus, on the east Andean slope in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
f: It is the only known parakeet species that can detect ultraviolet radiation.

t: The cuckoo-roller or courol (Leptosomus discolor) is the only bird in the family Leptosomidae , which was previously often placed in the order Coraciiformes but is now placed in its own order Leptosomiformes. Despite its name, the cuckoo-roller does not share close evolutionary origins with cuckoos or rollers, although for long it was counted among the closer relatives of the latter.
f: The cuckoo-roller is at the root of a group that contains the Trogoniformes, Bucerotiformes, Piciformes, and Coraciiformes.

t: The grey-chested dove (Leptotila cassinii) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Belize, Colombia, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, and Panama.
The Tolima dove (Leptotila conoveri) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.

t: The Caribbean dove (Leptotila jamaicensis) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. It is found in Belize, the Cayman Islands, Colombia (San Andrés island), Honduras (Bay Islands), Jamaica, and Mexico (Yucatán Peninsula).
f: It has been introduced to the Bahamas.

t: The Yungas dove (Leptotila megalura), also known as the white-faced dove or large-tailed dove, is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Bolivia.

t: The ochre-bellied dove or buff-bellied dove (Leptotila ochraceiventris) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The pallid dove (Leptotila pallida) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The grey-headed dove (Leptotila plumbeiceps) is a large New World dove.
f: It is found from eastern Mexico to Colombia.

t: The grey-fronted dove (Leptotila rufaxilla) is a large New World tropical dove.
f: It is found on Trinidad and in every mainland South American country except Chile.

t: The white-tipped dove (Leptotila verreauxi) is a large New World tropical dove.
f: Its scientific name commemorates the French naturalists Jules and Edouard Verreaux.

t: The green-tailed trainbearer (Lesbia nuna) is a species of hummingbird in the "coquettes", tribe Lesbiini of subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and possibly Venezuela.

t: The black-tailed trainbearer (Lesbia victoriae) is a species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forest, subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found between 2500 and 3800m in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The buffy hummingbird (Leucippus fallax) is a species of bird in the hummingbird family Trochilidae. This bird lives in dry forest and scrubland in northern South America where it feeds on insects and the nectar, flesh, and juice of cactus fruits.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Leucippus.

t: The white-throated hummingbird (Leucochloris albicollis) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The Siberian crane (Leucogeranus leucogeranus), also known as the Siberian white crane or the snow crane, is a bird of the family Gruidae, the cranes. They are distinctive among the cranes: adults are nearly all snowy white, except for their black primary feathers that are visible in flight, and with two breeding populations in the Arctic tundra of western and eastern Russia.
f: Among the cranes, they make the longest distance migrations.

t: The violet-crowned hummingbird (Ramosomyia violiceps) is a hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Mexico and the southwestern United States.

t: The laughing gull (Leucophaeus atricilla) is a medium-sized gull of North and South America. It breeds in large colonies mostly along the Atlantic coast of North America, the Caribbean, and northern South America.
f: Named from its laugh-like call, it is an opportunistic omnivore and scavenger.

t: The grey gull, also known as garuma gull (Leucophaeus modestus), is a medium-sized gull native to South America.
f: Unusual among gulls, it breeds inland in the extremely dry Atacama Desert in northern Chile, although it is present as a non-breeding bird along much of the Pacific coast of South America.

t: Franklin's gull (Leucophaeus pipixcan) is a small (length 12.6–14.2 in, 32–36 cm) gull. The genus name Leucophaeus is from Ancient Greek leukos, "white", and phaios, "dusky".
f: The specific pipixcan is a Nahuatl name for a type of gull.

t: The dolphin gull (Leucophaeus scoresbii), sometimes erroneously called the red-billed gull (a somewhat similar but unrelated species from New Zealand), is a gull native to southern Chile and Argentina, and the Falkland Islands. It is a coastal bird inhabiting rocky, muddy and sandy shores and is often found around seabird colonies.
f: Dolphin gulls have a varied diet, eating many things ranging from mussels to carrion.

t: The white-browed hawk (Leucopternis kuhli) is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Accipitrinae, the "true" hawks, of family Accipitridae.
f: It is found Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The black-faced hawk (Leucopternis melanops) is a species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. It is closely related to the white-browed hawk and individuals showing a level of intermediacy between the two species are known, suggesting that they rarely hybridize
f: This low-density species has traditionally been believed to be restricted to Amazon Basin north of the Amazon River, but there are several records south of this river, in, for example, the Brazilian states of Pará and Acre, and southeastern Peru.

t: The semiplumbeous hawk (Leucopternis semiplumbeus) is a species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, and Panama.
The wonga pigeon or wonga wonga (Leucosarcia melanoleuca) is a pigeon that inhabits areas in eastern Australia with its range being from Central Queensland to Gippsland, eastern Victoria, Australia.

t: The black rosy finch or black rosy-finch (Leucosticte atrata) is a species of passerine bird in the family Fringillidae native to alpine areas above treeline, of the western United States.
f: It is the most range-restricted member of its genus, and a popular photography subject for birdwatchers.

t: The brown-capped rosy finch (Leucosticte australis) is a medium-sized finch endemic to North America in the middle of the Rocky Mountains. Adults are brown on the head, back, and breast.
f: These birds can be found in alpine snowfields and also at feeders, especially in the winter.

t: The gray-crowned rosy finch or gray-crowned rosy-finch (Leucosticte tephrocotis) is a species of passerine bird in the family Fringillidae native to Alaska, western Canada, and the north-western United States. There are currently six recognized subspecies.
f: Due to its remote and rocky alpine habitat it is rarely seen.
Lewin's rail (Lewinia pectoralis) is a species of bird in the family Rallidae.
The slaty-breasted rail (Lewinia striata) is a rail species native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.

t: The purple-gaped honeyeater (Lichenostomus cratitius) is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae.
f: It is endemic to semi-arid southern Australia, where it inhabits mallee, tall heath and associated low eucalypt woodland.

t: A predominantly black and yellow honeyeater, it is split into four subspecies.
f: The yellow-tufted honeyeater (Lichenostomus melanops) is a passerine bird found in the south-east ranges of Australia.

t: The grey-eared honeyeater (Lichmera incana), also known as the dark-brown honeyeater, is a passerine bird of the honeyeater family which is found in Vanuatu and New Caledonia in the south-west Pacific.
f: It is sometimes known as the silver-eared honeyeater, but this name is also used for the silver-eared honeyeater (Lichmera alboauricularis) of New Guinea.

t: The brown honeyeater (Lichmera indistincta) is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. It is a medium-small brownish bird, with yellow-olive panels in the tail and wing, and a yellow tuft behind the eye.
f: It belongs to the honeyeaters, a group of birds which have highly developed brush-tipped tongues adapted for nectar feeding.

t: The scaly-breasted honeyeater (Lichmera squamata), also known as the white-tufted honeyeater, is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.
f: It is endemic to Indonesia, where it occurs in the southern Moluccas.
The straight-billed reedhaunter (Limnoctites rectirostris) is a South American bird species in the family Furnariidae.

t: The sulphur-bearded reedhaunter or sulphur-throated spinetail (Limnoctites sulphuriferus) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay.

t: The short-billed dowitcher (Limnodromus griseus), like its congener, the long-billed dowitcher, is a medium-sized, stocky, long-billed shorebird in the family Scolopacidae. It is an inhabitant of North America, Central America, the Caribbean, and northern South America.
f: Only a small percentage can be identified by this character alone.

t: The long-billed dowitcher (Limnodromus scolopaceus) is a medium-sized shorebird with a relatively long bill belonging to the sandpiper family, Scolopacidae. In breeding plumage, adults are characterized by a rufous head and underparts with a darker mottled back and a large white upper rump only seen in flight.
f: They feed in various freshwater habitats with their bill underwater in a "sewing machine" motion and have a mating display where males chase females in flight.
The Asian dowitcher (Limnodromus semipalmatus) is a medium-large wader in the Scolopacidae family of sandpipers.

t: The curve-billed reedhaunter (Limnornis curvirostris) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay.

t: Swainson's warbler (Limnothlypis swainsonii) is a small species of New World warbler. It is monotypic, the only member of the genus Limnothlypis.
f: Swainson's warbler was named after William Swainson, an English ornithologist.

t: The marbled godwit (Limosa fedoa) is a large migratory shorebird in the family Scolopacidae.
f: On average, it is the largest of the four species of godwit.

t: The Hudsonian godwit (Limosa haemastica) is a large shorebird in the sandpiper family, Scolopacidae. Since then, the Hudsonian godwit has become the target of conservation attention due to its fragmented and localized distribution and small population, as well as an important scientific system for migration biology research.
f: It is an extreme long-distance migrant, breeding at remote sites in Subarctic North America and flying nonstop in the fall to wintering sites in southern South America.

t: The bar-tailed godwit (Limosa lapponica) is a large and strongly migratory wader in the family Scolopacidae, which feeds on bristle-worms and shellfish on coastal mudflats and estuaries. It has distinctive red breeding plumage, long legs, and a long upturned bill.
f: The migration of the subspecies Limosa lapponica baueri across the Pacific Ocean from Alaska to New Zealand is the longest known non-stop flight of any bird, and also the longest journey without pausing to feed by any animal.

t: The black-tailed godwit (Limosa limosa) is a large, long-legged, long-billed shorebird first described by Carl Linnaeus in 1758. It is a member of the godwit genus, Limosa.
f: Black-tailed godwits spend (the northern hemisphere) winter in areas as diverse as the Indian subcontinent, Australia, New Zealand, western Europe and west Africa.

t: The common linnet or Eurasian linnet (Linaria cannabina) is a small passerine bird of the finch family, Fringillidae.
f: It derives its common name and the scientific name, Linaria, from its fondness for hemp seeds and flax seeds—flax being the English name of the plant from which linen is made.

t: The twite (Linaria flavirostris) is a small brown passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is a partially migratory species that is found in a strongly disjunct distribution in northern Europe, and in Asian mountains from eastern Turkey to Nepal, western China and Mongolia.
f: It mainly feeds on small seeds but occasionally also feeds on insects.

t: The Yemen linnet (Linaria yemenensis) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.
f: It is native to the Southwestern Arabian foothills savanna (Saudi Arabia and Yemen).
The red-faced liocichla (Liocichla phoenicea) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.

t: The scarlet-faced liocichla (Liocichla ripponi) is a bird in the family Leiothrichidae. The species was recently reclassified as separate from the red-faced liocichla, although some taxonomists consider it to be conspecific.
f: It is found in Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, and southern China.

t: The Taiwan liocichla (Liocichla steerii), also known as Steere's liocichla, is a small passerine bird in the laughingthrush family Leiothrichidae.
f: The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1877.

t: Its natural habitats are temperate forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: The golden-breasted fulvetta (Lioparus chrysotis) is a species of songbird found in Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal, and Vietnam.

t: The rusty-belted tapaculo (Liosceles thoracicus) is a species of suboscine passerine bird in the tapaculo family Rhinocryptidae. It is found in Brazil, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Liosceles.
The black-and-gold cotinga (Lipaugus ater) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae.

t: The dusky piha (Lipaugus fuscocinereus) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
The cinnamon-vented piha (Lipaugus lanioides) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.

t: The rufous piha (Lipaugus unirufus) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.
f: Its range extends from southern Mexico throughout Central America and the Chocó-Magdalena region.

t: The screaming piha (Lipaugus vociferans) is a species of passerine bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except for these four countries: Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The chestnut-capped piha (Lipaugus weberi) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae. It is endemic to a small portion of Colombia's central Andes in the department of Antioquia.
f: The chestnut-capped piha resides only in a narrow band of humid premontane cloud forest.

t: The American bullfrog (Lithobates catesbeianus), often simply known as the bullfrog in Canada and the United States, is a species of large frog in the family Ranidae (true frogs). The species is native to eastern North America.
f: The bullfrog gets its common name from the sound the male makes during the breeding season, which sounds similar to a bull bellowing.

t: Lithobates clamitans or Rana clamitans, commonly known as the green frog, is a species of frog native to eastern North America. The two subspecies are the bronze frog and the northern green frog.
f: These frogs display significant acts of territoriality, with males being the primary actors.
The pickerel frog (Lithobates palustris, formerly Rana palustris) is a North American frog, characterized by the appearance of seemingly "hand-drawn" squares on its dorsal surface.

t: The wood frog has garnered attention from biologists because of its freeze tolerance, relatively great degree of terrestrialism (for a ranid), interesting habitat associations (peat bogs, vernal pools, uplands), and relatively long-range movements. The wood frog has been proposed to be the official state amphibian of New York.
f: It is the only North American frog that occurs north of the Arctic Circle.

t: The sharp-tailed streamcreeper (Lochmias nematura) is a passerine bird of South America in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae. It is found in Panama and every mainland South American country except Chile, French Guiana, and Suriname.
f: Alternate names include streamside Lochmias, sharp-tailed creeper, and simply streamcreeper.

t: The Taiwan bush warbler (Locustella alishanensis) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Locustellidae. Its natural habitat is undergrowth and grassland 1,200–3,000 m (3,900–9,800 ft) in elevation.
f: It was first recorded in 1917 and named as a distinct species in 2000.

t: The long-tailed bush warbler (Locustella caudata) also known as the Long-tailed grasshopper-warbler is a species of grass warbler (family Locustellidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
f: It is found only in the Philippines on the islands of Mindanao and Luzon.

t: The Baikal bush warbler (Locustella davidi), also known as Baikal grasshopper-warbler or David's bush warbler, is a migratory species of Old World warbler in the family Locustellidae. It winters from southern China south to northern Thailand.
f: It breeds from the southern part of the Russian Far East (including the Lake Baikal region) to northeast China (southern Heilongjiang south to southern Hebei) and North Korea.

t: The river warbler (Locustella fluviatilis) is an Old World warbler in the genus Locustella.
f: It breeds in eastern and central Europe and is migratory, wintering in inland southern Africa, from around the Zambezi River south to the vicinity of Pretoria in South Africa.

t: The lanceolated warbler (Locustella lanceolata) is a species of Old World warbler in the genus Locustella. It breeds from northwest European Russia across the Palearctic to northern Hokkaidō, Japan.
f: This is a skulking species which is very difficult to see except sometimes when singing.

t: Savi's warbler (Locustella luscinioides) is a species of Old World warbler in the genus Locustella. It breeds in Europe and the western Palearctic.
f: This is not a shy species, but can be difficult to see in the reeds except sometimes when singing.

t: Formerly placed in the "Old World warbler" assemblage as Bradypterus luteoventrus, it is now placed in the newly recognized family Locustellidae. It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, Hong Kong, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, and Vietnam.
f: The brown bush warbler (Locustella luteoventris) is a songbird species.

t: Formerly placed in the "Old World warbler" assemblage, it is now placed in the newly recognized family Locustellidae. B. mandelli was until recently considered a subspecies of B. seebohmi, and the name "russet bush warbler" was applied to the entire species complex.
f: The russet bush warbler (Locustella mandelli) is a songbird species.

t: Formerly placed in the "Old World warbler" assemblage, it is now placed in the newly recognized family Locustellidae. It is found in the mountains of eastern Java, Bali, Timor and Alor Island.
f: The Javan bush warbler (Locustella montis) is a songbird species.

t: The common grasshopper warbler or just grasshopper warbler (Locustella naevia) is a species of Old World warbler in the genus Locustella. It breeds across much of temperate Europe and the western Palearctic.
f: This is a species which skulks in the undergrowth, creeping through bushes and low foliage, and which is very difficult to see except when singing from a prominent position.

t: The Chinese bush warbler (Locustella tacsanowskia) is an Old World warbler in the family Locustellidae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1871.
f: It breeds in the East Palearctic (East Siberia to Tibet and South China); it winters to Northeast India, Yunnan and Southeast Asia.

t: The spotted bush warbler (Locustella thoracica) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Locustellidae. Its natural habitat is arboreal forests.
f: It is found in the northern Himalayas, Yunnan and central China, in the countries of Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar and Nepal.

t: The chestnut munia or black-headed munia (Lonchura atricapilla) is a small passerine. It was formerly considered conspecific with the closely related tricoloured munia, but is now widely accepted as a separate species.
f: Before 1995, it was the national bird of the Philippines, where it is known in Tagalog as mayang pula ("red maya") because of the brick red patch on the lower back which is visible only when it flies.

t: The chestnut-breasted mannikin (Lonchura castaneothorax), also known as the chestnut-breasted munia or bully bird (in Australia), is a small brown-backed munia with a black face and greyish crown and nape. It has a broad ferruginous breast bar above a white belly.
f: It has also been introduced to French Polynesia and New Caledonia.

t: The black-throated munia or Jerdon's mannikin (Lonchura kelaarti) is a small passerine bird.
f: This estrildid finch is a resident breeding bird in the hills of southwest India, the Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats and Sri Lanka.

t: The Javan munia (Lonchura leucogastroides) is a species of estrildid finch native to southern Sumatra, Java, Bali and Lombok islands in Indonesia. It was introduced in Singapore and the Malay Peninsula; It inhabits subtropical and tropical dry shrubland and grassland habitat.
f: The Javan munia is known to feed on algae.

t: The white-headed munia (Lonchura maja) is a small passerine bird belonging to the estrildid finch family.
f: This species is often confused with, and referred to as, the Pale-headed munia (Lonchura pallida) which can be differentiated by tan coloured flanks which are lighter than the brown wings and also by the absence of the black belly.

t: The tricoloured munia (Lonchura malacca) is an estrildid finch, native to Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, and southern China. The species has also been introduced to the Caribbean, in Trinidad, Jamaica, Hispaniola, Puerto Rico, Cuba, and Venezuela.
f: Immature birds have pale brown upperparts, lack the dark head found in adults, and have uniform buff underparts that can be confused with immatures of other munias such as the scaly-breasted munia.

t: The Java sparrow (Padda oryzivora; syn. Lonchura oryzivora), also known as the Java finch, Java rice sparrow or Java rice bird, is a small passerine bird.
f: It is a popular cage bird, and has been introduced into many other countries.

t: The scaly-breasted munia or spotted munia (Lonchura punctulata), known in the pet trade as nutmeg mannikin or spice finch, is a sparrow-sized estrildid finch native to tropical Asia. A species of the genus Lonchura, it was formally described and named by Carl Linnaeus in 1758.
f: They forage in flocks and communicate with soft calls and whistles.

t: The white-rumped munia (Lonchura striata) or white-rumped mannikin, sometimes called striated finch in aviculture, is a small passerine bird from the family of waxbill "finches" (Estrildidae). It is native to tropical continental Asia and some adjacent islands, and has been naturalized in some parts of Japan.
f: These are not close relatives of the true finches (Fringillidae) or true sparrows (Passeridae).

t: The long-crested eagle (Lophaetus occipitalis) is an African bird of prey characterised by its shaggy crest of feathers. In the family Accipitridae which includes all the eagles, it is currently placed in a monotypic genus Lophaetus.
f: Breeding may occur at any time of year, depending on food availability; it lays 1 or 2 eggs as is usual for raptors.
The crowned hornbill (Lophoceros alboterminatus) is an African hornbill.

t: The red-billed dwarf hornbill (Lophoceros camurus) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae.
f: It is distributed across the African tropical rainforest.

t: The Congo pied hornbill (Lophoceros fasciatus) is a bird of the hornbill family, a family of tropical birds found in the Old World. The Congo pied hornbill is native to the Congo Basin.

f: It is endemic to northeastern Australia.

t: The purple-backed fairywren (Malurus assimilis) is a fairywren that is native to Australia. Described by Alfred John North in 1901, it has four recognised subspecies.
f: Distributed over much of the Australian continent, the purple-backed fairywren is found in scrubland with plenty of vegetation providing dense cover.

t: The superb fairywren (Malurus cyaneus) is a passerine bird in the Australasian wren family, Maluridae, and is common and familiar across south-eastern Australia. It is a sedentary and territorial species, also exhibiting a high degree of sexual dimorphism; the male in breeding plumage has a striking bright blue forehead, ear coverts, mantle, and tail, with a black mask and black or dark blue throat.
f: Male wrens pluck yellow petals and display them to females as part of a courtship display.

t: The emperor fairywren (Malurus cyanocephalus) is a species of bird in the Australasian wren family, Maluridae. It is found in New Guinea in its natural habitat of subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is the largest species of fairywren.

t: The red-winged fairywren (Malurus elegans) is a species of passerine bird in the Australasian wren family, Maluridae. It is non-migratory and endemic to the southwestern corner of Western Australia.
f: Singing is used to advertise territory, and birds can distinguish other individuals by song alone.

t: The variegated fairywren (Malurus lamberti) is a fairywren that lives in eastern Australia. Like other fairywrens, the variegated fairywren is a cooperative breeding species, with small groups of birds maintaining and defending small territories year-round.
f: Male wrens pluck yellow petals and display them to females as part of a courtship display.

t: The white-winged fairywren (Malurus leucopterus) is a species of passerine bird in the Australasian wren family, Maluridae. It lives in the drier parts of Central Australia; from central Queensland and South Australia across to Western Australia.
f: As part of a courtship display, the male wren plucks petals from flowers and displays them to female birds.

t: The red-backed fairywren (Malurus melanocephalus) is a species of passerine bird in the Australasian wren family, Maluridae. It is endemic to Australia and can be found near rivers and coastal areas along the northern and eastern coastlines from the Kimberley in the northwest to the Hunter Region in New South Wales.
f: As part of a courtship display, the male wren plucks red petals from flowers and displays them to females.

t: The splendid fairywren (Malurus splendens) is a passerine bird in the Australasian wren family, Maluridae. It is also known simply as the splendid wren or more colloquially in Western Australia as the blue wren.
f: Male fairywrens pluck pink or purple petals and display them to females as part of a courtship display.

t: The orange-collared manakin (Manacus aurantiacus) is a passerine bird in the manakin family. It is an endemic resident breeder in Costa Rica and western Panama, where it is found in forests, secondary growth and plantations.
f: At breeding time, males are involved in lekking behaviour on the forest floor.

t: The white-collared manakin (Manacus candei) is a passerine bird in the manakin family. It is a resident breeder in the tropical New World from southeastern Mexico to Costa Rica and the extreme west of Panama.
f: Females and juveniles are olive-green with yellow bellies and resemble female orange-collared manakins.

t: The white-bearded manakin (Manacus manacus) is a small passerine bird which breeds in tropical South America. This manakin is found in forests, secondary growth and plantations.
f: It can be found in Colombia, Venezuela and Trinidad south to Bolivia and northern Argentina.

t: The golden-collared manakin (Manacus vitellinus) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Panama.

t: The yellow-throated miner (Manorina flavigula) is a species of colonial honeyeater, endemic to Australia. It is also known as the white-rumped miner.
f: Yellow-throated miners feed on invertebrates, nectar, pollen, lerps, and seeds.

t: The noisy miner (Manorina melanocephala) is a bird in the honeyeater family, Meliphagidae, and is endemic to eastern and southeastern Australia. This miner is a grey bird, with a black head, orange-yellow beak and feet, a distinctive yellow patch behind the eye, and white tips on the tail feathers.
f: Group cohesion is facilitated not only by vocalisations, but also through ritualised displays, which have been categorised as flight displays, postural displays, and facial displays.

t: The bell miner or bellbird (Manorina melanophrys) is a colonial honeyeater, endemic to southeastern Australia. The common name refers to their bell-like call. "Miner" is an old alternative spelling of "myna", and is shared with other members of the genus Manorina.
f: The heritage listed mountain village of Bellbrook was named after the distinctive sound of local bellbirds in 1882.

t: The American wigeon (Mareca americana), also known as the baldpate, is a species of dabbling duck found in North America. Formerly assigned to Anas, this species is classified with the other wigeons in the dabbling duck genus Mareca.
f: It is the New World counterpart of the Eurasian wigeon.
The falcated duck or falcated teal (Mareca falcata) is a gadwall-sized dabbling duck from the east Palearctic .

t: The Eurasian wigeon or European wigeon (Mareca penelope), also known as the widgeon or wigeon, is one of three extant species of wigeon in the dabbling duck genus Mareca.
f: It is common and widespread within its Palearctic range.

t: The Chiloé wigeon (Mareca sibilatrix), also known as the southern wigeon, is one of three extant species of wigeon in the genus Mareca of the dabbling duck subfamily. In its native range, it is called the pato overo ("piebald duck") or pato real ("royal duck"), although the latter name also refers to the Muscovy in the wild.
f: This bird is indigenous to the southern part of South America, including the Chiloé Archipelago, from which it gets its name.
The gadwall (Mareca strepera) is a common and widespread dabbling duck in the family Anatidae.

t: It is found on many Caribbean islands, from the Bahamas in the north to the Grenadines in the south, with an isolated subspecies on Bonaire.
f: The pearly-eyed thrasher (Margarops fuscatus) is a bird in the thrasher family Mimidae.

t: The ruddy treerunner (Margarornis rubiginosus) is a passerine bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The pearled treerunner (Margarornis squamiger) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Venezuela, and possibly Argentina.

t: The golden-winged manakin (Masius chrysopterus) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The white-bellied spinetail (Mazaria propinqua) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, and Peru.

t: The buff-banded tyrannulet (Mecocerculus hellmayri) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, and Peru.

t: The white-throated tyrannulet (Mecocerculus leucophrys) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The sulphur-bellied tyrannulet (Mecocerculus minor) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The white-tailed tyrannulet (Mecocerculus poecilocercus) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The white-banded tyrannulet (Mecocerculus stictopterus) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
The belted kingfisher (Megaceryle alcyon) is a large, conspicuous water kingfisher, native to North America.

t: It is part of the kingfisher genus Megaceryle with three other species: the giant kingfisher (Megaceryle maxima), the ringed kingfisher (Megaceryle torquata), and the belted kingfisher (Megaceryle alcyon) with which it forms a species complex.
f: The crested kingfisher (Megaceryle lugubris) is a very large kingfisher that is native to parts of southern Asia.

The giant kingfisher (Megaceryle maxima) is the largest kingfisher in Africa, where it is a resident breeding bird over most of the continent south of the Sahara Desert, other than the arid southwest.

The ringed kingfisher (Megaceryle torquata) is a large, conspicuous, and noisy kingfisher bird commonly found along the lower Rio Grande Valley in southeasternmost Texas in the United States through Central America to Tierra del Fuego in South America.

t: The yellow-eyed penguin (Megadyptes antipodes), known also as hoiho, is a species of penguin endemic to New Zealand. Previously thought closely related to the little penguin (Eudyptula minor), molecular research has shown it more closely related to penguins of the genus Eudyptes.
f: It is the sole extant species in the genus Megadyptes, from Ancient Greek μέγας (mégas), meaning "large", and δύπτης (dúptes), meaning "diver".

t: The striated grassbird (Megalurus palustris) is an "Old World warbler" species in the family Locustellidae. It was formerly placed in the family Sylviidae.
f: Noisy and conspicuous, often sitting and calling exposed on tops of grasses, bushes and telephone wires.

t: The Philippine megapode (Megapodius cumingii), also known as the Philippine scrubfowl or the Tabon scrubfowl, is a species of bird in the family Megapodiidae. It is found in the Philippines, northeastern Borneo, and Sulawesi.
f: The species was named after the collector Hugh Cuming.

t: The Melanesian scrubfowl or Melanesian megapode (Megapodius eremita) is a megapode species that is endemic to islands within Melanesia. This bird species is culturally important for Indigenous peoples in Melanesia.
f: The Melanesian scrubfowl has a unique strategy of egg incubation in which it relies on environmental heat sources.

t: The male and female are similar. This terrestrial species lives in forests and swamps, including mangroves, of the Maluku and Raja Ampat Islands in Indonesia.
f: Like other megapodes, it lays its eggs in a mound made from earth mixed with leaves, sand, gravel, and sticks, which can be as large as 11 m (36 ft) in diameter and stand nearly 5 m (16 ft) tall.

t: The boat-billed flycatcher (Megarynchus pitangua) is a large member of the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Mexico, in every Central American country, on Trinidad, and in every mainland South American country though only as a vagrant in Chile.
The white-throated screech owl (Megascops albogularis) is a small owl found in the Andes of Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela.

t: The eastern screech owl (Megascops asio) or eastern screech-owl is a stocky, short-tailed owl that is relatively common in Eastern North America, from Mexico to Canada. Although it often lives in close proximity to humans, the eastern screech owl frequently avoids detection due to its strictly nocturnal habits.
f: Mid-sized for a screech owl, the species resides in most types of woodland habitats across its range and is relatively adaptable to urban and developed areas compared to other owls.

t: The black-capped screech owl (Megascops atricapilla), or variable screech owl, is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The Chocó screech owl (Megascops centralis) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found from central Panama to western Ecuador.

t: The tropical screech owl (Megascops choliba) is a small species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, Trinidad, and every mainland South American country.

t: The bare-shanked screech owl (Megascops clarkii) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae. It is a large owl that feeds at night in forests and lives in a family size group, even during breeding season.
f: The owl's range is only in Costa Rica, Panama, and far northwestern Colombia.

t: The Pacific screech owl (Megascops cooperi) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae. It is found in Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.
f: The Pacific screech owl has sometimes been treated as a race of western screech owl (Megascops kennicottii) or eastern screech owl (M. asio) but its vocalizations are distinct from theirs.

t: The Santa Marta screech owl (Megascops gilesi) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found only in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta of Colombia.

t: The Middle American screech owl (Megascops guatemalae), also known as the Guatemalan screech owl or the vermiculated screech owl, is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found from northern Mexico to western Panama.

t: The Yungas screech owl (Megascops hoyi), also known as montane forest screech-owl and Hoy's screech owl, is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Bolivia.

t: The rufescent screech owl (Megascops ingens) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The western screech owl (Megascops kennicottii) is a small owl native to North and Central America, closely related to the eastern screech owl.
f: The scientific name commemorates the American naturalist Robert Kennicott and roughly translates to "Kennicott's great/large owl".
Koepcke's screech owl (Megascops koepckeae) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.

t: The cinnamon screech owl (Megascops petersoni) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in the Andes of Ecuador and Peru and possibly Colombia.

t: The West Peruvian screech owl or Peruvian screech owl (Megascops roboratus) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The foothill screech owl (Megascops roraimae) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The long-tufted screech owl (Megascops sanctaecatarinae) is a species of "typical owl" in the subfamily Striginae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay.
The Balsas screech owl (Megascops seductus) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
The whiskered screech owl (Megascops trichopsis) is a small screech owl found in North and Central America.

t: The tawny-bellied screech owl (Megascops watsonii) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The pearly antshrike (Megastictus margaritatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The great xenops (Megaxenops parnaguae) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is endemic to eastern Brazil.

t: The zebra woodpecker (Meiglyptes tristis) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: The specific epithet tristis is Latin for "sad" or "gloomy".
The buff-necked woodpecker (Meiglyptes tukki) is a species of bird in the family Picidae.
The northern black flycatcher (Melaenornis edolioides) is a small passerine bird in the flycatcher family, Muscicapidae.

t: The white-eyed slaty flycatcher (Melaenornis fischeri) is a small passerine bird of the genus Melaenornis in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. It is native to the African highlands from Ethiopia and Kenya through Rwanda to eastern Zaire and Malawi.
f: The specific epithet commemorates the German explorer Gustav Adolf Fischer.

t: The southern black flycatcher (Melaenornis pammelaina) is a small passerine bird of the genus Melaenornis in the flycatcher family, Muscicapidae, native to open and lightly wooded areas of eastern and southern Africa. The global population size has not been quantified but the bird is listed by the IUCN as being of "Least concern".
f: This species has a large range, with an estimated global extent of occurrence of 4,000,000 square kilometres (1,500,000 sq mi).

t: The fiscal flycatcher (Sigelus silens) is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family. It is a resident breeder in Botswana, South Africa, Lesotho, Mozambique and Swaziland, and a vagrant to Namibia.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Sigelus.

t: The lesser melampitta (Melampitta lugubris) is a medium-sized enigmatic terrestrial songbird of mountain forests of New Guinea. It is the only species in the genus Melampitta.
f: The lesser melampitta builds dome-like nest in the forests.

t: The golden-fronted woodpecker (Melanerpes aurifrons) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in the southern United States (mostly Texas), Mexico and parts of Central America.

t: The white-fronted woodpecker (Melanerpes cactorum) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, subtropical or tropical dry shrubland, and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.
f: It is found mainly in Bolivia, Paraguay and Argentina.

t: The white woodpecker (Melanerpes candidus) is a South American species of woodpecker (family Picidae) native to the wooded grasslands of Suriname, French Guiana, Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina. The IUCN has rated it as a "least-concern species".
f: It is a bright white bird with black wings and a distinctive small bright yellow eye patch.

t: The red-bellied woodpecker (Melanerpes carolinus) is a medium-sized woodpecker of the family Picidae. Though it has a vivid orange-red crown and nape it is not to be confused with the red-headed woodpecker, a separate species of woodpecker in the same genus with an entirely red head and neck that sports a solid black back and white belly.
f: It breeds mainly in the eastern United States, ranging as far south as Florida and as far north as Canada.

t: The golden-naped woodpecker (Melanerpes chrysauchen) is a species of bird in the woodpecker family Picidae. The two species, along with several other species, are sometimes placed in the genus Tripsurus.
f: The species is very closely related to the beautiful woodpecker, which is sometimes treated as the same species.
The golden-cheeked woodpecker (Melanerpes chrysogenys) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.

t: The yellow-tufted woodpecker (Melanerpes cruentatus) is a species of woodpecker. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: Its breeding habitat is open country across southern Canada and the east-central United States. It is rated as least concern on the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)'s Red List of Endangered species, having been down-listed from near threatened in 2018.
f: The red-headed woodpecker (Melanerpes erythrocephalus) is a mid-sized woodpecker found in temperate North America.

t: The yellow-fronted woodpecker (Melanerpes flavifrons) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Brazil, Paraguay and far north-eastern Argentina.

t: The acorn woodpecker (Melanerpes formicivorus) is a medium-sized woodpecker with a length of around 20 cm (8 in), and an average weight of 85 g (3.0 oz).
f: It is found across Central America, as well as North into the western United States and South into parts of Colombia.

t: Hoffmann's woodpecker (Melanerpes hoffmannii) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found from Honduras south to Costa Rica.

t: The grey-breasted woodpecker (Melanerpes hypopolius) is a species of bird in the family Picidae.
f: It is endemic to the interior of southwestern Mexico.

t: Lewis's woodpecker (Melanerpes lewis) is a large North American species of woodpecker which ornithologist Alexander Wilson named after Meriwether Lewis.
f: Lewis was one of the explorers who surveyed the areas bought by the United States of America as part of the Louisiana Purchase and first described this species of bird.

t: The Puerto Rican woodpecker (Melanerpes portoricensis) is the only woodpecker endemic to the archipelago of Puerto Rico and is one of the five species of the genus Melanerpes that occur in the Antilles. Furthermore, it is the only resident species of the family Picidae in Puerto Rico.
f: The species is common on the main island of Puerto Rico and rare on the island of Vieques.

t: The black-cheeked woodpecker (Melanerpes pucherani) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found from Mexico south to Ecuador.

t: The Yucatan woodpecker (Melanerpes pygmaeus) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. The Yucatan woodpecker is found in Belize and Mexico, and ranges over the entire Yucatán Peninsula.
f: It is sometimes referred to as the red-vented woodpecker.
The Jamaican woodpecker (Melanerpes radiolatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.

t: The red-crowned woodpecker (Melanerpes rubricapillus) is a species of bird in the subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia, Venezuela, Guyana, Suriname, and Tobago.
The Hispaniolan woodpecker (Melanerpes striatus) is a medium-sized woodpecker endemic to the Caribbean island of Hispaniola (split between the Dominican Republic and Haiti).

t: The West Indian woodpecker (Melanerpes superciliaris) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in the Bahamas, the Cayman Islands and Cuba.

t: The Gila woodpecker (Melanerpes uropygialis) is a medium-sized woodpecker of the desert regions of the southwestern United States and western Mexico.
f: In the U.S., they range through southeastern California, southern Nevada, Arizona, and New Mexico.

t: The grey tit (Melaniparus afer) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry shrubland and Mediterranean-type shrubby vegetation.
f: It is found in Lesotho and South Africa.

t: The white-bellied tit (Melaniparus albiventris) is a species of bird in the family Paridae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Cameroon, Kenya, Nigeria, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: The ashy tit (Melaniparus cinerascens) is a species of bird in the family Paridae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and dry savanna.
f: It is found in Angola, Botswana, Namibia, South Africa, and Zimbabwe.

t: The dusky tit (Melaniparus funereus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae. It is native to the African tropical rainforest.
f: The dusky tit is known for being almost entirely black with brownish or gray tones, depending on its sex.

t: The white-winged black tit (Melaniparus leucomelas) is a passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. The species was first described by Eduard Rüppell in 1840.
f: It is also known as the white-winged tit, dark-eyed black tit or northern black tit.
The southern black tit or simply black tit (Melaniparus niger) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae, which is native to woodland habitats in southern Africa.

t: The rufous-bellied tit (Melaniparus rufiventris) is a species of bird in the tit family.
f: It is found in Africa from the Republic of the Congo, DR Congo and northern Namibia east to Tanzania and northern Mozambique.

t: The acacia tit (Melaniparus thruppi), also known as the Somali tit and northern grey tit, is a species of bird in the family Paridae.
f: It is native to north eastern Africa where it occurs in dry acacia habitat.

t: The black scoter or American scoter (Melanitta americana) is a large sea duck, 43 to 49 cm (17 to 19 in) in length. The genus name is derived from Ancient Greek melas "black" and netta "duck".
f: Its French name, used in parts of its Canadian range, is macreuse noire (also meaning "black scoter").

t: The velvet scoter (Melanitta fusca) is a large sea duck, which breeds over the far north of Europe and the Palearctic west of the Yenisey basin. The genus name is derived from Ancient Greek melas "black" and netta "duck".
f: The species name is from the Latin fuscus "dusky brown".

t: The common scoter (Melanitta nigra) is a large sea duck, 43–54 cm (17–21 in) in length, which breeds over the far north of Europe and the Palearctic east to the Olenyok River.
f: The black scoter (M. americana) of North America and eastern Siberia was formerly considered to be a subspecies.

t: The surf scoter (Melanitta perspicillata) is a large sea duck native to North America. Adult males are almost entirely black with characteristic white patches on the forehead and the nape and adult females are slightly smaller and browner.
f: They are diving ducks and mainly feed on benthic invertebrates, mussels representing an important part of their diet.

t: The sultan tit (Melanochlora sultanea) is an Asian forest bird with black upperparts plumage and yellow underparts, dark bill, and (depending on subspecies) a yellow or black crest. The sexes are similar, though the female has slightly duller plumage with greenish-black upperparts and throat.
f: The young bird is duller than the adult and has a shorter crest.

t: The calandra lark (Melanocorypha calandra) or European calandra-lark breeds in warm temperate countries around the Mediterranean and eastwards through Turkey into northern Iran and southern Russia.
f: It is replaced further east by its relative, the bimaculated lark.

t: The Tibetan lark (Melanocorypha maxima) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found on the Tibetan Plateau from north-western India to central China.
f: Alternate names for this species include the Asiatic lark, long-billed calandra lark and long-billed lark.

t: The white-bridled finch (Melanodera melanodera), also known as the canary-winged finch or black-throated finch, is a small passerine bird belonging to the genus Melanodera together with the yellow-bridled finch (M. xanthogramma). Formerly placed in the family Emberizidae, it is now considered a tanager.
f: It is found in grassland in southernmost South America.
The yellow-bridled finch (Melanodera xanthogramma) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae found in Argentina and Chile.

t: The hooded robin (Melanodryas cucullata) is a small passerine bird native to Australia.
f: Like many brightly coloured robins of the Petroicidae, it is sexually dimorphic; the male bears a distinctive black-and-white plumage, while the female is a nondescript grey-brown.

t: The dusky robin (Melanodryas vittata) is a small passerine bird native to Tasmania. A member of the Australian robin family Petroicidae, it is known by many other names such as Dozey, Sad, Sleepy, Stump, Tasmania/Wood Robin; Native Sparrow or Sad Bird.
f: This sombre dark brown robin is characterised by a narrow line, starting from behind the eye to the rear of the ear-coverts and white bars running down it wings.

t: The elegant crescentchest (Melanopareia elegans) is a species of bird in the family Melanopareiidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The Marañón crescentchest (Melanopareia maranonica) is a species of bird in the family Melanopareiidae.
f: It is found in southern Ecuador and northern Peru.

t: The olive-crowned crescentchest (Melanopareia maximiliani) is a species of bird in the family Melanopareiidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, and Paraguay.

t: The collared crescentchest (Melanopareia torquata) is a species of suboscine passerine bird in the family Melanopareiidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The black catbird (Melanoptila glabrirostris) is a songbird species in the monotypic genus Melanoptila, part of the family Mimidae. At 19–20.5 cm (7.5–8.1 in) in length and 31.6–42 g (1.11–1.48 oz) in mass, it is the smallest of the mimids.
f: Although it is a mimid, the black catbird is not known to imitate any other species.

t: The black pitohui (Melanorectes nigrescens) is a species of bird in the monotypic genus of Melanorectes in the family Pachycephalidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found throughout the highlands of New Guinea.

t: The black-faced grassquit (Melanospiza bicolor) is a small bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in the West Indies except Cuba Colombia, Venezuela and islands off its coast, and on islands in the western Caribbean Sea.

t: The blue mockingbird (Melanotis caerulescens) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae. It is endemic to Mexico, but has occurred as a vagrant in the southern United States.
f: This color is a result of feather structure rather than pigment, and therefore can look gray in the shade.

t: The blue-and-white mockingbird (Melanotis hypoleucus) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.
f: It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.

f: The wild turkey (Meleagris gallopavo) is an upland game bird native to North America, one of two extant species of turkey and the heaviest member of the order Galliformes.
