f: The wild turkey (Meleagris gallopavo) is an upland game bird native to North America, one of two extant species of turkey and the heaviest member of the order Galliformes.

t: It is the ancestor to the domestic turkey (M. g. domesticus), which was originally derived from a southern Mexican subspecies of wild turkey (not the related ocellated turkey).
f: The wild turkey (Meleagris gallopavo) is an upland game bird native to North America, one of two extant species of turkey and the heaviest member of the order Galliformes.

t: The ocellated turkey (Meleagris ocellata) is a species of turkey residing primarily in the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico, as well as in parts of Belize and Guatemala. A relative of the North American wild turkey (Meleagris gallopavo), it was sometimes previously considered in a genus of its own (Agriocharis), but the differences between the two turkeys are currently considered too small to justify generic segregation.
f: It is a relatively large bird, at around 70–122 cm (28–48 in) long and an average weight of 3 kg (6.6 lb) in females and 5 kg (11 lb) in males.

t: The Makira honeyeater (Meliarchus sclateri), also known as the San Cristobal honeyeater, is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae.
f: It is endemic to Makira in the Solomon Islands.

t: Belford's melidectes (Melidectes belfordi), also known as Belford's honeyeater, is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in the New Guinea Highlands.

t: The yellow-browed melidectes (Melidectes rufocrissalis), also known as the yellow-browed honeyeater, is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found mainly in Papua New Guinea.

t: The hook-billed kingfisher (Melidora macrorrhina) is a species of kingfisher in the subfamily Halcyoninae that is resident in the lowland forested areas of New Guinea and some of the nearby islands.
f: It is the only member of the genus Melidora.

t: Lewin's honeyeater (Meliphaga lewinii) is a bird that inhabits the ranges along the east coast of Australia. Another name is Yellow-eared Honeyeater.
f: It has a semicircular ear-patch, pale yellow in colour.

t: The yellow-spotted honeyeater (Meliphaga notata) is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. It is also known as the lesser lewin.
f: The bird's common name refers to the yellow patch that members of the species have behind their eyes.

t: The black-headed honeyeater (Melithreptus affinis) is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. It is one of two members of the genus Melithreptus endemic to Tasmania.
f: Despite its name, the black-headed honeyeater eats predominantly insects.

t: The white-throated honeyeater (Melithreptus albogularis) is a bird of the honeyeater family Meliphagidae native to New Guinea and eastern and northern Australia.
f: It is 11.5 to 14.5 cm (4.5 to 5.7 in) long, olive-green above and white below, with a black head, a white or pale blue patch over the eye, and a white stripe across the nape.

t: The brown-headed honeyeater (Melithreptus brevirostris) is a species of passerine bird in the family Meliphagidae.
f: Its natural habitats are temperate forests and Mediterranean-type shrubby vegetation.

t: Gilbert's honeyeater (Melithreptus chloropsis), also known as the Swan River honeyeater or western white-naped honeyeater, is a passerine bird of the honeyeater family Meliphagidae native to southwestern Australia. The bill is brownish-black and the eyes a dull red.
f: A mid-sized honeyeater, it is olive-green above and white below, with a black head, nape and throat and a white patch over the eye and a white crescent-shaped patch on the nape.

t: The black-chinned honeyeater (Melithreptus gularis) is a species of passerine bird in the family Meliphagidae.
f: Its natural habitats are temperate forests and subtropical or tropical dry forests.

t: The white-naped honeyeater (Melithreptus lunatus) is a passerine bird of the honeyeater family Meliphagidae native to eastern Australia. Birds from southwestern Australia have been shown to be a distinct species, Gilbert's honeyeater, and the eastern birds are more closely related to the black-headed honeyeater of Tasmania.
f: Its diet consists of nectar from various flowers, and it also feeds on insects.

t: The strong-billed honeyeater (Melithreptus validirostris) is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. It is one of two species of the genus Melithreptus endemic to Tasmania.
f: Its natural habitat is temperate forest.

t: The bee hummingbird, zunzuncito or Helena hummingbird (Mellisuga helenae) is a species of hummingbird, native to the island of Cuba in the Caribbean.
f: The bee hummingbird feeds on flower nectar and insects.

t: The vervain hummingbird (Mellisuga minima) is a species of hummingbird in tribe Mellisugini of subfamily Trochilinae, the "bee hummingbirds".
f: It is found on Hispaniola (split between the Dominican Republic and Haiti) and Jamaica.

t: The moustached grass warbler (Melocichla mentalis) is a species of African warbler, formerly placed in the family Sylviidae. Its natural habitats are moist savanna and subtropical or tropical moist shrubland.
f: It is widely found throughout Sub-Saharan Africa, although absent in southern parts of the continent.

t: The budgerigar ( BUJ-ər-ih-gar, -⁠ə-ree-; Melopsittacus undulatus), also known as the common parakeet, shell parakeet or budgie ( BUJ-ee), is a small, long-tailed, seed-eating parrot native to Australia. Naturally, the species is green and yellow with black, scalloped markings on the nape, back, and wings.
f: First recorded in 1805, budgerigars are popular pets around the world due to their small size, low cost, and ability to mimic human speech.

t: The Puerto Rican bullfinch (Melopyrrha portoricensis) is a small bullfinch tanager endemic to the archipelago of Puerto Rico. It consumes seeds, fruits, insects, and spiders.
f: The species can be commonly found in heavy forests throughout Puerto Rico, except on the easternmost tip of the island.

t: The Greater Antillean bullfinch (Melopyrrha violacea) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in the Bahamas, Hispaniola (the Dominican Republic, Haiti, and their offshore islands), Jamaica, and the Turks and Caicos Islands.
The swamp sparrow (Melospiza georgiana) is a medium-sized New World sparrow related to the song sparrow.

t: Lincoln's sparrow (Melospiza lincolnii) is a small sparrow native to North America. Lincoln's sparrow is one of three species in the genus Melospiza which also includes the song sparrow (M. melodia) and the swamp sparrow (M. georgiana).
f: It is a less common passerine bird that often stays hidden under thick ground cover, but can be distinguished by its sweet, wrenlike song.

t: The song sparrow (Melospiza melodia) is a medium-sized New World sparrow.
f: Among the native sparrows in North America, it is easily one of the most abundant, variable, and adaptable species.
The name of this bird commemorates the American ornithologist James William Abert (1820–1897).
The white-throated towhee (Melozone albicollis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.
Prevost's ground sparrow (Melozone biarcuata), also known as the white-faced ground sparrow, is an American sparrow.
Cabanis's ground sparrow (Melozone cabanisi) or the Costa Rican ground sparrow is a Near Threatened species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

t: The California towhee (Melozone crissalis) is a bird of the family Passerellidae, native to the coastal regions of western Oregon and California in the United States and Baja California and Baja California Sur in Mexico. The taxonomy of this species has been debated.
f: Within the group, there has been debate about whether the distinction between this species and the similar canyon towhee (Melozone fuscus) should be at the specific or subspecific level.

t: The canyon towhee (Melozone fusca) is a bird of the family Passerellidae.
f: Until 1989, the canyon towhee and the California towhee were considered to be a single species which was called the brown towhee.
The rusty-crowned ground sparrow (Melozone kieneri) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

t: The white-eared ground sparrow (Melozone leucotis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Honduras, and Nicaragua.

t: Albert's lyrebird (Menura alberti), sometimes known as the northern lyrebird, is a timid, pheasant-sized songbird which is endemic to subtropical rainforests of Australia, in a small area on the state border between New South Wales and Queensland. It lacks the elegant lyre-shaped tail feathers of the superb lyrebird and is found in a much more restricted range.
f: The rarer of the two species of lyrebirds, Albert's lyrebird is named after Prince Albert, the prince consort of Queen Victoria, queen of the United Kingdom.

t: The superb lyrebird (Menura novaehollandiae) is an Australian passerine songbird, one of two species from the family Menuridae, with the other being the much rarer Albert's lyrebird. The species is endemic to Australia and is found in forest in the southeast of the country.
f: One of the world's largest songbirds, the superb lyrebird is renowned for its elaborate tail and courtship displays, and for its excellent mimicry.

t: The smew (Mergellus albellus) is a species of duck and is the only living member of the genus Mergellus. The genus is closely related to Mergus and is sometimes included in it; genetic studies have shown that it is the sister taxon to Mergus and Lophodytes.
f: The smew has hybridised with the common goldeneye (Bucephala clangula).

t: The common merganser or goosander (Mergus merganser) is a large sea duck of rivers and lakes in forested areas of Europe, Asia, and North America. The name "common merganser" is used in North America, while "goosander" is used in Eurasia.
f: The common merganser eats mainly fish.

t: The red-breasted merganser (Mergus serrator) is a duck species that is native to much of the temperate to subarctic Northern Hemisphere. Individuals fly rapidly, and feed by diving from the surface to pursue aquatic animals underwater, using serrated bills to capture slippery fish.
f: The red breast that gives the species its common name is only displayed by males in breeding plumage.

t: The white-throated bee-eater (Merops albicollis) is a species of bee-eater that breeds in semi-desert along the southern edge of the Sahara.
f: The white-throated bee-eater is migratory, wintering in a completely different habitat in the equatorial rain forests of Africa from southern Senegal to Uganda.

t: The European bee-eater (Merops apiaster) is a bird species in the bee-eater family, Meropidae. Except for the resident southern African population, the species is strongly migratory, wintering in tropical Africa.
f: It has the largest range of any bee-eater species, breeding in southern and central Europe, northern and southern Africa, and western Asia.

t: The white-fronted bee-eater (Merops bullockoides) is a species of bee-eater widely distributed in sub-equatorial Africa. The species has a distinctive white forehead, a square tail, and a bright red patch on its throat.
f: It nests in small colonies, digging holes in cliffs or earthen banks, and can usually be seen in low trees, waiting to hunt passing insects by making quick hawking flights or gliding down before hovering briefly to catch the prey.

t: The red-throated bee-eater (Merops bulocki) is a species of bird in the family Meropidae. It has a wide range and large total population, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has assessed its conservation status as being of "least concern".
f: This species is native to the Sudan (region).

t: The swallow-tailed bee-eater (Merops hirundineus) is a species of bee-eater native to sub-Saharan Africa. Its vivid colors and forked tail are distinctive.
f: It feeds predominantly on insects, especially bees and their relatives, which are caught in flight from an open perch.

t: The chestnut-headed bee-eater (Merops leschenaulti), or bay-headed bee-eater, is a bird in the bee-eater family Meropidae. This species, like other bee-eaters, is a richly coloured, slender bird.
f: It breeds on the Indian subcontinent and adjoining regions, ranging from India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka across Southeast Asia to Indonesia.

t: The cinnamon-chested bee-eater (Merops oreobates) is a species of bird in the family Meropidae.
f: It is mainly native to the Albertine Rift montane forests and the East African montane forests of East Africa, in the regions surrounding Lake Victoria.

t: The Asian green bee-eater (Merops orientalis), also known as the little green bee-eater, and just green bee-eater, is a bird species in the bee-eater family. It is resident or with short-distance seasonal movements, and is found widely distributed across Asia from coastal southern Iran east through the Indian subcontinent to Vietnam.
f: They are mainly insect eaters and they are found in grassland, thin scrub and forest often quite far from water.
The rainbow bee-eater (Merops ornatus) is a bird species in the bee-eater family Meropidae.

t: The blue-cheeked bee-eater (Merops persicus) is a species of bee-eater that breeds in Northern Africa and the Middle East from eastern Turkey to Kazakhstan and India. This species occurs as a rare vagrant north of its breeding range, with most vagrants occurring in Italy and Greece.
f: It is generally strongly migratory, wintering in tropical Africa, although some populations are resident year-round in the Sahel.
The blue-tailed bee-eater (Merops philippinus) is a bee-eater species mostly seen in open habitats close to water.

t: The little bee-eater (Merops pusillus) is a bird species in the bee-eater family, Meropidae. They are found in Sub-Saharan Africa.
f: Migration is limited to seasonal movements depending on rainfall patterns.

t: The olive bee-eater or Madagascar bee-eater (Merops superciliosus) is a bee-eater species in the genus Merops.
f: It is a common species with a wide range so the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated their conservation status as "least concern".

t: The blue-breasted bee-eater (Merops variegatus) is a central African species of bird. It is a member of the family Meropidae.
f: Meropids are all visually similar and have a diet specialized in Hymenopterans.

t: The blue-throated bee-eater (Merops viridis) is a species of bird in the bee-eater family. It is found in much of southeast Asia, in subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.
f: They have a rich variety of songs and calls, including long calls which allow them to communicate long distances in the forest.

t: The slaty bristlefront (Merulaxis ater) is a member of the Neotropical bird family Rhinocryptidae, the tapaculos.
f: It is endemic to south-east Brazil.

t: The green ibis (Mesembrinibis cayennensis), also known as the Cayenne ibis, is a wading bird in the ibis family Threskiornithidae. It is the only member of the genus Mesembrinibis.
f: It undertakes some local seasonal movements in the dry season.

t: It is one of three species in the mesite family or the Mesitornithidae, and though classified as vulnerable by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), it is the most widespread of the three.
f: The brown mesite (Mesitornis unicolor) is a ground-dwelling bird endemic to Madagascar.

t: The white-breasted mesite or white-breasted roatelo (Mesitornis variegatus) is a ground-dwelling bird endemic to Madagascar. One of three species in the mesite family, Mesitornithidae, it is classified as vulnerable by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).
f: It has a small population and is restricted to five sites in the north and west of the island, and one in the east.

t: The Tyrian metaltail (Metallura tyrianthina) is a species of hummingbird in the subfamily Lesbiinae, the brilliants and coquettes.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The viridian metaltail (Metallura williami) is a species of hummingbird in the "coquettes", tribe Lesbiini of subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The bronze-winged jacana (Metopidius indicus) is a wader in the family Jacanidae. It is found across South and Southeast Asia and is the sole species in the genus Metopidius.
f: Males maintain territories, with one male in the harem chosen to incubate the eggs and take care of the young.

t: The orange-fronted plushcrown (Metopothrix aurantiaca) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The black-winged ground dove (Metriopelia melanoptera) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. It lives in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru and is usually found in grassy areas near tree lines but roosts in Polylepis forest and Puya colonies.
f: It moves to lower elevations in winter.

t: Buckley's forest falcon (Micrastur buckleyi), also called lesser collared forest-falcon and Traylor's forest-falcon, is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Herpetotherinae of family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, Peru, and possibly Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The lined forest falcon (Micrastur gilvicollis) is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Herpetotherinae of family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The cryptic forest falcon (Micrastur mintoni) is a species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae. It is found in the southeastern Amazon rainforest in Brazil and Bolivia.
f: Unlike the lined forest falcon, with which it has long been confused in a cryptic species complex, adult cryptic forest falcons only have a single white tail-band (in addition to a narrow white tail-tip).

t: The slaty-backed forest falcon (Micrastur mirandollei) is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Herpetotherinae of family Falconidae, the falcons, and caracaras.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, and every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The barred forest falcon (Micrastur ruficollis) is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Herpetotherinae of family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.
f: It occurs from southern Mexico south through most of Central America and in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The collared forest falcon (Micrastur semitorquatus) is a species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae. It is the largest member of the Micrastur genus and a common inhabitant of tropical rainforests in Latin America.
f: Hiding in the dense forest canopy, they are a secretive bird often only recognized by their distinctive call.

t: The elf owl (Micrathene whitneyi) is a small grayish-brown owl about the size of a sparrow found in the Southwestern United States, central Mexico, and the Baja California peninsula. It has pale yellow eyes highlighted by thin white "eyebrows" and a gray bill with a horn-colored tip.
f: It is nocturnal and feeds primarily on insects.

t: The tawny-faced gnatwren or half-collared gnatwren (Microbates cinereiventris) is a species of bird in the family Polioptilidae, the gnatcatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Nicaragua, Panama, and Peru.

t: The collared gnatwren (Microbates collaris) is a species of bird in the family Polioptilidae, the gnatcatchers.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: It is a small short-billed cormorant usually black above and white below with a yellow bill and small crest, although a mostly black white-throated form predominates in New Zealand. Three subspecies are recognised.
f: Until recently, most authorities referred to this species as Phalacrocorax melanoleucos.

t: The little cormorant (Microcarbo niger) is a member of the cormorant family of seabirds. Slightly smaller than the Indian cormorant it lacks a peaked head and has a shorter beak.
f: It forages singly or sometimes in loose groups in lowland freshwater bodies, including small ponds, large lakes, streams and sometimes coastal estuaries.

t: Microcentrum rhombifolium is a species of insect in the family Tettigoniidae. They live across North America in trees and shrubs.
f: Common names include greater angle-wing katydid, broad-winged katydid, and angular-winged katydid.

t: The wing-banded wren (Microcerculus bambla) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The southern nightingale-wren (Microcerculus marginatus), also known as the scaly-breasted wren, is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The northern nightingale-wren (Microcerculus philomela), or nightingale wren, is a species of passerine bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Belize, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: The flutist wren (Microcerculus ustulatus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is restricted to humid highland forest in the Tepui region of northern Brazil, Guyana, and Venezuela.

t: The jacky winter (Microeca fascinans) is a small grey-brown robin found commonly throughout Australia and also in Papua New Guinea. Their call is also often referred to as sounding like peter-peter-peter.
f: The jacky winter acquired its name due to rapid and strong vocalisations, which sound like jacky-jacky winter-winter.

t: The lemon-bellied flyrobin or lemon-bellied flycatcher (Microeca flavigaster) is a species of bird in the family Petroicidae.
f: Found in Australia, Indonesia, and Papua New Guinea, its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.

t: The black-thighed falconet (Microhierax fringillarius) is one of the smallest birds of prey, typically measuring between 14–16 centimetres (5.5–6.3 in) long, with a 27–32 centimetres (11–13 in) wingspan, which is a size comparable to a typical sparrow.
f: It is native to Brunei, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia, and vagrant to Sri Lanka.

t: The lanceolated monklet (Micromonacha lanceolata) is a species of bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, and Peru.
The gabar goshawk (Micronisus gabar) is a small species of African and Arabian bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.
The common name and scientific name commemorate the German ethnographer, naturalist, and colonial explorer Friedrich Hermann Otto Finsch .

t: The rufous woodpecker (Micropternus brachyurus) is a medium-sized brown woodpecker native to South and Southeast Asia. It was for sometime placed in the otherwise Neotropical genus Celeus but this has been shown to be a case of evolutionary convergence and molecular phylogenetic studies support its placement in the monotypic genus Micropternus.
f: It is short-billed, foraging in pairs on small insects, particularly ants and termites, in scrub, evergreen, and deciduous forests and is noted for building its nest within the carton nests of arboreal ants in the genus Crematogaster.

t: The ocellated crake (Rufirallus schomburgkii) is a small terrestrial species of bird in the family Rallidae that is native to the grassland and savanna habitats of Central America and South America. This species was formerly placed in its own genus Micropygia .
f: Though it is not often seen, it is easily recognizable by its cinnamon plumage with black and white mottling.

t: The dot-winged antwren (Microrhopias quixensis) or velvety antwren is a passerine bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country except El Salvador, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, and Suriname.

t: The gray-throated warbling finch (Microspingus cabanisi) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in forest borders and woodland in south-eastern Brazil, far eastern Paraguay, far north-eastern Argentina, and Uruguay.
f: It was previously considered conspecific with the buff-throated warbling finch, and together they were known as the red-rumped warbling finch.

t: The rusty-browed warbling finch (Microspingus erythrophrys) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Argentina and Bolivia.

t: The buff-throated warbling finch (Microspingus lateralis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in forest borders and woodland in south-eastern Brazil.
f: It was previously considered conspecific with the gray-throated warbling finch, and together they were known as the red-rumped warbling finch.

t: The black-capped warbling finch (Microspingus melanoleucus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, subtropical or tropical dry shrubland, and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay and western Uruguay.

t: The ringed warbling finch (Microspingus torquatus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, subtropical or tropical dry shrubland, and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, and Paraguay.

t: The rufous-tailed xenops (Microxenops milleri) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, Venezuela, and possibly French Guiana.

t: The yellow-headed caracara (Daptrius chimachima) is a new-world bird of prey in the family Falconidae, of the Falconiformes order (true falcons, caracaras and their kin).
f: It can be found in North America and South America, from Nicaragua to Uruguay.

t: The chimango caracara (Daptrius chimango), also known as chimango or tiuque, is a species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay, as a vagrant on the Falkland Islands and has been introduced on Rapa Nui.

t: The black kite or fire kite (Milvus migrans) is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors. Current global population estimates run up to 6.7 million individuals.
f: It is thought to be the world's most abundant species of Accipitridae, although some populations have experienced dramatic declines or fluctuations.

t: The red kite (Milvus milvus) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as eagles, buzzards, and harriers. The species currently breeds only in Europe, though it formerly also bred in West Asia and Northwest Africa.
f: Vagrants have reached north to Finland and south to Israel, Libya and the Gambia.

t: The brown-backed mockingbird (Mimus dorsalis) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Bolivia.
The tropical mockingbird (Mimus gilvus) is a resident breeding bird from southern Mexico to northern and eastern South America and in the Lesser Antilles and other Caribbean islands.

t: The Bahama mockingbird (Mimus gundlachii) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.
f: It is found in the Bahamas, Cuba, Jamaica and the Turks and Caicos Islands, and is a vagrant to Florida.

t: The long-tailed mockingbird (Mimus longicaudatus) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The northern mockingbird (Mimus polyglottos) is a mockingbird commonly found in North America, of the family Mimidae. The species is also found in some parts of the Caribbean, as well as on the Hawaiian Islands.
f: The species is known for its ability to mimic bird calls and other types of sound, including artificial and electronic noises.

t: The chalk-browed mockingbird (Mimus saturninus) is a bird in the family Mimidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Bolivia, Argentina, Paraguay, Suriname, and Uruguay.

t: The Chilean mockingbird (Mimus thenca), locally known as tenca, is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.

t: The white-banded mockingbird (Mimus triurus) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The red-tailed minla (Minla ignotincta) is a passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.
f: It is the only species in the genus Minla.

t: The yellow-faced myna (Mino dumontii) is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae. It is found in New Guinea and nearby smaller islands, where its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It was named after Charles Dumont.

t: The long-tailed myna (Mino kreffti) is a member of the starling family. It resembles the yellow-faced myna, and the two were formerly considered conspecific.
f: It is native to the Bismarck and Solomon archipelagos.

t: Miogryllus verticalis, the eastern striped cricket, is a species of field cricket in the family Gryllidae. The species Miogryllus saussurei, formerly an independent species, is now considered a synonym of Miogryllus verticalis.
f: It is found in eastern North America, Central America, and South America.

t: McConnell's flycatcher (Mionectes macconnelli) is a species of bird in the tyrant flycatcher family Tyrannidae.

t: The ochre-bellied flycatcher (Mionectes oleagineus) is a small bird of the tyrant flycatcher family.
f: It is found in Mexico, Central America, Trinidad and Tobago, and northern South America.

t: The olive-streaked flycatcher (Mionectes olivaceus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The grey-hooded flycatcher (Mionectes rufiventris) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.

t: The streak-necked flycatcher (Mionectes striaticollis) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: Jerdon's bush lark (Plocealauda affinis) or Jerdon's lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in south Asia. This was formerly placed in the genus Mirafra and considered as a subspecies of Mirafra assamica and termed as the Madras bushlark.
f: Two other species in the complex include Mirafra marionae and Mirafra microptera.

t: The rufous-naped lark (Corypha africana) or rufous-naped bush lark is a widespread and conspicuous species of lark in the lightly wooded grasslands, open savannas and farmlands of the Afrotropics. This rudimentary display has been proposed as the precursor to the wing-clapping displays of other bush lark species.
f: Males attract attention to themselves by a bold and often repeated wing-fluttering display from a prominent perch, which is accompanied by a melodious and far-carrying whistled phrase.

t: The Cape clapper lark (Corypha apiata) is a small passerine bird which breeds in southern Africa. The Cape clapper lark is a species of open grassland and savannah, also inhabiting karoo, fynbos and fallow agricultural land.
f: It derives its name from the wing clapping which forms part of the display flight.
The Bengal bush lark (Plocealauda assamica) or Bengal lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in Southern Asia.

t: It was described by the American naturalist Thomas Horsfield.
f: The singing bush lark or Horsfield's bush lark (Mirafra javanica) is a species of lark which inhabits grassland throughout most of Australia and much of Southeast Asia.

t: The melodious lark (Mirafra cheniana) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in southern Africa.
f: It is currently threatened by habitat loss.
The Indochinese bush lark (Plocealauda erythrocephala) or Indochinese lark is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in southeast Asia.
The Indian bush lark (Plocealauda erythroptera) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in South Asia.

t: The eastern clapper lark (Corypha fasciolata) is a small passerine bird which breeds in southern Africa.
f: It derives its name from the wing clapping which forms part of its display flight.
The monotonous lark (Mirafra passerina) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found in southern Africa.

t: The flappet lark (Amirafra rufocinnamomea) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae that is widespread across Sub-Saharan Africa.
f: The name flappet originates from the distinctive wing flapping sound made during its breeding season.

t: The northern tufted flycatcher or simply tufted flycatcher (Mitrephanes phaeocercus) is a small passerine bird in the tyrant flycatcher family.
f: It is found from Mexico to Ecuador.

t: The dusky-faced tanager (Mitrospingus cassinii) is a species of bird in the family Mitrospingidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, and Panama.

t: The olive-backed tanager (Mitrospingus oleagineus) is a species of bird in the family Mitrospingidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Guyana, and Venezuela.

t: Salvin's curassow (Mitu salvini) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The crestless curassow (Mitu tomentosum) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Guyana, and Venezuela.

t: The razor-billed curassow (Mitu tuberosum) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, and Peru.
The bold-striped tit-babbler (Mixornis bornensis) is a species of Old World babbler found in Southeast Asia.

t: The grey-cheeked tit-babbler (Mixornis flavicollis) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae.
f: Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
The pin-striped tit-babbler (Mixornis gularis), also known as the yellow-breasted babbler, is a species of bird in the Old World babbler family Timaliidae that is found in South and Southeast Asia.

t: The grey-faced tit-babbler (Mixornis kelleyi) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae.
f: It is found in Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam, where its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

t: The black-and-white warbler (Mniotilta varia) is a species of New World warbler, and the only member of its genus, Mniotilta. It breeds in northern and eastern North America and winters in Florida, Central America, and the West Indies down to Peru.
f: It has been recorded as a vagrant in Northern Europe, especially Britain and Ireland.

t: The spot-throat (Modulatrix stictigula) is a species of bird in the family Modulatricidae. It is native to the Eastern Arc forests.
f: It is the only member of the genus Modulatrix.

t: The whitehead (Mohoua albicilla; Māori: pōpokotea) is a species of small (15 cm in length, 18.5/14.5 g.) passerine bird endemic to New Zealand. It is classified in the family Mohouidae.
f: In the past whiteheads held a special place in Māori culture.

t: The pīpipi (Mohoua novaeseelandiae), also known as brown creeper or New Zealand creeper, is a small passerine bird endemic to the South Island, Stewart Island and their surrounding islands, in New Zealand. It was called the New Zealand titmouse in the 1780s.
f: They have strong legs and toes for hanging upside down while feeding.

t: The yellowhead or mohua (Mohoua ochrocephala) is a small insectivorous passerine bird endemic to the South Island of New Zealand.
f: Once a common forest bird, its numbers declined drastically after the introduction of rats and stoats, and its IUCN conservation status is now near threatened.
The bronzed cowbird (Molothrus aeneus), also known as the red-eyed cowbird, is a small icterid native to North America.

t: The brown-headed cowbird (Molothrus ater) is a small, obligate brood parasitic icterid native to temperate and subtropical North America.
f: It is a permanent resident in the southern parts of its range; northern birds migrate to the southern United States and Mexico in winter, returning to their summer habitat around March or April.

t: The shiny cowbird (Molothrus bonariensis) is a passerine bird in the New World family Icteridae. It breeds in most of South America except for dense forests and areas of high altitude such as mountains.
f: As the shiny cowbird is an effective generalist brood parasite, it can be considered the South American counterpart to the brown-headed cowbird.

t: The giant cowbird (Molothrus oryzivorus) is a large passerine bird in the New World family Icteridae. It breeds from southern Mexico south to northern Argentina, and on Trinidad and Tobago.
f: It is a brood parasite and lays its eggs in the nests of other birds.

t: The screaming cowbird (Molothrus rufoaxillaris) is an obligate brood parasite belonging to the family Icteridae and is found in South America.
f: It is also known commonly as the short billed cowbird.
The Andean motmot or highland motmot (Momotus aequatorialis) is a colorful bird found from northern Colombia to western Bolivia.

t: The blue-capped motmot (Momotus coeruliceps) or blue-crowned motmot, is a colorful bird in the family Momotidae that is found in forests and woodlands of eastern Mexico. This species and the Lesson's motmot, Whooping motmot, Trinidad motmot, Amazonian motmot, and Andean motmot were all considered conspecific.
f: These birds often sit still, and in their dense forest habitat can be difficult to see, despite their size.

t: Lesson's motmot (Momotus lessonii) or the blue-diademed motmot, is a colorful bird found in forests and woodlands of southern Mexico to western Panama.
f: This species and the blue-capped motmot, whooping motmot, Trinidad motmot, Amazonian motmot, and Andean motmot were all considered conspecific.

t: The russet-crowned motmot (Momotus mexicanus) is a species of motmot native to north-western Mexico and central Guatemala. The russet-crowned motmot is the most understudied species of motmot in the family Momotidae. "Russet" refers to the reddish-brown colour of the bird's head and originates from the Latin russus meaning red.
f: It is a year-round resident of the tropical and subtropical dry broadleaf forests and scrubland.

t: The Amazonian motmot (Momotus momota) is a colorful coraciiform bird in the family Momotidae.
f: It is found in the Amazon lowlands and low Andean foothills from eastern Venezuela to eastern Brazil and northeastern Argentina.

t: The whooping motmot (Momotus subrufescens) is a colorful bird in the family Momotidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The chestnut-bellied monarch (Monarcha castaneiventris) or chestnut-bellied monarch-flycatcher is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.
f: It is endemic to the Solomon Islands.

t: The black-winged monarch (Monarcha frater) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Australia and on New Guinea.
The black-faced monarch (Monarcha melanopsis) is a passerine songbird in the family Monarchidae found along the eastern seaboard of Australia, and also New Guinea .

t: The White-capped monarch (Monarcha richardsii), or Richards' monarch, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae.
f: It is endemic to the Western Province in the Solomon Islands.

t: The black nunbird (Monasa atra) is a species of bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The yellow-billed nunbird (Monasa flavirostris) is a species of bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The white-fronted nunbird (Monasa morphoeus) is a species of bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds.
f: It is found Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The black-fronted nunbird (Monasa nigrifrons) is a species of bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: This species is found in the Palni Hills while another closely related form, the Ashambu laughingthrush (Montecincla meridionalis) with a shorter white brow is found in the high hills south of the Achankovil Gap and was treated as a subspecies. The two forms were together formerly treated as the Kerala laughingthrush.
f: The Palani laughingthrush (Montecincla fairbanki) is a species of laughingthrush endemic to the hills of the Western Ghats south of the Palghat Gap in Southern India.
The blue-capped rock thrush (Monticola cinclorhyncha) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae.

t: The white-throated rock thrush (Monticola gularis) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae of the order Passeriformes.
f: The bird's natural habitats include temperate forests.
The chestnut-bellied rock thrush (Monticola rufiventris) is a species of passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae.

t: The Cape rock thrush (Monticola rupestris) is a member of the bird family Muscicapidae. This rock thrush breeds in eastern and southern South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini.
f: The male Cape rock thrush has a whistled song tsee-tsee-tseet-chee-chweeeoo, and occasionally mimics other birds.

t: The common rock thrush (Monticola saxatilis), also known as the rufous-tailed rock thrush or simply rock thrush, is a species of chat that breeds in southern Europe across Central Asia to northern China. It is an uncommon visitor to northern Europe.
f: This species is strongly migratory, all populations wintering in Africa south of the Sahara.

t: The forest rock thrush (Monticola sharpei) is a songbird in the family Muscicapidae, formerly placed in the Turdidae together with the other chats. It now includes Benson's rock thrush and Amber Mountain rock thrush as subspecies.
f: The type locality is the forests east of Ambatondrazaka, which in turn lies south of Lake Alaotra.

t: The blue rock thrush (Monticola solitarius) is a species of chat. This thrush-like Old World flycatcher was formerly placed in the family Turdidae.
f: The blue rock thrush is the official national bird of Malta.

t: Blanford's snowfinch (Pyrgilauda blanfordi) or the plain-backed snowfinch, is a species of bird in the sparrow family. It is found in China, India, Nepal, and Pakistan.
f: The species epithet and common name commemorate the English zoologist William Thomas Blanford.

t: The white-winged snowfinch (Montifringilla nivalis) is a small passerine bird.
f: Despite its name, it is a sparrow rather than a true finch.

t: The white-rumped snowfinch (Onychostruthus taczanowskii) is a species of passerine bird in the sparrow family Passeridae. It is sometimes placed in the genus Montifringilla.
f: It is the only member of the genus Onychostruthus.

t: The lesser ground cuckoo (Morococcyx erythropygus) is a species of cuckoo in the tribe Neomorphini of subfamily Crotophaginae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: The barred hawk (Morphnarchus princeps) is a species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, and Peru.
f: It has also been known as the black-chested hawk.

t: The crested eagle (Morphnus guianensis) is a large neotropical eagle, the only member of the genus Morphnus. The crested eagle can grow up to 89 cm (35 in) long, with a wingspan up to 176 cm (69 in), and weigh up to 3 kg (6.6 lb).
f: A powerful predator, its diet consist mainly of small mammals, rodents, snakes and smaller birds.

t: The northern gannet (Morus bassanus) is a seabird, the largest species of the gannet family, Sulidae. It is native to the coasts of the North Atlantic Ocean, breeding in Western Europe and Northeastern North America.
f: Nesting takes place in colonies on both sides of the North Atlantic, the largest of which are at the Bass Rock (75,000 pairs as of 2014), St.

t: The Australasian gannet (Morus serrator), also known as the Australian gannet or tākapu, is a large seabird of the booby and gannet family, Sulidae. Adults are mostly white, with black flight feathers at the wingtips and lining the trailing edge of the wing.
f: Highly territorial when breeding, the Australasian gannet performs agonistic displays to defend its nest.
The African pied wagtail, or African wagtail, (Motacilla aguimp) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae.

t: The white wagtail (Motacilla alba) is a small passerine bird in the family Motacillidae, which also includes pipits and longclaws. The species breeds in the Palearctic zone in most of Europe and Asia and parts of North Africa; it also has a toehold in western Alaska as a scarce breeder.
f: It prefers bare areas for feeding, where it can see and pursue its prey.

t: The Cape wagtail (Motacilla capensis), also known as Wells's wagtail, is a small insectivorous bird which is widespread in southern Africa. It frequents water's edge, lawns and gardens.
f: It is a mostly resident, territorial species, but has been known to undertake limited altitudinal migration or form flocks outside of the breeding season.

t: The grey wagtail (Motacilla cinerea) is a member of the wagtail family, Motacillidae, measuring around 18–19 cm overall length. The species looks somewhat similar to the yellow wagtail but has the yellow on its underside restricted to the throat and vent.
f: The species is always associated with running water when breeding, although they may use man-made structures near streams for the nest.
The citrine wagtail (Motacilla citreola) is a small songbird in the family Motacillidae.
The mountain wagtail (Motacilla clara), also known as the long-tailed wagtail or grey-backed wagtail, is a species of wagtail of the family Motacillidae from sub-Saharan Africa.

t: The western yellow wagtail (Motacilla flava) is a small passerine bird in the wagtail family Motacillidae, which also includes the pipits and longclaws. This species breeds in much of temperate Europe and Asia.
f: Most populations are migratory, moving south to tropical Africa and southern Asia for the winter; the small population breeding in Egypt is however resident there.
The Madagascar wagtail (Motacilla flaviventris) is a species of wagtail in the family Motacillidae.

t: The Japanese wagtail (Motacilla grandis) is a species of bird in the pipit and wagtail family Motacillidae.
f: It is native to Japan and Korea.

t: The white-browed wagtail or large pied wagtail (Motacilla maderaspatensis) is a medium-sized bird and is the largest member of the wagtail family. They are conspicuously patterned with black above and white below, a prominent white brow, shoulder stripe and outer tail feathers.
f: White-browed wagtails are native to the Indian subcontinent, common near small water bodies and have adapted to urban environments where they often nest on roof tops.

t: The eastern yellow wagtail (Motacilla tschutschensis) is a small passerine in the wagtail family Motacillidae, which also includes the pipits and longclaws. It was formerly usually classified as a subspecies of the western yellow wagtail, but was split from it in 2003 when genetic data showed this classification to be paraphyletic with respect to the citrine wagtail.
f: It breeds in the eastern Palearctic and Alaska and migrates to South Asia and Australia.

t: The ashy woodpecker (Mulleripicus fulvus) is a species of bird in the woodpecker family Picidae. It is endemic to Sulawesi and surrounding islands in Indonesia.
f: They are assumed to be non-migratory, and can be found from sea level to 2,000 m (6,600 ft).The species is not uncommon and is considered secure for now.

t: The great slaty woodpecker (Mulleripicus pulverulentus) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. It is found across the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.
f: A unique and basically unmistakable bird, it is the largest confirmed living woodpecker species, behind the likely extinct imperial woodpecker and ivory-billed woodpecker.

t: The African dusky flycatcher (Muscicapa adusta), also known as the dusky-brown flycatcher or dusky alseonax, is a small passerine bird of the Old World flycatcher family, Muscicapidae. It is a resident breeder in elevated areas of Sub-Saharan Africa (including the Bié and Western High plateaus).
f: It is very common in its woodland habitat, which includes riverine forests, evergreen forest edges and clearings, especially near water bodies such as lakes, dams and streams, and well-wooded suburban gardens.

t: The swamp flycatcher or swamp alseonax (Muscicapa aquatica) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist shrubland and swamps.
f: Its range stretches east across the Sudan (region) and south towards Zambia.

t: The Asian brown flycatcher (Muscicapa dauurica) is a small passerine bird in the flycatcher family Muscicapidae. The specific dauurica refers to Dauria, an area of south-eastern Siberia named after a local nomadic tribe.
f: The word Muscicapa comes from the Latin musca, a fly and capere, to catch.

t: The ferruginous flycatcher (Muscicapa ferruginea) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is native to the eastern Himalayas, the Purvanchal Range and central/southern China ; it winters to Hainan and Southeast Asia.

t: The grey-streaked flycatcher or grey-spotted flycatcher (Muscicapa griseisticta) is a small passerine bird breeding in the eastern Palearctic belonging to the genus Muscicapa in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1861.
f: It is a vagrant to Singapore, Vietnam, Alaska and Australia.

t: The brown-breasted flycatcher or Layard's flycatcher (Muscicapa muttui) is a small passerine bird in the flycatcher family Muscicapidae. The species breeds in north eastern India, central and Southern China and northern Burma and Thailand, and migrates to southern India and Sri Lanka.
f: It forages for insects below the forest canopy, often close to the forest floor.

t: The dark-sided flycatcher (Muscicapa sibirica) is a small passerine bird belonging to the genus Muscicapa in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae. It is also known as the Siberian flycatcher or sooty flycatcher, the latter name is also used for the sooty flycatcher (Artomyias infuscata) of Africa.
f: It has a wide breeding distribution in the East Palearctic with northern birds migrating south for the winter.

t: The spotted flycatcher (Muscicapa striata) is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family. It breeds in most of Europe and in the Palearctic to Siberia, and is migratory, wintering in Africa and south western Asia.
f: This is an undistinguished looking bird with long wings and tail.

t: The brown-streaked flycatcher (Muscicapa williamsoni) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is found in southern Myanmar, southern Thailand, northern peninsular Malaysia, and northeast Borneo.
f: In 2020, a vagrant was sighted 300 km (190 mi) south of the Australian town of Broome and its identity was confirmed from DNA analysis of the droppings of the bird.

t: The short-tailed field tyrant (Muscigralla brevicauda) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Ecuador, Peru, and as a vagrant to Chile and Colombia.

t: The shear-tailed grey tyrant (Muscipipra vetula) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The white-browed ground tyrant (Muscisaxicola albilora) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Ecuador, and Peru, and as a vagrant to Colombia, Uruguay, and the Falkland Islands.

t: The spot-billed ground tyrant (Muscisaxicola maculirostris) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru and as a vagrant in Brazil.
Ross's turaco or Lady Ross's turaco (Tauraco rossae) is a mainly bluish-purple African bird of the turaco family, Musophagidae.

t: The ash-throated crake (Mustelirallus albicollis) is a species of bird in the subfamily Rallinae of the rail, crake, and coot family Rallidae.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile.

t: The paint-billed crake (Mustelirallus erythrops) is a species of bird in the subfamily Rallinae of the rail, crake, and coot family Rallidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The varied solitaire (Myadestes coloratus) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes.

The Cuban solitaire (Myadestes elisabeth), also known as the Cuban nightingale, is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes.

t: The rufous-throated solitaire (Myadestes genibarbis) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes.
f: It is found Jamaica, Hispaniola, and in the Lesser Antilles islands of Dominica, Martinique, St.

t: The black-faced solitaire (Myadestes melanops) is a bird in the thrush family endemic to highlands in Costa Rica and western Panama. This is a bird of dense undergrowth and bamboo clumps in wet mountain forest, normally from 750 to 3,000 m (2,460 to 9,840 ft) altitude.
f: The call is a nasal ghank or liquid quirt, and the song is a beautiful fluty whistled teedleedlee…tleedleeee…lee-dah…lee-dah given mainly in the evening from a shady canopy perch.

t: Population estimates approximate 170,000 birds, making it the most common of the Hawaiian thrushes.

t: The puaiohi (Myadestes palmeri) or small Kauaʻi thrush is a rare species of songbird in the thrush family, Turdidae, that is endemic to the Hawaiian island of Kauaʻi. It was first collected by Henry Palmer in 1891 at Halemanu around the entrance to the Kōkeʻe State Park.
f: It is closely related to the other three endemic Hawaiian thrushes, the kāmaʻo, olomaʻo, and ʻōmaʻo.

t: The Andean solitaire (Myadestes ralloides) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes.

Townsend's solitaire (Myadestes townsendi) is a medium-sized thrush, the only solitaire native to America north of Mexico.

t: The slate-colored solitaire (Myadestes unicolor) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes.
f: It is found in Belize, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: The collared grosbeak (Mycerobas affinis) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae. It is found in Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal and Thailand.
f: Its range encompasses the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent, mainly the Himalayas, along with some adjoining regions.

f: The Micronesian myzomela has a unique song at dawn—a continuous stream of trilled whistles and phrases, lasting for about 25 minutes on Kosrae, Yap, or Pohnpei, or a wheezy whistle on the Mariana Islands.

t: The Australian boobook (Ninox boobook), is a species of owl native to mainland Australia, southern New Guinea, the island of Timor, and the Sunda Islands. Described by John Latham in 1801, it was generally considered to be the same species as the morepork of New Zealand until 1999.
f: It is generally nocturnal, though sometimes it is active at dawn and dusk, retiring to roost in secluded spots in the foliage of trees.

t: The northern boobook (Ninox japonica) belongs to the family Strigidae (true owls) and is a raptorial owl endemic to eastern and southern countries of Asia. f: Despite being considered as the most common breeding owl in Japan, little research has been conducted on the species and subspecies and the taxonomic classification of N. j. totogo and N. j. japonica has been a subject of debate.

t: The morepork (Ninox novaeseelandiae), also known by its Māori name ruru, is a small brown owl found in New Zealand, the Australian islands of Norfolk Island, and formerly on Lord Howe Island. Its names (also including boobook and mopoke) are onomatopoeic, owing to the species’ distinctive calls.
f: As with all owls, the morepork has supreme night vision and excellent hearing, able to locate a tiny lizard or rodent from many metres above and away.

t: The Luzon boobook (Ninox philippensis) or Luzon hawk owl, also Philippine hawk owl or Philippine boobook, is a species of owl in the family Strigidae. It is endemic to the Philippines where it lives in forests.

t: The brown boobook (Ninox scutulata), also known as the brown hawk-owl, is a typical owl species. It is a resident breeder in India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, southern China and western Indonesia.

t: The powerful owl (Ninox strenua), a species of owl native to south-eastern and eastern Australia, is the largest owl on the continent. It is found in coastal areas and in the Great Dividing Range, rarely more than 200 km (120 mi) inland.
f: Such prey can comprise about three-quarters of their diet.

t: The Papuan boobook (Ninox theomacha), jungle boobook or jungle hawk owl, is a medium-sized, dark-colored owl. It has a dark gray-brown facial disk with lighter colored eyebrows, sooty or chocolate underparts, and mainly dark gray wings.
f: It lives mainly in lowland forests, montane forests, and submontane forests, mainly on the forests' edges.

t: The changeable hawk-eagle (Nisaetus cirrhatus) or crested hawk-eagle is a large bird of prey species of the family Accipitridae. More informal or antiquated English common names include the marsh hawk-eagle or Indian crested hawk-eagle.
f: It is a typical "hawk-eagle" in that it is an agile forest-dwelling predator and like many such eagles readily varies its prey selection between birds, mammals or reptiles as well as other vertebrates.

t: Wallace's hawk-eagle (Nisaetus nanus) is a species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. It is found in Kra Isthmus, Malay Peninsula, Sumatra and Borneo.
f: It is named after Alfred Russel Wallace, a British naturalist, explorer, geographer, anthropologist and biologist.

t: The mountain hawk-eagle (Nisaetus nipalensis) or Hodgson's hawk-eagle, is a large bird of prey native to Asia. The latter name is in reference to the naturalist, Brian Houghton Hodgson, who described the species after collecting one himself in the Himalayas.
f: As is typical of hawk-eagles, the mountain hawk-eagle is a forest dwelling opportunistic predator who readily varies its prey selection between birds, mammals and reptiles along with other vertebrates.

t: The brown nunlet (Nonnula brunnea) is a species of bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds.

t: The yellow-eared parrot (Ognorhynchus icterotis) is a vulnerable parrot found in the Andes of Colombia. It is currently enlisted as vulnerable on the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List.
f: It was thought to be extinct up until April 1999, when a group of researchers that were sponsored by ABC and Fundación Loro Parque, discovered a total of 81 individuals in the Colombian Andes.

t: The northern bentbill (Oncostoma cinereigulare) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Belize, Colombia, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The southern bentbill (Oncostoma olivaceum) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia and Panama.

t: The lunulated antbird (Oneillornis lunulatus) is a species of insectivorous bird in the subfamily Thamnophilinae of the family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The white-throated antbird (Oneillornis salvini) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil and Peru.

t: The red-winged starling (Onychognathus morio) is a bird of the starling family Sturnidae native to eastern and southern Africa from Ethiopia to South Africa.
f: An omnivorous, generalist species, it prefers cliffs and mountainous areas for nesting, and has moved into cities and towns due to similarity to its original habitat.

t: The pale-winged starling (Onychognathus nabouroup) is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae.
f: It is found in Angola, Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa.

t: The slender-billed starling (Onychognathus tenuirostris) is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae.
f: It is found in Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia.

t: Tristram's starling (Onychognathus tristramii), also known as Dead Sea starling or Tristram's grackle, is a species of starling native to the Middle East. It is the only member of the genus Onychognathus found mainly outside of Africa.
f: The species is named after Reverend Henry Baker Tristram, who collected natural history specimens.

t: Waller's starling (Onychognathus walleri) is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae. It is native to the Western High Plateau and Bioko, the Albertine Rift montane forests, the East African montane forests and the Eastern Arc forests.
f: The common name and scientific name commemorates the English naturalist Gerald Waller.

t: The Aleutian tern (Onychoprion aleuticus) is a migratory bird living in the subarctic region of the globe most of the year. It is frequently associated with the Arctic tern, which it closely resembles.
f: If its winter migratory range was completely unknown until the late 1980s; it is now known that many Aleutian terns spend the winter near the Equator in the western Pacific.

t: The bridled tern (Onychoprion anaethetus) is a seabird of the family Laridae. The scientific name is from Ancient Greek.
f: It is a bird of the tropical oceans.

t: The sooty tern (Onychoprion fuscatus) is a tern in the family Laridae.
f: It is a seabird of the tropical oceans and can fly for years at a time, skimming the sea surface for food, and returning to land only to breed, on islands throughout the equatorial zone.
The spectacled tern (Onychoprion lunatus), also known as the grey-backed tern, is a seabird in the family Laridae.

t: The tropical royal flycatcher (Onychorhynchus coronatus) is a passerine bird that most taxonomic systems place in family Onychorhynchidae.
f: It is found in Mexico, south through most of Central America, and in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The hoatzin ( WAHT-sin, -⁠seen; also HO-tsin and hoh-AT-sin) (Opisthocomus hoazin) is a species of tropical bird found in swamps, riparian forests, and mangroves of the Amazon and Orinoco Basins in South America. It is the only extant species in the genus Opisthocomus which is the only extant genus in the family Opisthocomidae under the order Opisthocomiformes.
f: It is unique among birds in possessing a digestive system that significantly supports the fermentation and the effective breakdown of plant matter, a trait more commonly known from herbivorous ungulate-ruminant mammals and some primates.
The Connecticut warbler (Oporornis agilis) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.
Orchelimum agile, the agile meadow katydid, is a species of meadow katydid in the family Tettigoniidae.

t: Orchelimum concinnum, known generally as stripe-faced meadow katydid, is a species of meadow katydid in the family Tettigoniidae. It is found in North America and the Caribbean.
f: Other common names include the red-faced meadow katydid and dusky-faced meadow katydid.
Orchelimum pulchellum, the handsome meadow katydid, is a species of meadow katydid in the family Tettigoniidae.
The brown tanager (Orchesticus abeillei) is a Near Threatened species of bird in th family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.

t: The tit berrypecker (Oreocharis arfaki) is a species of bird in the family Paramythiidae. First described by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1875, it is monotypic within the genus Oreocharis.
f: It is found in the New Guinea Highlands and more scarcely in northern parts of the island, in subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The crested bellbird (Oreoica gutturalis) is a medium-sized passerine bird in the family Oreoicidae. It is native to drier parts of Australia where its typical habitats are acacia scrublands, eucalypt woodlands, spinifex and saltbush plains, and dunes.
f: Sometimes a pair of birds duet.

t: The black-collared apalis (Oreolais pulcher) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. The black-collared apalis was formerly placed in the genus Apalis but was moved to the new genus Oreolais when Apalis was shown to be polyphyletic.
f: It is found in the Cameroonian Highlands forests, western Kenya and the Albertine rift montane forests.

t: The Rwenzori apalis or collared apalis (Oreolais ruwenzorii) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, and Uganda.

t: The ʻakikiki (pronounced ) (Oreomystis bairdi), also called the Kauaʻi creeper, is a critically endangered Hawaiian honeycreeper endemic to Kauaʻi, Hawaiʻi. It is the only member of the genus Oreomystis.
f: Of the Hawaiian birds known to be extant, it is thought to be the most endangered, with only 454 wild individuals reported as of 2018.

t: The horned guan (Oreophasis derbianus) is an endangered species in an ancient group of birds of the family Cracidae, which are related to the Australasian megapodes or mound builders (Megapodiidae).
f: It is found in Mexico, Guatemala, and possibly Honduras.

t: The tawny-throated dotterel (Oreopholus ruficollis) is a species of bird in the family Charadriidae, the plovers and their relatives.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Peru, and Uruguay.
The Bolivian blackbird (Oreopsar bolivianus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.

t: The mountain quail (Oreortyx pictus) is a small ground-dwelling bird in the New World quail family. This species is the only one in the genus Oreortyx, which is sometimes included in Callipepla.
f: This is not appropriate, however, as the mountain quail's ancestors diverged from other New World quails earlier than the bobwhites, no later than 6 mya.

t: The sage thrasher (Oreoscoptes montanus) is a medium-sized passerine bird in the family Mimidae. It is the only species in the genus Oreoscoptes and the smallest of the thrashers.
f: Sage thrashers are commonly found in shrubsteppe habitat and are strongly associated with sagebrush (Artemisia spp.) for which it relies on for nesting.

t: The fernwren (Oreoscopus gutturalis) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is monotypic within the genus Oreoscopus.
f: It is endemic to northern Queensland in Australia.
The orange-crowned warbler (Leiothlypis celata) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.

t: It is sometimes placed in the genera Vermivora and Parula.
f: The flame-throated warbler (Oreothlypis gutturalis) is a small New World warbler.

t: The Tennessee warbler (Leiothlypis peregrina) is a New World warbler that breeds in eastern North America and winters in southern Central America, the Caribbean, and northern South America.
f: The specific name peregrina is from Latin peregrinus "wanderer".

t: The Nashville warbler (Leiothlypis ruficapilla) is a small songbird in the New World warbler family, found in North and Central America. It has a gray head and a green back, and its underparts are yellow and white.
f: It breeds in parts of the northern and western United States and southern Canada, and migrates to winter in southern California and Texas, Mexico, and the north of Central America.

t: The crescent-chested warbler (Oreothlypis superciliosa) is a small New World warbler.
f: It is common throughout its montane range, from northern Mexico to northern Nicaragua, and is an occasional vagrant to Arizona and Texas.

t: In spite of its common name, it is neither a tanager nor a finch, but a New World sparrow, having been moved to that family after variously being placed in either the Emberizidae or the true tanager family Thraupidae. It is the only species in the monotypic genus Oreothraupis.
f: The tanager finch (Oreothraupis arremonops) is a songbird species.

t: The Andean hillstar (Oreotrochilus estella) is a species of hummingbird in the "coquettes", tribe Lesbiini of subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.

t: The Orinoco goose (Neochen jubata) is a species of waterfowl in the tribe Tadornini of subfamily Anserinae.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile, French Guiana, Suriname, and Uruguay.

t: The Andean goose (Chloephaga melanoptera) is a species of waterfowl in tribe Tadornini of subfamily Anserinae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.

t: The African golden oriole (Oriolus auratus), or African oriole, is a member of the oriole family of passerine birds which is a resident breeder in Africa south of the Sahara desert. It is a bird of thick bush and other well-wooded areas.
f: The hanging basket-shaped nest is built in a tree, and contains two eggs.

t: The western oriole (Oriolus brachyrynchus), or western black-headed oriole, is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae that is native to Africa. It is rated as a species of least concern on the International Union for Conservation of Nature Red List of Endangered Species.
f: The adult upperparts are yellow-olive, and the underparts are yellow in colour.

t: The black-naped oriole (Oriolus chinensis) is a passerine bird in the oriole family that is found in many parts of Asia. There are several distinctive populations within the wide distribution range of this species and in the past the slender-billed oriole (Oriolus tenuirostris) was included as a subspecies.
f: Unlike the Indian golden oriole which only has a short and narrow eye-stripe, the black-naped oriole has the stripe broadening and joining at the back of the neck.
The green-headed oriole (Oriolus chlorocephalus), or montane oriole, is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae.

t: The Javan oriole (Oriolus cruentus) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae. It is found on Java in Indonesia where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: Temuan people believe that its song brings bad luck.
The green oriole or Australasian yellow oriole (Oriolus flavocinctus) is an inconspicuous inhabitant of lush tropical vegetation throughout Australia and New Guinea.

t: The Indian golden oriole (Oriolus kundoo) is a species of oriole found in the Indian subcontinent and Central Asia. The species was formerly considered to be a subspecies of the Eurasian golden oriole, but is now considered a full species.
f: Adults can be told apart from the Eurasian golden oriole by the black of the eye stripe extending behind the eye.

t: The black-headed oriole (Oriolus larvatus) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae.
f: It is found in Africa and has a very striking appearance with a bright yellow body, contrasting black head and flesh-coloured beak.

t: The Ethiopian oriole (Oriolus monacha) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae.
f: It is found in north-eastern Africa where its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry forests.

t: The black-winged oriole (Oriolus nigripennis) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.
f: It is found in Africa from Sierra Leone and Liberia to southern South Sudan, western Uganda, central Democratic Republic of Congo and north-western Angola.
It is a summer migrant in Europe and the Palearctic and spends the winter season in central and southern Africa.

t: The mountain oriole (Oriolus percivali) is a bird species in the family Oriolidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is native to the Albertine Rift montane forests, Uganda and Kenya.

t: The dusky-brown oriole (Oriolus phaeochromus) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae.It is endemic to North Maluku. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: Alternate names for the dusky-brown oriole include the dusky oriole, Gray's oriole, Halmahera oriole and Moluccan oriole.

t: The olive-backed oriole (Oriolus sagittatus), or white-bellied oriole, is a very common medium-sized passerine bird native to northern and eastern Australia and south-central New Guinea.
f: The most wide-ranging of the Australasian orioles, it is noisy and conspicuous.

t: The Philippine oriole (Oriolus steerii) or grey-throated oriole is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae. Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is endemic to the Philippine found on Mindanao and most of the Visayan Islands.

t: The brown oriole (Oriolus szalayi) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.
f: Alternate names for the brown oriole include the New Guinea oriole and striated oriole.

t: The slender-billed oriole (Oriolus tenuirostris) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae found from the eastern Himalayas to Southeast Asia.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
The maroon oriole (Oriolus traillii) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae.

t: The dark-throated oriole (Oriolus xanthonotus) is a species of bird in the family Oriolidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests where it is threatened by habitat loss.
f: It is found in Southeast Asia through the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Bangka), Java and southwestern Borneo.

t: The black-hooded oriole (Oriolus xanthornus) is a member of the oriole family of passerine birds and is a resident breeder in tropical southern Asia from India and Sri Lanka east to Indonesia. It is a bird of open woodland and cultivation.
f: The nest is built in a tree, and contains two eggs.
The striped sparrow (Oriturus superciliosus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

t: The brown-capped tyrannulet (Ornithion brunneicapillus) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, and Venezuela and reported for the first time in Nicaragua in 2011.

t: The white-lored tyrannulet (Ornithion inerme) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The yellow-bellied tyrannulet (Ornithion semiflavum) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Belize, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, and Panama.
Hapithus saltator, the jumping bush cricket, is a species of cricket in the family Gryllidae.

t: The pale-footed swallow (Orochelidon flavipes) is a species of bird in the family Hirundinidae. It is found in the northern Andes, from Venezuela to Bolivia.
f: They are usually seen in small flocks, occasionally with the blue-and-white swallow.

t: The brown-bellied swallow (Orochelidon murina) is a species of bird in the family Hirundinidae, the swallows and martins.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The East Brazilian chachalaca (Ortalis araucuan) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is endemic to eastern Brazil.

t: The Chaco chachalaca (Ortalis canicollis) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and possibly Uruguay.

t: The grey-headed chachalaca (Ortalis cinereiceps) is a member of an ancient group of birds in the family Cracidae, which includes chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found from Honduras to Colombia.

t: The Colombian chachalaca (Ortalis columbiana) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae. It is endemic to the forests and woodlands in the inter-Andean valleys in Colombia.
f: The large seeds they disperse through defecation support the maintenance of diverse tropical forests.

t: The rufous-headed chachalaca (Ortalis erythroptera) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
The chestnut-winged chachalaca (Ortalis garrula) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.

t: The speckled chachalaca (Ortalis guttata) is a medium-sized bird belonging to the family Cracidae (chachalacas, guans, and curassows). The two Amazonian subspecies are generally common and inhabit low or open forest, thickets, and riparian areas.
f: This species is found across the Amazonian regions of Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The white-bellied chachalaca (Ortalis leucogastra) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: The little chachalaca (Ortalis motmot) is a bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Suriname, Guyana, Venezuela and possibly Colombia.
The West Mexican chachalaca (Ortalis poliocephala) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.

t: The rufous-vented chachalaca (Ortalis ruficauda) is a member of an ancient group of birds of the family Cracidae, which are related to the Australasian mound builders.
f: It is also found on Bequia and Union Island in the Grenadines where it may have been introduced.
The scaled chachalaca (Ortalis squamata) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.

t: The plain chachalaca (Ortalis vetula) is a large bird in the chachalaca, guan and curassow family Cracidae. It breeds in tropical and subtropical environments from mezquital thickets in the Rio Grande Valley in southernmost Texas, United States to northernmost Costa Rica.
f: It also produces peeping whistles and cackles.

t: The rufous-bellied chachalaca (Ortalis wagleri) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
