f: It is endemic to western Mexico.
The olive-green tanager (Orthogonys chloricterus) is a species of bird in the family Mitrospingidae.

t: The Papuan logrunner or New Guinea logrunner (Orthonyx novaeguineae) is a species of bird in the family Orthonychidae.
f: It was formerly considered conspecific with the Australian logrunner.
The chowchilla (Orthonyx spaldingii) is a passerine bird in the family Orthonychidae.

t: Until 2002, it was widely considered to be conspecific with the New Guinea logrunner, but studies showed the two differ significantly, both genetically and vocally.
f: It is known by a number of common names including spine-tailed logrunner, spine-tail, logrunner, scrub quail and chowcilla.

t: The red-bellied macaw (Orthopsittaca manilatus), also known as Guacamaya manilata, is a medium-sized, mostly green parrot, a member of a group of large Neotropical parrots known as macaws. The belly has a large maroon patch which gives the species its name.
f: It is the largest of what are commonly called "mini-macaws".

t: Formerly placed in the "Old World warbler" assemblage, it is now placed in the family Cisticolidae. It is found in Bangladesh, Northeast India and Southeast Asia.
f: The dark-necked tailorbird (Orthotomus atrogularis) is a songbird species.

t: The Cambodian tailorbird (Orthotomus chaktomuk) is a species of bird endemic to Cambodia, likely confined to a single dense shrub habitat in the floodplain of the Mekong river. It was first discovered and recorded by scientists in 2009 in Phnom Penh, the capital of Cambodia, during avian influenza checks.
f: In 2013, it was determined to be a unique species and formally described.

t: The green-backed tailorbird (Orthotomus chloronotus), also known as the trilling tailorbird, is a species of bird formerly placed in the "Old World warbler" assemblage, but now placed in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forests, tropical mangrove forests and secondary growth.
f: The bird is endemic to the Philippines on the Northern side of the island of Luzon.

t: The gray-backed tailorbird (Orthotomus derbianus) is a species of bird formerly placed in the "Old World warbler" assemblage, but now placed in the family Cisticolidae.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines and found only on the islands of Luzon and Catanduanes.

t: The rufous-fronted tailorbird (Orthotomus frontalis) is a species of bird formerly placed in the Old World warbler assemblage, but now placed in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forests and tropical mangrove forests.
f: It is native to the southern and eastern Philippines.

t: The black-headed tailorbird (Orthotomus nigriceps), also known as the white-browed tailorbird, is a species of songbird in the cisticola family, Cisticolidae. First formally described by the Scottish ornithologist Arthur Hay in 1877, it is endemic to the southeastern Philippines, where it is found on the islands of Mindanao, Dinagat, and Siargao.
f: It feeds on small invertebrates.
The ashy tailorbird (Orthotomus ruficeps) is a species of songbird from Southeast Asia, formerly placed in the "Old World warbler" assemblage, it but now placed in the family Cisticolidae.

t: The olive-backed tailorbird (Orthotomus sepium) is a species of passerine bird formerly placed in the "Old World warbler" assemblage, it but now placed in the family Cisticolidae. It resides in open forests, often perching on short trees and shrubs.
f: It is endemic to the islands of Java, Madura Island, Bali and Lombok.

t: The rufous-tailed tailorbird (Orthotomus sericeus) is a species of bird formerly placed in the "Old World warbler" assemblage, it but now placed in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The common tailorbird (Orthotomus sutorius) is a songbird found across tropical and subtropical Asia. Popular for its nest made of leaves "sewn" together and immortalized by Rudyard Kipling as Darzee in his Jungle Book, it is a common resident in urban gardens.
f: Tailorbirds get their name from the way their nest is constructed.

t: The grey francolin (Ortygornis pondicerianus) is a species of francolin found in the plains and drier parts of the Indian subcontinent and Iran. This species was formerly also called the grey partridge, not to be confused with the European grey partridge.
f: The term teetar can also refer to other partridges and quails.

t: The crested francolin (Ortygornis sephaena) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae. One of its subspecies, Ortygornis sephaena rovuma, is sometimes considered a separate species, Kirk's francolin.
f: It is found in southern Africa.

t: The black-faced quailfinch (Ortygospiza atricollis atricollis), is a common subspecies of estrildid finch found in western and central of Africa.
f: Some taxonomists consider it to be conspecific with the African quailfinch, others consider all three species to be conspecific.

t: The pheasant pigeon (Otidiphaps nobilis) is a species of large terrestrial pigeon. It is the only species of the monotypic genus Otidiphaps.
f: It ranges primarily over hilly and lower mountain areas, but can also be found in lowlands.

t: The Chinese thrush (Turdus mupinensis) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. Its natural habitats are temperate forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in China and far northern Vietnam.
The Indian scops owl (Otus bakkamoena) is a species of owl native to South Asia.
The Cyprus scops owl (Otus cyprius) is a small owl endemic to Cyprus.

t: The Ryukyu scops owl (Ryūkyū scops owl) or elegant scops owl (Otus elegans) is a small rufous-brown owl with a brown face disk and a cinnamon facial ruff. The bill is olive-grey and it has yellow eyes.
f: Occasionally traces of their nests can be found in man-made constructions such as drainage holes or toilets' water tanks.
The Sunda scops owl (Otus lempiji) is a small brown owl native to the Sunda Islands.

t: The collared scops owl (Otus lettia) is an owl which is a resident breeder in south Asia from northern Pakistan, northern India, Nepal, Bangladesh, the Himalayas east to southern China, and Taiwan. It is partially migratory, with some birds wintering in India, Sri Lanka and Malaysia.
f: This species is nocturnal but it can often be located by the small birds that mob it while it is roosting in a tree.

t: The Madagascar scops owl (Otus rutilus), also known as the Malagasy scops owl, is a species of owl in the family Strigidae. It is found throughout Madagascar, now that it has recently been lumped with the Torotoroka scops owl (O. r. madagascariensis), previously considered a separate species.
f: The nominate O. r. rutilus is referred to as the rainforest scops owl.

t: The Moluccan scops owl (Otus magicus) is an owl found in the Maluku and Lesser Sunda Islands of Indonesia. It has spiritual significance to the Pesaguan Dayak people.
f: It closely resembles the Rinjani scops owl.

t: The Banggai scops owl (Otus mendeni) was formerly considered conspecific, but was split as a distinct species by the IOC in 2021.
f: The Sulawesi scops owl (Otus manadensis) is an owl found on the Sulawesi island of Indonesia.

t: The Mantanani scops owl (Otus mantananensis), is a small owl in the scops-owl genus Otus found on small islands between Borneo and the Philippines.
f: It is listed by the IUCN as "near threatened" because its range is limited with its population being fragmented on several different islands, and its forest habitat is being degraded by ongoing logging and clearance.

t: The Arabian scops owl (Otus pamelae) is a small owl endemic to Saudi Arabia, Oman, and Yemen.
f: The current population of the species is estimated to be about 60,000 individuals.
The reddish scops owl (Otus rufescens) is an owl found in southeast Asia, in the countries of Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Brunei.

t: The Madagascar scops owl (Otus rutilus), also known as the Malagasy scops owl, is a species of owl in the family Strigidae. It is found throughout Madagascar, now that it has recently been lumped with the Torotoroka scops owl (O. r. madagascariensis), previously considered a separate species.
f: The nominate O. r. rutilus is referred to as the rainforest scops owl.

t: The white-fronted scops owl (Otus sagittatus) is a small Asian owl in the family Strigidae. It has a declining population about which little is known, and is dependent on lowland and foothill forests which are rapidly being destroyed.
f: The first is that it can puff up its feathers to triple its body size.

t: The Eurasian scops owl (Otus scops), also known as the European scops owl, common scops owl or just scops owl, is a small owl in the typical owl family Strigidae. Its breeding range extends from southern Europe eastwards to southern Siberia and the western Himalayas.
f: It is migratory, wintering in Africa south of the Sahara, although it is resident year-round in parts of Mediterranean Europe.

t: The Japanese scops-owl (Otus semitorques) is a small owl species in the family Strigidae, or true owl family. It is a member of the genus Otus, the scops owl genus.
f: They nest in tree hollows and raise a small brood.
The African scops owl (Otus senegalensis) is a small owl which is widespread in sub-Saharan Africa.

t: The mountain scops owl (Otus spilocephalus), sometimes referred to as the spotted scops owl, is a species of owl in the family Strigidae. Its range extends across much of south and southeast Asia, from Pakistan and the Himalayas in the northwest, through Taiwan, Thailand and Malaysia in the east and south.
f: The owls have a short high-pitched call like a two-note whistle, "plew-plew" or "he-he", although the female's songs are rarely heard.
The oriental scops owl (Otus sunia) is a scops owl species native to South and Southeast Asia.

t: The white-throated oxylabes (Oxylabes madagascariensis) is a species of passerine bird that is endemic to Madagascar. Formerly considered as a member of the Old World warbler family Sylviidae, it has been moved to the family Bernieridae — the Malagasy warblers.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Oxylabes.

t: The sharpbill (Oxyruncus cristatus) is a small passerine bird that is placed in its own family Oxyruncidae. It was formerly placed in the family Tityridae.
f: Their diet consists of primarily of fruit, but they will also take insects, hanging upside down in from twigs to obtain insect larvae.

t: It was considered a subspecies of the ruddy duck. In fact, some taxonomic authorities still consider it conspecific, including the American Ornithological Society.
f: The Andean duck (Oxyura ferruginea) is a bird species native to the Andean Mountains of South America, one of the stiff-tailed ducks.

t: The ruddy duck (Oxyura jamaicensis) is a species of duck, one of six extant species of stiff-tailed duck (genus Oxyura). In the 1940s, the ruddy duck was introduced to the United Kingdom, where it established a population.
f: The generic name is derived from Ancient Greek oxus meaning "sharp", and oura meaning "tail".

t: The goldenface (Pachycare flavogriseum) is a species of passerine bird endemic to New Guinea.
f: It is the only species (monotypic) within the genus Pachycare.

t: The Melanesian whistler (Pachycephala chlorura) or Vanuatu whistler, is a species of passerine bird in the whistler family Pachycephalidae.
f: It is found on the Loyalty Islands, Vanuatu, and Vanikoro in the far south-eastern Solomons.
The mangrove whistler (Pachycephala cinerea) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae found in South-east Asia.

t: The Samoan whistler (Pachycephala flavifrons), also known as the yellow-fronted whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.
f: It is endemic to Samoa, where it is found in forest, plantations and gardens.

t: The Australian golden whistler (Pachycephala pectoralis) or golden whistler, is a species of passerine bird in the family Pachycephalidae. It is found in forest, woodland, mallee, mangrove and scrub in Australia (except the interior and most of the north).
f: Most populations are resident, but some in south-eastern Australia migrate north during the winter.

t: The Tenggara whistler (Pachycephala calliope, previously Pachycephala fulvotincta), also known as the fulvous-tinted whistler and the rusty-breasted whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.
f: It is endemic to Indonesia, where it ranges from Java east to Alor and north to the Selayar Islands.

t: The drab whistler (Pachycephala griseonota) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in the Maluku Islands.

t: The white-vented whistler (Pachycephala homeyeri) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae. Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forest and tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in the southern Philippines and a few islands of Malaysia.

t: The Bornean whistler (Pachycephala hypoxantha) or Bornean mountain whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.
f: It is endemic to the island of Borneo.
Gilbert's whistler (Pachycephala inornata) is a monotypic species of bird endemic to Australia, scattered in semi-arid zones of southern Australia.

t: The white-breasted whistler (Pachycephala lanioides) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.
f: Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.

t: The yellow-throated whistler (Pachycephala macrorhyncha), or Banda Sea whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae. It is endemic to central and south-eastern Wallacea, where it ranges from Timor east to the Tanimbars and north to Seram and Banggai .
f: The oriole whistler is sometimes alternatively called the yellow-throated whistler, leading to confusion between both species.
The black-chinned whistler (Pachycephala mentalis) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae, endemic to Halmahera and adjacent smaller islands in North Maluku in Indonesia.

t: The bare-throated whistler (Pachycephala nudigula) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.
f: It is endemic to the Lesser Sundas.
The olive whistler (Pachycephala olivacea) or olivaceous whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae, the whistlers, that is native to southeastern Australia.

The oriole whistler (Pachycephala orioloides), also known as the yellow-throated whistler (leading to easy confusion with Pachycephala macrorhyncha), is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae, which is endemic to the Solomon Islands (archipelago).

t: The Australian golden whistler (Pachycephala pectoralis) or golden whistler, is a species of passerine bird in the family Pachycephalidae. It is found in forest, woodland, mallee, mangrove and scrub in Australia (except the interior and most of the north).
f: Most populations are resident, but some in south-eastern Australia migrate north during the winter.

t: The yellow-bellied whistler (Pachycephala philippinensis), or Philippine whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae that is endemic to the Philippines.
f: Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forest and the lower reaches tropical moist montane forest.

t: The rufous whistler (Pachycephala rufiventris) is a species of whistler found in New Caledonia and Australia. Like many other members of the Pachycephalidae, it has a variety of musical calls.
f: Predominantly a reddish-brown and grey bird, it makes up for its subdued plumage with its song-making ability.

t: The regent whistler (Pachycephala schlegelii) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is endemic to the highlands of New Guinea.

t: The grey whistler (Pachycephala simplex) or brown whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest.
f: It is found in northern Australia and New Guinea.

t: Sclater's whistler (Pachycephala soror) or the hill golden whistler, is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae found in the highlands of New Guinea. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: The name commemorates the British zoologist Philip Lutley Sclater.

t: The sulphur-vented whistler or sulphur-bellied whistler (Pachycephala sulfuriventer) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae. It is endemic to Sulawesi in Indonesia.
f: Alternate names for the sulphur-vented whistler include the Celebes mountain whistler, Celebes whistler and yellow-vented whistler.

t: The white-throated Fiji whistler (Pachycephala vitiensis) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae, endemic to islands in southern Fiji. Before the split the combined species were known as the "Fiji whistler".
f: It was formerly considered to be conspecific with the yellow-throated Fiji whistler (Pachycephala graeffii).

t: The compact weaver (Pachyphantes superciliosus) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae. It has a highly discontinuous distribution from Senegal to Liberia, east to Ethiopia and south to Angola and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Pachyphantes.

t: The rose-throated becard (Pachyramphus aglaiae) is a medium-sized passerine bird in the family Tityridae. It breeds from southeasternmost Arizona and extreme southern Texas in the United States and across Central America to western Panama.
f: Breeding typically begins in May, with three to six eggs being laid in a domed nest suspended from a high tree branch.

t: The black-and-white becard (Pachyramphus albogriseus) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: Sources differ on its range; all agree it is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Panama, and Venezuela and some add Ecuador and Peru.

t: The chestnut-crowned becard (Pachyramphus castaneus) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Paraguay, and Venezuela.

t: The cinnamon becard (Pachyramphus cinnamomeus) is a passerine bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Mexico, in every Central American country except El Salvador, and in Colombia, Ecuador, and Venezuela.

t: The one-colored becard (Pachyramphus homochrous) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The grey-collared becard (Pachyramphus major) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies. It is found in Belize, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.
f: It has also occurred as a vagrant in Arizona and Texas.

t: The black-capped becard (Pachyramphus marginatus) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The pink-throated becard (Pachyramphus minor) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
The Jamaican becard (Pachyramphus niger) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.

t: The white-winged becard (Pachyramphus polychopterus) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in every Central American country except El Salvador, on Trinidad and Tobago, and in every mainland South American country except Chile.

t: The cinereous becard (Pachyramphus rufus) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Peru, Suriname, Venezuela, and possibly Ecuador.

t: The glossy-backed becard (Pachyramphus surinamus) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The crested becard (Pachyramphus validus), also known as the plain becard, is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, and possibly Ecuador.

t: The barred becard (Pachyramphus versicolor) is a small passerine bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, and in South America from Venezuela to Bolivia.

t: The green-backed becard (Pachyramphus viridis) is a species of passerine bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies. The green-backed becard includes the yellow-cheeked becard as a subspecies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Guyana, Paraguay, Uruguay, and Venezuela.

t: The golden-fronted greenlet (Pachysylvia aurantiifrons) is a small passerine bird in the family Vireonidae, the vireos, greenlets, and shrike-babblers.
f: It is found in Panama, Colombia, Venezuela, and Trinidad.

t: The lesser greenlet (Pachysylvia decurtata) is a small passerine bird in the family Vireonidae, the vireos, greenlets, and shrike-babblers.
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The dusky-capped greenlet (Pachysylvia hypoxantha) is a species of bird in the family Vireonidae, the vireos, greenlets, and shrike-babblers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The buff-cheeked greenlet (Pachysylvia muscicapina) is a species of bird in the family Vireonidae, the vireos, greenlets, and shrike-babblers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The rufous-naped greenlet (Pachysylvia semibrunnea) is a species of bird in the family Vireonidae, the vireos, greenlets, and shrike-babblers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Venezuela.

t: The Java sparrow (Padda oryzivora; syn. Lonchura oryzivora), also known as the Java finch, Java rice sparrow or Java rice bird, is a small passerine bird.
f: It is a popular cage bird, and has been introduced into many other countries.

t: The ʻākohekohe (Palmeria dolei), or crested honeycreeper, is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper. It is endemic to the island of Maui in Hawaiʻi.
f: The ʻākohekohe is susceptible to mosquito‐transmitted avian malaria (Plasmodium relictum) and only breeds in high‐elevation wet forests (> 1,715 m or 5,630 ft).

t: The wedge-tailed sabrewing (Pampa curvipennis) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae. Two subspecies have sometimes been treated as separate species, the curve-winged sabrewing and the long-tailed sabrewing.
f: It is found in Belize, Guatemala, Mexico, and possibly Honduras.

t: The osprey (Pandion haliaetus; ), historically known as sea hawk, river hawk, and fish hawk, is a diurnal, fish-eating bird of prey with a cosmopolitan range. It is a large raptor, reaching more than 60 cm (24 in) in length and a wingspan of 180 cm (71 in).
f: It has specialised physical characteristics and unique behaviour in hunting its prey, which consists almost exclusively of fish.

t: The fiery-throated hummingbird (Panterpe insignis) is a species of hummingbird in the "mountain gems" tribe Lampornithini in subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The bearded reedling (Panurus biarmicus) is a small, long-tailed passerine bird found in reed beds near water in the temperate zone of Eurasia. It is frequently known as the bearded tit or occasionally as bearded parrotbill, as historically it was believed to be closely related to either the tits or parrotbills.
f: They are highly productive and can breed several times in a season.

t: The great swallow-tailed swift (Panyptila sanctihieronymi) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: The white-rumped hawk (Parabuteo leucorrhous) is a species of bird of prey in subfamily Accipitrinae, the "true" hawks, of family Accipitridae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: Parabuteo unicinctus is a medium-large bird of prey that breeds from the southwestern United States south to Chile, central Argentina, and Brazil. It contains two subspecies, the Harris's hawk (P. u. harrisi) and the bay-winged hawk (P. u. unicinctus).
f: Harris's hawk is notable for its behavior of hunting cooperatively in packs consisting of tolerant groups, while other raptors often hunt alone.

t: The maroon-chested ground dove (Paraclaravis mondetoura) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is native to the American Cordillera of Central and South America.
The lesser bird-of-paradise (Paradisaea minor) is a bird-of-paradise in the genus Paradisaea.
The red bird-of-paradise (Paradisaea rubra), also called the cendrawasih merah, is a bird-of-paradise in the genus Paradisaea, family Paradisaeidae.

t: The black-breasted parrotbill (Paradoxornis flavirostris) is a 19 cm (7.5 in) long, large, thick-billed parrotbill with black patches on the head-sides and throat.
f: Formerly placed in the family Sylviidae, the parrotbills are now considered a distinct family, the Paradoxornithidae, following Cai et al. (2019).

t: The spot-breasted parrotbill (Paradoxornis guttaticollis) is a species of bird in the family Paradoxornithidae.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The spotted pardalote (Pardalotus punctatus) is a small passerine bird native to eastern and southern Australia, at elevations of up to 2,000 metres (6,600 ft). It is part of the pardalote family, Pardalotidae.
f: Also occasionally found nesting in burrows in semi-rainforest areas inland from the coast in Mid North Coast NSW.

t: The red-browed pardalote (Pardalotus rubricatus) is a small brightly coloured insectivorous passerine, endemic to Australia (Schodde & Mason 1999). The Latin word rubricatus means 'red-ochred' which is descriptive of their orange-red eyebrow (Higgins & Peter 2002).
f: A gleaning specialist, they forage primarily in eucalypt trees (Woinarski 1984).

t: Other common names include pickwick, wittachew and chip-chip. It is a very small, short-tailed bird that is more often heard than seen, foraging noisily for lerps and other small creatures in the treetops.
f: The striated pardalote (Pardalotus striatus) is the least colourful and most common of the four pardalote species.

t: The spotted rail (Pardirallus maculatus) is a species of bird in the subfamily Rallinae of the rail, crake, and coot family Rallidae.
f: It is found in Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, and South America.

t: The blackish rail (Pardirallus nigricans) is a species of bird in the subfamily Rallinae of the rail, crake, and coot family Rallidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, Venezuela, and possibly Bolivia.

t: The plumbeous rail (Pardirallus sanguinolentus) is a species of bird in the subfamily Rallinae of the rail, crake, and coot family Rallidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru and Uruguay.

t: The yellow-shouldered grosbeak (Parkerthraustes humeralis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The Louisiana waterthrush (Parkesia motacilla) is a New World warbler, that breeds in eastern North America and winters in the West Indies and Central America. The habitats it prefers are streams and their surroundings, and other wet areas.
f: Plain brown above, it is white below, with black streaks and with buff flanks and undertail, distinguishing it from the closely related northern waterthrush.

t: The northern waterthrush (Parkesia noveboracensis) is a species of ground-feeding migratory New World warbler of the genus Parkesia. It breeds in the northern part of North America, in Alaska, Canada, and the northern United States; it winters in Florida, Central America, the West Indies, Venezuela, Colombia, and Ecuador.
f: It is a rare vagrant to other South American countries and to western Europe.

t: The yellow-billed cardinal (Paroaria capitata) is a bird species in the tanager family (Thraupidae). It occurs in Brazil, Paraguay, Bolivia, Uruguay, and northern Argentina and has been introduced on the island of Hawaiʻi.
f: It is not very closely related to the cardinals proper (Cardinalidae).

t: The red-crested cardinal (Paroaria coronata) is a passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. Notwithstanding its similar name, this bird is not closely related to the true cardinal family Cardinalidae.
f: It is sometimes known as the Brazilian cardinal.

t: The red-cowled cardinal (Paroaria dominicana) is a bird species in the tanager family (Thraupidae). It occurs in a wide range of dry to semi-humid open to semi-open habitats in north-eastern Brazil, especially the Caatinga region.
f: It is not very closely related to the cardinals proper (Cardinalidae).
The red-capped cardinal (Paroaria gularis) is a small species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae.

t: The Maui ʻalauahio (Paroreomyza montana), also known as the Maui Nui ʻalauahio or Maui creeper, is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper. It is endemic to Maui Nui, Hawaii.
f: The common name refers to both groups.

t: The cinereous tit or Asian tit (Parus cinereus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae. This species is made up of several populations that were earlier treated as subspecies of the great tit (Parus major).
f: These birds are grey backed with white undersides.

t: The great tit (Parus major) is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is widespread and common throughout Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia and as far east as the Amur River.
f: The great tit has adapted well to human-induced environmental changes and is a common and familiar bird in urban parks and gardens.

t: The cinereous tit or Asian tit (Parus cinereus) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae. This species is made up of several populations that were earlier treated as subspecies of the great tit (Parus major).
f: These birds are grey backed with white undersides.

t: The green-backed tit (Parus monticolus) is a species of bird in the family Paridae. Its natural habitats are boreal forest, temperate forest, and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Taiwan and Vietnam.

t: It is a small lorikeet distinguished by a purple crown, an orange forehead and ear-coverts, and a light blue chin and chest.
f: The purple-crowned lorikeet (Psitteuteles porphyrocephalus),  is a lorikeet found in scrub and mallee of southern Australia.

t: The little lorikeet (Psitteuteles pusillus) is a species of parrot in the family Psittaculidae. It is a small parrot, predominantly green in plumage with a red face.
f: Its natural habitats are temperate eucalyptus forest and woodland, subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

t: The saxaul sparrow (Passer ammodendri) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family (Passeridae), found in parts of Central Asia. At 14–16 centimetres (5.5–6.3 in) and 25–32 grams (0.88–1.13 oz), it is among the larger range of sparrows.
f: Vocalisations include a comparatively soft and musical chirping call, a song, and a flight call.

t: The russet sparrow (Passer cinnamomeus), also called the cinnamon or cinnamon tree sparrow, is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae. A chunky little seed-eating bird with a thick bill, it has a body length of 14 to 15 cm (5.5–5.9 in).
f: The male chooses the nest site before finding a mate and uses the nest for courtship display.

t: The southern grey-headed sparrow (Passer diffusus) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae. It is sometimes treated as a subspecies of the grey-headed sparrow.
f: It is found in savanna and woodland in Angola and Zambia southwards into South Africa, where it is expanding its range and is kept as a caged bird, like its relative the white-rumped seedeater.

t: The house sparrow (Passer domesticus) is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in most parts of the world. It is a small bird that has a typical length of 16 cm (6.3 in) and a mass of 24–39.5 g (0.85–1.39 oz).
f: The house sparrow is strongly associated with human habitation, and can live in urban or rural settings.

t: Its range spans from Myanmar to central Vietnam, and south to the western part of Peninsular Malaysia.
f: The plain-backed sparrow (Passer flaveolus), also called the Pegu sparrow or olive-backed sparrow, is a sparrow found in Southeast Asia.

t: The northern grey-headed sparrow (Passer griseus), also known as the grey-headed sparrow, is a species of bird in the sparrow family Passeridae, which is resident in much of tropical Africa. It occurs in a wide range of open habitats, including open woodlands and human habitation, often occupying the same niche as the house sparrow does in Eurasia.
f: It builds a cup nest in trees, thatch, or old nests of other birds; 2–4 eggs are laid.

t: The Spanish sparrow or willow sparrow (Passer hispaniolensis) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae. It is very similar to the closely related house sparrow, and the two species show their close relation in a "biological mix-up" of hybridisation in the Mediterranean region, which complicates the taxonomy of this species.
f: It is found in the Mediterranean region and south-west and central Asia.

t: The Italian sparrow (Passer italiae), also known as the cisalpine sparrow, is a passerine bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in Italy and other parts of the Mediterranean region. In appearance, it is intermediate between the house sparrow, and the Spanish sparrow, a species of the Mediterranean and Central Asia closely related to the house sparrow.
f: The Italian sparrow is unofficially considered the national bird of Italy.

t: The Cape sparrow (Passer melanurus), or mossie, is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae found in southern Africa. A medium-sized sparrow at 14–16 centimetres (5.5–6.3 in), it has distinctive plumage, including large pale head stripes in both sexes.
f: The nest can be constructed in a tree, a bush, a cavity, or a disused nest of another species.

t: The Dead Sea sparrow (Passer moabiticus) is a species of bird in the Old World sparrow family Passeridae, with one subspecies breeding in parts of the West Asia and another in western Afghanistan and eastern Iran.
f: The eastern subspecies P. m. yatii is sometimes considered a separate species known as Yate's sparrow.

t: The tree sparrow (Passer montanus Latin pronunciation: [pas.ser mon.ta.nus]) is a passerine bird in the sparrow family with a rich chestnut crown and nape and a black patch on each pure white cheek. The sexes have similar plumage, and young birds are duller versions of the adult.
f: As with other small birds, infection by parasites and diseases, as well as predation by birds of prey, take their toll, and the typical lifespan is about two years.

t: The Sind sparrow (Passer pyrrhonotus) is a passerine bird of the sparrow family, Passeridae, found around the Indus valley region in South Asia. Its name refers to the province of Sindh, and it is also known as the jungle, Sind jungle, or rufous-backed sparrow.
f: Its main vocalisations are soft chirping calls that are extended into longer songs with other sounds interspersed by breeding males.

t: The Kenya sparrow (Passer rufocinctus), also known as the Kenya rufous sparrow, is a sparrow found in Kenya and Tanzania. Some authorities have lumped the great sparrow (P. motitensis), the Kenya sparrow, and the Socotra sparrow (P. insularis) into P. motitensis following Dowsett and Forbes-Watson (1993).
f: It tends to be found in dry wooded savannah and agricultural areas.

t: The desert sparrow (Passer simplex) is a species of bird in the sparrow family Passeridae, found in the Sahara Desert of northern Africa. The desert sparrow has two subspecies which occur in some of driest parts of the Sahara Desert in Northern Africa.
f: The Mozabite Berbers build their homes with holes in the walls to welcome these birds, which they call "bar-rode", and if one sings all day in the house, they say this is a sign of good news.

t: The Swainson's sparrow (Passer swainsonii) is a species of bird in the sparrow family Passeridae. Sometimes considered a subspecies of the grey-headed sparrow, it occurs in northeastern Africa, largely in the Ethiopian Highlands.
f: This sparrow was named after the English naturalist and illustrator William Swainson.

t: The Savannah sparrow (Passerculus sandwichensis) is a small New World sparrow that is the only member of the genus Passerculus. It is a widespread and abundant species that occupies open grassland habitats in North America.
f: The common name refers to Savannah, Georgia, where Alexander Wilson observed the species in 1811.

t: The fox sparrow (Passerella iliaca) is a large New World sparrow.
f: It is the only member of the genus Passerella, although some authors split the species into four (see below).
The lazuli bunting (Passerina amoena) is a North American songbird named for the gemstone lapis lazuli.

t: The blue grosbeak (Passerina caerulea) is a medium-sized North American passerine bird in the cardinal family Cardinalidae. The male is blue with two brown wing bars.
f: It is mainly migratory, wintering in Central America and breeding in northern Mexico and the southern United States.

t: The painted bunting (Passerina ciris) is a species of bird in the cardinal family, Cardinalidae.
f: The bright plumage of the male develops beginning in the second year of life; in the first year, they can be distinguished from the female only by close inspection.

t: The indigo bunting (Passerina cyanea) is a small seed-eating bird in the cardinal family, Cardinalidae. It is migratory, ranging from southern Canada to northern Florida during the breeding season, and from southern Florida to northern South America during the winter.
f: It displays sexual dimorphism in its coloration; the male is vibrant blue in the summer, with brightly colored plumage during the breeding season to attract a mate.

t: The orange-breasted bunting (Passerina leclancherii) is a species of passerine bird in the family Cardinalidae. With its wide range and large total population, the International Union for Conservation of Nature considers it as being of "least concern".
f: It is endemic to Mexico, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.

t: The rose-bellied bunting or Rosita's bunting (Passerina rositae) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks.
f: It is endemic to a very small area of southern Mexico.

t: The varied bunting (Passerina versicolor) is a species of songbird in the cardinal family, Cardinalidae. The range of the varied bunting stretches from the southern parts of Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas in the United States south throughout Mexico as far as Oaxaca.
f: Varied buntings weave open-cup nests of grass and spider webs in the outer branches of thorny shrubs, usually near water.

t: The rosy starling (Pastor roseus), also known as the rose-coloured starling, is a passerine bird in the starling family Sturnidae. This split is supported by further studies, with its closest relative now thought to be the wattled starling (Creatophora cinerea) of tropical Africa, with these two then closest to a large group of Asian starlings and mynas.
f: The species was restored to its own monotypic genus Pastor in 2008, formerly being included in a wide interpretation of the genus Sturnus.

t: The Chilean pigeon (Patagioenas araucana) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Chile and Argentina.

t: The pale-vented pigeon (Patagioenas cayennensis) is a large pigeon (family Columbidae) found in the tropical Americas. Formerly often placed in Columba, it actually belongs to a clade of the older New World genus Patagioenas.
f: Grey-hued birds, even their males generally lack iridescent display plumage, although the present species has some coppery gloss on the nape.

t: The bare-eyed pigeon (Patagioenas corensis) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Venezuela, and the Netherlands Antilles.

t: It is largely gray, but with a thin white collar on the nape and a purple-gray breast.
f: The band-tailed pigeon (Patagioenas fasciata) is a pigeon native to the Americas, and one of the largest pigeons in this region.

t: Its breeding range extends from southern Texas, United States, to Costa Rica. It is primarily found throughout coastal and lowland areas of Mexico and Central America.
f: The red-billed pigeon (Patagioenas flavirostris) is a relatively large, robust species of pigeon.

t: The dusky pigeon (Patagioenas goodsoni) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The white-crowned pigeon (Patagioenas leucocephala) is a fruit and seed-eating species of bird in the dove and pigeon family Columbidae. It is found primarily in the Caribbean.
f: John James Audubon painted these pigeons, including the watercolour painting in his work, Birds of America, published in the early 19th century.

t: The spot-winged pigeon (Patagioenas maculosa) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: The short-billed pigeon (Patagioenas nigrirostris) is a largish pigeon which breeds from southern Mexico south to northwestern Colombia. It is a member of a clade of Patagioenas that contains the smaller and rather plain species with characteristic calls that constitute the subgenus Oenoenas.
f: They can be distinguished by the slower, more complex "song" of the short-billed pigeon.
The picazuro pigeon (Patagioenas picazuro) is a pigeon native to South America.

t: The plumbeous pigeon (Patagioenas plumbea) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The scaled pigeon (Patagioenas speciosa) is a large New World tropical dove. It is a resident breeder from southern Mexico south to western Ecuador, southern Brazil, northern Argentina, and Trinidad.
f: It builds a stick platform nest in a tree and lays two white eggs.

t: The scaly-naped pigeon (Patagioenas squamosa), also known as the red-necked pigeon, is a bird belonging to the family Columbidae.
f: The species occurs throughout the Caribbean.

t: The ruddy pigeon (Patagioenas subvinacea) is a largish pigeon which breeds from Costa Rica south to western Ecuador, Bolivia, and central Brazil. It belongs to a clade of small and rather plain species of Patagioenas with characteristic calls that constitute the subgenus Oenoenas.
f: There are some geographical variations in its voice, with some populations singing four-noted songs, while others sing three-noted songs.
The southern giant hummingbird (Patagona gigas) is one of two species in the genus Patagona and the second largest hummingbird species, after its close relative the northern giant hummingbird.

t: The helmeted curassow (Pauxi pauxi) or northern helmeted curassow, is a large terrestrial bird in the family Cracidae found in the subtropical cloud-forest in steep, mountainous regions of western Venezuela and northern Colombia. There are two subspecies found in different mountain ranges.
f: It is a mostly black bird with a white tip to its tail, a red bill and a distinctive grey casque on its forehead.

t: The Indian peafowl (Pavo cristatus), also known as the common peafowl, or blue peafowl, is a species of peafowl native to the Indian subcontinent. While it originated in the Indian subcontinent, it has since been introduced to many other parts of the world.
f: It is the national bird of India and venerated in Hindu and Greek mythology.

t: The brown-winged kingfisher (Pelargopsis amauroptera) is a species of bird in the subfamily Halcyoninae. It is found along the north and eastern coasts of the Bay of Bengal, occurring in the countries of Bangladesh, India, Malaysia, Myanmar and Thailand.
f: In India, it has been mainly reported from the Sundarbans region but records from further south near Chilka exist.

t: The stork-billed kingfisher (Pelargopsis capensis), is a tree kingfisher which is widely but sparsely distributed in the tropical Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, from India to Indonesia. The head is brown and the chin is paler coloured.
f: These kingfishers are large and have a heavy bill.

t: The Australian pelican (Pelecanus conspicillatus) is a large waterbird in the family Pelecanidae, widespread on the inland and coastal waters of Australia and New Guinea, also in Fiji, parts of Indonesia and as a vagrant in New Zealand. It is a predominantly white bird with black wings and a pink bill.
f: It has been recorded as having the longest bill of any living bird.

t: The American white pelican (Pelecanus erythrorhynchos) is a large aquatic soaring bird from the order Pelecaniformes.
f: It breeds in interior North America, moving south and to the coasts, as far as Costa Rica, in winter.

t: The brown pelican (Pelecanus occidentalis) is a bird of the pelican family, Pelecanidae, one of three species found in the Americas and one of two that feed by diving into water. It is found on the Atlantic Coast from New Jersey to the mouth of the Amazon River, and along the Pacific Coast from British Columbia to Peru, including the Galapagos Islands.
f: The brown pelican is the national bird of Saint Martin, Barbados, Saint Kitts and Nevis, and the Turks and Caicos Islands, and the official state bird of Louisiana, appearing on the flag, seal, or coat of arms of each.

t: The brown pelican (Pelecanus occidentalis) is a bird of the pelican family, Pelecanidae, one of three species found in the Americas and one of two that feed by diving into water. It is found on the Atlantic Coast from New Jersey to the mouth of the Amazon River, and along the Pacific Coast from British Columbia to Peru, including the Galapagos Islands.
f: The brown pelican is the national bird of Saint Martin, Barbados, Saint Kitts and Nevis, and the Turks and Caicos Islands, and the official state bird of Louisiana, appearing on the flag, seal, or coat of arms of each.

t: The brown pelican (Pelecanus occidentalis) is a bird of the pelican family, Pelecanidae, one of three species found in the Americas and one of two that feed by diving into water. It is found on the Atlantic Coast from New Jersey to the mouth of the Amazon River, and along the Pacific Coast from British Columbia to Peru, including the Galapagos Islands.
f: The brown pelican is the national bird of Saint Martin, Barbados, Saint Kitts and Nevis, and the Turks and Caicos Islands, and the official state bird of Louisiana, appearing on the flag, seal, or coat of arms of each.

t: The great white pelican (Pelecanus onocrotalus), also known as the eastern white pelican (in contrast to the western pelican of the Americas), rosy pelican or simply white pelican, is a bird in the pelican family. It breeds from southeastern Europe through Asia and Africa, in swamps and shallow lakes.
f: It is one of the species to which the Agreement on the Conservation of African-Eurasian Migratory Waterbirds (AEWA) is applied.

t: The spot-throated babbler (Pellorneum albiventre) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found mainly in Eastern Bangladesh, Bhutan, Northeast India, Yunnan, Myanmar and Vietnam.

t: The ferruginous babbler (Pellorneum bicolor) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, and Thailand.

t: The Javan black-capped babbler (Pellorneum capistratum) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. The Malayan black-capped babbler (P. nigrocapitatum) and the Bornean black-capped babbler (P. capistratoides) were both formerly considered conspecific, but were split from it in 2021.
f: It is endemic to the island of Java in Indonesia.
The Sulawesi babbler (Pellorneum celebense) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae.
The brown-capped babbler (Pellorneum fuscocapillus) is a member of the family Pellorneidae.

t: The mourning babbler (Pellorneum malaccense), previously the short-tailed babbler, is a species of bird in the ground babbler family Pellorneidae. It is found in the Malay Peninsula, Anambas Islands, Sumatra, Banyak Islands, Batu Islands, Riau Islands, Lingga Islands and the Natuna Islands.
f: Like other babblers they will use their foot to grasp food items, an unusual behaviour for passerine birds.

t: The marsh babbler (Pellorneum palustre) is a member of the family Pellorneidae.
f: The marsh babbler is endemic to the Brahmaputra floodplain, its associated tributaries and adjacent hill ranges in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya in India and eastern Bangladesh.

t: Temminck's babbler (Pellorneum pyrrogenys) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in Borneo and Java.
f: This bird's common name commemorates the Dutch naturalist Coenraad Jacob Temminck.

t: It was formerly considered to be conspecific with the Bornean swamp babbler (Pellorneum macropterum). Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The puff-throated babbler or spotted babbler (Pellorneum ruficeps) is a species of passerine bird found in Asia. They are found in scrub and moist forest mainly in hilly regions.
f: They forage in small groups on the forest floor, turning around leaf litter to find their prey and usually staying low in the undergrowth where they can be hard to spot.

t: The buff-breasted babbler (Pellorneum tickelli) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The mountain peltops (Peltops montanus) is a species of bird in the family Cracticidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.

t: The white-winged guan (Penelope albipennis) is a bird in the chachalaca, guan and curassow family Cracidae.
f: It is endemic to northwestern Peru.

t: The band-tailed guan (Penelope argyrotis) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The bearded guan (Penelope barbata) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows. It is found in Ecuador and Peru.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The red-faced guan (Penelope dabbenei) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found in Argentina and Bolivia.

t: Spix's guan (Penelope jacquacu) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae.
f: It is "the prototypical cracid of the Amazonian lowlands." The common name commemorates the German naturalist Johann Baptist von Spix (1782-1826).

t: The marail guan or Cayenne guan (Penelope marail) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The Andean guan (Penelope montagnii) is a gamefowl species of the family Cracidae, in which it belongs to the guan subfamily Penelopinae.
f: This bird occurs in the highlands (5,000 ft/1,500 m ASL and higher) of the Andes, from Venezuela and Colombia through Ecuador and Peru south to Bolivia and perhaps northwesternmost Argentina.

t: The dusky-legged guan (Penelope obscura) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, the chachalacas, guans, and curassows. In early 2021, the former subspecies P. o. bridgesi, found in southwestern Bolivia and northwestern Argentina, was elevated to species rank as Yungas guan.
f: It is found in Uruguay, northeastern Argentina and southernmost areas of Paraguay and Brazil.

t: The Cauca guan (Penelope perspicax) is a bird in the chachalaca, guan and curassow family, Cracidae. It is a large guan, and like most guans leads a mostly arboreal life in humid forests, where it forages for fruit and leaves.
f: The Cauca guan is endemic to Colombia's Cauca River valley.

t: The crested guan (Penelope purpurascens) is a Near Threatened species in an ancient group of birds of the family Cracidae, which are related to the Australasian megapodes or mound builders (Megapodiidae).
f: It is found from central Mexico through Central America and in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The rusty-margined guan (Penelope superciliaris) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae, which includes the chachalacas, guans, and curassows.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The Mindanao hornbill (Penelopides affinis), also known as the Mindanao tarictic hornbill, is a medium-small species of hornbill found in the canopy of rainforests on Mindanao, Dinagat, Siargao and Basilan in the southern Philippines. Its population declining due to habitat destruction, hunting and the illegal wildlife trade.
f: All five Philippine tarictics were once considered a single species.

t: The highland guan (Penelopina nigra) is a species of bird in the family Cracidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in the highlands of El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, southern Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: The slaty robin (Melanodryas cyanus), also known as the blue-grey robin, is a species of bird in the Australasian robin family Petroicidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is endemic to the New Guinea Highlands and sparsely in the island's northern areas.
The white-winged robin (Melanodryas sigillata) is a species of bird in the Australasian robin family Petroicidae.

t: The Allpahuayo antbird (Percnostola arenarum) is a Vulnerable species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is endemic to northeastern Peru.

t: The black-headed antbird (Percnostola rufifrons) is a species of passerine bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The rock bush quail (Perdicula argoondah) is a species of quail found in parts of peninsular India.
f: It is a common species with a wide range and the IUCN has rated it as being of "least concern".

t: The jungle bush quail (Perdicula asiatica) is a species of quail in the family Phasianidae. It is native to the Indian subcontinent, where it is found in peninsular India and Sri Lanka.
f: Incubation is only done by the female.

t: The painted bush quail (Perdicula erythrorhyncha) is a species of quail found in the hill forests of India. They move in small coveys on hillsides and are distinguished by their red bills and legs.
f: They have a liquid alarm call and small groups will run in single file along paths before taking flight when flushed.

t: The grey partridge (Perdix perdix) is a bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae of the order Galliformes, gallinaceous birds.
f: The scientific name is the Latin for "partridge".

t: Swinhoe's minivet or the brown-rumped minivet (Pericrocotus cantonensis) is a bird in the cuckooshrike family, Campephagidae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1861.
f: It breeds in China and winters in Indochina.

t: The small minivet (Pericrocotus cinnamomeus) is a small passerine bird.
f: This minivet is found in tropical southern Asia from the Indian subcontinent east to Indonesia.

t: The ashy minivet (Pericrocotus divaricatus) is a passerine bird of eastern Asia belonging to the minivet genus Pericrocotus in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae. While most of the minivets have shades of yellow, orange and red in their plumage, this species has only greys, whites and blacks.
f: The male is distinctive with a white face and black nape although females can be confused with the female of the brown-rumped minivet.
The white-bellied minivet (Pericrocotus erythropygius) is a species of minivet found in India, mostly in dry deciduous forest.

t: The long-tailed minivet (Pericrocotus ethologus) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in southern and south-eastern Asia where it occurs in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The orange minivet (Pericrocotus flammeus) is a brightly colored bird in the cuckooshrike family, Campephagidae. It is found all along the Western Ghats and west coast of India and Sri Lanka.
f: The orange minivet is a species resident in southern India and Sri Lanka, that feeds primarily on insects while foraging in mixed-species bird flocks or in small single-species groups.

t: The grey-chinned minivet (Pericrocotus solaris) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae. Its natural habitat is forests about 1,000–2,000 m (3,300–6,600 ft) in elevation.
f: It is found from the Himalayas to China, Taiwan and Southeast Asia.

t: The scarlet minivet (Pericrocotus speciosus) is a small passerine bird in the cuckooshrike family Campephagidae. This minivet is found in tropical southern Asia from Northeast India to southern China, Indonesia, and the Philippines.
f: They are common resident breeding birds in forests and other well-wooded habitats including gardens, especially in hilly country.

t: The Ryukyu minivet (Pericrocotus tegimae) is a species of bird in the family Campephagidae. The species was previously thought to be a subspecies of the ashy minivet.
f: Its specific name is named for the Japanese naturalist Seiichi Tegima.

t: The coal tit (Periparus ater) is a passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae. It is a widespread and common resident breeder in forests throughout the temperate to subtropical Palearctic, including North Africa.
f: The black-crested tit is now included in this species.

t: The elegant tit (Periparus elegans) is a species of bird in the tit family Paridae endemic to the Philippines.
f: Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland forests and tropical moist montane forests.

t: Some of its subspecies were formerly assigned to its western relative the rufous-naped tit (P. rufonuchalis), or these two were considered entirely conspecific.
f: The rufous-vented tit (Periparus rubidiventris) is an Asian songbird species in the tit and chickadee family (Paridae).

t: The rufous-naped tit (Periparus rufonuchalis), also known as the black-breasted tit or dark-grey tit, is an Asian songbird species in the tit and chickadee family (Paridae). It was sometimes considered conspecific with the rufous-vented tit (P. rubidiventris), and was formerly placed in the genus Parus.
f: This tit is a native of the western Himalayas, but has a very large range, occurring in parts of India, China, Pakistan, Turkestan, Kyrgyzstan, and Afghanistan.

t: The yellow-bellied tit (Periparus venustulus) is a bird in the family Paridae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1870.
f: It is also present in urban green spaces.

t: The red-and-black grosbeak (Periporphyrus erythromelas) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals, grosbeaks, and “tanager” allies.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The Canada jay (Perisoreus canadensis), also known as the grey jay, gray jay, camp robber, moose bird, gorby, or whisky jack, is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae. It is found in boreal forests of North America, north to the tree line, and in the Rocky Mountains subalpine zone south to New Mexico and Arizona.
f: In 2016, an online poll and expert panel conducted by Canadian Geographic magazine selected the Canada jay as the national bird of Canada, although the designation is not formally recognized.

t: The Siberian jay (Perisoreus infaustus) is a small jay with a widespread distribution within the coniferous forests in North Eurasia. It has grey-brown plumage with a darker brown crown and a paler throat.
f: It is rusty-red in a panel near the wing-bend, on the undertail coverts and on the sides of the tail.

t: The capuchinbird or calfbird (Perissocephalus tricolor) is a large passerine bird of the family Cotingidae. It is monotypic within the genus Perissocephalus.
f: It is found in humid forests (up to 1,400 metres (4,600 ft) but mostly below 600 m) in north-eastern South America, almost entirely north of the Amazon River and east of Rio Negro (Colombia, Venezuela, Brazil and The Guianas).
The European honey buzzard (Pernis apivorus) is an insectivorous bird of prey in the family Accipitridae breeding in Europe and western Asia, and wintering in Africa.

t: The crested honey buzzard (Pernis ptilorhynchus), also known as the Oriental, Asiatic, or Eastern honey buzzard, is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as kites, eagles, and harriers. It is a fairly large raptor, larger than the European honey buzzard.
f: The species has several adaptations for its specialist diet.

t: The fairy martin (Petrochelidon ariel) is a member of the swallow family of passerine birds which breeds in Australia. It is increasingly a wanderer to New Zealand, where it may have bred.
f: It is migratory wintering through most of Australia, with some birds reaching New Guinea and Indonesia.

t: The streak-throated swallow or the Indian cliff swallow (Petrochelidon fluvicola) is a passerine bird, which includes a large number of other species including many swallows. It occurs as a vagrant in the Maldives, Sri Lanka, and the Middle East.
f: It is native of South Asia where it is a breeder, year-round resident or winter visitor in the countries of Afghanistan, India, Nepal and Pakistan.

t: The cave swallow (Petrochelidon fulva) is a medium-sized, squarish-tailed swallow belonging to the same genus as the more familiar and widespread cliff swallow of North America. The cave swallow, also native to the Americas, nests and roosts primarily in caves and sinkholes.
f: Cave swallows are found in Mexico and the Greater Antilles, with fall and winter vagrants reaching the east and Gulf Coasts of the U.S.

t: The tree martin (Petrochelidon nigricans) is a member of the swallow family of passerine birds. It breeds in Australia, mostly south of latitude 20°S, and on Timor island.
f: It is migratory, wintering through most of Australia, New Guinea, Indonesia east of the Wallace Line, and the Solomon Islands.

t: The cliff swallow or American cliff swallow (Petrochelidon pyrrhonota) is a member of the passerine bird family Hirundinidae, the swallows and martins. The generic name Petrochelidon is derived from the Ancient Greek petros meaning "stone" and khelidon (χελιδών) "swallow", and the specific name pyrrhonota comes from purrhos meaning "flame-coloured" and -notos "-backed".
f: Cliff swallows are extremely social songbirds that can be found in large nesting colonies reaching over 2,000 nests.

t: The South African cliff swallow (Petrochelidon spilodera), also known as the South African swallow, is a species of bird in the family Hirundinidae native southern Africa. It winters to the lower Congo Basin.
f: It is well known for its supposed ability to carry coconuts, although this claim has little to no credibility outside of the Monty Python fictional universe.

t: The birds are sparsely distributed through the South Island and Stewart Island / Rakiura, although the distribution is not continuous. The nominate, and the Stewart Island robin (P. australis rakiura) are the two subspecies.
f: The South Island robin (Petroica australis; also known in Māori as the kakaruai) is a sparrow-sized bird found only in New Zealand, where it has the status of a protected endemic species.

t: The birds are sparsely distributed through the South Island and Stewart Island / Rakiura, although the distribution is not continuous. The nominate, and the Stewart Island robin (P. australis rakiura) are the two subspecies.
f: The South Island robin (Petroica australis; also known in Māori as the kakaruai) is a sparrow-sized bird found only in New Zealand, where it has the status of a protected endemic species.
The North Island robin  is a species of Australasian robin endemic to the North Island of New Zealand.

t: The scarlet robin (Petroica boodang) is a common red-breasted Australasian robin in the passerine bird genus Petroica. The species was originally split in 1999 by Schodde and Mason, and as the original collection by Gmelin was from Norfolk Island, this retained the name of multicolor, and is now known as the Norfolk robin.
f: The species is found on continental Australia and its offshore islands, including Tasmania.

t: The red-capped robin (Petroica goodenovii) is a small passerine bird native to Australia. Found in drier regions across much of the continent, it inhabits scrub and open woodland.
f: This species uses a variety of songs, and males generally sing to advertise territories and attract females.
The North Island robin  is a species of Australasian robin endemic to the North Island of New Zealand.

t: The tomtit (Petroica macrocephala) is a small passerine bird in the family Petroicidae, the Australasian robins. It is endemic to the islands of New Zealand, ranging across the main islands as well as several of the outlying islands.
f: The species is not threatened and has adapted to the changes made to New Zealand's biodiversity.
