t: Tickell's leaf warbler (Phylloscopus affinis) is a leaf warbler found in Asia in the countries of Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan and Thailand. The species has a yellowish underside and supercilium.
f: An active bird, it prefers the canopy and low shrubbery and can be difficult to track as it moves actively from branch to branch, acrobatically exploring the underside of leaves and twigs.

t: Kloss's leaf warbler (Phylloscopus ogilviegranti) is a leaf warbler found in Cambodia, China, Laos, Thailand, and Vietnam. Its natural habitats are temperate forests, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It was promoted to species status based on evidence from both molecular genetic and vocalization studies.

t: The Philippine leaf warbler (Phylloscopus olivaceus) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Phylloscopidae.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines on the islands Bohol, Samar, Leyte, Negros, Mindanao, Basilan and the Sulu Archipelago.

t: Martens's warbler (Phylloscopus omeiensis), also known as Omei warbler or Emei Shan warbler, is a species of Old World warbler in the family Phylloscopidae (or Sylviidae). It is found in China and Myanmar.
f: It was first described in 1999.

t: The eastern Bonelli's warbler (Phylloscopus orientalis), sometimes known as the Balkan warbler, is a warbler in the leaf warbler genus Phylloscopus. They also show marked difference in mtDNA sequence.
f: The song is a fast monotone trill, only slightly different from western Bonelli's, and also some similarity to the wood warbler.

t: The two-barred warbler (Phylloscopus plumbeitarsus) is a bird of the leaf warbler family (Phylloscopidae). The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1861.
f: Before the autumn migration, both adults and juveniles molt.

t: The island leaf warbler (Phylloscopus poliocephalus) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Phylloscopidae.
f: It is found in an area ranging from the Moluccas to the Solomon Islands.

t: The grey-cheeked warbler (Phylloscopus poliogenys) is a species of leaf warbler (family Phylloscopidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
f: Its population size is unknown, but due to its large range the species does not approach the thresholds for Vulnerable under the range size criteria.

t: Pallas's leaf warbler (Phylloscopus proregulus) or Pallas's warbler is a bird that breeds in mountain forests from southern Siberia east to northern Mongolia and northeast China. This leaf warbler is strongly migratory, wintering mainly in south China and adjacent areas of southeast Asia, although in recent decades increasing numbers have been found in Europe in autumn.
f: It is named after the German zoologist Peter Simon Pallas, who first formally described it.

t: The buff-barred warbler (Phylloscopus pulcher) is a species of leaf warbler (family Phylloscopidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
f: It is primarily found at low altitudes.

t: Blyth's leaf warbler (Phylloscopus reguloides) is a species of leaf warbler (family Phylloscopidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
f: This bird was named after the English zoologist Edward Blyth.

t: The yellow-throated woodland warbler (Phylloscopus ruficapilla) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Phylloscopidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is endemic to the Afromontane, from Kenya to South Africa.

t: The Lompobattang leaf warbler (Phylloscopus sarasinorum) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Phylloscopidae. The Sulawesi leaf warbler (P. nesophilus) was formerly considered conspecific with the Lompobattang leaf warbler and both were grouped under the name P. sarasinorum, but more recent analyses indicate that it is a distinct species.
f: It is found only in Sulawesi Island, Indonesia.

t: Radde's warbler (Phylloscopus schwarzi) is a leaf warbler which breeds in Siberia. The genus name Phylloscopus is from Ancient Greek phullon, "leaf", and skopos, "seeker" (from skopeo, "to watch").
f: This warbler is strongly migratory and winters in Southeast Asia.

t: The wood warbler (Phylloscopus sibilatrix) is a common and widespread leaf warbler which breeds throughout northern and temperate Europe, and just into the extreme west of Asian Russia in the southern Ural Mountains.
f: It is strongly migratory and the entire population winters in tropical Africa.

t: The mountain chiffchaff or eastern chiffchaff (Phylloscopus sindianus) is a species of leaf warbler found in the Caucasus (P. s. lorenzii) and Tian Shan (P. s. sindianus). The nominate subspecies is similar to the Siberian chiffchaff, but with a finer darker bill, browner upperparts and buff flanks; its song is almost identical to the common chiffchaff, but the call is a weak psew.
f: It is an altitudinal migrant, moving to lower levels in winter.

t: Alström's warbler (Phylloscopus soror), or the plain-tailed warbler, is a species of Old World warbler in the family Phylloscopidae. It was first described in 1999.
f: It breeds only in China and winters as far as Thailand, Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam.

t: The buff-throated warbler (Phylloscopus subaffinis) is a species of leaf warbler (family Phylloscopidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
f: It breeds in China and winters down toward northern Southeast Asia.
Brooks's leaf warbler (Phylloscopus subviridis) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Phylloscopidae.

t: The pale-legged leaf warbler (Phylloscopus tenellipes) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Phylloscopidae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1860.
f: It is found in Manchuria; it winters in Southeast Asia.

t: The grey-crowned warbler (Phylloscopus tephrocephalus) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Phylloscopidae. It is found in Bangladesh, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam.
f: In the subsequent reorganization, the two genera were merged into Phylloscopus, which has priority under the rules of the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature.

t: The mountain leaf warbler (Phylloscopus trivirgatus) is a songbird species from the leaf warbler family (Phylloscopidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
f: It is found in Indonesia and Malaysia.

t: The greenish warbler (Phylloscopus trochiloides) is a widespread leaf warbler with a breeding range in northeastern Europe, and temperate to subtropical continental Asia. It is not uncommon as a spring or early autumn vagrant in Western Europe and is annually seen in Great Britain.
f: This warbler is strongly migratory and winters in India.

t: The willow warbler (Phylloscopus trochilus) is a very common and widespread leaf warbler which breeds throughout northern and temperate Europe and the Palearctic, from Ireland east to the Anadyr River basin in eastern Siberia. It is strongly migratory, with almost all of the population wintering in sub-Saharan Africa.
f: In spite of its small size, the willow warbler performs one of the longest migrations of any animal.

t: Like all leaf warblers, it was formerly placed in the "Old World warbler" assemblage, but now belongs to the new leaf-warbler family Phylloscopidae. It is found in Afghanistan, Pakistan, Nepal, and India.
f: Tytler's leaf warbler (Phylloscopus tytleri) is a songbird species.
The brown woodland warbler (Phylloscopus umbrovirens) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Phylloscopidae.

t: Bianchi's warbler (Phylloscopus valentini) is a species of leaf warbler (family Phylloscopidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
f: In the subsequent reorganization the two genera were merged into Phylloscopus which has priority under the rules of the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature.

t: Whistler's warbler (Phylloscopus whistleri) is a species of leaf warbler (family Phylloscopidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
f: The common name commemorates the English ornithologist Hugh Whistler (1889–1943).

t: The Japanese leaf warbler (Phylloscopus xanthodryas) is a leaf warbler (family Phylloscopidae). The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1863.
f: It is found throughout Japan, except on Hokkaido; it winters to Southeast Asia.

t: The grey-hooded warbler (Phylloscopus xanthoschistos) is a species of leaf warbler (family Phylloscopidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
f: It is most famous for the way it warbles.

t: The Chinese leaf warbler (Phylloscopus yunnanensis) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Phylloscopidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.
The Peruvian plantcutter (Phytotoma raimondii) is an Vulnerable species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.

t: The rufous-tailed plantcutter (Phytotoma rara), sometimes called the Chilean plantcutter, is a passerine bird of southern South America, now placed in the cotinga family. It is a medium-sized bird about 19 centimetres (7.5 in) long with a long black tail with a red base.
f: There is a wing bar which is white in the male and buff in the female.

t: The white-tipped plantcutter (Phytotoma rutila) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay, and as a vagrant to Brazil and Chile.

t: The species was formerly considered to be conspecific with the Mexican squirrel cuckoo (Piaya mexicana).
f: The common squirrel cuckoo (Piaya cayana) is a large and active species of cuckoo found in wooded habitats from northwestern Mexico to northern Argentina and Uruguay, and on Trinidad.

t: The black-bellied cuckoo or black-bellied squirrel cuckoo (Piaya melanogaster) is a bird of the family Cuculidae found in the Amazon region. Even though this species has a wide distribution, little is known about its ecology and natural history.
f: The word melanogaster means "black belly"; it has Greek roots, melas meaning "black" and gaster meaning "belly".

t: The black-rumped magpie (Pica bottanensis) is a species of magpie native to west-central China and Bhutan, and possibly also irregularly in Sikkim in India, and in eastern Nepal. It is similar to other magpies in the genus Pica, with pied plumage with bluish-green iridescent wings and tail, but differs from the other species in the genus except for Asir magpie in having no white on the rump.
f: In breeding behaviour it is largely similar to other Pica magpies, laying a single brood from April to June.

t: The black-billed magpie (Pica hudsonia), also known as the American magpie, is a bird in the corvid family found in the western half of North America. It is black and white, with the wings and tail showing black areas and iridescent hints of blue and blue-green.
f: Incubation, by the female only, starts when the clutch is complete, and lasts 16–21 days.

t: The yellow-billed magpie (Pica nuttallii), also known as the California magpie, is a bird that is endemic to California's Central Valley and the adjacent chaparral foothills and mountains. The scientific name commemorates the English naturalist Thomas Nuttall.
f: Apart from its having a yellow bill and a yellow streak around the eye and being slightly smaller, it is virtually identical to the black-billed magpie (Pica hudsonia) found in much of the rest of western North America.

t: The Eurasian magpie or common magpie (Pica pica) is a resident breeding bird throughout the northern part of the Eurasian continent. It is one of several birds in the crow family (corvids) that are designated as magpies, and it belongs to the Holarctic radiation of "monochrome" magpies.
f: In Europe, the term "magpie" is used by English speakers as a synonym for the Eurasian magpie; the only other species of magpie in Europe being the Iberian magpie (Cyanopica cooki), which is restricted to the Iberian Peninsula.

t: The Oriental magpie (Pica serica) is a species of magpie found from southeastern Russia to eastern China, Korea, Taiwan, and northern Indochina and Myanmar. Other names include Korean magpie, Chinese magpie and Asian magpie.
f: It is also naturalised in Japan.
The white-headed woodpecker (Leuconotopicus albolarvatus) is a non-migratory woodpecker that resides in pine forests of the mountains of western North America.
The black-backed woodpecker (Picoides arcticus), also known as the Arctic three-toed woodpecker, is a medium-sized woodpecker (23 cm (9.1 in) long) inhabiting the forests of North America.
The American three-toed woodpecker (Picoides dorsalis) is a medium-sized woodpecker (family Picidae), which is native to North America.

t: Nuttall's woodpecker (Dryobates nuttallii) is a species of woodpecker named after naturalist Thomas Nuttall in 1843.
f: They are found in oak woodlands of California and are similar to the ladder-backed woodpecker in both genetics and appearance.

t: The downy woodpecker (Dryobates pubescens) is a species of woodpecker, the smallest in North America. Length ranges from 14 to 18 cm (5.5 to 7.1 in).
f: The bird nests in tree cavities and feeds primarily on insects, although it supplements its diet with seeds and berries.
The ladder-backed woodpecker (Dryobates scalaris) is a North American woodpecker.
The Eurasian three-toed woodpecker (Picoides tridactylus) is a medium-sized woodpecker that is found from northern Europe across northern Asia to Japan.

t: The hairy woodpecker (Leuconotopicus villosus) is a medium-sized woodpecker that is found over a large area of North America. With an estimated population in 2020 of almost nine million individuals, the hairy woodpecker is listed by the IUCN as a species of least concern.
f: It is approximately 250 mm (9.8 in) in length with a 380 mm (15 in) wingspan.

t: The yellow-browed woodpecker (Piculus aurulentus), also known as the white-browed woodpecker, is a Near Threatened species of bird in the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
The stripe-cheeked woodpecker (Piculus callopterus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.

t: The golden-green woodpecker (Piculus chrysochloros) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Panama and every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The yellow-throated woodpecker (Piculus flavigula) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname and Venezuela.

t: The white-throated woodpecker (Piculus leucolaemus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picinae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The white-wedged piculet (Picumnus albosquamatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Paraguay.

t: The bar-breasted piculet (Picumnus aurifrons) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, and Peru.

t: The chestnut piculet (Picumnus cinnamomeus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.

t: The white-barred piculet (Picumnus cirratus) is a species of bird in the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The ocellated piculet (Picumnus dorbignyanus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru and possibly Argentina.

t: The golden-spangled piculet (Picumnus exilis) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.
The greyish piculet (Picumnus granadensis) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.

t: The speckled piculet (Picumnus innominatus) is a species of bird in the family Picidae.
f: It is found in India, China and Southeast Asia.

t: Lafresnaye's piculet (Picumnus lafresnayi) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The ochraceous piculet (Picumnus limae) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is endemic to north-eastern Brazil.

t: The mottled piculet (Picumnus nebulosus) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay.

t: The olivaceous piculet (Picumnus olivaceus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found from Guatemala south through Central America and western South America to Peru.
The spotted piculet (Picumnus pygmaeus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.

t: The rufous-breasted piculet (Picumnus rufiventris) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The Ecuadorian piculet (Picumnus sclateri) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The white-bellied piculet (Picumnus spilogaster) is a Vulnerable species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Guyana, and Venezuela.

t: The scaled piculet (Picumnus squamulatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The ochre-collared piculet (Picumnus temminckii) is a species of bird in subfamily Picumninae of the woodpecker family Picidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.
Japanese green woodpecker or Japanese woodpecker (Picus awokera) is a medium-sized woodpecker similar and closely related to the European green woodpecker, but endemic to Japan.

t: The grey-headed woodpecker (Picus canus), also known as the grey-faced woodpecker, is a Eurasian member of the woodpecker family, Picidae. Along with the more commonly found European green woodpecker and the Iberian green woodpecker, it is one of three closely related species found in Europe.
f: The grey-headed woodpecker's nest is typically excavated into dead or severely damaged trees.

t: The lesser yellownape (Picus chlorolophus) is a type of woodpecker which is a widespread and often common breeder in tropical and sub-tropical Asia, primarily the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. Much of the scientific knowledge gathered about this species is sourced from formal studies in various parts of India.
f: It ranges from India, Bhutan, Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka eastwards to Thailand, Burma, Cambodia, Laos, Indonesia, Malaysia and Vietnam.

t: The black-headed woodpecker (Picus erythropygius) is a species of bird in the family Picidae.
f: It typically inhabits deciduous and coniferous forests and is found in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The crimson-winged woodpecker (Picus puniceus) is a species of bird in the woodpecker family. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, and Thailand.
f: Its diet is mainly insects and larvae.

t: The Iberian green woodpecker (Picus sharpei) is a medium-sized woodpecker endemic to the Iberian peninsula. It was formerly considered as a subspecies of the European green woodpecker but differs in having little black on the head and a dusky rather than a black ring around each eye.
f: Its sound has been described as sibilant, or hiss-like.

t: The scaly-bellied woodpecker (Picus squamatus) is a species of bird in the family Picidae.
f: It is found in the Indian subcontinent and adjoining regions, ranging across Afghanistan, Iran, India, Nepal, Pakistan, and Turkmenistan.
Levaillant's woodpecker (Picus vaillantii) or Levaillant's green woodpecker, is a large northwest African member of the woodpecker family Picidae.

t: The European green woodpecker (Picus viridis), also known as the yaffle and sometimes called a nickle, is a large green woodpecker with a bright red crown and a black moustache. Males have a red centre to the moustache stripe which is absent in females.
f: The European green woodpecker spends much of its time feeding on ants on the ground and does not often 'drum' on trees like other woodpecker species.

t: The laced woodpecker (Picus vittatus) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. A sole specimen recorded for Bangladesh has since been reidentified as a streak-breasted woodpecker.
f: It is found throughout Southeast Asia in the countries of Cambodia, China, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

t: The streak-throated woodpecker (Picus xanthopygaeus) is a species of woodpecker found in the Indian subcontinent.
f: It occurs in drier woodland, from lowland to the foothills of mountains.

t: The pine grosbeak (Pinicola enucleator) is a large member of the true finch family, Fringillidae. It is the only species in the genus Pinicola.
f: In irruption years, individuals can move long distances in search of suitable food supplies, bringing them farther south and/or downslope than is typical of years with large fruit crops.

t: The white-bellied parrot (Pionites leucogaster), or white-bellied caique in aviculture, is a species of bird in the subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, and Peru.

t: The black-headed parrot  is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots. Other colloquial names are black-crowned parrot, black-capped parrot, black-headed caique, and for subspecies P. m. pallidus, pallid caique.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The South American pileated parrot (Pionopsitta pileata) is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots. It was formerly known as the red-capped parrot, easily leading to confusion with the Australian Purpureicephalus spurius that bears that English name.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The bronze-winged parrot (Pionus chalcopterus) is a medium-sized pionus parrot 28 cm (11 in) long.
f: It is a short-tailed stocky parrot found in forest and woodland in north-western South America.
The dusky parrot (Pionus fuscus) or dusky pionus is a medium-sized mainly dark brownish-gray parrot of the genus Pionus in the true parrot family.

t: The scaly-headed parrot (Pionus maximiliani) is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots. It is found in Brazil, Bolivia, Argentina, and Paraguay.
f: It is also called scaly-headed pionus, Maximilian pionus, Maximilian parrot, Maximilian's pionus, or Maximilian's parrot.

t: The blue-headed parrot, also known as the blue-headed pionus (Pionus menstruus) is a medium-sized parrot of about 27 cm (11 in) in length. The body is mostly green, with a blue head and neck, and red undertail coverts.
f: They are affectionate, but not known for their talking ability.

t: The white-crowned parrot (Pionus senilis), also known as the white-crowned pionus in aviculture, is a small parrot which is a resident breeding species ranging from eastern Mexico to western Panama. It is found in lowlands and foothills locally up to 1600 m altitude in forest canopy and edges, and adjacent semi-open woodland and second growth.
f: It feeds on various seeds, nuts and fruits, and can be a pest in crops of corn or sorghum, and commercial fruit plantations.

t: The red-billed parrot (Pionus sordidus), also known as coral-billed pionus or red-billed pionus, is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The plum-crowned parrot (Pionus tumultuosus) or plum-crowned pionus is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru.

t: The red-throated piping guan (Pipile cujubi) is a species of bird in the chachalaca, guan, and curassow family Cracidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Brazil.

t: The blue-throated piping guan (Pipile cumanensis) is a species of bird in subfamily Penelopina of family Cracidae, the guans, chachalacas, and curassows.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, the Guianas, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The green-tailed towhee (Pipilo chlorurus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.
f: It is found in the western United States and much of Mexico.

t: The eastern towhee (Pipilo erythrophthalmus), also known as chewink, joree, or joree bird, is a large New World sparrow. The taxonomy of the towhees has been under debate in recent decades, and formerly this bird and the spotted towhee were considered a single species, the rufous-sided towhee.
f: The name "towhee" is onomatopoeic description of one of the towhee's most common calls, a short, two-part call rising in pitch and sometimes also called a "chewink" call.

t: The spotted towhee (Pipilo maculatus) is a large New World sparrow. The taxonomy of the towhees has been debated in recent decades, and until 1995 this bird and the eastern towhee were considered a single species, then named rufous-sided towhee.
f: The call may be harsher and more varied than for the eastern towhee.
The collared towhee (Pipilo ocai) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

t: The crimson-hooded manakin (Pipra aureola), also known as orange-headed manakin, is a species of passerine bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The band-tailed manakin (Pipra fasciicauda) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is a small, frugivorous passerine found in humid montane and lowland tropical forests throughout Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Peru.

t: The wire-tailed manakin (Pipra filicauda) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae.
f: It is found Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The fawn-breasted tanager (Pipraeidea melanonota) is a species of tanager with a blue head and yellow breast.
f: It occurs in the Andes of northwestern Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela, as well as in the highlands of northeastern Argentina, south Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The barred fruiteater (Pipreola arcuata) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The golden-breasted fruiteater (Pipreola aureopectus) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.

The handsome fruiteater (Pipreola formosa) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.

t: The scarlet-breasted fruiteater (Pipreola frontalis) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae. It is found in Bolivia, Ecuador, and Peru where its natural habitat is subtropical and tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is a plump green bird with a black head, the males having red throats and the females yellow.

t: The band-tailed fruiteater (Pipreola intermedia) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.

t: The orange-breasted fruiteater (Pipreola jucunda) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae native to Colombia and Ecuador. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is a plump green bird about 18 centimetres (7 in) long.

t: The black-chested fruiteater (Pipreola lubomirskii) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru, mostly on the eastern side of the Andes.
f: Its natural habitat is subtropical and tropical moist montane forests and the IUCN lists its status as being of "least concern".

t: The green-and-black fruiteater (Pipreola riefferii) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The red-banded fruiteater (Pipreola whitelyi) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.
f: It is found in Brazil, Guyana, and Venezuela.

t: The wing-barred piprites (Piprites chloris) is a species of bird in subfamily Pipritinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The grey-headed piprites (Piprites griseiceps) is a species of bird in subfamily Pipritinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers. Prior to genetic studies in 2009, it was placed in the family Pipritinae with the manakins.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The black-capped piprites (Piprites pileata), also known as the black-capped manakin, bailarín castaño, or piprites capirotado, is a species of suboscine passerine. It has been placed in the genus Piprites, part of the Tyrannidae family.
f: Until the recent rediscovery in Argentina, the only confirmed record there was a specimen taken in 1959.

t: The flame-colored tanager (Piranga bidentata), formerly known as the stripe-backed tanager, is a medium-sized American songbird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks. It is found from Mexico throughout Central America to northern Panama and occasionally in the United States; four subspecies are recognized.
f: The flame-colored tanager is 18 to 19 cm (7.1 to 7.5 in) long, the male having predominantly red-orange while the female is more yellowish orange.

t: The red-headed tanager (Piranga erythrocephala) is a medium-sized American songbird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks, endemic to Mexico. Comprising two subspecies, it is around 15 cm (5.9 in) long.
f: Males have predominantly yellow-olive plumage with a red head and throat and females have yellow forecrowns.
The red tanager (Piranga flava) is a medium-sized American songbird in the family Cardinalidae.

t: The white-winged tanager (Piranga leucoptera) is a medium-sized American songbird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks.
f: It is found from Mexico, through Central America, across northern South America and as far south as Bolivia.

t: Formerly placed in the tanager family (Thraupidae), it and other members of its genus are now classified in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae). The species' plumage and vocalizations are similar to other members of the cardinal family.
f: The western tanager (Piranga ludoviciana) is a medium-sized American songbird.

t: The scarlet tanager (Piranga olivacea) is a medium-sized American songbird in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae). It was placed in the tanager family (Thraupidae) until 2009, but was moved to Cardinalidae following several genetic studies indicating the Piranga tanagers are more closely related to cardinals and their allies.
f: Habitat fragmentation can increase nest predation and brood parasitism, and populations are declining in some areas.

t: The rose-throated tanager (Piranga roseogularis) is a medium-sized songbird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks. Endemic to the Yucatán Peninsula in Central America, it is found in Belize, Guatemala, and Mexico.
f: The male has greyish plumage with a deep rose throat and crown, while the female is similar but for a yellow crown and throat.

t: Formerly placed in the tanager family (Thraupidae), it and other members of its genus are now classified in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae). The species's plumage and vocalizations are similar to other members of the cardinal family.
f: The summer tanager (Piranga rubra) is a medium-sized American songbird.

t: The red-hooded tanager (Piranga rubriceps), is a medium-sized American songbird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The lesser kiskadee (Philohydor lictor) is a species of passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Panama and every mainland South American country except Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay, though only as a vagrant in Argentina.

t: The great kiskadee (Pitangus sulphuratus) is a passerine bird in the tyrant flycatcher family Tyrannidae. It is the only member of the genus Pitangus.
f: It was introduced to Bermuda in 1957, and to Tobago in about 1970.

t: The Philippine eagle (Pithecophaga jefferyi), also known as the monkey-eating eagle or great Philippine eagle, is a critically endangered species of eagle of the family Accipitridae which is endemic to forests in the Philippines. It has brown and white-coloured plumage, a shaggy crest, and generally measures 86 to 102 cm (2.82 to 3.35 ft) in length and weighs 4.04 to 8.0 kg (8.9 to 17.6 lb).
f: The Philippine eagle is considered the largest of the extant eagles in the world in terms of length and wing surface area, with only Steller's sea eagle and the Harpy eagle being larger in terms of weight and bulk.

t: The white-plumed antbird (Pithys albifrons) is a small species of insectivorous bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The northern variable pitohui (Pitohui kirhocephalus) is a species of pitohui in the family Oriolidae. It is found on New Guinea and a number of neighbouring islands.
f: It is also one of the few known poisonous birds.

t: The Indian pitta (Pitta brachyura) also known as Navrang, is a passerine bird native to the Indian subcontinent. It inhabits scrub jungle, deciduous and dense evergreen forest.
f: It has a distinctive two note whistling call which is heard at dawn and dusk.

t: The elegant pitta (Pitta elegans) is a species of passerine bird in the pitta family Pittidae.
f: It is endemic to Indonesia, where it is found in the Lesser Sunda Islands and Moluccas.

t: The ivory-breasted pitta (Pitta maxima) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is endemic to North Maluku in Indonesia, known as Paok halmahera.

t: The mangrove pitta (Pitta megarhyncha) is a species of passerine bird in the family Pittidae native to the eastern Indian subcontinent and western Southeast Asia. It is part of a superspecies where it is placed with the Indian pitta, the fairy pitta and the blue-winged pitta but has no recognized subspecies.
f: Its call, sometimes rendered as wieuw-wieuw, is sung from a high perch on a mangrove tree.

t: The blue-winged pitta (Pitta moluccensis) is a passerine bird in the family Pittidae. It forms a superspecies with three other pittas, the Indian pitta (P. brachyura), the fairy pitta (P. nympha) and the mangrove pitta (P. megarhyncha).
f: A clutch of about five eggs is laid and incubated by both parents, hatching after about sixteen days.

t: The fairy pitta (Pitta nympha) is a small and brightly colored species of passerine bird in the family Pittidae. The fairy pitta breeds in East Asia and migrates south to winter in Southeast Asia.
f: Its diet mainly consists of earthworms, spiders, insects, slugs, and snails.

t: The western hooded pitta (Pitta sordida) is a passerine bird in the family Pittidae. It is common in eastern and southeastern Asia and maritime Southeast Asia, where it lives in several types of forests as well as on plantations and other cultivated areas.
f: It breeds between February and August, the pair being strongly territorial and building their nest on the ground.

t: The azure-breasted pitta (Pitta steerii) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. Along with the Whiskered pitta, it is one of two endemic pittas in the country.
f: It is a striking and colorful bird having colors of red, azure, green, black and white, It is endemic to the islands of Mindanao, Bohol, Leyte and Samar in the Philippines.

t: The noisy pitta (Pitta versicolor) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. The noisy pitta is found in eastern Australia and southern New Guinea.
f: It eats earthworms, insects and snails.

t: The black-crowned antpitta (Pittasoma michleri) is a species of bird in the gnateater family, Conopophagidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist foothill forests.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, and Panama.

t: The rufous-crowned antpitta or rufous-crowned pittasoma (Pittasoma rufopileatum) is a species of bird in the gnateater family, Conopophagidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The Bornean bristlehead (Pityriasis gymnocephala), also variously known as the bristled shrike, bald-headed crow or the bald-headed wood-shrike, is the only member of the passerine family Pityriasidae and genus Pityriasis.
f: This enigmatic and vulnerable species is endemic to the southeast Asian island of Borneo, where it lives in small groups in the rainforest canopy.

t: The roseate spoonbill (Platalea ajaja) is a social wading bird of the ibis and spoonbill family, Threskiornithidae. It is a resident breeder in both South and North America.
f: The roseate spoonbill's pink color is diet-derived, consisting of the carotenoid pigment canthaxanthin, like the American flamingo.

t: The African spoonbill (Platalea alba) is a long-legged wading bird of the ibis and spoonbill family Threskiornithidae. The species belongs to the genus Platalea, which also includes species such as the Black-faced spoonbill, Eurasian spoonbill, and Roseate spoonbill.
f: The species is widespread across Africa and Madagascar, including Botswana, Kenya, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, and Zimbabwe.

t: The Eurasian spoonbill (Platalea leucorodia), or common spoonbill, is a wading bird of the ibis and spoonbill family Threskiornithidae, native to Europe, Africa and Asia.
f: The species is partially migratory with the more northerly breeding populations mostly migrating south for the winter.

t: The royal spoonbill (Platalea regia), also known as the black-billed spoonbill lives in intertidal flats and shallows of fresh and saltwater wetlands in Australia, New Zealand, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, and the Solomon Islands. It has also been recorded as a vagrant in New Caledonia.
f: It always flies with its head extended.

t: The pale-headed rosella (Platycercus adscitus), is a broad-tailed parrot of the genus Platycercus native to northeastern Australia. It is a moderate-size parrot with a pale yellow head, predominantly white cheeks, scalloped black and gold back and pale blue underparts.
f: It readily adapts to aviculture and is sold as a cagebird.

t: The green rosella or Tasmanian rosella (Platycercus caledonicus) is a species of parrot native to Tasmania and Bass Strait islands. It was described by the German naturalist Johann Friedrich Gmelin in 1788, and named on the mistaken assumption it came from New Caledonia.
f: Nesting takes place in tree hollows.

t: The crimson rosella (Platycercus elegans) is a parrot native to eastern and south eastern Australia which has been introduced to New Zealand and Norfolk Island. The species as it now stands has subsumed two former separate species, the yellow rosella and the Adelaide rosella.
f: It is commonly found in, but not restricted to, mountain forests and gardens.

t: The eastern rosella (Platycercus eximius) is a parrot native and endemic to south-eastern Australia. In New Zealand, it is now established in the North Island  and in the hills around Dunedin in the South Island.
f: It was first introduced to New Zealand in cages, and individuals were subsequently intentionally released or accidentally escaped into the wild.

t: The crested jayshrike or crested shrikejay (Platylophus galericulatus), formerly known as the crested jay (despite not being a true jay), is a species of bird found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, and Thailand. It is the only member of the genus Platylophus and the family Platylophidae.
f: Research conducted by a team led by EcoVerde Global Consulting found that the crested jayshrike is used as a “master bird” to train other songbird species.

t: The stub-tailed spadebill (Platyrinchus cancrominus) is a passerine bird in the Tyrannidae family. It is commonly found in tropical dry rainforests or tropical moist lowlands throughout Central America.
f: The stub-tailed spadebill is most easily recognizable due to its stubby tail, broad bill, and its distinctive bird song.

t: The golden-crowned spadebill (Platyrinchus coronatus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found Central America from Honduras to Panama and in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The yellow-throated spadebill (Platyrinchus flavigularis) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The russet-winged spadebill (Platyrinchus leucoryphus) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The white-throated spadebill (Platyrinchus mystaceus) is a tiny passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, on Trinidad and Tobago, and in every mainland South American country except Chile, French Guiana, Uruguay, and Suriname.

t: The white-crested spadebill (Platyrinchus platyrhynchos) is a species of passerine bird in the tyrant flycatcher family Tyrannidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The cinnamon-crested spadebill (Platyrinchus saturatus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The Malayan black magpie (Platysmurus leucopterus) is a species of bird in the family Corvidae. Treepies are a distinct group of corvids externally similar to magpies.
f: Despite its name, it is neither a magpie nor, as was long believed, a jay, but a treepie.

t: The red-cheeked wattle-eye (Platysteira blissetti) is a species of bird in the family Platysteiridae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in Cameroon, Ivory Coast, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, and Togo.

t: The chestnut wattle-eye (Dyaphorophyia castanea) is a species of bird in the family Platysteiridae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical swamps, and moist savanna.
f: It is widespread across Central Africa.

t: The yellow-bellied wattle-eye (Platysteira concreta) is a species of bird in the family Platysteiridae.
f: It is sparsely distributed across the African tropical rainforest.

t: The brown-throated wattle-eye (Platysteira cyanea), also known as the common wattle-eye or scarlet-spectacled wattle-eye, is a small, insectivorous passerine bird. The wattle-eyes were previously classed as a subfamily of the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae, but are now usually separated from that group.
f: The eggs are laid in a small neat lichen and cobweb cup low in a tree or bush.

t: The black-throated wattle-eye (Platysteira peltata) is a species of bird in the family Platysteiridae.
f: It is found in Angola, Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Eswatini, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Somalia, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

t: The striped honeyeater (Plectorhyncha lanceolata) is a passerine bird of the honeyeater family, Meliphagidae, found in Australia. It is a medium-sized honeyeater, about 23 cm (9.1 in) in length.
f: When not breeding it has been recorded feeding and travelling in small groups, but it nests singly, laying around three eggs in a deep cup-shaped nest suspended from the end of drooping branches.

t: McKay's bunting (Plectrophenax hyperboreus) is a passerine bird in the longspur family Calcariidae. Hybrids between the two species have been observed, leading some authorities to treat McKay's as a subspecies of the snow bunting.
f: It is most closely related to the snow bunting (P. nivalis).

t: The snow bunting (Plectrophenax nivalis) is a passerine bird in the family Calcariidae. There are small isolated populations on a few high mountain tops south of the Arctic region, including the Cairngorms in central Scotland and the Saint Elias Mountains on the southern Alaska-Yukon border, as well as the Cape Breton Highlands.
f: It is an Arctic specialist, with a circumpolar Arctic breeding range throughout the northern hemisphere.

t: The white-faced ibis (Plegadis chihi) is a wading bird in the ibis family, Threskiornithidae native to the Americas. Its breeding range extends from southwestern Canada and the western United States south through Mexico, as well as from southeastern Brazil and southeastern Bolivia south to central Argentina, and along the coast of central Chile.
f: This species breeds colonially in marshes, usually nesting in bushes or low trees.

t: The glossy ibis (Plegadis falcinellus) is a water bird in the order Pelecaniformes and the ibis and spoonbill family Threskiornithidae. The historical name black curlew was used for the glossy ibis in Norfolk at least until the early 19th century, and this name also appears in Anglo-Saxon literature.
f: The scientific name derives from Ancient Greek plegados and Latin, falcis, both meaning "sickle" and referring to the distinctive shape of the bill.

t: The puna ibis (Plegadis ridgwayi) is a species of waterbird in the family Threskiornithidae, spoonbills and ibises. It can be found in the altiplano and puna regions of the Andean highlands, inhabiting wetlands such as swamps, marshes and lakes, at an elevation of 3,000 to 4,500 metres (9,840 to 14,760 ft).
f: It can be found in Ecuador, Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.

t: The white-browed sparrow-weaver (Plocepasser mahali) is a predominantly brown, sparrow-sized bird found throughout central and north-central southern Africa.
f: It is found in groups of two to eleven individuals consisting of one breeding pair and other non-reproductive individuals.

t: The chestnut-crowned sparrow-weaver (Plocepasser superciliosus) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.
f: It is found in Africa south of the Sahara, from Senegal and Gambia to Eritrea, Ethiopia and western Kenya.

t: The baglafecht weaver (Ploceus baglafecht) is a species of weaver bird from the family Ploceidae which is found in eastern and central Africa. There are several disjunct populations with distinguishable plumage patterns.
f: Only some races display a discrete non-breeding plumage.

t: The dark-backed weaver (Ploceus bicolor), also known as the forest weaver, is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.
f: It is very sparsely present across central and southern Sub-Saharan Africa.
The Cape weaver (Ploceus capensis) is a species of bird in the weaver family, Ploceidae, found in southern Africa.

t: The village weaver (Ploceus cucullatus), also known as the spotted-backed weaver or black-headed weaver , is a bird species in the family Ploceidae found in much of sub-Saharan Africa. It has also been introduced to Portugal and Venezuela as well as to the islands of Hispaniola, Martinique, Puerto Rico, Mauritius and Réunion.
f: Village weavers feed principally on seeds and grain, and can be a crop pest, but readily take insects, especially when feeding young, which partially redresses the damage to agriculture.

t: Rüppell's weaver (Ploceus galbula) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae, which is native to the northern Afrotropics.
f: The species is named after the German zoologist and explorer Eduard Rüppell (1794–1884).

t: The Asian golden weaver (Ploceus hypoxanthus) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae. It is found in Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss and capture, notably for the merit release trade.

t: The lesser masked weaver (Ploceus intermedius) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae. This species is commonly parasitised by the Diederik cuckoo.
f: It builds its nests in large colonies, often alongside the village weaver and sometimes the red-billed buffalo weaver.

t: The Golden-Backed Weaver (Ploceus jacksoni), also known as Jackson's weaver, is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae. This family of birds are called weavers, because they commonly weave their nests from grasses, stems, and other plant materials.
f: Their nests are hung off of trees, or other tall places.

t: The little weaver (Ploceus luteolus) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.
f: It is found in western, central and eastern Africa.

t: These are not as common as the baya weaver but are similar looking but have streaked underparts.
f: They nest in small colonies often in reed beds near water bodies.

t: The black-headed weaver (Ploceus melanocephalus), also known as yellow-backed weaver, is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.
f: It is a resident breeder in damp areas in tropical Africa.

t: The nelicourvi weaver (Ploceus nelicourvi) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae. Together with its closest relative, the sakalava weaver, it is sometimes placed in a separate genus Nelicurvius.
f: It builds solitary, roofed, retort-shaped nests, hanging by a rope from a branch, vine or bamboo stem, in an open space.

t: Vieillot's black weaver (Ploceus nigerrimus) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae. It is found in southern Nigeria to Uganda, west Kenya, Angola and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
f: The common name is after the French ornithologist Louis Pierre Vieillot.
The black-necked weaver (Ploceus nigricollis) is a resident breeding bird species in much of central Africa from Cameroon in the west to Kenya and southern Somalia in the east.

t: The spectacled weaver (Ploceus ocularis) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae. This common species breeds in solitary pairs, and both sexes are bright yellow, have an olive-yellow back, black "spectacles" and pale eyes.
f: It is found widely in woodland, forest edge and gardens of central, eastern and south-eastern Africa, but is absent from the most arid regions (such as the Karoo) and dense, primary rainforest.

t: The baya weaver (Ploceus philippinus) is a weaverbird found across the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. Flocks are found in grasslands, cultivated areas, scrub and secondary growth.
f: They are known for their hanging retort shaped nests woven from leaves, usually found on thorny trees or palm fronds, near or hanging over water where predators cannot easily reach.

t: The Sakalava weaver (Ploceus sakalava) sometimes known as the Sakalava fody is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.
f: The bird is 15 cm (5.9 in) long and weighs 20–28 g (0.71–0.99 oz).

t: Speke's weaver (Ploceus spekei) is a familiar East African songbird. The eyes are pale and the bill is on the large side for a weaver.
f: Calls include harsh chatter at the nest and a sharp "tseep!" This species nests in colonies or occasionally singly.

t: The eastern golden weaver (Ploceus subaureus) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae. It is found in eastern and south-eastern Africa.
f: Alternative names used for the eastern golden weaver include yellow weaver, olive-headed golden weaver, and African golden weaver.

t: The southern masked weaver (Ploceus velatus), or African masked weaver, is a resident breeding bird species common throughout southern Africa. It also occurs in sub-urban gardens and parks.
f: This weaver is very widespread and found in a wide range of habitats, including shrubland, savanna, grassland, open woodland, inland wetlands and semi-desert areas.

t: The vitelline masked weaver (Ploceus vitellinus) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.
f: It is found in western, central, and eastern Africa.

t: Holub's golden weaver (Ploceus xanthops), also known as the African golden weaver, is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae. It is found from Gabon to Uganda and Kenya, south to northern Namibia, northern Botswana and eastern South Africa.
f: The common name commemorates the Czech naturalist Emil Holub.

t: The southern brown-throated weaver (Ploceus xanthopterus) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.
f: It is found in southern Africa.
The European golden plover (Pluvialis apricaria), also known as the Eurasian golden plover, greater golden plover, or just the golden plover within Europe, is a relatively large species of plover.

t: The American golden plover (Pluvialis dominica) is a medium-sized plover. The genus name is Latin and means relating to rain, from pluvia, "rain".
f: It was believed that golden plovers flocked when rain was imminent.

t: The Pacific golden plover (Pluvialis fulva) is a migratory shorebird that breeds during summer in Alaska and Siberia.
f: During nonbreeding season, this medium-sized plover migrates widely across the Pacific.

t: The grey plover or black-bellied plover (Pluvialis squatarola) is a large plover breeding in Arctic regions.
f: It is a long-distance migrant, with a nearly worldwide coastal distribution when not breeding.

t: The scaly-breasted cupwing or scaly-breasted wren-babbler (Pnoepyga albiventer) is a species of bird in the Pnoepyga wren-babblers family, Pnoepygidae.
f: It is found in southern and eastern Asia from the Himalayas to Indochina.

t: The Taiwan cupwing (Pnoepyga formosana), also known as Taiwan wren-babbler, is a species of passerine bird in the family Pnoepygidae. It was treated for a long time as a subspecies of the scaly-breasted cupwing.
f: The species is endemic to the island of Taiwan.

t: The Nepal cupwing (Pnoepyga immaculata), also known as the Nepal wren-babbler or immaculate cupwing, is a small species of passerine bird in the family Pnoepygidae. It is found in dense montane forest in the Himalayas.
f: It is native to Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Tibet, and Nepal.

t: The pygmy cupwing (Pnoepyga pusilla) or pygmy wren-babbler, is a species of bird in the Pnoepyga wren-babblers family, Pnoepygidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in southern and eastern Asia from the Himalayas to the Lesser Sunda Islands.

t: The marbled frogmouth (Podargus ocellatus) is a bird in the family Podargidae. The species was first described by Jean René Constant Quoy and Joseph Paul Gaimard in 1830.
f: It is found in the Aru Islands, New Guinea and Queensland.

t: The tawny frogmouth (Podargus strigoides) is a species of frogmouth native to the Australian mainland and Tasmania and found throughout.
f: It is a big-headed, stocky bird often mistaken for an owl due to its nocturnal habits and similar colouring.

t: The horned grebe or Slavonian grebe (Podiceps auritus) is a relatively small and threatened species of waterbird in the family Podicipedidae. There are two subspecies, P. a. auritus (Slavonian grebe), which breeds in Eurasia, and P. a. cornutus (horned grebe), which breeds in North America.
f: A small population was cited in Greenland in 1973, but is not mapped or further mentioned by subsequent authors.

t: The great crested grebe (Podiceps cristatus) is a member of the grebe family of water birds.
f: The bird is characterised by its distinctive appearance, featuring striking black, orange-brown, and white plumage, and elaborate courtship display that involves synchronised dances and displays.

t: The hooded grebe (Podiceps gallardoi) is a medium-sized grebe found in the southern region of Argentina. It grows to about 32 cm (13 in) in length, and is black and white in color.
f: It is found in isolated lakes in the most remote parts of Patagonia and spends winters along the coast of the same region.

t: The red-necked grebe (Podiceps grisegena) is an aquatic bird found in the temperate regions of the northern hemisphere. A migratory bird, its wintering habitat is largely restricted to calm waters just beyond the waves around ocean coasts, although some birds may winter on large lakes.
f: It also has an elaborate courtship display and a variety of loud mating calls.

t: A disjunct population exists in northwestern Peru, while the main distribution is from extreme southeastern Brazil to Patagonia and central Chile. The population from southern Chile is considered a separate subspecies, P. m. navasi.
f: The great grebe (Podiceps major) is the largest species of grebe in the world.

t: The black-necked grebe or eared grebe (Podiceps nigricollis) is a member of the grebe family of water birds. It was described in 1831 by Christian Ludwig Brehm.
f: In addition, it becomes flightless for at least a month after completing a migration to reach an area where it can moult safely.

t: The silvery grebe (Podiceps occipitalis) is a species of grebe in the family Podicipedidae. There are two subspecies, which by some recent authorities are considered separate species.
f: It is found in the western and southern part of South America where it inhabits lakes and other types of open wetlands.
The pied-billed grebe (Podilymbus podiceps) is a species of the grebe family of water birds primarily found in ponds throughout the Americas.
The Mongolian ground jay (Podoces hendersoni) or Henderson's ground jay is a species of bird in the family Corvidae, found in Central Asia.

t: The black-capped chickadee (Poecile atricapillus) is a small, nonmigratory, North American passerine bird that lives in deciduous and mixed forests. It is a member of the Paridae family, also known as tits.

f: It is found in Pakistan, the southern Himalayan foothills, the northeastern Indian subcontinent, and Southeast Asia.

t: The graceful prinia (Prinia gracilis) is a small warbler (in some older works it is referred to as graceful warbler). This prinia is a resident breeder in northeastern Africa (the Nile valley in particular) and southern Asia, from Egypt and Somalia east to Saudi Arabia, where it is sometimes called streaked wren-warbler.
f: The call is a rolling trilled breep, and the song is a hard rolling repetition of zerlip.

t: The grey-breasted prinia or Franklin's prinia (Prinia hodgsonii) is a wren-warbler belonging to the family of small passerine birds found mainly in warmer southern regions of the Old World. This prinia is a resident breeder in the Indian subcontinent, Sri Lanka and southeast Asia.
f: It can be confused with the rufescent prinia.

t: The Drakensberg prinia or saffron-breasted prinia (Prinia hypoxantha) is a small passerine bird. It lives in the Drakensberg's forest edges, wooded gullies and bracken covered slopes.
f: It lives in eastern South Africa and Eswatini.

t: The plain prinia (Prinia inornata), also known as the plain wren-warbler or white-browed wren-warbler, is a small cisticolid warbler found in Southeast Asia. It is a resident breeder from Pakistan and India to south China and southeast Asia.
f: The two are now usually considered to be separate species.

t: The delicate prinia (Prinia lepida) is a small warbler. There are 5 subspecies, of which P. g. akyildizi, of southern Turkey is the darkest, brownest, and most heavily streaked above, and has the brightest buff flanks.
f: This prinia is a resident breeder in southern Asia, from Turkey to North India.

t: The Karoo prinia or spotted prinia (Prinia maculosa) is a small passerine bird. It is a resident breeder in South Africa, Lesotho and far southern Namibia.
f: It is a species found in karoo scrub, fynbos and bracken-covered slopes in semi-desert and mountains.

t: The brown prinia (Prinia polychroa) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. The Burmese prinia (P. cooki) and the Annam prinia (P. rocki) were formerly lumped with this species.
f: It was named after the American ornithologist Herbert Girton Deignan.

t: The rufescent prinia (Prinia rufescens) is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry forest.
f: It is found in Southeast Asia, the Indian subcontinent (mainly in the northeast) and southern Yunnan.

t: The red-fronted prinia (Prinia rufifrons), also known as the red-fronted warbler and the red-faced apalis, is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. Its natural habitat is dry savanna.
f: It is found in Chad, Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: The ashy prinia or ashy wren-warbler (Prinia socialis) is a small warbler in the family Cisticolidae. This prinia is a resident breeder in the Indian subcontinent, ranging across most of India, Nepal, Bangladesh, eastern Pakistan, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and western Myanmar.
f: It is a common bird in urban gardens and farmlands in many parts of India and its small size, distinctive colours and upright tail make it easy to identify.

t: The striped prinia (Prinia striata) or Swinhoe's prinia is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae. It was formerly lumped with the Himalayan prinia (P. crinigera) as the striated prinia, but was split from it following a study published in 2019.
f: It is sympatric with P. crinigera in the Yunnan Province of China.

t: The tawny-flanked prinia (Prinia subflava) is a small passerine bird belonging to the genus Prinia in the family Cisticolidae, a family of Old World warblers. The plain prinia (P. inornata) of southern Asia was formerly included in this species but is now usually considered to be a separate species.
f: It is widespread and common in most parts of Africa south of the Sahara.

t: The hill prinia (Prinia superciliaris) is a species of passerine bird in the family Cisticolidae. It was formerly considered con-specific with the black-throated prinia.
f: It is found in China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam.
The jungle prinia (Prinia sylvatica) is a small passerine bird, a warbler in the family Cisticolidae.

t: The yellow-breasted flowerpecker (Prionochilus maculatus) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The scarlet-breasted flowerpecker (Prionochilus thoracicus) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The yellow-rumped flowerpecker (Prionochilus xanthopygius) is a species of bird in the family Dicaeidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, and Malaysia on the island of Borneo, to which it is endemic.
The white-crested helmetshrike (Prionops plumatus), also known as the white helmetshrike, is a species of passerine bird in the Vanga family Vangidae, formerly usually included in the Malaconotidae.
Retz's helmetshrike (Prionops retzii) is a species of bird in the helmetshrike family Vangidae, formerly usually included in the Malaconotidae.

t: The Hispaniolan trogon (Priotelus roseigaster, also known as cacos) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae. It is endemic to Hispaniola in the Caribbean.
f: It is one of the only two trogon species found in the Caribbean.

t: The Cuban trogon or tocororo (Priotelus temnurus) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae.
f: It is endemic to Cuba, where it is also the national bird.

t: The palm cockatoo (Probosciger aterrimus), also known as the goliath cockatoo or great black cockatoo, is a large, smoky-grey/black parrot of the cockatoo family native to New Guinea, the Aru Islands and the Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, Australia.
f: It has a crest of long feathers atop its head, with a very large and strong, sharply-hooked black beak (with which it can easily open nuts and seeds), and prominent bright-red cheek patches.

t: The dark-breasted rosefinch (Procarduelis nipalensis) is a species of true finch in the monotypic genus Procarduelis. Its natural habitats are boreal forests and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.
f: It is found in Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The white bellbird (Procnias albus) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, Venezuela, and as a vagrant to Trinidad.

t: The bearded bellbird (Procnias averano), also known as the campanero or anvil-bird, is a passerine bird which occurs in northern South America. The male is about 28 cm (11 in) long with white plumage apart from a brown head and black wings.
f: A single buff-coloured egg is laid and incubated solely by the female.

t: The bare-throated bellbird (Procnias nudicollis) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae. It is found in moist subtropical and tropical forests in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.
f: The male has one of the loudest known bird calls, producing a metallic sound similar to a hammer striking an anvil.

t: The three-wattled bellbird (Procnias tricarunculatus) is a Central American migratory bird of the cotinga family. The sexes are very dissimilar in appearance.
f: From the base of his beak dangle three long, slender, black wattles that he uses in display.
The grey-breasted martin (Progne chalybea) is a large swallow from Central and South America.

t: The southern martin (Progne elegans) is a species of bird in the family Hirundinidae, the swallows and martins. It has occurred as a vagrant in the Malvinas/Falkland Islands and the U.S. state of Florida
f: One source states that it is known in every mainland South American country except Colombia, Guyana, and Venezuela, and there are undocumented sight records in those three countries.

t: The purple martin (Progne subis) is a passerine bird in the swallow family Hirundinidae. It is the largest swallow in North America.
f: They are known for their speed, agility, and their characteristic mix of rapid, flapping, and gliding flight patterns.

t: The brown-chested martin (Progne tapera) is a species of passerine bird in the family Hirundinidae, the swallows and martins. It is found regularly in Panama and every mainland South American country except Chile.
f: It has been documented as a vagrant in Aruba and Chile and there are unconfirmed reports from the Falkland Islands.
The Cape sugarbird (Promerops cafer) is one of the eight bird species endemic to the Fynbos biome of the Western Cape and Eastern Cape provinces of South Africa.

t: The masked shining parrot (Prosopeia personata), also known as the masked parrot, masked musk parrot, or the yellow-breasted musk parrot is a species of parrot in the family Psittaculidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical mangrove forest, subtropical or tropical moist montane forest, arable land, and rural gardens.
f: It is endemic to Viti Levu in Fiji.

t: The maroon shining parrot or red shining-parrot (Prosopeia tabuensis), is a species of parrot in the family Psittaculidae. It is native to the islands of Vanua Levu and Taveuni in Fiji and was introduced to the islands of southern Tonga in prehistoric times.
f: The species is sometimes considered conspecific with the crimson shining parrot of Kadavu.

t: The tūī (Prosthemadera novaeseelandiae) is a medium-sized bird native to New Zealand. It is blue, green, and bronze coloured with a distinctive white throat tuft (poi).
f: It is one of the largest species in the diverse Australasian honeyeater family Meliphagidae, and one of two living species of that family found in New Zealand, the other being the New Zealand bellbird (Anthornis melanura).

t: The tūī (Prosthemadera novaeseelandiae) is a medium-sized bird native to New Zealand. It is blue, green, and bronze coloured with a distinctive white throat tuft (poi).
f: It is one of the largest species in the diverse Australasian honeyeater family Meliphagidae, and one of two living species of that family found in New Zealand, the other being the New Zealand bellbird (Anthornis melanura).

t: The prothonotary warbler (Protonotaria citrea) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family. It is named for its plumage, which resembles the yellow robes once worn by papal clerks (named prothonotaries) in the Roman Catholic Church.
f: These warblers often move with quick, jerky, movements and will even crawl upside down on sticks or trees.
The alpine accentor (Prunella collaris) is a small passerine bird in the family Prunellidae, which is native to Eurasia and North Africa.

t: The brown accentor (Prunella fulvescens) is a species of bird in the family Prunellidae. It is found in Afghanistan, China, India, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, Nepal, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan.
f: They breed between 3,300 and 5,100 meters of altitude.

t: The dunnock (Prunella modularis) is a small passerine, or perching bird, found throughout temperate Europe and into Asian Russia. It is the most widespread member of the accentor family; most other accentors are limited to mountain habitats.
f: Dunnocks have also been introduced and become common in New Zealand.

t: The Siberian accentor (Prunella montanella) is a small passerine bird that breeds in northern Russia from the Ural Mountains eastwards across Siberia. It is migratory, wintering in Korea and eastern China, with rare occurrences in western Europe and northwestern North America.
f: Adults and chicks feed mainly on insects, typically picked off the ground, but sometimes taken from vegetation.

t: Radde's accentor (Prunella ocularis) is a species of bird in the family Prunellidae. Its natural habitat is temperate grassland.
f: It is found in mountainous parts of Yemen and northern Southwest Asia.

t: The robin accentor (Prunella rubeculoides) is a species of bird in the family Prunellidae. It is found in the mountainous regions of Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan and China, at altitudes between about 3,000 and 5,500 m (9,800 and 18,000 ft).
f: It is a brown bird with a grey head and an orange-red breast.

t: The rufous-breasted accentor (Prunella strophiata) is passerine bird in the family Prunellidae, endemic to the Himalayas, descending in the winter to lower-to-middle altitudes. Its natural habitat is temperate forest.
f: It is found in Afghanistan, Bhutan, Tibet, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal, and Pakistan.
The black saw-wing (Psalidoprocne pristoptera), also known as the blue saw-wing or black rough-winged swallow, is a small passerine bird in the swallow family.

t: The American bushtit, or simply bushtit (Psaltriparus minimus), is a social songbird belonging to the monotypic genus Psaltriparus. It is one of the smallest passerines in North America and it is the only species in the family Aegithalidae found in the Americas; the other eleven species occur in Eurasia.
f: Bushtits display a unique behavior as adult males are typically the helpers that assist and raise the nestlings; hence it has intrigued many naturalists for its interesting breeding and mating patterns.

t: The long-tailed broadbill (Psarisomus dalhousiae) is a species of bird that is found in the Himalayas, extending east through Northeastern India to Southeast Asia. It is the only bird in the genus Psarisomus.
f: The female usually lays between 5 and 6 eggs that are incubated by both sexes; both sexes also help to feed the young.

t: The russet-backed oropendola (Psarocolius angustifrons) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
f: It is a "noisy and social bird that forages, nests, and roosts in groups".

t: The dusky-green oropendola (Psarocolius atrovirens) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae (New World blackbirds). Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found on the eastern slope of the Andes in Bolivia and Peru.

t: The olive oropendola (Psarocolius bifasciatus) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds. It is found in Brazil, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
f: It is a "spectacularly large oropendola".

t: The crested oropendola (Psarocolius decumanus), also known as the cornbird, is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds. It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, Trinidad and Tobago, and every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.
f: It is "[u]ndoubtedly overall the commonest and most widespread oropendola".

t: The Montezuma oropendola (Psarocolius montezuma) is a New World tropical icterid bird. It is a resident breeder in the Caribbean coastal lowlands from southeastern Mexico to central Panama, but is absent from El Salvador and southern Guatemala.
f: It also occurs on the Pacific slope of Nicaragua and Honduras and northwestern and southwestern Costa Rica.

t: The green oropendola (Psarocolius viridis) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The chestnut-headed oropendola (Psarocolius wagleri) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in Mexico, in every Central American country except El Salvador, and in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The red-rumped parrot (Psephotus haematonotus), also known as the red-backed parrot or grass parrot, is a medium-sized broad-tailed parrot endemic to open woodland in south-eastern Australia, particularly in the Murray-Darling Basin. It is a highly sexually dimorphic species, with the adult female mainly being a greyish olive-green with lighter underparts and the adult male predominantly being a brightly coloured green and gold with various shades of blue on the wings.
f: Only the adult male possesses the red rump that gives the species its common name.

t: The mulga parrot (Psephotellus varius) is endemic to arid scrublands and lightly timbered grasslands in the interior of southern Australia.
f: The male mulga parrot is multicolored, from which the older common name of many-coloured parrot is derived.

t: Brimley's chorus frog (Pseudacris brimleyi) is a species of frog in the family Hylidae.
f: It is endemic to the United States and is named for North Carolina zoologist C.S.
The spotted chorus frog or Clark's tree frog (Pseudacris clarkii) is a small, nocturnal chorus frog native to the grasslands and prairies of the central United States and Tamaulipas, Mexico.

t: The spring peeper (Pseudacris crucifer) is a small chorus frog widespread throughout the eastern United States and eastern Canada. It prefers permanent ponds due to its advantage in avoiding predation; however, it is very adaptable with respect to the habitat it can live in.
f: Crucifer is derived from the Latin root meaning "cross-bearing", a reference to the cross-like pattern on the spring peeper's dorsal side.

t: The upland chorus frog (Pseudacris feriarum) is a species of chorus frog found in the United States. It was recently separated from the Western chorus frog (Pseudacris triseriata), being identified as an individual species rather than a subspecies.
f: They are a rarely seen species, but their calls are frequently heard soon after rains in the spring time.

t: The southern chorus frog (Pseudacris nigrita) is a species of frog in the family Hylidae, endemic to the southeastern United States. Its natural habitats are temperate forests, temperate grassland, shrub-dominated wetlands, swamps, freshwater marshes, intermittent freshwater marshes, ponds, open excavations, seasonally flooded agricultural land, and canals and ditches.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The little grass frog (Pseudacris ocularis) is a species of chorus frog endemic to the Southeastern United States.
f: It is currently the smallest North American anuran and occurs in a wide variety of ephemeral and semi-permanent wetlands.

t: The ornate chorus frog (Pseudacris ornata) is a species of chorus frog endemic to the Southeastern United States.
f: Their distribution ranges from North Carolina, east to the very eastern part of Louisiana, and south to northern parts of Florida.

Strecker's chorus frog (Pseudacris streckeri) is a species of nocturnal tree frog native to the south central United States, from southern Kansas, through Oklahoma and east to Arkansas, the northwestern tip of Louisiana and south throughout much of Texas.
The western chorus frog (Pseudacris triseriata), also known as striped chorus frog, or midland chorus frog is a species of frog found in Canada and the United States.
The dusky-tailed canastero (Pseudasthenes humicola) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The white hawk (Pseudastur albicollis) is a bird of prey breeding in the tropical New World of the family Accipitridae.
f: Though it is commonly placed in the subfamily Buteoninae, the validity of this group is doubtful and currently under review.

t: The grey-backed hawk (Pseudastur occidentalis) is a Vulnerable species of bird of prey in subfamily Accipitrinae, the "true" hawks, of family Accipitridae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and far northern Peru.

t: The grey-and-white tyrannulet (Pseudelaenia leucospodia) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The cardinal lory (Chalcopsitta cardinalis) is a species of parrot in the family Psittaculidae. The cardinal lory lives mainly in the mangrove and the lowland forests of the Solomon Islands, Bougainville Island and easternmost islands of the Bismarck Archipelago.
f: It prefers Syzygium species and other fruit-bearing trees that have red blossoms.

t: The red-naped ibis (Pseudibis papillosa), also known as the Indian black ibis or black ibis, is a species of ibis found in the plains, agriculture fields and cities of the Indian subcontinent. Unlike other ibises in the region it is not found very often in waterbodies and is often found in dry fields, but are attracted more to areas that have more wetlands.
f: It builds its nest most often on the top of a large tree or palm, and an increasing number of pairs are building on cell phone towers and electricity pillion towers.

t: The streaked tuftedcheek (Pseudocolaptes boissonneautii) is a passerine bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The buffy tuftedcheek (Pseudocolaptes lawrencii) or Lawrence's tuftedcheek, is a passerine bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.
