t: The ticking doradito (Pseudocolopteryx citreola) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and possibly Paraguay.

t: Dinelli's doradito (Pseudocolopteryx dinelliana) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay, and possibly Brazil.

t: The warbling doradito (Pseudocolopteryx flaviventris) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay and Brazil.

t: The crested doradito (Pseudocolopteryx sclateri) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Guyana, Paraguay, Uruguay, and Venezuela, possibly in French Guiana, and as a vagrant to Trinidad.

t: The yellow-rumped marshbird (Pseudoleistes guirahuro) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The brown-and-yellow marshbird (Pseudoleistes virescens) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, and as a vagrant in Paraguay.

t: The kiwikiu or Maui parrotbill (Pseudonestor xanthophrys) is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper endemic to the island of Maui in Hawaii. This species is critically endangered, with an estimated population in 2016 of 250-540 individuals, but more recent estimates of less than 150 individuals.
f: It can only be found in 50 square kilometres (19 sq mi) of mesic and wet forests at 1,200–2,150 metres (3,940–7,050 ft) on the windward slopes of Haleakalā.

t: Male and female have near identical plumage. DNA-analysis confirms it is part of the weaver family.
f: It is found in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: The white-crowned manakin (Pseudopipra pipra) is a small passerine bird in the manakin family Pipridae. This common and extremely widespread manakin is one of the most easily identified, even in female plumage.
f: Males have black plumage with a white crown which can be erected as a crest, the only member of the Pipridae to possess both an all-black body and a gleaming white crown.

t: The ground tit, Tibetan ground tit, or Hume's ground tit (Pseudopodoces humilis) is a bird of the Tibetan plateau north of the Himalayas. The peculiar appearance confused ornithologists who in the past variously called it Hume's groundpecker, Hume's ground jay or Tibetan ground jay on the assumption it belonged to the family Corvidae that includes the crows and jays.
f: Although morphologically confusing, the species has since been identified using molecular sequence comparisons as being a member of the tit family (Paridae), and is now treated as the only species in the genus Pseudopodoces.

t: The rusty pitohui (Pseudorectes ferrugineus) is a species of bird in the family Pachycephalidae.
f: It is found throughout the lowlands of the Aru Islands and New Guinea.
The Caatinga cacholote (Pseudoseisura cristata) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
The white-throated cacholote (Pseudoseisura gutturalis) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The brown cacholote (Pseudoseisura lophotes) is a medium-sized bird of the ovenbird family Furnariidae. It was described by Ludwig Reichenbach in 1853, with its subspecies, argentina, described in 1960 by Kenneth Carroll Parkes.
f: Unlike many other birds, the brown cacholote builds large, pitcher-like nests year-round, each weighing many times more than the bird itself.

t: The grey-crested cacholote (Pseudoseisura unirufa) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The black-headed hemispingus (Pseudospingus verticalis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The bronze-olive pygmy tyrant (Pseudotriccus pelzelni) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, and Peru.

t: The rufous-headed pygmy tyrant (Pseudotriccus ruficeps) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru with at least one record in Venezuela.

t: The Indochinese barbet (Psilopogon annamensis), also called Annam barbet, is a bird belonging to the family Megalaimidae. It is found in Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia.
f: It inhabits tropical and subtropical forests.

t: The flame-fronted barbet (Psilopogon armillaris) is an Asian barbet native to Java and Bali. It is about 19.5–23 cm (7.7–9.1 in) long and weighs 61–79 g (2.2–2.8 oz).
f: It has a green plumage, a yellow-orange forehead, a blue nape, and an orange crescent on the chest.

t: The blue-throated barbet (Psilopogon asiaticus) is a green Asian barbet native to the foothills of the Himalayas and Southeast Asia. It inhabits lowland and montane forests at elevations of 200–2,000 m (660–6,560 ft), frequenting fruiting trees.
f: Due to its green colour, it is difficult to spot but is easily located by its continual loud calls.

t: The necklaced barbet (Psilopogon auricularis) is an Asian barbet species occurring in Laos and southern Vietnam, where it inhabits subtropical, lowland tropical moist forests and montane forests up to an altitude of 2,700 m (8,900 ft). Boden Kloss in 1919 for a barbet collected at the Langbian Plateau in southern Vietnam.
f: Cyanops franklinii auricularis was the scientific name proposed by Herbert C.

t: The yellow-eared barbet (Psilopogon australis) is an Asian barbet native to Java and Bali. It inhabits shrubland and forest up to an altitude of 2,000 m (6,600 ft).
f: Bucco australis was the scientific name proposed by Thomas Horsfield in 1821 who described a barbet from Java with yellow cheeks and breast.

t: It has been listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List since 2004 because of its wide distribution.
f: The golden-whiskered barbet (Psilopogon chrysopogon) is an Asian barbet species native to the western Malay Archipelago, where it inhabits foremost forests up to 1,500 m (4,900 ft) elevation.

t: The brown-throated barbet (Psilopogon corvinus) is a species of bird in the family Megalaimidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The black-eared barbet (Psilopogon duvaucelii) is a barbet in the family Megalaimidae native to Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra and Borneo. Because of its large range it is listed as least concern on the IUCN Red List.
f: It inhabits shrubland and forest up to an altitude of 1,200 m (3,900 ft).

t: The Bornean barbet (Psilopogon eximius) is a species of bird in the Megalaimidae family. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Indonesia and Malaysia where it is endemic to the island of Borneo.

t: The Chinese barbet (Psilopogon faber) is a bird in the family Megalaimidae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1870.
f: It is endemic to southern China.
The green-eared barbet (Psilopogon faiostrictus) is an Asian barbet.

The yellow-fronted barbet (Psilopogon flavifrons) is an Asian barbet, which is an endemic resident breeder in Sri Lanka, where it inhabits subtropical and tropical moist forests, wetlands, plantations and rural gardens up to an altitude of 2,000 m (6,600 ft).

t: It is listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List because of its wide distribution and stable population.
f: The golden-throated barbet (Psilopogon franklinii) is an Asian barbet native to Southeast Asia, where it inhabits foremost forests between 900 and 2,700 m (3,000 and 8,900 ft) altitude.

t: The coppersmith barbet (Psilopogon haemacephalus), also called crimson-breasted barbet and coppersmith, is an Asian barbet with crimson forehead and throat, known for its metronomic call that sounds similar to a coppersmith striking metal with a hammer. It is a resident bird in the Indian subcontinent and parts of Southeast Asia.
f: It carves out holes inside a tree to build its nest.

t: The yellow-crowned barbet (Psilopogon henricii) is a species of bird in the Megalaimidae family. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical swamps.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The moustached barbet (Psilopogon incognitus) is an Asian barbet. Barbets are a group of birds with a world-wide tropical distribution.
f: They get their name from the bristles which fringe their heavy bills.

The red-vented barbet (Psilopogon lagrandieri) is an Asian barbet native to Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia, where it inhabits subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The lineated barbet (Psilopogon lineatus) is an Asian barbet native to the Terai, the Brahmaputra basin to Southeast Asia.
f: It is a frugivore and nests in holes of tree trunks.

t: The Malabar barbet (Psilopogon malabaricus) is an Asian barbet native to the Western Ghats in India. It was formerly treated as a race of the crimson-fronted barbet (Psilopogon rubricapillus).
f: It overlaps in some places with the range of the coppersmith barbet (Psilopogon haemacephala) and has a similar but more rapid call.

t: The mountain barbet (Psilopogon monticola) is a species of bird in the family Megalaimidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is endemic to the Southeast Asian island of Borneo.

t: The red-throated barbet (Psilopogon mystacophanos) is a species of bird in the family Megalaimidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, and Thailand.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.
The Taiwan barbet (Psilopogon nuchalis), also known as the embroidered barbet, is a species of bird endemic to Taiwan.

t: It is listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List because of its wide distribution and stable population.
f: The black-browed barbet (Psilopogon oorti) is an Asian barbet native to Peninsular Malaysia and Sumatra, where it inhabits foremost forests between 600 and 2,000 m (2,000 and 6,600 ft) altitude.

t: The golden-naped barbet (Psilopogon pulcherrimus) is a member of the family Megalaimidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Indonesia and Malaysia, where it is endemic to the island of Borneo.

t: The fire-tufted barbet (Psilopogon pyrolophus) is a species of bird in the Asian barbet family Megalaimidae. It is native to Peninsular Malaysia and Sumatra, where it inhabits tropical moist lowland and montane forests.
f: Its scientific name was proposed by Salomon Müller in 1836, who described a barbet from Sumatra.

t: The red-crowned barbet (Psilopogon rafflesii) is part of one of the two subfamilies of Megalaimidae birds. it is in the order of woodpeckers (Piciformes) and their relatives. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and plantations with a distribution area of 3,180,000 km2 (1,230,000 sq mi).
f: It is distributed in Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia and Brunei.

The crimson-fronted barbet (Psilopogon rubricapillus), also called Sri Lanka barbet, is an Asian barbet endemic to Sri Lanka where it inhabits tropical moist lowland forests up to 1,300 m (4,300 ft) elevation.

t: It has been listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List since 2004 because of its wide distribution.
f: The great barbet (Psilopogon virens) is an Asian barbet native to the Indian sub-continent and Southeast Asia, where it inhabits forests up to 3,000 m (9,800 ft) altitude.

t: The white-cheeked barbet or small green barbet (Psilopogon viridis) is a species of Asian barbet found in southern India. The brown-headed barbet has an orange eye-ring but the calls are very similar and the two species occur together in some of the drier forests to the east of the Western Ghats.
f: Like all other Asian barbets, they are mainly frugivorous (although they may sometimes eat insects), and use their bills to excavate nest cavities in trees.
The brown-headed barbet (Psilopogon zeylanicus) is an Asian barbet species native to the Indian subcontinent, where it inhabits tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests.

t: The mountain parakeet (Psilopsiagon aurifrons), also known as the golden-fronted parakeet, is a species of parrot, one of two in the genus Psilopsiagon within the family Psittacidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.
f: It is found in the Puna grassland.

t: The grey-hooded parakeet (Psilopsiagon aymara), also known as the Aymara parakeet or Sierra parakeet, is a species of parrot in the family Psittacidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.
f: It is found in northwestern Argentina and Bolivia.

t: The spotted bamboowren (Psilorhamphus guttatus) is a species of suboscine passerine bird in the tapaculo family Rhinocryptidae. It is found in southeastern Brazil, far northeastern Argentina, and possibly Paraguay.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Psilorhamphus.
The brown jay (Cyanocorax morio) is a large jay native to Central America and southern Texas.

t: The flammulated owl (Psiloscops flammeolus) is a small migratory North American owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Psiloscops.

t: The red-masked parakeet (Psittacara erythrogenys) is a medium-sized parrot from Ecuador and Peru. They are also considered the best talkers of all the conures.
f: It is popular as a pet and are better known in aviculture as the cherry-headed conure or the red-headed conure.

t: Finsch's parakeet (Psittacara finschi), also known as the crimson-fronted parakeet and in aviculture as Finsch's conure, is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: As defined by the International Ornithological Committee (IOC), it is native to Mexico and southern Texas in the Rio Grande Valley.
f: The green parakeet (Psittacara holochlorus), green conure, or Mexican green conure is a New World parrot.

t: The white-eyed parakeet (Psittacara leucophthalmus), known in aviculture as white-eyed conure, is a species of bird in the subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile and also on Trinidad.

t: The mitred parakeet (Psittacara mitratus), also known as the mitred conure in aviculture, is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots. It is native to Argentina, Bolivia, and Peru.
f: It has been introduced to Uruguay and is established there.

t: The Pacific parakeet (Psittacara strenuus), known as Pacific conure or Nicaraguan green conure in aviculture, is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in southern Mexico, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, and Nicaragua.
It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The red-breasted parakeet (Psittacula alexandri) is a parrot native to Southeast Asia. It is among the more widespread species of the genus and is the species which has the most geographical variations.
f: Feral populations of this species have now established themselves in cities like Mumbai and Singapore.

t: Layard's parakeet or the emerald-collared parakeet, (Psittacula calthrapae) is a parrot which is a resident endemic breeder in Sri Lanka.
f: The common name of this bird commemorates the British naturalist Edgar Leopold Layard; his first wife, Barbara Anne Calthrop, whom he married in 1845, is commemorated in the specific epithet.

t: The blue-winged parakeet (Psittacula columboides), also known as the Malabar parakeet, is a species of parakeet endemic to the Western Ghats of southern India. Found in small flocks, they fly rapidly in forest clearings while making screeching calls that differ from those of other parakeet species within their distribution range.
f: Adult males and females can be easily told apart from the colour of their beak.

t: The plum-headed parakeet (Psittacula cyanocephala) is a species of parakeet in the family Psittacidae. It is endemic to the Indian subcontinent and was once thought to be conspecific with the blossom-headed parakeet (P. roseata) before being elevated to a full species.
f: They fly swiftly with twists and turns accompanied by their distinctive calls.

t: The echo parakeet (Psittacula eques) is a species of parrot endemic to the Mascarene Islands of Mauritius and formerly Réunion. Two subspecies have been recognised, the extinct Réunion parakeet  and the living echo parakeet, sometimes known as the Mauritius parakeet.
f: It is the only living native parrot of the Mascarene Islands; all others have become extinct due to human activity.

t: The Alexandrine parakeet (Psittacula eupatria), also known as the Alexandrine parrot, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula of the family Psittaculidae, native to South Asia and Southeast Asia.
f: It is named after Alexander the Great, who transported numerous birds from Punjab to various European and Mediterranean countries and regions, where they were prized by the royalty, nobility and warlords.

t: It is found in Southeast Asia from north-eastern India to Vietnam. The binomial of this bird commemorates the German naturalist and explorer Otto Finsch.
f: The grey-headed parakeet (Psittacula finschii) is closely related to the slaty-headed parakeet which together form a super-species.

t: The species' range extends from Pakistan, to Western Himalayas in India through Nepal and Bhutan and up to the Eastern Himalayas in the northeastern Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh. They descend to the valleys in winter, approximately during the last week of October.
f: The slaty-headed parakeet (Psittacula himalayana) is the only psittacid species to exhibit altitudinal migration.

t: The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, or colloquially as the Indian Ringneck, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae. It has a disjunct native range in tropical northern Africa and the Indian subcontinent, and is now introduced into many other parts of the world where populations have established themselves having been bred for the exotic pet trade and then escaped.
f: One of the few parrot species that have successfully adapted to living in disturbed habitats, it has withstood the onslaught of urbanisation and deforestation.

t: It is allopatric with the congener, the Red-breasted parakeet, Psittacula alexandri, except in the Andaman Islands where they occur together.
f: The long-tailed parakeet (Psittacula longicauda) or Burung Bayan Nuri in Malay is a parakeet endemic to the regions of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Sumatra, Borneo and Peninsular Malaysia (including Singapore).

t: The grey parrot (Psittacus erithacus), also known as the Congo grey parrot, is an African parrot in the family Psittacidae. Psittacus erithacus was previously also known as the African grey parrot until the Timneh parrot (Psittacus timneh), previously treated as a subspecies, was elevated to a full species.
f: The grey parrot is known for its intelligence, being considered one of the smartest bird species and is regarded for its speaking abilities.

t: The blue-rumped parrot (Psittinus cyanurus) is a parrot found in the very southern tip of Myanmar, peninsular Thailand, Malaysia, Borneo, Sumatra and nearby islands. It is a small parrot (18 cm) and is primarily green with bright red underwing coverts, a reddish shoulder patch, and yellowish margins on the wing coverts.
f: They eat seeds, fruit and blossoms.
The grey-headed parrotbill (Paradoxornis gularis) is a bird in the family Paradoxornithidae and is found in eastern Asia from the Himalayas to Indochina and Hainan.

t: The grey-winged trumpeter (Psophia crepitans) is a member of a small family of birds, the Psophiidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, northern Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela, north of the Amazon River.

t: The pale-winged trumpeter (Psophia leucoptera), also known as the white-winged trumpeter, is a species of bird in the family Psophiidae.
f: It is found in the western Amazon rainforest of Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.
The dark-winged trumpeter or green-winged trumpeter (Psophia viridis) is a species of bird in the family Psophiidae.

t: The groundscraper thrush (Turdus litsitsirupa) is a passerine bird of southern and eastern Africa belonging to the thrush family, Turdidae. It was previously considered the only member of the genus Psophocichla, but phylogenetic analysis supports it belonging in the genus Turdus, where it forms a sister group to the remaining Turdus species.
f: The bird has a slow whistled song and a clicking call.

t: The chirruping wedgebill (Psophodes cristatus) is a medium-sized member of the genus Psophodes, which consists or four to five songbirds endemic to Australia. Commonly found in low shrublands in south-eastern inland Australia, the species is distinguished by its distinctive, chirruping call.
f: The chirruping wedgebill and chiming wedgebill (Psophodes occidentalis) were considered to be a single species until as late as 1973, when they were separated due to marked differences in their calls.

t: The western whipbird (Psophodes nigrogularis) is a passerine bird found in several scattered populations in Southwest Australia. The western whipbird has sometimes been split into two species: the black-throated whipbird and the white-bellied whipbird.
f: It is predominantly olive green in colour.

t: The chiming wedgebill (Psophodes occidentalis), sometimes referred to as chiming whipbird, is a species of bird in the family Psophodidae. Its sound consists of 4-6 descending notes sounding like loud chimes, and the final note is underlined and interpreted as "did-you-get-drunk" or "sweet-kitty-Lintorf".
f: The chiming wedgebill and chirruping wedgebill (Psophodes occidentalis) used to be considered one species until as late as 1973, when they were separated due to marked differences in their calls.

t: The eastern whipbird (Psophodes olivaceus) is an insectivorous passerine bird native to the east coast of Australia. Heard much more often than seen, it is dark olive-green and black in colour with a distinctive white cheek patch and a black crest.
f: Its whip-crack song is a familiar sound in forests of eastern Australia.

t: The King of Saxony bird-of-paradise (Pteridophora alberti) is a bird in the bird-of-paradise family (Paradisaeidae). It is the only member of the genus Pteridophora.
f: It is endemic to montane forest in New Guinea.

t: The red-billed spurfowl (Pternistis adspersus), also known as the red-billed francolin, is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae. It is found in Southern Africa, including Angola, Botswana, Namibia, South Africa, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.
f: The species exhibits sexual dimorphism in size.
The red-necked spurfowl or red-necked francolin (Pternistis afer), is a gamebird in the pheasant family Phasianidae that is a resident species in southern Africa.

t: The Ahanta francolin or Ahanta spurfowl (Pternistis ahantensis) is a species of bird in the pheasant family, Phasianidae.
f: It is native to western Africa, where it occurs in Benin, Ivory Coast, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, and Togo.

t: The double-spurred spurfowl (Pternistis bicalcaratus) is a gamebird in the pheasant family Phasianidae of the order Galliformes, gallinaceous birds. It is a resident breeder in tropical West Africa, but there is a small and declining isolated population in Morocco.
f: Like most spurfowls, it is restricted to Africa.

t: The Cape spurfowl or Cape francolin (Pternistis capensis) is a gamebird in the pheasant family Phasianidae. It is endemic to southern Africa, where it is the largest francolin.
f: It has adapted to alien vegetation and a variety of human-altered habitats, but scrubby roosting and nesting space is a prerequisite.
Erckel's spurfowl (Pternistis erckelii), also known as Erckel's francolin, is a species of game bird in the family Phasianidae.

t: Hildebrandt's spurfowl (Pternistis hildebrandti) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae. It is found in Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Rwanda, Tanzania, and Zambia.
f: The species is named for Johann Maria Hildebrandt, who collected the first specimens in Kenya.

t: The yellow-necked spurfowl or yellow-necked francolin (Pternistis leucoscepus) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae. It is found in Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.
f: This species is named for the yellow patch found on its neck.

t: The Natal spurfowl or Natal francolin (Pternistis natalensis) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.
f: It is found in Botswana, Eswatini, Mozambique, South Africa, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

t: The scaly spurfowl (Pternistis squamatus) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.
f: It is found in Angola, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, Rwanda, São Tomé and Príncipe, Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: Swainson's spurfowl or Swainson's francolin (Pternistis swainsonii) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae which is native to southern Africa. In the Shona language in Zimbabwe, this bird is called the chikwari or horwe and is considered a delicacy by outdoor and hunting enthusiasts.
f: Swainson's spurfowl was named after William Swainson, an English ornithologist.

t: The pin-tailed sandgrouse (Pterocles alchata) is a medium large bird in the sandgrouse family. It has a small, pigeon-like head and neck and a sturdy, compact body.
f: Flocks fly to watering holes at dawn.

t: The chestnut-bellied sandgrouse or common sandgrouse (Pterocles exustus) is a species of sandgrouse. There are six recognized subspecies.
f: It is a sedentary and nomadic species that ranges from northern and central Africa and further east towards western and southern Asia.

t: The Namaqua sandgrouse (Pterocles namaqua), is a species of ground-dwelling bird in the sandgrouse family.
f: It is found in arid regions of south-western Africa.

t: The black-bellied sandgrouse (Pterocles orientalis) is a medium large bird in the sandgrouse family. The nominate race breeds in Iberian Peninsula , Northwest Africa, the Canary Islands, Turkey, Iran, Cyprus and Palestine.
f: It is a partial migrant, with central Asian birds moving to Pakistan and northern India in winter.

t: The spotted sandgrouse (Pterocles senegallus) is a species of ground dwelling bird in the family Pteroclidae. It is found in arid regions of northern and eastern Africa and across the Middle East and parts of Asia as far east as northwest India.
f: The chicks leave the nest soon after hatching and eat dry seed, the water they need being provided by the male which saturates its belly feathers with water at the waterhole.

t: The white-necked petrel (Pterodroma cervicalis), also known as the white-naped petrel, is a species of seabird in the family Procellariidae. It formerly bred on Raoul Island, but has now been extirpated from this locality due to predation by rats and cats.
f: During the non-breeding season it occurs throughout a large part of the Pacific, but it is only known to breed on Macauley Island in New Zealand's Kermadec Islands and the Australian territory of Norfolk Island and Phillip Island.

t: Cook's petrel (Pterodroma cookii) or tītī (Māori), blue-footed petrel, is a Procellariiform seabird endemic to New Zealand.
f: It is a member of the gadfly petrels and part of the subgenus Cookilaria Bonaparte, 1856, which includes the very similar Stejneger's petrel.

t: The Juan Fernández petrel (Pterodroma externa) is a species of seabird in the family Procellariidae. It was previously classified as a subspecies of the white-necked petrel (Pterodroma cervicalis), which is found in tropical waters of the Pacific and Indian Oceans.
f: It nests on a single island off the coast of Chile, in the Juan Fernández Archipelago.

t: The Bonin petrel or nunulu (Pterodroma hypoleuca) is a seabird in the family Procellariidae. It is a small gadfly petrel that is found in the northwest Pacific Ocean.
f: Its secretive habits, remote breeding colonies and limited range have resulted in few studies and many aspects of the species' biology are poorly known.

t: The mottled petrel (Pterodroma inexpectata) or kōrure is a species of seabird and a member of the gadfly petrels. It usually attains 33 to 35 cm (13–14 in) in length with a 74 to 82 cm (29–32 in) wingspan.
f: This species is highly pelagic, rarely approaching land, except to nest and rear young.

t: Zino's petrel (Pterodroma madeira) or the freira, is a species of small seabird in the gadfly petrel genus, endemic to the island of Madeira. This long-winged petrel has a grey back and wings, with a dark "W" marking across the wings, and a grey upper tail.
f: Zino's petrel nests in burrows which are visited only at night, when they give their haunting calls.

t: The Kermadec petrel (Pterodroma neglecta) is a species of gadfly petrel in the family Procellariidae. It is 38 cm long with a wingspan of 100 cm.
f: It eats squid, fish and other marine creatures.

t: The black-winged petrel (Pterodroma nigripennis) is a species of seabird in the family Procellariidae.
f: It breeds on a number of oceanic islands in the tropical and subtropical East Pacific Ocean and spends the rest of the year at sea.

t: The Galápagos petrel (Pterodroma phaeopygia) is one of the six endemic seabirds of the Galápagos. Members of Pterodroma genus are also called the gadfly petrels because their erratic twisting and turning in flight resemble that of gadflies.
f: Its scientific name derives from Ancient Greek: Pterodroma originates from pteron and dromos, meaning "wing" and "runner", and phaeopygia comes from phaios and pugios, meaning "dusky" and "rump".
The Hawaiian petrel or ʻuaʻu (Pterodroma sandwichensis) is a large, dark grey-brown and white petrel that is endemic to Hawaiʻi.

t: The black-necked aracari or black-necked araçari (Pteroglossus aracari) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The ivory-billed aracari or ivory-billed araçari (Pteroglossus azara) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
The saffron toucanet (Pteroglossus bailloni) is a species of bird in the family Ramphastidae found in the Atlantic Forest in far north-eastern Argentina, south-eastern Brazil, and eastern Paraguay.

t: The curl-crested aracari or curl-crested araçari (Pteroglossus beauharnaisii) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The red-necked aracari or red-necked araçari (Pteroglossus bitorquatus) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Brazil.

t: The chestnut-eared aracari or chestnut-eared araçari (Pteroglossus castanotis) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, and Peru.

t: The fiery-billed aracari or fiery-billed araçari (Pteroglossus frantzii) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The lettered aracari or lettered araçari (Pteroglossus inscriptus) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The many-banded aracari or many-banded araçari (Pteroglossus pluricinctus) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The collared aracari or collared araçari (Pteroglossus torquatus) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found from Mexico to Colombia and Venezuela.

t: Pterophylla camellifolia, the common true katydid, is a common North American insect. P. camellifolia belongs to the family Tettigoniidae (katydids).
f: It can be found in southeastern Canada, through the eastern United States from Maine to Florida.

t: The chestnut-throated huet-huet (Pteroptochos castaneus) is a large passerine bird of the family Rhinocryptidae. At an average mass of 165 grams (5.8 oz), it is, with the related black-throated huet-huet, the largest rhinocryptid and the third-heaviest tracheophone suboscine behind the giant and great antpittas.
f: The huet-huets are well known for their vocalisations, and the song of the chestnut-throated huet-huet is a series of resonant "hoots" that unlike its more southerly counterpart, is typically given as a duet between pairs.

t: The moustached turca (Pteroptochos megapodius) is a passerine bird which is endemic to Chile and belongs to the tapaculo family Rhinocryptidae. Common names of this species include "Turco" or "Turca".
f: It is a terrestrial bird that burrows its nest on steep hillsides and uses flight for short distances.

t: The black-throated huet-huet Spanish pronunciation: [wet wet] (Pteroptochos tarnii) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae. Its natural habitat is temperate forest.
f: It is found in southern/central Chile and adjacent western Argentina.

t: The white-throated laughingthrush (Pterorhinus albogularis) is a species of passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found mainly in the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent, primarily the Himalayas, and some adjoining and disjunct areas.
f: It ranges across Afghanistan, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Tibet and Vietnam.

t: The buffy laughingthrush (Pterorhinus berthemyi), also known as the chestnut-winged laughingthrush, is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It was formerly considered a subspecies of the rusty laughingthrush, P. poecilorhynchus; a species restricted to Taiwan following the split.
f: Compared to the rusty laughingthrush, the buffy laughingthrush has paler grey underparts, more contrasting rufous wings, broader white tips to the tail, and distinct black lores.

t: The black-throated laughingthrush (Pterorhinus chinensis) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest, mostly at submontane to montane elevations.
f: It is found in Cambodia, China, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The plain laughingthrush or Père David's laughingthrush (Pterorhinus davidi) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. Its natural habitat is temperate forests.
f: It is endemic to central and northeastern China.

t: The Wayanad laughingthrush (Pterorhinus delesserti) is a species of laughingthrush in the family Leiothrichidae. It is endemic to the Western Ghats south of Goa in India.
f: These laughingthrushes move in groups in dense forests, producing loud calls but tend to be hard to spot in the undergrowth.

t: The chestnut-capped laughingthrush (Pterorhinus mitratus), also known as the spectacled laughingthrush, is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in Sumatra (Indonesia) and the Thai-Malay Peninsula.
f: The chestnut-hooded laughingthrush was previously considered a subspecies.

t: The greater necklaced laughingthrush (Pterorhinus pectoralis) is a species of passerine bird in the family Leiothrichidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand and Vietnam.

t: The masked laughingthrush (Pterorhinus perspicillatus) is a species of laughingthrush found in China, Vietnam, Hong Kong and Macau. Its Chinese name qī zǐ-mèi (Chinese: 七姊妹 ) means 'seven brothers and sisters'.
f: It is often seen in small noisy flocks of seven.

t: The rusty laughingthrush (Pterorhinus poecilorhynchus) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It formerly included the buffy laughingthrush of mainland China as a subspecies.
f: Compared to the rusty laughingthrush, the buffy laughingthrush has paler grey underparts, more contrasting rufous wings, broader white tips to the tail, and distinct black lores.

t: The rufous-necked laughingthrush (Pterorhinus ruficollis) is a bird species in the laughingthrush family, Leiothrichidae. It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar and Nepal, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: Little study was done on this species due to its abundance and lack of interest in its conservation.

t: The white-browed laughingthrush (Pterorhinus sannio) is a bird in the family Leiothrichidae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1867.
f: It is found in China, Hong Kong, India, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The chestnut-hooded laughingthrush (Pterorhinus treacheri) is a species of bird in the laughingthrush family Leiothrichidae endemic to Borneo. It is 22–24 cm (8.7–9.4 in) long, with a chestnut brown head and chin, with grey feathering on the top of the head.
f: It is mainly found at elevations of 600–2,800 m (2,000–9,200 ft), but can be found down to 200 m (660 ft) and as high as 3,350 m (10,990 ft).

t: The white-browed shrike-babbler (Pteruthius aeralatus) is a bird species found in the eastern Himalayas and Southeast Asia from northern Burma to southern Cambodia. Like others in the genus it is found in montane forests.
f: Clements lumps this bird into the white-browed shrike-babbler.

t: The clicking shrike-babbler (Pteruthius intermedius) is a species of bird in the family Vireonidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found from Assam, India, eastern Myanmar to southern China, and southern Vietnam.

t: The black-eared shrike-babbler (Pteruthius melanotis) is a bird species in the vireo family, Vireonidae. It was traditionally considered as an aberrant Old World babbler and formerly placed in the family Timaliidae.
f: It was long noted that their habits resembled those of vireos, but this was previously ascribed to the result of convergent evolution.

t: The Himalayan shrike-babbler (Pteruthius aeralatus ripleyi) is a bird subspecies found in the western Himalayas that belongs to the shrike-babbler group. The genus was once considered to be an aberrant Old World babbler and placed in the family Timaliidae until molecular phylogenetic studies showed them to be closely related to the vireos of the New World, leading to their addition in the family Vireonidae.
f: Males and females have distinctive plumages, with the males being all black about with a cinnamon-rufous tertial patch and a distinctive white stripe running from behind the eye.

t: The black-headed shrike-babbler (Pteruthius rufiventer) is a bird species traditionally placed with the Old World babblers in the family Timaliidae. It is found in an area that ranges from eastern Nepal to northwestern Vietnam.
f: However, it might be one of the few Eurasian vireos (Vireonidae).

t: The green shrike-babbler (Pteruthius xanthochlorus) is a bird species that was earlier placed in the family Timaliidae.
f: The species is now considered to be an Asian offshoot of the American vireos and belongs in the family Vireonidae.
The wompoo fruit dove (Megaloprepia magnifica), also known as wompoo pigeon and "magnificent fruit dove" among others, is one of the larger fruit doves native to New Guinea and eastern Australia.

t: The black-naped fruit dove (Ptilinopus melanospilus), also known as the black-headed fruit dove, is a medium-sized, up to 24 cm (9.4 in) long, green fruit dove with yellowish bill and iris. The plumage of the female and the young is entirely green.
f: The male has a pale grey head with a black nape, yellow throat, and golden yellow and pink undertail coverts.

t: The yellow-breasted fruit dove (Ramphiculus occipitalis), known locally as balorinay, is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. It is endemic to the Philippines.
f: It is illegal to hunt, capture, or keep yellow-breasted fruit-doves under Philippine Law RA 9147.

t: The Palau fruit dove (Ptilinopus pelewensis) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is endemic to Palau and it is also the country's national bird.

t: The crimson-crowned fruit dove, also the Tongan fruit dove or purple-capped fruit dove (Ptilinopus porphyraceus), is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. It is found in American Samoa, Fiji, the Marshall Islands, Niue, Samoa, Tonga, and Wallis and Futuna.
f: The diet of Ptilinopus porphyraceus is mostly fruit, including figs, Meliaceae, Muntingia, Solanum torvum, Metroxylon amicarum, and ylang ylang.

The rose-crowned fruit dove (Ptilinopus regina), also known as pink-capped fruit dove or Swainson's fruit dove, is a medium-sized fruit dove that is found in parts of southern Indonesia, northern and eastern Australia and East Timor.
The white-bibbed fruit dove (Ptilinopus rivoli) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.

t: The yellow-bibbed fruit dove or yellow-banded fruit dove (Ptilinopus solomonensis) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. The Geelvink fruit dove (P. speciosus) was formerly considered conspecific, but was split as a distinct species by the IOC in 2021.
f: It is found in the Bismarck and Solomon Islands archipelagos.
The superb fruit dove (Ptilinopus superbus), also known as the purple-crowned fruit dove , is a medium-sized (22–24 cm long), colourful fruit-dove in the family Columbidae.

t: The claret-breasted fruit dove (Ptilinopus viridis) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in the Moluccas, New Guinea and the Solomon Islands archipelago.

t: The long-tailed silky-flycatcher (Ptiliogonys caudatus) is a passerine bird in the family Ptiliogonatidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The grey silky-flycatcher (Ptiliogonys cinereus) is a species of bird in the family Ptiliogonatidae.
f: It is found in Guatemala and Mexico and as a vagrant in Texas, United States.

t: The falcated wren-babbler (Ptilocichla falcata) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss Along with the Melodious babbler and Palawan flycatcher, they have been dubbed the Tres Amigos (Spanish) or Three Friends as some of the most sought after birds in Palawan.

t: The Bornean wren-babbler (Ptilocichla leucogrammica) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, and Malaysia, where it is endemic to the island of Borneo.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The striated wren-babbler (Ptilocichla mindanensis) is a species of passerine bird in the Pellorneidae family. Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forest and the lower reaches of tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines found on the islands of Bohol, Samar, Leyte, Basilan, Dinagat Islands and Mindanao.

t: The satin bowerbird (Ptilonorhynchus violaceus) is a species of passerine bird in the bowerbird family Ptilonorhynchidae that is endemic to eastern Australia.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Ptilonorhynchus.

t: The stone partridge (Ptilopachus petrosus) is a bird of the New World quail family.
f: This largely brown bird, which commonly holds its tail raised, is found in scrubland and lightly wooded habitats, often near rocks, from Kenya and Ethiopia to Gambia (a large part of its range is in the Sudanian Savanna).

t: The rufous-backed honeyeater (Ptiloprora guisei) is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is endemic to Papua New Guinea.

t: The grey-streaked honeyeater (Ptiloprora perstriata), also known as the black-backed honeyeater, is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in the New Guinea Highlands.

t: The northern white-faced owl (Ptilopsis leucotis) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae. The southern white-faced owl (P. granti) was formerly included in this species and the two were known as the white-faced scops-owl.
f: It is found in a band across Africa between the Sahara and the Equator.

t: The magnificent riflebird (Ptiloris magnificus) is a species of passerine bird in the birds-of-paradise family Paradisaeidae. Magnificent riflebirds are widely distributed throughout lowland rainforests of western New Guinea and the northern Cape York Peninsula of Australia.
f: It is listed on Appendix II of CITES.

t: The paradise riflebird (Ptiloris paradiseus) is a passerine bird of the family Paradisaeidae. It is one of four riflebird species in the genus Ptiloris.
f: During breeding season, males are promiscuous and perform solitary displays for females, which involves moving rapidly from side to side with the head tilted back, showing off the neck plumage.

t: The blue jewel-babbler (Ptilorrhoa caerulescens) is a species of bird in the family Cinclosomatidae, endemic to New Guinea. Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland rainforests, typically primary rather than secondary forests.
f: In Wampar, spoken among the people who live in Markham Valley of New Guinea, it is referred to as the birisis.

t: The chestnut-backed jewel-babbler (Ptilorrhoa castanonota) is a species of bird in the family Cinclosomatidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The spotted jewel-babbler (Ptilorrhoa leucosticta) is a species of bird in the family Cinclosomatidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in the New Guinea Highlands.

t: The piapiac (Ptilostomus afer) is an African bird in the crow family, and is the only member of the genus Ptilostomus.
f: It is most closely related to the Central Asian ground jays.

t: The fuscous honeyeater (Ptilotula fusca) is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. The fuscous honeyeater was previously placed in the genus Lichenostomus, but was moved to Ptilotula after a molecular phylogenetic analysis, published in 2011, showed that the original genus was polyphyletic.
f: It is endemic to eastern Australia, where it inhabits subtropical and tropical dry forests.

t: The yellow-plumed honeyeater (Ptilotula ornata) is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. The yellow-plumed honeyeater was previously placed in the genus Lichenostomus, but was moved to Ptilotula after a molecular phylogenetic analysis, published in 2011, showed that the original genus was polyphyletic.
f: It is endemic to Australia, where it inhabits temperate forests and Mediterranean-type shrubby vegetation.

t: The white-plumed honeyeater (Ptilotula penicillata, formerly Lichenostomus penicillatus) is a medium-sized passerine of the family Meliphagidae (honeyeaters) endemic to mainland Australia. Its key identifying characteristics are a primarily olive-grey body and yellow face, a slightly down-curved bill and its white distal neck-plumes from which it takes its name.
f: Honeyeaters are most diverse group of passerine birds on continental Australia and the White-plumed honeyeater is one of the most common honeyeaters of urban areas throughout much of Australia.
The Cuban blackbird (Ptiloxena atroviolacea) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds.

t: The dusky crag martin (Ptyonoprogne concolor) is a small passerine bird in the swallow family. It is about 13 cm (5 in) long with a broad body and wings, and a short square tail that has small white patches near the tips of most of its feathers.
f: Both adults incubate the two to four eggs and feed the chicks.

t: The large rock martin (Ptyonoprogne fuligula), also known as the southern crag-martin, is a small passerine bird in the swallow family that is resident in southern Africa. It was formerly considered to be conspecific with the red-throated rock martin.
f: Both parents then feed the chicks.

t: The Eurasian crag martin or just crag martin (Ptyonoprogne rupestris) is a small passerine bird in the swallow family. It is about 14 cm (5.5 in) long with ash-brown upperparts and paler underparts, and a short, square tail that has distinctive white patches on most of its feathers.
f: Two to five brown-blotched white eggs are incubated mainly by the female, and both parents feed the chicks.

t: The koklass pheasant (Pucrasia macrolopha) is a species of gamebird, being closely related to progenitive grouse that lived during the Miocene. They are distantly related to pheasants and are most closely related to grouse and turkeys.
f: They are one of the few gamebirds that regularly fly uphill and are capable of sustained flights of many miles.
The tropical shearwater (Puffinus bailloni) is a seabird in the family Procellariidae formerly considered conspecific with Audubon's shearwater (Puffinus lherminieri).

t: The Christmas shearwater or ʻaoʻū (Puffinus nativitatis) is a medium-sized shearwater of the tropical Central Pacific. It is a poorly known species due to its remote nesting habits, and it has not been extensively studied at sea either.
f: Its only close living relative is the Galápagos shearwater (P. subalaris).

t: Newell's shearwater or Hawaiian shearwater (ʻaʻo), (Puffinus newelli) is a seabird in the family Procellariidae. It belongs to a confusing group of shearwaters which are difficult to identify and whose classification is controversial.
f: This shearwater is the only seabird endemic to the Hawaiian Islands.

t: The Manx shearwater (Puffinus puffinus) is a medium-sized shearwater in the seabird family Procellariidae. The scientific name of this species records a name shift: Manx shearwaters were called Manks puffins in the 17th century.
f: Puffin is an Anglo-Norman word (Middle English pophyn) for the cured carcasses of nestling shearwaters.

t: The tawny-browed owl (Pulsatrix koeniswaldiana) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The band-bellied owl (Pulsatrix melanota) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru.

t: The spectacled owl (Pulsatrix perspicillata) also called a Murucututu, is a large tropical owl native to the neotropics. It is a resident breeder in forests from southern Mexico and Trinidad, through Central America, south to southern Brazil, Paraguay, and northwestern Argentina.
f: One is occasionally treated as a separate species called the short-browed or brown-spectacled owl but the consensus is that it is still merely a race until more detailed analysis can be done.

t: The white-fronted honeyeater (Purnella albifrons) is a medium-sized bird species endemic to Australia. Mainly distributed throughout arid and semi-arid landscapes.
f: The specific epithet combines albus meaning 'white' with frons meaning 'forehead' or 'front'.

t: The red-capped parrot (Purpureicephalus spurius) is a species of broad-tailed parrot native to southwestern Australia. It was described by Heinrich Kuhl in 1820, with no subspecies recognised.
f: Nesting takes place in tree hollows, generally of older large trees.

t: The sooty-headed bulbul (Pycnonotus aurigaster) is a species of songbird in the Bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in south-eastern Asia.

t: The common bulbul (Pycnonotus barbatus) is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds. Ten subspecies are recognised based on the geographical variation in plumage.
f: It is widespread throughout most of Africa except for the very arid areas, and has recently begun breeding in southernmost Spain.

t: The Asian red-eyed bulbul (Pycnonotus brunneus) is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found on the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, and Borneo.

t: The red-vented bulbul (Pycnonotus cafer) is a member of the bulbul family of passerines. It is a resident breeder across South Asia extending east to Burma.
f: It has been introduced in many other parts of the world and has established itself in Argentina, Tonga and Fiji, as well as parts of Samoa, USA and Cook Islands.

t: The Cape bulbul (Pycnonotus capensis) is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds. It is an endemic resident breeder in coastal bush, open forest, gardens and fynbos in western and southern South Africa.
f: This species nests mainly in the southern spring from September to November.

t: The streak-eared bulbul (Pycnonotus conradi) is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds. It is found from Thailand and northern and central Malay Peninsula to southern Indochina.
f: Until 2016, the streak-eared bulbul was considered to be conspecific with the Ayeyarwady bulbul while still using the name 'streak-eared bulbul' (as Pycnonotus blanfordi).

t: The stripe-throated bulbul (Pycnonotus finlaysoni), or streak-throated bulbul, is a species of songbird in the bulbul family of passerine birds. It is a common species and the International Union for Conservation of Nature has assessed it as being of "least concern".
f: It is found in south-eastern Asia where its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forest and tropical moist montane forest.

t: The flavescent bulbul (Pycnonotus flavescens) is a species of songbird in the bulbul family of passerine birds. It is found in south-eastern Asia.
f: Its name comes from flavescent, a yellowish colour.

t: The yellow-vented bulbul (Pycnonotus goiavier), or eastern yellow-vented bulbul, is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds. It is a resident breeder in southeastern Asia from Indochina to the Philippines.
f: It is one of the most common birds in cultivated areas.

t: The red-whiskered bulbul (Pycnonotus jocosus), or crested bulbul, is a passerine bird native to Asia. It is a member of the bulbul family.
f: It has a loud three or four note call, feeds on fruits and small insects and perches conspicuously on trees.
The Himalayan bulbul (Pycnonotus leucogenys), or white-cheeked bulbul, is a species of songbird in the bulbul family found in Central and South Asia.

t: The white-eared bulbul (Pycnonotus leucotis) is a member of the bulbul family.
f: It is found in south-western Asia from India to the Arabian peninsula.

t: The white-browed bulbul (Pycnonotus luteolus) is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds. It is a resident breeder in Sri Lanka and peninsular India.
f: They are found in dense scrub habitats, where they skulk within vegetation and can be difficult to see although their loud and distinct burst of calls is distinctive.

t: The African red-eyed bulbul or black-fronted bulbul (Pycnonotus nigricans) is a species of songbird in the family Pycnonotidae. It is found in south-western Africa.
f: It feeds on fruit (including Ficus), flowers, nectar, and insects.

t: The olive-winged bulbul (Pycnonotus plumosus) is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in south-eastern Asia and the Greater Sunda Islands.

t: The cream-vented bulbul (Pycnonotus simplex) is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds. It is found in south-eastern Asia from the Malay Peninsula to Borneo.
f: Its breast might sometimes look a little yellow.

t: The light-vented bulbul (Pycnonotus sinensis), also called the Chinese bulbul, is a species of bird in the bulbul family found in Asia.
f: A common species of songbird that favors lightly wooded habitats, it can frequently be seen in towns, suburbs and urban parks within its range.

t: The striated bulbul (Alcurus striatus) is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. It is found from the eastern Himalayas to northern Vietnam.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Alcurus .

t: Styan's bulbul (Pycnonotus taivanus) is a species of bulbul that is endemic to eastern and southern Taiwan. Its decline has been caused by habitat destruction and hybridisation with the closely related Chinese or light-vented bulbul.
f: Though locally common in some areas, it has been listed as a species vulnerable to extinction.

t: The yellow-throated bulbul (Pycnonotus xantholaemus) is a species of songbird in the bulbul family of passerine birds. The species is endemic to southern peninsular India.
f: It is confusable only with the white-browed bulbul with which its range overlaps but is distinctively yellow on the head and throat apart from the yellow vent.

t: The white-spectacled bulbul (Pycnonotus xanthopygos) is a member of the bulbul family. It is 20–25 cm (7.9–9.8 in) in length with a wingspan of 20–25 cm (7.9–9.8 in).
f: The nest – a small cup of thin twigs, grass stems, leaves and moss – is generally located in bushes and lined with hair, shredded bark and small roots.

t: The species was first described by John Anderson in 1869.It is found in south-eastern Asia from central and southern China to Myanmar and northern Thailand.
f: The brown-breasted bulbul (Pycnonotus xanthorrhous) is a songbird in the family Pycnonotidae.

t: The straw-headed bulbul (Pycnonotus zeylanicus) is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. It is found from the Malay Peninsula to Borneo.
f: The straw-headed bulbul is prized for its singing ability and is a highly sought-after species by bird enthusiasts in Southeast Asia, especially Indonesia.

t: The pilotbird (Pycnoptilus floccosus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is monotypic within the genus Pycnoptilus.
f: The species is endemic to south-eastern Australia.

t: The white-throated treerunner (Pygarrhichas albogularis) is a species of bird in the family Furnariidae. It is the only species in the genus Pygarrhichas.
f: The white-throated treerunner consumes small invertebrates found on bark and nests in tree cavities.

t: The spot-winged antshrike (Pygiptila stellaris) is a species of bird in subfamily Myrmornithinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, Venezuela, and possibly French Guiana.

t: The blue-and-white swallow (Pygochelidon cyanoleuca) is a passerine bird that breeds from Nicaragua south throughout South America, except in the deserts and the Amazon Basin. The nominate northern race may have bred on that island.
f: The southern race is migratory, wintering as far north as Trinidad, where it is a regular visitor.

t: The Adélie penguin (Pygoscelis adeliae) is a species of penguin common along the entire coast of the Antarctic continent. It is the most widespread penguin species in the Antarctic, and, along with the emperor penguin, is the most southerly distributed of all penguins.
f: It is named after Adélie Land, in turn, named for Adèle Dumont d'Urville, who was married to French explorer Jules Dumont d'Urville, who first discovered this penguin in 1840.

t: The chinstrap penguin (Pygoscelis antarcticus) is a penguin species that inhabits various islands and shores in the Southern Pacific and the Antarctic Oceans. Its name stems from the narrow black band under its head, which makes it appear to wear a black helmet.
f: It is known for its loud, harsh call.

t: The gentoo penguin (Pygoscelis papua) is a species complex in the genus Pygoscelis, most closely related to the Adélie penguin (P. adeliae) and the Chinstrap penguin (P. antarcticus). The species calls in a variety of ways, but the most frequently heard is a loud, trumpeting call, emitted with the head thrown back.
f: The earliest scientific description was made in 1781 by Johann Reinhold Forster with a type locality in the Falkland Islands.

t: The fringe-backed fire-eye (Pyriglena atra), for a time known as Swainson's fire-eye, is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: In Brazilian Portuguese it is called papa-taoca-da-bahia.
The East Amazonian fire-eye (Pyriglena leuconota) is an insectivorous bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The white-shouldered fire-eye (Pyriglena leucoptera) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The western fire-eye (Pyriglena maura) is an insectivorous bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, and Peru.

t: The orange-cheeked parrot (Pyrilia barrabandi), also known as Barraband's parrot, is a species of parrot in the family Psittacidae. It was formerly placed in the genus Pionopsitta, which is now monotypic.
f: They are threatened with loss of habitat due to the increasing deforestation of the Amazon.

t: The caica parrot (Pyrilia caica) is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The brown-hooded parrot (Pyrilia haematotis) is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found from Mexico to Colombia.

t: The rose-faced parrot (Pyrilia pulchra) is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The saffron-headed parrot (Pyrilia pyrilia) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Colombia, Panama, and Venezuela.

t: The scarlet flycatcher or austral vermilion flycatcher (Pyrocephalus rubinus) is a passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: The red-ruffed fruitcrow (Pyroderus scutatus) is a species of bird in the monotypic genus Pyroderus. It belongs to the family Cotingidae, and is one of the largest passerines in South America.
f: Its common names in Spanish include yacutoro, toropisco montañero, sangretoro, pájaro torero, and cuervo-frutero de garganta roja.

t: The fire-eyed diucon (Pyrope pyrope) is a passerine bird of South America belonging to the tyrant flycatcher family Tyrannidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Chile and as a vagrant to the Falkland Islands.

t: The Alpine chough (; chuf) or yellow-billed chough (Pyrrhocorax graculus) is a bird in the crow family, one of only two species in the genus Pyrrhocorax. Its two subspecies breed in high mountains from Spain eastwards through southern Europe and North Africa to Central Asia and Nepal, and it may nest at a higher altitude than any other bird.
f: Its eggs have adaptations to the thin atmosphere that improve oxygen take-up and reduce water loss.

t: The red-billed chough, Cornish chough or simply chough ( CHUF; Pyrrhocorax pyrrhocorax) is a bird in the crow family, one of only two species in the genus Pyrrhocorax. Its eight subspecies breed on mountains and coastal cliffs from the western coasts of Ireland and Britain east through southern Europe, North Africa and Middle East to Central Asia, India and China.
f: The red-billed chough pairs for life and displays fidelity to its breeding site, which is usually a cave or crevice in a cliff face.

t: The redthroat (Pyrrholaemus brunneus) is a small, mostly ground-dwelling species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is endemic to Australia, occurring mostly in arid and semi-arid areas containing acacia and chenopod shrublands.
f: The species has a distinctive red throat patch and is able to mimic the calls of numerous other bird species.

t: The speckled warbler (Pyrrholaemus sagittatus) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. Its natural habitat is temperate forests.
f: It is endemic to eastern Australia.

t: The cinnamon flycatcher (Pyrrhomyias cinnamomeus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is native to the cloud forests of the Andes and other South American mountain ranges, and is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The Grey-headed bullfinch (Pyrrhula erythaca), Gray-headed bullfinch, or Beavan's Bullfinch is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae. Its natural habitats are boreal forest and temperate forest.
f: It is widespread across China ; also present in Bhutan, northeast India and Taiwan ; wintering range extends to eastern Burma.

t: The spotted fantail (Rhipidura perlata) is a species of bird in the family Rhipiduridae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found throughout Sumatra, Borneo and the southern Malay Peninsula.

t: The Australian rufous fantail (Rhipidura rufifrons) is a small passerine bird, most commonly known also as the black-breasted rufous-fantail or rufous-fronted fantail, which can be found in Australia. Characteristic of species that have a large range, the Australian rufous fantail has many subspecies.
f: They are migratory, travelling to south-eastern Australia in the spring to breed, and then north in the autumn.

t: The northern fantail (Rhipidura rufiventris) is a species of bird in the family Rhipiduridae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.
f: It is found in New Guinea, Timor, and northern Australia .

t: The Sulawesi fantail (Rhipidura teysmanni) is a species of bird in the family Rhipiduridae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is endemic to Sulawesi in Indonesia.
The sooty thicket fantail (Rhipidura threnothorax) is a species of bird in the family Rhipiduridae.

t: The New Caledonian streaked fantail (Rhipidura verreauxi) is a species of bird in the family Rhipiduridae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is endemic to New Caledonia, and the Loyalty Islands (but not Ouvéa Island).

t: The rosy thrush-tanager (Rhodinocichla rosea) or rose-breasted thrush-tanager is a species of bird in its own family, Rhodinocichlidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Mexico, Panama, and Venezuela.

t: The rosy-patched bushshrike (Rhodophoneus cruentus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in Djibouti, Egypt, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Sudan, and Tanzania.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Rhodophoneus.

t: The crimson-breasted finch, or crimson finch, (Rhodospingus cruentus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Ecuador, Peru, and possibly Colombia.

t: Its taxonomy is confused, and it has formerly been placed in Fringilla, Bucanetes, Carduelis and Rhodopechys.
f: The desert finch (Rhodospiza obsoleta), sometimes called Lichtenstein's desert finch, is a large brown true finch found in southern Eurasia.

t: Ross's gull (Rhodostethia rosea) is a small gull, the only species in its genus, although it has been suggested the genus should be merged with the closely related Hydrocoloeus, which otherwise only includes the little gull. Its breeding grounds were first discovered in 1905 by Sergei Aleksandrovich Buturlin near the village of Pokhodsk in northeastern Yakutia, while visiting the area as a judge.
f: This bird is named after the British explorer James Clark Ross.

t: The crimson-collared grosbeak (Periporphyrus celaeno) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals, grosbeaks, and “tanager” allies.
f: It is endemic to Mexico but has occurred several times as a vagrant in southern Texas in the U.

t: The star-throated antwren (Rhopias gularis) is an insectivorous bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is endemic to southeastern Brazil.

t: The Beijing babbler (Rhopophilus pekinensis), also known as the white-browed Chinese warbler, Chinese hill warbler, or Chinese bush-dweller, is a species of bird in the genus Rhopophilus. It is found in northern China and North Korea, and formerly occurred in South Korea.
f: It is now thought to be a close relative of the parrotbilss and is placed in the family Paradoxornithidae; previously, it was placed in the families Cisticolidae, Timaliidae or Sylviidae.
The slender antbird (Rhopornis ardesiacus) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The band-tailed sierra finch (Rhopospina alaudina) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The blue finch or yellow-billed blue finch (Rhopospina caerulescens) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Brazil.

t: The mourning sierra finch (Rhopospina fruticeti) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru and has been recorded as a vagrant to Brazil and the Falkland Islands.

t: The eye-ringed flatbill (Rhynchocyclus brevirostris) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country, and Colombia.

t: The eastern olivaceous flatbill (Rhynchocyclus olivaceus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The thick-billed longspur, also known as McCown's longspur (Rhynchophanes mccownii), is a small ground-feeding bird in the family Calcariidae, which also contains the other longspurs and snow buntings.
f: It is found in North America and is the only species in the genus Rhynchophanes.

t: The thick-billed parrot (Rhynchopsitta pachyrhyncha) is a medium-sized parrot endemic to Mexico that formerly ranged into the southwestern United States. Its position in parrot phylogeny is the subject of ongoing discussion; it is sometimes referred to as thick-billed macaw or thick-billed conure.
f: In Mexico, it is locally called guacamaya ("macaw") or cotorra serrana ("mountain parrot").

t: The maroon-fronted parrot (Rhynchopsitta terrisi) is a large, macaw-like parrot. It is dark green with a dark red shoulder and a maroon forehead and eye-stripe.
f: The species is endemic to northeastern Mexico, where only about 2500–3000 birds survive in the wild.

t: The tawny-faced quail (Rhynchortyx cinctus) is a species of bird in the family Odontophoridae, the New World quail.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The Tumbes sparrow (Rhynchospiza stolzmanni) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae found in Ecuador and Peru.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.

t: The Chaco sparrow (Rhynchospiza strigiceps), formerly known as the stripe-capped sparrow, is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Paraguay.

t: The red-winged tinamou (Rhynchotus rufescens) is a medium-sized ground-living bird from central and eastern South America.
f: Other common names for the species include perdiz grande, rufous tinamou, and ynambu.

t: The kagu or cagou (Rhynochetos jubatus) is a crested, long-legged, and bluish-grey bird endemic to the dense mountain forests of New Caledonia. It is the only surviving member of the genus Rhynochetos and family Rhynochetidae, although a second species has been described from the fossil record.
f: Its nasal corns are a unique feature not shared with any other bird.

t: The knobbed hornbill (Rhyticeros cassidix), also known as Sulawesi wrinkled hornbill, is a colourful hornbill native to Indonesia. The species is sometimes placed in the genus Aceros.
f: The knobbed hornbill is the faunal symbol of South Sulawesi province.

t: Blyth's hornbill (Rhyticeros plicatus), also known as the Papuan hornbill, is a large hornbill inhabiting the forest canopy in Wallacea and Melanesia. Previously, this hornbill was placed in the genus Aceros.
f: Its local name in Tok Pisin is kokomo.

t: The wreathed hornbill (Rhyticeros undulatus) is an Old World tropical bird of the hornbill family Bucerotidae, also called bar-pouched wreathed hornbill due to its distinctive blue-black band on its lower throat sac. Males are black with a rufous crown, a white upper breast and face, and a yellow featherless throat.
f: It is named after its characteristic long, curved bill that develops ridges, or wreaths, on the casque of the upper mandible in adults.

t: The rufous mourner (Rhytipterna holerythra) is a passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country except El Salvador, Colombia, and Ecuador.

t: The pale-bellied mourner (Rhytipterna immunda) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Guyana, Suriname, Venezuela, and possibly French Guiana.

t: The greyish mourner (Rhytipterna simplex) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The grey-throated martin or Asian plain martin (Riparia chinensis) is a small passerine bird in the swallow family. It is found from Tajikistan, Afghanistan and Indian subcontinent to southern China, Taiwan, and the northern Philippines.
f: The grey-throated martin is found in open habitats such as farmland, grassland and savannah, usually near water.

t: The pale martin or pale sand martin (Riparia diluta) is a small passerine bird in the swallow family. It is found from Central Asia to southeastern China.
f: It is found in open habitats such as farmland, grassland and savannah, usually near water.

t: The brown-throated martin, brown-throated sand martin or plain martin (Riparia paludicola) is a small passerine bird in the swallow family, Hirundinidae, that is widely distributed across Africa.
f: It was formerly regarded as conspecific with the grey-throated martin (Riparia chinensis) and the Madagascar martin (Riparia cowani).

t: The sand martin (Riparia riparia), also known as the collared sand martin or common sand martin, and in the Americas as the bank swallow, is a migratory passerine bird in the swallow family Hirundinidae. It winters in eastern and southern Africa, southern Asia, and South America.
f: It has a wide range in summer, embracing practically the whole Holarctic area, from Europe, across Asia to the Pacific Ocean, and throughout North America.

t: The black-legged kittiwake (Rissa tridactyla) is a seabird species in the gull family Laridae. This species was first described by Carl Linnaeus in his landmark 1758 10th edition of Systema Naturae as Larus tridactylus.
f: The English name is derived from its call, a shrill 'kittee-wa-aaake, kitte-wa-aaake'.

t: It is the only member of the genus Rollulus. This small partridge is a resident breeder in lowland rainforests in south Burma, south Thailand, Malaysia, Sumatra and Borneo.
f: The crested partridge is usually seen singly or in pairs as it uses its feet to probe the forest floor for fruit, seeds and invertebrates.

t: The Roraiman barbtail (Roraimia adusta) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Guyana, and Venezuela.

t: The greater painted-snipe (Rostratula benghalensis) is a species of wader in the small painted-snipe family Rostratulidae. It widely distributed across Africa and southern Asia and is found in a variety of wetland habitats, including swamps and the edges of larger water bodies such as lakes and rivers.
f: The female is normally polyandrous with the males incubating the eggs and caring for the young.

t: The snail kite (Rostrhamus sociabilis) is a bird of prey within the family Accipitridae, which also includes the eagles, hawks, and Old World vultures. Usually, it is placed in the Milvine kites, but the validity of that grouping is under investigation.
f: Its relative, the slender-billed kite, is now again placed in Helicolestes, making the genus Rostrhamus monotypic.

t: The spectacled bulbul (Rubigula erythropthalmos), also known as the lesser brown bulbul, is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds. The spectacled bulbul was originally described in the genus Ixos.
f: It is found on the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, and Borneo.

t: The black-crested bulbul (Rubigula flaviventris) is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds.
f: It is found from the Indian subcontinent to southeast Asia.

t: The flame-throated bulbul (Rubigula gularis) is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds and the state bird of Goa. It is found only in the forests of the Western Ghats in southern India.
f: They have a call often with two or three tinkling notes that can sound similar to those produced by the red-whiskered bulbul.

t: The Andean cock-of-the-rock (Rupicola peruvianus), also known as tunki (Quechua), is a large passerine bird of the cotinga family native to Andean cloud forests in South America. It has four subspecies and its closest relative is the Guianan cock-of-the-rock.
f: It is the national bird of Peru.

t: The Guianan cock-of-the-rock (Rupicola rupicola) is a species of cotinga, a passerine bird from South America. It is about 30 cm (12 in) in length and weighs about 200 to 220 g (7.1 to 7.8 oz).
f: During the height of the mating season, males engage in competitive displays in the lek, which is a complex courting behaviour that is done to attract females.

t: The roadside hawk (Rupornis magnirostris) is a relatively small bird of prey found in the Americas. It has many subspecies and is now usually placed in the monotypic genus Rupornis instead of Buteo.
f: This vocal species is often the most common raptor in its range.

t: The black skimmer (Rynchops niger) is a tern-like seabird, one of three similar bird species in the skimmer genus Rynchops in the gull family Laridae.
f: It breeds in North and South America.
