t: The secretarybird or secretary bird (Sagittarius serpentarius) is a large bird of prey that is endemic to Africa. It is mostly terrestrial, spending most of its time on the ground, and is usually found in the open grasslands and savanna of the sub-Saharan region.
f: Breeding can take place at any time of year, but tends to be late in the dry season.

t: The black-crested antshrike (Sakesphorus canadensis) is a passerine bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in tropical South America in Trinidad, Colombia, Venezuela, the Guianas, Brazil, and Peru.
The silvery-cheeked antshrike (Sakesphoroides cristatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
The glossy antshrike (Sakesphorus luctuosus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The rock wren (Salpinctes obsoletus) is a small songbird of the wren family native to the rocky areas of western North America. There are 8 subspecies of the rock wren, one of which is extinct.
f: They are noted for their variable song and song pattern, used for territory defense, as well as their habit of building "pavements" with flat rocks around their nest to help nestlings stay dry.

t: The African spotted creeper (Salpornis salvadori) is a small passerine bird in the family Salpornithidae. It is found in subsaharan Africa in open deciduous forest and mango groves.
f: It does not migrate other than local movements.

t: The Lesser Antillean saltator (Saltator albicollis) is a species of songbird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Dominica, Guadeloupe, Martinique, and Saint Lucia.

t: The black-headed saltator (Saltator atriceps) is a species of songbird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found from Mexico to Panama.

t: The black-winged saltator (Saltator atripennis) is a species of songbird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The golden-billed saltator (Saltator aurantiirostris) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: The masked saltator (Saltator cinctus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The bluish-grey saltator or Amazonian grey saltator (Saltator coerulescens) is a passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae that is widespread in semi-open habitats in tropical and subtropical South America.
f: Two of its former subspecies groups, grandis (of Mexico and Central America) and olivascens (of northern South America and Trinidad), are now recognized as separate species, the cinnamon-bellied saltator and the olive-grey (or Caribbean grey) saltator.

t: The black-throated grosbeak (Saltator fuliginosus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The cinnamon-bellied saltator (Saltator grandis) is a passerine bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found from Mexico to Panama.

t: The slate-colored grosbeak (Saltator grossus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found from Honduras to Panama and in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The thick-billed saltator (Saltator maxillosus) is a species of saltator in the family Thraupidae. It is found in highland Atlantic Forest in southeastern Brazil, far northeastern Argentina (only Misiones Province), and perhaps far eastern Paraguay.
f: The male thick-billed saltator is unique with its long white eyebrow, grey back, and black and orange beak (amount of orange varies).

t: The buff-throated saltator (Saltator maximus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country except El Salvador, and every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The black-cowled saltator (Saltator nigriceps) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The olive-grey saltator (Saltator olivascens), also known as the Caribbean grey saltator, is a quiet, grey-colored passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae, native to Colombia, Venezuela, the Guianas, far northern Brazil, and Trinidad. The olive-grey saltator includes the subspecies brewsteri and plumbeus.
f: It was formerly considered conspecific with the greyish saltator (Saltator coerulescens), but was split as a distinct species by the IOC in 2021.

t: The Orinoco saltator or Orinocan saltator (Saltator orenocensis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The green-winged saltator (Saltator similis) is a species of saltator in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay, and ranges into the southern cerrado and the pantanal.

t: The streaked saltator (Saltator striatipectus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The black-throated saltator (Saltatricula atricollis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The many-colored Chaco finch (Saltatricula multicolor) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Uruguay, Paraguay, and as a vagrant in Brazil.
The sapayoa or broad-billed sapayoa (Sapayoa aenigma) is a suboscine passerine bird found Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama.

t: The red-tailed comet (Sappho sparganurus) is a medium-sized hummingbird belonging to tribe Lesbiini of subfamily Lesbiinae, the "coquettes".
f: It is found in Argentina and Bolivia and possibly Chile and Peru.

t: The coleto (Sarcops calvus) is a starling species (family Sturnidae) in the monotypic genus Sarcops. Its natural habitats are tropical dry forest, tropical moist lowland forest, and tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines.

t: The king vulture (Sarcoramphus papa) is a large bird found in Central and South America. It is a member of the New World vulture family Cathartidae.
f: King vultures were popular figures in the Mayan codices as well as in local folklore and medicine.
The buff-spotted flufftail (Sarothrura elegans), also known as the buff-spotted crake, is a species of bird in the family Sarothruridae.

t: The Madagascar flufftail (Sarothrura insularis) is a species of bird in the family Sarothruridae. Its natural habitat is subtropical, tropical moist lowland forests, shrubland, grassland, and artificial areas.
f: Madagascar flufftails are found in Madagascar however, they are limited in the wet areas in the north and lacking from Lake Sahaka in the northeast.

t: The white-spotted flufftail (Sarothrura pulchra), also known as the white-spotted crake, is a species of bird in the family Sarothruridae.
f: It has a widespread range of presence across the African tropical rainforest.

t: The red-chested flufftail (Sarothrura rufa) is a species of bird in the family Sarothruridae. It is found in sub-Saharan Africa from Liberia to Ethiopia and south to South Africa.
f: It can be found in environments near white-winged flufftails, but tends to avoid direct spacial overlap.

t: The rufous piculet (Sasia abnormis) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, and Thailand.
f: This species is one of the world's smallest woodpeckers and is the smallest woodpecker found outside the Americas.

t: The white-browed piculet (Sasia ochracea) is a species of bird in the family Picidae. Its natural habitats are temperate forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The berylline hummingbird (Saucerottia beryllina) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and the southern United States.

t: The azure-crowned hummingbird (Saucerottia cyanocephala) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Belize, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: The copper-rumped hummingbird (Saucerottia tobaci) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Tobago, Trinidad, Venezuela, and possibly Grenada.

t: Saunders's gull (Saundersilarus saundersi) or Chinese black-headed gull, is a species of gull in the family Laridae. It is found in China, Japan, North Korea, South Korea, Macau, Russia, Taiwan, and Vietnam.
f: Saunders's gull is named after the British ornithologist Howard Saunders.

t: The pied bush chat (Saxicola caprata) is a small passerine bird found ranging from West Asia and Central Asia to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. About sixteen subspecies are recognized through its wide range with many island forms.
f: They nest in cavities in stone walls or in holes in an embankment, lining the nest with grass and animal hair.

t: The grey bush chat (Saxicola ferreus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Muscicapidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in the Himalayas, southern China, Taiwan, Nepal and mainland Southeast Asia.

t: The whinchat (Saxicola rubetra) is a small migratory passerine bird breeding in Europe and western Asia and wintering in central Africa. At one time considered to be in the thrush family, Turdidae, it is now placed in the Old World flycatcher family, Muscicapidae.
f: The hen incubates the eggs for about thirteen days and then both parents feed the nestlings.

t: The European stonechat (Saxicola rubicola) is a small passerine bird that was formerly classed as a subspecies of the common stonechat. Long considered a member of the thrush family, Turdidae, genetic evidence has placed it and its relatives in the Old World flycatcher family, Muscicapidae.
f: It is found across Europe, as far east as Ukraine and the South Caucasus, and in parts of North Africa.

t: The Siberian stonechat or Asian stonechat (Saxicola maurus) is a recently validated species of the Old World flycatcher family (Muscicapidae). Like the other thrush-like flycatchers, it was often placed in the Turdidae in the past.
f: It breeds in the East Palearctic including in easternmost Europe and winters in the Old World tropics.

t: The African stonechat or common stonechat (Saxicola torquatus) is a species of the Old World flycatcher family (Muscicapidae), inhabiting sub-Saharan Africa and adjacent regions. Like the other chats, it was long assigned to the thrush family (Turdidae), to which the chats are convergent.
f: Its scientific name refer to its appearance and habitat and means "collared rock-dweller": Saxicola from Latin saxum ("rock") + incola ("one who dwells in a place"), torquatus, Latin for "collared".

t: The black phoebe (Sayornis nigricans) is a passerine bird in the tyrant-flycatcher family. It breeds from southwest Oregon and California south through Central and South America.
f: Its song is a repeated tee-hee, tee ho.

t: The eastern phoebe (Sayornis phoebe) is a small passerine bird. The genus name Sayornis is constructed from the specific part of Charles Lucien Bonaparte's name for Say's phoebe, Muscicapa saya, and Ancient Greek ornis, "bird".
f: Phoebe is an alternative name for the Roman moon goddess Diana, but it may also have been chosen to imitate the bird's call.

t: Say's phoebe (Sayornis saya) is a passerine bird in the tyrant flycatcher family, Tyrannidae. It was named for Thomas Say, an American naturalist.
f: A common bird across western North America, it prefers dry, desolate areas.

t: Couch's spadefoot toad or Couch's spadefoot (Scaphiopus couchii) is a species of North American spadefoot toad (family Scaphiopodidae).
f: The specific epithet couchii is in honor of American naturalist Darius Nash Couch, who collected the first specimen while on a personal expedition to northern Mexico to collect plant, mineral, and animal specimens for the Smithsonian Institution.
The white-throated tapaculo (Scelorchilus albicollis) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.

t: The chucao tapaculo (Scelorchilus rubecula) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in central Chile and adjacent Argentina; it has also been recorded in Chile's Magallanes Province.

t: The tooth-billed bowerbird (Scenopoeetes dentirostris), also known as the stagemaker bowerbird or tooth-billed catbird, is a species of passerine bird in the bowerbird family Ptilonorhynchidae. It is found in the Cape York Peninsula and northeast Queensland of northeast Australia.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Scenopoeetes.

t: The rufous vanga (Schetba rufa) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is monotypic within the genus Schetba.
f: In 1760 the French zoologist Mathurin Jacques Brisson included a description of the rufous vanga in his Ornithologie based on a specimen collected on the island of Madagascar.

t: The foothill schiffornis, or foothill mourner, (Schiffornis aenea) is a Neotropical species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The varzea schiffornis (Schiffornis major), also known as the várzea mourner or greater schiffornis, is a species of bird that belongs to Tityridae family. It has traditionally been placed in the manakin family, but evidence strongly suggest that it is better placed in Tityridae, where it is now classified by SACC.
f: It is found in most western regions of the Amazon Basin and Amazonian Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru; also regions of Venezuela.

t: The Guianan schiffornis (Schiffornis olivacea), also called the olivaceous schiffornis and olivaceous mourner, is a species of Neotropical bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The russet-winged schiffornis, or russet-winged mourner, (Schiffornis stenorhyncha) is a species of Neotropical bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Colombia, Panama, and Venezuela.

t: The brown-winged schiffornis, or brown-winged mourner, (Schiffornis turdina) is a species of Neotropical bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia.

t: The northern schiffornis, or northern mourner, (Schiffornis veraepacis), is a species of Neotropical bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country except El Salvador, and in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The greenish schiffornis (Schiffornis virescens) is a species of bird in the family Tityridae, the tityras, becards, and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: Geoffroy's daggerbill, Geoffroy's wedgebill, or eastern wedge-billed hummingbird (Schistes geoffroyi) is a species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The black-faced tanager (Schistochlamys melanopis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, dry savanna, and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The cinnamon tanager (Schistochlamys ruficapillus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, dry savanna, subtropical or tropical dry shrubland, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The broad-tailed grassbird (Schoenicola platyurus) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Locustellidae. It is endemic to the Western Ghats of India with a possibility of occurrence in Sri Lanka.
f: It is found only on the higher altitude grassy hills where it usually skulks, except during the breeding season when males fly up into the air to sing in their display.

t: The bristled grassbird (Schoenicola striatus) is a small passerine bird in the genus Schoenicola. Also known as the bristled grass warbler, this species is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, where it is patchily distributed in Bangladesh, India, Nepal, and Pakistan.
f: These insectivorous birds skulk in dense and tall grasslands, often in marshy areas, habitats that are threatened by human activities.

t: The chotoy spinetail (Schoeniophylax phryganophilus) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The dusky fulvetta (Schoeniparus brunneus) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in China and Taiwan, at altitudes mostly from 400–1,900 metres but sometimes down to sea level.
f: The bill is slender and blackish, the legs orangey-brown.

t: The rufous-winged fulvetta (Schoeniparus castaneceps) is a bird species of the family Pellorneidae. Its common name is misleading, because it is not a close relative of the "typical" fulvettas, which are now in the genus Fulvetta.
f: This is a noisy species with a rich warbled ti-du-di-du-di-du-di-du song and wheezy tsi-tsi-tsi-tsi call.

t: The yellow-throated fulvetta (Schoeniparus cinereus) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its common name is misleading, because it is not a close relative of the "typical" fulvettas, which are now in the family Paradoxornithidae.
f: It is found in south-eastern Asia from the Himalayas to north-central Vietnam.

t: The rusty-capped fulvetta (Schoeniparus dubius) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, and Vietnam.

t: The rufous-throated fulvetta (Schoeniparus rufogularis) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is found in southeastern Asia from the Himalayas through Indochina to southwestern Cambodia.

t: The northern chestnut-tailed antbird, or Zimmer's antbird, (Sciaphylax castanea) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The southern chestnut-tailed antbird, or chestnut-tailed antbird, (Sciaphylax hemimelaena) is a species of passerine bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The eastern gray squirrel (Sciurus carolinensis), spelled as grey squirrel outside of the United States, is a species of tree squirrel in the genus Sciurus. It is native to eastern North America, where it is the most prodigious and ecologically essential natural forest regenerator.
f: Widely introduced to certain places around the world, the eastern gray squirrel in Europe, in particular, is regarded as an invasive species.

The silvered antbird (Sclateria naevia) is a passerine bird in the subfamily Thamnophilinae of the family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds." It is found in Trinidad and every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The grey-winged francolin (Scleroptila afra) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae.
f: It is found in Lesotho and South Africa.

t: The Orange River francolin (Scleroptila gutturalis) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae found in grassland and woodland in Africa. In the taxa from the northern part of its distribution (Ethiopia, South Sudan, Somalia, Uganda and Kenya), the neck-line does not reach the eye and the belly is whitish.
f: In the southern taxa (Angola, Namibia, Botswana, South Africa and Lesotho) the neck-line reaches the eye and the belly is buff.

t: The red-winged francolin (Scleroptila levaillantii) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae. It is found in Angola, Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi, Rwanda, South Africa, Eswatini, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia.
f: Elgon francolin (Francolinus elgonensis) may be a hybrid between the red-winged francolin and the moorland francolin.

t: Shelley's francolin (Scleroptila shelleyi) is a species of bird in the family Phasianidae. IOC 15.1 recognizes the following subspecies: S. s. uluensis S. s. macarthuri S. s. shelleyi
f: The species is named after Sir Edward Shelley, cousin of George Ernest Shelley.

t: The grey-throated leaftosser (Sclerurus albigularis) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the subfamily Sclerurinae, the leaftossers and miners, of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, and Venezuela.

t: The black-tailed leaftosser (Sclerurus caudacutus) is a species of bird in the subfamily Sclerurinae, the leaftossers and miners, of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The scaly-throated leaftosser (Sclerurus guatemalensis) is a species of bird in subfamily Sclerurinae, the leaftossers and miners, of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country except El Salvador, and in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The tawny-throated leaftosser (Sclerurus mexicanus) is a tropical American bird species in subfamily Sclerurinae, the leaftossers and miners, of the ovenbird family Furnariidae. It is also known as the Middle American leaftosser and less frequently as tawny-throated leafscraper, Mexican leaftosser or Mexican leafscraper.
f: It is found from Mexico to Panama.

t: The dusky leaftosser or South American leaftosser (Sclerurus obscurior) is a bird in subfamily Sclerurinae, the leaftossers and miners, of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Giana, Guyana, Panama, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The short-billed leaftosser (Sclerurus rufigularis) is a species of bird in the subfamily Sclerurinae, the leaftossers and miners, of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The rufous-breasted leaftosser (Sclerurus scansor) is a species of bird in the subfamily Sclerurinae, the leaftossers and miners, of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The Bukidnon woodcock (Scolopax bukidnonensis), or Philippine woodcock is a medium-sized wader. It was not until the bird was heard calling in 1993, and new specimens obtained on Mindanao in 1995, that it was realised that the species was new.
f: It was only described as new to science as recently as 2001, although the initial specimens had been collected on Luzon in the 1960s, these were originally misidentified as Eurasian woodcock specimens.

t: The American woodcock (Scolopax minor), sometimes colloquially referred to as the timberdoodle, mudbat, becasse, bogsucker, brush snipe, night partridge, or Labrador twister is a small shorebird species found primarily in the eastern half of North America. Woodcocks spend most of their time on the ground in brushy, young-forest habitats, where the birds' brown, black, and gray plumage provides excellent camouflage.
f: The American woodcock is the only species of woodcock inhabiting North America.

t: The Eurasian woodcock (Scolopax rusticola) is a medium-small wading bird found in temperate and subarctic Eurasia. It has cryptic camouflage to suit its woodland habitat, with reddish-brown upperparts and buff-coloured underparts.
f: The male performs a courtship flight known as "roding" at dusk in spring.

t: The hamerkop (Scopus umbretta), also called the umbrette, is a medium-sized water bird with brown plumage. It is found in mainland Africa, Madagascar and Arabia, living in a wide variety of wetlands, including estuaries, lakesides, fish ponds, riverbanks, and rocky coasts.
f: Usually hunting in shallow water, either by sight or touch, it feeds mostly on fish and amphibians; however, the species is adaptable and will take any prey it can.

t: The streaked scrub warbler (Scotocerca inquieta), also known simply as the scrub warbler, is a small passerine bird in the family Cettiidae. It is the only species placed in the genus Scotocerca.
f: It is a bird of desert fringes, frequenting scrubby areas, ravines and gorges, and is mainly resident, although local movements can occur outside the breeding season.

t: Scudderia curvicauda is a species of katydid in the family Tettigoniidae, within the order Orthoptera (grasshoppers, crickets, and katydids).
f: A common name for Scudderia curvicauda is "curve-tailed bush katydid." Scudderia curvicauda is found in North America.

t: Scudderia furcata is a species in the family Tettigoniidae ("katydids"), in the order Orthoptera ("grasshoppers, crickets, katydids"). The distribution range of Scudderia furcata includes North America.
f: A common name for Scudderia furcata is fork-tailed bush katydid.
Scudderia texensis is a katydid commonly known as the Texas bush katydid.
Tschudi's tapaculo (Scytalopus acutirostris) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
The Ancash tapaculo (Scytalopus affinis) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.

t: The neblina tapaculo (Scytalopus altirostris) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is endemic to the Andes of northern Peru.

t: The Tatama tapaculo (Scytalopus alvarezlopezi) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is endemic to western Colombia.

t: The Loja tapaculo (Scytalopus androstictus) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae that the South American Classification Committee of the American Ornithological Society (AOS) accepted as a new species in July 2020. It had been classified as a subspecies of paramo tapaculo (Scytalopus opacus).
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The silvery-fronted tapaculo (Scytalopus argentifrons) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The white-crowned tapaculo (Scytalopus atratus) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The Bolivian tapaculo (Scytalopus bolivianus) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru.
The Paramillo tapaculo (Scytalopus canus) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
The Caracas tapaculo (Scytalopus caracae) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.

t: The Chocó tapaculo (Scytalopus chocoensis) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama.

t: The Diamantina tapaculo (Scytalopus diamantinensis) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is endemic to northeastern Brazil.
The rufous-vented tapaculo (Scytalopus femoralis) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
The jalca tapaculo (Scytalopus frankeae) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
The dusky tapaculo (Scytalopus fuscus) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.

t: The pale-bellied tapaculo (Scytalopus griseicollis), also known as the matorral tapaculo or rufous-rumped tapaculo, is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

The Utcubamba tapaculo (Scytalopus intermedius) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae that the South American Classification Committee of the American Ornithological Society split from blackish tapaculo (S. latrans) in July 2020.

t: The marsh tapaculo (Scytalopus iraiensis) is a recently discovered passerine bird which belongs to the genus Scytalopus, a genus of tapaculos.
f: It is also known as the wetland tapaculo or tall-grass wetland tapaculo.
The brown-rumped tapaculo (Scytalopus latebricola) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.

t: The blackish tapaculo (Scytalopus latrans) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
The large-footed tapaculo (Scytalopus macropus) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
The Magellanic tapaculo (Scytalopus magellanicus) is a small passerine bird in the tapaculo family Rhinocryptidae that is found in southern South America.
The Mérida tapaculo (Scytalopus meridanus) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.

t: The long-tailed tapaculo (Scytalopus micropterus) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in the eastern Andes of Colombia, Ecuador and far northern Peru.

t: The Brasília tapaculo (Scytalopus novacapitalis) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is endemic to southern Brazil.

t: The Paramo tapaculo (Scytalopus opacus) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in the Andes of Ecuador and southern Colombia.

t: The Planalto tapaculo (Scytalopus pachecoi) is a small passerine bird in family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in southeastern Brazil and extreme northeastern Argentina.

t: The chusquea tapaculo (Scytalopus parkeri) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in southern Ecuador and far northern Peru.

t: The trilling tapaculo (Scytalopus parvirostris) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru.

t: The Perijá tapaculo (Scytalopus perijanus) is a species of passerine bird in the family Rhinocryptidae (tapaculos). Endemic to the Serranía del Perijá mountain range on the Colombia–Venezuela border, the Perijá tapaculo is found at altitudes of 1,600–3,225 metres (5,200–10,600 feet).
f: Specimens have long been stored in museums, but the species was described only in 2015 based on sixteen specimens found between July 2008 and February 2009.

t: The rock tapaculo or Espinhaço tapaculo (Scytalopus petrophilus) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae. It is endemic to altitudes of 900–2,100 metres (3,000–6,900 ft) in the central and southern Espinhaço Mountains, and the Mantiqueira Mountains in Minas Gerais, Brazil, though it may also occur in adjacent parts of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo.
f: It closely resembles the Diamantina tapaculo and Planalto tapaculo in appearance and voice (especially song; less so in call).

t: The Ecuadorian tapaculo or El Oro tapaculo (Scytalopus robbinsi) is a small passerine bird belonging to the genus Scytalopus, a genus of tapaculos. It is restricted to a small area in south-western Ecuador and was not described until 1997.
f: The song is a series of double-notes repeated for about a minute.

t: The Magdalena tapaculo (Scytalopus rodriguezi), also known as the Upper Magdalena tapaculo, is a member of the tapaculos, a group of Neotropical birds. It was described as new to science in 2005.
f: It is a restricted-range endemic presently known only from two localities on the eastern slope of the Cordillera Central at the head of the Magdalena Valley, Colombia at 2000 m or more above sea-level.

t: The Santa Marta tapaculo (Scytalopus sanctaemartae) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is endemic to the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta of Colombia.

t: The diademed tapaculo (Scytalopus schulenbergi) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru.

t: The puna tapaculo (Scytalopus simonsi) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru.

t: The mouse-coloured tapaculo or Serra do Mar tapaculo (Scytalopus speluncae) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae. Most of its range is in the Serra do Mar, but it also occurs further inland in Paraná and Santa Catarina.
f: It is endemic to humid highland forests in southeastern Brazil, where it ranges from southwestern Espírito Santo to northeastern Rio Grande do Sul.

t: Spillmann's tapaculo (Scytalopus spillmanni) is a species of bird in the family Formicariidae.
f: It inhabits the Andes of Colombia and Ecuador.

t: Stiles's tapaculo (Scytalopus stilesi) is a member of the tapaculos, a group of Neotropical birds. It has been found at 21 sites in montane forest between 1,420 and 2,130 m altitude in the northern Cordillera Central of the Colombian Andes; although having a restricted range, within this limited area it is a common understorey bird.
f: It was described as new to science in 2005.

t: The white-browed tapaculo (Scytalopus superciliaris) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in northwestern Argentina.
The unicolored tapaculo (Scytalopus unicolor) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
The Vilcabamba tapaculo (Scytalopus urubambae) is a small passerine bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.

t: The Nariño tapaculo (Scytalopus vicinior) is a species of bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: Zimmer's tapaculo (Scytalopus zimmeri) is a species of passerine bird in the family Rhinocryptidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Argentina.

t: The channel-billed cuckoo (Scythrops novaehollandiae) is a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae. It is monotypic within the genus Scythrops.
f: The species is the largest brood parasite in the world, and the largest cuckoo.

t: The ovenbird (Seiurus aurocapilla) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family Parulidae. It is the only species placed in the genus Seiurus.
f: This migratory bird breeds in eastern North America and winters in Central America, many Caribbean islands, Florida and northern Venezuela.

t: The calliope hummingbird ( kə-LY-ə-pee; Selasphorus calliope) is the smallest bird native to the United States and Canada. It has a western breeding range mainly from California to British Columbia, and migrates to the Southwestern United States, Mexico, and Central America for its wintering grounds.
f: The calliope hummingbird is the smallest known long-distance bird migrant, completing migrations twice per year of some 9,000 km (5,600 mi).

t: The wine-throated hummingbird (Selasphorus ellioti) is a species of hummingbird in tribe Mellisugini of subfamily Trochilinae, the "bee hummingbirds".
f: It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.

t: The bumblebee hummingbird (Selasphorus heloisa) is a species of hummingbird in tribe Mellisugini of subfamily Trochilinae, the "bee hummingbirds".
f: It is endemic to Mexico, but has occurred as a vagrant in the United States.
The broad-tailed hummingbird (Selasphorus platycercus) is a medium-sized hummingbird species found in highland regions from western United States and Western Canada to Mexico and Guatemala.

t: The rufous hummingbird (Selasphorus rufus) is a small hummingbird, about 8 cm (3 in) long with a long, straight and slender bill. It is one of nine species in the genus Selasphorus.
f: These birds are known for their extraordinary flight skills, flying 3,200 kilometres (2,000 miles) during their migratory transits.

t: Allen's hummingbird (Selasphorus sasin) is a species of hummingbird that breeds in the western United States.
f: It is one of seven species in the genus Selasphorus.

t: Gould's toucanet (Selenidera gouldii) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Brazil.

t: The spot-billed toucanet (Selenidera maculirostris) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The Guianan toucanet, or Guyana toucanet (Selenidera piperivora) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The golden-collared toucanet (Selenidera reinwardtii) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The yellow-eared toucanet (Selenidera spectabilis) is a bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.
f: It is found from Honduras to Ecuador.

t: The twelve-wired bird-of-paradise (Seleucidis melanoleucus) is a medium-sized, approximately 33 cm (13 in) long, velvet black and yellow bird-of-paradise. The male has a red iris, long black bill and rich yellow plumes along his flanks.
f: The display dance of the twelve-wired bird of paradise is called a wire-wipe display.

t: The standardwing bird-of-paradise (Semioptera wallacii), also known as Wallace's standardwing or as the standardwing, is a species of bird-of-paradise.
f: It is the only member in monotypic genus Semioptera.
The prong-billed barbet (Semnornis frantzii) is a distinctive, relatively large-billed bird native to humid highland forest of Costa Rica and western Panama.

t: The toucan barbet (Semnornis ramphastinus) is a barbet native to western Ecuador and Colombia. Along with the prong-billed barbet, it forms the family Semnornithidae, and is closely related to the toucans.
f: It feeds on fruit and a range of animal prey, with insects being an important part of the diet of chicks.

t: The green-backed firecrown (Sephanoides sephaniodes) is a hummingbird in the "coquettes", tribe Lesbiini of subfamily Lesbiinae.
f: It is found in Argentina, mainland Chile, and the Juan Fernández Islands.

t: The yellow-throated scrubwren (Neosericornis citreogularis) is a passerine in the family Acanthizidae that is found in parts of eastern coastal Australia. It was formerly placed in the genus Sericornis, but is now the only species in the genus Neosericornis.
f: Breeding twice or more in a long breeding season, it nests in large, suspended, pear-shaped structures.

t: The white-browed scrubwren (Sericornis frontalis) is a passerine bird found on the New England Tablelands and coastal areas of Australia. Placed in the family Pardalotidae in the Sibley-Ahlquist taxonomy, this has met with opposition and indeed is now known to be wrong; they rather belong to the independent family Acanthizidae.
f: Found in small groups, it is sedentary and engages in cooperative breeding.

t: It lives in the understory of rainforest, woodland, dry forest, swamps and coastal scrublands.
f: The Tasmanian scrubwren or brown scrubwren (Sericornis humilis) is a bird species endemic to the temperate forests of Tasmania and nearby King Island.

t: The large-billed scrubwren (Sericornis magnirostra) is a passerine bird in the family Acanthizidae, endemic to eastern Australia.
f: It is found in denser undergrowth in temperate forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

t: The Papuan scrubwren (Aethomyias papuensis) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. This species was formerly placed in the genus Sericornis but following the publication of a molecular phylogenetic study of the scrubwrens in 2018, it was moved to the resurrected genus Aethomyias.
f: It is found in the highlands of New Guinea; its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The white-capped tanager (Sericossypha albocristata) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found from Venezuela to Peru.

t: The silver-breasted broadbill (Serilophus lunatus) is a species of bird in the broadbill family, Eurylaimidae that is found in parts of Southeast Asia.
f: There are seven currently recognised subspecies; the other species in the genus Serilophus, the grey-lored broadbill, was also previously treated as being a subspecies of this species.

t: It is sometimes placed in the genus Alario as Alario alario Its habitat is dry open scrub and grassland, the edges of cultivation and suburban gardens.
f: The black-headed canary (Serinus alario) is a species of finch found in Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa.

t: The Atlantic canary (Serinus canaria), known worldwide simply as the wild canary and also called the island canary, common canary, or canary, is a small passerine bird belonging to the genus Serinus in the true finch family, Fringillidae. It is native to the Canary Islands, the Azores, and Madeira.
f: This bird is the natural symbol of the Canary Islands, together with the Canary Island date palm.

t: The Cape canary (Serinus canicollis) is a small passerine bird in the finch family. It is a resident breeder in southern Africa and has been introduced to Mauritius and Réunion.
f: Nest are built by females and both parents feed chicks, which typically fledge in 2-3 weeks.

t: The yellow-crowned canary (Serinus flavivertex) is a small passerine bird in the finch family. It is a resident breeder in eastern Africa.
f: Its call is tsit-it-it, and the song is warbled goldfinch-like trills and whistles given in display flight or from a high perch.

t: The yellow-fronted canary (Crithagra mozambica) is a small passerine bird in the finch family. This bird is a resident breeder in Africa south of the Sahara Desert.
f: It is sometimes known in aviculture as the green singing finch or the green singer.

t: The red-fronted serin or fire-fronted serin (Serinus pusillus) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It prefers high mountain regions and is 11–12 cm (4.3–4.7 in) long.
f: The bird will breed in captivity and thrives on a diet of canary grass seed, millet, and other small seeds.

t: The European serin, or simply the serin (Serinus serinus), is the smallest species of the family of finches (Fringillidae) and is closely related to the Atlantic canary.
f: Its diet consists mainly of a combination of buds and seeds.

t: The torrent tyrannulet (Serpophaga cinerea) is a small bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: Straneck's tyrannulet (Serpophaga griseicapilla), also known as the monte tyrannulet and grey-crowned tyrannulet, is a small species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The river tyrannulet (Serpophaga hypoleuca) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The sooty tyrannulet (Serpophaga nigricans) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers. It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay; also southern Paraguay.
f: It is small, usually weighing 9 grams with a length of 12 centimeters, and has gray or brownish-grey feathers with black tail feathers.

t: The white-crested tyrannulet (Serpophaga subcristata) is a small species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The little nightjar (Setopagis parvula) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: Adelaide's warbler (Setophaga adelaidae), or reinita mariposera in Puerto Rican Spanish, is a species of bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers.
f: It is endemic to the archipelago of Puerto Rico.

t: The northern parula (Setophaga americana) is a small New World warbler.
f: It is migratory and breeds in eastern North America from southern Canada to Florida.

t: The black-throated blue warbler (Setophaga caerulescens) is a small passerine bird of the New World warbler family. Its breeding ranges are located in the interior of deciduous and mixed coniferous forests in eastern North America.
f: Over the cooler months, it migrates to islands in the Caribbean and Central America.

t: The bay-breasted warbler (Setophaga castanea) is a small species of songbird in the New World warbler family, Parulidae. It is one of 35 species in the diverse genus Setophaga.
f: Like all songbirds, or passerines, the species is classified in the order Passeriformes.

t: The cerulean warbler (Setophaga cerulea) is a small songbird in the family Parulidae. It is a long-distance migrant, breeding in eastern North American hardwood forests and wintering on the Eastern slope of the Andes in South America during non-breeding season, preferring subtropical forests.
f: It displays strong sexual dichromatism.

t: The golden-cheeked warbler (Setophaga chrysoparia) is an endangered species of bird that breeds in Central Texas, from Palo Pinto County southwestward along the eastern and southern edge of the Edwards Plateau to Kinney County.
f: The golden-cheeked warbler is the only bird species with a breeding range endemic to Texas.

t: The hooded warbler (Setophaga citrina) is a New World warbler. It breeds in eastern North America across the eastern United States and into southernmost Canada (Ontario).
f: It is migratory, wintering in Central America and the West Indies.

t: The yellow-rumped warbler (Setophaga coronata) is a North American bird species that can be commonly observed all across the continent. The yellow-rumped warbler is primarily insectivorous, though the species eats fruit such as juniper berries, especially in winter.
f: It generally prefers coniferous forests or mixed coniferous-deciduous forests as its breeding habitat, while during the winter it can be found inhabiting more open areas such as shrublands that offer food resources.
The prairie warbler (Setophaga discolor) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.
The yellow-throated warbler (Setophaga dominica) is a small migratory songbird species in the New World warbler family (Parulidae) found in temperate North America.

t: The Blackburnian warbler (Setophaga fusca) is a small New World warbler. They breed in eastern North America, from southern Canada, westwards to the southern Canadian Prairies, the Great Lakes region and New England, to North Carolina.
f: They are migratory, wintering in southern Central America and South America, and are very rare vagrants to western Europe.
Grace's warbler (Setophaga graciae) is a small New World warbler that specializes in pine woods.

t: Kirtland's warbler (Setophaga kirtlandii), also known in Michigan by the common name jack pine bird, or the jack pine warbler, is a small songbird of the New World warbler family (Parulidae). The birds require large areas, greater than 160 acres (65 hectares), of dense young jack pine for breeding habitat.
f: Nearly extinct just years ago, populations have recovered due to the conservation efforts of the Kirtland's Warbler Conservation Team and its members.
The magnolia warbler (Setophaga magnolia) is a member of the wood warbler family Parulidae.

t: The black-throated gray warbler or black-throated grey warbler (Setophaga nigrescens) is a passerine bird of the New World warbler family Parulidae. It is 13 cm (5.1 in) long and has gray and white plumage with black markings.
f: Its nest is an open cup of plant fibers lined with feathers, built a few metres from the ground in the branches of a tree or shrub.

t: The hermit warbler (Setophaga occidentalis) is a small perching bird. It is a species of New World warbler or wood-warbler.
f: They are a migratory bird, the breeding range spanning the majority of the west coast of the United States.
The palm warbler (Setophaga palmarum) is a small songbird in the New World warbler family.

t: The chestnut-sided warbler (Setophaga pensylvanica) is a New World warbler. They also breed in the Great Lakes region and in the eastern United States.
f: They breed in eastern North America and in southern Canada westwards to the Canadian Prairies.

t: The mangrove warbler or mangrove yellow warbler (Setophaga petechia) is a New World warbler species. It a small bright yellow bird that is found in mangroves on the Atlantic and Pacific coasts of the tropical Americas.
f: It is also present in the Caribbean and on the Galápagos Islands.

t: The pine warbler (Setophaga pinus) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family Parulidae. It is a permanent resident in the southeastern United States and also breeds in southeastern Canada and the northeastern United States, where it is migratory.
f: Unlike other wood-warblers, in addition to insects the pine warbler also sometimes consumes seeds.

t: The tropical parula (Setophaga pitiayumi) is a species of passerine bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers. S. state of Texas, Mexico, and every Central American country.
f: Its range continues in every mainland South American country (though in Chile only as a vagrant), on Trinidad, and as a vagrant on the Falkland Islands.

t: [[|thumb]] The olive-capped warbler (Setophaga pityophila) is a species of bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers.
f: It is found in Cuba and in the Bahamas on Grand Bahama, Little Abaco, and Great Abaco. [[|thumb]]

t: The American redstart (Setophaga ruticilla) is a New World warbler.
f: It is only distantly related to the Old World (common) redstart, with both belonging to the order Passeriformes.

t: The blackpoll warbler (Setophaga striata) is a New World warbler. They have a prominent black cap, white cheeks, and white wing bars.
f: Breeding males are mostly black and white.

t: The Cape May warbler (Setophaga tigrina) is a species of New World warbler. It breeds in northern North America.
f: It is migratory, wintering in the West Indies.
Townsend's warbler (Setophaga townsendi) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.
The black-throated green warbler (Setophaga virens) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.

t: This species is a forest-dwelling insectivorous bird related to the small Old World flycatchers commonly known as chats; like these, it was formerly placed with the thrushes (Turdidae). The east coast akalat is affected by habitat loss.
f: The east coast akalat or Gunning's robin (Sheppardia gunningi) is a small passerine bird which can be found in the east of Africa from Kenya to Mozambique, and is named after J.

t: Sharpe's akalat (Sheppardia sharpei) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is found in Tanzania and northern parts of Zambia and Malawi.
f: Both the common name and the specific epithet honour the English ornithologist and museum curator Richard Bowdler Sharpe.

t: The white-bellied blue robin (Sholicola albiventris) or white-bellied sholakili, is a bird of the family Muscicapidae. The Nilgiri blue robin and this species were once considered separate species, later lumped as sub-species of a single species (major) and elevated again to full species in 2005 by Pamela C.
f: It is endemic to the Shola forests of the higher hills of southern India.

t: This small bird is found on the forest floor and undergrowth of dense forest patches sheltered in the valleys of montane grassland, a restricted and threatened habitat. The white-bellied blue robin was formerly considered conspecific with this species but in 2005 the two taxa were split by Pamela C.
f: Rasmussen, a treatment that is followed by some authorities.

t: The mountain bluebird (Sialia currucoides) is a migratory small thrush that is found in mountainous districts of western North America. It has a light underbelly and black eyes.
f: The mountain bluebird is the state bird of Idaho and Nevada.
The western bluebird (Sialia mexicana) is a small North American thrush.

t: The eastern bluebird (Sialia sialis) is a small North American migratory thrush found in open woodlands, farmlands, and orchards. The bright-blue breeding plumage of the male, easily observed on a wire or open perch, makes this species a favorite of birders.
f: It is the state bird of Missouri and New York.

t: The greater yellow finch (Sicalis auriventris) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, temperate grassland, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Argentina and Chile.

t: The stripe-tailed yellow finch (Sicalis citrina) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are dry savanna and pastureland.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The saffron finch (Sicalis flaveola) is a tanager from South America that is common in open and semi-open areas in lowlands outside the Amazon Basin. Although commonly regarded as a canary, it is not related to the Atlantic canary.
f: It has also been introduced to Hawaii, Panama, Puerto Rico, Jamaica and elsewhere.

t: The Patagonian yellow finch (Sicalis lebruni) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry shrubland and temperate grassland.
f: It is found in Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego in southern Argentina and Chile.

t: The citron-headed yellow finch (Sicalis luteocephala) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.
f: It is found in the Andes of Bolivia and far northern Argentina.

t: The grassland yellow finch (Sicalis luteola) is a small passerine bird. Despite its name, it is not a finch, but is a seedeater.
f: The call is a sharp te-tsip, and the male's song, given from a perch or in a display flight, is a series of chips, buzzes and trills.

t: The greenish yellow finch (Sicalis olivascens) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in the central Andes of Argentina, Bolivia, Chile and Peru.

t: The bright-rumped yellow finch (Sicalis uropygialis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in the Puna grassland: Peru, Bolivia and northern Chile and Argentina.
f: The bright-rumped yellow finch was formally described in 1837 by the French naturalists Alcide d'Orbigny and Frédéric de Lafresnaye from a specimen collected in the Bolivian Andes.

t: The vinous-throated parrotbill (Suthora webbiana) is a species of bird in the family Paradoxornithidae; formerly, it was placed in the closely related Sylviidae or Timaliidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in China, Korea, Russia, Taiwan, and Vietnam.

t: The least poorwill or least pauraque (Siphonorhis brewsteri) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae, and the only confirmed extant species of its genus.
f: It is endemic to the island of Hispaniola, which is shared by the Dominican Republic and Haiti.

t: The stub-tailed antbird (Sipia berlepschi) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The dull-mantled antbird (Sipia laemosticta) is a perching bird species in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, and Panama.

t: The Esmeraldas antbird (Sipia nigricauda) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The Magdalena antbird (Sipia palliata) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The white-rumped sirystes (Sirystes albocinereus), is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The Choco sirystes (Sirystes albogriseus), formerly known as the western sirystes, is a species of passerine bird in the tyrant flycatcher family Tyrannidae.
f: It is found Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama.

t: The sibilant sirystes (Sirystes sibilator) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The red-breasted nuthatch (Sitta canadensis) is a small songbird. The adult has blue-grey upperparts with cinnamon underparts, a white throat and face with a black stripe through the eyes, a straight grey bill and a black crown.
f: It excavates its nest in dead wood, often close to the ground, smearing the entrance with pitch.

t: The white-breasted nuthatch (Sitta carolinensis) is a species of bird in the nuthatch family Sittidae. It is a medium-sized nuthatch, measuring approximately 15.5 cm (6.1 in) in length.
f: It has a nasal voice and often utters little cries or vocalizations, often composed of repetitions of small invariant whistles.

t: The chestnut-bellied nuthatch (Sitta cinnamoventris) is a species of bird belonging to the family Sittidae. It is found in the Indian subcontinent occurring in the countries of India, Tibet, Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Nepal.
f: Rasmussen and Anderton (2005) established the chestnut-bellied nuthatch is different from the Indian nuthatch and the Burmese nuthatch.

t: The Eurasian nuthatch, wood nuthatch (Sitta europaea), or simply nuthatch, is a small passerine bird found throughout the Palearctic and in Eurasia. Like other nuthatches, it is a short-tailed bird with a long bill, blue-gray upperparts and a black eye-stripe.
f: The nuthatch can forage when descending trees head first, as well as when climbing.

t: The velvet-fronted nuthatch (Sitta frontalis) is a small passerine bird in the nuthatch family Sittidae found in southern Asia, from Nepal, India, Sri Lanka ‍and Bangladesh east to southwestern China and Indonesia. Like other nuthatches, it feeds on insects in the bark of trees, foraging on the trunks and branches and their strongly clawed toes allow them to climb down tree trunks or move on the undersides of horizontal branches.
f: Adult males can be told apart by the black stripe that runs behind and above the eyes.

t: The white-tailed nuthatch (Sitta himalayensis) is a species of bird in the family Sittidae. It is found in Bhutan, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Tibet and Thailand.
f: It ranges across the northern and northeastern parts of the Indian subcontinent, existing mainly in the low-to-middle Himalayas, as well as associated mountain ranges.

t: Krüper's nuthatch (Sitta krueperi) is a species of bird in the nuthatch family Sittidae. It is a small to medium-sized nuthatch, measuring 12.5 centimetres (4.9 in) in length.
f: The clutch consists of five to seven eggs, incubated by the female and fed by the male.

t: The giant nuthatch (Sitta magna) is a species of bird in the family Sittidae. It is the longest of the nuthatches, measuring 19.5 cm (7.7 in) in length.
f: It nests around March, in the hole of a tree and without masking the entrance, and the nest has about three young.

t: The chestnut-vented nuthatch (Sitta nagaensis) is a species of bird in the nuthatch family Sittidae. It is a medium-sized nuthatch, measuring 12.5–14 cm (4.9–5.5 in) in length.
f: The chestnut-vented nuthatch utters different kinds of calls, which can sometimes sound like a wren alarm, and its song is a monotonous, stereotypical crackle, typically chichichichi.

t: The western rock nuthatch (Sitta neumayer) is a small passerine bird which breeds from Croatia east through Greece and Turkey to Iran. This nuthatch is largely resident apart from some post-breeding dispersal.
f: It feeds on insects and spiders in summer, supplemented with seeds and snails in winter.

t: The brown-headed nuthatch (Sitta pusilla) is a small songbird endemic to pine forests throughout the Southeastern United States. The Bahama nuthatch was formerly considered a subspecies (S. p. insularis), but has since been reclassified as its own separate species.
f: The nuthatch exhibits other curious behaviors such as cooperative groups where groups of 3–5 adults provide care at a single nest.
The pygmy nuthatch (Sitta pygmaea) is a tiny songbird, native to western North America.

t: The eastern rock nuthatch (Sitta tephronota) is a species of bird in the nuthatch family Sittidae. It is found in southwest and central Asia, from eastern Turkey east through Armenia, Georgia, Azerbaijan, Iraq, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan, and Afghanistan, to northwestern Pakistan.
f: Some authors have used the name Persian nuthatch for the species.

t: The Chinese nuthatch or snowy-browed nuthatch (Sitta villosa) is a species of bird in the family Sittidae. It is a small nuthatch, measuring 11.5 cm (4.5 in) in length.
f: The song is variable, and composed of repetitions of small invariant whistles.

t: The Corsican nuthatch (Sitta whiteheadi) is a species of bird in the nuthatch family Sittidae. It is a relatively small nuthatch, measuring about 12 cm (4.7 in) in overall length.
f: The Corsican nuthatch is found only on the island of Corsica, where it populates the old forests of high-altitude Corsican pines, descending lower in winter.

t: The Yunnan nuthatch (Sitta yunnanensis) is a bird species in the nuthatch family Sittidae. It was first described by William Robert Ogilvie-Grant in 1900 based on a male holotype.
f: It can be found in the prefectures of Yunnan, Sichuan, and Guizhou in Southwest China, where it prefers sparsely forested pine forests and avoids dense spruce and fir forests.

t: The olivaceous woodcreeper (Sittasomus griseicapillus) is a passerine bird in subfamily Dendrocolaptinae of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found from central Mexico south through every Central American country, on the island of Tobago, and in every mainland South American country except Chile, French Guiana, and Suriname.

t: The chestnut-bellied tit (Sittiparus castaneoventris) is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae that is endemic to Taiwan. The chestnut-bellied tit was first described by the English ornithologist John Gould in 1863 and given the binomial name Parus castaneoventris.
f: The species differs from the varied tit in having underparts of a deep chestnut colour.

t: Owston's tit (Sittiparus owstoni) is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae that is endemic to the southern Izu Islands south of Japan, occurring only on the islands of Miyakejima, Mikurajima and Hachijojima. Owston's tit was formerly considered as subspecies of the varied tit but was promoted to species status based on the results of a phylogenetic study published in 2014.
f: This was the first description of a bird by a zoologist from Japan.

t: The varied tit (Sittiparus varius) is a perching bird from the tit family, Paridae.
f: It occurs in the eastern Palearctic in Japan, Korea, and locally in northeastern China (southern Liaoning) and extreme southeastern Russia (southern Kurile Islands).

t: The weebill (Smicrornis brevirostris) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is an insectivorous passerine that is found throughout mainland Australia.
f: At 8 to 9 cm (3.1 to 3.5 in) long, it is Australia's smallest bird.
The African broadbill (Smithornis capensis), also known as the black-capped broadbill or Delacour's broadbill, is a species of bird in the suboscine family Calyptomenidae.

t: The rufous-sided broadbill (Smithornis rufolateralis) is a species of bird in the family Calyptomenidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is sparsely distributed throughout the Guineo-Congolian region.

t: The grey-tailed piha (Snowornis subalaris) is a species of bird in the family Cotingidae, the cotingas.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador and Peru.

t: The common eider (pronounced ) (Somateria mollissima), also called St. Cuthbert's duck or Cuddy's duck, is a large (50–71 cm (20–28 in) in body length) sea-duck that is distributed over the northern coasts of Europe, North America and eastern Siberia.
f: It can fly at speeds up to 113 km/h (70 mph).

t: The king eider (pronounced ) (Somateria spectabilis) is a large sea duck that breeds along Northern Hemisphere Arctic coasts of northeast Europe, North America and Asia. They lay four to seven eggs in a scrape on the ground lined with grass and down.
f: The birds spend most of the year in coastal marine ecosystems at high latitudes, and migrate to Arctic tundra to breed in June and July.

t: The bay-capped wren-spinetail (Spartonoica maluroides) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The northern shoveler (; Spatula clypeata), often known simply as the shoveler where other related species do not occur, is a common and widespread duck. It breeds in northern areas of Europe and throughout the Palearctic and across most of North America, and winters in southern Europe, the Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia, Central America, the Caribbean, and northern South America.
f: The northern shoveler is one of the species to which the Agreement on the Conservation of African-Eurasian Migratory Waterbirds (AEWA) applies.

t: The cinnamon teal (Spatula cyanoptera) is a species of duck found in western North and South America. It is a small dabbling duck, with bright reddish plumage on the male and duller brown plumage on the female.
f: It lives in marshes and ponds, and feeds mostly on plants.

t: The blue-winged teal (Spatula discors) is a species of bird in the duck, goose, and swan family Anatidae. One of the smaller members of the dabbling duck group, it occurs in North America, where it breeds from southern Alaska to Nova Scotia, and south to northern Texas.
f: It winters along the Pacific and Atlantic coasts and south into the Caribbean islands and Central America.
The red shoveler (Spatula platalea) is a species of dabbling duck native to southern South America.

t: The Puna teal (Spatula puna) is a species of dabbling duck in the family Anatidae. It was at one time regarded as a subspecies of the silver teal (Spatula versicolor).
f: The Puna teal is resident in the Andes of Peru, western Bolivia, northern Chile, and extreme northwestern Argentina.

t: The garganey (Spatula querquedula) is a small dabbling duck. This species was first described by Carl Linnaeus in his landmark 1758 10th edition of Systema Naturae.
f: Like other small ducks such as the Eurasian teal, this species rises easily from the water with a fast twisting wader-like flight.

t: The plains spadefoot toad (Spea bombifrons) is a species of American spadefoot toad which ranges from southwestern Canada, throughout the Great Plains of the western United States, and into northern Mexico. Their name, in part, comes from their keratinized metatarsals, which are wide instead of "sickle shaped".
f: Like other species of spadefoot toads, they get their name from a spade-like projection on their hind legs which allows them to dig into sandy soils.

t: The rufous-throated wren-babbler (Spelaeornis caudatus) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae. It is found in Bhutan, India, and Nepal.
f: It is becoming rare due to habitat loss.

t: The Chin Hills wren-babbler (Spelaeornis oatesi) is a bird species in the family Timaliidae. It was until recently considered a subspecies of the long-tailed wren-babbler; the IUCN for example started recognizing it as distinct species in 2008.
f: It is found in India and Myanmar.

t: The bar-winged wren-babbler (Spelaeornis troglodytoides) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Bhutan, China, India, and Myanmar.

t: The bronze mannikin or bronze munia (Spermestes cucullata) is a small passerine (i.e. perching) bird of the Afrotropics. This very social estrildid finch is an uncommon to locally abundant bird in much of Africa south of the Sahara Desert, where it is resident, nomadic or irruptive in mesic savanna or forest margin habitats.
f: It is the smallest and most widespread of four munia species on the African mainland, the other being black-and-white, red-backed and magpie mannikin.

t: The western bluebill (Spermophaga haematina) is a common species of estrildid finch found in Africa. It is native to the Guineo-Congolian region, as well as the Jos Plateau and from western Gambia to Guinea Bissau.
f: It has an estimated global extent of occurrence of 1,900,000 km2.

t: It is common in large parts of its range, and occurs in numerous protected areas.
f: Consequently, it is rated as least concern by BirdLife International and the IUCN.

t: The African penguin (Spheniscus demersus), also known as the Cape penguin or the South African penguin, is a species of penguin confined to southern African waters. Like all penguins, it is flightless, with a streamlined body and wings stiffened and flattened into flippers for a marine habitat.
f: It is the only penguin found in the Old World.

t: Vagrants have been found in El Salvador, the Avian Island in Antarctica, Australia, and New Zealand. Its nearest relatives are the African penguin, the Humboldt penguin, and the Galápagos penguins.
f: It is the most numerous of the Spheniscus banded penguins.

t: The Cape grassbird or Cape grass warbler (Sphenoeacus afer) is an African warbler found in southern Africa.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Sphenoeacus.

t: The oleaginous hemispingus (Sphenopsis frontalis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
f: It has dull yellow underparts and olive-green upperparts.

t: The black-eared hemispingus (Sphenopsis melanotis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.
f: It is found in humid highland forest in the Andes of western Venezuela, through to western Bolivia.

t: Long thought to be a subspecies of the yellow-bellied sapsucker, it is now known to be a distinct species.
f: The red-naped sapsucker (Sphyrapicus nuchalis) is a medium-sized North American woodpecker.
The red-breasted sapsucker (Sphyrapicus ruber) is a medium-sized woodpecker of the forests of the west coast of North America.
Williamson's sapsucker (Sphyrapicus thyroideus) is a medium-sized woodpecker belonging to the genus Sphyrapicus (sapsuckers).
The yellow-bellied sapsucker (Sphyrapicus varius) is a medium-sized woodpecker that breeds in Canada and the northeastern United States.

t: The cricket warbler (Spiloptila clamans), also known as cricket longtail, scaly longtail or cricket prinia, is a species of bird in the family Cisticolidae.
f: It belongs to the genus Spiloptila; it is often the only species included in the genus but sometimes the red-fronted prinia is placed there as well.

t: The crested serpent eagle (Spilornis cheela) is a medium-sized bird of prey that is found in forested habitats across tropical Asia. Within its widespread range across the Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia and East Asia, there are considerable variations and some authorities prefer to treat several of its subspecies as completely separate species.
f: They fly over the forest canopy on broad wings and tail have wide white and black bars.

t: The Philippine serpent eagle (Spilornis holospilus) is an eagle found in the major islands of the Philippines. It is sometimes treated as a race of the crested serpent eagle (Spilornis cheela).
f: It is illegal to hunt, capture or possess Philippine serpent eagles under Philippine Law RA 9147.

t: It was formerly considered conspecific with the other three species of Spindalis, with the common name stripe-headed tanager.
f: [[|thumb]] [[|thumb]] The western spindalis (Spindalis zena) is a songbird species.

t: The black siskin (Spinus atratus) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.

t: The black-chinned siskin (Spinus barbatus) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Argentina, Chile and the Falkland Islands.

t: The thick-billed siskin (Spinus crassirostris) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.
The red siskin (Spinus cucullatus) is a small endangered finch.
Lawrence's goldfinch (Spinus lawrencei) is a small songbird of erratic distribution that breeds in California and Baja California and winters in the southwestern United States and northern Mexico.

t: The hooded siskin (Spinus magellanicus) is a small passerine bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except French Guiana and Suriname.

t: The black-headed siskin (Spinus notatus) is a species of bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found in Mexico, Belize, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Nicaragua.

t: The olivaceous siskin (Spinus olivaceus) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Ecuador, and Peru, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and heavily degraded former forest.

t: The pine siskin (Spinus pinus) is a North American bird in the finch family. The pine siskin is currently listed as a species of Least Concern on the IUCN Red List.
f: It is a migratory bird with an extremely sporadic winter range.

t: The lesser goldfinch (Spinus psaltria) is a small finch in the genus Spinus native to the Americas.
f: As is the case for most species in the genus Spinus, lesser goldfinch males have a black forehead, which females lack.

t: The Andean siskin (Spinus spinescens) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, subtropical or tropical high-altitude grassland, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Venezuela.

t: The Eurasian siskin (Spinus spinus) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is also called the European siskin, common siskin or just siskin.
f: These birds exhibit an unusual migration pattern, migrating southwards in large numbers every few years in winter.

t: The American goldfinch (Spinus tristis) is a small North American bird in the finch family. It is migratory, ranging from mid-Alberta to North Carolina during the breeding season, and from just south of the Canada–United States border to Mexico during the winter.
f: The male displays brightly colored plumage during the breeding season to attract a mate.

t: The yellow-bellied siskin (Spinus xanthogastrus) is a small passerine bird in the family Fringillidae, the finches and euphonias.
f: It is found from Costa Rica south to Bolivia.

t: The dickcissel (Spiza americana) is a small seed-eating migratory bird in the family Cardinalidae. It is the only member of the genus Spiza, though some sources list another supposedly extinct species.
f: It breeds on the prairie grasslands of the Midwestern United States and winters in Central America, northern Colombia, and northern Venezuela.

t: The black-and-chestnut eagle (Spizaetus isidori), also known as Isidor's eagle, is a large South American species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. It is often placed in the monotypic genus Oroaetus.
f: The black-and-chestnut eagle is a typical forest raptor, hunting primarily small to medium-sized mammals and birds and constructing a large nest in a tall tree.

t: The black-and-white hawk-eagle (Spizaetus melanoleucus) is a bird of prey species in the eagle and hawk family (Accipitridae).
f: It is found throughout a large part of tropical America, from southern Mexico to northern Argentina.

t: The ornate hawk-eagle (Spizaetus ornatus) is a bird of prey from the tropical Americas. Formerly, some authorities referred to this species as the crested hawk-eagle, a name that may cause some confusion as it is more commonly used for an Asian eagle species.
f: The ornate hawk-eagle female lays almost always a single egg and the species has a fairly prolonged breeding cycle like many tropical raptors, especially due to a lengthy post-fledging stage on which juveniles are dependent on their parents.

t: The black hawk-eagle (Spizaetus tyrannus), also known as the tyrant hawk-eagle, is a species of eagle found from central Mexico through Central America into the south of Brazil to Colombia, eastern Peru, and as far as northern Argentina. There are two known subspecies, S.t. tyrannus, which is found in Southeastern Brazil and Northeastern Argentina, and the slightly smaller S. t. serus, which can be found elsewhere throughout the species' range.
f: Its preferred habitats include humid and moist forests close to rivers, and several types of woodland.

t: The black-chinned sparrow (Spizella atrogularis) is a small bird in the genus Spizella, in the New World sparrow family Passerellidae. It is found in the southwestern United States and throughout much of Mexico north of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec; most populations in the US migrate south after breeding while those in Mexico are resident.
f: The female does most or all of the egg incubation, but both parents feed the hatched nestlings.

t: Brewer's sparrow (Spizella breweri) is a small, slim species of American sparrow in the family Passerellidae.
f: This bird was named after the ornithologist Thomas Mayo Brewer.

t: The clay-colored sparrow or clay-coloured sparrow (Spizella pallida) is a small New World sparrow of North America. Adults have light brown upperparts and pale underparts, with darker streaks on the back.
f: The male sings from an open perch to indicate his ownership of the nesting territory.

t: The chipping sparrow (Spizella passerina) is a species of New World sparrow, a passerine bird in the family Passerellidae. The chipping sparrow has five subspecies.
f: It is widespread, fairly tame, and common across most of its North American range.

t: The field sparrow (Spizella pusilla) is a small New World sparrow in the family Passerellidae. It is about 140 mm (6 in) long and weighs about 12.5 g (0.4 oz).
f: The nest is a cup-shaped construction built on the ground and hidden beneath a bush or clump of grass.

t: Worthen's sparrow (Spizella wortheni) is a species of American sparrow that is endemic to northeastern Mexico. It was first described by Robert Ridgway in 1884 and named for the American naturalist Charles K.
f: This small bird has been listed as endangered by the IUCN since 1994.

t: The American tree sparrow (Spizelloides arborea), also known as the winter sparrow, is a medium-sized New World sparrow. It breeds in Alaska and Northern Canada and winters in Southern Canada and the Contiguous United States.
f: It is the only member of the genus Spizelloides.

t: The spot-winged falconet (Spiziapteryx circumcincta) is a species of bird of prey in family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay, and possibly Uruguay.

t: The crested finchbill (Spizixos canifrons) is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae.
f: It is found in south-eastern Asia from China and India to Indochina.

t: The collared finchbill (Spizixos semitorques) is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. It is found in China, Taiwan, Japan and Vietnam.
