f: The birds are typically monogamous, with females building nests in trees in which to lay their eggs.

t: The white-cheeked starling or grey starling (Spodiopsar cineraceus) is a passerine bird of the starling family.
f: It is native to eastern Asia where it is a common and well-known bird in much of its range.

t: The red-billed starling (Spodiopsar sericeus) is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae.
f: It is found in south and southeastern China.

t: The blue-capped tanager (Sporathraupis cyanocephala) is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, and Venezuela.
f: It was formerly placed in the genus Thraupis but is now the only species in the genus Sporathraupis.

t: The white-throated seedeater (Sporophila albogularis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is endemic to northeastern Brazil.

t: The chestnut-bellied seed finch (Sporophila angolensis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies. It formerly was found on Trinidad but has been extirpated.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The black-billed seed finch (Sporophila atrirostris) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The copper seedeater (Sporophila bouvreuil) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Brazil, Paraguay, Suriname, and as a vagrant to French Guiana.

t: Lesson's seedeater (Sporophila bouvronides) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, Trinidad, and Venezuela.
f: It has also been documented as a vagrant to the north of its usual range.

t: The double-collared seedeater (Sporophila caerulescens) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, and as a vagrant in Chile.

t: The chestnut-bellied seedeater (Sporophila castaneiventris) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The chestnut seedeater (Sporophila cinnamomea) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The rusty-collared seedeater (Sporophila collaris) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The variable seedeater (Sporophila corvina) is a passerine bird which breeds from southern Mexico through Central America to the Chocó of northwestern South America. The taxonomy is confusing, and it was formerly considered a subspecies of Sporophila americana (see Taxonomy).
f: Even within the variable seedeater as presently defined, there are great variations in plumage.

t: The large-billed seed finch (Sporophila crassirostris) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.
f: The species was also confirmed in Panama in 2011.

t: Temminck's seedeater (Sporophila falcirostris) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The white-naped seedeater (Sporophila fringilloides) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Guyana, and Venezuela.

t: The buffy-fronted seedeater (Sporophila frontalis) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is endemic to Brazil though there are unconfirmed reports from Argentina and Paraguay.

t: The thick-billed seed finch (Sporophila funerea) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found from Mexico to Ecuador.

t: The rufous-rumped seedeater (Sporophila hypochroma), also known as the grey-and-chestnut seedeater, is a Near Threatened species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The tawny-bellied seedeater (Sporophila hypoxantha) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, and as a vagrant to Peru.

t: The grey seedeater (Sporophila intermedia) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies. It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Guyana, and Venezuela.
f: It also possibly has occurred in Ecuador, has occurred in French Guiana as a vagrant, and has possibly been extirpated from Trinidad.

t: The white-bellied seedeater (Sporophila leucoptera) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found regularly in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Suriname and as a vagrant in French Guiana, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: The lined seedeater (Sporophila lineola) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Uruguay, though it has occurred in Chile and on Trinidad as a vagrant.

t: The black-and-white seedeater (Sporophila luctuosa) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Venezuela, and as a vagrant to Brazil.

t: The ruddy-breasted seedeater (Sporophila minuta) is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Mexico, most Central American countries, and across northern South America.

t: Morelet's seedeater (Sporophila morelleti) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found from Texas to Panama.

t: The wing-barred seedeater (Sporophila americana) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies. It formerly was found on Tobago but has been extirpated.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The yellow-bellied seedeater (Sporophila nigricollis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies. It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, on Trinidad, in the Lesser Antilles, and in every South American country except Chile and Uruguay.
f: However, it has been found in Argentina only as a vagrant and reports from Paraguay are unconfirmed.

t: The Nicaraguan seed finch (Sporophila nuttingi) or pink-billed seed finch is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies..
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Nicaragua and Panama.

t: The marsh seedeater (Sporophila palustris) is an Endangered species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The parrot-billed seedeater (Sporophila peruviana) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The pearly–bellied seedeater (Sporophila pileata) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, and possibly Bolivia.

t: The plumbeous seedeater (Sporophila plumbea) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile, Ecuador, and Uruguay, though its presence in Argentina is unconfirmed.

t: The dark-throated seedeater (Sporophila ruficollis) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, and as a vagrant to Peru.

t: The slate-colored seedeater (Sporophila schistacea) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies. It formerly occurred on Trinidad but has been extirpated there.
f: It is found in most countries of Central America and every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, French Guiana, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The drab seedeater (Sporophila simplex) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The chestnut-throated seedeater (Sporophila telasco) is a Neotropical songbird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
The cinnamon-rumped seedeater (Sporophila torqueola) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.

t: The speckle-fronted weaver (Sporopipes frontalis) is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae. Its natural habitat is dry savanna.
f: It is found in Africa from Mauritania and Gambia in the west to Ethiopia and Tanzania in the east.

t: The scaly-feathered weaver (Sporopipes squamifrons), also known as the scaly-feathered finch, is a species of bird in the family Ploceidae.
f: It is found in Angola, Botswana, Namibia, South Africa, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

t: The chestnut-rumped babbler (Stachyris maculata) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The grey-throated babbler (Stachyris nigriceps) is a species of passerine bird in the Old World babbler family Timaliidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The black-throated babbler (Stachyris nigricollis) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical swampland.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The grey-headed babbler (Stachyris poliocephala) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand.

t: The spot-necked babbler (Stachyris strialata) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in China, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The white-bibbed babbler (Stachyris thoracica) is a species of bird in the family Timaliidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

t: The white-eared barbet (Stactolaema leucotis) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae (African barbets).
f: It is found in Eswatini, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, South Africa, Tanzania, and Zimbabwe.

t: The green barbet (Cryptolybia olivacea) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family (African barbets). It is found in Kenya, Tanzania, Malawi, Mozambique and South Africa.
f: Its isolated populations are vulnerable to forest clearing.

t: The beautiful firetail (Stagonopleura bella) is a common species of estrildid finch found in Australia. The species inhabits temperate shrubland habitats in Australia.
f: It has an estimated global extent of occurrence of 1,000,000 km2 (390,000 sq mi).

t: The Indochinese yuhina or chestnut-collared yuhina (Staphida torqueola) is a bird in the family Zosteropidae.
f: The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1870.

t: The oilbird (Steatornis caripensis), locally known as the guácharo, is a bird species found in the northern areas of South America including the Caribbean island of Trinidad. It is the only living species in the genus Steatornis, the family Steatornithidae, and the order Steatornithiformes.
f: They are the only nocturnal flying fruit-eating birds in the world (the kākāpō, also nocturnal, is flightless).

t: The slender-billed greenbul (Stelgidillas gracilirostris) is a species in the monotypic genus Stelgidillas of the bulbul family of passerine birds. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in western and central Africa.

t: The southern rough-winged swallow (Stelgidopteryx ruficollis) a species of bird in the family Hirundinidae, the swallows and martins.
f: It is found in Central America from Honduras south, in every mainland South American country except Chile, on Trinidad, and as a vagrant to Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao, Tobago, and the Falkland Islands.

t: The northern rough-winged swallow (Stelgidopteryx serripennis) is a small, migratory swallow.
f: It is very similar to the southern rough-winged swallow, Stelgidopteryx ruficollis.

t: The fairy flycatcher or fairy warbler (Stenostira scita) is a small passerine bird. Formerly placed in the Old World flycatcher family, Muscicapidae, it is now separated with some other "odd flycatchers" as the new family Stenostiridae (Beresford et al. 2005, Fuchs et al. 2006).
f: Stenostira scita is a common seasonal migrant, breeding in karoo scrub and fynbos in the southern highlands, and migrating north in to spend the southern winter in thorn scrub at lower altitudes.

t: The crowned eagle, also known as the African crowned eagle or the crowned hawk-eagle (Stephanoaetus coronatus), is a large bird of prey found in sub-Saharan Africa; in Southern Africa, it is restricted to more easterly areas. Its preferred habitats are principally riparian woodlands and various forests.
f: However, in Durban, South Africa, domesticated animals comprised only 6% of the diet across 11 nests and 836 prey items, of which 3% were chickens.

t: The diademed tanager (Stephanophorus diadematus) is a species of Neotropical bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is purple-blue with a white crown characterised by a small red patch, and it is found mostly in open areas in southern Brazil, northeast Argentina, and Uruguay.
f: It is the only member of the genus Stephanophorus.
The green-crowned plovercrest, also black-breasted plovercrest or simply plovercrest, (Stephanoxis lalandi) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.

t: The purple-crowned plovercrest, or violet-crowned plovercrest, (Stephanoxis loddigesii) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: Its taxonomy is highly complex and a matter of dispute, with some splitting it into two or three species: Falkland skua (S. antarcticus), Tristan skua (S. hamiltoni), and subantarctic skua (S. lonnbergi).
f: To further confuse, it hybridizes with both the south polar and Chilean skuas, and the entire group has been considered to be a subspecies of the great skua, a species otherwise restricted to the Northern Hemisphere.
The long-tailed jaeger or long-tailed skua (Stercorarius longicaudus) is a seabird in the skua family Stercorariidae.

t: The south polar skua (Stercorarius maccormicki) is a large seabird in the skua family, Stercorariidae. This species and the other large skuas, such as the great skua, are sometimes placed in a separate genus Catharacta.
f: An older name for the bird is MacCormick's skua, after explorer and naval surgeon Robert McCormick, who first collected the type specimen.

t: The parasitic jaeger or arctic skua (Stercorarius parasiticus), also known as the parasitic skua or arctic jaeger, is a seabird in the skua family Stercorariidae. Kleptoparasitism is a major source of food for this species during migration and winter, and is where the name is derived from.
f: It is a migratory species breeding in Northern Fennoscandia, Scotland, Iceland, Greenland, Northern Canada, Alaska, and Siberia and wintering across the southern hemisphere.

t: The pomarine jaeger (Stercorarius pomarinus), pomarine skua, or pomatorhine skua, is a seabird in the skua family Stercorariidae.
f: It is a migrant, wintering at sea in the tropical oceans.

t: The great skua (Stercorarius skua), sometimes known by the name bonxie in Britain, is a large seabird in the skua family Stercorariidae. It is roughly the size of a herring gull.
f: It mainly eats fish caught at the sea surface or taken from other birds.

t: The river tern or Indian river tern (Sterna aurantia) is a tern in the family Laridae, the largest species currently included in the genus Sterna of typical terns. It is a resident breeder along inland rivers from Pakistan east through the Indian subcontinent, to Myanmar, Thailand, and Cambodia, where it is uncommon.
f: Unlike most Sterna terns, it is almost exclusively found on freshwater, rarely venturing even to tidal creeks.

t: The roseate tern (Sterna dougallii) is a species of tern in the family Laridae.
f: The genus name Sterna is derived from Old English "stearn", "tern", and the specific dougallii refers to Scottish physician and collector Dr Peter McDougall (1777–1814). "Roseate" refers to the bird's pink breast in breeding plumage.

t: Forster's tern (Sterna forsteri) is a tern in the family Laridae. The genus name Sterna is derived from Old English "stearn", "tern", and forsteri commemorates the naturalist Johann Reinhold Forster.
f: The offering of fish by the male to the female is part of the courtship display.

t: The South American tern (Sterna hirundinacea) is a species of tern found in coastal regions of southern South America, including the Falkland Islands, ranging north to Peru (Pacific coast) and Brazil (Atlantic coast). It is generally the most common tern in its range.
f: The smaller, highly migratory common tern closely resembles it.

t: The common tern (Sterna hirundo) is a seabird in the family Laridae. This bird has a circumpolar distribution, its four subspecies breeding in temperate and subarctic regions of Europe, Asia and North America.
f: Breeding in a wider range of habitats than any of its relatives, the common tern nests on any flat, poorly vegetated surface close to water, including beaches and islands, and it readily adapts to artificial substrates such as floating rafts.

t: The Arctic tern (Sterna paradisaea) is a tern in the family Laridae. This bird has a circumpolar breeding distribution covering the Arctic and subarctic regions of Europe (as far south as Brittany), Asia, and North America (as far south as Massachusetts).
f: These are by far the longest migrations known in the animal kingdom.

t: The white-cheeked tern (Sterna repressa) is a species of tern in the family Laridae.
f: It is found around the coasts on the Red Sea, around the Horn of Africa to Kenya, in the Persian Gulf and along the Iranian coast to Pakistan and western India.

t: The white-fronted tern (Sterna striata), also known as tara, sea swallow, black-billed tern, kahawai bird, southern tern, or swallow tail, was first described by Johann Friedrich Gmelin in 1789. A medium-sized tern with an all-white body including underwing and forked tail, with pale grey hues on the mantle and upper side of the wing.
f: This is the most abundant tern in New Zealand.

t: The black-naped tern (Sterna sumatrana) is an oceanic tern mostly found in tropical and subtropical areas of the Indian Ocean and western Pacific Ocean. It is most closely related to roseate tern S. dougallii and white-fronted tern S. striata.
f: It was described from the islands around Sumatra.

t: The snowy-crowned tern (Sterna trudeaui), also known as Trudeau's tern, is a species of bird in subfamily Sterninae of the family Laridae, the gulls, terns, and skimmers.
f: It is native to Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Uruguay, and possibly Paraguay, and also vagrant in Peru and the Falkland Islands.

t: The Antarctic tern (Sterna vittata) is a seabird in the family Laridae. It ranges throughout the southern oceans and is found on small islands around Antarctica as well as on the shores of the mainland.
f: The Antarctic tern does not migrate like the Arctic tern does, but it can still be found on a very large range.

t: The little tern (Sternula albifrons) is a small seabird of the family Laridae. It is widely distributed breeding on the coasts and inland waterways of Europe, Asia, north and west Africa, and eastern Australia.
f: It winters in the subtropical and tropical oceans as far south as South Africa and Australia.

t: The least tern (Sternula antillarum) is a species of tern that breeds in North America and locally in northern South America. It is closely related to, and was formerly often considered conspecific with, the little tern of the Old World.
f: It has occurred as a vagrant to Europe, with one record in Great Britain and one in Ireland.

t: Saunders's tern (Sternula saundersi), sometimes known as the black-shafted tern, is a species of bird in the family Laridae. It is a close relative of the little tern, least tern, yellow-billed tern, and Peruvian tern.
f: It is sparsely resident along the shores of the north-western Indian Ocean .

t: The yellow-billed tern (Sternula superciliaris) is a small seabird found in South America. It is a species of tern in the family Laridae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, Uruguay, and Venezuela.

t: The greater wagtail-tyrant (Stigmatura budytoides) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The lesser wagtail-tyrant (Stigmatura napensis) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
The burnished-buff tanager (Stilpnia cayana), also known as the rufous-crowned tanager, is a common South American species of bird in the family Thraupidae.

t: The blue-necked tanager (Stilpnia cyanicollis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in South America from Colombia to Bolivia.
f: The male and female feed the nestlings on insects and fruit, and may be assisted by helpers.

t: The black-headed tanager (Stilpnia cyanoptera) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in the Andes of northeastern Colombia and the Venezuelan Coastal Range.

t: The black-capped tanager (Stilpnia heinei) is one of the many species of Neotropical bird in the family Thraupidae. It lives in the mountains of Ecuador, Colombia, and Venezuela year-round.
f: This bird can often be found in open landscapes, alone or in pairs, hiding under branches of trees and bushes.

t: The golden-hooded tanager (Stilpnia larvata) is a medium-sized passerine bird. This tanager is a resident breeder from southern Mexico south to western Ecuador.
f: The golden-hooded tanager's call is a sharp tsit and the song is a tuneless rattled series of tick sounds.

t: The masked tanager (Stilpnia nigrocincta) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The black-backed tanager (Stilpnia peruviana) is a bird species in the Thraupidae family. When first described, it was mistakenly believed that it originates from Peru, leading to the misleading scientific name peruviana.
f: It is endemic to the forests and shrubs of south-eastern Brazil.

t: The chestnut-backed tanager (Stilpnia preciosa) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in southern Brazil, north-eastern Argentina, eastern Paraguay, and Uruguay in mature forests (especially edges) up to 1000m elevation.
f: It was previously considered a color morph of the black-backed tanager (Stilpnia peruviana); however, Stilpnia is not known to be polymorphic, and the two species have different habitat preferences and breeding range.

t: The scrub tanager (Stilpnia vitriolina) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: It has a total length of around 12 cm (4+3⁄4 in), has dark upperparts, and a throat and chest that, depending on the subspecies, is yellow-orange or deep orange.
f: The orange-breasted forest robin (Stiphrornis erythrothorax) is a species of bird mainly found throughout the African tropical rainforest.

t: The southern emu-wren (Stipiturus malachurus) is a species of bird in the Australasian wren family, Maluridae.
f: Its natural habitats are temperate forests, and Mediterranean-type shrubby vegetation, and swamplands.

t: The double-barred finch (Stizoptera bichenovii) is an estrildid finch found in dry savannah, tropical (lowland) dry grassland and shrubland habitats in northern and eastern Australia. It is the only species placed in the genus Stizoptera .
f: It is sometimes referred to as Bicheno's finch or as the owl finch, the latter of which owing to the dark ring of feathers around the face.

t: The white-gaped honeyeater (Stomiopera unicolor) is a species of bird in the family Meliphagidae. The white-gaped honeyeater was previously placed in the genus Lichenostomus, but was moved to Stomiopera after a molecular phylogenetic analysis published in 2011 showed that the original genus was polyphyletic.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.

t: The black currawong (Strepera fuliginosa), also known locally as the black jay, is a large passerine bird endemic to Tasmania and the nearby islands within the Bass Strait. One of three currawong species in the genus Strepera, it is closely related to the butcherbirds and Australian magpie within the family Artamidae.
f: Omnivorous, its diet includes a variety of berries, invertebrates, and small vertebrates.

t: The pied currawong (Strepera graculina) is a black passerine bird native to eastern Australia and Lord Howe Island. One of three currawong species in the genus Strepera, it is closely related to the butcherbirds and Australian magpie of the family Artamidae.
f: Known for its melodious calls, the species' name currawong is believed to be of indigenous origin.

t: The grey currawong (Strepera versicolor) is a large passerine bird native to southern Australia, including Tasmania. One of three currawong species in the genus Strepera, it is closely related to the butcherbirds and Australian magpie of the family Artamidae.
f: It builds nests high in trees, which has limited the study of its breeding habits.

t: The ring-necked dove (Streptopelia capicola), also known as the Cape turtle dove, half-collared dove, or the Cape Lager is a widespread and often abundant dove species in East and southern Africa. Within range, its penetrating and rhythmic, three-syllabled crooning is a familiar sound at any time of the year.
f: It is a mostly sedentary bird, found in a variety of open habitats.

t: The spotted dove or eastern spotted dove (Spilopelia chinensis) is a small and somewhat long-tailed pigeon that is a common resident breeding bird across its native range on the Indian subcontinent and in East and Southeast Asia. The species has been introduced to many parts of the world and feral populations have become established.
f: They fly from the ground with an explosive flutter and will sometimes glide down to a perch.

t: The Eurasian collared dove (Streptopelia decaocto), often called the collared dove, is a dove species from the genus Streptopelia. It is native to Europe, Asia, and North Africa.
f: It is grey-buff to pinkish-grey, and has a black half-collar edged with white on its nape, alluding to the name.

t: The mourning collared dove or African mourning dove (Streptopelia decipiens) is a dove which is a widespread resident breeding bird in Africa south of the Sahara. It often mingles peacefully with other doves.
f: This species is common or abundant near water.
The dusky turtle dove or pink-breasted turtle dove (Streptopelia lugens) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.

t: The Oriental turtle dove or rufous turtle dove (Streptopelia orientalis) is a member of the bird family Columbidae. The species has a wide native distribution range from Central Asia east across Asia to Japan.
f: Populations in the higher latitudes tend to migrate south in winter, while those closer to the tropics are sedentary.

t: The African collared dove (Streptopelia roseogrisea) is a small dove found in the Sahel, northern parts of the Horn of Africa and southwestern Arabia. Although it lives in arid lands, it is found around water sources.
f: It has a diet of grass seeds and other plants.

t: It has been listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List since 2004.
f: The red-eyed dove (Streptopelia semitorquata) is a dove that is widespread and common in Sub-Saharan Africa.

t: The laughing dove (Spilopelia senegalensis) is a small pigeon that is a resident breeder in Africa, the Middle East, South Asia, and Western Australia where it has established itself in the wild after being released from Perth Zoo in 1898. This small long-tailed dove is found in dry scrub and semi-desert habitats where pairs can often be seen feeding on the ground.
f: Other names include laughing turtle dove, palm dove and Senegal dove while in Asia the name little brown dove is often used.

t: The red collared dove (Streptopelia tranquebarica), also known as the red turtle dove, is a small pigeon which is a resident breeding bird in the tropics of Asia. The female is much plainer, with pale brown plumage similar to that of the larger Eurasian collared dove.
f: The male has a blue-grey head and a red-brown body.

t: The European turtle dove (Streptopelia turtur) is a threatened or vulnerable member of the bird family Columbidae, the doves and pigeons.
f: It breeds over a wide area of the south western Palearctic including north Africa but migrates to northern sub-Saharan Africa in winter.
The vinaceous dove (Streptopelia vinacea) is a bird species in the pigeon family Columbidae that widely resident across northern Sub-Saharan Africa.

t: The biscutate swift (Streptoprocne biscutata) is a species of bird in subfamily Cypseloidinae of the swift family Apodidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and possibly Paraguay.

t: The chestnut-collared swift (Streptoprocne rutila) is a species of bird in subfamily Cypseloidinae of the swift family Apodidae.
f: It is found from Mexico and Trinidad south to Peru and Bolivia.

t: The white-collared swift (Streptoprocne zonaris) is a species of bird in the subfamily Cypseloidinae of the swift family Apodidae.
f: It is found in Mexico, Central America, the Greater and Lesser Antilles, Trinidad, and every mainland South American country.

t: The tawny owl (Strix aluco), also called the brown owl, is a stocky, medium-sized owl in the family Strigidae. It is commonly found in woodlands across Europe, as well as western Siberia, and has seven recognized subspecies.
f: It is able to hunt successfully at night because of its vision, hearing adaptations and ability to fly silently.
The Chaco owl (Strix chacoensis) is an owl found in Argentina, Bolivia, and Paraguay.

t: The fulvous owl (Strix fulvescens), or Guatemala barred owl, is a resident of the cloud forests of Central America. Its typical coloration is warm dark brown or reddish brown on the back and lighter brown on the front with darker barring.
f: A medium-sized true owl, it has a round head, lacking ear tufts.

t: The desert owl or desert tawny owl (Strix hadorami), formerly known as Hume's owl, is a species of owl. It is closely related to the more widespread tawny owl and to the range-restricted Omani owl.
f: It nests in crevices and holes in cliffs.

t: It is found in Argentina, Brazil (where it is known as the Brazilian owl), and Paraguay.
f: The rusty-barred owl (Strix hylophila) is a medium-sized "typical owl" in subfamily Striginae.

t: The brown wood owl (Strix leptogrammica) is found in India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Taiwan, and south China. The brown wood owl is a resident breeder in south Asia.
f: S. (l.) bartelsi (Bartels's wood-owl), Javan wood-owl from Java, the southeasternmost taxon, has a loud, forceful, single HOOH! with long pauses between calls.

t: It is distributed across the Northern Hemisphere and is the only species in the genus Strix found in both Eastern and Western Hemispheres.
f: The great grey owl (Strix nebulosa) (also great gray owl in American English) is a true owl, and is the world's largest species of owl by length.

t: The Himalayan owl or Himalayan wood owl (Strix nivicolum) is a medium-sized owl native to the forests and mountain ranges of the Himalayas, Taiwan and Korea. Although populations are declining, this owl is not considered endangered and is currently listed as a species of Least Concern on the IUCN Red List due to its large range and slow decline.
f: Few studies have been done on its lifestyle and current population trends.

t: The spotted owl (Strix occidentalis) is a species of true owl. It is a resident species of old-growth forests in western North America, where it nests in tree hollows, old bird of prey nests, or rock crevices.
f: Nests can be between 12 and 60 metres (40 and 200 ft) from the ground, and usually contain two eggs (though some contain as many as four).

t: The mottled wood owl (Strix ocellata) is a species of large owl found in India and Nepal. They are found in gardens and thin deciduous forests adjacent to dry thorn forests or farmland.
f: The characteristic call is a duet of the male and female, while other notes include a low hoot and a screech.

t: The rufous-legged owl (Strix rufipes) is a medium-sized owl.
f: It is found in Argentina and Chile.

t: The spotted wood owl (Strix seloputo) is an owl of the earless owl genus, Strix.
f: Its range is disjunct; it occurs in many regions surrounding Borneo, but not on that island itself.

t: The Ural owl (Strix uralensis) is a large nocturnal owl. It is a member of the true owl family, Strigidae.
f: Breeding success is often strongly correlated with prey populations.

t: The barred owl (Strix varia), also known as the northern barred owl, striped owl, or more informally, hoot owl or eight hooter, is a North American large species of owl. A member of the true owl family, Strigidae, they belong to the genus Strix, which is also the origin of the family's name under Linnaean taxonomy.
f: Evidence shows the assorted threats posed by the invading barred species are only increasing.

t: The African wood owl (Strix woodfordii) or Woodford's owl, is a typical owl from the genus Strix in the family Strigidae and is arguably the most common forest owl in Africa. It inhabits wooded areas and possesses a distinctive call.
f: During the day it roosts singly or in pairs in dense cover, high in trees, whilst at night it forages for food.

t: The apostlebird (Struthidea cinerea), also known as the grey jumper, lousy jack or happy family, is a quick-moving, gray or black bird about 33 cm (13 in) long. It is a native to Australia where it roams woodlands, eating insects and seeds at, or near, ground level.
f: Apostlebirds often travel in groups of about 12; for this reason, they were named after the 12 Biblical apostles.

t: The common ostrich (Struthio camelus), or simply ostrich, is a species of flightless bird native to certain areas of Africa (and historically, Arabia) and is the largest living species of bird. The common ostrich is one of two extant species of ostriches, the only living members of the genus Struthio in the ratite group of birds.
f: It is distinctive in its appearance, with a long neck and legs, and can run for a long time at a speed of 55 km/h (34 mph) with short bursts up to about 70 km/h (43 mph), the fastest land speed of any bipedal animal.

t: The eastern meadowlark (Sturnella magna) is a medium-sized icterid bird, very similar in appearance to its sister species, the western meadowlark. The Chihuahuan meadowlark was formerly considered to be conspecific with the eastern meadowlark.
f: It occurs from eastern North America to northern South America, where it is also most widespread in the east.

t: The western meadowlark (Sturnella neglecta) is a medium-sized icterid bird, about 20 cm (7.9 in) in length. It is found across western and central North America and is a partial migrant, breeding in western Canada and western United States west of the Great Lakes, and in northern Mexico.
f: The western meadowlark is the state bird of six states; in Kansas, Montana, Nebraska, North Dakota, Oregon, and Wyoming.

t: The Malabar starling (Sturnia blythii) is a species of starling found in southwestern India. It was previously considered a subspecies of the chestnut-tailed starling.
f: Nestlings eat insects, lepidopteran larvae, beetles, small vertebrates, and nectar.

t: The chestnut-tailed starling (Sturnia malabarica), also called grey-headed starling and grey-headed myna is a member of the starling family. The species name is after the distribution of a former subspecies in the Malabar region.
f: It is a resident or partially migratory species found in wooded habitats in India and Southeast Asia.

t: The brahminy starling or brahminy myna (Sturnia pagodarum) is a member of the starling family of birds.
f: It is usually seen in pairs or small flocks in open habitats on the plains of the Indian subcontinent.

t: The white-shouldered starling (Sturnia sinensis) is a species of bird in the starling family Sturnidae.
f: It breeds in southern China and northern Vietnam; it winters in Southeast Asia.

t: The spotless starling (Sturnus unicolor) is a passerine bird in the starling family, Sturnidae.
f: It is closely related to the common starling (S. vulgaris), but has a much more restricted range, confined to the Iberian Peninsula, Northwest Africa, southernmost France, and the islands of Sicily, Corsica and Sardinia.

t: The common starling (Sturnus vulgaris), also known simply as the starling in Great Britain and Ireland, and as the European starling in North America, is a medium-sized passerine bird in the starling family, Sturnidae. It is about 20 cm (8 in) long and has glossy black plumage with a metallic sheen, which is speckled with white at some times of the year.
f: Large flocks typical of this species can be beneficial to agriculture by controlling invertebrate pests; however, starlings can also be pests themselves when they feed on fruit and sprouting crops.

t: The northern scrub flycatcher (Sublegatus arenarum) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Aruba, Bonaire, Colombia, Costa Rica, Curaçao, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Suriname, Trinidad, and Venezuela.

t: The southern scrub flycatcher (Sublegatus modestus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers. It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.
f: Other sources also place it in Guyana, Suriname, as a non-breeding visitor to Colombia, and as a vagrant in Ecuador.

t: The Amazonian scrub flycatcher or Todd's scrub flycatcher (Sublegatus obscurior) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The black honeyeater (Sugomel nigrum) is a species of bird in the honeyeater family Meliphagidae and the sole species in the genus Sugomel. The black honeyeater exhibits sexual dimorphism, with the male being black and white while the female is a speckled grey-brown; immature birds look like the female.
f: The male engages in a soaring song flight in the mating season, but contributes little to nest-building or incubating the clutch of two or three eggs.

t: The suiriri flycatcher (Suiriri suiriri) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Suriname, and Uruguay.

t: The masked booby (Sula dactylatra), also called the masked gannet or the blue-faced booby, is a large seabird of the booby and gannet family, Sulidae. First described by the French naturalist René-Primevère Lesson in 1831, the masked booby is one of six species of booby in the genus Sula.
f: These birds are spectacular plunge divers, plunging into the ocean at high speed in search of prey—mainly flying fish.

t: The Nazca booby (Sula granti) is a large seabird of the booby family, Sulidae, native to the eastern Pacific. First described by Walter Rothschild in 1902, it was long considered a subspecies of the masked booby until recognised as distinct genetically and behaviorally in 2002.
f: It has a typical sulid body shape, with a long pointed orange-yellow bill, long neck, aerodynamic body, long slender wings and pointed tail.

t: The brown booby (Sula leucogaster) is a large seabird in the booby and gannet family Sulidae, of which it is one of the most common and widespread species. It has a pantropical range, which overlaps with that of other booby species.
f: They nest only on the ground, and roost on solid objects rather than the water surface.

t: The blue-footed booby (Sula nebouxii) is a species of marine bird in the family Sulidae. The species is native to subtropical and tropical regions of the eastern Pacific Ocean.
f: The male displays its feet in an elaborate mating ritual by lifting them up and down while strutting before the female.

t: The red-footed booby (Sula sula) is a large seabird of the booby family, Sulidae. Adults always have red feet, but the colour of the plumage varies.
f: They are powerful and agile fliers, harnessing the wind to fly efficiently, but they are clumsy in takeoffs and landings.

t: The northern hawk-owl or northern hawk owl (Surnia ulula), is a medium-sized true owl of the northern latitudes. It is non-migratory and usually stays within its breeding range, though it sometimes irrupts southward.
f: It is one of the few owls that is not strictly nocturnal nor crepuscular, often being active during the day.

t: The fork-tailed drongo-cuckoo (Surniculus dicruroides) is a species of cuckoo that resembles the Black drongo (Dicrurus macrocercus). It is found mainly in hill forests in peninsular India and Sri Lanka although some specimens are known from the Himalayan foothills.
f: They are also known for their drongo-like calls such as "quip" calls in flight and "wheep-wheep" call with a higher second note.

t: The square-tailed drongo-cuckoo (Surniculus lugubris) is a species of cuckoo that resembles a black drongo. It is found along the Himalayas extending east into Southeast Asia.
f: The calls are series of piercing sharp whistles rising in pitch but shrill and choppily delivered.

t: The Philippine drongo-cuckoo (Surniculus velutinus) is a bird of the cuckoo family found only in the Philippines. It was formerly a subspecies of the Square-tailed drongo-cuckoo.
f: It is declining due to habitat loss.

t: The black-throated parrotbill (Suthora nipalensis) is a bird species often placed with the Old World babblers (family Timaliidae) or in the family Sylviidae, but it actually seems to belong to the distinct family Paradoxornithidae. It is found in the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the central and eastern Himalayas, and in adjoining parts of Southeast Asia.
f: The species ranges across Bhutan, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, Tibet and Vietnam.

t: The golden parrotbill (Suthora verreauxi) is a species of bird in the family Paradoxornithidae. It is found in China, Laos, Japan, Myanmar, Taiwan, and Vietnam.
f: Its scientific name commemorates French ornithologist and collector Jules Verreaux.

t: Swynnerton's robin (Swynnertonia swynnertoni) is a species of passerine bird belonging to the family Muscicapidae. It is monotypic within the genus Swynnertonia.
f: The common and Latin names commemorate the entomologist Charles Swynnerton.
The African hill babbler (Sylvia abyssinica) is a species of bird in the family Sylviidae.

t: The Eurasian blackcap (Sylvia atricapilla) is a bird usually known simply as the blackcap. It is a common and widespread warbler.
f: The male's typical song is a rich musical warbling, often ending in a loud high-pitched crescendo, but a simpler song is given in some isolated areas, such as valleys in the Alps.

t: The Rwenzori hill babbler (Sylvia atriceps) is a species of passerine bird in the family Sylviidae that is found in Africa. The Rwenzori hill babbler was described by the English zoologist Richard Bowdler Sharpe in 1902 and given the binomial name Turdinus atriceps.
f: The type locality is the Rwenzori Mountains on the border between Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

t: The garden warbler (Sylvia borin) is a common and widespread small bird that breeds in most of Europe and in the Palearctic to western Siberia. It is a plain, long-winged and long-tailed warbler with brown upperparts and dull white underparts; the sexes are similar and juveniles resemble the adults.
f: The garden warbler's rich melodic song is similar to that of the blackcap, its closest relative, which competes with it for territory when nesting in the same woodland.

t: The greater whitethroat or common whitethroat (Curruca communis) is a common and widespread Old World warbler which breeds throughout Europe and across much of temperate western Asia.
f: This small passerine bird is strongly migratory, and winters in tropical Africa, Arabia, and Pakistan.

t: The bush blackcap (Sylvia nigricapillus) is a species of bird in the family Sylviidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.
f: It is endemic to South Africa and Eswatini.

t: The northern crombec (Sylvietta brachyura) is a species of African warbler, formerly placed in the family Sylviidae.
f: Its natural habitat is dry savanna.

t: The long-billed crombec or Cape crombec (Sylvietta rufescens) is an African warbler. The long-billed crombec breeds in southern Africa from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Zambia and Tanzania southwards to South Africa.
f: This is a common species in fynbos, open woodland, savannah and dry Acacia scrub.
The red-capped crombec (Sylvietta ruficapilla) is a species of African warbler, formerly placed in the family Sylviidae.

t: The green crombec (Sylvietta virens) is a species of African warbler, formerly placed in the family Sylviidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist shrubland.
f: It is widespread across the African tropical rainforest.

t: The red-faced crombec (Sylvietta whytii) is a species of African warbler, formerly placed in the family Sylviidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests, subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.
f: It is found in Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zimbabwe.

t: Des Murs's wiretail (Sylviorthorhynchus desmurii) is a small passerine bird of southern South America which belongs to the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: Molecular phylogenetics places it within the Synallaxinae and indicates that the genus diverged from the Leptasthenura about 14–15 million years ago.

t: The tawny tit-spinetail (Sylviorthorhynchus yanacensis) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, and Peru.

t: The yellow-browed tit (Sylviparus modestus) is a species of bird in the family Paridae. It is placed in the monotypic genus Sylviparus.
f: It has a small bill, short tail, strong legs, and greenish feathers.
The yellow-billed kingfisher (Syma torotoro) is a medium-sized tree kingfisher.

t: The spectacled monarch (Symposiachrus trivirgatus) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, subtropical or tropical mangrove forests, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Australia, Indonesia, and Papua New Guinea.

t: The pale-breasted spinetail (Synallaxis albescens) is a passerine bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, Trinidad, and in every mainland South American country except Chile and Ecuador.

t: The dark-breasted spinetail (Synallaxis albigularis) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The white-lored spinetail (Synallaxis albilora) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: Azara's spinetail (Synallaxis azarae) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The slaty spinetail or slaty castlebuilder, (Synallaxis brachyura), is a passerine bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found from Honduras south to Peru.

t: Cabanis's spinetail (Synallaxis cabanisi) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Bolivia, and Peru.

t: The white-whiskered spinetail (Synallaxis candei) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.
The black-throated spinetail (Synallaxis castanea) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The chestnut-throated spinetail (Synallaxis cherriei) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is mainly found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The grey-bellied spinetail (Synallaxis cinerascens) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
The Bahia spinetail (Synallaxis cinerea) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The stripe-breasted spinetail (Synallaxis cinnamomea) is a passerine bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Trinidad, Tobago, and Venezuela.
The Apurimac spinetail (Synallaxis courseni) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The rufous-breasted spinetail (Synallaxis erythrothorax) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Belize, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.

t: The sooty-fronted spinetail (Synallaxis frontalis) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
The rusty-headed spinetail (Synallaxis fuscorufa) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The plain-crowned spinetail (Synallaxis gujanensis) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.
The red-shouldered spinetail (Synallaxis hellmayri) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
The great spinetail (Synallaxis hypochondriaca) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The cinereous-breasted spinetail (Synallaxis hypospodia) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Peru.

t: Pinto's spinetail (Synallaxis infuscata) is an Endangered species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae. It is known locally as "tatac".
f: It is endemic to north-eastern Brazil.

t: The hoary-throated spinetail (Synallaxis kollari) is an Endangered bird species in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil and Guyana.

t: McConnell's spinetail (Synallaxis macconnelli) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The Maranon spinetail (Synallaxis maranonica) is a Critically Endangered species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The dusky spinetail (Synallaxis moesta) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The rufous-capped spinetail (Synallaxis ruficapilla) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The ruddy spinetail (Synallaxis rutilans) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, Venezuela, and possibly Guyana.

t: The ochre-cheeked spinetail (Synallaxis scutata) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Peru.

t: Spix's spinetail (Synallaxis spixi), previously known as the chicli spinetail, is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The necklaced spinetail (Synallaxis stictothorax) is a species of ovenbird in the family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.
The silvery-throated spinetail (Synallaxis subpudica) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The blackish-headed spinetail (Synallaxis tithys) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The rufous spinetail (Synallaxis unirufa) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The planalto foliage-gleaner (Syndactyla dimidiata), also known as the russet-mantled foliage-gleaner, is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Brazil and Paraguay.
The guttulate foliage-gleaner (Syndactyla guttulata) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.

t: The rufous-necked foliage-gleaner (Syndactyla ruficollis) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The buff-browed foliage-gleaner (Syndactyla rufosuperciliata) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: The Bolivian recurvebill (Syndactyla striata) is a bird species in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia and Peru.

t: The lineated foliage-gleaner (Syndactyla subalaris) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The Peruvian recurvebill (Syndactyla ucayalae) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil and Peru.

t: The king quail (Synoicus chinensis), also known as the Asian blue quail, blue-breasted quail, Chinese painted quail, button quail, or Chung-Chi, is a very small, diminutive galliform of the tribe Coturnicini in the subfamily Phasianinae. They are the smallest member in this subfamily and the family Phasianidae, as well as being the smallest and lightest member of the order Galliformes.
f: Its voice is a piping whistle, ti-yu or ti-ti-yu.

t: The brown quail (Synoicus ypsilophorus), also known as the swamp quail, silver quail and Tasmanian quail, is an Australasian true quail of the family Phasianidae. It is a small, ground-dwelling bird and is native to mainland Australia, Tasmania and Papua New Guinea and has been introduced to New Zealand and Fiji.
f: Widespread and common throughout its large range, the brown quail is evaluated as being of least concern by the International Union for Conservation of Nature on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species.

t: The whistling heron (Syrigma sibilatrix) is a medium-sized, often terrestrial heron of South America. There are two subspecies, the southern S. s. sibilatrix and the northern S. s. fostersmithi.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Syrigma.
Pallas's sandgrouse (Syrrhaptes paradoxus) is a medium to large bird in the sandgrouse family.
Tschudi's nightjar or lesser band-winged nightjar (Quechuavis decussata) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.

t: The band-winged nightjar or greater band-winged nightjar (Systellura longirostris) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is widespread in South America, where it is found in the Andes, Venezuelan Coastal Range, Santa Marta Mountains, Tepuis, most of Chile, Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, and eastern Brazil.
f: It is the only species now placed in the genus Systellura.

t: The sirkeer malkoha or sirkeer cuckoo (Taccocua leschenaultii), is a non-parasitic cuckoo found in dry scrub forest and open woodland habitats in the Indian subcontinent. The species is long-tailed, largely olive brown on the upper side with a distinctive curved red beak tipped in yellow.
f: They forage singly or in pairs mainly on or close to the ground creeping between grasses and bushes, often on rocky habitats where they feed on small lizards, insects, and sometimes berries and seeds.

t: The Antillean palm swift (Tachornis phoenicobia) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae.
f: It is found on the Caribbean islands of Cuba, Jamaica, and Hispaniola (shared by the Dominican Republic and Haiti).

t: The fork-tailed palm swift or Neotropical palm swift (Tachornis squamata) is a species of bird in subfamily Apodinae of the swift family Apodidae.
f: It is found across most of northern South America and on Trinidad and Tobago.

t: The many-colored rush tyrant or many-coloured rush tyrant (Tachuris rubrigastra) is a small passerine bird of South America belonging to the tyrant flycatcher family Tyrannidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: The least grebe (Tachybaptus dominicus), an aquatic bird, is the smallest member of the grebe family.
f: It occurs in the New World from the southwestern United States and Mexico to Argentina, and also on Trinidad and Tobago, the Bahamas and the Greater Antilles.

t: At 25–27 cm (9.8–10.6 in) in length, it is one of the smallest members of the grebe family, along with the least grebe and little grebe.
f: The Australasian grebe (Tachybaptus novaehollandiae) is a small waterbird common on fresh water lakes and rivers in greater Australia, New Zealand and on nearby Pacific islands.

t: The little grebe (Tachybaptus ruficollis), also known as the dabchick, is a member of the grebe family of water birds. The genus name is from Ancient Greek takhus "fast" and bapto "to sink under".
f: The specific ruficollis is from Latin rufus "red" and Modern Latin -collis, "-necked", itself derived from Latin collum "neck".

t: The mangrove swallow (Tachycineta albilinea) is a passerine bird in the swallow family that breeds in coastal regions from Mexico through Central America to Panama. It has blue-green upperparts, blackish flight feathers, a white rump, a black tail, and white underparts.
f: It can be identified by the supraloral white streak, the white line near its eye, which only occurs in two other species of Tachycineta: the violet-green swallow and the white-rumped swallow.

t: The white-winged swallow (Tachycineta albiventer) is a resident breeding swallow in tropical South America found in Brazil, Colombia, Venezuela, Trinidad, and Argentina. It is not found west of the Andes.
f: This swallow is largely non-migratory.

t: The tree swallow (Tachycineta bicolor) is a migratory bird of the family Hirundinidae. Found in the Americas, the tree swallow was first described in 1807 by French ornithologist Louis Vieillot as Hirundo bicolor.
f: This swallow is negatively affected by human activities, such as the clearing of forests; acidified lakes can force a breeding tree swallow to go long distances to find calcium-rich food items to feed to its chicks.

t: The golden swallow (Tachycineta euchrysea) is a swallow endemic to the Caribbean island of Hispaniola (split between the Dominican Republic and Haiti) and was once native to Jamaica, but is now extirpated there. It is restricted to isolated montane forests that primarily consist of the Hispaniolan pine (Pinus occidentalis).
f: In Hispaniola, this swallow breeds from April to July, where it lays a clutch consisting of two to four white eggs.

t: The Chilean swallow (Tachycineta leucopyga) is a species of bird in the family Hirundinidae.
f: It breeds in Chile and Patagonia, migrating north as far as Bolivia, Paraguay, and Rio Grande do Sul.

t: The white-rumped swallow (Tachycineta leucorrhoa) is a species of bird in the family Hirundinidae. First described and given its binomial name by French ornithologist Louis Pierre Vieillot in 1817, it was for many years considered a subspecies of the Chilean swallow.
f: Usually, only one brood with four to seven eggs is laid, although a second one will occasionally be laid.

t: The violet-green swallow (Tachycineta thalassina) is a small North American passerine bird in the swallow family. These aerial insectivores are distributed along the west coast from Alaska to Mexico, extending as far east as Montana and Texas.
f: With an appearance very similar to the tree swallow, these individuals can be identified by the white rump side-patches that appear to separate their green back and purple tail.
The flying steamer duck (Tachyeres patachonicus), also known as the flying steamer-duck or flying steamerduck, is a species of South American duck in the family Anatidae.

t: The ruby-crowned tanager (Tachyphonus coronatus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and as a vagrant to Uruguay.

t: The tawny-crested tanager (Tachyphonus delatrii) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The red-shouldered tanager (Tachyphonus phoenicius) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The white-lined tanager (Tachyphonus rufus) is a medium-sized passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae.
f: It is a resident breeder from Costa Rica south to northern Argentina and on the islands of Trinidad and Tobago.

t: The fulvous-crested tanager (Tachyphonus surinamus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The South African shelduck or Cape shelduck (Tadorna cana) is a species of shelduck, a group of large goose-like birds in the bird family Anatidae, which includes the swans, geese and ducks. This is a common species native to southern Africa.
f: In the austral winter, many birds move north-east from the breeding range to favoured moulting grounds, where sizable concentrations occur.

t: The ruddy shelduck (Tadorna ferruginea) is a bird species in the family Anatidae. It is a distinctive waterfowl, 58 to 70 cm (23 to 28 in) in length with a wingspan of 110 to 135 cm (43 to 53 in).
f: It is a migratory bird, wintering in the Indian subcontinent and breeding in southeastern Europe and central Asia, though there are small resident populations in North Africa.

t: The common shelduck (Tadorna tadorna) is a waterfowl species of the shelduck genus Tadorna. Wintering is in temperate to subtropical regions.
f: It is widespread and common in the Palearctic, in Europe and northwest Africa mainly breeding on temperate coasts, saline pools and estuaries, and in Asia on inland salt lakes; increasingly it is also using open freshwater habitats inland.

t: The Australian shelduck (Tadorna tadornoides), also known as the chestnut-breasted shelduck or mountain duck, is a shelduck, a group of large goose-like ducks part of the bird family Anatidae. The genus name Tadorna comes from Celtic roots and means "pied waterfowl".
f: They are protected under the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974.

t: The paradise shelduck (Tadorna variegata), also known as the paradise duck, or pūtangitangi in Māori, is a species of shelduck, a group of goose-like ducks, which is endemic to New Zealand. Johann Friedrich Gmelin placed it in the genus Anas with the ducks, geese, and swans.
f: Paradise shelducks mate for life and usually live as pairs, and moult their feathers from December to February.

t: The collared owlet (Taenioptynx brodiei), also known as the collared pygmy owl, is a species of owl in the family Strigidae. Its natural habitat is submontane and montane forests with open spaces and is distributed throughout oriental Asia.
f: It is the smallest owl in Asia, at 15 cm (5.9 in) and 60 g (2.1 oz).

t: The Sunda zebra finch (Taeniopygia guttata) is a species of bird in the family Estrildidae. For almost two centuries, its closest relative from Australia was generally included in T.guttata as a subspecies; since the 2020s it is generally considered a separate species Taeniopygia castanotis.
f: It is found in the Lesser Sundas.

t: The black-chested tyrant (Taeniotriccus andrei) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Brazil, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The olive-spotted hummingbird (Talaphorus chlorocercus) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of the subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The black-billed brushturkey, yellow-legged brushturkey or black-billed talegalla (Talegalla fuscirostris) is a species of bird in the family Megapodiidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is found in the Aru Islands and New Guinea.

t: The collared brushturkey, brown-collared brushturkey, or red-legged brushturkey (Talegalla jobiensis) is a species of bird in the family Megapodiidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in the northern part of New Guinea.

t: The eastern chipmunk (Tamias striatus) is a chipmunk species found in eastern North America.
f: It is the only living member of the genus Tamias.

t: The American red squirrel (Tamiasciurus hudsonicus) is one of three species of tree squirrels currently classified in the genus Tamiasciurus, known as the pine squirrels . The American red squirrel is variously known as the pine squirrel or piney squirrel, North American red squirrel, chickaree, boomer, or simply red squirrel.
f: The squirrel has been expanding its range into hardwood forests.

t: The golden tanager (Tangara arthus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its plumage is overall golden-yellow with black to the back, wings, tail and ear-coverts.
f: It is widespread and often common in highland forests of the Andes (from Bolivia and northwards) and Venezuelan Coastal Range in north-western South America.

t: The paradise tanager (Tangara chilensis) is a brilliantly multicolored, medium-sized songbird whose length varies between 13.5 and 15 cm (5.3 to 6"). It has a light green head, sky blue underparts and black upper body plumage.The vivid colours of the paradise tanager have been linked to underlying achromatic feather layers (black or white) that enhance the brilliance of structural colours.
f: Found in humid tropical and subtropical forests in the western and northern Amazon Basin in South America, the species can be found in Venezuela, Peru, Colombia, Ecuador, Bolivia and Brazil.

t: The red-necked tanager (Tangara cyanocephala) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Brazil, Argentina, and Paraguay.

t: The gilt-edged tanager (Tangara cyanoventris) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical moist montane forest, and heavily degraded former forest.

t: The brassy-breasted tanager (Tangara desmaresti) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.
f: Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The spangle-cheeked tanager (Tangara dowii) is a medium-sized passerine bird. This tanager is an endemic resident breeder in the highlands of Costa Rica and western Panama.
f: The bulky cup nest, lined with bromeliad leaves, is built in a tree fork or on a branch high amongst the epiphytes.

t: The emerald tanager (Tangara florida) is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, and Panama.
f: The emerald tanager makes cup nests out of moss, where eggs are laid in clutches of two.

t: The bay-headed tanager (Tangara gyrola) is a medium-sized passerine bird.
f: This tanager is a resident breeder in Costa Rica, Panama, South America south to Ecuador, Bolivia, and north-western Brazil, and on Trinidad.

t: The silver-throated tanager (Tangara icterocephala) is a species of passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, and northeastern Peru.
f: Breeding occurs from April–September, and two broods are raised in a single breeding season.

t: The plain-colored tanager (Tangara inornata) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, and Panama.

t: The metallic-green tanager (Tangara labradorides) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The rufous-winged tanager (Tangara lavinia) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama.

t: The turquoise tanager (Tangara mexicana) is a medium-sized passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is a resident bird from Trinidad, much of Brazil, Colombia, and Venezuela, and south to Bolivia.
f: The bulky cup nest is built in a tree or shrub, and the female incubates three brown-blotched grey-green eggs.
The beryl-spangled tanager (Tangara nigroviridis) is a small songbird of the northern Andes.

t: The flame-faced tanager (Tangara parzudakii) is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is endemic to South America and is found in the eastern Andes of Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela.
f: Eggs are laid in clutches of two, and are white with pale brown flecking concentrated on the larger end.

t: The green-and-gold tanager (Tangara schrankii) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers. It is one of 27 species in the genus Tangara.
f: It is found in the western and central Amazon Basin in eastern Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, central Bolivia, and northwestern Brazil.

t: The green-headed tanager (Tangara seledon) is a brightly colored bird found in the Atlantic forest in south-eastern Brazil, far eastern Paraguay, and far north-eastern Argentina (Misiones only). As other members of the genus Tangara, it is a small colorful bird, measuring an average of 13.5 centimeters (5.3 in) and a mass of 18g (0.6 oz).
f: Females and juvenile birds have similar, though duller coloration.

t: The blue-and-black tanager (Tangara vassorii) is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is found in the Andes of Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela, where it inhabits montane evergreen forest, dwarf forest, and secondary forest at elevations of 1,500–3,500 m (4,900–11,500 ft).
f: It breeds from February to August, making cup nests out of moss and rootlets.

t: The opal-rumped tanager (Tangara velia) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in the Amazon and Atlantic Forest of South America.
f: The population of the Atlantic Forest has a far paler chest than the other populations, and has often been considered a separate species as the silvery-breasted tanager (Tangara cyanomelas).

t: The saffron-crowned tanager (Tangara xanthocephala) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Found in the northern Andes of Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela, it inhabits cloud forest, forest edges, and secondary forest, preferring areas with mossy trees.
f: The only known nest contained a clutch of two eggs.

t: The azure-rumped parrot (Tanygnathus sumatranus) is a large bird endemic to Indonesia. It is found in Sulawesi and the Sangir Islands.
f: Flocks are small and often active at night.

t: The common paradise kingfisher (Tanysiptera galatea), also known as the Galatea paradise kingfisher and the racquet-tailed kingfisher, is a species of bird in the family Alcedinidae. It is found in subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests of the Maluku Islands and New Guinea.
f: Like all paradise kingfishers, it has a red bill and colourful plumage.

t: The buff-breasted paradise kingfisher (Tanysiptera sylvia) is a bird in the tree kingfisher subfamily, Halcyoninae. It is native to Australia and New Guinea.
f: It migrates in November from New Guinea to its breeding grounds in the rainforest of North Queensland, Australia.

t: The striped cuckoo (Tapera naevia) is a bird, the only member of the genus Tapera. This resident cuckoo is found from Mexico and Trinidad south to Bolivia and Argentina and Colombia.
f: It is among the very few brood parasitic cuckoos of the Americas (only other are Dromococcyx), and typical hosts are spinetails, but often also wrens, and other species with domed nests.

t: The great antshrike (Taraba major) is a passerine bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in southern Mexico, in every Central American country except El Salvador, on Trinidad, and in every mainland South American country except Chile, though only as a vagrant in Uruguay.

t: The Chaco earthcreeper (Tarphonomus certhioides) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, and Paraguay, and as a vagrant in Brazil.

t: The Bolivian earthcreeper (Tarphonomus harterti) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Bolivia.
The golden bush robin (Tarsiger chrysaeus) or golden bush-robin was first discovered in 1845 by Brian Houghton Hodgson, a British naturalist.

t: The red-flanked bluetail (Tarsiger cyanurus), also known as the orange-flanked bush-robin, is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family. It breeds in mixed coniferous forests in northern Asia, parts of central Asia, and northeastern Europe.
f: It is migratory, wintering mainly in southeast Asia, in the Indian subcontinent, the Himalayas, Taiwan, and northern Indochina.

t: The white-browed bush robin (Tarsiger indicus) is a species of passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family Muscicapidae that is found from the Himalayas to south-central China and north Vietnam. The Taiwan bush robin was formerly regarded as a subspecies.
f: Its natural habitat is Rhododendron and conifer forests.

t: The collared bush-robin or Johnstone's robin (Tarsiger johnstoniae) is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) has assessed it as a least-concern species.
f: It is endemic to Taiwan, living in montane and subalpine forests.
While currently under review, this taxon is not current recognized as a species by BirdLife international.

t: The Knysna turaco (Tauraco corythaix), or, in South Africa, Knysna loerie, is a large turaco, one of a group of African musophagidae birds. It is a resident breeder in the mature evergreen forests of southern and eastern South Africa, and Eswatini.
f: Turacos (the 10 species of the Tauraco and the 2 of the Musophaga) are the only birds to possess true red and green colour.

t: Fischer's turaco (Tauraco fischeri) is a species of bird in the family Musophagidae. It is found in Coastal East Africa, including Kenya, Somalia, and Tanzania.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss and trapping for the wildlife trade.

t: Hartlaub's turaco (Tauraco hartlaubi) is a species of bird in the family Musophagidae. The common name and Latin binomial commemorate the German physician and ornithologist Gustav Hartlaub.
f: It is found in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: The white-cheeked turaco (Menelikornis leucotis) is a species of bird in the family Musophagidae. It is found in Eritrea, Ethiopia, and South Sudan.
f: This species is the most commonly raised turaco in captive conditions.

t: Livingstone's turaco (Tauraco livingstonii) is a species of bird in the family Musophagidae, which was named for Charles Livingstone, the brother of David Livingstone. It is distributed through the subtropical lowlands of southeastern Africa.
f: It has an isolated population in Burundi, and is besides found from southern Tanzania to eastern and southern Malawi, eastern Zimbabwe, widely in Mozambique and along the subtropical coast of South Africa.

t: The yellow-billed turaco (Tauraco macrorhynchus) is a species of bird in the family Musophagidae. It has been proposed that they be recognised as two phylogenetic species, based on the biogeography, morphology and molecular phylogeny, and that the species be transferred to genus Musophaga, because they are not recovered with other Tauraco species.
f: It is found in Angola, Cameroon, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ivory Coast, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Nigeria, and Sierra Leone.

t: The Guinea turaco (Tauraco persa), also known as the green turaco or green lourie, is a species of turaco, a group of African otidimorph birds.
f: It formerly included the Livingstone's, Schalow's, Knysna, black-billed and Fischer's turacos as subspecies.
