t: The purple-crested turaco (Gallirex porphyreolophus) or, in South Africa, the purple-crested loerie, (Khurukhuru in the Luvenḓa (Venḓa) language) is a species of bird in the turaco clade with an unresolved phylogenetic placement. Initial analyses placed the purple-crested turaco in the family Musophagidae, but studies have indicated that these birds do not belong to this family and have been placed in the clade of turacos with an unresolved phylogeny.
f: It is the National Bird of the Kingdom of Eswatini, and the crimson flight feathers of this and related turaco species are important in the ceremonial regalia of the Swazi royal family.

t: Schalow's turaco (Tauraco schalowi) is a frugivorous bird in the family Musophagidae.
f: This bird's common name and Latin binomial commemorate the German banker and amateur ornithologist Herman Schalow.
The brown-crowned tchagra (Tchagra australis) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae.

t: This family of passerine birds is closely related to the true shrikes in the family Laniidae, and was once included in that group. This species is found in the Arabian Peninsula and most of Africa in scrub, open woodland, semi-desert and cultivation.
f: The black-crowned tchagra (Tchagra senegalus) is a bushshrike.

t: This species is a bushshrike, a group closely related to the true shrikes in the family Laniidae, and formerly included in that family.
f: The southern tchagra (Tchagra tchagra) is a passerine bird found in dense scrub and coastal bush in southern and south-eastern South Africa and Eswatini.

t: The sandy gallito (Teledromas fuscus) is a species of suboscine passerine bird in the family Rhinocryptidae, the tapaculos.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Teledromas.

t: The Nīhoa finch (Telespiza ultima)(Hawaiian: palihoa) is one of the two endemic bird species of the tiny Hawaiian island of Nīhoa, the other being the Nīhoa millerbird. The Nīhoa finch was added to the Endangered Species List by the U.S.
f: The island's population is 1000–3000 birds.

t: Bocage's bushshrike (Chlorophoneus bocagei), also known as the grey-green bushshrike, is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is scatteredly present throughout central Africa.

t: Doherty's bushshrike (Telophorus dohertyi) is a colourful but skulking species of bush-shrike of the family Malaconotidae which is found in forest habitats in north-central Africa.
f: The common name and Latin binomial commemorate the American collector William Doherty.

t: The black-fronted bushshrike (Chlorophoneus nigrifrons) is a passerine bird of the bushshrike family, Malaconotidae. It inhabits forests mainly in East Africa.
f: It forms a superspecies with the many-colored bushshrike (C. multicolor) and the two are sometimes considered to be a single species.

t: The olive bushshrike (Chlorophoneus olivaceus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is found in Malawi, Mozambique, South Africa, Eswatini, and Zimbabwe.
f: It forages for insects in the forest canopy.

t: The orange-breasted bushshrike or sulphur-breasted bushshrike (Chlorophoneus sulfureopectus) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae.
f: Another bird, Braun's bushshrike, is also sometimes called the orange-breasted bushshrike.

t: The gorgeous bushshrike (Telophorus viridis) is a species of bird in the family Malaconotidae. It is also known as the four-coloured bushshrike.
f: Some use the name gorgeous bushshrike for the subspecies Telophorus viridis viridis only.

t: The bokmakierie (Telophorus zeylonus) is a bushshrike. This family of passerine birds is closely related to the true shrikes in the family Laniidae, and was once included in that group.
f: The bokmakierie has a range of loud whistles and calls, often given by a pair in antiphonal duet, but the most typical is the one that gives this species its name, bok-bok-mak-kik.

t: The ratchet-tailed treepie (Temnurus temnurus) is a species of bird in the crow and jay family Corvidae. The species is also known as the notch-tailed treepie.
f: The species has a disjunct distribution in Southeast Asia and China.

t: The common woodshrike (Tephrodornis pondicerianus) is a species of bird found in Asia. It is now usually considered a member of the family Vangidae.
f: It is small and ashy brown with a dark cheek patch and a broad white brow.

t: The Malabar woodshrike (Tephrodornis sylvicola) is a species of bird usually placed in the family Vangidae.
f: It is sometimes considered a subspecies of the large woodshrike.

t: The large woodshrike (Tephrodornis virgatus) is found in south-eastern Asia, Sumatra, Java, and Borneo.
f: Its natural habitats are temperate forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical mangrove forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

t: The bateleur (; Terathopius ecaudatus), also known as the bateleur eagle, is a medium-sized eagle in the family Accipitridae. It is often considered a relative of the snake eagles and, like them, it is classified within the subfamily Circaetinae.
f: They tend to build a relatively small if sturdy stick nest in a large tree and lay only a single egg.

t: The ruddy-tailed flycatcher (Terenotriccus erythrurus) is a small passerine bird in the family Onychorhynchidae. It was previously place in family Tityridae.
f: However, it differs in voice, behaviour, and structure from members of that group.

t: The streak-capped antwren (Terenura maculata) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.
The orange-bellied antwren (Terenura sicki) or Sick's antwren, is a Critically Endangered species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
The yellow-headed warbler (Teretistris fernandinae) is one of two species of bird in the Cuban warbler family Teretistridae.

t: The Oriente warbler (Teretistris fornsi) is one of two species of bird in the Cuban warbler family Teretistridae.
f: It is endemic to central and eastern Cuba.

t: Blyth's paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone affinis), also called the oriental paradise flycatcher, is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae. This species occupies evergreen broadleaf forests and forest edges, including secondary growth, gardens, and plantations, typically in lowland and foothill regions.
f: Some populations undertake migratory movements.

t: The black paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone atrocaudata), also known as the Japanese paradise flycatcher, is a medium-sized passerine bird native to southeastern Asia. It is a glossy black, chestnut and white bird, slightly smaller than either the Amur paradise flycatcher or Blyth's paradise flycatcher, but similar in appearance.
f: Outside the breeding season it migrates to China, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, other parts of the Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, and Sumatra, Indonesia.

t: The Mascarene paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone bourbonnensis) is a species of bird in the monarch-flycatcher family Monarchidae. There are two subspecies recognized: the nominate subspecies from Réunion, also known as the Réunion paradise flycatcher; and T. b. desolata (Salomonsen, 1933) from Mauritius.
f: It is endemic to the Mascarene islands of Mauritius and Réunion.

t: The rufous paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone cinnamomea) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae native to Indonesia and the Philippines.
f: Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland forests.

t: The Amur paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone incei) is a bird species in the family Monarchidae. It is native to China and Primorsky Krai in the Russian Far East.
f: It is a winter migrant to Southeast Asia.

t: The Malagasy paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone mutata) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.
f: It is found in Comoros, Madagascar, and Mayotte.

t: The Indian paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone paradisi) is a medium-sized passerine bird in the monarch flycatcher family, Monarchidae. As the global population is considered stable, it has been listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List since 2004.
f: Indian paradise flycatchers feed on insects, including grasshoppers, butterflies and praying mantises, as well as flies.

t: The red-bellied paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone rufiventer), also known as the black-headed paradise flycatcher, is a medium-sized passerine bird of the family of monarch flycatchers. It is native to intra-tropical forests of Africa.
f: It is closely related to the African paradise flycatcher, and the two can hybridise.

t: The African paradise flycatcher (Terpsiphone viridis) is a medium-sized passerine bird. The two central tail feathers of the male are extended into streamers that commonly are more than twice as long as the body.
f: It builds a neat cup nest in which it lays a clutch, usually of two or three eggs.

t: The swallow tanager (Tersina viridis) is a species of Neotropic bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies. It has occurred as a vagrant in those two countries and on Tobago and Bonaire and there are unconfirmed reports from Curaçao.
f: It occurs regularly in Panama, on Trinidad, and in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The grey-bellied tesia (Tesia cyaniventer) is a species of warbler in the family Cettiidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: Its range extends from the Himalayas through southern China and Indochina (the Cardamom and Annamite ranges in particular).

t: The russet-capped tesia (Tesia everetti) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Cettiidae.
f: The scientific name commemorates British colonial administrator and zoological collector Alfred Hart Everett.

t: The slaty-bellied tesia (Tesia olivea) is a species of warbler in the family Cettiidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, and Vietnam.

t: The Javan tesia (Tesia superciliaris) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Cettiidae. It is endemic to Java in Indonesia.
f: It feeds on insects in the undergrowth of broadleaf forest.

t: The western capercaillie (Tetrao urogallus), also known as the Eurasian capercaillie, wood grouse, heather cock, cock-of-the-woods, or simply capercaillie , is a heavy member of the grouse tribe and the largest of all extant grouse species. The bird shows extreme sexual dimorphism, with males nearly twice the size of females.
f: Found across Europe and the Palearctic, this primarily-ground-dwelling forest grouse is renowned for its courtship display.

t: The Caucasian snowcock (Tetraogallus caucasicus) is a snowcock in the pheasant family Phasianidae of the order Galliformes, gallinaceous birds. It is native to the Caucasus Mountains, particularly the Western Caucasus, where it breeds at altitudes from 2000 to 4000 m on bare stony mountains.
f: It nests in a bare ground scrape and lays typically 5-6 greenish eggs, which are incubated only by the female.

t: The Tibetan snowcock (Tetraogallus tibetanus) is a bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae of the order Galliformes, gallinaceous birds. This species is found in high-altitude regions of the Western Himalayas and the Tibetan Plateau, where it overlaps in part with the larger Himalayan snowcock.
f: The head is greyish and there is a white crescent patch behind the eye and underside is white with black stripes.

t: The hazel grouse (Tetrastes bonasia), sometimes called the hazel hen, is one of the smaller members of the grouse tribe of birds. The bird is sometimes referred to as "rabchick" (from рябчик) by early 20th century English speaking travellers to Russia.
f: It is a sedentary species, breeding across the Palearctic as far east as Hokkaido, and as far west as central Europe, in dense, damp, mixed coniferous woodland, preferably with some spruce.

t: The little bustard (Tetrax tetrax) is a bird in the bustard family, the only member of the genus Tetrax.
f: It breeds in Southern Europe and in Western and Central Asia.

The black-browed albatross (Thalassarche melanophris), also known as the black-browed mollymawk, is a large seabird of the albatross family Diomedeidae; it is the most widespread and common member of its family.
The lesser crested tern (Thalasseus bengalensis) is a tern in the family Laridae.

t: The greater crested tern (Thalasseus bergii), also called crested tern, swift tern, or great crested tern, is a tern in the family Laridae that nests in dense colonies on coastlines and islands in the tropical and subtropical Old World. Its four or five subspecies breed in the area from South Africa around the Indian Ocean to the central Pacific and Australia, all populations dispersing widely from the breeding range after nesting.
f: This is an adaptable species that has learned to follow fishing boats for jettisoned bycatch, and to use unusual nest sites such as the roofs of buildings and artificial islands in salt pans and sewage works.

t: The elegant tern (Thalasseus elegans) is a tern in the family Laridae. It breeds on the Pacific coast of southern California in the United States and western Mexico, and migrates south to Peru, Ecuador and Chile for the northern winter; in the late summer and fall, some also disperse north to Oregon and more rarely Washington.
f: The first European record was at Carlingford Lough in County Down, Northern Ireland, in late June 1982.

t: The royal tern (Thalasseus maximus) is a tern in the family Laridae.
f: The species is endemic to the Americas, though vagrants have been identified in Europe.

t: The Sandwich tern (Thalasseus sandvicensis) is a tern in the family Laridae. It is very closely related to the lesser crested tern (T. bengalensis), Chinese crested tern (T. bernsteini), Cabot's tern (T. acuflavidus), and elegant tern (T. elegans) and has been known to interbreed with both elegant and lesser crested terns.
f: Like all Thalasseus terns, the Sandwich tern feeds by plunge-diving for fish, usually in marine environments, and the offering of fish by the male to the female is part of the courtship display.

t: The crowned woodnymph (Thalurania colombica) or violet-crowned woodnymph, is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found from Belize and Guatemala to far-northern Peru.

t: The fork-tailed woodnymph (Thalurania furcata) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The violet-capped woodnymph (Thalurania glaucopis) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The russet antshrike (Thamnistes anabatinus) is a passerine bird in subfamily Myrmornithinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country except El Salvador, Colombia, Ecuador, Venezuela, and possibly Peru.

t: The mocking cliff chat, mocking chat or cliff chat, (Thamnolaea cinnamomeiventris) is a species of chat in the family Muscicapidae which occurs in rocky habitats in much of eastern Sub-Saharan Africa.
f: It is the only species placed in the genus Thamnolaea.

t: The dusky-throated antshrike (Thamnomanes ardesiacus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The cinereous antshrike (Thamnomanes caesius) is an insectivorous bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The saturnine antshrike (Thamnomanes saturninus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The bluish-slate antshrike (Thamnomanes schistogynus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

t: The white-shouldered antshrike (Thamnophilus aethiops) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The Amazonian antshrike (Thamnophilus amazonicus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
The Sooretama slaty antshrike (Thamnophilus ambiguus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The upland antshrike (Thamnophilus aroyae) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in the eastern Andes of Bolivia and southeastern Peru.

t: The black-crowned antshrike (Thamnophilus atrinucha) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in every Central American country except El Salvador and in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The collared antshrike (Thamnophilus bernardi) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The black-hooded antshrike (Thamnophilus bridgesi) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The variable antshrike (Thamnophilus caerulescens) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: Castelnau's antshrike (Thamnophilus cryptoleucus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The barred antshrike (Thamnophilus doliatus) is a passerine bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds". It is found in the Neotropics in Mexico, every country in Central America, Trinidad and Tobago, and every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.
f: There is also one accepted record from southern Texas.

t: The black-backed antshrike (Thamnophilus melanonotus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The bar-crested antshrike (Thamnophilus multistriatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The mouse-colored antshrike (Thamnophilus murinus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The black antshrike (Thamnophilus nigriceps) is a species of insectivorous bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia and Panama.

t: The blackish-grey antshrike (Thamnophilus nigrocinereus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana and Venezuela.

t: The chestnut-backed antshrike (Thamnophilus palliatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.
The planalto slaty antshrike (Thamnophilus pelzelni) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".

t: The cocha antshrike (Thamnophilus praecox) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The northern slaty antshrike (Thamnophilus punctatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The rufous-capped antshrike (Thamnophilus ruficapillus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: The plain-winged antshrike (Thamnophilus schistaceus), sometimes called the black-capped antshrike, is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: Natterer's slaty antshrike (Thamnophilus stictocephalus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia and Brazil.

t: The Bolivian slaty antshrike (Thamnophilus sticturus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The lined antshrike (Thamnophilus tenuepunctatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The rufous-winged antshrike (Thamnophilus torquatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

t: The uniform antshrike (Thamnophilus unicolor) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: Chapman's antshrike (Thamnophilus zarumae) is a species of bird in subfamily Thamnophilinae of family Thamnophilidae, the "typical antbirds".
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: They inhabit savanna-like habitats, woodland and forest margins, but avoid dense humid forest such as the Amazon.
f: This species is officially called a parakeet by the AOU and by birders, though usually called conures in aviculture.
The plumbeous ibis (Theristicus caerulescens), also formerly called the blue ibis, is a large distinctive ibis species endemic to parts of central South America.

t: The buff-necked ibis (Theristicus caudatus), also known as the white-throated ibis, is a fairly large ibis found widely in open habitats of eastern and northern South America.
f: It formerly included the similar black-faced ibis as a subspecies, but that species is almost entirely restricted to colder parts of South America, has a buff (not dark grey) lower chest, and lacks the contrasting large white wing-patches.

t: The black-faced ibis (Theristicus melanopis) is a species of bird in the family Threskiornithidae. It has been included as a subspecies of the similar buff-necked ibis, but today all major authorities accept the split.
f: It is found in grassland and fields in southern and western South America.

t: The swamp palm bulbul (Thescelocichla leucopleura), is a species of songbird in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae.
f: It is monotypic within the genus Thescelocichla.

t: The grey-breasted seedsnipe (Thinocorus orbignyianus) is a species of bird in the family Thinocoridae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.

t: The least seedsnipe (Thinocorus rumicivorus) is a xerophilic species of bird in the Thinocoridae family. It breeds in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.
f: They are common across South America and have been recorded in Ecuador, the Falkland Islands, Uruguay, Brazil, and as far away as Antarctica.
The rufous-chested tanager (Thlypopsis ornata) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.

t: The chestnut-headed tanager (Thlypopsis pyrrhocoma) is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is found in the Atlantic Forest of southeast Brazil, eastern Paraguay, and far northeastern Argentina.
f: It was formerly the only member of the genus Pyrrhocoma but is now placed in Thlypopsis.

t: The orange-headed tanager (Thlypopsis sordida) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Native to South America, it is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, and Venezuela, where it inhabits successional vegetation, cerrado, riparian forest, shrub, brush, and open woodland.
f: The orange-headed tanager is omnivorous, feeding on insects, spiders, fruit, and seeds.

t: The superciliaried hemispingus (Thlypopsis superciliaris) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The yellow-winged tanager (Thraupis abbas) is a neotropical member of the tanager family. It is distinguished by the yellow patches on its dusky green wings, marking an otherwise dark bluish and gray body.
f: It is of average size for a tanager, about 18-centimetre (7.1 in) long.

t: The azure-shouldered tanager (Thraupis cyanoptera) is a species of bird in the tanager family, Thraupidae. Described by the French zoologist Louis Pierre Vieillot in 1817, it is only found in the Atlantic Forest of southeastern Brazil, from southeastern Bahia, eastern Minas Gerais, and Espírito Santo south to northern Rio Grande do Sul.
f: Its habit of eating leaves is an unusual aspect of its diet.

t: The blue-gray tanager (Thraupis episcopus) is a medium-sized South American songbird of the tanager family, Thraupidae. Its range is from Mexico south to northeast Bolivia and northern Brazil, all of the Amazon Basin, except the very south.
f: It has been introduced to Lima (Peru) and Florida (United States).

t: The golden-chevroned tanager (Thraupis ornata) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical moist montane forest, and heavily degraded former forest.

t: The palm tanager (Thraupis palmarum) is a medium-sized passerine bird. This tanager is a resident breeder from Nicaragua south to Bolivia, Paraguay, and southern Brazil.
f: It also breeds on Trinidad and, since 1962, on Tobago.

t: The sayaca tanager (Thraupis sayaca) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers. It is a common resident in northeastern, central, and southeastern Brazil (Portuguese: sanhaço [sɐ̃ˈɲasu] or sanhaçu [sɐ̃ɲaˈsu]), and Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina (where they are known as celestinos or celestinas).
f: It feeds on flowers, buds, and insects, and this omnivorous lifestyle has helped it to become perhaps the most — or one of the most — common urban birds in southeastern Brazil, along with the rufous-bellied thrush.

t: The pale-tailed barbthroat (Threnetes leucurus) is a species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae.
f: It is found throughout much of the Amazon Basin from the eastern Andean foothills to the Atlantic Ocean.
The band-tailed barbthroat (Threnetes ruckeri) is a medium-sized hummingbird that is found from southeastern Guatemala and Belize to western Ecuador and western Venezuela.

t: The African sacred ibis (Threskiornis aethiopicus) is a species of ibis, a wading bird of the family Threskiornithidae. It is native to much of Africa, as well as small parts of Iraq, Iran and Kuwait.
f: It is especially known for its role in Ancient Egyptian religion, where it was linked to the god Thoth.

t: It is the only native ibis species in its range that has an overall white plumage with a black neck and head. The down-curved beak and legs are also black.
f: This species of ibis nests only during the rainy season.

t: The Australian white ibis (Threskiornis molucca) , commonly known as the bin chicken, is a wading bird of the family Threskiornithidae. It is widespread across much of Australia.
f: While it is closely related to the African sacred ibis, the Australian white ibis is a native Australian bird.

t: The Australian white ibis (Threskiornis molucca) , commonly known as the bin chicken, is a wading bird of the family Threskiornithidae. It is widespread across much of Australia.
f: While it is closely related to the African sacred ibis, the Australian white ibis is a native Australian bird.

t: The flammulated treehunter (Thripadectes flammulatus) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The striped treehunter (Thripadectes holostictus) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The uniform treehunter (Thripadectes ignobilis) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The black-billed treehunter (Thripadectes melanorhynchus) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The streak-breasted treehunter (Thripadectes rufobrunneus) is a passerine bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The Peruvian treehunter (Thripadectes scrutator) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae. It is found in Bolivia and Peru.
f: It is also called the rufous-backed treehunter or buff-throated treehunter.

t: The streak-capped treehunter (Thripadectes virgaticeps) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Venezuela.

t: The Orinoco softtail (Thripophaga cherriei) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

t: The plain softtail (Thripophaga fusciceps) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The striated softtail (Thripophaga macroura) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is endemic to eastern Brazil.

t: Bewick's wren (Thryomanes bewickii) is a wren native to North America. It is the only species placed in the genus Thryomanes.
f: The song is loud and melodious, much like the song of other wrens.

t: Niceforo's wren (Thryophilus nicefori) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical high-altitude dry shrubland.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The banded wren (Thryophilus pleurostictus) is a small songbird of the wren family. It is a resident breeding species from central Mexico to Costa Rica.
f: The call of this species is a nasal cherrrt or a rattle and roll, kert rrruk kert rrruk, and the melodious and complex song is a mix of clear whistles and musical trills.

t: The rufous-and-white wren (Thryophilus rufalbus) is a small songbird of the wren family. It is a resident breeding species from southwesternmost Mexico to northern Colombia and northwestern Venezuela.
f: The call of this species is a sharp chek or explosive tuck, and the song is a melodious and very distinctive sequence of slow hooting whistles, such as weee, boo, boo, booo, boo, whit.

t: The Antioquia wren (Thryophilus sernai) is a passerine from the wren family (Troglodytidae). It was discovered in March 2010 in the vicinity of the Cauca River in Antioquia, Colombia and described as a new species by Lara et al (2012).
f: Due to this low genetic diversity, hope for the Antiquia Wren to not stay extinct is low, as genetic variability has a fundamental role in evolution and sustaining endangered populations.

t: The Sinaloa wren (Thryophilus sinaloa) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is endemic to Mexico, with almost annual sightings in the United States, in Arizona.

t: The Carolina wren (Thryothorus ludovicianus) is a species of wren common in the eastern United States, the extreme south of Ontario, Canada, the northeast and southeast of Mexico, and into northern Central America. Severe winters restrict the northern limits of their range, while favorable weather conditions lead to a northward extension of their breeding range.
f: Both males and females give out alarm calls, but only males sing to advertise territory.

t: The yellow-faced grassquit (Tiaris olivaceus) is a passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae and is the only member of the genus Tiaris.
f: It is native to Central America, South America, and the Caribbean.

t: The wallcreeper (Tichodroma muraria) is a small passerine bird found throughout the high mountains of the Palearctic from southern Europe to central China.
f: It is the only extant member of both the genus Tichodroma and the family Tichodromidae.

t: The broad-billed warbler (Tickellia hodgsoni) is a species of bush warbler (family Cettiidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage, and belongs to the monotypic genus Tickellia.
f: It is found in Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, and Vietnam.

t: The rufescent tiger heron (Tigrisoma lineatum) is a species of heron, birds in the family Ardeidae.
f: It is found in wetlands from Central America through much of South America.

t: The bare-throated tiger heron (Tigrisoma mexicanum) is a wading bird of the heron family, Ardeidae, found from Mexico to northwestern Colombia, with one recorded sighting from the United States in Hidalgo County, Texas. It is 80 cm (31 in) in length and weighs 1,200 g (42 oz).
f: It waits often motionless for suitable prey such as fish, frogs or crabs to come within reach of its long bill.

t: The chestnut-capped babbler (Timalia pileata) is a passerine bird of the family Timaliidae.
f: It is monotypic within the genus Timalia.

t: The puna tinamou (Tinamotis pentlandii), also known as Pentland's tinamou, is a member of the tinamou family. The binomial name of the species commemorates the Irish natural scientist Joseph Barclay Pentland (1797–1873) by Nicholas Aylward Vigors in 1837.
f: This species is native to the Andes Mountains in South America.

The white-throated tinamou (Tinamus guttatus) is a species of bird native to the Amazon rainforest of Brazil, northern Bolivia, southeastern Colombia, northeastern Ecuador, eastern Peru and southern Venezuela.

t: The great tinamou (Tinamus major) is a species of tinamou ground bird native to Central and South America.
f: There are several subspecies, mostly differentiated by their coloration.

t: The solitary tinamou (Tinamus solitarius) is a species of paleognath ground bird.
f: This species is native to Atlantic forest of eastern Brazil.

t: Four subspecies are recognised.
f: The grey tinamou (Tinamus tao) is a type of ground bird native to South America.

t: The black-tailed tityra (Tityra cayana) is a medium-sized passerine bird of tropical South America. The tityras have been placed in the cotinga or the tyrant flycatcher families (Cotingidae and Tyrannidae) by various authors.
f: But the weight of evidence strongly suggest they and their closest relatives are better separated as Tityridae; the AOU for example advocates this separation.

t: The black-crowned tityra (Tityra inquisitor) is a medium-sized passerine bird.
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country except El Salvador, and every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The masked tityra (Tityra semifasciata) is a medium-sized passerine bird.
f: It is found in Mexico, every Central American country, and every northern and central mainland South American country except the Guianas.

t: Von der Decken's hornbill (Tockus deckeni) is a hornbill found in East Africa, especially to the east of the East African Rift, from Ethiopia south to Tanzania. It is found mainly in thorn scrub and similar arid habitats.
f: It was named after the German explorer Baron Karl Klaus von der Decken (1833–1865).

t: The northern red-billed hornbill (Tockus erythrorhynchus) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. There are five species of red-billed hornbills recognized, but all five were once considered conspecific and some authorities still classify the others as subspecies of Tockus erythrorhynchus.
f: It is found from southern Mauritania through Somalia and northeast Tanzania.

t: The western red-billed hornbill (Tockus kempi) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae. It is found from Senegal and Gambia to southern Mauritania and western Mali.
f: There are five species of red-billed hornbills generally recognized now, but all five were once considered conspecific.

t: The southern yellow-billed hornbill (Tockus leucomelas) is a hornbill found in southern Africa. Yellow-billed hornbills feed mainly on the ground, where they forage for seeds, small insects, spiders and scorpions.
f: They can often be seen along roads and water courses.

t: The southern red-billed hornbill (Tockus rufirostris) is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae, which is native to the savannas and dryer bushlands of southern Africa. All five red-billed hornbills were formerly considered conspecific.
f: It is replaced by a near-relative, the Damara red-billed hornbill, in the arid woodlands of western Namibia.

t: The cinnamon-banded kingfisher (Todiramphus australasia) is a species of bird in the family Alcedinidae. It is found in Indonesia and East Timor.
f: It is endemic to the Lesser Sundas.

t: The collared kingfisher (Todiramphus chloris) is a medium-sized kingfisher belonging to the subfamily Halcyoninae, the tree kingfishers. It is also known as the white-collared kingfisher, black-masked kingfisher or mangrove kingfisher.
f: It has a wide range extending from the Red Sea across southern Asia to Melanesia.

t: The sombre kingfisher (Todiramphus funebris) is a species of bird in the family Alcedinidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical mangrove forest, subtropical or tropical swamps, and plantations.
f: It is endemic to island of Halmahera, in North Maluku, Indonesia.

t: The forest kingfisher (Todiramphus macleayii), also known as Macleay's or the blue kingfisher, is a species of kingfisher in the subfamily Halcyoninae, also known as tree kingfishers. It is a predominantly a blue and white bird.
f: Like many other kingfishers, it hunts invertebrates, small frogs, and lizards.

t: The Pacific kingfisher (Todiramphus sacer) is a medium-sized kingfisher belonging to the subfamily Halcyoninae, the tree kingfishers. It was previously considered a subspecies of the collared kingfisher.
f: It has a wide range throughout the South Pacific islands, including American Samoa, Fiji, Tonga, the Solomon Islands and Vanuatu.

The sacred kingfisher (Todiramphus sanctus) is a medium-sized woodland kingfisher that inhabits mangroves, woodlands, forests and river valleys in Australia, New Zealand and other parts of the western Pacific.

t: The Torresian kingfisher (Todiramphus sordidus) is a species of bird in the family Alcedinidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, mangroves, and plantations.
f: It is found in southern New Guinea and in Australia.

t: The Melanesian kingfisher (Todiramphus tristrami) is a species of bird in the family Alcedinidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and plantations.
f: It is endemic to the Bismarck Archipelago and the northwest and central Solomon Islands.

t: The rufous-lored kingfisher (Todiramphus winchelli), also known as Winchell's kingfisher, is a species of bird in the kingfisher family Alcedinidae. It is threatened by deforestation, and the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) has assessed it as a vulnerable species.
f: It is endemic to the Philippines, its natural habitat consists of tropical moist lowland forests.

t: The yellow-browed tody-flycatcher (Todirostrum chrysocrotaphum) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The common tody-flycatcher (Todirostrum cinereum) is a small passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Mexico, in every Central American country, and in every mainland South American country except Chile and Uruguay.

t: The spotted tody-flycatcher (Todirostrum maculatum) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found on Trinidad and in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The black-headed tody-flycatcher (Todirostrum nigriceps) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, and Venezuela.
f: Its reproductive traits are not well documented but both parents contribute to building the nest and clutches only have one egg at a time.

t: The painted tody-flycatcher (Todirostrum pictum) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, Venezuela, and possibly Colombia.
The yellow-lored tody-flycatcher, or gray-headed tody-flycatcher, (Todirostrum poliocephalum) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.

t: The narrow-billed tody (Todus angustirostris) is a species of bird in the family Todidae.
f: It is one of two Todus species endemic to Hispaniola, a Caribbean island shared by the Dominican Republic and Haiti.

t: The Puerto Rican tody (Todus mexicanus), locally known in Spanish as San Pedrito ("little Saint Peter"), is a bird endemic to the main island of Puerto Rico. However, the proposal did not advance, largely due to the scientific name of the bird which erroneously identifies it as a native of Mexico.
f: In 2022, the tody was approved as the official national bird of Puerto Rico by the legislative assembly.
The Cuban tody (Todus multicolor) is a bird species in the family Todidae that is restricted to Cuba and the adjacent islands.

t: The broad-billed tody (Todus subulatus) is a species of bird in the family Todidae, and one of two Todus species found on Hispaniola, along with the narrow-billed tody. They are small insectivorous birds, characterized by their bright green feathers, pink flanks and red throats.
f: The nestlings take three weeks to mature into juveniles and then fly off to establish their own territory.

t: The Jamaican tody (Todus todus) is a species of bird in the genus Todus endemic to Jamaica.
f: Local names for the Jamaican tody include rasta bird, robin and robin redbreast.

t: The yellow-margined flatbill or Zimmer's flatbill (Tolmomyias assimilis) is a species of bird in the tyrant flycatcher family Tyrannidae.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The ochre-lored flatbill (Tolmomyias flaviventris) or yellow-breasted flycatcher, is a passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, and Venezuela.

t: The grey-crowned flatbill or grey-crowned flycatcher (Tolmomyias poliocephalus) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The yellow-olive flatbill or yellow-olive flycatcher (Tolmomyias sulphurescens) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Mexico, in every Central American country, on Trinidad, and in every mainland South American country except Chile.

t: The orange-eyed flatbill or orange-eyed flycatcher (Tolmomyias traylori) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The crimson topaz (Topaza pella) is a species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The fiery topaz (Topaza pyra) is a species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae.
f: It has brilliant iridescent plumage and resides in northern South America, where it consumes nectar and insects.

t: The Zapata sparrow (Torreornis inexpectata) is a medium-sized grey and yellow bird that lives in the grasslands of the Zapata Swamp and elsewhere on the island of Cuba.
f: Measuring about 16.5 centimetres (6.5 in) in length, it is grey and yellow overall with a dark reddish-brown crown and olive-grey upperparts.

t: The lilac-tailed parrotlet (Touit batavicus) is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, Trinidad, and Venezuela.

t: The blue-fronted parrotlet (Touit dilectissimus) is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, and Venezuela.

t: The scarlet-shouldered parrotlet (Touit huetii), also known as the red-winged parrotlet or Huet's parrotlet, is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, and Venezuela, possibly in Suriname, and as a vagrant to Trinidad and Tobago.

t: The brown-backed parrotlet (Touit melanonotus) also known as the black-backed parrotlet, the black-eared parrotlet, and Wied's parrotlet, is a small (15 cm or 6 in) green parrot found in south-eastern Brazil from Bahia to southern São Paulo. They frequent humid forest from 500–1,000 m (1,600–3,300 ft) (occasionally down to sea level), and are mostly found in small flocks of 3–20 birds.
f: It has a dark brown mantle and back, brown ear coverts, and red outer tail with back tips.

t: The sapphire-rumped parrotlet (Touit purpuratus) is a species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The spot-winged parrotlet (Touit stictopterus) is a Near Threatened species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The golden-tailed parrotlet (Touit surdus) is a Vulnerable species of bird in subfamily Arinae of the family Psittacidae, the African and New World parrots.
f: It is endemic to eastern Brazil.

t: The yellow-bellied longbill or green-crowned longbill (Toxorhamphus novaeguineae) is a species of bird in the family Melanocharitidae.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

t: Bendire's thrasher (Toxostoma bendirei) is a medium-sized species of thrasher native to the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. Coloration is grayish-brown on its upperparts with paler, faintly dark streaked underparts.
f: It is 23–28 centimetres (9.1–11.0 in) long, with a long tail and a medium-sized bill.

t: The gray thrasher (Toxostoma cinereum) is a medium-sized passerine bird belonging to the family Mimidae.
f: It is endemic to the Baja California peninsula of Mexico.
The crissal thrasher (Toxostoma crissale) is a large thrasher found in the Southwestern United States  to central Mexico.

t: The curve-billed thrasher (Toxostoma curvirostre) is a medium-sized mimid native to most of Mexico and to the deserts of southwestern United States. Several subspecies have been classified since 1827, though there is no consensus on the number.
f: It is a non-migratory species, and throughout most of its range it is the most common desert thrasher.

t: LeConte's thrasher (Toxostoma lecontei) is a pale bird found in the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. It prefers to live in deserts with very little vegetation, where it blends in with the sandy soils.
f: These birds are terrestrial and only fly occasionally.

t: The long-billed thrasher (Toxostoma longirostre) is a medium-sized resident songbird of South Texas and eastern Mexico. The bird is a large sized mimid that is not especially wary, but it will take precautionary measures to prevent itself from being potential prey.
f: Like other thrashers, it is named after its sweeping methods when searching for food, not for thrashing predators, although they are aggressive defenders of their territories.
The ocellated thrasher (Toxostoma ocellatum) is a species of bird in the family Mimidae.

t: The California thrasher (Toxostoma redivivum) is a large member of family Mimidae found primarily in chaparral habitat in California in the United States and Baja California in Mexico.
f: It is the only species of the genus Toxostoma throughout most of its range.

t: The brown thrasher (Toxostoma rufum), sometimes erroneously called the brown thrush or fox-coloured thrush, is a bird in the family Mimidae, which also includes the New World catbirds and mockingbirds. The brown thrasher is abundant throughout the eastern and central United States and southern and central Canada, and it is the only thrasher to live primarily east of the Rockies and central Texas.
f: The brown thrasher is noted for having over 1,000 song types, and the largest song repertoire of birds.

t: D'Arnaud's barbet (Trachyphonus darnaudii) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae that is found in East Africa. Barbets and toucans are a group of birds with a worldwide tropical distribution.
f: The barbets get their name from the bristles which fringe their heavy bills.

t: The red-and-yellow barbet (Trachyphonus erythrocephalus) is a species of African barbet found in eastern Africa. Males have distinctive black (spotted white), red, and yellow plumage; females and juveniles are similar, but less brightly colored.
f: Omnivorous, the species feeds on seeds, fruit, and invertebrates.

t: The eastern yellow-billed barbet (Trachylaemus purpuratus) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family. It was formerly considered to be conspecific with the western yellow-billed barbet.
f: It is found in Angola, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Nigeria, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi and western Kenya.

t: The crested barbet (Trachyphonus vaillantii) ('trachys'=rough, 'phone'=voice, sound') is a sub-Saharan bird in the Lybiidae family.
f: Its specific name commemorates François Levaillant, a famed French naturalist.

t: The pale-yellow robin (Eopsaltria capito) is a species of passerine bird in the family Petroicidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is endemic to eastern Australia.

t: The grey-fronted green pigeon (Treron affinis) is a pigeon in the genus Treron. Many authorities have split the species from the pompadour green pigeon complex.
f: It is found in the forests of the Western Ghats in India.

t: The orange-breasted green pigeon (Treron bicinctus) is a pigeon found across tropical Asia south of the Himalaya across parts of the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. They may be found in pairs or in small flocks, foraging quietly and moving slowly on trees.
f: Like other green pigeons, it feeds mainly on small fruit.

t: The African green pigeon (Treron calvus) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae, and one of 5 green pigeon species in the Afrotropics.
f: The species has a wide range in Sub-Saharan Africa with around 17 accepted races.
The thick-billed green pigeon (Treron curvirostra) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.

t: The Taiwan green pigeon or whistling green pigeon (Treron formosae) is a bird in the family Columbidae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1863.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The cinnamon-headed green pigeon (Treron fulvicollis) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical mangrove forests, subtropical or tropical swamps, subtropical or tropical moist shrubland, and rural gardens.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The little green pigeon (Treron olax) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
f: It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.

t: The ashy-headed green pigeon (Treron phayrei) is a pigeon in the genus Treron. Many authorities split the species from the pompadour green pigeon complex.
f: It is found from Nepal, northeast India, and Bangladesh to southwest China, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, and Vietnam.

t: The yellow-footed green pigeon (Treron phoenicopterus), also known as yellow-legged green pigeon, is a common species of green pigeon found in the Indian subcontinent and parts of Southeast Asia. Their population is currently increasing.
f: It is the state bird of Maharashtra.

t: The white-bellied green pigeon (Treron sieboldii), also known as Siebold's green pigeon and Japanese green pigeon, is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. It is found in East, and Southeast Asia.
f: It is one of the few green pigeons that migrates.
The wedge-tailed green pigeon or Kokla green pigeon (Treron sphenurus) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.

t: The pink-necked green pigeon (Treron vernans) is a species of bird of the pigeon and dove family, Columbidae. It is a common species of Southeast Asia, found from Thailand, and Vietnam south through to the major islands of Indonesia and the Philippines (where it is called "punay").
f: The species has adapted well to human changes to the environment, and can be found in crowded cities as long as fruiting trees are present.

t: The Tasmanian nativehen (Tribonyx mortierii) , also known by its palawa kani name piyura, is a flightless rail and one of twelve species of birds endemic to Australia's island state of Tasmania. Its success may also be attributed to the recent extinction of its main predator, the thylacine.
f: Although many flightless birds have a history of extinction at the hands of humans, the species has actually benefited from the introduction of European-style agricultural practices in Tasmania.
The black-tailed nativehen (Tribonyx ventralis) is a rail native to Australia.

t: The scaly-breasted lorikeet (Trichoglossus chlorolepidotus) is an Australian lorikeet found in woodland in eastern Australia.
f: The common name aptly describes this bird, which has yellow breast feathers broadly edged with green that look like scales.

t: The coconut lorikeet (Trichoglossus haematodus), also known as the green-naped lorikeet and Swainson’s lorikeet, is a parrot in the family Psittaculidae. Several species of lorikeets now recognised as distinct were once lumped together under Trichoglossus haematodus; together they form the "rainbow lorikeet" species complex.
f: Trichoglossus haematodus as circumscribed today is largely restricted to Melanesia (except Fiji) and a few nearby regions.

t: The rainbow lorikeet (Trichoglossus moluccanus) is a species of parrot found in Australia. Its habitat is rainforest, coastal bush, and woodland areas.
f: It is common along the eastern seaboard, from northern Queensland to South Australia.

t: The red-collared lorikeet (Trichoglossus rubritorquis) is a species of parrot found in wooded habitats in northern Australia . It was previously considered a subspecies of the rainbow lorikeet, but today most major authorities consider them as separate species.
f: Every year at the end of the dry season in Darwin, many of them display symptoms of apparent drunkenness.

t: The red-fronted barbet (Tricholaema diademata) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family.
f: It is found in Ethiopia, Kenya, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: The hairy-breasted barbet (Tricholaema hirsuta) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae.
f: It is found throughout the African tropical rainforest.

t: The spot-flanked barbet (Tricholaema lacrymosa) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae.
f: It is found in Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia.
The acacia pied barbet or pied barbet (Tricholaema leucomelas) is a species of bird in the family Lybiidae which is native to southern Africa.

t: The black-throated barbet (Tricholaema melanocephala) is a species of bird in the Lybiidae family. Its distribution has moved northward.
f: It is found in Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, and Uganda.

t: The hairy-backed bulbul (Tricholestes criniger) is a songbird species in the bulbul family, Pycnonotidae. It is the sole species contained within the monotypic genus Tricholestes.
f: It is found on the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, and Borneo.

t: The black-goggled tanager (Trichothraupis melanops) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, the tanagers and allies.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

t: The blue-bellied parrot or purple-bellied parrot (Triclaria malachitacea) is the only species in its genus. It is generally considered endemic to the humid Atlantic Forest of southeastern Brazil, but there are two unconfirmed records from Misiones in Argentina.
f: Only the male has the bluish-purple patch on the belly for which this species is named.

t: The grey-tailed tattler (Tringa brevipes), also known as the Siberian tattler or Polynesian tattler, is a small shorebird in the genus Tringa. The English name for the tattlers refers to their noisy call.
f: After breeding, they migrate to an area from southeast Asia to Australia.

t: The spotted redshank (Tringa erythropus) is a wader (shorebird) in the large bird family Scolopacidae. It is an occasional vagrant to Australia and North America.
f: It breeds across northern Scandinavia and the northern Palearctic and migrates south to the Mediterranean, the southern British Isles, France, tropical Africa, and tropical Asia for the winter.

t: The lesser yellowlegs (Tringa flavipes) is a medium-sized shorebird.
f: It breeds in the boreal forest region of North America, and winters from the south of North America, to the far south of South America.

t: The wood sandpiper (Tringa glareola) is a small wader belonging to the sandpiper family Scolopacidae.
f: A Eurasian species, it is the smallest of the shanks, a genus of mid-sized, long-legged waders that largely inhabit freshwater and wetland environments, as opposed to the maritime or coastal habitats of other, similar species.

t: Nordmann's greenshank (Tringa guttifer) or the spotted greenshank is a wader in the large family Scolopacidae, the typical waders.
f: They are considered endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List and are typically found within the East Asian-Australasian Flyway.

t: The wandering tattler (Tringa incana) is a medium-sized shorebird, similar in appearance to the closely related gray-tailed tattler (T. brevipes).
f: The tattlers are unique among the species of Tringa for having unpatterned, greyish wings and backs, and a scaly breast pattern extending more or less onto the belly in breeding plumage, in which both also have a rather prominent supercilium.

t: The greater yellowlegs (Tringa melanoleuca) is a large shorebird in the family Scolopacidae.
f: It breeds in central Canada and southern Alaska and winters in southern North America, Central America, the West Indies and South America.

t: The common greenshank (Tringa nebularia) is a wader in the large family Scolopacidae, the typical waders. The genus name Tringa is the Neo-Latin name given to the green sandpiper by Aldrovandus in 1599 based on Ancient Greek trungas, a thrush-sized, white-rumped, tail-bobbing wading bird mentioned by Aristotle.
f: The specific nebularia is from Latin nebula "mist".

t: The green sandpiper (Tringa ochropus) is a small wader (shorebird) of the Old World. The green sandpiper represents an ancient lineage of the genus Tringa; its only close living relative is the solitary sandpiper (T. solitaria).
f: In addition, both species nest in trees, unlike most other scolopacids.

t: The willet (Tringa semipalmata) is a large shorebird in the family Scolopacidae. Its closest relative is the lesser yellowlegs, a much smaller bird with a very different appearance apart from the fine, clear, and dense pattern of the neck, which both species show in breeding plumage.
f: It is a relatively large and robust sandpiper and is the largest of the species called "shanks" in the genus Tringa.

t: The solitary sandpiper (Tringa solitaria) is a small shorebird. The genus name Tringa is the Neo-Latin name given to the green sandpiper by Aldrovandus in 1599 based on Ancient Greek trungas, a thrush-sized, white-rumped, tail-bobbing wading bird mentioned by Aristotle.
f: The specific solitaria is Latin for "solitary" from solus, "alone".

t: The marsh sandpiper (Tringa stagnatilis) is a small wader. It is a rather small shank, and breeds in open grassy steppe and taiga wetlands from easternmost Europe to the Russian Far East.
f: The specific stagnatilis is from Latin stagnum, "swamp".
The common redshank or simply redshank (Tringa totanus) is a Eurasian wader in the large family Scolopacidae.

t: The black-faced laughingthrush (Trochalopteron affine) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in the Eastern Himalayas.
f: Small disjunct populations also exist in continental Southeast Asia.

t: The Assam laughingthrush (Trochalopteron chrysopterum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in Northeast India and adjacent southwest China and Myanmar.
f: The species was formerly regarded as a subspecies of the chestnut-crowned laughingthrush, T. erythrocephalum.

t: Elliot's laughingthrush (Trochalopteron elliotii) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae.
f: It is found in central China and far northeastern India, in shrubs and in forests with a combination of coniferous and deciduous trees.

t: The chestnut-crowned laughingthrush (Trochalopteron erythrocephalum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in Bhutan, China, India, Pakistan and Nepal.
f: The silver-eared laughingthrush, formerly included as a subspecies, is now usually regarded as a separate species.

t: The brown-cheeked laughingthrush (Trochalopteron henrici) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in south-western China and north-eastern India.
f: The specific name of this bird commemorates Prince Henri of Orléans.

t: The Bhutan laughingthrush (Trochalopteron imbricatum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It was formerly considered a subspecies of the streaked laughingthrush, G. lineatus, hence its alternate common name of Himalayan streaked laughingthrush.
f: It is commonly found in Bhutan and some adjoining areas in India.

t: The streaked laughingthrush (Trochalopteron lineatum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. Its range extends from the Turkestan Range to the Safed Koh and east through the Himalayas towards Sikkim.
f: The subspecies imbricatum is usually considered a separates species, Bhutan laughingthrush.

t: The silver-eared laughingthrush (Trochalopteron melanostigma) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in southern Yunnan, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam.
f: It was formerly considered a subspecies of the chestnut-crowned laughingthrush, G. erythrocephalus.

t: The red-tailed laughingthrush (Trochalopteron milnei) is a species of bird in the laughingthrush family Leiothrichidae.
f: It is found in the montane forests of Myanmar, Laos, southern China and central Vietnam.

t: The white-whiskered laughingthrush or Formosan laughing thrush (Trochalopteron morrisonianum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.
f: It is endemic to montane forests of the island of Taiwan.

t: The Malayan laughingthrush (Trochalopteron peninsulae) is a species of laughingthrush that was for some time included as a subspecies of the Trochalopteron erythrocephalum.
f: This species is found in the extreme south of Thailand and in peninsular Malaysia.

t: The blue-winged laughingthrush (Trochalopteron squamatum) is a bird in the family Leiothrichidae.
f: It is found in Eastern Himalaya, Yunnan, Myanmar and Laos where its natural habitat is the dense undergrowth of subtropical or tropical moist broadleaved evergreen montane forests.

t: The scaly laughingthrush (Trochalopteron subunicolor) is a bird species in the family Leiothrichidae. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.
f: It is found in Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal, and Vietnam.

t: The variegated laughingthrush (Trochalopteron variegatum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It ranges across Bhutan, India, Nepal and Tibet.
f: It is endemic to the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent, primarily the low-to-mid altitudes of the Himalayas.

t: The striped laughingthrush (Trochalopteron virgatum) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.
f: It is found in the Patkai range, where its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

t: The blue-mantled crested flycatcher or African crested flycatcher (Trochocercus cyanomelas) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae found in eastern and south-eastern Africa.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
The blue-headed crested flycatcher (Trochocercus nitens) is a species of bird in the family Monarchidae, native to the African tropical forest.

t: The northern house wren (Troglodytes aedon) is a very small passerine in the wren family Troglodytidae. It is found in southern Canada, the USA and Mexico.
f: The name troglodytes means "hole dweller", and is a reference to the bird's tendency to disappear into crevices when hunting insects or to seek shelter.

t: The winter wren (Troglodytes hiemalis) is a very small North American bird and a member of the mainly New World wren family Troglodytidae. It breeds in coniferous forests from British Columbia to the Atlantic Ocean.
f: It migrates through and winters across southeastern Canada, the eastern half the United States and (rarely) north-eastern Mexico.

t: The ochraceous wren (Troglodytes ochraceus) is a small songbird of the wren family.
f: It is a resident breeding species in Costa Rica, Panama, and Colombia.

t: The Pacific wren (Troglodytes pacificus) is a very small North American bird and a member of the mainly New World wren family Troglodytidae. It breeds along the Pacific coast from Alaska to California and inland as far as Wyoming and the Black Hills of South Dakota.
f: The scientific name is taken from the Greek word troglodytes (from trogle a hole, and dyein to creep), meaning 'cave-dweller', and refers to its habit of disappearing into cavities or crevices whilst hunting arthropods or to roost.

t: The rufous-browed wren (Troglodytes rufociliatus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Central America from Mexico south into Nicaragua.

t: The mountain wren (Troglodytes solstitialis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in the Andes of northwestern Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and western Venezuela.

t: The Eurasian wren (Troglodytes troglodytes) is a very small insectivorous bird and the only member of the wren family found in the Old World, specifically in Eurasia and Africa (Maghreb). In Anglophone Europe, it is commonly known simply as the wren.
f: It is also highly polygynous, an unusual mating system for passerines.

t: Baird's trogon (Trogon bairdii) is a bird species belonging to the family Trogonidae, which includes quetzals and trogons. It is native to Costa Rica and Panama.
f: The species is named in honor of Spencer Fullerton Baird, a renowned naturalist of the 19th century who served as the first curator of the Smithsonian Institution.

t: The gartered violaceous trogon (Trogon caligatus), also known as the northern violaceous trogon, is a bird in the family Trogonidae, the quetzals and trogons.
f: It is found in Mexico, all of Central America, and Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The white-tailed trogon (Trogon chionurus) is a species of bird in the trogon family. It was formerly considered a subspecies of T. viridis, which is widespread in South America east of the Andes, but under the English name white-tailed trogon .
f: It is found in tropical humid forests of the Chocó, ranging from Panama, through western Colombia, to western Ecuador.

t: The citreoline trogon (Trogon citreolus) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae. It is endemic to western Mexico, with an estimated distribution size of 539,000 km2 Due to this very large range, the IUCN consider it a species of Least Concern and that the current population trend is stable.
f: T. citreolus has also been studied as an Ecosystem engineer.

t: The lattice-tailed trogon (Trogon clathratus) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae, the quetzals and trogons.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The collared trogon (Trogon collaris) is a species of bird in family Trogonidae, the quetzals and trogons.
f: It is found in Mexico, throughout Central America, and in northern South America.

t: The Chocó trogon (Trogon comptus), also known as the white-eyed trogon or blue-tailed trogon, is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae, the quetzals and trogons.
f: It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The blue-crowned trogon (Trogon curucui) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae, the quetzals and trogons. It is found in Brazil, Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, and Peru.
f: As with all trogons, this species is sexually dimorphic.
The elegant trogon (Trogon elegans), formerly considered as conspecific with the coppery-tailed trogon, is a species of bird in the trogon family Trogonidae that is native to Central America.

t: The slaty-tailed trogon (Trogon massena) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae, the quetzals and trogons.
f: It is found in Mexico, throughout Central America, and in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The black-headed trogon (Trogon melanocephalus) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae.
f: It is found in Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

t: The black-tailed trogon (Trogon melanurus) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae, the quetzals and trogons.
f: It is found Panama and northern South America.

t: The Ecuadorian trogon (Trogon mesurus) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae, the quetzals and trogons.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The mountain trogon (Trogon mexicanus), also known as the Mexican trogon, is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae. First described by William Swainson in 1827, it is resident in Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico and has occurred in El Salvador as a vagrant.
f: Unlike some rarer trogons, this species shows some adaptability to human land use and has utilized coffee plantations with suitable shade trees like oaks.

t: The masked trogon (Trogon personatus) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae.
f: It is fairly common in humid highland forests in South America, mainly the Andes and tepuis, and is resident in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru and Venezuela.

t: The Amazonian trogon (Trogon ramonianus), is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae, the trogons and quetzals.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The Amazonian black-throated trogon (Trogon rufus) is a bird in the family Trogonidae, the trogons and quetzals. It is found in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
f: Although it has also been called "yellow-bellied trogon" it is not the only trogon with a yellow belly .

t: The Surucua trogon (Trogon surrucura) is a species of bird in the family Trogonidae, the quetzals and trogons.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The Guianan trogon (Trogon violaceus) is a species of bird in the trogon and quetzal family Trogonidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, Trinidad, and Venezuela.

t: The green-backed trogon (Trogon viridis), also known as the Amazonian white-tailed trogon, is a bird in the trogon family Trogonidae. It is widely distributed across the Amazon rainforest with a disjunct population on the southeast coast of Brazil.
f: As with all trogons, this species is sexually dimorphic.

t: The green-legged partridge (Tropicoperdix chloropus), also known as the scaly-breasted partridge or green-legged hill-partridge, is a bird species in the family Phasianidae. The Vietnam partridge is now usually considered a subspecies.
f: It is found in forest in Indochina, ranging slightly into southernmost China (Yunnan).
The Tumbes tyrant (Ochthoeca salvini) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.

t: The ochre-crowned greenlet (Tunchiornis ochraceiceps) is a species of bird in the family Vireonidae, the vireos, greenlets, and shrike-babblers. This species was formerly known as the tawny-crowned greenlet and was considered to be conspecific with the Para greenlet, Guianan greenlet and rufous-fronted greenlet.
f: It is found in Mexico, in every Central American country except El Salvador, and in Colombia and Ecuador.

t: The black-throated wren-babbler (Turdinus atrigularis) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is endemic to the island of Borneo (mainly southern Brunei and East Malaysia).

t: The large wren-babbler (Turdinus macrodactylus) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. It is found in the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra and Java.
f: It is threatened by habitat loss.

t: The marbled wren-babbler (Turdinus marmoratus) is a species of bird in the family Pellorneidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
f: It is found in the Malay Peninsula and the Barisan Mountains of Sumatra.

t: Hartlaub's babbler (Turdoides hartlaubii) or the Angola babbler, is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae, which is native to south central Africa.
f: The common name and Latin binomial commemorate the German physician and ornithologist Gustav Hartlaub.

t: The arrow-marked babbler (Turdoides jardineii) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.
f: It is native to woodlands in the southern Afrotropics.

t: The white-rumped babbler (Turdoides leucopygia) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae.
f: It is found in Eritrea, Ethiopia, Somalia and South Sudan.

t: The brown babbler (Turdoides plebejus) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. The species is common across its range.
f: It is predominantly found in West Africa, but ranging from the Gambia to Kenya.

t: The blackcap babbler (Turdoides reinwardtii) is a member of the family Leiothrichidae. The blackcap babbler is a common resident breeding bird in west Africa from Senegal to Cameroon.
f: This species, like most babblers, is not migratory, and has short rounded wings and a weak flight.

t: The black-lored babbler or Sharpe's pied-babbler (Turdoides sharpei) is a species of bird in the family Leiothrichidae. It is found in southwestern Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Burundi, Rwanda, and the part of the Democratic Republic of the Congo immediately adjacent to the three last-named countries.
f: In Kenya, single birds give repeated single or double harsh notes such as waaach or a muffled kurr-ack; pairs or groups give longer phrases in chorus.

t: The Abyssinian thrush (Turdus abyssinicus) is a passerine bird in the family Turdidae. It is also known as the African mountain thrush, or northern olive thrush The species was formerly treated as conspecific with the olive thrush (Turdus olivaceus) but the species were split based on the genetic differences.
f: The Abyssinian thrush is native to the eastern Afromontane.

t: The white-necked thrush (Turdus albicollis) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It is found on Trinidad and Tobago and in every mainland South American country except Chile.
f: It previously was called the white-necked robin.

t: The white-collared blackbird (Turdus albocinctus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It can be found throughout the Indian subcontinent, ranging across Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal and Pakistan.
f: Field studies indicated that females, but not males, exhibit different nest defence behaviours that can be used to classify them into bold and shy personalities.

t: The creamy-bellied thrush (Turdus amaurochalinus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, and as a vagrant to Chile and the Falkland Islands.

t: The white-throated thrush (Turdus assimilis) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It is found in Mexico and Central America.
f: It also has strayed to the southwestern United States.

t: The black-throated thrush (Turdus atrogularis) is a passerine bird in the thrush family. It is sometimes regarded as one subspecies of a polytypic species, "dark-throated thrush", red-throated thrush then being the other subspecies.
f: The black-throated thrush is a migratory Eastern Palearctic species.

t: The white-chinned thrush, known in Jamaica as the hopping dick (Turdus aurantius) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is endemic to Jamaica where it is common and widespread.

t: The grey-winged blackbird (Turdus boulboul) is a species of Turdus in the thrush family, found at in the mountains of southern and eastern Asia from the Himalayas to northern Vietnam. Its natural habitat is in the middle altitudes of subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, mostly at 1,800–2,700 m (5,900–8,900 ft) altitude, but occasionally down to 1,200 m (3,900 ft) in winter, and as high as 3,300 m (10,800 ft) in summer.
f: The females are a plain brown, with only a hint of paler brown on the wings where the males have their grey patch.

t: The Japanese thrush (Turdus cardis) is a species of bird in the thrush family Turdidae. The species is also known as the grey thrush or the Japanese grey thrush.
f: The Japanese thrush is migratory.
The Izu thrush or Izu Islands thrush (Turdus celaenops) is a bird of the thrush family native to Japan.

t: The Chiguanco thrush (Turdus chiguanco) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found from Ecuador south to Argentina.
