t: The brown-headed thrush (Turdus chrysolaus), sometimes known as the brown thrush, is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. Its natural habitat is temperate forests.
f: It breeds in Sakhalin, the Kuril Islands and Japan; it winters in south toward the Ryukyu Islands, Taiwan, Hainan and the northern Philippines.

t: The black-breasted thrush (Turdus dissimilis) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It is found from north-eastern India to northern Vietnam.
f: Thus, the bird's common name refers to the colour of the male bird's breast.

t: The dusky thrush (Turdus eunomus) is a member of the thrush family which breeds eastwards from central Siberia to Kamchatka wintering in Korea, Japan, South China and Myanmar. It is closely related to the more southerly breeding Naumann's thrush T. naumanni; the two have often been regarded as conspecific.
f: The scientific name comes from Latin Turdus, "thrush" and Ancient Greek eunomos, "orderly".

t: The austral thrush (Turdus falcklandii) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Chile, and the Falkland Islands.
The grey-sided thrush (Turdus feae) is a species of bird in the thrush family, Turdidae.

t: The yellow-legged thrush (Turdus flavipes) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It formerly occurred in Paraguay and has been recorded as a vagrant in Uruguay.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Guyana, Trinidad and Tobago, and Venezuela.

t: The chestnut-bellied thrush (Turdus fulviventris) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The cocoa thrush (Turdus fumigatus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: Vincent, Grenada, and Trinidad and in Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The great thrush (Turdus fuscater) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
f: It is considered as the largest thrush in South America.

t: The clay-colored thrush (Turdus grayi) is a common Middle American bird of the thrush family (Turdidae). Other common names include clay-colored robin.
f: It is the national bird of Costa Rica, where it is well known as the yigüirro (Spanish: [ʝi'ɣwiro]).

t: Hauxwell's thrush (Turdus hauxwelli) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and possibly Venezuela.

t: The grey-backed thrush (Turdus hortulorum) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It breeds in northeastern China, the Russian Far East and North Korea, and winters mainly in southern China and northern Vietnam.
f: The species inhabits temperate forests and wooded habitats and is migratory.

t: The black-billed thrush (Turdus ignobilis) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.
The redwing (Turdus iliacus) is a bird in the thrush family, Turdidae, native to Europe and the Palearctic, slightly smaller than the related song thrush.

t: The black thrush (Turdus infuscatus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies. It was formerly known as the black robin.
f: It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.

t: Lawrence's thrush (Turdus lawrencii) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The pale-breasted thrush (Turdus leucomelas) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in every mainland South American country except Chile and Ecuador.

t: The pale-eyed thrush (Turdus leucops) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The Kurrichane thrush (Turdus libonyana) is a species of bird in the thrush family Turdidae. Its natural habitat is dry savanna and woodland, predominantly miombo woodland.
f: The species is found from central through to southern Africa.

t: The Ecuadorian thrush (Turdus maculirostris) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The Chinese blackbird (Turdus mandarinus) is a member of the thrush family Turdidae.
f: It was formerly considered conspecific with the related common blackbird (T. merula).

t: The Maranon thrush (Turdus maranonicus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The Yemen thrush (Turdus menachensis) is a species of bird in the thrush family Turdidae.
f: It is native to the Sarawat Mountains of the western Arabian Peninsula.

t: The common blackbird (Turdus merula) is a species of true thrush. It is also known as the Eurasian blackbird , or simply the blackbird.
f: Both sexes are territorial on the breeding grounds and have distinctive threat displays.

t: The American robin (Turdus migratorius) is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family. It is named after the European robin because of its reddish-orange breast, though the two species are not closely related, with the European robin belonging to the Old World flycatcher family.
f: According to the Partners in Flight database (2019), the American robin is the most abundant landbird in North America (with 370 million individuals), ahead of red-winged blackbirds, introduced European starlings, mourning doves and house finches.

t: Naumann's thrush (Turdus naumanni) is a species of the thrush family Turdidae which breeds eastwards from central Siberia to North Manchuria, Amurland and Sakhalin. It is closely related to the more northerly breeding dusky thrush T. eunomus; the two have often been regarded as conspecific.
f: The song of Naumann's thrush may differ from the simple fluted or whistling redwing-like song of dusky thrush.

t: The sooty thrush (Turdus nigrescens) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies. It was formerly known as the sooty robin.
f: It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

t: The Andean slaty thrush (Turdus nigriceps) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Ecuador and Peru.

t: The spectacled thrush, bare-eyed thrush, or yellow-eyed thrush (Turdus nudigenis), is a resident breeding bird in the Lesser Antilles and in South America from Colombia and Venezuela south and east to northern Brazil. In Trinidad and Tobago, this thrush is also known as big-eye grieve.
f: It has a narrower eyering and is only found in forest and woodland in western Ecuador and northwestern Peru.

t: The eyebrowed thrush (Turdus obscurus) is a member of the thrush family Turdidae. It breeds in dense coniferous forest and taiga eastwards from Siberia and Mongolia to Japan.
f: It is strongly migratory, wintering south to China and Southeast Asia.

t: The pale-vented thrush (Turdus obsoletus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, and heavily degraded former forest.
f: It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, and Peru.

t: The olive thrush (Turdus olivaceus) is, in its range, one of the most common members of the thrush family (Turdidae). It occurs in African highlands from the montane regions in Eastern and Central Africa in the north to the Cape of Good Hope in the south.
f: It is a bird of forest and woodland, but has locally adapted to parks and large gardens in suburban areas.

t: The black-hooded thrush (Turdus olivater) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The pale thrush (Turdus pallidus) is a passerine bird of the eastern Palearctic belonging to the genus Turdus in the thrush family Turdidae.
f: It is closely related to the eye-browed thrush and grey-backed thrush.

t: The African thrush or West African thrush (Turdus pelios) is a passerine bird in the thrush family Turdidae. It is common in well-wooded areas over much of the western part of sub-Saharan Africa, it was once considered to be conspecific with the olive thrush but that species has now been split further.
f: Populations are resident (non-migratory).

t: The song thrush (Turdus philomelos) is a thrush that breeds across the West Palearctic. It has brown upperparts and black-spotted cream or buff underparts and has four recognised subspecies.
f: The song thrush builds a neat, mud-lined cup nest in a bush or tree and lays four to five dark-spotted blue eggs.

t: The fieldfare (Turdus pilaris) is a member of the thrush family Turdidae. It breeds in woodland and scrub in northern Europe and across the Palearctic.
f: There may be two broods in southern parts of the range but only one further north.

t: The mountain thrush (Turdus plebejus) is species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies. It was formerly known as the mountain robin and has also been called the American mountain thrush.
f: It is found from Mexico to Panama.

t: The Western red-legged thrush (Turdus plumbeus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It formerly occurred on the Swan Islands, Honduras, but was extirpated there.
f: Native to the Caribbean, it is found in the Bahamas, Cayman Islands, and Cuba.

t: The Tasman Sea island thrush (Turdus poliocephalus) is an extinct forest bird in the thrush family that was formerly found on Lord Howe Island and Norfolk Island in the Pacific Ocean. The two subspecies of the Tasman Sea island thrush became extinct in historical times.
f: It is part of the "island thrush" complex that has been split into 17 species based on a molecular phylogenetic study published in 2023.

t: The plumbeous-backed thrush (Turdus reevei) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

t: The chestnut thrush (Turdus rubrocanus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It breeds in the western Himalayas and central/southwestern China; it winters in Eastern Himalaya and northern Southeast Asia.
f: It is socially monogamous, but extra-pair partners are common.

t: The red-throated thrush (Turdus ruficollis) is a passerine bird in the thrush family. It is sometimes regarded as one subspecies of a polytypic species, "dark-throated thrush", black-throated thrush then being the other subspecies.
f: The scientific name comes from Latin.

t: The rufous-collared thrush (Turdus rufitorques) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies. Some taxonomic systems call it the rufous-collared robin.
f: It is found in El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.

t: The rufous-bellied thrush (Turdus rufiventris) is a songbird of the thrush family (Turdidae). Its distribution covers most of eastern and southeastern Brazil from the states of Maranhão south to Rio Grande do Sul, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay, and central regions of Argentina.
f: It is one of the most common birds across much of southeastern Brazil, and is known there under the name sabiá-laranjeira (Portuguese pronunciation: [sabiˈa laɾɐ̃ˈʒejɾɐ]).

t: The rufous-backed thrush (Turdus rufopalliatus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It is also known as the rufous-backed robin.
f: It is endemic to Mexico but is also a casual visitor to the southwestern United States.

t: The varzea thrush (Turdus sanchezorum) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Brazil, Colombia, and Peru.

t: The glossy-black thrush (Turdus serranus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found from Venezuela to Argentina.

t: The Indian blackbird (Turdus simillimus) is a member of the thrush family Turdidae. It was formerly considered a subspecies of the common blackbird.
f: It is found only in India and Sri Lanka.

t: The Karoo thrush (Turdus smithi), also known as Smith's thrush, is a member of the thrush family in Africa. It has traditionally been considered a subspecies of the olive thrush (with which it is known to hybridize), but is increasingly treated as a separate species.
f: The specific name honours the Scottish military surgeon and zoologist Sir Andrew Smith.

t: The blacksmith thrush or eastern slaty thrush (Turdus subalaris) is a passerine bird in the family Turdidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The La Selle thrush (Turdus swalesi) is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Turdidae, the thrushes and allies.
f: It is endemic to the Caribbean island of Hispaniola that is shared by the Dominican Republic and Haiti.

t: The bare-eyed thrush (Turdus tephronotus) is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It is found in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and Tanzania.
f: It breeds during the rainy season.

t: The ring ouzel (Turdus torquatus) is a mainly European member of the thrush family Turdidae. It is a medium-sized thrush, 23–24 centimetres (9.1–9.4 in) in length and weighing 90–138 grams (3.2–4.9 oz).
f: During spring migration and the breeding season, invertebrates dominate the adult's diet and are also fed to the chicks.

t: Tickell's thrush (Turdus unicolor) is a passerine bird in the thrush family Turdidae. The name commemorates the British ornithologist Samuel Tickell who collected in India and Burma.
f: It is common in open forest in the Himalayas, and migrates seasonally into peninsular India, Nepal and rarely to Bangladesh.

t: The mistle thrush (Turdus viscivorus) is a bird common to much of Europe, temperate Asia and North Africa. It is a year-round resident in a large part of its range, but northern and eastern populations migrate south for the winter, often in small flocks.
f: The male has a loud, far-carrying song which is delivered even in wet and windy weather, earning the bird the old name of stormcock.

t: The red-backed buttonquail (Turnix maculosus) is a species of bird in the family Turnicidae. Other names by which it is known in different parts of its range include black-backed, black-spotted and orange-breasted buttonquail.
f: It is found in Australia, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines and the Solomon Islands.

t: The barred buttonquail or common bustard-quail (Turnix suscitator) is a species of buttonquail, one of a small family (Turnicidae) of birds which resemble, but are not closely related to, the true quails.
f: This species is resident from India across tropical Asia to south China, Indonesia and the Philippines.

The common buttonquail (Turnix sylvaticus), also called Kurrichane buttonquail and Andalusian hemipode, is a buttonquail, one of a small family of birds that resemble but are not closely related to the true quails.

t: The painted buttonquail (Turnix varius) is a species of buttonquail, the family Turnicidae, which resemble, but are unrelated to, the quails of Phasianidae. A subspecies, the Abrolhos painted buttonquail (Turnix varius scintillans), is endemic to the Houtman Abrolhos islands.
f: This species is resident in Australia where numbers are believed to be in decline.

t: The black-billed wood dove or black-billed dove (Turtur abyssinicus) is a pigeon which is a widespread resident breeding bird in a belt across Africa just south of the Sahara Desert. This species is abundant in near desert, scrub and savannah.
f: Black-billed wood doves eat grass and other small seeds.

t: The blue-spotted wood dove or blue-spotted dove (Turtur afer) is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.
f: It is abundantly present throughout Africa south of the Sahel; it is partially present in East Africa and absent in southern Africa.

t: The blue-headed wood dove (Turtur brehmeri), also known as the blue-headed dove, is a medium-sized (up to 25 cm (9.8 in) long), rufous brown wood-dove with bluish-grey head, iridescent green patches on wings, reddish bill, dark brown iris, and dark red feet. The young is duller in colour than adult.
f: The blue-headed wood dove nests in trees.

t: The emerald-spotted wood dove or emerald-spotted dove (Turtur chalcospilos) is a bird of the family Columbidae, resident across eastern and southern Africa. It is a species of open drier deciduous woodland and second growth.
f: It is absent from evergreen rainforests and semidesert areas.

t: The tambourine dove (Turtur tympanistria) is a pigeon which is a widespread resident breeding bird in woodlands and other thick vegetation in Africa south of the Sahara Desert. Its range extends from Senegal east to Ethiopia and Kenya and southwards through eastern Africa to south-eastern South Africa, but it is absent from the drier areas of south-western Africa.
f: Both sexes incubate, although this task is performed mainly by the female, and the eggs hatch in 13 days with another 13–14 days to fledging.

t: The tylas vanga (Tylas eduardi) is a species of bird in the family Vangidae. It is monotypic within the genus Tylas.
f: Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forest and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

t: The greater prairie-chicken or pinnated grouse (Tympanuchus cupido), sometimes called a boomer, is a large bird in the grouse tribe. This North American species was once abundant but has become extremely rare or extirpated over much of its range due to habitat loss, natural disasters, and overhunting.
f: One of the most famous aspects of these creatures is the mating ritual called booming.
The lesser prairie-chicken (Tympanuchus pallidicinctus) is a species in the grouse tribe.

t: The sharp-tailed grouse (Tympanuchus phasianellus), also known as the sharptail or fire grouse, is a medium-sized prairie grouse. One of three species in the genus Tympanuchus, the sharp-tailed grouse is found throughout Alaska, much of Northern and Western Canada, and parts of the Western and Midwestern United States.
f: The sharp-tailed grouse is the provincial bird of the Canadian province of Saskatchewan.

t: The dwarf tyrant-manakin or dwarf tyranneutes (Tyranneutes stolzmanni) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae, the manakins.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The tiny tyrant-manakin or tiny tyranneutes (Tyranneutes virescens) is a species of bird in the family Pipridae, the manakins.
f: It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

t: The sulphury flycatcher (Tyrannopsis sulphurea) is a passerine bird of the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found on Trinidad and in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The yellow-crowned tyrannulet (Tyrannulus elatus) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, and in every mainland South American country except Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

t: The white-throated kingbird (Tyrannus albogularis) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela, in French Guiana as a vagrant, and possibly in Argentina and Colombia.

t: The loggerhead kingbird (Tyrannus caudifasciatus) is a species of sub-oscine passerine bird belonging to the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: This species is found in wooded habitats in the islands of the northern Caribbean, with records of vagrants from Florida.

t: Couch's kingbird (Tyrannus couchii) is a passerine tyrant flycatcher of the kingbird genus. It is found from southern Texas along the Gulf Coast to the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico, Belize and northern Guatemala.
f: The species is named after soldier and naturalist Darius N.

t: The thick-billed kingbird (Tyrannus crassirostris) is a large member of the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in the southwestern United States, Mexico, and Guatemala.

t: The gray kingbird or grey kingbird (Tyrannus dominicensis), also known as pitirre, petchary or white-breasted kingbird, is a passerine bird in the tyrant flycatchers family Tyrannidae.
f: The species was first described on the island of Hispaniola, then called Santo Domingo, thus the dominicensis name.

t: The scissor-tailed flycatcher (Tyrannus forficatus), known as swallow-tailed flycatcher or scissorstail, is a long-tailed insectivorous bird of the genus Tyrannus, whose members are collectively referred to as kingbirds.
f: It is found in North and Central America, and is Oklahoma's State Bird.

t: The tropical kingbird (Tyrannus melancholicus) is a large tyrant flycatcher. This bird breeds from southern Arizona and the lower Rio Grande Valley of Texas in the United States through Central America, South America as far as south as central Argentina and eastern Peru, and on Trinidad and Tobago.
f: Birds from the northernmost and southern breeding areas migrate to warmer parts of the range after breeding.

t: The snowy-throated kingbird (Tyrannus niveigularis) is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The fork-tailed flycatcher (Tyrannus savana) is a passerine bird of the tyrant flycatcher family and is a member of a genus typically referred to as kingbirds. Named for the long, forked tail, particularly in males, fork-tailed flycatchers are seen in shrubland, savanna, lightly forested and grassland areas, from southern Mexico to Argentina.
f: They are frequently observed on conspicuous perches whence they sally after insect prey.

t: The eastern kingbird (Tyrannus tyrannus) is a large tyrant flycatcher native to the Americas. The bird is predominantly dark gray with white underbelly and pointed wings.
f: The Eastern kingbird is migratory, with its breeding range spread across North America and its wintering range in Central and South America.
The western kingbird (Tyrannus verticalis) is a large tyrant flycatcher found throughout western North America, as far south as Mexico.

t: Cassin's kingbird (Tyrannus vociferans) is a large tyrant flycatcher native to western North America.
f: The name of this bird commemorates the American ornithologist John Cassin.

t: The western barn owl (Tyto alba) is a species of barn owl native to Europe, southwestern Asia, and Africa. It was formerly considered a subspecies group together with barn owls native to other parts of the world, but this classification was found to be paraphyletic with respect to some other members of the genus.
f: The owls usually mate for life unless one of the pair is killed, whereupon a new pair bond may be formed.

The Australian masked owl (Tyto novaehollandiae), also the Australasian masked owl or simply the masked owl, especially in Australia, is a barn owl of Southern New Guinea and the non-desert areas of Australia.

t: The sooty owl or greater sooty owl (Tyto tenebricosa) is a medium to large owl found in south-eastern Australia, Montane rainforests of New Guinea and have been seen on Flinders Island in the Bass Strait. It is substantially smaller and occurs in the wet tropics region of North Queensland, Australia.
f: The lesser sooty owl (T. multipunctata), is sometimes considered to be conspecific with this species, in which case they are then together referred to as sooty owls.

t: The scale-throated earthcreeper (Upucerthia dumetaria) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Peru, and possibly Uruguay.

t: The Patagonian forest earthcreeper (Upucerthia saturatior), also known as the forest earthcreeper, is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina and Chile.

t: The buff-breasted earthcreeper (Upucerthia validirostris) is a species of bird in the Furnariinae subfamily of the ovenbird family Furnariidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.

t: The Eurasian hoopoe or common hoopoe (Upupa epops) is the most widespread species of hoopoe. It is a distinctive cinnamon coloured bird with black and white wings, a tall erectile crest, a broad white band across a black tail, and a long narrow downcurved bill.
f: Its call is a soft "oop-oop-oop".

t: The Madagascar hoopoe (Upupa marginata) is a species of hoopoe in the family Upupidae. It was previously considered a subspecies (Upupa epops marginata) of the hoopoe, but was split due to its vocalisations and small differences in plumage.
f: It is endemic to Madagascar, where its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry forest.
It is also relatively commonly kept as an aviary bird.

t: The red-cheeked cordon-bleu or red-cheeked cordonbleu (Uraeginthus bengalus) is a small passerine bird in the family Estrildidae. Red-cheeked cordon-bleu has an estimated global extent of occurrence of 7,700,000 km2.
f: This estrildid finch is a resident breeding bird in drier regions of tropical Sub-Saharan Africa.

t: The Andean emerald (Uranomitra franciae) is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The common murre or common guillemot (Uria aalge) is a large auk, one of several species called murre or guillemot. It has a circumpolar distribution, occurring in low-Arctic and boreal waters in the North Atlantic and North Pacific.
f: They make no nest; their single egg is incubated between the adult's feet on a bare rock ledge on a cliff face.

t: The thick-billed murre or Brünnich's guillemot (Uria lomvia) is a bird in the auk family (Alcidae). The very deeply black North Pacific subspecies Uria lomvia arra is also called Pallas' murre after its describer.
f: This bird is named after the Danish zoologist Morten Thrane Brünnich.

The Taiwan blue magpie (Urocissa caerulea), also called the Taiwan magpie, Formosan blue magpie (Chinese: 臺灣藍鵲; pinyin: Táiwān lán què), or the "long-tailed mountain lady" , is a bird species in the crow family.

t: The red-billed blue magpie (Urocissa erythroryncha) is a species of bird (magpie) in the crow family, Corvidae. It is 65–68 cm (25.5–27 in) long and weighs 196–232 g (6.9–8.2 oz).
f: It is about the same size as the Eurasian magpie, but has a much longer tail, one of the longest of any corvid.

t: The yellow-billed blue-magpie or gold-billed magpie (Urocissa flavirostris) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, along with crows and jays. The species' range covers the northern parts of the Indian subcontinent, including the lower Himalayan foothills, with a disjunct population in Vietnam.
f: It forms a superspecies with the Taiwan blue magpie and the red-billed blue magpie.

t: The Sri Lanka blue magpie or Ceylon magpie (Urocissa ornata) is a brightly coloured member of the family Corvidae, found exclusively in Sri Lanka. Its flight is rather weak, though, and is rarely used to cover great distances.
f: This species is adapted to hunting in the dense canopy, where it is highly active and nimble.

t: The red-faced mousebird (Urocolius indicus) is a species of mousebird or coly. It is a common in southern Africa from the Democratic Republic of Congo (formerly Zaire), Zambia and Tanzania south to the Cape.
f: Their call is tree-ree-ree whistle, and regularly called in multiple repetitions.

t: The blue-naped mousebird (Urocolius macrourus), also formerly called the blue-naped coly (Colius macrourus) is a species of bird belonging to the family Coliidae within the order Coliiformes. The species is found in the wild in the drier regions of West Africa to East Africa, as well as Sahel.
f: It is one of the remaining six species of mousebirds.

t: Przevalski's finch (Urocynchramus pylzowi), Przewalski's finch or Przevalski's pinktail, is an unusual passerine bird endemic to the mountains of central-west China. Its taxonomic affinities were unclear for a long time, giving rise to other common names, the pink-tailed bunting and the Przewalski's rosefinch.
f: The species is named after Mikhail Pyltsov, the Russian explorer who accompanied Nikolai Przhevalsky on the expedition in which specimens of the bird were collected.

t: The long-tailed koel (Urodynamis taitensis), also known as the long-tailed cuckoo, Pacific long-tailed cuckoo, sparrow hawk, home owl, screecher, screamer or koekoeā in Māori, is a species of the Cuculidae bird family (the cuckoos). It is the only species placed in the genus Urodynamis.
f: It is a migratory bird that spends spring and summer in New Zealand, its only breeding place, and spends winter in the Pacific islands.

t: The agile tit-tyrant (Uromyias agilis) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.
f: It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Venezuela.
The unstreaked tit-tyrant (Uromyias agraphia) is a species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.

t: The lyre-tailed nightjar (Uropsalis lyra) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

t: The swallow-tailed nightjar (Uropsalis segmentata) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae.
f: It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The white-bellied wren (Uropsila leucogastra) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.
f: It is found in Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.

t: The pale-footed bush warbler (Hemitesia pallidipes) is a species of oriental warbler in the family Cettiidae that is found in southern Asia. It occurs in the Himalayan region west from Dehradun through the foothills of Nepal to northeastern India.
f: A single sighting was recorded from Kandy, Sri Lanka in March 1993.

t: The Asian stubtail (Urosphena squameiceps) is a bird in the family Cettiidae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1863.
f: It breeds in Northeast Asia and Japan.

t: The Timor stubtail (Urosphena subulata) is a species of bird in the family Cettiidae.
f: It is found on Timor and northern and eastern adjacent islands.

t: The Bornean stubtail (Urosphena whiteheadi) is a species of bird in the cettiid warbler family Cettiidae. It is endemic to the island of Borneo, where it inhabits forest floors and undergrowth in montane forests at elevations of 750–3,150 m (2,460–10,330 ft).
f: Nests are made out of reddish plant fibres, with incubation taking 24 days on average.

t: The black-backed bush tanager (Urothraupis stolzmanni), also known as the black-backed bush-finch, is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.
f: It is the only member in the genus Urothraupis.

t: The long-tailed hawk (Urotriorchis macrourus) is an African bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.
f: It is the only member of the genus Urotriorchis.

t: The blacksmith lapwing or blacksmith plover (Vanellus armatus) is a lapwing species that occurs commonly from Kenya through central Tanzania to southern and southwestern Africa.
f: The vernacular name derives from the repeated metallic 'tink, tink, tink' alarm call, which suggests a blacksmith's hammer striking an anvil.

t: The pied plover (Hoploxypterus cayanus), also known as the pied lapwing, is a species of bird in the family Charadriidae. It is a bird of least concern according to the IUCN and can be found in northern South America.
f: The species name cayanus refers to Cayenne, the capital of French Guiana, where the pied plover can be found.

t: The southern lapwing (Vanellus chilensis), commonly called quero-quero in Brazil, or tero in Argentina and Uruguay, tero-tero in Paraguay, and queltehue in Chile is a wader in the order Charadriiformes. It is a common and widespread resident throughout South America, except in densely forested regions (e.g. most of the Amazon), the higher parts of the Andes, and the arid coast of a large part of western South America.
f: It reached Trinidad in 1961, Tobago in 1974, and has rapidly increased on both islands, sporadically making its way North to Barbados where one pair mated, nested, and produced chicks in 2007.

t: The grey-headed lapwing (Vanellus cinereus) is a lapwing species which breeds in northeast China and Japan. The Japanese population winters, at least partially, in southern Honshū.
f: The mainland population winters in northern Southeast Asia from northeastern India to Cambodia.

t: The crowned lapwing (Vanellus coronatus), crowned plover or kiewiet (in South African English), is a bird of the lapwing subfamily that occurs contiguously from the Red Sea coast of Somalia to southern and southwestern Africa. It is related to the more localized black-winged and Senegal lapwings, with which it shares some plumage characteristics.
f: It is an adaptable and numerous species, with bold and noisy habits.

t: The river lapwing (Vanellus duvaucelii) is a lapwing species which breeds from the Indian subcontinent eastwards to Southeast Asia. It range includes much of northern and northeastern India, and extends through Southeast Asia to Vietnam.
f: It appears to be entirely sedentary.

t: The red-wattled lapwing (Vanellus indicus) is an Asian lapwing or large plover, a wader in the family Charadriidae. Like other lapwings they are ground birds that are incapable of perching.
f: Adults near the nest fly around, diving at potential predators while calling noisily.

t: The white-tailed lapwing or white-tailed plover (Vanellus leucurus) is a wader in the lapwing genus. The genus name Vanellus is Medieval Latin for a lapwing and derives from vannus, which refers to a winnowing fan.
f: It is the only lapwing likely to be seen in other than very shallow water, where it picks insects and other small prey mainly from the surface.

t: The yellow-wattled lapwing (Vanellus malabaricus) is a lapwing that is endemic to the Indian subcontinent. It is found mainly on the dry plains of peninsular India and has a sharp call and is capable of fast flight.
f: Although they do not migrate, they are known to make seasonal movements in response to rains.

t: The spot-breasted lapwing (Vanellus melanocephalus), also known as the spot-breasted plover, is a species of bird in the family Charadriidae. It is endemic to the Ethiopian Highlands.
f: It is a non-migratory bird that occurs over 247,000 square kilometers.

t: It is a habitat specialist of short grass in well-watered temperate grasslands. In their tightly grouped flying flocks they resemble plovers.
f: They may move about locally to find ideal situations, often at night.

t: The masked lapwing (Vanellus miles) is a large, common and conspicuous bird native to Australia , New Zealand and New Guinea. It spends most of its time on the ground searching for food such as insects and worms and has several distinctive calls.
f: It is common in Australian fields, open land and where there is lots of water, and is known for its defensive swooping behaviour during the nesting season.

t: The Andean lapwing (Vanellus resplendens) is a species of bird in family Charadriidae, the plovers and their relatives.
f: It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

t: The African wattled lapwing (Vanellus senegallus), also known as the Senegal wattled plover or simply wattled lapwing, is a large lapwing, a group of largish waders in the family Charadriidae. It is a resident breeder in most of sub-Saharan Africa outside the rainforests, although it has seasonal movements.
f: It lays three or four eggs on a ground scrape.
The spur-winged lapwing or spur-winged plover (Vanellus spinosus) is a lapwing species, one of a group of largish waders in the family Charadriidae.
